title: regex: interval bounds are not capped at RE_DUP_MAX (a{32768} compiles)
description: string/regex.rs parse_brace_quantifier / parse_bre_brace_quantifier never check the interval bound against RE_DUP_MAX (32767); a{32768} compiles and the Compiler emits 32768 NFA copies (a memory-amplification hazard). glibc rejects it. Fix: define RE_DUP_MAX=32767 and return REG_BADBR (POSIX.2) when min/max exceeds it.
close_reason: regex parse_brace_quantifier/parse_bre_brace_quantifier now reject interval bounds above RE_DUP_MAX (32767) with REG_BADBR per POSIX.2, closing the a{32768} memory-amplification hazard. New test brace_interval_edges asserts a{32768} fails and a{32767} compiles.

title: [STANDING WARNING] The 2026-08-04 'superseded by <sha>' comment sweep is unreliable — 4 of 7 audited were wrong; never close on one without re-reading source
description:
A comment sweep on 2026-08-04 added 'BLOCKER: superseded by <sha> ...' to a large number of open beads. Those comments are being used to close beads. THEY MUST NOT BE, on their own.

AUDITED 2026-08-05 (OliveChapel), 7 beads checked against the source at HEAD. FOUR were wrong:

  bd-c7cs3h  syslog setlogmask     FALSE ON BOTH HALVES.
      Claimed the syslog path 'filters via SYSLOG_MASK'. SYSLOG_MASK had exactly two readers and
      both were inside setlogmask() itself; syslog/vsyslog/syslog_send never consulted it. The fix
      HAD landed (dc6bdb4e0) and was silently DELETED by e634aff2a. Six weeks with syslog ignoring
      setlogmask entirely. The cited 'differential gate 3376bed21' belongs to a DIFFERENT bead
      (bd-22qdtd) and never calls syslog().
  bd-7rbh4r  tempnam TMPDIR        FALSE.
      Claimed 'performs glibc-style candidate selection before allocation'. tempnam hardcoded /tmp
      when dir was NULL, never read TMPDIR, never checked directory existence, and defaulted the
      prefix to 'tmp' instead of 'file'. Four divergences, of which the bead title named one.
  bd-egk49q  humanize_number errno FALSE ON THE COVERAGE HALF.
      The errno MAPPING survived in stdlib_abi.rs, so the claim looked right. Every assertion for it
      had been deleted by bd829b12f. Contract held, coverage did not — which is why nobody noticed.
  bd-5zrf92  obsolete signal wrappers  TOO WEAK TO BE MEANINGFUL.
      Two agents cited 'regression coverage'. The coverage passed only signal 0, which cannot
      distinguish a range check from a zero special-case. Strengthening it found a LIVE defect:
      sigignore(32)/(33) returned 0 where glibc returns -1/EINVAL.

Three were accurate: bd-emgdrv (real fix, real differential gate — closed on replay), bd-vxpc1y and
bd-enxo3y (source correct, but NO gate that could fail, so they needed one written).

So of 7: 2 outright false, 1 false on coverage, 1 too weak, 2 correct-but-ungated, 1 fully correct.
Only ONE of seven was safe to close as the comment implied.

ROOT CAUSE for two of them: bd-bldxfy found that e634aff2a and bd829b12f (2026-06-26, nine seconds
apart, both describing narrow unrelated work) silently deleted ~1300 lines including shipped fixes
and their tests. The sweep read the beads and the commit log, not the source at HEAD, so it could
not see that the cited fixes no longer existed.

THE RULE, which costs two greps:
  1. Does the SOURCE at HEAD still do the thing? Read the function, do not trust the commit message.
     A function can survive while a rule inside it was deleted — that is exactly bd-c7cs3h.
  2. Does the CITED GATE exercise THIS behaviour? Open it. Check the bead id it names and whether it
     drives the actual observable. A gate for a neighbouring bead, or one that only sets up state,
     does not count.
  3. If the source is right but nothing could fail on the original bug, the bead is NOT done —
     write the gate, then close on it.
Closing over a live defect is not cheap. Two greps are.

DONE = this warning is reflected where closers will see it. Concretely: a note in AGENTS.md's
closure-discipline section pointing at this bead, and the ~245 ready beads carrying a 'superseded by'
comment are either re-verified or have that comment demoted to advisory. Re-verifying all of them is
a large job and should be split; the immediate requirement is that NO further bead is closed on the
strength of one of these comments alone.

Evidence: bd-bldxfy (deletion audit), bd-c7cs3h, bd-7rbh4r, bd-egk49q, bd-5zrf92, bd-emgdrv,
bd-vxpc1y, bd-enxo3y — each closure note records what was checked and what it found.

Also recorded, for whoever picks up the re-verification: the worktree used to prove bd-c7cs3h's gate goes red was removed with explicit user approval (git worktree remove, 2026-08-06T01:46:19Z), so /data/projects/.worktrees no longer holds a deliberately broken syslog_send.

title: ffs-types: S_IS* predicates lack proptest MR coverage
description:
Finding (via /testing-metamorphic skill, seventh visit, different
target): the seven POSIX S_IS* predicates landed by bd-vnfhb
(`is_regular_file`, `is_directory`, `is_symlink`,
`is_character_device`, `is_block_device`, `is_fifo`, `is_socket`)
have ONE fixed-input kernel-conformance test pinning the canonical
S_IF* constants. The full u16 input space (65536 values) is
unexplored.

Concrete metamorphic relations not yet pinned:

  MR-A — Mask isolation: for any u16 mode,
         predicate(mode) == predicate(mode & S_IFMT)
         (the predicate ignores lower 12 bits / permissions /
         sticky/setuid/setgid).

  MR-B — Mutual exclusivity (no overlap): for any u16 mode, AT MOST
         ONE of the seven predicates returns true. A regression that
         changed `==` to `&` in any predicate would fail this MR.

  MR-C — Total coverage on the canonical 7-element set: each S_IF*
         constant satisfies EXACTLY one predicate. Pinned by the
         fixed-input test but worth re-stating in proptest form for
         the full input space (modes outside the 7 canonical values
         must satisfy NONE; the 7 canonical values must satisfy
         exactly one).

A regression that flipped a mask from `& S_IFMT` to `& S_IFREG`
would silently misclassify every mode. Fixed-input tests catch
hand-picked cases; proptest scale catches off-by-one or sense
errors across the full 16-bit space.

Acceptance: 3 new proptests in the existing tests module of
crates/ffs-types/src/lib.rs covering MR-A, MR-B, and MR-C.
notes: Shipped: 3 new MR proptests in crates/ffs-types/src/lib.rs's proptest! block. MR-A (mask isolation — every predicate ignores the lower 12 bits), MR-B (mutual exclusivity — at most one predicate returns true for any u16), MR-C (total coverage — modes in the canonical S_IF* set satisfy exactly one predicate; modes outside satisfy none). Pairs with bd-vnfhb (the predicates themselves, kernel-conformance fixed-input pin) — same target, lifted from fixed-input to proptest scale. All 3 pass via rch exec -- cargo test -p ffs-types --lib proptest_s_is_predicates.

title: [reality-check WS-2] Wire the runtime-math control plane live (currently dormant by default)
description: Owner decision 2026-05-20: dormancy is a defect, wire it live. The ~71 runtime-math kernels are real code but inert in the shipped default config: OBSERVE_FEEDBACK_STATE is DISABLED and never enabled outside tests, runtime_policy::decide() returns passthrough in strict mode and never initializes RUNTIME_READY under LD_PRELOAD, so ~64 exotic cached_state atomics are frozen at 0. Approach: safe RUNTIME_READY arming modeled as a constrained POMDP to avoid the known re-entrancy deadlock; enable OBSERVE_FEEDBACK; strict-mode observation policy (observe and route, never rewrite); per-call monitor selection as submodular maximization under a latency knapsack via design.rs and bandit.rs so the math schedules itself within budget; reconcile the 12 FFI-PCC certificates that bypass the membrane even in hardened mode. Done-when: a workload shows non-zero exotic kernel state and at least one decision changed by a runtime-math signal, perf gate green or budget honestly revised. Full context: REALITY_CHECK_BRIDGE_PLAN.md WS-2.
close_reason: done

title: [RC-WS2.1] Safe RUNTIME_READY arming under LD_PRELOAD via constrained-POMDP model
description: decide() never initializes RUNTIME_READY under LD_PRELOAD because of a known pipeline re-entrancy deadlock. Use a constrained-POMDP framing (belief over past-the-membrane-sensitive-startup-window, action arm-or-wait) as the design JUSTIFICATION, but per the developer-transparency contract the SHIPPED runtime arming must compile down to a compact deterministic guard -- not literal POMDP machinery on the hot path. RUNTIME_READY flips at a provably-safe milestone via a simple guard; the POMDP analysis is recorded as design rationale only. Riskiest bead in WS-2. Unit tests (happy/edge/error): window-closed observation triggers arm; window-open keeps waiting; a re-entrant decide() call during arming returns a safe passthrough and does not deadlock. e2e: a constructor-heavy C++ binary preloads with the kernel armed and no deadlock; structured logging of the arming transition.
close_reason: done

title: [RC-WS2.2] Enable OBSERVE_FEEDBACK by default and feed exotic kernel state
description: OBSERVE_FEEDBACK_STATE is DISABLED and never enabled outside tests, so ~64 exotic cached_state atomics are frozen at 0 and contribute a constant zero to every decision. Enable it by default and feed the atomics from live observations. Unit tests (happy/edge/error): enabled feeds atomics; an observation with no signal leaves state coherent; a malformed observation is rejected without poisoning state. e2e: after a representative workload, at least 90 percent of the exotic cached_state atomics are non-zero (matching the plan success metric). Structured logging of the feedback path.
close_reason: done

title: [RC-WS2.3] Strict-mode observation policy in decide()
description: decide() returns passthrough for all of strict mode today. Make it run the kernel in strict mode for observation and FullValidate routing only, with no Repair rewrites so strict stays ABI-faithful. Test: a strict-mode workload emits evidence records and performs no behavior rewrite.
close_reason: done

title: [RC-WS2.4] Submodular-knapsack per-call monitor scheduler
description: Wiring all 71 kernels per call cannot meet the under-20ns budget. Per-call monitor selection is submodular maximization under a latency knapsack: greedy (1 minus 1/e)-optimal selection of the most informative kernel subset, with design.rs supplying the information matrix and bandit.rs routing depth. The math schedules itself. Depends on RC-WS2.1 and RC-WS2.2. Test: per-call monitor count is bounded; greedy selection matches the (1 minus 1/e) bound on a fixture.
close_reason: done

title: [RC-WS2.5] Reconcile the 12 FFI-PCC certificates that bypass the membrane
description: 12 FFI-PCC certificates short-circuit the hottest symbols (malloc, free, memcpy, memcmp, strlen, snprintf) in BOTH modes, so hardened mode performs no repair on them. Per symbol, either prove the certificate sound and document it as an intentional fast-path exemption, or route it through the membrane in hardened mode. May reveal a correctness hole, not just a perf shortcut. Test: a hardened-mode double-free on a certificated symbol is repaired, or the exemption carries a proof.
close_reason: done

title: [RC-WS2.6] Runtime-math liveness gates
description: Add gates that prove the kernels are live: assert OBSERVE_FEEDBACK enabled in the shipped artifact; assert each kernel output reaches a decision; snapshot a workload kernel-state vector as a golden. Test: the liveness gate fails if OBSERVE_FEEDBACK is disabled or any kernel output is unreachable.
close_reason: done

title: [RC-WS2.7] Perf re-validation with the runtime math live
description: Re-measure strict and hardened per-call overhead with the math live, AND re-run the full WS-1 heavyweight workload battery (python3, perl/node, coreutils) under the new configuration -- wiring the math live adds overhead and must not re-break python3 or any binary WS-1 fixed. If the under-20ns strict and under-200ns hardened budgets cannot hold, revise the published budget honestly and update README and FEATURE_PARITY rather than leaving an unmet claim. Depends on RC-WS2.4, RC-WS2.5 (FFI-PCC reconciliation changes hot-path cost), and the RC-WS1 e2e battery. Test: perf gate green AND the WS-1 heavyweight battery still green, or the budget revised with measured evidence and structured logs.
close_reason: done

title: [RC-WS2.E2E] End-to-end runtime-math-live verification with decision-trace logging
description: A deterministic e2e harness running a representative workload with the runtime math armed, emitting a structured JSON-line decision trace per call (monitors consulted, kernel states, chosen action). Asserts: exotic kernel states are non-zero after the workload; at least one decision was changed by a runtime-math signal; per-call monitor count stays within the latency budget; no deadlock on constructor-heavy C++ binaries; strict mode observes without rewriting; and the FRANKENLIBC_RUNTIME_MATH=off kill-switch fully disables the math while basic membrane validation still runs. Happy/edge/error coverage. Confirms the companion unit tests for every WS-2 bead exist and pass.
close_reason: done

title: [RC-WS2.8] Runtime-math kill-switch escape hatch
description: Wiring the runtime-math control plane live (WS-2) changes the decision path of every libc call. A user hit by an unexpected regression needs to disable the runtime math WITHOUT disabling the whole membrane or reverting to an old build. Add a process-level escape hatch (FRANKENLIBC_RUNTIME_MATH=on|off) resolved once at init alongside FRANKENLIBC_MODE and immutable after: when off, decide() uses the basic null/bloom/arena/fingerprint/canary validation path with no runtime-math kernel consultation; the membrane safety checks still run. Unit tests (happy/edge/error): off disables only the math, on (default) keeps it live, an invalid value falls back to on with a logged warning, the value is immutable after init. e2e: run a workload with the switch off and assert zero runtime-math decision records while basic membrane validation still occurs; structured logging. Document the knob in DEPLOYMENT.md and the WS-4.6 compatibility guide.
close_reason: done

title: [RC-WS6.3] Owned unwinder replaces libgcc fallback end-to-end
description: Exercise owned_unwind_abi.rs end-to-end and remove the libgcc fallback from the L2 path. Done-when: a C++ exception unwinds through the owned unwinder with rch-backed evidence and no host libgcc dependency.
notes: Owned unwinder phase-1/phase-2 implementation complete (bd-gq1kz7.4 closed). LD_PRELOAD end-to-end proof blocked: (1) static fixtures embed libgcc _Unwind_* symbols, LD_PRELOAD cannot interpose; (2) dynamic fixtures trigger libstdc++ initialization exceptions that require .eh_frame data from shared libraries, but owned unwinder only searches frames registered via __register_frame. Full replacement proof requires either (a) dl_iterate_phdr-based .eh_frame discovery for arbitrary loaded objects, or (b) standalone interpreter mode where FrankenLibC is the PT_INTERP and controls all symbol resolution.
close_reason: Closed by commit 41e4422d and bd-b2m2h6. The owned-unwind E2E now builds a shared C++ throw/catch fixture with no libgcc_s/libunwind DT_NEEDED entries, leaves _Unwind_RaiseException unresolved until FrankenLibC is loaded RTLD_GLOBAL, verifies the fixture has PT_GNU_EH_FRAME, and catches successfully without any manual __register_frame call. Evidence: remote standalone+owned-unwind-stub release build, owned_unwind_abi_test 21/21, check_owned_unwinder_e2e.sh pass, workspace cargo check/clippy via rch, cargo fmt --check, jq, git diff --check.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Blocked after inspection by SnowyMill. The current owned_unwind_abi.rs is explicitly gated behind standalone,owned-unwind-stub and documents itself as an abort-mode symbol-edge substitute, not a general unwinder. _Unwind_RaiseException, _Unwind_Resume, _Unwind_SetGR, and _Unwind_SetIP abort, while tests/conformance/standalone_owned_unwind_experiment.v1.json marks the owned-unwind lane report-only with replacement_level_change_allowed=false and promotion_allowed_on_pass=false. That cannot satisfy this bead's done-when of a C++ exception unwinding end-to-end through an owned unwinder with no host libgcc dependency. Needs either a real DWARF/personality unwinder design/implementation bead or a narrowed blocker-reduction bead for the existing abort-mode symbol-edge lane.

title: ssignal_and_gsignal_deliver_signal test fails (SIGNAL_HIT is 0)
description: The `ssignal_and_gsignal_deliver_signal` test in `unistd_abi_test.rs` fails because the signal handler installed by `ssignal` is not observing `SIGUSR1` when raised via `gsignal`. title: PORT: 3 Linux 6.7+ futex2 syscall wrappers (futex_wake/wait/requeue)
description: Add 3 Linux 6.7+ futex2 syscall wrappers to close the futex2 family gap. title: P0: wcstok overreads tracked unterminated delimiter
description:
[CRITICAL] `frankenlibc_abi::wchar_abi::wcstok` bounds the token buffer through the runtime policy decision on `start`, but it scans the delimiter string with `scan_w_string(delim, None)` and therefore ignores `known_remaining(delim)`. A valid caller can pass a tracked delimiter buffer without a NUL terminator; the ABI code then performs an unbounded unsafe read past that allocation while building the delimiter set.

Evidence:
- `crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/wchar_abi.rs:1556-1563` accepts non-null `delim` and `save_ptr`.
- `crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/wchar_abi.rs:1578-1584` makes the runtime decision using only `start` as the address and `known_remaining(start)` as the suspiciousness input.
- `crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/wchar_abi.rs:1591-1593` calls `scan_w_string(delim, None)` unconditionally.
- `crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/wchar_abi.rs:135-153` shows `scan_w_string(..., None)` loops until a NUL with raw pointer reads.
- Recent coverage in `crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/conformance_diff_wchar.rs:461-490` always builds `delim` via `wcstring`, so it never exercises an unterminated tracked delimiter.

Repro test shape: allocate `delim = malloc(4).cast::<u32>()`, write one comma codepoint with no trailing NUL, then call `wcstok(input, delim, &mut save)` in hardened mode. Expected: reject safely or bound the delimiter scan to `known_remaining(delim)`. Actual today: unbounded `scan_w_string(delim, None)` can read past the tracked allocation.

Fix direction: compute a delimiter bound from `known_remaining(delim as usize).map(bytes_to_wchars)`, pass it to `scan_w_string`, and treat `(len, false)` as an adverse safe failure instead of constructing an unterminated delimiter slice.
close_reason: fixed: wcstok now bounds delimiter scans with known_remaining(delim) and rejects tracked unterminated delimiters before constructing the delimiter slice; validated rustfmt --check on touched files, git diff --check, rch cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test wchar_abi_test wcstok, rch cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test conformance_diff_wchar diff_wcspbrk_wcstok_subprocess, rch cargo check -p frankenlibc-abi --all-targets, rch cargo clippy -p frankenlibc-abi --all-targets -- -D warnings, and UBS on touched wchar files

title: __libc_fatal fork tests wedge: the pre-abort flush ALLOCATES in a forked child (fixed in 1b02e1053)
description:
FIXED in 1b02e1053; filed after the fact because the fix was mistakenly attributed to bd-3aktsp, which is an unrelated memory-reading flake.

SYMPTOM. glibc_internal_abi_test came out 271 passed / 1 failed under a 54-target parallel run on a shared worker, and 272 / 0 in isolation on the identical commit. The failing arm was one of the three that fork: libc_fatal_aborts_child_with_message one run, libc_fatal_null_message_still_aborts_with_fallback the next. A different arm each time is the signature of a fork race, not a defect in any one arm.

WHY IT READ AS A FLAKE. wait_for_sigabrt_child used a 5-second wall-clock deadline, which a busy shared worker can cross innocently. Raising it to 60s and reporting which outcome actually occurred produced the diagnosis on the first run:

  child 2027520 did not raise SIGABRT within 60s (still alive: true)

Still alive after 60s is wedged, not slow.

CAUSE. fflush_managed_only_for_abort, called by abort() before it raises SIGABRT, was already careful about LOCKS — every acquisition on that path is a try_lock, precisely so abort never blocks on a lock a vanished thread holds. But it snapshotted the stream registry into a Vec so it could drop the registry lock before flushing, and that snapshot calls fl's own allocator. A child forked out of a multi-threaded process inherits the allocator's lock frozen-held if any other thread was inside malloc at fork time, and unlike the try_locks there is no fallback — it hangs forever. An abort path must be allocation-free, not merely lock-careful.

FIX. Iterate the map in place; no allocation. Holding the registry lock across the per-stream try_locks adds no deadlock because every acquisition is still a try_lock and simply skips a stream it cannot take. The three children also _exit(101) after __libc_fatal now, so a breach of the noreturn contract is reported as a breach rather than as a hang.

EVIDENCE. The 54-target parallel invocation that gave 271/1 twice now gives 272/0, and three isolated runs are 272/0 in under a second each with no stall.

FOLLOW-ON WORTH CHECKING: any other path reachable from abort() or from a post-fork child that allocates. Lock-carefulness is not enough — grep the abort and fatal paths for Vec/String/format!/to_string/collect.
close_reason: Fixed in 1b02e1053: allocation removed from the pre-abort flush; 54-target parallel run 271/1 -> 272/0, three isolated runs 272/0 sub-second

title: [RED][dark-gate] frankenlibc_conformance --lib SEGFAULTS mid-suite at clean HEAD: 129 of 173 tests report, 44 are silent, zero FAILED lines
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-15 (BlackThrush) on a CLEAN baseline, so this is not a working-tree artifact:

  RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 env -u CARGO_TARGET_DIR rch exec --base HEAD --clean-overlay --no-overlay -- cargo test -p frankenlibc_conformance --lib

on RCH worker vmi1227854 (176.5s) ends with:

  error: test failed, to rerun pass '-p frankenlibc_conformance --lib'
  Caused by: process didn't exit successfully: .../debug/deps/frankenlibc_conformance-d08b2dbbe49c0676 (signal: 11, SIGSEGV: invalid memory reference)
  WRAPEXIT=101

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN A FAILING TEST. The binary dies mid-run, so:
  - 129 of 173 tests printed a result; 44 printed NOTHING
  - 'FAILED' appears ZERO times
  - 'test result:' appears ZERO times -- there is no summary line at all
Anything that greps for FAILED, or reads a count, sees a clean run. This is the same silent-green class as bd-86hcwh (dark test targets) and the 'zero is not evidence' rule: the 44 unreported tests are not passing, they are UNRUN, and nobody can tell which 44 they are from the log alone because libtest interleaves parallel threads.

REPRODUCED TWICE in the same session, on two different code states (clean HEAD via --no-overlay, and HEAD plus an unrelated test-only overlay), so it is not intermittent-rare and not caused by the overlay.

NOT YET IDENTIFIED: which test crashes. libtest ran multi-threaded, so the last 'ok' line does not name it.

FIRST STEP, cheap and decisive: rerun with '-- --test-threads=1'. With one thread the crash point is the test AFTER the last reported 'ok', which names the culprit in one run. Then re-run that test alone under a debugger or with RUST_BACKTRACE=1 to get the frame.

CONTEXT: the fortify fixture arms intentionally abort children ('*** buffer overflow detected ***: terminated' and '*** fortify fixture ***: terminated' appear repeatedly in the log and are EXPECTED -- those are forked children exercising __chk_fail). The SIGSEGV is the PARENT test process, which is not expected. A plausible starting hypothesis is a forked-child arm returning into libtest state it must not touch, but that is a hypothesis, not evidence.

BLOCKS: bd-ry1dg5 cannot be verified on the whole-suite gate while this stands -- the whole-suite run is exactly what its flake needs, and that run currently cannot produce a summary.
close_reason: Root-caused to fcloseall unregistering the standard streams, whose sentinel ids were then passed to host stdio as FILE pointers. Fixed in ab176d5ba. Same command and worker before/after: clean HEAD 129 of 173 reported then SIGSEGV with no summary line; with the fix 'test result: ok. 173 passed; 0 failed'. 44 previously-silent tests are now green. Gated by stdio_abi_test fcloseall_keeps_the_standard_streams_registered (1 passed, vmi1227854). Class follow-on filed as bd-xmlbtg.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FIXED AND CLOSED on cited evidence: commit ab176d5ba, RCH worker vmi1227854.

ROOT CAUSE (read from source, then confirmed by a minimal reproducer). fl maps stdin/stdout/stderr to SENTINEL ids 0x1000_0001..=0x1000_0003 (stdio_abi.rs:542), and every host-delegating stdio entry point falls back to HOST stdio for any id the registry does not contain, passing that id through as if it were a FILE pointer. fcloseall iterated the registry and closed EVERY entry including the three pre-registered standard cells, so the next standard-stream call reached glibc with the address 0x1000_0002 and glibc killed the process with 'Fatal error: glibc detected an invalid stdio handle'.

MINIMAL DETERMINISTIC REPRODUCER, using the prebuilt clean-HEAD binary on vmi1227854 (sha256 c8aec4c5a48f0565cc63c56839e2d089894ef59fc7fabd1480aea36cbc4b1346, job dir de0dc5866c4e3ab1):
  wave06 ALONE                -> ok, 1 passed
  wave04 + wave06             -> ok, 2 passed
  wave02 + wave06             -> Fatal error: glibc detected an invalid stdio handle, RC=134
wave02 is the wave containing the fcloseall case. Single-threaded the process aborts (SIGABRT); multi-threaded it segfaults (SIGSEGV) -- the two different signals in the two runs on this bead are the SAME cause.

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE, confirming this bead's premise: the process dies mid-run, so libtest emits no summary and no FAILED line. At clean HEAD 129 of 173 tests reported and 44 reported NOTHING. They were not passing, they were UNRUN.

FIX: fcloseall flushes the standard streams and skips them, closing only non-standard ones. This matches the fixture's own name (fcloseall_flush_only) and matches the host -- measured on live glibc 2.42, fcloseall() returns 0 and a subsequent fflush(NULL) is still safe, so glibc leaves no dangling standard handle either.

EVIDENCE, same command, same worker, before and after:
  clean HEAD (--base HEAD --clean-overlay --no-overlay): 129 of 173 reported, then SIGSEGV, zero 'test result:' lines
  with ab176d5ba: 'test result: ok. 173 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out'
44 tests went from silent to green, and the suite exits 0.

GATE: stdio_abi_test fcloseall_keeps_the_standard_streams_registered, '1 passed' on vmi1227854. It asserts the registry invariant rather than demonstrating the crash, because a regression aborts the binary and an aborted binary reports nothing -- which is the exact failure mode this bead is about.

FOLLOW-ON FILED: bd-xmlbtg. The host-delegation guard tests registry membership, not whether the pointer is real, so any OTHER caller that unregisters a standard stream re-opens this crash elsewhere. This bead removed the one trigger; that bead is the class.

title: dlfcn: main handle sees RTLD_GLOBAL symbols
abi: efun_abi panic-on-poison Mutex sites are unsound for extern "C" callers
description:
Skill: /deadlock-finder-and-fixer audit of crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/ (77 lock-acquisition sites across 28 .rs files). The audit found 0 lock-order inversions and 0 nested-guard re-entry deadlocks (project lock discipline is sound — pthread_abi REGISTRY -> SNAPSHOTS/MTT/DTT order is consistent across native_pthread_create/join/detach/timedjoin/tryjoin paths, stdio_abi exit handlers correctly swap-extract-then-invoke under bd-3jpoz fix, iconv_abi lookup_handle drops outer lock before inner, dirent_abi closedir removes-then-locks correctly).

But it found 3 panic-on-poison Mutex sites in efun_abi.rs that are inconsistent with the project-wide `.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())` convention used in 50+ other lock sites:

  crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/efun_abi.rs:55  (report_failure)
  crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/efun_abi.rs:73  (esetfunc)
  crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/efun_abi.rs:313 (test_helpers::reset_efun)

These sit on the failure path of every NetBSD efun-family symbol (emalloc, ecalloc, erealloc, estrlcpy, estrlcat, estrdup, estrndup, efopen, estrtoi, estrtou). report_failure is invoked from extern "C" -> if EFUN_CELL is ever poisoned, .unwrap() panics, and the panic unwinds across the C ABI boundary (extern "C", not extern "C-unwind") — undefined behavior per the Rust reference.

In practice the EFUN_CELL critical section is narrow (function-pointer copy), so realistic poisoning is unlikely today. But: (a) inconsistent with project convention, (b) any future code change inside the critical section that can panic immediately turns these into latent UB, (c) the cost of fixing matches the surrounding pattern exactly.

Fix: replace the three .lock().unwrap() sites with .lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()) to match the project pattern. No semantic change for the no-poison happy path; recovers gracefully from a poisoned mutex by reading through the inner value.

Verification: cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi efun, cargo clippy -p frankenlibc-abi -- -D warnings, and the existing efun_abi test suite (estrlcpy_*, emalloc_*, esetfunc_*) covers all three sites.
notes: SwiftKnoll validation refresh after local commit f0c96a36: rustfmt --edition 2024 --check crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/efun_abi.rs passed; git diff --check on the tracker delta passed; RCH cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test efun_abi_test -- --nocapture passed 31/31; RCH cargo clippy -p frankenlibc-abi -- -D warnings passed; br dep cycles --no-db --json returned count=0. Note: the earlier broad cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi efun command exited 0 but selected zero tests, so efun_abi_test is the actual test evidence.
close_reason: Fix shipped (commit f0c96a36). Replaced three .lock().unwrap() panic-on-poison sites in efun_abi.rs (report_failure, esetfunc, test_helpers::reset_efun) with .lock().unwrap_or_else(|poison| poison.into_inner()) to match the project-wide ABI lock convention used in 50+ other sites. Tests pass (rch exec -- cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi efun, exit 0 in 45s), clippy clean (-D warnings), fmt clean. Audit summary: /deadlock-finder-and-fixer scan of all 77 lock-acquisition sites across the abi crate's 28 files found no lock-order inversions or nested-guard re-entry deadlocks — pthread_abi REGISTRY -> SNAPSHOTS/MTT/DTT order is consistent across create/join/detach/timedjoin/tryjoin paths, stdio_abi exit handlers correctly swap-extract-then-invoke (bd-3jpoz fix in place), iconv_abi/dirent_abi outer-then-inner registry locking releases outer before taking inner, termios_abi sequentially acquires FD/PTR signature locks then logs lock. These three efun_abi sites were the only convention outliers.

title: [bug][string] raw_avx_copy_backward dest-align peel corrupts overlapping memmove (two independent defects)
description:
conformance_diff_memmove was RED at HEAD and untracked. Found by the execution sweep (bd-aykfv1). memmove is a core function; this corrupts data on overlapping moves of n >= 128 on any AVX host.

SYMPTOM: fl duplicates one byte and drops the next, e.g. len=200 disp=1 produced '... 0, 31, 31, 62 ...' and '... 209, 240, 240, 46 ...' where glibc has '... 0, 31, 62 ...' and '... 209, 240, 15, 46 ...'.

TWO INDEPENDENT DEFECTS IN ONE PEEL. raw_avx_copy_backward aligns the destination END before its descending vmovdqa loop, via 'copy_unaligned_32(dst+n-32, src+n-32)', under a comment asserting it was 'ALWAYS safe for backward overlap'. It was not:

1. RANGE. The peel writes a full 32 bytes at [n-32, n), which reaches BELOW dst+l, while the descending loop afterwards still has to READ src[0, l). At len=200 disp=1 (top_head=9, l=191) the peel wrote base[233..265] and the loop then re-read base[233..255] it had just clobbered.

2. DIRECTION. copy_unaligned_32 is an ASCENDING pair of 16-byte moves (low half, then high half). In a BACKWARD context with overlap distance < 16 its first store clobbers its own second load. At len=200 disp=15 the low half stored base[247..263] and the high half then loaded base[248..264]. Fixing only (1) left this one live — the gate went from failing at disp=1 to failing at disp=15.

The forward peel (raw_avx_copy_forward) already carries a distance guard 'dst+32 <= src' for exactly this class; the backward peel had no equivalent.

FIXED at the commit citing this bead: the peel now copies EXACTLY the top top_head bytes [l, n), descending, using copy_unaligned_16 (atomic: one u128 load, then the store, so safe at any overlap distance) plus a byte tail. Nothing is written below dst+l, so the main loop's source is untouched by construction, and no ascending pair is used in a descending context. top_head < 32 so the peel is at most one 16-byte block plus a short tail, once.

AUDIT DONE: the other copy_unaligned_32 call sites (raw_avx_copy head/tail, raw_overlap_copy) are all DISJOINT-memcpy paths where ascending order is correct; raw_overlap_copy is only reached from raw_memmove_bytes when the regions are proven disjoint. The backward peel was the only ascending-pair-in-descending-context.

WHY IT SURVIVED: conformance_diff_memmove encodes the right corpus (every displacement in [-64,64] at many lengths) AND a golden digest, and it was simply never executed — 'cargo check --all-targets' compiles a test target without running it. The digest now matches again, so fl reproduces the corpus that was recorded when the code was last correct.
close_reason:
DONE at 0ad3912e3.

EVIDENCE:
  cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test conformance_diff_memmove
  test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test string_abi_test
  test result: ok. 201 passed; 0 failed; 8 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  cargo test -p frankenlibc-core --lib string::
  test result: ok. 462 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored; 0 measured; 2760 filtered out
  cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test conformance_diff_memcpy
  test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out

NO NEW GATE, AND THE EXISTING ONE IS STRONGER THAN ANY I WOULD HAVE WRITTEN: conformance_diff_memmove already sweeps every displacement in [-64,64] across 23 lengths and pins a golden digest. It was RED before this change and is green after, digest included — so fl again reproduces the corpus recorded when the code was last correct. That is the same evidence a mutation run gives, from a gate that was already there.

THE SECOND DEFECT WOULD HAVE BEEN MISSED BY A ONE-SHOT FIX. Correcting the range problem alone moved the gate from failing at disp=1 to failing at disp=15. Only re-running it exposed the direction problem. A fix validated by reasoning rather than by the gate would have shipped half of this.

FIX: the dest-END-align peel now copies EXACTLY the top top_head bytes [l, n), descending, via copy_unaligned_16 (atomic — one u128 load then the store, hence safe at any overlap distance) plus a byte tail. It writes nothing below dst+l, so the descending loop's source is untouched by construction, and no ascending pair runs in a descending context. top_head < 32, so the peel is one 16-byte block plus a short tail, executed once.

AUDIT: every other copy_unaligned_32 call site is a disjoint-memcpy path where ascending order is correct, and raw_overlap_copy is only reached from raw_memmove_bytes once the regions are proven disjoint. The backward peel was the only ascending-pair-in-descending-context in the file.

PERF NOTE, NOT MEASURED: the peel is now byte/16-wide instead of one 32-byte pair, and it no longer bails to the unaligned loop, so the aligned descending loop still runs. I did not benchmark this; the gate is a correctness gate. If someone re-tunes this path, the corpus above is the thing to keep green.

title: perf: %s newline fast-path for printf family (the canonical line-print) via bytes+trailing helper
notes:
SCOPE CAVEAT (prevents a regression): exclude UNBUFFERED writers from the %s-newline 2-part path. dprintf writes to a raw fd; emitting str then newline as two write_all_fd calls is TWO write() syscalls vs render's single write of str+newline -- net SLOWER (syscall overhead beats the saved copy). Only the BUFFERED FILE writers (printf/fprintf, which append to the stream buffer, no per-write syscall) should take the 2-part fast path; dprintf/vdprintf keep rendering. So the lever is: buffered FILE writers get zero-copy 2-part (write str-buf + newline-byte to the buffer); bounded buffer writers (snprintf) get the gated trailing-newline truncation; unbuffered/raw-fd writers keep rendering. Plus the earlier note: build-str-newline-into-pool gives zero savings (only zero-copy wins).

IMPLEMENTATION cod-b/DarkRiver: code-first lever landed in crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/stdio_abi.rs. Exact non-NULL "%s\n" now classifies as a direct string payload with trailing newline. snprintf/sprintf/vsnprintf/vsprintf copy string bytes directly and append the newline only within the existing truncation boundary. fprintf/printf/vfprintf/vprintf use a split two-slice path only for managed memory-backed streams or fully buffered streams with enough remaining capacity; line-buffered, unbuffered, raw-fd, host-delegated, and capacity-overflow cases render the original single buffer. dprintf/vdprintf intentionally unchanged. Added guard tests printf_direct_payload_classifies_string_newline_only_for_nonnull_s, printf_direct_payload_copy_preserves_snprintf_truncation_boundary, and printf_direct_newline_stream_only_absorbs_full_buffered_without_flush. Added Criterion target stdio_glibc_baseline_snprintf_s_newline in crates/frankenlibc-bench/benches/stdio_glibc_baseline_bench.rs. Artifact tests/artifacts/perf/bd-0m5vaw-printf-s-newline-fastpath.md records the negative-evidence ledger and pending keep/reject predicate. Validation run now: AGENT_NAME=DarkRiver CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/projects/.rch-targets/frankenlibc-cod-b cargo check -p frankenlibc-abi passed; AGENT_NAME=DarkRiver CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/projects/.rch-targets/frankenlibc-cod-b cargo check -p frankenlibc-bench --features abi-bench --bench stdio_glibc_baseline_bench passed. Existing unrelated iconv/ABI warning debt remains. No tests/rch/Criterion run per campaign instruction; status intentionally remains in_progress for batch timing/conformance verdict.

title: [perf][resolv] resolve_hosts_subset / gethostbyname hosts path: check for per-call hosts-backend clone + re-parse (other half of getaddrinfo's residual 9.5us)
close_reason:
SHIPPED. read_hosts_backend() returned an owned clone of the whole /etc/hosts, and core lookup_hosts ran parse_hosts_line on EVERY line (owned address Vec + Vec<Vec<u8>> hostnames), cloning each match into a result Vec<Vec<u8>>. Three call sites paid it per call: resolve_hosts_subset, lookup_hosts_ipv4_by_name, and getaddrinfo's /etc/hosts node branch (the other half of that row's residual 9.5us). Same defect as the services scan, one file over.

LEVER: new allocation-free core scanner frankenlibc_core::resolv::for_each_hosts_match(content, name, visit) - same comment stripping, field separators, "non-empty hostname list AND valid IPv4/IPv6 address" acceptance test, file order, at most one match per line; address slice aliases content. New with_hosts_backend_snapshot in resolv_abi mirrors the services/protocols borrowing accessors. All three sites converted. getaddrinfo still visits EVERY match (visit always returns false), exactly as the old loop; the two helpers stop at the first parseable address. Backend-error behaviour preserved.

SUBSTRATE v2: measured with a TRULY INTERLEAVED PAIRED SAMPLER, not criterion arms. Criterion runs group members sequentially, so side-by-side ORIG/CAND does NOT cancel drift. New harness crates/frankenlibc-bench/examples/hosts_lookup_ab.rs alternates ORIG and CAND within one measured routine, one call of each per paired sample, order swapped every sample; host glibc via dlmopen is a third interleaved arm. Every input through black_box, every result consumed through black_box. verify() asserts fl == host glibc on address AND canonical name before any timing, so a DCE'd arm cannot pass.

MEASURED (one binary, one rch exec invocation, hz2; 1900 paired samples, 20 reps/arm):
  orig(clone+parse)  median 6845.52 ns/call  cv 14.43%
  cand(borrow+scan)  median 3269.75 ns/call  cv 22.16%
  host glibc         median 9159.02 ns/call  cv  8.45%
PAIRED cand/orig median 0.4799 => 2.08x faster (drift-cancelled; paired-ratio cv 20.94%).
cand/glibc = 0.357x => 2.80x faster than host glibc.
ORIG is reconstructed in-process (runs the removed clone+parse, then the deployed call), so it overstates ORIG and 2.08x is an UNDER-estimate.

CORRECTION to my earlier ratios (substrate v2 defect 1): bd-qds9jk 3.00x, bd-xmng5n 2.24x, bd-77h82y 1.93-1.99x, bd-nyrnnq 31.3x all used sequential criterion group members - worker identity cancels, inter-arm drift does not. I had flagged this in bd-77h82y and bounded it by pass replication. Weakness, not invalidation: 31.3x and 3.00x are far outside plausible drift; 1.93x/2.24x are the ones a paired sampler should re-check. Defect 2 (black_box/DCE) does not apply: each ORIG arm produced a large distinct delta, which is positive execution proof.

CONFORMANCE (all remote, verified [RCH] remote markers): frankenlibc-core resolv unit tests 270 passed / 0 failed (the new scanner lives there); conformance_diff_getaddrinfo 7/0 (byte-exact vs live glibc for the converted node branch); resolv_abi_test 182/0/31; inet_abi_test 69/0/13; conformance_diff_netdb_aliases 1/1; conformance_diff_netdb_r_aliases 1/1. ubs exit 0. rustfmt clean.

RCH DISCIPLINE: rch exec defaults to Strict remote OFF and will build LOCALLY when it cannot reserve a slot. Mandatory form: RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 env -u CARGO_TARGET_DIR rch exec -- cargo <sub> ... Verify each run prints [RCH] remote <worker>. All four invocations here did (hz2, hz2, vmi1152480, vmi1152480).

STILL BLOCKED (bd-3dxo1a): per-arm self-time needs perf, hence a local release-perf debuginfo build, forbidden by the disk constraint. Execution proven instead by the byte-identity verify() and the 2.08x paired delta. No self-time numbers were invented.

Ledgered: docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md 2026-07-10 (cc_fl). NEXT: five remaining read_hosts_backend() sites; cross-family NSS caching (blocked on a fresh frame table); fair getaddrinfo host baseline (bd-ynaqwe).

title: error_at_line with NULL file_name omits the space separator (glibc prints 'progname: msg')
description:
MEASURED on live glibc 2.42 (compiled C probe, /data/tmp/.../p2.c, output via cat -A):

  error_at_line(0,0,"f.c",7,"with file")  -> 'PROG:f.c:7: with file'
  error_at_line(0,0,NULL, 7,"null file")  -> 'PROG: null file'      <- colon THEN SPACE
  error_at_line(0,0,"",   7,"empty file") -> 'PROG::7: empty file'  <- empty name still prints ':7: '

glibc emits the progname as '%s:' and then, when file_name is NULL, a single space instead of the
'%s:%d: ' file/line group. fl writes the 'PROG:' prefix and then nothing at all for NULL, so it
produces 'PROG:null file' -- missing the space. The empty-string case is already correct in fl.

FOUND by the bd-enxo3y error_one_per_line gate: its NULL-filename suppression steps are the first
arms in the repo to call error_at_line with file_name == NULL, and they failed on this instead of on
suppression. Observed diff:
  fl    = 'PROG:boom\n'
  glibc = 'PROG: boom\n'

Also applies with error_print_progname installed: glibc calls the hook in place of 'PROG:' and still
emits the space, so the fix must not be conditional on the hook.

DONE = error_at_line_honors_error_one_per_line_like_glibc and
error_at_line_repeats_when_error_one_per_line_is_clear (crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/conformance_diff_error_at_line.rs)
go green on their NULL steps, plus an arm pinning the three shapes above (non-NULL, NULL, empty)
against live glibc.
close_reason:
FIXED + GATED. Commit 757ad815a.

error_at_line now emits a single space in place of the '%s:%d: ' file/line group when file_name is NULL, so a NULL name yields 'progname: message' like glibc instead of 'progname:message'.

GROUND TRUTH (measured, not recalled) on live glibc 2.42 via a compiled C probe, read with cat -A:
  error_at_line(0,0,"f.c",7,"with file")  -> 'PROG:f.c:7: with file'
  error_at_line(0,0,NULL, 7,"null file")  -> 'PROG: null file'
  error_at_line(0,0,"",   7,"empty file") -> 'PROG::7: empty file'
So an empty-but-non-NULL name is a DIFFERENT case and was already correct in fl: it still prints the group, as ':<line>: '. Only NULL was wrong.

IMPLEMENTATION (crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/stdlib_abi.rs::error_at_line): the existing 'if !filename.is_null() && readable && utf8' block gains an else that writes a single space. Emitted regardless of error_print_progname, which replaces only the 'progname:' part -- so a hook plus a NULL filename is also correct now. The else additionally covers a non-NULL filename the membrane cannot read to a NUL: glibc would have dereferenced it, and the no-file rendering is the closest safe answer.

GATE: error_at_line_null_filename_keeps_the_space_separator compares all three shapes above against live glibc, then names the distinction directly -- NULL output must end ': msg\n' and must NOT end ':msg\n' (the pre-fix shape, which an over-eager fix dropping the group entirely would also produce), while the empty-name output must end '::7: msg\n'. The bd-enxo3y one-per-line arms cover it too; both were RED before this fix and are green after.

EVIDENCE (rch remote, worker vmi1227854, source commit 757ad815a):
  cargo test -j2 -p frankenlibc-abi --test conformance_diff_error_at_line -> 9 passed; 0 failed
  cargo clippy -j2 -p frankenlibc-abi --lib --test conformance_diff_error_at_line -- -D warnings -> zero findings on touched files

FOUND BY: the bd-enxo3y gate's NULL suppression steps. Reported as a measured diff (fl='PROG:boom\n' vs glibc='PROG: boom\n') before any code changed.

title: Refine hostile-image safety with resource caps and containment proofs
description:
Supplemental refinement for bd-rchk0.5.11. The adversarial threat model lists malformed images and resource-exhaustion corpus cases, but implementation needs a concrete containment proof so hostile images cannot consume unbounded CPU, memory, disk, file descriptors, mount time, or proof-artifact space while still producing a misleading readiness result.

Scope: define hostile-image resource budgets and containment behavior for ext4/btrfs parsing, mount preflight, repair-ledger ingestion, proof-bundle validation, and operator commands. The expected safe behavior should be deterministic: reject, quarantine, cap, downgrade, or require long-campaign handling with an owning bead.

Required proof before close:
1. Unit/schema tests reject threat cases missing resource class, limit value/unit, enforcement point, expected classification, cleanup policy, remediation id, and release-gate effect.
2. Unit tests cover oversized metadata, cyclic metadata references, deeply nested directories, huge xattr payloads, truncated/corrupt repair ledgers, path traversal artifacts, symlinked proof paths, excessive log output, excessive artifact count, timeout, and file-descriptor exhaustion fixtures.
3. E2E/security smoke runs bounded hostile fixtures and proves every case exits with reject/quarantine/cap/unsupported classification rather than success, hang, host mutation, or unstructured panic.
4. Logs include threat scenario id, input hash, resource limits, observed CPU/time/memory/disk counters where available, enforcement point, classification, cleanup status, artifact paths, remediation id, and reproduction command.
5. Release gates and README safety wording cannot mark hostile-image handling as stronger than experimental unless these containment artifacts are fresh and every critical threat class has an explicit pass, cap, quarantine, unsupported, or follow-up result.
close_reason: Implemented hostile-image containment resource controls, observed counters, bounded fixture matrix, negative validation cases, E2E smoke, docs, and release-gate-safe wording.

title: Refine proof overhead budgets with retention and reproduction-preserving compression
description:
Supplemental refinement for bd-rchk0.5.14. Budgeting proof overhead is not just about runtime and artifact size; the project also needs a retention and compression policy that keeps reproduction-critical evidence while preventing proof runs from filling disks, hiding failures, or leaking unnecessary host details.

Scope: define retention tiers for developer smoke, CI required, nightly/stress, permissioned mount, and release-readiness profiles. Specify which logs/artifacts are mandatory, which may be compressed, which may be sampled, which may be redacted, and which must never be dropped before validator and remediation consumers finish.

Required proof before close:
1. Unit/schema tests reject retention policies missing profile, artifact class, retention duration/count, compression setting, redaction policy, mandatory fields, reproduction command preservation, maximum size, and exception expiry.
2. Unit tests cover pass, warn, fail, over-budget, missing mandatory log, compression success, compression corruption, redaction mismatch, stale exception, cleanup failure, and reproduction-command loss cases.
3. E2E smoke generates fixture proof artifacts, applies retention/compression/redaction policy, validates the resulting bundle offline, and proves mandatory reproduction fields and raw failure diagnostics remain accessible.
4. Logs include budget profile, artifact class, original size, compressed size, retention decision, redaction policy version, dropped/sampled field list, exception id, validator result, cleanup status, and reproduction command.
5. Release gates cannot accept a proof bundle whose retention or compression policy removed fields required by remediation, cross-lane correlation, tamper validation, or reproduction.
close_reason: Implemented proof overhead retention/compression/redaction policy with class-specific gates, reproduction-preserving artifact validation, E2E smoke, and docs.

title: printf '*' negative width/precision: neg width should left-justify, neg precision should be ignored
description: In crates/frankenlibc-core/src/stdio/printf.rs, when width comes from '*' argument (Width::FromArg), a negative integer argument is not translated into '-' flag + abs(width) as C11 7.21.6.1 para 5 requires. Surfaced by bd-12hh printf_conformance matrix (sprintf_star_neg_width case: format='%*d', args=[-5, 42] — expected '42   ', got 2000+ spaces). resolve_width() also returns 0 for FromArg which means it never reads the * argument at all; the two bugs compound.
close_reason: extract_va_args! now reads '*' width/precision as c_int (with sign-extension to u64), so render_printf's existing negative-value handling at lines 3139-3163 is reached. sprintf_star_neg_width and sprintf_star_neg_precision now pass end-to-end. Committed 717fae6.

title: fuzz: cargo +nightly fuzz run fails to link with libc.map version script
description: All fuzz_targets in crates/frankenlibc-fuzz fail at link time when invoked via 'cargo +nightly fuzz run'. The frankenlibc-abi cdylib is built with version_scripts/libc.map listing many GLIBC_2.2.5 symbols (memcpy, __errno_location, __libc_start_main, etc) that aren't defined in the fuzz build because the abi is being linked into a libfuzzer dylib rather than the final libc.so. cargo build (no fuzz flags) succeeds — only the cargo-fuzz wrapper that injects -Cpasses=sancov-module + -Zsanitizer=address triggers the linker error. Likely fix: gate the version_scripts via a cfg(not(fuzzing)) in build.rs or expose a fuzz-friendly cargo feature that omits the script. Reproduce: 'cargo +nightly fuzz run --fuzz-dir crates/frankenlibc-fuzz fuzz_dirent -- -max_total_time=5'.
close_reason: build.rs now skips applying libc.map version script when CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS contains '--cfg=fuzzing'. cargo +nightly fuzz run links cleanly and finds real bugs (proven by bd-m40be). Committed 3b74c87.

title: PORT: __pthread_create / __pthread_join / __pthread_detach / __pthread_exit (glibc reserved aliases)
description: Port the four glibc reserved-namespace aliases for the pthread thread-lifecycle entry points: __pthread_create, __pthread_join, __pthread_detach, __pthread_exit. glibc emits these underscored variants both as internal-use entry points and as the symbols libstdc++ links against for std::thread / std::async machinery. Without them callers see undefined-reference errors when linking libstdc++-using code statically. Implementation: thin no_mangle Rust extern "C" wrappers that delegate to the public pthread_create/join/detach/exit in pthread_abi. Tests verify each alias produces the same observable thread lifecycle as its public counterpart on a worker that returns a sentinel value.

title: REVIEW: [HIGH] getrlimit/setrlimit reject 9 standard Linux RLIMIT_* values
description:
FOUND + FIXED via differential harness vs glibc (commit 6c5c98ac).

frankenlibc_core::resource::valid_resource enumerated only a sparse subset of rlimit identifiers (CPU/FSIZE/DATA/STACK/CORE/NOFILE/AS), causing getrlimit and setrlimit to return EINVAL for RLIMIT_RSS, RLIMIT_NPROC, RLIMIT_MEMLOCK, RLIMIT_LOCKS, RLIMIT_SIGPENDING, RLIMIT_MSGQUEUE, RLIMIT_NICE, RLIMIT_RTPRIO, and RLIMIT_RTTIME — all 9 valid Linux rlimits.

Reachability: any program that queries per-user process limits, queued-signal budget, mlock allowance, file-locks limit, message-queue size, nice ceiling, or RT scheduling limits would get EINVAL where they expected a real kernel value. ulimit shell builtin, container runtimes, JVM init, etc.

Fix: replace sparse `matches!` allowlist with contiguous range check (RLIMIT_CPU..=RLIMIT_RTTIME). Add the 9 missing constants. Update unit test to cover all 11 standard rlimits.

Severity: HIGH — silent EINVAL on valid kernel resources.
close_reason: Shipped in commits 12cbadb0 / 6c5c98ac.

title: [bug][search] tdelete of a MISSING key drops nodes — LLRB delete run without its existence precondition
description:
conformance_diff_tsearch was RED at HEAD (found by the sweep, bd-aykfv1), AND so was core's own unit test missing_deletes_preserve_set_and_llrb_invariants. Neither was being run.

SYMPTOM: fl's in-order walk silently loses a contiguous band of keys. Random trial 3 of the tsearch corpus:
  fl:    [... 83, 86, 137, 138 ...]
  glibc: [... 83, 86, 87, 89, 103, 111, 123, 137, 138 ...]
Five keys gone. tfind then reports them absent, so a caller sees data it inserted simply vanish.

CAUSE: RbTree::delete ran Sedgewick's LLRB delete_rec for keys that are NOT in the tree. That algorithm's stated precondition is that the key EXISTS — the descent applies move_red_left/move_red_right unconditionally to manufacture a red node to remove, and the step 'if needle == h.key && h.right.is_none() { return None }' discards a whole node. Driven at an absent key those steps restructure a tree that had nothing to remove and drop subtrees. tdelete on a missing key is an ordinary documented no-op, so any normal caller reaches this.

Note the return value was ALREADY correct (None) while nodes vanished underneath it — a test asserting only the return value passes while the tree is being corrupted. The existing core arm did assert the full walk, which is why it caught it once anyone ran it.

FIXED at the commit citing this bead: RbTree::delete does a find() membership pre-check and returns None without touching the tree when the key is absent. The pre-check is a correctness requirement, not an optimisation, and is documented as such at the call site.

MUTATION-VERIFIED: removing the guard fails BOTH the new post-deletion arm and the pre-existing insert-only arm; restoring it turns both green, along with conformance_diff_tsearch's 400 random trials.

WIDENS bd-aykfv1: that sweep executed abi conformance_diff_* binaries only. This bug was ALSO caught by a frankenlibc-core unit test that was equally unrun, so the 'red gates nobody executes' problem is not confined to the abi conformance targets. A core-side sweep (cargo test -p frankenlibc-core --lib) should be run and triaged the same way.
close_reason:
DONE at a35732373.

EVIDENCE:
  cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test conformance_diff_tsearch
  test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  cargo test -p frankenlibc-core --lib search::
  test result: ok. 31 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored; 0 measured; 3192 filtered out
  cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test search_abi_test
  test result: ok. 38 passed; 0 failed; 5 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out

FIX: RbTree::delete does a find() membership pre-check and returns None without touching the tree when the key is absent. Sedgewick's LLRB deletion has an existence PRECONDITION; the pre-check is what enforces it, so it is a correctness requirement rather than an optimisation, and is documented as such at the call site so nobody removes it as dead work.

MUTATION-VERIFIED: removing the guard fails both the new post-deletion arm and the pre-existing insert-only arm; restoring it turns both green along with the tsearch corpus (400 random trials + curated cases).

A CORRECTION I HAD TO MAKE MID-TASK. I first wrote in the new test's doc comment that the pre-existing arm missing_deletes_preserve_set_and_llrb_invariants 'passed throughout', to justify the new arm as non-duplicate. The mutation run refuted that: without the guard BOTH fail. I had assumed it passed without running it — the same mistake this whole vein is about. The comment now states the real relationship: the pre-existing arm covers insert-only trees, the new one covers post-deletion shapes, and both were red.

NEW COVERAGE: the added arm interleaves real deletions first, then probes absent keys at every gap, asserting the in-order walk, len, the LLRB structural invariants and subsequent find() — not just the return value. That last point matters: tdelete ALREADY returned the correct None while nodes vanished underneath it, so any arm checking only the return value passes while the tree is being corrupted.

WIDENS bd-aykfv1. That sweep executed abi conformance_diff_* binaries only. This defect was also caught by a frankenlibc-core unit test that was equally unrun, so 'red gates nobody executes' is not confined to the abi conformance targets. A core-side sweep (cargo test -p frankenlibc-core --lib) should be run and triaged the same way; I have added that to bd-aykfv1's scope note rather than opening a third bead.

FROM the red sweep: cfbaud (bd-lmhxt4), memmove (bd-0lqilq) and tsearch are fixed; 25 abi rows remain.

THE RULE, MEASURED. The bead title says glibc 'leaves them empty when 0'. It does not — it drops uid and gid for every NIS ('+'/'-') entry regardless of value, because its NIS branch is one fprintf with no number in it. Live host:
  +user uid=0 gid=0 -> "+user:x:::::"      +user uid=5 gid=0 -> "+user:x:::::"
  +user uid=5 gid=7 -> "+user:x:::g:d:s"   root  uid=0 gid=0 -> "root:x:0:0:root:/root:/bin/sh"
  +grp  gid=0 -> "+grp:x::"                +grp  gid=9 -> "+grp:x::"
  -grp  gid=0 members=[alice,bob] -> "-grp:x::alice,bob"
The ordinary-entry rows matter: uid 0 IS written there, so the elision keys on the NIS prefix alone, not on the value. NIS group member lists are still written.

FIX: 'if !(nis && v == 0)' -> 'if !nis' in format_passwd_line and format_group_line, with the measured table recorded in both comments.

NO SEPARATE MUTATION TEST NEEDED: the pre-existing +keep rows ARE the mutation. They failed before the change and pass after it, which is the same evidence a mutation run produces. The case tables additionally gain the rows that discriminate: ordinary-with-0 (must KEEP the number), NIS with both fields non-zero, and the '-' mirrors.

WHY IT WENT UNNOTICED: a red test target is only evidence if someone runs it. 'cargo check --all-targets' compiles this target but never executes it, so the repo's usual baseline check could not have surfaced this.

OBSERVATION, NOT ATTRIBUTED: one run of glibc_internal_abi_test showed '271 passed; 1 failed' while three test binaries ran concurrently; 4/4 green when run alone afterwards, and the failing arm name was not captured. Consistent with this binary's known load-sensitivity (bd-d3tvn3 family), and my change touches only pwd/grp line formatting, but I did not prove that, so it is recorded rather than dismissed. (mirror of bd-nuuk1l; same commit fixes format_group_line)

title: fix(stdlib): system() must ignore SIGINT/SIGQUIT and block SIGCHLD during the command (POSIX)
description: system() forked /bin/sh and waited without the POSIX-mandated signal handling: it must ignore SIGINT and SIGQUIT in the calling process and block SIGCHLD for the duration of the command, restoring all three afterward (glibc via posix_spawn SETSIGDEF/SETSIGMASK). Without it (1) a SIGINT raised while system() runs wrongly fires the caller's handler, and (2) a caller's SIGCHLD handler can reap the command's child, making system()'s wait4 fail with ECHILD. Verified deterministically: a command 'kill -INT $PPID; exit 7' signals the parent; glibc keeps the caller's SIGINT handler from firing, fl did not. Fixed: ignore SIGINT/SIGQUIT + block SIGCHLD in parent before fork (kernel rt_sigaction/rt_sigprocmask, saving prior dispositions), reset to SIG_DFL + restore mask in child before exec, restore in parent on all return paths. Gate conformance_diff_system_signals.
close_reason: Shipped: system() now ignores SIGINT/SIGQUIT + blocks SIGCHLD (parent), resets to DFL + restores mask (child), restores on all paths; gate conformance_diff_system_signals.

title: Refine repair corpus with ledger chain-of-custody and wrong-image proofs
description:
Supplemental refinement for bd-rchk7.2. Repair and ledger corruption fixtures must prove not only decoder success/failure but also ledger chain-of-custody: symbols, manifests, image hashes, and verification rows must belong to the image under repair. Otherwise a stale or wrong-image ledger can produce convincing but unsafe repair evidence.

Scope: add corpus requirements for ledger identity, symbol generation, image hash binding, wrong-image rejection, stale-ledger rejection, partial-write handling, tamper evidence, and post-repair symbol refresh. The corpus should include positive recovery cases and negative cases where refusal is the correct result.

Required proof before close:
1. Unit/schema tests reject corpus rows missing original image hash, corrupted image hash or corruption manifest hash, ledger id, symbol generation, repair-symbol budget, expected recoverability, verification expectation, and chain-of-custody fields.
2. Unit tests cover valid ledger, wrong-image ledger, stale ledger, truncated ledger, tampered ledger row, duplicate ledger row, insufficient symbols, excessive symbols from unrelated image, partial ledger write, and post-repair symbol refresh mismatch.
3. Harness/E2E smoke runs a bounded subset and emits per-case artifacts with expected outcome, observed outcome, refusal reason, ledger row ids, image hashes, and reproduction command.
4. Logs include corpus id, seed, original/corrupted/repaired image hashes, ledger id, symbol generation, decoder parameters, expected classification, observed classification, cleanup status, artifact paths, and reproduction command.
5. Automatic repair, remediation, and release-gate beads cannot use repair corpus evidence unless wrong-image and stale-ledger refusal cases are present and passing.

title: efun_abi.rs inline #[cfg(test)] tests never compile (module is #[cfg(not(test))] in lib.rs)
description:
crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/lib.rs declares most ABI modules as `#[cfg(not(test))] pub mod <name>;`, which excludes them from the lib's own unit-test build. Any inline `#[cfg(test)]` module inside such a file is therefore never compiled and its tests silently never run -- they do not appear in `cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --lib -- --list` and nothing reports them as skipped.

FOUND while fixing bd-ul4pyl: I added an inline unit test to err_abi.rs, it produced 201 lib tests with none matching the filter, and the cause was the cfg gate. err_abi.rs now carries a comment recording this, and that bead's coverage moved to an integration test.

crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/efun_abi.rs:318 has an inline `#[cfg(test)]` block under the same gate, so those assertions are dead code that has never executed. Anything they were meant to protect is currently ungated.

DONE = either (a) the efun_abi inline tests are moved to crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/ so they actually run and are shown passing, or (b) evidence that they are redundant with existing integration coverage, cited test-by-test. Sweep the other #[cfg(not(test))] modules for the same pattern while there -- rg '^#\[cfg\(test\)\]' across crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/ cross-referenced against the module list in lib.rs.

A regression guard is worth considering: a test that asserts no file declared #[cfg(not(test))] in lib.rs contains a #[cfg(test)] module.
close_reason:
FIXED. Source commit 57c688178. Follow-on debt filed as bd-xh08pf.

THE NAMED TARGET, resolved as the bead's option (b) with the evidence it asked for.
efun_abi.rs:318 held `#[cfg(test)] pub(crate) mod test_helpers`. The bead calls these "assertions
[that] are dead code that has never executed"; the first half is right and the second is more
absolute than the bead put it — the block contained ZERO #[test] functions. It was a single
`reset_efun()` helper whose doc comment claimed it was "exposed for the integration tests", which
its own gate makes impossible: efun_abi is `#[cfg(not(test))] pub mod efun_abi;` (lib.rs:110-111),
so in the lib test build the module does not exist, and in every other build `cfg(test)` is false.
The two cfgs are mutually exclusive, so the block compiled in NEITHER configuration, and integration
tests — which link the non-test build — could never have reached it.

REDUNDANCY EVIDENCE, cited as required: crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/efun_abi_test.rs already
achieves exactly what the helper was for. It serialises access to the global callback with its own
EFUN_TEST_LOCK and resets state per test, across 31 tests:
  cargo test -j 2 -p frankenlibc-abi --test efun_abi_test
  -> ok. 31 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
So nothing was lost by removing the block. It is replaced by a comment recording the trap and
pointing at the ratchet, rather than deleted silently.

THE SWEEP the bead also asked for. 11 gated modules still carry a REAL dead inline block, stranding
54 #[test] functions that have never executed:
  fenv_abi 11, pthread_abi 6, stdio_abi 6, iconv_abi 6, termios_abi 6, c11threads_abi 5,
  io_internal_abi 5, glibc_internal_abi 4, grp_abi 2, wchar_abi 2, unistd_abi 1
Filed as bd-xh08pf with the per-module counts, the reason it is not mechanical (these blocks reach
module-private items, so each needs a reachable surface or per-test redundancy evidence), and a
suggested order.

A CORRECTION TO MY OWN SWEEP, worth recording because it repeats a defect I fixed earlier this
session. My first pass reported 13 modules including err_abi and malloc_abi. Both were FALSE: their
only occurrences of the attribute are inside COMMENTS — err_abi's comment documents this very trap,
added under bd-ul4pyl. I had scanned raw text, which is precisely the comment-blindness the
support-matrix scanner had in bd-4habm0. The ratchet's own "a listed module that is now clean must
be removed from the list" arm caught it on the first run and forced the correction. The real figure
is 11 modules / 54 tests.

DURABLE PART — crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/no_dead_inline_tests.rs, so this class cannot regrow:
  - no module outside KNOWN_DEAD_INLINE_TESTS may gain the pattern; the failure message names the
    module and the number of #[test] fns it would strand;
  - a listed module that gets cleaned up must be REMOVED from the list, so the list tightens and
    cannot become a permanent excuse (this is the arm that caught my miscount);
  - the list must describe reality — every entry exists and is still gated;
  - efun_abi.rs specifically must stay clean;
  - and the lib.rs parse must find >20 gated modules, so a parser regression cannot silently make
    the whole ratchet vacuous — the bd-1l9rlp lesson applied to my own gate.
It is comment-blind for the reason above.
  cargo test -j 2 -p frankenlibc-abi --test no_dead_inline_tests
  -> ok. 3 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out

title: [perf][time] Measure the %Z-guarded tm_zone copy (shipped 8e8bc628a, behavior-green, perf UNMEASURED)
description:

WHAT SHIPPED. read_tm_zone fills bd.zone ([u8; 16]) with a 15-iteration byte copy from the caller's
tm_zone on EVERY %-containing strftime call. bd.zone is consumed by exactly one directive, %Z (core

title: RaptorQ Runtime: Pattern extraction from FrankenSQLite spec (systematic+repair+proof+tuning)
description:
Extract and restate the RaptorQ design pattern from FrankenSQLite in a runtime_math-compatible form.

Key spec concepts to port (pattern-level):
- Systematic fast path: read/store source symbols without GF(256) solve.
- Deterministic repair symbol generation from (ObjectId/epoch seed, K, symbol_size).
- Two overheads: additive decode slack + multiplicative loss budget.
- Optional adaptive overhead tuning using anytime-valid evidence (e-process) + evidence ledger.
- Explainable decode proofs on failure.

Deliverable:
- A short, self-contained design note (in bead comment) that future work can implement without re-reading the FrankenSQLite spec.
design: Design note captured in-repo: crates/glibc-rs-membrane/src/runtime_math/raptorq_pattern_frankensqlite.md (systematic+repair symbols, deterministic repair schedule, overhead formula, anytime-valid tuning hook, decode proofs; strict/hardened constraints).

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## Design Note: RaptorQ Pattern (FrankenSQLite) Restated for glibc_rust Runtime

### Why We Want This In libc
We already have runtime_math controllers that make membrane decisions (Allow / FullValidate / Repair / Deny). When something bad happens we want an *audit-grade* trail that survives partial loss (ring-buffer overwrites, sampling, crashes, dropped events) and remains explainable.

RaptorQ's key “alien artifact” idea is **appendable redundancy**:
- emit cheap *systematic* symbols first (fast path)
- optionally emit deterministic *repair* symbols later (background cadence)
- decode and generate proofs offline (harness/tooling), not on the hot path

### Constraints (glibc_rust-specific)
- No `/dp/asupersync` runtime dependency. Runtime may implement a tiny encoder itself.
- Strict mode must not pay codec costs on the hot path.
- Hardened mode may pay bounded overhead but must remain deterministic and measurable.

### Portable Pattern (What We Copy)
1. **Source block / epoching**
   - Group a bounded window of evidence events into an *epoch*.
   - Epoch defines: `K_source` (number of systematic records), `T` (record/symbol size), and seed.
2. **Systematic fast path**
   - Emit/store raw evidence records as systematic symbols `ESI = 0..K_source-1`.
   - Layout should favor sequential capture/export (contiguous run) to minimize read overhead in tooling.
3. **Deterministic repair generation**
   - Generate repair symbols `ESI = K_source..K_source+R-1` deterministically from `(epoch_id, K_source, T, policy)`.
   - Determinism is the superpower: tooling can reproduce encoding schedule and validate.
4. **Overhead = additive slack + multiplicative budget**
   - Keep an additive decode slack `slack_decode` (FrankenSQLite V1 uses `+2`).
   - Add multiplicative overhead `overhead_percent` as needed.
5. **Anytime-valid tuning**
   - Use an anytime-valid monitor (e-process) to decide when to raise redundancy.
   - Record changes in an evidence ledger.
6. **Decode proofs**
   - When tooling decodes/repairs, it emits a proof artifact describing which symbols were used and why the decode is trusted.

### Concrete Formulas (From FrankenSQLite Spec Excerpts)
These are the “load-bearing” knobs we can reuse verbatim:

- Additive slack:
  - `slack_decode = 2` (default)

- Repair symbol count selection:
  - `R = max(slack_decode, ceil(K_source * overhead_percent / 100))`

- Back-of-envelope loss fraction tolerated (engineering approximation):
  - `loss_fraction_max ≈ max(0, (R - slack_decode) / (K_source + R))`

### Deterministic Seed Derivation (Portable Rule)
FrankenSQLite uses a deterministic seed derived from a stable identifier (e.g., changeset id):
- `seed = xxh3_64(id_bytes)`

glibc_rust mapping recommendation:
- Define an `epoch_id` that is stable within-process (and includes a monotonic counter).
- Derive seed from `(epoch_id || build_id || mode)` to avoid collisions across runs.

### Record/Envelope Mapping (What We Emit)
FrankenSQLite’s SymbolRecord idea maps cleanly to libc evidence:

- **EvidenceSymbolRecord** (proposal)
  - Header: `{ magic, version, epoch_id, seqno, family, mode, action, flags }`
  - Coding: `{ esi, k_source, r_repair, symbol_size_T, seed }`
  - Integrity: `{ payload_hash (xxh3_128 or blake3), prev_hash (hash-chain) }`
  - Payload: fixed-size `T` bytes (small; e.g., 64–256B), or padded.

Notes:
- “Auth tags” are optional: for libc evidence we may just do hash-chains + optional MAC in tooling.
- Source symbols should be cheap to write (memcpy into ring buffer + atomic seqno).
- Repair symbols should be generated on cadence (every N decisions, timer tick, or on exit).

### Where Decode Happens
- Runtime: encode only (systematic always; repair optional).
- Harness/tooling: decode, verify hashes/chain, emit DecodeProof.

### Open Design Choice (Explicit)
We must choose whether runtime implements:
- a small XOR-only fountain (LT-like) code (fastest, simplest), or
- a tighter RaptorQ-compatible schedule (harder), or
- “RaptorQ-inspired” parity that tooling decodes with a matching decoder.

This is decided in `bd-3a9`.

### Acceptance Criteria For The Pattern Extraction
- A concrete mapping of the above into glibc_rust terms (epoch, record format, seed, R selection).
- Explicit non-goals: no GF(256) Gaussian solve on hot path; no asupersync runtime dep.
- A minimal test matrix for future implementation:
  - drop/bitflip simulation
  - deterministic reproduction
  - decode-proof verification

title: [perf][iconv] direct-first DBCS UTF-16 scalar dispatch
description: Fresh structural iconv lever. Profile/attribution: retained big5hkscs_to_utf16 workload contains 512 normal A4..F9 DBCS cells; the 4 combining exceptions are 88xx, so current multi.iter().find performs 2,048 guaranteed failed key comparisons per conversion before the O(1) direct lookup. Rewrite: probe the direct table first and consult the multi exception list only on direct's zero sentinel. EV=(impact 3 * confidence 5)/effort 2 = 7.5. Proof obligations: direct and multi key domains disjoint; preserve invalid/incomplete/E2BIG accounting; exhaustive Big5-HKSCS and SJISX0213 glibc differential coverage. Gate: one foreground remote-only --profile release big5hkscs_to_utf16 bench; keep only on a clear same-binary win, otherwise revert source and ledger the reject.
close_reason: SHIPPED: direct-first scalar lookup removes 2,048 guaranteed failed multi-exception comparisons from the 512-cell Big5-HKSCS UTF-16 workload; one remote ordinary-release gate improved the retained fl/glibc ratio 2.61x -> 2.204x and exhaustive Big5-HKSCS + SHIFT_JISX0213 differential tests passed 6/6.

title: EPIC: Killer Demo - Memory Safety Membrane Showcase
description:
Build a compelling, CI-executable demonstration that showcases FrankenLibC's core value proposition: the Transparent Safety Membrane detecting and repairing memory safety violations in real-time. The demo runs a known use-after-free sample program and shows three modes side by side: (1) glibc baseline — the UAF silently corrupts memory, program produces wrong output or crashes non-deterministically. (2) FrankenLibC strict mode — the UAF is detected by the generational arena (generation mismatch), logged to the evidence ledger with full context (allocation site, free site, use site, generation numbers), but the program continues with ABI-compatible behavior (same as glibc — the corruption happens but is observed and recorded). (3) FrankenLibC hardened mode — the UAF is detected, the corrupted pointer is quarantined, the TSM applies a repair action (return NULL with errno=EFAULT or return safe default), and the program continues safely with the repair logged to the evidence ledger. The demo produces: (a) Terminal output showing the three modes with color-coded annotations. (b) Evidence ledger dump showing the detection chain. (c) Performance comparison (strict overhead <20ns, hardened overhead <200ns). (d) The demo is a single 'cargo run --example killer_demo' command, CI-executable, deterministic output. This is the 'show don't tell' artifact for FrankenLibC's pitch.

## Success Criteria
See `acceptance_criteria` field.
design:

- Color-coded terminal output: ANSI escape codes for red (glibc crash/corruption), yellow (strict detection), green (hardened repair).
- Evidence ledger dump: print formatted decision cards from hardened mode run.
- Performance comparison: measure and display overhead for strict (<20ns) and hardened (<200ns).
- Deterministic: fixed random seed for allocation pattern, no timing-dependent output.
