title: iconv: UTF-8 decoder incomplete-vs-invalid + single-byte codepage undefined-position parity vs glibc
description: Found by new iconv_differential_fuzz (live host-glibc oracle, 42k randomized conversions across ISO-8859-*/CP125x/CP437/850/866/KOI8-R <-> UTF-8, comparing return value + errno + output bytes + inbytesleft). TWO real bugs: (1) UTF-8 decode (decode_utf8) used strict RFC-3629 + length-before-continuation-check, so 'E4 DD' (lead+non-continuation) returned EINVAL where glibc=EILSEQ, and 'F7 82 9B' (valid-so-far incomplete 4-byte, 0xF5-0xFD lead) returned EILSEQ where glibc=EINVAL. (2) single-byte decoders for the ISO-8859 family (and others) substituted U+FFFD and reported SUCCESS for undefined codepage positions where glibc returns EILSEQ (e.g. ISO-8859-7 0xAE/0xD2/0xFF). ISO-8859 tables use 0xFFFD as the undefined sentinel, CP* tables use 0xFFFF.
close_reason: done

title: iconv: unmarked UTF-32 BOM decode + lazy encode-BOM parity vs glibc
description: Found by new iconv_wide_differential_fuzz + iconv_unmarked_utf32_bom_vs_glibc (live glibc oracle). Unmarked UTF-32 codec: (1) DECODE ignored a leading BOM — fl emitted FF FE 00 00 as U+FEFF and read a 00 00 FE FF (BE) BOM as a bogus LE unit (EILSEQ), where glibc consumes the BOM and switches endianness (no BOM => native LE). (2) ENCODE emitted the BOM eagerly at loop start, so empty input — or input that errors before the first char — produced a spurious FF FE 00 00 where glibc emits no BOM (BOM only accompanies real output). Explicit-endianness UTF-16LE/BE + UTF-32LE/BE verified clean (40k conversions). Multibyte CJK (BIG5/EUC-JP/Shift-JIS) decoders are stubs (separate), and unmarked UTF-16 codec is unimplemented (bd to follow).

Breakdown by (fl,glibc) width pair: fl=1/glibc=-1 (38286, UNASSIGNED codepoints: glibc returns -1, fl defaults to 1 — needs a General_Category/assigned-set table); fl=1/glibc=2 (20921, WIDE+emoji ranges fl's list misses — needs EastAsianWidth W/F); fl=2/glibc=-1 (4320, unassigned within CJK-ext blocks fl blanket-marks wide); fl=1/glibc=0 (1472, combining marks Mn/Me/Cf fl misses); fl=2/glibc=1 (771, emoji width version-skew); fl=-1/glibc=0 (97, tag chars U+E0001/E0020.. glibc=0 fl=-1); smaller classes. DEEP FIX (not whack-a-mole): regenerate the width table from Unicode DerivedGeneralCategory + EastAsianWidth, version-matched to the host glibc, via a build-time generator (same data-pipeline shape needed for the CJK iconv codecs). Many classes are Unicode-version-coupled so exact parity requires matching glibc's Unicode version. Diagnostic harness committed as wcwidth_sweep_explore.rs (#[ignore]). Sibling structural gap: bd for CJK iconv codec tables.

title: scanf %i: C23 0b binary prefix — fl extension vs host glibc (parity-policy decision)
description:
Found by sscanf_differential_fuzz (live host-glibc oracle). fl scanf %i (core/stdio/scanf.rs base detector) recognizes a C23 0b/0B binary prefix; the host glibc on the worker (strtol base 0) does NOT — sscanf("0b5","%i",&x) gives glibc x=0 consumed 1 (reads octal '0', stops at 'b'). 21/102000 fuzz cases diverged, all %i+0b.

RECLASSIFIED from bug to parity-policy decision: fl DELIBERATELY supports C23 0b in %i — it is pinned by 3 core scanf unit tests (test_scan_* assert SignedInt(10) for "0b1010"). This mirrors prior deliberate-divergence precedents (regex REG_ICASE, mbsrtowcs *src) where fl keeps its own consistent/standards-forward behavior over a host-glibc-version quirk. Removing it broke those 3 tests and removed a real feature, so NOT done unilaterally.

OWNER DECISION NEEDED: keep the C23 0b extension (current state; diverges from this older host glibc but matches C23 / newer glibc) OR drop it for strict host-parity (update the 3 unit tests). The sscanf_differential_fuzz now scopes %i+0b out of its assertion (documented inline) so the fuzzer stays green either way.
close_reason: done

title: scanf %lf/%le/%lg rejects valid float prefix before a second '.'

title: strfmon/strfmon_l/__strfmon_l were stubs ignoring the format string
description: fl's strfmon, strfmon_l, and __strfmon_l were near-total stubs: they read ONE f64 and emitted format!("{:.2}"), ignoring the format string entirely — no literal text, no multiple conversions, no field width / left-precision (#) / right-precision (.p) / flags (= ^ + ( ! -) / sign placement / parens. Implemented a 100% safe-Rust C/POSIX-locale formatter in frankenlibc-core (locale::strfmon::strfmon_c) and routed all three ABI entry points through a shared strfmon_emit. title: fnmatch: two bracket/class parity bugs vs glibc (CASEFOLD folds classes; classifier mis-terminates on [:class:])
description:
Found by new fnmatch_differential_fuzz (live host-glibc oracle, 200k randomized pattern/string/flag combos). TWO bugs in core/string/fnmatch.rs:
1) FNM_CASEFOLD wrongly case-folded POSIX named classes: parse_bracket_subexpr fell back to testing swap_ascii_case(c) against [:class:] so [[:upper:]] matched 'a' under CASEFOLD. glibc folds only literals and ranges, testing named classes against the ORIGINAL byte. Fix: drop the swap-case fallback (and the now-unused swap_ascii_case helper); a buggy unit test (posix_class_casefold) that asserted the wrong behavior was corrected.
2) classify_bracket did not skip POSIX sub-expressions when scanning for the closing ']', so the inner ']' of [:class:] (and [.coll.]/[=equiv=]) was mistaken for the bracket terminator. A bracket that actually runs off the end, e.g. [![:upper:]\]..., was wrongly classified Terminated instead of LiteralFallback. Fix: skip [:...:]/[.....]/[=...=] sub-expressions (mirrors the matcher's parse_bracket_subexpr) and return LiteralFallback if a sub-expression is itself unterminated.
Verified: 200000 fuzz comparisons 0 divergences + 26 core unit + fnmatch_differential_probe + clippy clean.
notes: RESOLVED. Both fnmatch bugs (FNM_CASEFOLD folding named classes; classify_bracket mis-terminating on [:class:]/[.coll.]/[=equiv=]) were fixed by concurrent commit a4444de9 (another agent independently found the same root causes + shipped a fnmatch_differential_fuzz). I had independently reached the same diagnosis/fix; my commit 3a4739f4 landed on top as a clippy cleanup (collapsed the [:class:] match to posix_class_match().unwrap_or_default(), removing a manual_unwrap_or_default warning a4444de9 left). Verified on committed HEAD: fnmatch_differential_fuzz 200000 comparisons 0 divergences, 26 core string::fnmatch unit tests, clippy clean (0 fnmatch hits). Per AGENTS.md rule 9, did not revert the concurrent agent's work. Agent Mail reservation mailbox was busy; proceeded and reconciled post-hoc.

title: argz append/delete: host-glibc differential blocked by malloc_abi/glibc heap coexistence (NOT an argz logic bug)
description: A new two-phase randomized differential fuzzer (crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/argz_mutation_differential_fuzz.rs) replays identical random sequences of argz_add/append/insert/delete/replace on an fl argz buffer and a host glibc argz buffer and compares snapshots. It reproduces a Rust UB precondition violation INSIDE fl's argz (debug build): 'ptr::copy_nonoverlapping requires that both pointer arguments are aligned and non-null and the specified memory ranges do not overlap' -> non-unwinding panic / SIGABRT. Triggers on valid C-ABI inputs (non-empty entries too); host glibc runs the same sequences cleanly. Earlier an interleaved variant also produced 'free(): double free detected in tcache', suggesting real heap corruption in release too. Root-cause not yet pinned (no backtrace; non-unwinding abort). fl-only over 48k ops did NOT crash for one op-order but the two-phase op-order does, so it is input-order-dependent. REPRO: cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test argz_mutation_differential_fuzz -- --ignored --nocapture. Committed #[ignore] as a preserved reproducer. Candidate sites: argz_append/argz_insert/argz_replace copy_nonoverlapping calls in crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/string_abi.rs (argz_add_bytes is fully guarded; argz_delete uses ptr::copy).
notes: RECLASSIFIED (c7a45435), downgraded P2->P4. Investigated: fl argz logic is CORRECT. Replaying ALL FIVE mutations (add/append/insert/delete/replace) against ONLY fl over 4000 randomized scenarios runs clean. The earlier copy_nonoverlapping precondition violation was a slice::to_vec artifact (fl malloc_abi source vs global-alloc snapshot dest flagged 'overlapping') — fixed by snapshotting with a manual byte loop. The remaining SIGSEGV occurs only when the HOST glibc argz oracle allocates persistent buffers alongside fl's malloc_abi in the same test process (surfaces on argz_append's larger buffers) = a malloc_abi/glibc heap-coexistence interaction (see bd-4scbmf), NOT an argz defect. add/insert/replace differential is robust (verified 3x) and committed. REMAINING (low pri): to differentially test append/delete, build a PURE-RUST argz reference model (no host glibc argz) so there is no second allocator to coexist with; OR investigate whether malloc_abi's arena can collide with glibc's heap under large-alloc patterns (bd-4scbmf).
close_reason: Fixed: added a pure-Rust argz mutation reference model and a second randomized fuzzer covering argz_append/argz_delete along with add/insert/replace, avoiding the host-glibc allocator coexistence failure. Evidence: argz_mutation_differential_fuzz passes 2/2 with 33593 model ops including append/delete and 34110 host-glibc add/insert/replace ops; string_abi_test argz passes 7/7 plus 1 ignored hardened-only test; conformance_diff_argz passes 3/3 with 14 corpus cases and 0 divergences; cargo check -p frankenlibc-abi --tests passes with unrelated warnings; cargo clippy -p frankenlibc-abi --test argz_mutation_differential_fuzz --no-deps -- -D warnings passes; touched-file rustfmt check passes.

title: argz_replace used whole-entry matching instead of glibc substring replacement
description: Found by new argz_mutation_differential_fuzz. fl argz_replace compared each entry to the search string for EQUALITY (entry_bytes == find) and replaced the whole entry, but glibc replaces every SUBSTRING occurrence of str within each entry: replace("c"->"aac") turns entry "ac" into "aaac". Also the replace_count semantics: glibc increments it ONCE PER MATCHING ENTRY (not per occurrence), even when an entry has several occurrences (all replaced in the bytes). Fixed both in crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/string_abi.rs argz_replace. Verified: argz_mutation_differential_fuzz (add/insert/replace) 34110 ops 0 divergences vs host glibc; conformance_diff_argz + 200 string_abi_test green.
notes: Fixed in fd640602. argz_replace now does substring replacement within each entry + per-entry replace_count, matching glibc. Verified: argz_mutation_differential_fuzz 34110 ops 0 divergences + conformance_diff_argz + 200 string_abi_test green.

title: strfromd/strfromf/strfroml render non-finite values as Rust 'NaN' instead of glibc 'nan'/'NAN'/'-inf'
description: Found by new strfromd_differential_fuzz (live host-glibc oracle, 200k randomized in-spec %{a,A,e,E,f,F,g,G}[.prec] over normals/subnormals/inf/nan/±0). render_strfrom (crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/string_abi.rs) routed non-finite values through Rust's float formatting, yielding 'NaN' / 'inf' — but glibc strfromd spells them 'nan'/'inf' for lowercase specifiers, 'NAN'/'INF' for uppercase (A/E/F/G), with a leading '-' when the sign bit is set, ignoring precision. Fixed by special-casing !is_finite before the per-spec match. Verified: strfromd_differential_fuzz 200000 comparisons 0 divergences; existing string_abi_test strfrom* + conformance_diff_string_mut green.
notes: Fixed in febf5e0b. render_strfrom special-cases non-finite before the per-spec match (nan/inf lowercase, NAN/INF for A/E/F/G, '-' on sign bit). Verified: strfromd_differential_fuzz 200000 cmp 0 divergences + existing strfrom tests + conformance_diff_string_mut green.

title: mbrtoc16/c16rtomb keep UTF-16 surrogate state in a thread-local instead of the caller's mbstate_t
description: Found by new mbrtoc16_interleaved_differential_fuzz (live host-glibc, two interleaved conversion streams with distinct mbstate_t). mbrtoc16 and c16rtomb stored the pending UTF-16 surrogate (low surrogate for decode, high surrogate for encode) in a THREAD-LOCAL (c16_surrogate), but glibc keeps it in the caller's mbstate_t. So interleaving two supplementary-plane conversions on different mbstate_t on one thread made stream B's surrogate clobber stream A's pending one (reentrancy/parity bug). Fixed: store the surrogate in *ps when ps is non-null (fl's mbrtowc/mbrtoc32 ignore ps, so no collision with multibyte decode state), falling back to the thread-local only when ps is null (matching glibc's internal static state). Verified: mbrtoc16_interleaved fuzz 100000 scenarios 0 divergences (FAILS pre-fix, confirmed); also added c32rtomb_differential_fuzz (300000 cmp 0 div incl surrogate/out-of-range rejection). wchar_abi_test 118 pass.
notes: Fixed in 4f5e5dd7. mbrtoc16/c16rtomb now store the pending surrogate in *ps (per-stream, glibc-matching) when ps!=null, thread-local fallback when null. Verified: mbrtoc16_interleaved fuzz 100000 scenarios 0 div (FAILS pre-fix, confirmed); c32rtomb fuzz 300000 cmp 0 div; wchar_abi_test 118 pass; clippy clean.

title: mbrtowc does not resume an incomplete multibyte sequence across calls (ignores mbstate_t)
description: Found by new mbrtowc_streaming_differential_fuzz (live host-glibc, C.UTF-8, feeds random UTF-8 strings 1-2 bytes per call with a shared mbstate_t). fl mbrtowc IGNORED its ps arg and re-decoded from s each call, so a multibyte char split across calls gave -2 then EILSEQ where glibc stores the partial bytes in ps and resumes (e.g. [0xCB] then [0xA0] -> glibc returns the char U+02E0, fl returns EILSEQ). POSIX violation. FIX: mbrtowc now accumulates partial lead bytes in ps[0..4] (count + bytes) and reassembles before decoding via the shared utf8_decode_step; ps==null keeps the old stateless path. Coupled change: moved the mbrtoc16/c16rtomb pending-surrogate slot from ps[0..4] to ps[4..8] so the two states never overlap. Verified: mbrtowc_streaming 50000 strings 0 div (FAILED pre-fix); mbrtoc16_interleaved 100000 0 div; c32rtomb 300000 0 div; mbrtowc_differential_probe + conformance_diff_mbrtowc + rfc2279 + mbtowc_wctomb + wchar_abi_test all green.
notes: Fixed in 16071a63. mbrtowc accumulates partial bytes in ps[0..4] + reassembles via utf8_decode_step; surrogate slot moved to ps[4..8]. Verified: mbrtowc_streaming 50000 0 div (FAILS pre-fix); mbrtoc16_interleaved + c32rtomb + mbrtowc probes + wchar_abi_test all green.

title: mbrtoc8 was a stub: no UTF-8 validation, no per-byte (-3) output buffering, wrong returns
description: Found by new mbrtoc8_differential_fuzz (live host-glibc, C.UTF-8, 100k random UTF-8 strings incl invalid/truncated tails). C23 mbrtoc8 (unistd_abi.rs) just returned the single byte at *s with return 1 and no validation/state. glibc consumes the whole multibyte char on the first call (return = byte count) and emits its UTF-8 bytes one char8_t at a time as (size_t)-3 without consuming input — e.g. a 2-byte char d4 a7: glibc (2,0xd4) then (-3,0xa7); fl gave (1,0xd4),(1,0xa7). fl also never returned EILSEQ for invalid sequences or -2 for incomplete. FIX: real stateful mbrtoc8 — validate via shared utf8_decode_step, buffer the trailing output bytes in ps[0..4] (returned via -3), accumulate partial input in ps[4..8] (resume across calls), EILSEQ/-2 paths; thread-local fallback for ps==NULL. Verified: mbrtoc8_differential_fuzz 100000 strings 0 divergences; c8rtomb test + clippy green.
notes: Fixed in b7596015. Real stateful C23 mbrtoc8: utf8_decode_step validation, output-byte queue in ps[0..4] (-3 emits), partial-input accumulator in ps[4..8], EILSEQ/-2 paths, thread-local for ps==NULL. Verified: mbrtoc8_differential_fuzz 100000 strings 0 divergences (valid+invalid+truncated); c8rtomb + clippy green. Pushed main+master.

title: c8rtomb was a stub: no byte accumulation, no UTF-8 validation, wrong returns
description: Found by new c8rtomb_differential_fuzz (live host-glibc, C.UTF-8, 100k random UTF-8 strings fed one char8_t per call + invalid/overlong/surrogate/range injection). C23 c8rtomb (unistd_abi.rs) just did *s=c8; return 1 for every byte. glibc accumulates UTF-8 code units in ps and returns 0 mid-sequence, then writes the WHOLE multibyte char and returns its byte count on completion; EILSEQ (-1) on any byte that can't extend a valid sequence. e.g. 3-byte char fed byte-by-byte: glibc (0),(0),(3,[..]); fl gave (1,[..])x3. FIX: real stateful c8rtomb with RFC-3629-STRICT incremental validation (Unicode Table 3-7 lead-specific 2nd-byte ranges) — early overlong (0xE0/0xF0), surrogate (0xED), >U+10FFFF (0xF4) and invalid-lead (0x80-0xC1, 0xF5-0xFF) rejection; accumulate partial bytes in ps[0..4]; thread-local for ps==NULL. NOTE: c8rtomb is strict where the shared utf8_decode_step is deliberately lenient (tuned for glibc's DECODE path mbrtowc/mbrtoc8), so the strict validator is c8rtomb-local. Verified: c8rtomb_differential_fuzz 100000 strings 0 divergences; mbrtoc8 still 0 div; clippy clean.
notes: Fixed in 20af2237. Real stateful c8rtomb: RFC-3629-strict incremental validation (Table 3-7), accumulate in ps[0..4], TLS for ps==NULL. Verified c8rtomb fuzz 100000 0 div + mbrtoc8 0 div + clippy clean. Pushed main+master.

title: mbsnrtowcs resumable/stateful path (non-null ps, mid-char nms splits) had no test coverage
description: The existing n_bounded_wchar_differential_probe is fixed-case and passes a NULL ps, so it never exercised mbsnrtowcs's RESUMABLE path: many calls with a SHARED non-null mbstate and small nms windows that end mid-character, where each call stores a partial sequence in ps (via the mbrtowc fix in bd-2g7oyh.220) and the next must resume. Added mbsnrtowcs_resume_differential_fuzz (live host-glibc, C.UTF-8): 60000 random UTF-8 strings (+ invalid-byte injection) consumed across random small nms windows, comparing the full per-call (return, *src offset, wide chars) sequence. RESULT: 0 divergences — confirms the resume logic + the mbrtowc ps-storage mechanism are glibc-correct end-to-end, and guards both against regression.
notes: Shipped in 50bbbcd4. mbsnrtowcs_resume_differential_fuzz: 60000 strings (+ invalid bytes) across random small nms windows with shared non-null mbstate, 0 divergences vs host glibc. Verifies the resume logic + mbrtowc ps-storage (.220) end-to-end; guards against regression. clippy clean.

title: strerror missing high errno descriptions (102-133); hstrerror wrong for 0/negative/out-of-range
description: Found by new strerror_scan_differential_fuzz (live host-glibc, errno -2..=140 + EAI + h_errno). TWO bugs: (1) strerror returned 'Unknown error N' for errno 102..=133 (ENETRESET, ESHUTDOWN, EHOSTDOWN, EHOSTUNREACH, ESTALE, EDQUOT, ENOMEDIUM, EKEYEXPIRED, EOWNERDEAD, ENOTRECOVERABLE, ERFKILL, EHWPOISON, ...) because its core table was incomplete, while strerrordesc_np already had the complete glibc-exact table. Fixed: rendered_strerror_message now delegates to strerrordesc_np. (2) hstrerror returned the project-internal 'Resolver internal error' for h_errno 0 and out-of-range (5+), where glibc returns 'Resolver Error 0 (no error)' for 0 and 'Unknown resolver error' for >4, reserving 'Resolver internal error' for NEGATIVE values. Fixed to match glibc's value-based mapping. Also shipped nl_langinfo_scan (55 portable items incl CRNCYSTR/ERA/ALT_DIGITS) and signal_strings_scan (strsignal/sigdescr_np/sigabbrev_np over -2..=70) — both 0 divergences (coverage). Verified: all 3 scans 0 div; conformance_diff_string/err_h/string_mut + metamorphic_strerror + string_abi_test green.
notes: Fixed in c14a6d2b. strerror now delegates to strerrordesc_np's complete table (errno 102-133 added); hstrerror matches glibc value-based mapping (negative->internal, 0->no error, >4->unknown). + nl_langinfo (55 items) & signal-strings scans (0 div coverage). Verified all 3 scans + conformance_diff_string/err_h/string_mut + metamorphic + string_abi_test green. Pushed main+master.

title: gmtime/localtime overflow boundary too conservative — returns NULL for years glibc still represents
description: Found by new gmtime_r_wide_range_differential_fuzz (live host-glibc, 400k random i64 epochs biased to the year-overflow boundary). epoch_to_broken_down_checked (core/time/mod.rs) used a conservative ±EPOCH_RANGE_LIMIT (6.7768e16 s) cutoff and returned None for epochs near -6.78e16 where glibc still returns a valid tm (tm_year ~ -2147483510, well within c_int). glibc's actual contract: NULL only when tm_year (= year - 1900) overflows c_int. Since civil_from_days is O(1), fixed to compute the year directly and check the i32 boundary exactly (no approximation, no year-walking loop risk). Affects gmtime/gmtime_r/localtime/localtime_r (all share the checked fn). Verified: gmtime_r_wide_range fuzz 400000 cmp 0 divergences; conformance_diff_time + timegm_normalize + time_abi_test + core time unit tests green.
notes: Fixed in 0d8d6c37. epoch_to_broken_down_checked computes the year via O(1) civil_from_days and checks tm_year fits c_int exactly (was conservative ±EPOCH_RANGE_LIMIT). Fixes gmtime/gmtime_r/localtime/localtime_r. Verified: gmtime_r_wide_range 400000 cmp 0 div + conformance_diff_time + timegm_normalize + time_abi_test + core time tests green. Pushed main+master.

title: asctime/asctime_r truncate instead of returning NULL for out-of-range year (>26-byte output)
description: Found by new asctime_r_differential_fuzz (live host-glibc, 200k random tm with wide tm_year). format_asctime (core/time/mod.rs) TRUNCATED the output to the 26-byte buffer (dropping the trailing newline) for years whose '%d' exceeds 4 chars (year < -999 or > 9999), e.g. year -1000 -> fl 'Mon Jan 16 14:51:06 -1000' (no newline). glibc bounds asctime/asctime_r to the 26-byte contract and returns NULL (EOVERFLOW) when the formatted string + NUL would exceed 26 bytes. Fixed: format_asctime returns 0 (-> asctime_r/ctime NULL) when bytes.len()+1 > 26. Affects asctime/asctime_r/ctime/ctime_r. Also shipped timegm_wide_range_differential_fuzz (300k tm normalization + wide years, 0 div coverage). Verified: asctime fuzz 200000 0 div; conformance_diff_time + time_abi_test + core time green.
notes: Fixed in 457f1e12. format_asctime returns 0 (NULL) when output+NUL > 26 bytes (year >4 chars), matching glibc EOVERFLOW. Affects asctime/asctime_r/ctime/ctime_r. + timegm_wide_range fuzz (300k 0 div coverage). Verified asctime fuzz 200000 0 div + conformance_diff_time + time_abi_test + core time green. Pushed main+master.

title: ether_ntoa formats with leading zeros (%02x); glibc uses %x (no leading zeros)
description: Found by new ether_ntoa_differential_fuzz (live host-glibc). core ether::format_ether_addr produced a fixed 17-char 'xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx' (leading zeros, %02x), but glibc ether_ntoa[_r] uses 'sprintf("%x:%x:%x:%x:%x:%x")' — NO leading zeros, lowercase: {0,1,0x0a,0x0b,0x0c,0xff} -> '0:1:a:b:c:ff', not '00:01:0a:0b:0c:ff'. Fixed: format_ether_addr now writes the glibc %x form (variable length, returns byte count). Updated callers (ether_ntoa/ether_ntoa_r), core unit tests, the stdlib_abi_test roundtrip assertion, and the conformance ether_text_class reference. ether_aton already accepted variable-width groups (fuzz confirms). ALSO fixed a LATENT failing test on main from bd-2g7oyh.225: stdlib_abi_test::hstrerror_reports_known_and_unknown_codes asserted hstrerror(9999)=='Resolver internal error' but the .225 fix correctly made out-of-range-positive return 'Unknown resolver error' (negative -> internal); updated the assertion. Verified: ether_ntoa fuzz 400000 0 div; core ether (23) + stdlib_abi_test (405) + harness wave08 conformance (6) green.
notes: Fixed in 6cb85421. ether_ntoa now uses glibc %x form (no leading zeros); core format_ether_addr rewritten + callers/tests/conformance ref updated. Also fixed latent main test break from .225 (hstrerror(9999) -> 'Unknown resolver error'). Verified ether fuzz 400000 0 div + core ether(23) + stdlib_abi_test(405) + harness wave08(6) green. Plus strftime_buffer_wide_year coverage (300k 0 div). Pushed main+master.

title: [parity][coverage] inet_net_ntop/pton + inet_nsap_addr/ntoa: randomized full-grammar differential fuzzers vs host libresolv (0 div)
description:
Existing inet_net/inet_nsap differential probes were fixed-case. Added two randomized live differential fuzzers (deterministic LCG, host libresolv oracle via #[link(name="resolv")]):
- inet_net_ntop_differential_fuzz: ntop random [u8;4] x bits 0..=32; pton sweeps the quirky libresolv CIDR grammar (decimal a.b.c.d/bits, classful no-slash, 0x/0X hex nibble form, leading-zero decimal, malformed double-dot/trailing-junk/empty, random byte soup). 400k comparisons, 0 divergences.
- inet_nsap_differential_fuzz: ntoa random binary (incl >255 clamp); addr sweeps hex pairs with .  /+ // separators, odd digit counts, mid-byte separators, whitespace/0x rejection, random soup, tight output buffers. 300k comparisons, 0 divergences.
Result: fl inet_net_ntop/pton and inet_nsap_addr/ntoa are glibc(libresolv)-exact across the full randomized grammar surface. No source change; coverage only. Confirms the BIND-derived NSAP separator/uppercase rules and net_pton classful+hex inference match the live oracle.
close_reason: Shipped both randomized differential fuzzers (commit 5affd105). 400k+300k comparisons, 0 divergences vs host libresolv. fl inet_net_ntop/pton + inet_nsap_addr/ntoa proven glibc-exact across full grammar. Coverage only, no source change.

title: [perf] strlen 4096 glibc gap: fold SIMD panels with min before NUL reduction
description: PROFILE-BACKED (rch glibc_baseline_bench, this session): glibc_baseline_strlen_4096 frankenlibc_core p50=87.996ns vs host_glibc p50=20.823ns => 4.2x slower, the single largest remaining vs-upstream gap (memcpy/memset at parity, strcmp 1.45x). Current strlen main loop (str.rs:136) processes one 64-byte Simd panel per iteration with a per-panel .any() horizontal reduction. glibc AVX2 strlen folds 4 vectors with vpminub before a single compare+test. LEVER (one): add a 256-byte block loop that folds 4x Simd<u8,64> with simd_min (unsigned vpminub) then a single simd_eq(0).any(), advancing i by 256 over NUL-free regions; existing 64-byte/word/byte tail loops still find the exact NUL index unchanged. title: [parity][bug] random/initstate: generator type ignored — always TYPE_3 regardless of state-buffer size (glibc selects TYPE_0/1/2/3/4 by size)
description:
frankenlibc random()/initstate() always used the glibc TYPE_3 (degree-31) additive-feedback generator regardless of the state-buffer size passed to initstate(seed, buf, n). glibc selects ONE OF FIVE generators by n: TYPE_0 (deg 0, pure LCG) for 8<=n<32, TYPE_1 (deg 7) for 32<=n<64, TYPE_2 (deg 15) for 64<=n<128, TYPE_3 (deg 31) for 128<=n<256, TYPE_4 (deg 63) for n>=256. So after initstate with any non-128 buffer, fl's random() sequence diverged from glibc from the very first call.

Found by a new randomized differential fuzzer (random_initstate_differential_fuzz) driving frankenlibc_core::stdlib directly vs host glibc across all five size classes: fl produced the IDENTICAL sequence for sizes 8/16/31/32/48/63/64/96/127 (proving size was ignored) while glibc produced a distinct sequence per class.

Fix (core/src/stdlib/random_sv.rs): generalized RandomState to carry rand_type/deg/sep + a 63-word table; faithful glibc __srandom_r seeding via Schrage decomposition (bit-exact for all seeds incl high-bit-set, where the old rem_euclid diverged) and __random_r next() with the TYPE_0 LCG branch and exact cursor-advance; initstate/setstate select the type from buffer size. Also bumped ABI RANDOM_STATE_MAX_BYTES 128->256 so setstate recovers the same size (hence type) initstate selected (a 256-byte buffer was initializing as TYPE_4 but restoring as TYPE_3). Default random()/srandom()/rand()/srand() stay TYPE_3, behavior-identical (all existing parity tests preserved). Validated: 42000 initstate + 5000 default-srandom comparisons, 0 divergences vs host glibc.

Faithful __srandom_r/__random_r port + ABI RANDOM_STATE_MAX_BYTES 128->256 for setstate type consistency. 42k+5k differential comparisons vs host glibc, 0 divergences; all existing parity tests preserved.

title: [parity][bug] reentrant random_r/srandom_r/initstate_r/setstate_r are stubs — single LCG step, not glibc TYPE_0..4 additive feedback
description:
The reentrant System V RNG was a stub: random_r did ONE LCG step (val*1103515245+12345 >>1) over the first 4 bytes of the random_data struct; srandom_r/initstate_r just wrote the seed to those 4 bytes; setstate_r did nothing. RANDOM_R_BUF_BYTES was size_of::<u32>()=4 (glibc struct random_data is 48 bytes). So the entire reentrant family diverged from glibc's TYPE_0..4 additive-feedback generators from the first draw, and did not honor statelen-based type selection, srandom_r reseed, or setstate_r at all.

Fix: added a pure-safe-Rust reentrant API in core/stdlib/random_sv.rs (random_r_initstate/step/srandom/setstate/flush + RandomRState), reusing the shared seed_table/next_draw kernels (extracted from the global generator). The ABI now treats random_data as a 48-byte opaque blob holding a pointer to the caller's statebuf + cursor/type, with glibc-compatible statebuf word layout (word0 = MAX_TYPES*rear+type encoding, word1..=deg = state). initstate_r selects type by statelen; setstate_r flushes the old generator's live cursor then restores (matching glibc's save-then-restore order, which preserves the live cursor on same-buffer rebind via the fptr=(rptr+sep)%deg invariant).

Found + proven by a new core-vs-host-glibc differential fuzzer (random_r_reentrant_differential_fuzz): 30000 initstate+draw comparisons across all 5 size classes + 20000 srandom_r/setstate_r comparisons, 0 divergences. Drives the core API (not the membrane ABI) to avoid the glibc-heap coexistence crash (bd-2g7oyh.212). Updated stdlib_abi_test random_r test to the correct glibc contract (48-byte random_data + statebuf + initstate_r first).

title: [parity][accuracy][math] clog catastrophic cancellation near |z|=1 — log(hypot) loses ~7 digits; glibc uses log1p
description: fl's complex clog computed the real part as log(hypot(re,im)), which cancels catastrophically when |z| ~ 1 (the log is near zero). A differential fuzzer vs host glibc measured up to 1.5e7 ULP near the unit circle. Fixed with glibc's approach: 0.5*log1p(re^2+im^2-1) where re^2+im^2-1 is formed with fma-compensated squares + Knuth 2Sum so the residual survives even at ~45deg on the unit circle (where ax^2 and ay^2 cancel and ax^2-1 is no longer exact by Sterbenz). Result: clog max 5 ULP vs glibc across all regimes, 0 special-value mismatches. Improves all c_log dependents (cpow, casin/cacos/catan/casinh/cacosh/catanh).

title: [parity][math] ctanh/ctan: inf/inf -> NaN for large real (ctanh) or imag (ctan) part; glibc returns saturated +-1
description: fl computed ctanh(z) = csinh(z)/ccosh(z) via c_div, which forms inf/inf -> NaN once |Re z| is large (both sinh and cosh overflow). Same for ctan via csin/ccos for large |Im z|. complex_math_differential_fuzz measured ctanh 56977/200000 and ctan 65834/200000 inf/nan category mismatches vs host glibc (glibc saturates to +-1 + i*0). Fixed with glibc's overflow-stable identity tanh(x+iy) = (sinh x cosh x + i sin y cos y)/(sinh^2 x + cos^2 y) whose denominator scales with the numerator, a |x|>354 saturation branch (real=+-1, imag=4 sin cos exp(-2|x|) -> +-0), and C99 Annex G non-finite handling. ctan derives via ctan(z) = -i tanh(iz). Result: ctanh/ctan now 0 category mismatches, max 6 ULP, 0/1 signed-zero (a lone denormal-vs-0 edge at the exp underflow boundary where fl is the more correctly-rounded). Regression guard added to the fuzzer. Remaining complex special-value/sign-flip gaps (cexp/csin/ccos/csinh/ccosh + casin/cacos/casinh/cacosh/catan/catanh) stay in bd-2g7oyh.237.

title: [parity][math] csinh/ccosh: inf*0 -> NaN special values (im=0 with overflowing real); glibc gives signed 0
description: fl computed csinh(x+iy)=sinh(x)cos(y)+i cosh(x)sin(y) and ccosh likewise. When the hyperbolic factor overflows (large |x|) and the trig factor is exactly 0 (notably y==0), the product is inf*0=NaN, where glibc gives a signed 0. complex_math_differential_fuzz: csinh 8821/200000, ccosh 8737/200000 inf/nan category mismatches. Reimplemented both via glibc-faithful c_sinh/c_cosh helpers with full C99 Annex G special-value handling (signed-zero imag at y==0 with sign(x)^sign(iy) for ccosh; +-inf/NaN corner cases matched to glibc bit-exact via a deterministic 9x9 grid test). Result: category mismatches 8821/8737 -> 38/56, 0 signed-zero mismatches, max 5 ULP. Residual ~38/56 are the narrow |x|~710 overflow band where glibc scales e^|x|/2=2^1022*exp(|x|-t) to a finite value (a separate scaling sub-bug, also affecting csin/ccos's 49; the naive 1-step scale was ~277 ULP off glibc so left for a focused follow-up). Remaining complex gaps (cexp special values, csin/ccos overflow scaling, inverse-fn sign flips) stay in bd-2g7oyh.237.
close_reason: Fixed in 39a11ae7. csinh/ccosh reimplemented via glibc-faithful c_sinh/c_cosh with Annex G special values (signed-zero imag at y==0, inf/nan corners bit-exact via 9x9 grid test). Category mismatches 8821/8737 -> 38/56, 0 signbit, max 5 ULP. Residual = narrow |x|~710 overflow-scaling band (left for follow-up in bd-2g7oyh.237).

title: [parity][math] complex exp/hyperbolic/trig overflow band: |Re z|~710 yields inf where glibc scales to finite (csinh/ccosh/cexp/csin/ccos)
description: For |Re z| in ~(709, 711) the exponential overflows to inf, so the naive csinh/ccosh (sinh(x)/cosh(x)) and cexp (e^x) overflow and the trig-scaled result is a spurious inf, where glibc keeps a finite value (e.g. cexp(711.6+0.09i) glibc=(inf, 1.04e308) but fl gave (inf, inf)). complex_math_differential_fuzz residual: csinh 38, ccosh 56, cexp 26, csin 49, ccos 49. Fixed with the split e^x = (e^(x/2))^2 (h = exp(x/2), well in range; sinh(x)==cosh(x)==e^x/2 to full f64 precision past the threshold) so a finite result with a small trig factor survives. A prior naive 1-step scale (exp(x-t_float)*2^1023) was ~277 ULP off because t_float != 1023*ln2 exactly; the (e^(x/2))^2 split avoids that. Also rederived csin(z)=-i*csinh(iz), ccos(z)=ccosh(iz) so they inherit the scaling AND the .241/.242 special values, and fixed a latent c_sinh inf-branch sign bug (real = sign(rx)^sign(cos y), was just sign(rx) — hidden because the grid's cos(1e6)>0). Result: csinh/ccosh/cexp/csin/ccos all 0 category + 0 signed-zero mismatches, max 5 ULP vs host glibc. Residual: csin/ccos both-infinite corners (e.g. csin(inf+i*inf) imag sign) where glibc uses an independent convention from the i*z identity (ultra-exotic, random fuzzer clean). Elementary complex transcendentals now glibc-parity. Remaining in bd-2g7oyh.237: inverse-fn sign flips (casin/cacos/catan/casinh/cacosh/catanh).
close_reason: Fixed in HEAD. Overflow band scaled via e^x=(e^(x/2))^2 split (avoids the 277-ULP t_float error); csin/ccos rederived from c_sinh/c_cosh to inherit scaling + special values; fixed latent c_sinh inf-branch real-sign bug. csinh/ccosh/cexp/csin/ccos all 0 category + 0 signbit, max 5 ULP. Elementary complex transcendentals now glibc-parity. Residual: csin/ccos both-infinite corners (independent glibc convention, ultra-exotic). Remaining: inverse-fn sign flips in bd-2g7oyh.237.

title: [parity][math] catanh/catan branch-cut sign flips + accuracy near +-1 (naive 0.5*clog((1+z)/(1-z)))
description: fl computed catanh(z)=0.5*clog((1+z)/(1-z)) via c_div/c_log, which mishandled the branch-cut signs on (-inf,-1] and [1,inf) (full sign flips, e.g. catan(0-1.345i) real -pi/2 vs glibc +pi/2) and left rounding noise where the result is exactly real/imaginary. complex_math_differential_fuzz: catanh/catan ~9.2e18 ULP (sign flips) + ~34800 category mismatches each. Reimplemented c_atanh with the cancellation-free closed form Re=0.25*log(((1+x)^2+y^2)/((1-x)^2+y^2)), Im=0.5*atan2(2y,(1-x)(1+x)-y^2): log1p(4x/den) for the bulk, switching to log(num)-log(den) only near the z=-1 branch point (num<0.5*den, where log1p cancels), plus the large-|z| limit atanh(z)~1/z+i*sign(y)*pi/2 and C99 Annex G special values. catan derives via catan(z)=-i*atanh(iz). Result: catanh 10 ULP, catan 12 ULP, both 0 category + 0 signed-zero mismatches. Deterministic catanh special grid (special-exact, finite<=4 ULP) added. Remaining in bd-2g7oyh.237: casin/cacos/casinh/cacosh sign flips (asin family, needs Hull-Fairgrieve-Tang).
close_reason: Fixed in HEAD. catanh/catan reimplemented as closed-form c_atanh (Re=0.25*log(num/den) via log1p switching to log(num)-log(den) near z=-1; Im=0.5*atan2) + large-|z| limit + Annex G specials; catan derives via -i*atanh(iz). Sign flips gone: catanh 10 ULP, catan 12 ULP, 0 category + 0 signbit. Deterministic catanh special grid added. Remaining: asin family (casin/cacos/casinh/cacosh) in bd-2g7oyh.237.

title: [parity][math] asin family casin/cacos/casinh/cacosh: branch-cut sign flips + cancellation (naive log/sqrt)
description: fl computed casin/casinh via -i*clog(iz+csqrt(1-z^2)) and cacos/cacosh via pi/2-casin / clog(z+csqrt(z^2-1)), which flipped signs across the [1,inf)/(-inf,-1] branch cuts (e.g. cacosh(-1e6+0i) real -14.5 vs glibc +14.5) and lost precision via cancellation. complex_math_differential_fuzz: all 4 ~9.2e18/1.9e9 ULP (sign flips) + ~17000-30000 category mismatches each. Reimplemented with the Hull-Fairgrieve-Tang arcsine/arccosine (hft_asin/hft_acos: a=(|z+1|+|z-1|)/2, b=x/a, real via asin(b)/atan crossover, imag via log1p(a-1...)/acosh(a)) which keeps signs and accuracy across the cuts and avoids overflow (acosh for large a) and cacos cancellation near z=1 (direct acos). casinh=base (C99 Annex G specials); casin=-i*asinh(iz); cacos via hft_acos; cacosh=+-i*acos with Re>=0 (sign bit + NaN routing). Result: casin/cacos/casinh/cacosh all 5 ULP, 0 category + 0 signed-zero. Deterministic casinh/cacosh special grid added. COMPLETES bd-2g7oyh.237 (all 13 nontrivial complex fns now glibc-parity).
close_reason: Fixed in HEAD. casin/cacos/casinh/cacosh reimplemented via Hull-Fairgrieve-Tang arcsine/arccosine (a=(|z+1|+|z-1|)/2, b=x/a; Re via asin(b)/acos(b)/atan crossover; Im via log1p/acosh). casinh=base+Annex G; casin=-i*asinh(iz); cacosh=+-i*acos w/ Re>=0. Sign flips gone: all 4 at 5 ULP, 0 cat + 0 signbit. Deterministic casinh/cacosh special grid added. COMPLETES the complex inverse functions — all 13 nontrivial complex.h transcendentals now glibc-parity.

title: [parity][bug] sscanf %[...] reversed range (lo>hi) drops members; glibc treats as literals {lo,-,hi}
description: frankenlibc sscanf scanset parsing (core/stdio/scanf.rs) handled a REVERSED range X-Y (lo>hi, e.g. z-0 or a-.) by adding NO members while still consuming all 3 chars — so the set silently dropped them. glibc instead treats a reversed range as three literal members {X, -, Y}. Found by a new randomized scanset-edge differential fuzzer (sscanf_scanset_differential_fuzz) vs host glibc: e.g. sscanf("-#", "%[ a-.]%n") returns 1/"-" on glibc but 0 on fl (the literal '-' from the reversed a-. range); sscanf with %[^ez-0] matched one extra char because '0' was dropped from the set. Fixed: when lo>hi, mark chars[lo], chars['-'], chars[hi] as set members (matching glibc s scanset builder). Result: 199621 randomized scanset comparisons (ranges incl reversed, ]-as-first-member, leading/trailing literal dash, negation, field width) 0 divergences. (Unterminated scansets like %[^] — malformed/UB where glibc rejects and fl accepts — are out of scope, filtered.) No regression: core scanf unit tests (70), scanf_differential_probe, sscanf_differential_fuzz all green.
close_reason: Fixed in HEAD. sscanf scanset reversed range (lo>hi) now adds literals {lo,-,hi} matching glibc (was dropping all 3). Found+guarded by new sscanf_scanset_differential_fuzz (199621 cases, 0 div: ranges incl reversed, ]-first, leading/trailing dash, negation, field width). No regression (70 unit + probe + existing fuzzer green).

title: [parity][bug] wcstol/wcstoul skip Unicode whitespace (U+00A0/U+2003/U+3000); glibc C-locale iswspace is ASCII-only
description: frankenlibc wide wcstol_impl/wcstoul_impl (core/stdlib/conversion.rs) skipped leading whitespace via wide_is_space, which used char::is_whitespace() — Rust's Unicode-aware classification (U+00A0 NO-BREAK SPACE, U+2003 EM SPACE, U+3000 IDEOGRAPHIC SPACE, U+2000 EN QUAD, etc.). glibc's wcstol/wcstoul run iswspace in the C locale, which recognizes ONLY the ASCII whitespace set (space + \t\n\v\f\r), so a leading non-ASCII space is a non-digit at position 0 (no conversion). Found by a new randomized wide differential fuzzer (wcstol_differential_fuzz) vs host glibc: e.g. wcstol([U+00A0, '4', '2'], 10) returned 42/consumed-2 on fl but 0/consumed-0 on glibc. Fixed wide_is_space to matches!(wc, 0x20 | 0x09..=0x0D) (ASCII-only). Updated 2 unit tests that asserted the buggy Unicode-skip. wcstod is unaffected (it projects wide->ASCII via project_wide_ascii which truncates at the first >0x7f char, then uses byte strtod — already glibc-correct). Result: 299645 randomized wide comparisons (base 0/2..36, prefixes, overflow, non-ASCII digit/space lookalikes) 0 divergences (the C23 0b binary prefix is a deliberate fl extension per bd-2g7oyh.203 and is scoped out). No regression: 95 conversion unit tests green.
close_reason: Fixed in HEAD. wide_is_space was char::is_whitespace() (Unicode) -> ASCII-only matches!(wc, 0x20|0x09..=0x0D) matching glibc C-locale iswspace; wcstol/wcstoul no longer over-skip U+00A0/U+2003/U+3000. Found+guarded by new wcstol_differential_fuzz (299645 cases, 0 div; 0b extension scoped out). wcstod unaffected (ASCII-projection). No regression (95 unit tests green).

title: [perf][no-gaps] strcpy_4096 two-stream copy-plus-NUL detector
description:
Fresh pass-11 RCH criterion profile on worker vmi1156319 (2026-06-08) shows strcpy_4096 is the top current profile-backed residual: FrankenLibC p50=152.297 ns mean=160.343 ns p95=198.744 ns p99=239.354 vs host glibc p50=74.933 ns mean=80.975 ns p95=118.057 ns p99=141.904. Adjacent rows on the same profile: memcmp_4096 p50 gap 102.874 vs 68.875 but repeated memcmp equality-control-plane families were recently rejected; strchr_absent p50 91.652 vs 67.309; strspn_long p50 296.688 vs 258.075; allocator 64/256 gaps smaller and just attacked. Prior strcpy families: bd-2g7oyh.144 shipped fused scan/store for NUL-free 512B blocks; bd-2g7oyh.246 rejected final-block NUL rank-select after block_has_nul_512. Do not repeat either.

Candidate one-lever: replace the current late-copy algorithmic shape for the fully slice-bounded, NUL-terminated fast path with a safe-Rust two-stream copy-plus-NUL detector: copy a bounded 512B source block into dest first, then run the existing folded NUL control-plane detector on the copied block/source block and return immediately when the terminator falls inside the block. This attacks the structural double walk (scan first, then copy / final scalar copy) rather than the rejected final-block resolver. It preserves all fallback/no-NUL/panic paths and writes only within dest because the branch requires src.last()==0 and dest.len()>=src.len().

Required loop: RCH focused baseline before edit; one source lever only in crates/frankenlibc-core/src/string/str.rs; prove first-NUL ordering and return count unchanged, trailing bytes after first NUL may be copied only inside the already-valid dest buffer and are not observable under strcpy's C-string contract but existing trailing-dest unit must still pass for short/fallback path, panic contract unchanged, FP/RNG N/A, golden strcpy transcript SHA; same-worker RCH rebench; keep only Score>=2.0 or restore/reject; commit before/after numbers, close bead, push main and main:master, reprofile.
close_reason: KEPT strcpy NUL-prefix certificate + bulk copy. Same-worker RCH vmi1156319 pre-edit profile strcpy_4096 FL p50 152.297 ns mean 160.343 ns; candidate p50 117.405 ns mean 138.153 ns. Focused baseline on vmi1293453 was FL p50 70.140 ns mean 74.037 vs host p50 37.455 ns mean 42.875; RCH did not route post there. Behavior proof: RCH cargo test -p frankenlibc-core strcpy passed 5/5 with golden SHA, trailing-dest, and no-NUL panic contract. RCH check -p frankenlibc-core --all-targets passed; clippy blocked only by unrelated existing lints in math/exp.rs, stdio/file.rs, string/regex.rs. Score 9.0. title: [parity][bug][fnmatch] FNM_EXTMATCH residual: leading-* exposing '.' to a wildcard (PERIOD) + literal '/' inside a group (PATHNAME)
description: Found by un-scoping fnmatch_extmatch_differential_fuzz to PATHNAME/PERIOD. The common PERIOD bug (mid-component '.' rejected by a wildcard inside a group occurrence) is FIXED (sub_full_match clears FNM_PERIOD for non-leading sub-slices; commit pins conformance_diff_fnmatch_extperiod). TWO residual clusters remain: (1) PERIOD + a leading '*' (or '*' generally) that EXPOSES a '.' to a following wildcard: `*?+(?|b)*` on 'c.' EXT|PERIOD -> glibc NOMATCH, fl MATCH (glibc extends leading-dot protection across the *; `?+(?)` on 'c.' correctly matches in both, so it is specific to the *-exposes-dot interaction). (2) PATHNAME + a literal '/' INSIDE an extglob group: `*@(/)*` on 'aa/' EXT|PATHNAME -> glibc NOMATCH (a group occurrence cannot span/contain '/' under PATHNAME), fl MATCH; yet `@(a/b)` on 'a/b' EXT|PATHNAME -> glibc MATCH (probed) so the rule is subtle. Both are intricate glibc semantics; deferred. Repro: re-add PATHNAME/PERIOD flags + '/' to gen_consuming_atom in the fuzzer.
close_reason: RESOLVED as glibc-inconsistency, fl deliberately more consistent (won't-mirror, same policy as ecvt/remquo/regex-nested-submatch). Minimized BOTH residual clusters to single glibc inconsistencies: (1) PERIOD: glibc matches *+(?) on 'c.' AND ?+(?) on 'c.' but REJECTS *?+(?) on 'c.' — the '.' is mid-string (index 1, not leading) so all should match; glibc's rejection of only the *?+group composition is an artifact. (2) PATHNAME: glibc lets an extglob group match a literal '/' in @(/),a@(/)b,@(/)c,*(/),+(/),?(/) but REJECTS *@(/)* on 'aa/' (the same group sandwiched between two *s) — also an artifact. In both, fl returns the sensible/consistent result (MATCH). PINNED by NEW conformance_diff_fnmatch_extglob_glibc_quirks.rs (asserts the glibc inconsistency + fl's consistent behavior; flags for re-eval if a future glibc becomes consistent). The COMMON PERIOD bug (mid-component '.' rejected by a group-internal wildcard, e.g. +(a|?) on bc..) was the real bug and is FIXED in 00de649e.

title: [parity][bug][wchar] fgetwc rejects obsolete 5/6-byte UTF-8; fgetws(n=1) returns NULL instead of empty string
description: Found by NEW wide-stdio differential probe vs live glibc C.UTF-8. (1) fgetwc lead-byte length detection (wchar_abi.rs ~2807) only handled 1-4 byte leads and rejected 5/6-byte leads (0xF8..0xFD) with EILSEQ BEFORE reading continuations — yet wchar_core::mbtowc already decodes obsolete RFC-2279 5/6-byte for C.UTF-8 parity (bd-kryp2k). So fgetwc was inconsistent with fl mbrtowc/mbtowc: file F8 88 80 80 80 0A -> glibc [U+200000, \n] but fl [WEOF]. (2) fgetws(ws,1,stream) returned NULL (loop never runs, written==0 -> NULL) but C99/glibc write L0 and return ws (n=1 reads 0 chars, no EOF). FIXED both: extend lead detection to 5/6-byte (mbtowc validates overlong/decode); track hit_eof so fgetws returns NULL only on real EOF-before-any-char. Pinned by NEW conformance_diff_wide_stdio.rs.
close_reason: Both fixed in wchar_abi.rs. title: [parity][bug][wchar] fputwc errors on unconvertible wide char instead of glibc '?'-substitution
description: Found by NEW wide-stdio write-side differential probe. glibc wide-stdio (fputwc/fputws/putwc/putwchar) substitutes a single ? (0x3f) byte for a wide char its UTF-8 gconv cannot represent (a surrogate 0xD800-0xDFFF, or a value > U+7FFFFFFF), and reports SUCCESS (returns wc, errno unchanged) — its gconv fallback, NOT C99 EILSEQ/WEOF (which glibc wcrtomb DOES return; glibc fputwc and wcrtomb deliberately differ). fl wctomb correctly rejects these, but fl fputwc returned WEOF+EILSEQ (wrote nothing) — diverging from glibc. Since fl is a glibc DROP-IN, mirror glibc: fputwc writes ? and returns wc on unconvertible. Fix at the fputwc choke point (fputws/putwc/putwchar all delegate). fwprintf %lc with a surrogate is a separate path, out of scope. Encodable-but-unusual chars (0x110000->F4 90 80 80, up to U+7FFFFFFF->6-byte) already encode correctly. Pinned by NEW conformance_diff_wide_stdio_write.rs.
close_reason: Fixed: fputwc now substitutes '?' (single byte) + returns wc as success for unconvertible wide chars (surrogates, >U+7FFFFFFF), mirroring glibc gconv instead of C99 EILSEQ/WEOF. fputws/putwc/putwchar delegate. Pinned by NEW conformance_diff_wide_stdio_write.rs (live-glibc write-side differential). db9a9ca2

title: getdate/getdate_r: no POSIX default-fill — partial specs return raw strptime vs glibc current-time seeding + rc=8 invalid-date
description: fl getdate_core (unistd_abi.rs ~24270) zero-inits tm and returns the raw strptime result with NO POSIX default-fill. glibc seeds unspecified fields from current local time and applies rules, so partial specs diverge hugely. Ground truth (NOW=Tue 2026-06-09 13:59, probed): full date '12/25/2030' -> time defaults to CURRENT h:m:s + wday/yday/isdst computed (fl returns h=m=s=0, wday=yday=0); 'January 05'(%B %d) -> year=current, time=current (fl: year=0); '10:30'(%H:%M) -> today, rolled to TOMORROW since past, sec=0 (fl: mday=0); '23:59:58' -> today (future); 'Monday'(%A) -> next Monday's date, time=current; date-no-year -> current year NO rollover; 'February 30' -> rc=8 (invalid real date); month-13 -> rc=7. Degenerate single-field specs (month-only 'March'->mday=3/yr2027, day-only '15'->yr=-1885, yday-only) are glibc-idiosyncratic garbage = won't-mirror. BLOCKER for full parity: glibc derives isdst + rollover via LOCAL mktime; fl mktime is UTC-only (documented TZ scope) -> getdate matches glibc only under TZ=UTC. Fix: implement default-fill (current-time seed, time-field/date-field rules, weekday next-occurrence, time-only tomorrow-rollover, rc=8 invalid-date validation) + final mktime normalize; gate with fl-vs-glibc same-process differential under TZ=UTC.
close_reason: Fixed (e5ffb353): getdate/getdate_r now apply glibc POSIX default-fill. Sentinel-init tm -> strptime -> fill unspecified fields from current local time: no-time->current h:m:s / any-time->lower fields 0; year->current (no rollover); weekday-only->next occurrence; time-only->today rolled to tomorrow if past; impossible real date (Feb 30)->8; empty input->7 (was 8); final mktime normalizes wday/yday. Degenerate single-field specs (month/day/yday-only) are glibc-idiosyncratic garbage = won't-mirror (excluded). isdst+rollover need local mktime; fl mktime UTC-only (documented TZ scope) so parity under TZ=UTC. NEW conformance_diff_getdate.rs same-process gate. unistd_abi getdate test + time regressions + clippy green.

title: strptime: tm_wday/tm_yday not filled from resolved date (glibc want_xday)
description: fl strptime left tm_wday and tm_yday untouched after parsing a date, whereas glibc recomputes BOTH from the resolved (tm_year,tm_mon,tm_mday) whenever a year (%Y/%y/%C), month (%m/%b/%B/%h), day (%d/%e) or day-of-year (%j) field was parsed — its want_xday flag. Even a plain strptime('2024-06-15','%Y-%m-%d') sets wday=6,yday=166 in glibc; fl left them 0/garbage. Also the %U/%W week-derivation set mon/mday but not yday, and the %j derivation set mon/mday/yday but not wday. Probed vs live glibc (zero-init tm): want_xday triggers on year/mon/mday/yday but NOT weekday-alone (%a/%w/%u), NOT ISO-alone (%V/%G/%g), NOT time-only. Explicitly parsed weekday or %j kept as given. Degenerate excluded (won't-mirror): week-0 pre-January (glibc OOB-table garbage e.g. mday=-370; fl sane) and out-of-range %j=400 (glibc wraps, fl rejects). Fix: glibc-exact day_of_the_week/day_of_the_year helpers + end-of-parse fill gated on want_xday. NEW conformance_diff_strptime_xday.rs.
close_reason: Fixed (aad2a4f9): strptime now fills tm_wday+tm_yday from the resolved date via glibc-exact day_of_the_week/day_of_the_year, gated on want_xday (year/month/day/yday parsed, or date derived from %j/%U/%W). Weekday-alone, ISO-%V/%G-alone and time-only do not trigger; explicit weekday/%j kept. Plain %Y-%m-%d now sets wday/yday (was 0). Won't-mirror: week-0 pre-Jan (glibc OOB garbage) + out-of-range %j. NEW conformance_diff_strptime_xday.rs; time_abi(60)+conformance_diff_time(12)+wcsftime(11)+strptime fuzzers+clippy green.

title: wordexp: bash-only ${} operators silently accepted instead of WRDE_SYNTAX; ${var:?} drops value
description: fl wordexp's expand_braced_param (core stdlib/wordexp.rs) had a catch-all _ arm that looked up the whole ${} body as a variable name, so bash-only operators glibc rejects with WRDE_SYNTAX(5) were silently accepted as rc=0 empty: substring ${var:off}/${var:off:len}, pattern subst ${var/p/r}//, case ${var^^}/${var,,}/${var^}, transform ${var@U}, subscript ${var[i]}, and dangling ${var:}. Also ${var:?}/${var?} returned empty even when the var was SET (looked up wrong key) — glibc yields the value. Probed vs live glibc. Fix: add ExpandError::Syntax (->WRDE_SYNTAX in both abi expand paths), add proper ? handling (value when set, empty when unset — glibc does not abort), and reject any other operator after a real name. Out of scope (documented): empty-name/special-param forms ${@}/${*}/${0}/${!var}/${#} (positional/process params fl does not model) and arithmetic $((expr)) (unimplemented, rc 4). NEW conformance_diff_wordexp_operators.rs.
close_reason: Fixed (03fc0e4e): expand_braced_param now returns ExpandError::Syntax (->WRDE_SYNTAX) for bash-only operators after a real name (substring :off[:len], subst /p/r //, case ^^/,,/^, transform @U, subscript [i], dangling :), and handles ?/:? correctly (value when set, empty when unset). Mapped Syntax in both core + split-mask abi expand paths. Matches glibc across operator matrix. Out of scope (documented): empty-name/special-param forms (${@}/${0}/${!var}/${#}) + arithmetic $((expr)). NEW conformance_diff_wordexp_operators.rs; core wordexp(20)+abi wordexp fuzzer/probe/conformance+clippy green.

title: scanf: GNU m alloc modifier (%ms/%m[/%mc) unimplemented; narrow %Nc fails when width>input
description: Two scanf gaps found by differential probing vs live glibc. (1) GNU 'm' assignment-allocation modifier (%ms, %m[...], %mc) was unimplemented: the scanf spec parser only recognized h/l/j/z/t/L length mods, so 'm' was read as the conversion char and the whole sscanf failed (ret 0). glibc allocates a buffer and stores char* in the caller's char**. (2) narrow %Nc required the FULL width to be present and failed otherwise (e.g. %5c on 'ab' -> ret 0), whereas glibc reads what IS available and succeeds (the wide/%lc path already did this correctly, citing glibc). Fix: core scanf parses 'm' -> ScanSpec.alloc; ABI String/Char write arms malloc(len+1 / len) + store char** when alloc (NUL for %ms/%m[, none for %mc); narrow scan_char reads min(width,available). NEW conformance_diff_scanf_malloc.rs. Follow-up: wide %mls content is narrow-encoded (same pre-existing %ls limitation in the write path).

(2) narrow %Nc now reads min(width,available) like glibc + the wide path (was failing when width>input, e.g. %5c on 'ab'). title: strftime %z hardcodes +0000 ignoring tm_gmtoff (glibc formats the field)
description: fl strftime %z emitted a hardcoded '+0000' regardless of the broken-down time's tm_gmtoff. glibc formats %z as +/-HHMM from tm_gmtoff (seconds east of UTC), honoring whatever set it — localtime, strptime %z, or the caller. So strptime('+0530','%z') then strftime('%z') roundtrips '+0530' in glibc but gave '+0000' in fl; probed offsets 19800->+0530, -28800->-0800, -1800->-0030, 34200->+0930, 900->+0015 all diverged. Fix: added BrokenDownTime.tm_gmtoff (i64), populated in read_tm from libc::tm, formatted in core %z. fl gmtime/localtime still produce 0 (UTC) so the common case stays +0000. NEW conformance_diff_strftime_gmtoff.rs. OUT OF SCOPE (follow-up): %Z (timezone name) reads the opaque tm_zone pointer + has a process-TZ NULL-fallback fl (UTC-only, never derefs tm_zone) cannot match.
close_reason: Fixed (fd782829): strftime %z now formats +/-HHMM from tm_gmtoff like glibc (was hardcoded +0000). Added BrokenDownTime.tm_gmtoff, populated in read_tm, formatted in core %z. fl gmtime/localtime still produce 0 (UTC) so common case = +0000. NEW conformance_diff_strftime_gmtoff.rs (whole/half/quarter-hour/neg/sub-minute offsets). core time(42)+conformance_diff_time(12)/wcsftime(11)+strftime fuzzers+clippy green. Out of scope: %Z timezone name (opaque tm_zone deref + process-TZ NULL fallback, fl UTC-only).

title: strftime %Z hardcodes GMT — ignores tm_zone; diverges for localtime/explicit/null-fallback
description: fl strftime %Z always emits 'GMT'. glibc rule (probed, TZ=UTC): echo tm_zone when non-NULL, else process tzname[isdst]. Ground truth: glibc gmtime sets tm_zone='GMT' (%Z='GMT'); localtime(UTC) sets tm_zone='UTC' (%Z='UTC'); zeroed/NULL tm_zone -> tzname -> 'UTC' under TZ=UTC; caller-set tm_zone='PST' -> %Z='PST'. fl's write_tm sets tm_zone='UTC' for ALL (gmtime+localtime), so fl's tm_zone field ALSO diverges (gmtime should be 'GMT'). Current hardcoded 'GMT' MATCHES glibc only for the gmtime->%Z common case; diverges for localtime, explicit tm_zone, and the NULL fallback. COHERENT FIX (multi-part, deferred): (1) add owned zone to core BrokenDownTime (inline [u8;N]); (2) ABI read_tm derefs caller tm_zone (REVERSES the deliberate never-deref-tm_zone safety stance, time_abi.rs ~768 — acceptable for ABI compat, glibc derefs it); (3) core %Z echoes zone if set else 'UTC' (fl UTC-only world, NOT process TZ); (4) fl gmtime sets tm_zone='GMT', localtime keeps 'UTC'; (5) update core test mod.rs:1151 (asserts %Z='GMT' for zoneless bd -> would become 'UTC'). NULL-fallback under non-UTC TZ stays unmatchable (no tzdb). Companion to strftime %z fix fd782829 (bd-2g7oyh.302) which added tm_gmtoff.
close_reason: Fixed (98f94082): strftime %Z echoes tm_zone (was hardcoded GMT), else UTC fallback; gmtime labels GMT, localtime UTC; tm_zone deref scoped to strftime only (read_tm stays zone-agnostic for mktime safety). NEW conformance_diff_strftime_zone.rs. Out of scope: process-zone fallback under non-UTC TZ (no tzdb).

title: printf %p ignores 0/+/space flags (glibc renders non-NULL pointer like %#x)
description: fl printf %p honoured only width + left-justify, ignoring the 0 (zero-pad), + and space flags. glibc renders a non-NULL pointer like %#x of its value: 0/precision/# apply, AND (unlike real %x) the +/space sign flags prepend +/space. Probed: %020p of 0x1234 -> glibc 0x000000000000001234 (fl space-padded), %+p -> +0x1234 (fl 0x1234), % p -> ' 0x1234', %+.5p -> +0x01234. NULL -> '(nil)' (string, width/justify only) was already correct. Fix: (1) widen the 'p' flag_mask from 0b00001 (only -) to 0b11111 in tools/stdio_synth/src/lib.rs (source) + regenerated printf_tables.rs snapshot; (2) format_pointer non-NULL now delegates the 0x-body to format_unsigned (alt-form x spec) and places the +/space sign + field padding around it (sign at front for zero-pad, after spaces for space-pad). NEW conformance_diff_printf_pointer.rs.
close_reason: Fixed (88858b77): %p now honours 0/+/space flags like glibc (%#x rendering of non-NULL pointer). Widened 'p' flag_mask 0b00001->0b11111 in stdio_synth source + regenerated printf_tables snapshot; format_pointer delegates 0x-body to format_unsigned + places +/space sign + field padding (sign front for zero-pad, after spaces for space-pad). NULL still '(nil)'. NEW conformance_diff_printf_pointer.rs (flag matrix incl NULL). core printf(50)+stdio_printf(11)+int/float/positional fuzzers+clippy green.

title: scanf hex-float: smallest subnormals underflow to 0 (2_f64.powi overflow)
description: scan_hex_float (core stdio/scanf.rs) scaled the significand with val *= 2_f64.powi(total_exp). For a large negative exponent powi computes 1.0/2^|exp|, and 2^1074 overflows to inf, so 1.0/inf = 0.0 -> the smallest subnormal double 0x1p-1074 (5e-324) wrongly parsed as 0.0 via sscanf('0x1p-1074','%lf'). glibc -> 5e-324. Probed: whole subnormal boundary diverged at the powi-overflow point. Fix: scale with libm::ldexp(significand as f64, total_exp) (== scalbn) which handles the full subnormal/overflow range with correct rounding; saturating exponent arithmetic. Verified bit-exact vs glibc across subnormal-boundary + half-way rounding (0x1p-1075->0, 0x3p-1075->min subnormal) + normal/specials. NEW conformance_diff_scanf_hexfloat.rs.
close_reason: Fixed (8f0dda24): scan_hex_float now scales with libm::ldexp instead of *2_f64.powi(exp) — powi computed 1/2^|exp| and 2^1074 overflowed to inf, so 0x1p-1074 (5e-324, smallest subnormal) underflowed to 0. ldexp handles full subnormal/overflow range with correct rounding; saturating exponent. Bit-exact vs glibc across subnormal boundary + half-way rounding + normal/specials. NEW conformance_diff_scanf_hexfloat.rs. core scanf(70)+scanf float fuzzers+clippy green.

title: strfmon: negative-zero sign handling diverges from glibc (won't-mirror candidate)
description: fl strfmon classifies -0.0 via value.is_sign_negative() (TRUE) -> full negative formatting; glibc classifies via value<0.0 (FALSE for -0.0) -> treats -0.0 as POSITIVE for parens/sign-positioning, but the '-' still appears because glibc renders the VALUE's own sign in the digit string. Observed (C locale): %(n of -0.0 -> fl '(0.00)' vs glibc '-0.00' (glibc: NO parens for -0.0); %#10.3n of -0.0 -> fl '-         0.000' (minus far-left) vs glibc '         -0.000' (minus adjacent to digit, after left-prec fill); %=*8n similar. Normal negatives (-1.0) match exactly. fl is internally CONSISTENT (-0.0 = negative everywhere); glibc's split (sign-bit for the minus, value<0 for parens/placement, with the minus living in the rendered magnitude not the sign slot) is subtle/borderline-inconsistent. Matching it requires render_value (core/locale/strfmon.rs ~160) to format_fixed the signed value for -0.0 and rework left-prec padding around the embedded minus — high-fiddliness for an astronomically rare edge. PROPOSED: document as glibc -0.0 quirk (won't-mirror, like ecvt bd-2g7oyh.101 / regex-anchor / remquo). Only -0.0 affected (7/216 probed strfmon flag×value combos).
close_reason: Fixed (d79ed524) — turned out cleanly fixable, NOT a won't-mirror quirk. glibc model: negative=value<0.0 (strict, -0.0 is positive for parens/placement) but the '-' is rendered from the value's own sign. Fix (core/locale/strfmon.rs render_value): negative=value<0.0; mag=format_fixed(if negative {value.abs()} else {value}) so -0.0 keeps its '-' (format! renders -0.0 as -0.00) and lands in the positive sign slot. All 7 prior -0.0 divergences (%(n no-parens, %#10.3n/%=*#8n placement) now match; normal +/- unchanged. NEW conformance_diff_strfmon_negzero.rs. core strfmon(4)+fuzzer(2)+clippy green.

title: gcvt: drops the sign of a negative NaN (returns 'nan' for -nan)
description: render_gcvt (core/stdlib/ecvt.rs ~232) unconditionally returned 'nan' for any NaN, dropping the sign bit — so gcvt(-nan,...) gave 'nan' vs glibc '-nan' (glibc's %g preserves the NaN sign). The adjacent is_infinite branch DID check the sign (-inf vs inf), but the NaN branch did not. printf %g of -nan was already correct (separate path); only gcvt's own renderer was wrong. ecvt/fcvt of -nan/specials are fine. Fix: mirror the inf branch — return '-nan' when value.is_sign_negative(). NEW conformance_diff_cvt_specials.rs (gcvt/ecvt/fcvt over nan/-nan/inf/-inf/-0.0 — values the random fuzzers don't generate).
close_reason: Fixed (c2509bbb): render_gcvt NaN branch now checks value.is_sign_negative() and returns '-nan' for negative NaN, mirroring the inf branch and glibc's %g. Was unconditionally 'nan'. printf %g + ecvt/fcvt already correct. NEW conformance_diff_cvt_specials.rs (gcvt/ecvt/fcvt × nan/-nan/inf/-inf/-0.0). core ecvt(9)+gcvt fuzzer(1)+clippy green.

title: printf: NULL %s with precision<6 truncates '(null)' instead of printing empty
description: fl printf substitutes '(null)' for a NULL %s/%ls arg then runs it through the precision-truncation path, so %.3s of NULL gave '(nu' and %5.3s gave '  (nu'. glibc substitutes '(null)' ONLY when precision is unspecified or >= 6 (the length of '(null)'); a smaller precision yields the EMPTY string (%.3s of NULL -> '', %5.3s -> '     ', %-8.2s -> 8 spaces). Found by probing NULL %s with a precision/width matrix vs live glibc (5/21 combos diverged: %.3s %.4s %5.3s %-8.2s %.3ls). Fix (stdio_abi.rs ~3404): when precision is Fixed(p) and p < 6, substitute b"" instead of b"(null)". NEW conformance_diff_printf_null_string.rs.
close_reason: Fixed (65b972df): NULL %s/%ls now substitutes empty string instead of '(null)' when precision is Fixed(p) with p<6, matching glibc (which uses '(null)' only when precision unspecified or >=6). %.3s of NULL was '(nu' -> now ''; %5.3s '  (nu' -> '     '. NEW conformance_diff_printf_null_string.rs. stdio_printf(11)+positional/wide-string+core printf fuzzers+clippy green.

title: strftime: %E%/%O% renders literal instead of glibc's literal-percent
description: fl strftime's E/O-modifiable tables (core/time/mod.rs ~386) included the format-control specifiers n and t (so %En->newline, %Et->tab) but NOT % — so %E%/%O% rendered the literal '%E%'/'%O%' instead of glibc's '%' (the E/O modifier applied to the % conversion = literal percent, like %En->newline). Also fixed %E%Y etc. (was '%E%Y', now '%Y'). Found by probing malformed/edge strftime format strings vs live glibc. Fix: add '%' to E_MODIFIABLE and O_MODIFIABLE. NEW conformance_diff_strftime_eo_modifier.rs. NOTE: 2 remaining edge divergences NOT addressed: (1) %s of a tm uses local mktime in glibc vs fl's UTC-only timegm (documented TZ-scope limitation, no tzdb); (2) %9 / %9% (a field width with no following conversion or before %%) -> glibc width-pads the literal ('%9'->'       %9') = a glibc quirk fl renders the literal instead.
close_reason: Fixed (ff3803e2): added '%' to E_MODIFIABLE/O_MODIFIABLE tables (core/time/mod.rs ~386) so %E%/%O% render '%' like glibc (the E/O modifier applied to the % conversion), matching the existing %En->newline/%Et->tab handling. Also fixes %E%Y->'%Y'. NEW conformance_diff_strftime_eo_modifier.rs (modifier x specifier matrix). NOT addressed (documented in bead): %s local-mktime TZ limitation + %9 glibc width-pads-literal quirk. core time(42)+conformance_diff_time(12)/wcsftime(11)+strftime fuzzer+clippy green.

title: [parity][tsearch] twalk level/shape differs from glibc (fl LLRB vs glibc red-black tree)
description: fl backs tsearch with a balanced left-leaning red-black tree (frankenlibc-core search/rb_tree.rs); glibc uses a classic parent-pointer red-black tree. For the same insertion order the two build different (both valid) trees, so twalk reports different `level` (depth) values and a different leaf-vs-internal classification. POSIX leaves tree SHAPE unspecified, so this is conformant, but it is an observable divergence (programs that indent by twalk level see different output). Empirically (zz_probe_twalk.rs): insert 1..7 -> glibc root=2 (skewed), fl root=4 (balanced); the in-order KEY sequence is identical on both. SET/ORDER parity (insert/find/delete/in-order walk) is now PINNED by conformance_diff_tsearch.rs (curated + 400 random scripts, 0 div). To MIRROR glibc's exact level/shape would require reimplementing glibc misc/tsearch.c's specific RB insert+delete rebalancing bit-for-bit (multi-hour, parity-risky). Decision pending: document-as-conformant-divergence (like ecvt rounding bd-2g7oyh.101) vs deep glibc-RB-shape mirror. Probe: crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/zz_probe_twalk.rs
close_reason: Resolved as documented CONFORMANT DIVERGENCE (POSIX leaves tsearch tree shape unspecified; fl balanced LLRB vs glibc parent-pointer RB → different twalk level/leaf-classification, both valid). Same disposition as ecvt bd-2g7oyh.101. Observable set/order contract already byte-exact (conformance_diff_tsearch). Documented at twalk impl + added fl-only shape regression pin tsearch_twalk_shape_pin (commit ecc54237a). A bit-for-bit glibc-RB mirror is multi-hour + parity-risky for a POSIX-unspecified detail → NOT done by design.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: RECOMMENDATION (cc): resolve as DOCUMENTED CONFORMANT DIVERGENCE, same precedent as ecvt rounding (bd-2g7oyh.101). Rationale: (1) POSIX explicitly leaves tsearch tree SHAPE unspecified — fl's balanced LLRB is fully conformant, NOT a bug. (2) The observable SET/ORDER contract (insert/find/delete/in-order key sequence) is already byte-exact vs glibc and PINNED by conformance_diff_tsearch (curated + 400 random scripts, 0 div). (3) The ONLY divergence is twalk's level (depth) + leaf-vs-internal classification, which depends on the unspecified shape and is rarely consumed by real programs. (4) Mirroring glibc requires a bit-for-bit reimplementation of misc/tsearch.c's specific RB insert+delete rebalancing — multi-hour and parity-RISKY (could regress the already-perfect set/order parity), for ~zero EV. Net: NOT worth a structural rewrite of a correct, conformant, well-tested tree to chase an unspecified-by-POSIX shape detail. Suggest closing as wontfix/by-design with this note (owner call).

title: perf(qsort): 8-byte i64 natural fast lane (Score 2.5-4.8x within lane window)
close_reason: Implemented width==8 i64 natural fast lane in stdlib/sort.rs mirroring the existing i32 lane. qsort with int64/pointer keys is the dominant 8-byte case; previously it drove pdqsort_recurse through O(n log n) indirect comparator FFI callbacks. The lane sorts raw i64 via std sort_unstable (no per-cmp callback) + a single O(n) verify against the caller's comparator, committing only if the arrangement is genuinely non-decreasing. Parity-safe by construction: u64/descending/float/struct comparators fail verify -> original bytes restored -> generic fallback (zero behavioral diff). For accepted comparators the output bytes are fully determined (sorted i64; equal keys byte-identical regardless of tie order) so output is bit-identical to glibc. title: perf(qsort): LSD radix lane for large integer arrays (Score 3.0-5.7x, N>2048)
close_reason: Added an LSD radix lane for large 4-/8-byte integer arrays (num>2048) in stdlib/sort.rs. Above the comparison fast-lane window the generic pdqsort pays an indirect comparator call per comparison and LOST to glibc's cache-friendly mergesort at large N (baseline Score gl/fl: n=4096 i32 1.17/i64 1.08; n=65536 1.15/1.12; n=262144 i32 0.96/i64 0.97 — fl SLOWER). Radix is a different complexity class: O(n*key_bytes) linear counting passes, no per-element comparison. Maps each key to an order-preserving unsigned rank by flipping the sign bit (two's-complement -> unsigned byte order), LSD 8-bit-digit sort with ping-pong aux buffer + constant-digit pass skip, writes back original integer bytes. Parity-safe by the same verify-then-commit contract as the i32/i64 comparison lanes: committed only if the result is non-decreasing under the caller's comparator; unsigned/descending/float/struct comparators fail the single O(n) verify -> original bytes restored -> generic pdqsort fallback, zero behavioral diff. Natural-int comparators yield output bit-identical to glibc (equal keys byte-identical -> tie order immaterial). PROOF: NEW conformance_diff_qsort_radix.rs proves byte-identical-to-glibc across n in {2047,2048,2049,3000,4096,16384,65537} x 7 distributions (rand/dups/equal/sorted/reverse/smallpos/mixedsign) x {i32,u32,desc32,i64,u64,desc64} comparators; golden sha256 58476694b71197edca053aa5005549084f0d7be5046ac029697565bbfaac4127. BENCH (local, glibc qsort oracle): Score(gl/fl) n=4096 i32 1.17->4.36 i64 1.08->4.40; n=16384 1.07->5.66 / 1.18->4.72; n=65536 1.15->4.46 / 1.12->4.24; n=262144 0.96->3.01 / 0.97->3.02. Core sort unit 31 green; full core lib 3079 (3 unrelated glob error-callback tests flaky under parallel suite, pass 23/23 in isolation); prior i64 fast-lane gate + stdlib_abi qsort green.

title: perf(qsort): extend radix lane to 2-byte (i16/u16) keys (Score 3.6-8.5x)
close_reason: Extended the integer radix lane (sort.rs) to 2-byte (i16/u16) keys with a low threshold (NARROW_RADIX_LANE_MIN=256). 2-byte keys had NO fast lane (only width 4/8 did) → always pdqsort, which loses to a 2-pass LSD radix because 16-bit keys have 65536 distinct values (pdqsort's equal-block partition gives little help, unlike bytes). The existing try_qsort_integer_radix_lane/radix_sort_u64_lsd already generalize over width; only the dispatch guard + threshold + debug_assert changed. Same verify-then-commit parity contract: committed only if non-decreasing under caller cmp; u16/descending/non-natural fail O(n) verify → restore original → pdqsort fallback. title: perf(qsort): dedicated 1-byte counting-sort lane (Score 34-169x)
close_reason: Added a dedicated 1-byte counting-sort lane to stdlib/sort.rs (try_qsort_u8_counting_lane, num>256). Closes the width-1 follow-up from bd-2g7oyh.348: the GENERIC u64-widening radix REGRESSED bytes (8x memory traffic), so width 1 had been left on pdqsort. A counting sort is the right complexity class for bytes: one 256-bucket histogram pass + one memset run per distinct value = O(n+256), no key widening, no per-element comparison. Same verify-then-commit parity as the other lanes: materialise unsigned-ascending order and verify non-decreasing under the caller's comparator; on failure re-emit signed-ascending (0x80..=0xFF first, the signed-char case) and verify; if neither holds, restore the saved original bytes and fall back to pdqsort (so even exotic comparators stay byte-identical to glibc). Equal-comparing bytes are identical bytes → tie order immaterial → committed output bit-identical to glibc. PROOF: NEW conformance_diff_qsort_count8.rs byte-identical-to-glibc across n∈{255,256,257,512,1024,4096,65537} × 7 dists (rand/dups4/equal/sorted/reverse/signedish/twoval) × {u8,i8,desc}; golden sha256 d921063982f5f15c80b8cc02a19e9f32ab897de8ad113a0f1c7076c3ae95b946. title: [parity] ecvt/fcvt nan/inf sign convention divergence vs glibc

Verified vs host glibc 2.38 C probes on {nan,-nan,inf,-inf} for ecvt/fcvt/ecvt_r/fcvt_r. New pinned core unit test + ABI integration test. title: getopt: implement W; extension (-W foo == --foo)
description:
fl getopt_long does NOT implement the GNU 'W;' optstring extension: when the optstring contains a char followed by ';' (conventionally "W;"), '-W foo' / '-Wfoo' must be processed as the long option '--foo' (with =value handling). glibc routes -W's argument through long-option matching.

Differential probe vs host glibc (in-process, optind=0 reset, struct option {verbose=v,file(req)=f,color(opt)=c,help=h}):
  optstr="W;ab:"  -W file x      host=[('f',"x",optind4)] -1   fl=[('W',"",2)] -1
  optstr="W;ab:"  -Wfile=q       host=[('f',"q",2)] -1        fl=[('W',"",1),('?'×6 garbage),...]
  optstr="W;ab:"  -W verbose     host=[('v',"",3)] -1         fl=[('W',"",2)] -1

Everything else in getopt_long is CLEAN vs glibc (verified same probe): permutation, +/- prefix (with optind=0 full reset), -- terminator, clustered short, optional args ::, abbreviated long opts, ambiguous-prefix '?', unknown short/long '?', missing-arg ':'/'?', optopt on error returns.

Impl notes: fl getopt is a faithful glibc PERMUTE-engine port (unistd_abi.rs getopt_internal + core getopt::step_short/getopt_arg_mode). W; needs (1) getopt_arg_mode/step_short to treat 'X;' as required-arg so -W consumes its operand, and (2) a getopt_try_long variant that matches a NAME STRING (not an argv position) so -W's arg can be dispatched as --name. Risk: touches well-tested core; needs full getopt regression. Repro harness: tests/zz_probe_getopt_long.rs (untracked).

POSIX note: 'W;' is a GNU extension; obscure but real glibc behavior. Parity gap, low priority.

title: significand/significandf omit FE_INVALID on 0/inf/NaN (glibc raises it via internal ilogb)
description: Differential probe (zz_probe_modf_signif_flags.rs) vs host glibc 2.42: significand(0)/significand(inf)/significand(NaN) and the f32 significandf return the correct VALUE (0/inf/nan respectively) but raise NO FP exception, whereas glibc raises FE_INVALID for all three (glibc significand = scalbn(x,-ilogb(x)); ilogb(0/inf/nan) raises FE_INVALID, which propagates). Normal finite-nonzero values match glibc exactly (value+flags). modf/modff are CLEAN (no divergence). This is the MISSING-flag direction (opposite of the spurious-FE_INEXACT rounding vein just fixed: roundeven 62fdb0887, round/roundf 17a315ebb, lround 8c7793e53, nearbyint 44fff8ce5). LOW VALUE (obsolete SVID fn, edge inputs only) but a real parity gap. FIX: in significand/significandf wrappers (math_abi.rs), raise FE_INVALID when the input is 0/inf/NaN (e.g. force_eval 0.0/0.0 on the cold path, like the fromfp family) before returning. NOTE: math_abi.rs was under an active BoldFalcon file reservation when found — land when free. Probe left at crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/zz_probe_modf_signif_flags.rs.

title: [perf][no-gaps] qsort: pattern-defeating quicksort (pdqsort) replaces median-of-3 introsort
description: Replace the median-of-three Lomuto introsort (insertion-sort fallback on deep recursion = O(n^2) worst case) with a full pattern-defeating quicksort (Orson Peters pdqsort) ported to byte-chunk + comparator callback in 100% safe Rust. Adds: sorted-run detection (partial insertion sort), equal-block collapse for low-cardinality keys, deterministic pattern-breaking shuffles, and a heapsort fallback guaranteeing O(n log n) worst case. Behavior parity absolute (unstable sort, same multiset/order as glibc qsort). Bench (library-equivalent monomorphized comparator) vs old: all_equal 14-39x, sorted 4-15x, reverse 5-18x, low_card 3.5-7x, duplicate-heavy 1.7-2.9x; random par-to-1.76x with realistic comparators. Comparisons strictly fewer (template n=10k 271809->81504), swaps ~half.
