title: bd-66wz subtask: Pointer validation adversarial pipeline tests (free/UAF/canary/foreign)
description:
Background
- The `ValidationPipeline` is the TSM enforcement surface: its outcomes drive Allow/Repair/Deny decisions in libc entrypoints.
- We need direct adversarial regression tests proving the pipeline never returns permissive abstractions for non-live pointers, even when caches and heuristics are involved.

Scope
- Expand unit tests in `crates/frankenlibc-membrane/src/ptr_validator.rs` (and, where appropriate, `arena.rs` / `fingerprint.rs`) to cover adversarial sequences and edge outcomes.
- Prefer testing via `ValidationPipeline::{allocate, free, validate}` instead of reaching into `arena` directly, so the page-oracle/bloom/TLS-cache integration is exercised.

Required Adversarial Cases
1) Foreign pointer validate: returns `Foreign(_)`, and must never claim bounded Valid/Writable remaining-bytes.
2) Foreign free: `ValidationPipeline::free()` must return `FreeResult::ForeignPointer` (and must not crash).
3) Double free: first free => `Freed` (or `FreedWithCanaryCorruption` if provoked); second free => `DoubleFree`.
4) UAF via generation: after free, `validate(addr)` must not yield `CachedValid(_)` and must yield a restrictive outcome (`TemporalViolation` or non-readable).
5) Canary corruption path: corrupt trailing canary; free returns `FreedWithCanaryCorruption`; subsequent validate for addr must remain non-readable/non-writable.
6) Cache interaction: populate TLS cache with a valid pointer; free it; validate again must miss cache and must not return a live abstraction.

Safety/Lattice Assertions
- For each case above, assert `can_read/can_write` matches expectation and that the extracted `PointerAbstraction` state is not `Valid/Writable` for freed/quarantined pointers.

Acceptance
- New tests added to `crates/frankenlibc-membrane/src/ptr_validator.rs` are deterministic, fast, and produce helpful failure context (case_id, sequence step).
- No new unsafe code outside the existing test intentional-overflow blocks.

Notes
- This bead is test-first: if a test fails, fix the pipeline/arena behavior with the smallest correct change and add a regression assertion.

title: bd-66wz subtask: Deterministic property/invariant tests for allocator+membrane state transitions
description:
Background
- Unit tests cover specific sequences; we also need broad invariant pressure over many sequences to catch edge transitions (especially around cache invalidation and quarantine accounting).
- We require determinism (replayable seeds) and short runtime so these can run in CI on every change.

Scope
- Add deterministic property-style tests (no external RNG dependency required) for allocator+membrane state transitions.
- Prefer a tiny local PRNG (e.g. xorshift64*) with fixed seeds so failures are reproducible without environment variables.

Invariant Set (examples; encode as named invariants in assertions)
1) No stale-permissive cache: after any operation that frees an allocation, subsequent `validate(addr)` must not return `CachedValid(_)` for that addr unless a new allocation was performed and revalidated.
2) Quarantine accounting soundness: quarantine_bytes and entry counts never go negative; bounded by max constraints after drain.
3) Temporal safety while tracked: if an allocation has been freed and is still tracked in quarantine/arena, `can_read/can_write` for that addr is false.
4) Determinism: given the same seed and step count, the sequence of operations and observed outcomes is identical.

Test Plan
- Generate N sequences across a small set of fixed seeds.
- Each step randomly chooses: allocate(size), free(ptr), validate(ptr), corrupt_canary(ptr) (guarded by ptr live), etc.
- Track a simple shadow model for expected permissiveness (live vs freed-tracked vs foreign) and assert pipeline outcomes respect it.

Acceptance
- Property/invariant tests live in `crates/frankenlibc-membrane` (module choice: `arena.rs`/`ptr_validator.rs`/new `tests/` module) and run under `cargo test -p frankenlibc-membrane`.
- Runtime is bounded and deterministic (<2s total locally).
- On failure, output includes: seed, step index, op, ptr addr, expected class, actual outcome.

Notes
- If adding a crate like `proptest` is considered later, keep this deterministic harness as the baseline (proptest can be an additive layer, not a replacement).

title: wordexp $((...)) arithmetic: assignment (= += etc), increment (++/--), and comma operators unsupported (glibc supports them)
design: Follow-up to bd-yb9f9r. core::stdlib::wordexp::eval_arith handles the full operator/precedence/short-circuit/ternary set but NOT: assignment (= *= /= %= += -= <<= >>= &= ^= |=), pre/post increment/decrement (++x x++ --x x--), or the comma operator. arith_tokenize errors on bare '=' (returns Syntax). glibc's shell arithmetic engine supports all of these, so e.g. $(( x = 5 )) -> 5, $(( x=5, x*2 )) -> 10, $(( x=3, ++x )) -> 4 in glibc but WRDE_SYNTAX in fl. In wordexp the assignments don't persist (subshell) so they're rarely useful, but they're valid POSIX arithmetic. Fix: add ATok::Assign/Comma/PlusPlus/MinusMinus to the tokenizer; thread a mutable HashMap<String,i64> through arith_eval for assignment lvalues (seeded lazily from lookup on first read); comma as the lowest-precedence binary (eval both, return right); pre/post inc-dec as unary on an lvalue. Common integer arithmetic (already shipped) is unaffected. Found via self-audit of the new evaluator.
close_reason: Refuted by live glibc 2.42: wordexp arithmetic has NO assignment/increment/comma, so implementing this bead would have created a divergence. Closed with 22 refutation arms that fail if anyone implements it. The measurement also exposed a real defect in the opposite direction -- the arithmetic body was not being parameter-expanded -- which is fixed in unistd_abi.rs + core wordexp.rs and gated (4 passed on vmi1152480, red before the fix).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
PREMISE REFUTED BY LIVE MEASUREMENT, and a REAL divergence found in the opposite direction. Fixed and gated; bead closed as refuted-plus-fixed.

WHAT THE BEAD ASKED FOR IS A DIVERGENCE. It says glibc supports assignment/increment/comma in wordexp arithmetic, citing $((x = 5)) -> 5, $((x=5, x*2)) -> 10, $((x=3, ++x)) -> 4. Probed against LIVE glibc 2.42 (ctypes wordexp oracle, flags=0):
  $(( x = 5 ))      rc=5 WRDE_SYNTAX      (bead expected 5)
  $(( x=5, x*2 ))   rc=5 WRDE_SYNTAX      (bead expected 10)
  $(( x=3, ++x ))   rc=5 WRDE_SYNTAX      (bead expected 4)
  $(( ++x ))/$((x++))/$((x+=2))  all rc=5
  $(( 1, 2 ))       rc=0 -> '1'           (comma is a STOP, not an operator; an implementation would answer 2)
Implementing this bead would have broken parity, not fixed it. fl already matched glibc on all of it.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY BROKEN. Building the refutation arms exposed a live defect the gate had no arm for: glibc expands the arithmetic BODY before parsing it, so with FLARITH=41 exported, $(($FLARITH+1)) is '42' -- fl returned WRDE_SYNTAX. Same class: $(()) and $(($UNSET)) are '0' in glibc, fl errored. Both halves now fixed:
  - crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs: the $(( )) branch of expand_vars_with_split_mask_dyn recurses through the same expander on the body before eval_arith (so parameter expansion, ${#NAME}, ${NAME:-word} and nested $(( )) all work inside arithmetic, while backslash/quotes keep a name away from the parser, exactly as measured).
  - crates/frankenlibc-core/src/stdlib/wordexp.rs: same in the core copy, plus eval_arith('') -> 0, because glibc's empty-body rule is LENGTH, not content: $(()) is 0 but $(( )) is WRDE_SYNTAX, and $(($UNSET)) is 0 but $(( $UNSET )) is WRDE_SYNTAX.

GATE. conformance_diff_wordexp_arith gains 22 refutation arms, a 32-word env-driven differential (ENV_WORDS) and two named tests: wordexp_arithmetic_has_no_assignment_increment_or_comma_operator (asserts the ORACLE rejects each form first, so it cannot pass by both sides being broken; this is what fails if anyone implements this bead) and wordexp_arithmetic_expands_its_body_but_has_no_parser_variables (collects all mismatches instead of stopping at the first). All four tests are serialised under one lock because the env-driven half sets variables and wordexp reads environ. OBSERVED: 'test result: ok. 4 passed; 0 failed' on RCH worker vmi1152480 -- and the same file FAILED before the fix with 'fl=(rc=5, []) glibc=(rc=0, ["42"])'. Neighbours green after the fix: conformance_diff_wordexp 2, _operators 1, _tilde 1, wordexp_differential_fuzz 1, wordexp_differential_probe 1 (vmi1153651); frankenlibc-core stdlib::wordexp 20 passed (vmi1227854).

NOT FIXED, out of scope, separate defect: fl refuses ALL command substitution with WRDE_CMDSUB even without WRDE_NOCMD, so $(($(echo 41)+1)) is CMDSUB where glibc gives '42'. That is the unimplemented-cmdsub gap, not an arithmetic gap; no arm was added for it here so this gate stays honest about what it covers.

title: closefrom silently no-ops on kernels <5.9 (close_range ENOSYS discarded, no fallback)
close_reason:
Fixed in f6a87baae. closefrom was one line that discarded the close_range result: 'let _ = syscall::sys_close_range(lowfd as u32, !0u32, 0);'. TWO silent defects, both defeating the only thing closefrom exists to do (keep descriptors from surviving an exec).

DEFECT 1 (the filed one): no fallback. close_range needs kernel 5.9+ and can also be denied by seccomp; on any such system closefrom left EVERY descriptor open and returned normally. Now follows glibc's chain: close_range -> walk /proc/self/fd closing each fd >= lowfd -> (no /proc, e.g. chroot/minimal container) sweep up to the soft RLIMIT_NOFILE.

DEFECT 2 (found while fixing 1, not filed): 'lowfd as u32' on a NEGATIVE lowfd. closefrom(-1) asked close_range to start near 2^32 and therefore closed NOTHING -- the exact inverse of the contract. MEASURED against live glibc 2.42 by ctypes probe, each case in its own subprocess reporting via exit code because closefrom can close the probe's own stdout:
  closefrom(50)  -> marker fd 100 CLOSED, stdout open
  closefrom(200) -> marker open, stdout open
  closefrom(0)   -> everything closed
  closefrom(-1)  -> everything closed  (glibc clamps to 0; MAX(0,lowfd) in its source)
Now clamps with lowfd.max(0).

WHY THE EXISTING GATE MISSED BOTH: conformance_diff_closefrom.rs only exercised the close_range fast path, which succeeds on every machine able to run the suite, so the discarded-result bug was invisible. Its doc comment even asserted that 'the older-kernel brute-force fallback the fix added shares the same observable contract' -- describing a fallback that did not exist in the code. That claim is now true and gated instead of asserted.

EVIDENCE (remote via RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2, -j2, CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/tmp/rch_target_frankenlibc_greenglen):
  cargo test -j2 -p frankenlibc-abi --test conformance_diff_closefrom -> 5 passed; 0 failed.

GATE: the two fallbacks are now driven DIRECTLY (made pub for exactly that reason, with a doc comment saying so) rather than assumed equivalent -- otherwise they are dead code under test on any modern kernel. Arms: close_range path (pre-existing), proc fallback, rlimit fallback, negative lowfd, and a no-op control at lowfd=200 above everything open so 'closes fds >= lowfd' is measured rather than 'closes fds'. All run inside forked children reporting by exit code, since the fds under test include the ones stdio needs.

NEGATIVE CASE (proved, and each failure attributable to its own probe): restoring 'lowfd as u32' failed ONLY closefrom_negative_lowfd_closes_everything_like_glibc; making the /proc walk iterate without closing failed ONLY closefrom_proc_fallback_closes_the_same_fds_as_close_range; the rlimit fallback and the no-op control stayed GREEN. Critically the PRE-EXISTING arm closefrom_closes_fds_at_or_above_lowfd stayed GREEN under both probes, which is the direct demonstration of why this defect shipped. Probes then removed; grep over crates/ confirms none remain.

GATES: rustfmt --edition 2024 on both touched files: clean. clippy -p frankenlibc-abi --all-targets -D warnings: zero findings in either touched file.

NO REGRESSION: cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test unistd_abi_test -> 535 passed / 5 failed, identical to the clean-HEAD baseline measured this session (rch exec --base HEAD --clean-overlay --no-overlay: 535/5, same five names, all environmental or flaky as recorded on bd-566mlx).

IMPLEMENTATION NOTE: the fallback uses raw syscalls (sys_openat / sys_getdents64 / sys_close / sys_getrlimit) and parses linux_dirent64 by offset rather than going through std::fs, which would re-enter libc and risk the interposed-symbol recursion hazard. source_commit=34c7203e6 -> f6a87baae. Unrelated working-tree changes by other agents were not reverted or disturbed.

title: Add system environment fingerprint helper for live runner anchoring
description:
Background: bd-juvqm.3 (commit 1ae4d464) and bd-8b70o (commit f9776a42) require an `environment_fingerprint` string in every LiveMeasurementRow. Today every caller has to invent that string, leading to cross-run drift. The env fingerprint is the anchoring field that lets a downstream comparison decide whether two p99 measurements are even comparable.

Deliverables:
1. Add `frankenlibc_harness::system_fingerprint::environment_fingerprint() -> String` returning a stable fingerprint of the form `linux-<arch>-<cpus>cpu-<kernel>` derived deterministically from `/proc/cpuinfo`, `/proc/sys/kernel/osrelease`, and `uname -m`-equivalent data.
2. Add `EnvironmentFingerprintComponents { os: String, arch: String, cpus: u32, kernel_release: String }` so callers can decompose the string for diff reports.
3. Provide a `from_components(&Components) -> String` round-trip so tests can assert the canonical formatting.
4. Add a fail-closed `validate_environment_fingerprint(&str) -> Result<EnvironmentFingerprintComponents, EnvFingerprintError>` parser.
5. Optional override via `FRANKENLIBC_ENV_FINGERPRINT` env var (similar to bd-qfbhc's asupersync override pattern) so CI can pin a known-stable string.
6. New conformance manifest `tests/conformance/system_environment_fingerprint_contract.v1.json` pinning the format, the override env var, and the rejected_evidence_kinds.
7. Harness test that exercises (a) a synthetic Components round-trip, (b) the env override, (c) a parser-rejection path.

Acceptance:
- `environment_fingerprint()` is deterministic for a fixed (env, fs) state.
- `FRANKENLIBC_ENV_FINGERPRINT=<custom>` short-circuits with that value.
- Parser rejects malformed strings with a precise error variant.
- Lib const + manifest enum match — drift fails closed.
- Harness runs via rch cargo test -p frankenlibc-harness.
- Closure evidence cites a sample fingerprint string + decomposed Components.

title: ffs-block: MemIoEngine lacks documented lock-order invariant (data → stats) and regression test
description:
Finding (via /deadlock-finder-and-fixer skill, NEW target): crates/ffs-block/src/io_engine.rs:247 has MemIoEngine = { data: Mutex<Vec<u8>>, stats: Mutex<IoEngineStats> }. submit_batch acquires data first (line 300), then stats inside the loop multiple times per op (line 301, 307, 319, 325, 337, 342). Stats is also acquired by stats() (line 355) and Debug fmt (line 293) WITHOUT holding data. The pattern is correct (data is the OUTER lock, stats is the INNER lock, never the reverse) but UNDOCUMENTED.

A future refactor that introduced a code path acquiring stats THEN data would create an AB-BA deadlock under contention. The Debug-fmt path takes only stats (safe); a refactor that added data-access to Debug-fmt would silently invert the order.

Pairs with bd-7zd94 (PersistentMvccStore lock-order), bd-bky2f (ShardedMvccStore), bd-pfv55 (FuseInodeLocks), bd-6owbg (FaultInjector + ThrottleInjector never-hold-both), bd-chmw4 (wal_writer atomic-rollback), bd-gqswx (commit_internal/rollback), bd-lebu5 (DurabilityNotifier invariants).

Acceptance: doc comment on MemIoEngine naming the data → stats lock-order invariant + the rule that any path holding both must acquire data FIRST. Plus a regression test that exercises high-contention concurrent submit_batch + stats() calls and asserts no deadlock + correct stats accumulation.
close_reason: done

title: [perf][lock-free] getenv read path: replace ENVIRON_LOCK mutex with a seqlock (1.71x miss)
description: getenv takes ENVIRON_LOCK (parking_lot mutex) per call to guard the environ-array walk against a concurrent setenv host_passthrough_realloc (UAF protection, stdlib_abi.rs native_getenv, 'REVIEW round 3'). That uncontended mutex CAS per call plus the membrane decide() make getenv ~1.71x slower than glibc on a miss (which walks all entries). glibc's getenv read path is lock-free. ALIEN-GRAVEYARD lever: a SEQLOCK — setenv (writer) increments a generation counter under the existing mutex around the realloc; getenv (reader) reads gen, walks environ, re-reads gen, and retries if it changed (Acquire/Release ordering). This makes the read path mutex-free while preserving the array-stability guarantee. The returned value pointer keeps the same POSIX 'may be overwritten by a later setenv' semantics as today. RISK: memory-ordering correctness + the realloc UAF window during a walk — needs a strong concurrent stress test (many reader threads + a setenv-spamming writer, under tsan/loom-style checking) and review by the environ-table owner (the lock has review history). NOT a rushed solo edit. Target: getenv 1.71x -> ~1.1x (residual = membrane decide, see bd-bp358k).

title: [HIGH] pthread_cond_init rejects a host-initialized pthread_condattr_t with EINVAL (2 tests deterministically fail)
description:
## Symptom

`cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test pthread_cond_core_test` has two deterministic failures:

```
test condvar_init_accepts_initialized_attr ... FAILED
test condvar_init_accepts_monotonic_attr_clock ... FAILED

thread 'condvar_init_accepts_initialized_attr' panicked at crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/pthread_cond_core_test.rs:86:9:
assertion `left == right` failed
  left: 22
 right: 0

thread 'condvar_init_accepts_monotonic_attr_clock' panicked at crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/pthread_cond_core_test.rs:107:9:
assertion `left == right` failed
  left: 22
 right: 0

test result: FAILED. 16 passed; 2 failed
```

rc=22 is EINVAL. Our `pthread_cond_init` is rejecting the `pthread_condattr_t` pointer with EINVAL where the test expects success (rc=0).

## Test bodies (authoritative — not me)

crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/pthread_cond_core_test.rs:80 (condvar_init_accepts_initialized_attr):
```rust
let mut attr: libc::pthread_condattr_t = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
assert_eq!(libc::pthread_condattr_init(&mut attr), 0);          // HOST libc init
assert_eq!(pthread_cond_init(cond, &attr), 0);                  // OURS — FAILS here, got 22
assert_eq!(pthread_cond_destroy(cond), 0);
assert_eq!(libc::pthread_condattr_destroy(&mut attr), 0);
```

crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/pthread_cond_core_test.rs:96 (condvar_init_accepts_monotonic_attr_clock): same pattern, plus libc::pthread_condattr_setclock(&mut attr, CLOCK_MONOTONIC).

## Diagnosis

The tests use HOST libc's `pthread_condattr_init` / `pthread_condattr_setclock` to populate `attr`, then pass that `attr` pointer to OUR `pthread_cond_init`. Our impl validates the incoming attr against its own expected layout / sentinel bytes and returns EINVAL because the host-initialized bytes don't match.

This is a cross-impl boundary question rather than a pure regression — the test fixture deliberately mixes host-initialized attrs with our cond_init because that is the real-world LD_PRELOAD pattern: user code links against host libc's condattr_init at compile time but our pthread_cond_init interposes at link time. If our cond_init rejects host-initialized condattrs in production, every real user program breaks under FRANKENLIBC_MODE=hardened.

## Fix direction

Two options:

1. **Relax validation**: treat any non-null `attr` pointer as acceptable, pull the clock / pshared via portable accessors (`pthread_condattr_getclock` / `getpshared`) instead of inspecting our own layout. This matches glibc's own behavior — glibc never rejects a validly-constructed condattr of either origin.
2. **Pass-through**: when the attr's layout doesn't match our internal format, fall through to host `pthread_cond_init` the same way bd-21ypi (138c07c3) routes non-native pthread_t handles. Consistent with the existing host-handoff pattern.

Option 1 is simpler; option 2 matches the existing architectural pattern for 'didn't originate in us'.

## Provenance

Found by cc-libc FULL REVIEW MODE at HEAD 6c0380b4 br-bd-qhnxc: dispatch host pthread cancellation. The bd-qhnxc fix unblocked pthread_abi_test, which let cargo test --workspace --all-targets get further than before and expose this second pthread-cluster failure. Fix commits previously landing on the condvar path: 2e1d65bc 'test(abi): expand pthread condvar core tests', d7b4a832 'expand pthread condvar and thread lifecycle test coverage' — so the tests are intentional coverage, not accidental.

## Blast radius

Two deterministic failures in crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/pthread_cond_core_test.rs. Blocks frankenlibc-abi integration-test suite from passing. Doesn't trip any SIGABRT or memory corruption.
close_reason: Accepted host-initialized pthread_condattr_t via host getclock fallback; workspace now advances to glibc_internal_abi_test allocator abort

title: ffs-block: FaultInjector + ThrottleInjector lack never-hold-both lock-ordering doc
description:
Finding (via /deadlock-finder-and-fixer skill, fourth visit,
different target): both `FaultInjector` and `ThrottleInjector`
(crates/ffs-block/src/lib.rs:4307, :4511) hold two `Mutex`es each
(`rules` + `log` for FaultInjector; `config` + `log` for
ThrottleInjector). Static audit confirms every callsite uses a
**never-hold-both** discipline:

  * `FaultInjector::check_fault` (l. 4367) acquires `rules`,
    explicitly drops it (`drop(rules)` on l. 4398), THEN acquires
    `log`. Never both held simultaneously.
  * `FaultInjector::reset` (l. 4360) acquires/releases `rules` and
    `log` sequentially.
  * `ThrottleInjector::apply_delay` (l. 4600) clones `config` from
    a brief `config.lock()` (released at end of expression), then
    later acquires `log.lock()` to push the record.
  * Both Debug impls acquire one Mutex per `.field()` call;
    successive `.field()` calls release their guards between calls.

There is NO function or doc currently holding both locks. But the
invariant is undocumented:

  1. **No struct-level doc comment** names the **never-hold-both**
     contract on either injector. A future contributor adding a
     "fail_and_log" combined function could nest `log.lock()` under
     `rules.lock()` and silently introduce a deadlock against any
     concurrent code path.
  2. **No regression test** exercises the lock acquisition paths
     under contention.

Same prevention pattern as bd-7zd94 (PersistentMvccStore),
bd-bky2f (ShardedMvccStore), bd-pfv55 (FuseInodeLocks). Difference:
those structs hold both locks (with a documented order); these
NEVER hold both — a stricter contract that's even easier to violate
silently.

Acceptance: doc blocks on both `FaultInjector` and `ThrottleInjector`
naming the **never-hold-both** invariant with rationale. Plus one
regression test per injector spawning concurrent fault/inject + log
+ reset workers with a watchdog timeout that catches any hang.
notes: Shipped: struct-level docs on FaultInjector + ThrottleInjector in crates/ffs-block/src/lib.rs naming the never-hold-both lock-ordering invariant (rules + log for FaultInjector; config + log for ThrottleInjector — neither lock is held while the other is acquired). Per-field doc on each Mutex annotates the constraint. Added two regression tests (fault_injector_concurrent_inject_and_reset_no_hang and throttle_injector_concurrent_apply_and_reset_no_hang) each spawning 4 concurrent workers (register/inject/log/reset) guarded by a 15s watchdog. Pairs with bd-7zd94 / bd-bky2f / bd-pfv55 (lock-order-fixed) — these are the stricter never-hold-both contract. Both tests pass in 0.05s via rch exec -- cargo test -p ffs-block --lib.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
GROUND TRUTH (measured, not recalled): live glibc 2.42 files-backed gethostbyname()
semantics, captured 2026-08-04 on thinkstation1 by bind-mounting synthetic /etc/hosts
files into a mount namespace and calling the host's own gethostbyname via ctypes:

  bwrap --dev-bind / / --bind <fake_hosts> /etc/hosts python3 ghbn_oracle.py <name>

/etc/host.conf on this host and on the Contabo workers has `multi on` (Debian default),
which is what makes glibc merge every matching row instead of returning the first.

ALGORITHM (AF_INET, files backend, multi on):

1. Row parse: strip from '#'; split on isspace (space, tab, \r); field 0 = address,
   fields 1.. = hostnames; a row with zero hostnames is ignored. Address must parse
   under inet_pton, so leading-zero octets ("010.0.0.1") are REJECTED.

2. Address interpretation for an AF_INET query:
     - inet_pton(AF_INET) ok            -> that address
     - else inet_pton(AF_INET6) ok and:
         v4-mapped (::ffff:a.b.c.d)     -> low 4 bytes
         loopback (::1, 0:0:...:1)      -> 127.0.0.1        <-- the vmi1227854 case
         anything else                  -> row ignored entirely
     - else row ignored

3. A numeric dotted-quad query short-circuits BEFORE the file is read:
   gethostbyname("10.0.0.1") -> h_name="10.0.0.1", aliases=[], one address, even when
   a matching row with aliases exists.

4. Name match is ASCII case-insensitive against canonical name OR any alias.

5. The FIRST row that both matches and yields a usable address SEEDS the result:
     h_name    = that row's canonical name (field 1) -- NOT the queried string
     aliases   = that row's remaining hostnames, in file order
     addresses = [that row's address]

6. Every LATER matching row appends, in this order:
     its aliases (all of them, in file order)
     then its canonical name, IFF canonical != h_name compared BYTE-FOR-BYTE
       (case-SENSITIVE: a row whose canonical is "HOST" when h_name is "host" DOES
        get appended)
     then its address
   NO de-duplication anywhere: duplicate alias strings and duplicate addresses are
   both preserved verbatim.

7. h_addrtype = AF_INET (2), h_length = 4. No cap on alias or address count
   (40 aliases across 4 rows verified fine).

VERIFIED VECTORS (hosts content -> query -> glibc result):

  "127.0.0.1 localhost\n127.0.0.2 localhost alias1 alias2"      localhost
    -> name=localhost aliases=[alias1,alias2] addrs=[127.0.0.1,127.0.0.2]

  "127.0.0.1 localhost dup\n127.0.0.2 localhost dup"            localhost
    -> name=localhost aliases=[dup,dup] addrs=[127.0.0.1,127.0.0.2]      (NO dedup)

  "127.0.0.1 localhost\n127.0.0.2 other localhost"              localhost
    -> name=localhost aliases=[localhost,other] addrs=[127.0.0.1,127.0.0.2]
       (queried name CAN appear in its own alias list; later canonical appended last)

  "127.0.0.1 canon myalias"                                     myalias
    -> name=canon aliases=[myalias] addrs=[127.0.0.1]            (h_name != query)

  "127.0.0.1 canon myalias\n127.0.0.2 myalias tail"             myalias
    -> name=canon aliases=[myalias,tail,myalias] addrs=[127.0.0.1,127.0.0.2]

  "::1 localhost ip6-localhost ip6-loopback"                    localhost
    -> name=localhost aliases=[ip6-localhost,ip6-loopback] addrs=[127.0.0.1]

  "::1 localhost ip6-localhost ip6-loopback\n127.0.0.1 localhost"  localhost
    -> name=localhost aliases=[ip6-localhost,ip6-loopback] addrs=[127.0.0.1,127.0.0.1]
       ^ EXACTLY the bd-6rrgjs report from vmi1227854.

  "2001:db8::1 v6only\n127.0.0.5 v6only tail"                   v6only
    -> name=v6only aliases=[tail] addrs=[127.0.0.5]   (unusable row skipped, next seeds)

  "::ffff:10.1.2.3 mapped"                                      mapped
    -> name=mapped aliases=[] addrs=[10.1.2.3]

  "::ffff:0:10.9.8.7 host a1"                                   host   -> NULL
       (not v4-mapped, not loopback)

  "127.0.0.1 LOCALHOST Alias1\n127.0.0.2 localhost ALIAS1"      LoCaLhOsT
    -> name=LOCALHOST aliases=[Alias1,ALIAS1,localhost] addrs=[127.0.0.1,127.0.0.2]
       ^ proves the canonical-vs-h_name test is case-SENSITIVE

  "10.0.0.1 host dup\n10.0.0.2 dup host"                        host
    -> name=host aliases=[dup,host,dup] addrs=[10.0.0.1,10.0.0.2]

  "10.0.0.1 host a1\n10.0.0.2 HOST a2"                          host
    -> name=host aliases=[a1,a2,HOST] addrs=[10.0.0.1,10.0.0.2]

  "010.0.0.1 host a1\n10.0.0.2 host a2"                         host
    -> name=host aliases=[a2] addrs=[10.0.0.2]

Reproduction scripts (probe batteries + ctypes oracle) are at
/data/tmp/claude-1000/-data-projects-frankenlibc/4b8c9531-66db-466d-b47c-e332b2728484/scratchpad/
{ghbn_oracle.py, probe_cases.sh, probe_cases2.sh}.

DELTA vs THE IMPLEMENTATION CURRENTLY UNCOMMITTED IN THE WORKING TREE
(crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/resolv_abi.rs, GethostbynameTarget, as of 2026-08-04):
  a) h_name is set to the QUERIED name (GethostbynameTarget::new(name_cstr.to_bytes())).
     glibc uses the seeding row's canonical name. Fails the "match by alias" vector.
  b) push_alias de-duplicates case-insensitively and drops any alias equal to h_name.
     glibc de-duplicates nothing. Fails the [dup,dup] and [localhost,other] vectors.
  c) the canonical name of every later matching row is never appended at all.
     Fails the [dup,host,dup] and [a1,a2,HOST] vectors.
  d) address parsing is `address_text.parse::<Ipv4Addr>()` only, so a `::1 localhost`
     row is skipped. That is precisely the row producing the reported
     aliases=[ip6-localhost,ip6-loopback] + duplicate 127.0.0.1 on vmi1227854, so
     the reported case is NOT fixed by the current patch.
  e) HOSTENT_MAX_ALIASES / HOSTENT_MAX_ADDRESSES caps have no glibc counterpart.

Reported by the Claude pane, which is NOT taking this bead (surface already in flight).

title: ffs-ondisk: ext4_casefold_{key,names_collide} lacks metamorphic relation tests
description:
Finding (via /testing-metamorphic skill, NEW target): ext4_casefold_key (crates/ffs-ondisk/src/ext4.rs:3331) and ext4_casefold_names_collide (l. 3336) implement the casefold collision contract used by lookup_in_dir_block_casefold for case-insensitive ext4 directories. The function has 4 hand-written unit tests but ZERO metamorphic-relation proptests. The contract should satisfy classic equivalence-relation laws plus idempotence and an ASCII case-substitution invariant — none of which are pinned.

Untested algebraic laws:
  * MR1 — Reflexivity: collide(x, x) MUST be true for ALL inputs (incl. invalid UTF-8, empty, long).
  * MR2 — Symmetry: collide(a, b) MUST equal collide(b, a).
  * MR3 — Idempotence of folding: key(key(name)) MUST equal key(name); folded output is stable under re-folding.
  * MR4 — Transitivity (via key equality): if key(a)==key(b) and key(b)==key(c), then key(a)==key(c) and collide(a,c) MUST be true.
  * MR5 — ASCII case-substitution invariance: for any ASCII bytestring, its uppercase variant MUST collide with itself.
  * MR6 — Diagnostics consistency: diagnostics(name).folded_key MUST equal key(name), and source_len MUST equal name.len().

Each MR catches a different class of regression: a determinism bug (e.g., a HashMap iteration leaking into the fold output) breaks MR1+MR3, a non-symmetric comparator breaks MR2, an unbalanced sharp-s expansion breaks MR3, an ASCII case bug breaks MR5, a divergence between diagnostics and the canonical key path breaks MR6.

Acceptance: 6 proptest cases co-located in the existing proptest! block at the end of crates/ffs-ondisk/src/ext4.rs that exercise these relations across UTF-8, invalid-UTF-8, and edge-case inputs.
close_reason: done

title: Refine mounted write errors with errno parity and broad-fallback budgets
description:
Supplemental refinement for bd-rchk0.3.4. Mounted write error reporting must distinguish kernel-style errno compatibility, FrankenFS-specific safety refusals, host capability failures, and genuinely unknown product failures. A generic EIO/EINVAL fallback may sometimes be correct, but it needs an explicit budget and follow-up path so operators are not left with opaque failures.

Scope: define an error-class mapping table from representative mounted operations to normalized errno, user-facing class, remediation id, evidence fields, and broad-fallback justification. Include ext4/btrfs differences, FUSE DefaultPermissions pitfalls, unsupported V1 scope, stale snapshot/lease, writeback-cache guard, repair interaction, cancellation, host capability skip, and cleanup failure.

Required proof before close:
1. Unit tests reject mapping rows missing operation class, normalized errno, user-facing class, remediation id, artifact fields, redaction policy, and broad-fallback rationale where used.
2. Unit tests cover permission denial, unsupported operation, stale snapshot, stale repair lease, writeback-cache gate refusal, missing ledger, unsafe repair refusal, host FUSE skip, btrfs DefaultPermissions ownership, harness failure, cleanup failure, and unknown product failure.
3. E2E mounted or fixture smoke proves representative failures emit expected errno/class/remediation fields and that broad EIO/EINVAL fallbacks create or link follow-up beads once their budget is exceeded.
4. Logs include operation id, scenario id, raw errno, normalized errno, error class, remediation id, broad-fallback budget state, stdout/stderr paths, artifact paths, and reproduction command.
5. Readiness reports must fail closed if mounted write failures collapse distinct host/setup/product/safety classes into a single opaque error without an owning follow-up.

title: EPIC: Killer Demo — Self-Healing Durability
description:
# EPIC: Killer Demo — Self-Healing Durability

## PURPOSE
Create a compelling, CI-executable demonstration of FrankenFS self-healing: flip random bits in blocks, show automatic repair using RaptorQ symbols, and output a human-readable repair ledger explaining exactly what was reconstructed. This is the "show, don't tell" proof of FrankenFS's core innovation.

## DEMO SCRIPT

### Setup (automated)
1. Create 128MB ext4 image with FrankenFS (RaptorQ enabled, 5% overhead)
2. Write 100 files with known content (photos, text, binaries)
3. Record BLAKE3 checksums for all files
4. Print: "Filesystem created: 100 files, all checksums verified"

### Corruption (visible to audience)
5. Print: "Injecting corruption: flipping random bits in 3% of blocks..."
6. Corrupt 3% of data blocks with random bit flips
7. Print block IDs and bit positions of corrupted blocks
8. Attempt to read files — show which files have corrupted bytes

### Repair (the magic moment)
9. Print: "Triggering self-healing scrub..."
10. Run scrub daemon (or explicit repair command)
11. Show real-time progress: "Scanning block group 1/32... corruption detected at block 1042... repairing with 4 symbols... OK"
12. Print: "Repair complete in 2.3 seconds"

### Verification (proof)
13. Read all 100 files, verify BLAKE3 checksums
14. Print: "All 100 files verified — zero data loss"
15. Print repair ledger: table of every repair action with timing, blocks, symbols used

### Output Format
```
=== FrankenFS Self-Healing Demo ===
Created: 100 files (128MB image, 5% RaptorQ overhead)
Corrupted: 47 blocks across 8 block groups (3% corruption rate)

Repair Results:
  Block Group  Corrupted  Repaired  Symbols Used  Time
  1            3          3         4             12ms
  4            8          8         12            34ms
  7            6          6         8             28ms
  ...
  Total        47         47        72            180ms

Verification: 100/100 files checksums match — ZERO DATA LOSS
Evidence ledger: 47 CorruptionDetected + 47 RepairSucceeded records
```

## REQUIREMENTS
- Must run without root (FUSE user mount)
- Must complete in < 30 seconds
- Must be deterministic (seeded corruption)
- Must be a single command: `cargo run --bin ffs-demo -- self-healing`
- Must work in CI (no GUI, no interactive input)

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] Demo runs successfully with single command
- [ ] All corrupted blocks repaired
- [ ] Repair ledger is human-readable and correct
- [ ] Demo completes in < 30 seconds
- [ ] Runs in CI without root
- [ ] Output suitable for README/blog post

## Success Criteria
1. All children closed
2. Demo runs with single command in < 30s
3. All corrupted blocks repaired (zero data loss)
4. Output suitable for README/blog post
5. CI-executable without root or FUSE
notes: DEPENDENCY NOTE: This demo is the capstone of the self-healing story. It depends on bd-15c.11 (5% corruption E2E test) which depends on the full scrub daemon pipeline. Do not attempt this until bd-15c.11 passes. The demo script should reuse the same test infrastructure but with human-readable output formatting. Consider adding a --verbose flag for technical audiences and a --summary flag for non-technical audiences.

title: log2p1f diverges from glibc across the f32 domain — conformance_diff_c23_logexp_f32 RED at HEAD
description:
conformance_diff_c23_logexp_f32 fails on a clean pinned HEAD (rch exec --base HEAD --clean-overlay --no-overlay), so this is pre-existing and unrelated to the f128 restore (bd-ocwiw9). Verified identical before and after that restore, same first mismatch:

  assertion left == right failed: C23 log/exp f32 diverged from glibc
  first: log2p1f(-0.9989925)
    left: 224048
   right: 0

The left value is the mismatch COUNT over the gate's sweep, so this is not one edge case — log2p1f disagrees with glibc across a large part of the domain, starting near the -1 pole where log2(1+x) goes to -inf and cancellation is worst.

C23 log2p1(x) = log2(1+x). The likely defect is computing it as log2(1.0 + x) in f32, which loses the whole point of the p1 form; glibc evaluates it without forming 1+x. Check whether logp1f/log10p1f in the same gate share the fault before fixing one in isolation.

DONE = conformance_diff_c23_logexp_f32 green, with the fix stating which forms were wrong and citing the measured glibc values it now matches. Do not narrow the gate's sweep to make it pass.
close_reason:
FIXED. Source commit 61dfc6d6f.

ROOT CAUSE — a FIFTH instance of the Jun-26 silent-deletion class, and a partial one.
1d7920b9e (bd-sqk053) had already made all four of these byte-exact by routing them through fl's
f64 versions. 517d0a233 ("abi/math: C99 Annex G special values for complex exp/hyperbolic", the
-6914-line deletion commit) reverted TWO of the four — log2p1f and log10p1f went back to the
single-precision log1pf(x)/LN_k_f32 form — while leaving exp2m1f and exp10m1f on their f64 routes.
That is why the gate reported log2p1f as the first mismatch and why the bead's guess ("check
whether logp1f/log10p1f share the fault") was half right: log10p1f shared it, logp1f did not.

  git log -S 'log2p1(x as f64) as f32' -- crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/math_abi.rs
    517d0a233  abi/math: C99 Annex G special values for complex exp/hyperbolic   <- deleted it
    1d7920b9e  fix(math): byte-exact C23 log2p1f/log10p1f/exp2m1f/exp10m1f (bd-sqk053)  <- added it

The bead's suspected mechanism was right in substance: glibc computes these in double and rounds
once, so doing the work in f32 loses ~2 ULP across the domain — worst near the -1 pole, which is
where the sweep hits it first.

FIX: two bodies restored, log2p1f -> log2p1(x as f64) as f32, log10p1f -> log10p1(x as f64) as f32.
No other function touched. The gate's sweep was NOT narrowed.

MEASURED, SAME GATE, TWO ARMS (the second is the control the bead's premise needed):
  export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/tmp/rch_target_frankenlibc_sandycove_om1s58
  RCH_ENV_ALLOWLIST=CARGO_TARGET_DIR RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec -- \
    cargo test -j 2 -p frankenlibc-abi --test conformance_diff_c23_logexp_f32 -- --nocapture
  -> test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 0.38s

  Clean HEAD, my change excluded (rch exec --base HEAD --clean-overlay --no-overlay), same command:
  -> frankenlibc: panic payload: assertion `left == right` failed: C23 log/exp f32 diverged from
     glibc; first: log2p1f(-0.9989925)   left: 224048   right: 0
     test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out

So the RED reproduces byte-identically to this bead's recorded signature at clean HEAD and goes
green with the two-line restore — the gate is demonstrably load-bearing, not passing on a string.
The gate reaches glibc through an explicit libm.so.6 dlopen handle, bypassing fl's no_mangle
interposition, and sweeps 400k points per function across the -1 pole comparing raw bits.

fmt clean (cargo fmt --check -p frankenlibc-abi, no math_abi.rs diff). Compilation observed: the
gate binary built and executed on rch worker.

PRE-EXISTING, NOT MINE, NOT FIXED HERE: frankenlibc-abi and frankenlibc-core both carry many
pre-existing clippy errors (f128 approximate-consts; 3 "equal expressions as operands to `/`" NaN
idioms in math/exp.rs:815, math/float.rs:55, math/float32.rs:992), so a `-D warnings` workspace
clippy cannot pass for reasons unrelated to this bead.

No unrelated user or agent changes were stashed, reverted, or deleted.

title: [perf] frankenlibc-core::string::mem::memcmp (mem.rs:54) — scalar byte loop, 1255ns/4096B (~40x memcpy/byte)
description:
PROFILING handoff from SnowyMill (run 20260601-perf-26a69011, git 26a69011). MEASUREMENT ONLY.

SCENARIO: memcmp over equal N-byte buffers (full scan), criterion string_bench, mode=raw, rch worker AMD EPYC, sample-size 40.

BASELINE p50 ns/op by size: 16->8.5, 64->30.7, 256->111.2, 1024->393.6, 4096->1255.3 (0.306 ns/byte).
PEER CONTRAST (same suite, same 4096 bytes): memcpy 31.6ns (0.0077 ns/byte, SIMD via copy_from_slice) -> memcmp is ~40x slower per byte; strcmp 351.8ns -> memcmp ~3.6x slower than strcmp despite doing structurally simpler work (fixed length, no NUL scan).

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed by source): crates/frankenlibc-core/src/string/mem.rs:54 memcmp is a scalar byte-at-a-time loop: while i<count { let av=a[i]; let bv=b[i]; if av!=bv {return ...}; i+=1 }. No word/SIMD bulk comparison. memcpy right above it uses copy_from_slice (lowers to SIMD memcpy) which is why it is 40x faster per byte.

FIX DIRECTION (optimizer, one lever; preserve exact Ordering semantics incl. unsigned-byte tie-break at first differing byte): compare usize-sized chunks (read_unaligned / chunks_exact::<8>) for equality, and only on a differing chunk fall back to byte compare to find the first differing byte and its ordering; tail bytes via the existing scalar loop. Expect to approach memcpy/strcmp ns/byte. Re-run: rch exec -- cargo bench -p frankenlibc-bench --bench string_bench -- --sample-size 40. Validate against existing memcmp conformance tests (Ordering for <, =, > and partial-length n).

EVIDENCE: tests/artifacts/perf/20260601-perf-26a69011/string_bench.summary.md + string_bench.raw.log.
close_reason: Fixed in e2e61482. Replaced scalar equal-buffer memcmp scan with safe 8-byte chunk equality plus byte fallback for first-difference ordering. RCH before/after p50 raw: memcmp_16 7.759ns -> 2.917ns, memcmp_64 26.353ns -> 5.842ns, memcmp_256 108.320ns -> 15.859ns, memcmp_1024 402.212ns -> 62.250ns, memcmp_4096 1593.221ns -> 208.501ns. Behavior proof: existing memcmp test-line sha256 stayed eef1f26220f1736c43e59f193a2b8b1fb9a8ecf5dbb2a5abf2fb31071ac18312; new regression pins first-difference ordering inside bulk chunk and unsigned tail ordering. Validation: rch bench/test/check/clippy passed; cargo fmt --check, git diff --check, and UBS passed locally.

title: PORT: getenv_r (NetBSD re-entrant getenv)
description: Port the NetBSD libc `getenv_r(name, buf, buflen)` re-entrant environment lookup. Looks up the value of the environment variable `name` and copies it into the caller-provided `buf` (which must hold at least `strlen(value)+1` bytes). Returns 0 on success, -1 with errno=ENOENT if the variable is not set, or -1 with errno=ERANGE if `buf` is too small for the value plus NUL. Useful for callers that want to avoid the global-pointer aliasing risk of plain getenv. Implementation: thin abi shim around the existing getenv() that copies bytes into the caller buffer with bounds checking; tests cover lookup-success, missing-variable, undersized-buffer, NULL-name/buf guards.

title: Normalize leading -- in RCH admissibility preflight
description:
The repo-native `scripts/check_rch_remote_admissibility.sh` accepts a validation command as positional text and passes it to `rch diagnose --dry-run`. Agents commonly invoke command-wrapper scripts with a leading `--` separator, e.g. `bash scripts/check_rch_remote_admissibility.sh -- cargo check ...`. Today that form is forwarded literally, causing `rch diagnose` to reject the command before offload classification and leaving the preflight with a misleading `missing_offload_classification` blocker instead of the real RCH pressure signatures.

Acceptance: the wrapper strips exactly one leading `--` command separator before building `VALIDATION_COMMAND`; the checked-in preflight contract includes this calling convention and a negative/control assertion; both invocation forms produce the same blocked/admissibility interpretation for the current RCH state; validation uses shell/JQ only and does not run cargo or cleanup.
close_reason: Shipped in working tree: scripts/check_rch_remote_admissibility.sh now strips one leading `--` command separator before composing VALIDATION_COMMAND. Updated tests/conformance/rch_remote_admissibility_preflight.v1.json to document the convention, add leading_command_separator_not_forwarded negative control, and list both normal and leading-separator validation invocations. Validation: bash -n scripts/check_rch_remote_admissibility.sh; jq empty tests/conformance/rch_remote_admissibility_preflight.v1.json; regenerated current-head RCH approval packet b78f4534 with 94 candidates; bash scripts/check_rch_pressure_packet_goldens.sh passed events=37; normal wrapper invocation exited 2 as expected; leading-`--` wrapper invocation exited 2 as expected; jq verified validation_command normalized to cargo check -p frankenlibc-abi --features=standalone and missing_offload_classification absent; jq verified approval_packet_status=available_current with approval_ready_candidates>0; jq verified contract_status=pass/status=blocked/status_on_current_blocked_state=blocked/all negative controls pass; grep verified operator hints in both stderr files; git diff --check passed; br dep cycles count=0. title: [RC-WS6.1] Make owned __libc_start_main / csu / TLS init the default path
description: Native startup (phase 0) is opt-in via env var; the default __libc_start_main delegates to host glibc. Make the owned csu and TLS init path the default. Unit tests (happy/edge/error): clean argv/envp/auxv parse; a truncated auxv vector; an unterminated argv; secure-mode classification from auxv. e2e: a statically-traced startup proof shows no host __libc_start_main call, init/fini-array and atexit order are correct, and errno TLS isolation holds across threads; structured logging of every startup checkpoint.

title: [RC-WS6.2] Owned dynamic loader that natively loads ELF shared objects
description: Owned dynamic loader sub-epic. Today dlopen delegates ALL ELF loading to host glibc (code comment: our dlopen cannot load ELF files natively); dl_iterate_phdr and dladdr delegate unconditionally. This is the single hardest item in the L2 program because dynamic linking is globally coupled to process behavior, so it is decomposed into five child beads: ELF image mapping (.2.1), relocation processing (.2.2), symbol resolution and dependency graph (.2.3), TLS for loaded objects (.2.4), and init/fini ordering (.2.5). Done-when: dlopen of an arbitrary shared object with transitive dependencies succeeds natively with no host ld-linux fallback, verified by the WS-6 e2e harness. Full context: REALITY_CHECK_BRIDGE_PLAN.md WS-6.
close_reason: Closed loader parent after all five child beads reached closed state: bd-73h55.2.1 image mapping, bd-73h55.2.2 relocation processing, bd-73h55.2.3 dependency graph/symbol scope, bd-73h55.2.4 dynamic TLS, and bd-73h55.2.5 init/fini lifecycle ordering. This unblocks bd-73h55.8 for the end-to-end WS6 standalone-readiness harness. Validation evidence from child closeouts includes rch exec -- cargo test/check/clippy -p frankenlibc-core --all-targets and loader lifecycle/TLS focused E2E/unit lanes.

title: EPIC: Runtime Hot-Path Perf Gates (strict <20ns, hardened <200ns)
description:
Goal: enforce extreme-software-optimization discipline for runtime_math.

Why:
- runtime_math is on the membrane hot path. Any regression here leaks into every libc call we gate.

Constraints:
- Strict mode must stay <20ns/call overhead target.
- Hardened mode must stay <200ns/call overhead target.
- No behavior regressions without explicit isomorphism proof + fixture evidence.

Outputs:
- Microbench + profile baselines for RuntimeMathKernel::decide + observe_validation_result.
- Golden snapshot outputs to detect accidental semantic drift.
- A repeatable baseline/profile/verify loop that future work MUST follow.
close_reason: done

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## Epic Notes: Extreme-Optimization Discipline For runtime_math

This epic encodes the non-negotiable loop: **baseline -> profile -> prove -> implement -> verify -> repeat**.

### What We Are Protecting
runtime_math runs at the ABI boundary of libc call paths. Any accidental overhead shows up everywhere.

Budgets (from AGENTS.md):
- strict overhead target: <20ns/call (fast exits)
- hardened overhead target: <200ns/call (bounded heavy path)

### What Counts As “Hot Path”
- `RuntimeMathKernel::decide` on the strict path
- per-call evidence recording (if enabled)
- pointer-validation stage ordering / cached biases

### Hard Rules
- No transcendental math, matrix solves, or heap allocation on strict fast path.
- Any stochastic element must be deterministic from seed (replayable).
- Any “expensive” kernel must be cadence-driven (epoch update) not per call.

### Measurement Artifacts Required
- Criterion microbench for `decide` / `observe` (ns/op + percentiles)
- Profile recipe (flamegraph/perf) pinned to a reproducible command
- Golden snapshot outputs + sha256 regression gate
- Isomorphism proof template for policy changes (behavior invariants)

### Definition Of Done
- We can quantify overhead deltas per kernel addition.
- We can detect regressions in CI before merging.
- We have an explicit narrative for every optimization: what changed, why safe, how measured.

title: [RED] 8 conformance-matrix cases fail now that the harness builds again (2 hardened iconv deny-arms accept denied input)
description:
First conformance-matrix run after bd-kcmnj4 unblocked the harness (b1b443efc + asupersync-conformance 0.4.4 from the registry). These 8 were invisible for as long as the harness was dark.

Command (exit 0), binary built on rch worker ovh-a from HEAD 033bcad41 + b1b443efc:
  ./target/debug/harness conformance-matrix --fixture tests/conformance/fixtures --isolate \
      --case-timeout-ms 5000 --output target/conformance/conformance_matrix.current.v1.json
  -> total=3371, passed=3363, failed=8, errors=0

THE TWO THAT ARE POLICY HOLES, NOT COSMETICS — a hardened deny-arm is accepting input it must refuse:
  iconv/phase1 :: iconv :: hardened :: hardened_iso2022jp_deferred_denied
      spec: TSM hardened iconv WS-6 ISO-2022-JP deferred deny
      expected 'open_err errno=22'; actual 'ok nonrev=0 in_left=0 out_left=5 out=[227,129,130]'
      i.e. iconv_open SUCCEEDED and converted, where hardened mode is specified to deny.
  iconv/phase1 :: iconv :: hardened :: hardened_unsupported_encoding_denied
      fromcode=UTF-7. expected 'open_err errno=22'; actual 'ok nonrev=0 in_left=0 out_left=7 out=[65]'

THE OTHER SIX, each failing in BOTH strict and hardened (so not a mode-policy issue):
  stdio/libio :: freopen   :: freopen_null_path_class_{strict,hardened}
      spec: POSIX freopen null-path mode-change class, expected FREOPEN_NULL_PATH_STREAM_NULL
  stdio/libio :: freopen64 :: freopen64_null_path_class_{strict,hardened}
      spec: GNU freopen64 null-path mode-change class
  unistd :: fcrypt :: fcrypt_null_inputs_{strict,hardened}
      spec: libcrypt fcrypt null input failure, expected FCRYPT_NULL_PTR_EINVAL

Note the host_output field on the iconv rows is 'SKIP' with host_parity=true, so these are
fl-vs-spec rows, not fl-vs-glibc rows — triage each for whether the SPEC arm or fl is wrong, exactly
as bd-aykfv1 requires (category (a) real defect vs (b) wrong-premise arm).

DONE = each of the 8 triaged to (a)/(b) with a fix or a corrected arm, and the matrix run clean.

comments.author: YellowPlateau
comments.text:
TRIAGE, 6 of the 8 rows, done with live host oracles rather than by reading the arms (YellowPlateau).

freopen/freopen64 null-path, all 4 rows -> CATEGORY (b), the ARM is wrong, fl is right.
The arms expect FREOPEN_NULL_PATH_STREAM_NULL, i.e. that freopen(NULL, mode, stream) returns NULL.
It does not on this host. Live glibc, one process, controlled tmpfile:
    fopen(path,'r')                   -> 0xeb13b90
    freopen(NULL,'r',stream)          -> 0xeb13b90  errno=0
    freopen(NULL,'w',stream)          -> 0xeb13b90  errno=0
glibc implements the POSIX null-path MODE CHANGE (it reopens through /proc/self/fd) and returns the
SAME stream. fl's observed FREOPEN_STREAM_REOPENED is therefore host-correct and the expectation is
what needs fixing. Note host_output on these rows is 'SKIP' with host_parity=true, which is exactly
how an arm like this survives: nothing ever compared it to a host.

fcrypt null inputs, both rows -> CATEGORY (b) on the same pattern, with a caveat.
fcrypt is not exported by this host at all:
    libcrypt.so.1: undefined symbol: fcrypt
    libc.so.6:     undefined symbol: fcrypt
so there is no direct oracle. Its documented alias, crypt, gives:
    libxcrypt crypt(NULL,NULL) -> b'*0'  errno=22
i.e. a NON-NULL failure token plus EINVAL. The arm expects FCRYPT_NULL_PTR_EINVAL meaning a NULL
return; that is pre-libxcrypt glibc behaviour and no longer what any crypt on this host does. fl's
FCRYPT_NULL_PTR_UNEXPECTED_NONNULL is consistent with the live implementation. Before flipping this
arm, confirm fl also sets errno=EINVAL — the arm's name only records null-ness, so a non-NULL return
with the WRONG errno would pass a naively-corrected arm. That is the negative case this row needs.

Still untriaged, and the two that matter most: the two hardened iconv deny-arms
(hardened_iso2022jp_deferred_denied, hardened_unsupported_encoding_denied). Those are fl-vs-policy,
not fl-vs-host, so the (b) escape hatch above does not apply to them by default.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
AmberQuarry 2026-08-15: the 6 remaining arms are corrected and landed in e2d1f63a7; the 2 iconv rows were already fixed by b93de94ef. All 8 rows are now addressed in-tree.

WHAT I DID NOT TAKE ON TRUST: YellowPlateau's triage of the freopen/fcrypt rows was correct, but I re-measured both against the live host rather than closing on a peer's reading. glibc 2.42: freopen(NULL,"r"|"w"|"r+",stream) returns the SAME FILE* with errno untouched (seeded 4242, still 4242 after) -- the POSIX null-path MODE CHANGE, via /proc/self/fd. libxcrypt: fcrypt is exported by neither libcrypt.so.1 nor libc.so.6, and crypt(NULL,NULL) returns the non-NULL token "*0" with errno=EINVAL. fl already matched both, so both are category (b).

THE ARMS WERE STRENGTHENED, NOT JUST RE-POINTED -- this bead's own triage asked for the negative case, and the old tokens could not carry it:
  - freopen/freopen64 now distinguish stream IDENTITY: a non-null return that is a DIFFERENT
    stream reports FREOPEN_STREAM_REPLACED and fails. fl reports REOPENED, i.e. the returned
    pointer is measured equal to the input, same as glibc. The old token accepted any non-null.
  - fcrypt now records the failure TOKEN and the errno (FCRYPT_NULL_PTR_TOKEN_*0_EINVAL), so a
    non-null return with the wrong/unset errno, or a plausible-looking hash instead of "*0",
    fails. Correcting only null-ness -- the naive fix -- would have passed all three.

GATES OBSERVED COMPILING AND EXECUTING on an rch worker against the committed tree:
  stdio_libio_wave04_fixture_cases_match_execute_fixture_case        ... ok
  unistd_process_filesystem_wave10_fixture_cases_match_...           ... ok
  execute_iconv_case_hardened_unsupported_encoding_denied            ... ok  (7 passed)
Both wave gates were RED before this change, so before and after are both measured.

NOTE ON THE ARMS' PROVENANCE, because it is the reusable lesson: every one of these arms
carried oracle_source="FrankenLibC <fn> ... replay" and host_output=SKIP. The expectation was
recorded from fl's own output and never compared to a host, which is exactly how an arm can be
wrong and stay green for months. The corrected arms name the live measurement instead.

STILL OPEN ON THIS BEAD: the 'matrix run clean' clause. I did not re-run conformance-matrix.
Two things a future agent should know before doing so:
  - tests/conformance/errno_edge_report.v1.json is ALREADY stale at HEAD, independently of this
    change: regenerating it flips profil -> WrapsHostLibc, __isoc99_sscanf/__isoc99_vsscanf ->
    Implemented and adds 2 missing vsscanf execution rows (failing_edge_cases 0 -> 2, that is

    as green.
  - two further fixture gates are red on a single unrelated arm-premise defect (acct as root):

title: math passthrough probes assert at the FIRST drifting symbol, hiding every later one — cost two round-trips today
description:
Observed 2026-08-15 while closing bd-atanhf-tiny-x-251ulp-s1p6z2.

f32_trig_inverse_cbrt_passthroughs_within_4_ulp_of_glibc scans 14 f32 symbols, but its inner scan helper asserts as soon as one exceeds 4 ULP. So the gate can only ever name ONE symbol per run, and the ones after it are not merely unreported -- they are unexecuted.

That cost two full fix-verify round-trips today:
  run 1: 'atanhf drifted 251 ULP vs glibc at x=-1.9116941e-12'
  fix atanhf -> run 2: 'log1pf drifted 548 ULP vs glibc at x=-8.282635e-14'
Both were real, independent defects in the same file and the same tiny-|x| class. Nothing told us the second existed until the first was fixed and pushed. If there is a third, we still do not know.

FIX: accumulate drifts into a Vec and assert once at the end, listing every symbol with its worst ULP and the x where it occurred -- the shape math_special_value_differential_battery in this same file already uses for its diffs vector. Apply to the f64 sibling trig_inverse_cbrt_passthroughs_within_4_ulp_of_glibc too, which has the identical structure and therefore the identical blind spot.

VALUE IS THE RUN, NOT THE REFACTOR: the point is to learn whether more symbols in these two families are drifting right now. Report the full list either way -- 'no further drift' is the useful answer if that is what it is, and it is not currently known.

NOT a new framework: this changes assert-inside-loop to assert-once in two existing tests.
close_reason:
Shipped 2e81accd5, pushed to main and main:master.

Both passthrough probes now accumulate drifts into a Vec and assert once at the end, so a run names every drifting symbol with its worst ULP and the x where it occurred, instead of stopping at the first.

PROVEN TO REPORT MORE THAN ONE, which is the whole point and would otherwise be an untested refactor. With the threshold temporarily forced to report every scan and nothing else changed, on an rch worker:
  test f32_trig_inverse_cbrt_passthroughs_within_4_ulp_of_glibc ... FAILED
  test trig_inverse_cbrt_passthroughs_within_4_ulp_of_glibc ... FAILED
  21 f32 passthrough symbol(s) drift >4 ULP vs glibc:
  sinf 1 ULP, sinf_big 1, cosf 1, tanf 1, asinf 1, acosf 1, atanf 1, cbrtf 0, asinhf 2, ...
All 21 f32 scans reported in ONE run, plus the f64 test's own list, where the old code stopped at sinf. Threshold restored, then re-verified against the exact committed tree: test result: ok. 6 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored.

THE ANSWER THE BEAD ASKED FOR, which is the actual deliverable rather than the refactor: with every scan now executing, both families are GREEN at the real 4-ULP contract, and the forced listing shows the true worst drifts are 1-2 ULP across sinf/cosf/tanf/asinf/acosf/atanf/asinhf/cbrtf. So there is NO third drifting symbol hiding behind atanhf and log1pf. That was genuinely unknown before -- the f32 test had never once run past its first failure -- and it is the negative evidence the bead asked to be reported either way.

Cost this addressed, for the record: atanhf's 251-ULP drift hid log1pf's 548-ULP drift completely, and the second only surfaced after the first was fixed and pushed, i.e. two full fix-verify round-trips for what one run can now report.

description: The SWAR decimal parse family is done (strtol/strtoul/scanf, 1.4-2.4x). Hex (base 16) is the next common base (addresses, hashes, colors, hexdumps). RECIPE: for base==16 with >=8 hex bytes, load 8 LE, validate all-hex + decode nibbles, combine into u32 (4-bit shifts), accumulate acc*2^32+chunk with checked overflow. The HARD part is SWAR hex validation across 3 char ranges [0-9 A-F a-f]: lowercase via word|0x2020..., then per-byte detect [0x30,0x39] OR [0x61,0x66]. Nibble decode: (lw & 0x0f0f...) + ((lw>>6)&0x0101...)*9 gives 0-15 for valid hex. Validation must reject 0x3a-0x60 gap (e.g. ':' decodes to nibble 10 but is invalid) — use the two-range high-bit SWAR trick or re-encode-and-compare. MANDATORY: SWAR-vs-scalar fuzz guard (constants/ranges must be exact) like the decimal version. Target ~1.7x on 16-hex-digit, beating glibc. Parent bd-2g7oyh.

title: nftw logical walk: no (dev,ino) revisit suppression — duplicate subtrees and unbounded recursion on symlink cycles
description:
In the LOGICAL walk (FTW_PHYS clear) glibc's nftw remembers every directory it has entered by
(st_dev, st_ino) and silently omits any directory it reaches a second time — no callback at all
for the repeat. FrankenLibC's walker keeps no such record, so it both re-reports shared
directories and, on a symlink cycle, recurses until the stack is exhausted.

MEASURED against live glibc 2.42 on thinkstation1 (ctypes harness driving the host's own nftw;
scratchpad/nftw_oracle4.py):

  1) self-referential symlink   BASE/d/file, BASE/d/loop -> BASE
     glibc LOGICAL: / , /d , /d/file            <- /d/loop omitted, walk terminates, rc=0
     glibc PHYS   : / , /d , /d/file , /d/loop(FTW_SL)
     FrankenLibC LOGICAL: / -> /d -> /d/loop -> /d -> /d/loop -> ... unbounded recursion.
     walk_rec in crates/frankenlibc-core/src/ftw/walker.rs recurses per directory entry with no
     visited set and no depth bound, so this is a stack-overflow abort on a tree any user can
     create with `ln -s .. loop`.

  2) two paths to one directory  aaa_target/inner ; mmm_link -> aaa_target ;
                                 zzz_other/link_back -> aaa_target
     glibc LOGICAL reports the target exactly once, under whichever path readdir reached first
     (observed: /zzz_other/link_back as FTW_D plus its inner), and omits BOTH remaining routes.
     glibc PHYS reports /aaa_target as FTW_D and the two links as FTW_SL, descending only the
     real directory.
     FrankenLibC LOGICAL descends every route and reports the contents once per route.

Scope note: the suppression is keyed on directories only and applies only when FTW_PHYS is
clear — the PHYS walk never follows a link, so it needs no record. A fix wants the (dev, ino)
set threaded through walk_rec (inserted on entering a directory, consulted before descending),
which is also the natural place to bound recursion depth against nopenfd, currently ignored.

The differential test belongs in crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/conformance_diff_ftw_nftw.rs and
must include the self-loop case; note that until the fix lands that case cannot be run against
FrankenLibC without crashing the test process, so land the guard before the assertion.

Found while building the FTW_ACTIONRETVAL differential coverage for bd-nwrdyu; kept out of that
bead because it is a different defect on a different code path.
close_reason: Logical nftw walk now suppresses directory revisits by (dev,ino) — cfade4b56 (core walker) + f118feb8a (AbiStat::inode_id). Symlink cycles terminate instead of exhausting the stack, and a subtree reachable two ways is walked once. Scope measured against live glibc: directories only (hard-linked files still reported twice), global to the walk rather than the ancestor chain, no callback at all on the repeat, identical under FTW_DEPTH, and nothing suppressed under FTW_PHYS. Evidence: 30/30 core ftw tests and 32/32 conformance_diff_ftw_nftw including 4 new same-invocation differential tests that build a real 'ln -s .. loop' cycle on disk; ubs 0 critical. Full detail in the bead comment.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FIXED. nftw's logical walk now keeps every directory it enters keyed by (dev, ino) and skips a
repeat entirely, so a symlink cycle terminates instead of exhausting the stack.

IMPLEMENTATION
  crates/frankenlibc-core/src/ftw/walker.rs
    - StatLike gains inode_id() (st_ino); the trait already carried dev_id() for FTW_MOUNT.
    - walk_tree allocates a BTreeSet<(u64,u64)> and threads it through walk_rec. Empty until the
      first directory, so a walk rooted at a plain file allocates nothing.
    - walk_rec, once the entry is known to be a directory and past the FTW_MOUNT check:
        if !PHYSICAL && !visited.insert((dev, ino)) { return Continue }
      Short-circuiting means the set is never even touched on a physical walk.
  crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs
    - AbiStat::inode_id() -> self.0.st_ino (3 lines; the swarm was notified because another agent
      had that file open for bd-qzt4pj at the time).

SCOPE, every clause measured against live glibc 2.42 rather than assumed
(scratchpad/nftw_oracle{3,4,6}.py):
  - DIRECTORIES ONLY. A file reached as itself, as a hard link and through a symlink is reported
    all three times even though the first two share (dev, ino) exactly. Suppression exists to stop
    re-descending, and only directories are descended.
  - GLOBAL TO THE WALK, not the ancestor chain. Two SIBLING symlinks onto one directory: the
    first is reported and descended, the second produces no callback at all. An ancestor-stack
    design would have reported both.
  - NO CALLBACK AT ALL on the repeat — not a callback carrying some flag.
  - FTW_DEPTH suppresses identically.
  - FTW_PHYS suppresses nothing: it never follows a symlink, so it cannot revisit. Both links and
    the real directory are all still reported, links as FTW_SL.

EVIDENCE
  cargo test -j 1 -p frankenlibc-core --lib ftw::           -> 30 passed; 0 failed
    5 new: logical_walk_terminates_on_a_symlink_cycle,
           logical_walk_reports_a_shared_directory_once_under_the_first_path,
           logical_walk_suppression_also_applies_under_ftw_depth,
           physical_walk_suppresses_nothing,
           files_sharing_an_inode_are_never_suppressed
    All 12 pre-existing walker tests still pass.
  cargo test -j 1 -p frankenlibc-abi --test conformance_diff_ftw_nftw  -> see below
    4 new same-invocation differential tests build real symlinks on disk (a `ln -s .. loop`
    cycle, and three routes onto one directory) and compare the full ordered visit sequence
    against the host glibc:
           diff_nftw_logical_walk_terminates_on_a_symlink_cycle,
           diff_nftw_logical_walk_reports_a_shared_directory_once,
           diff_nftw_physical_walk_keeps_every_route,
           diff_nftw_logical_cycle_suppression_holds_under_depth
  ubs on both changed files: 0 critical.

TEST-INFRASTRUCTURE NOTE for anyone extending walker.rs's mock: its MockStat previously left ino
at Default::default() for every node. Under the new check that would make every directory collide
on inode 0 and suppress the whole tree after the first, so all mock nodes now carry distinct
inodes, and MockFs::read_dir follows symlinks the way a real opendir does (otherwise a logical
walk could never descend one). New mock nodes need a distinct ino.

NOT ADDRESSED HERE: recursion is still unbounded for a genuinely deep acyclic tree, and nopenfd
is still ignored. The cycle case — the one a user can trigger with a single ln -s — is closed.

title: REVIEW: [HIGH] strtod missed errno=ERANGE on overflow/underflow
description:
FOUND + FIXED via differential harness vs glibc (commit 0bd439d2).

strtod("1e400", &end) returned +Infinity (correct) but failed to set errno=ERANGE (POSIX violation). Same for strtod("1e-400", &end) which returned 0.0 without ERANGE. Glibc sets ERANGE in both cases.

Reachability: any program that uses strtod to parse numeric input and relies on errno to distinguish overflow-Inf from literal "INF" (or underflow-0 from literal "0") would silently misclassify. Common in JSON/config parsers and scientific code.

Fix in crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/stdlib_abi.rs strtod(): after parsing, set errno=ERANGE if val.is_infinite() AND consumed prefix doesn't contain "inf" literal, OR val==0.0 AND consumed prefix contains any non-zero digit.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 0bd439d2; differential test diff_strtod_cases now passes including 1e400/1e-400 ERANGE cases.

title: [bug][resolv] fl _gethtent yields 2 IPv4 /etc/hosts entries where glibc gethostent yields 3 — pre-existing iterator divergence surfaced by hostent_iter_ab
close_reason:
FIXED. Source commit 98975eb0b. The bead was REAL; the blocker comment on it is refuted.

THE BLOCKER COMMENT WAS WRONG ON THE POINT THAT MATTERED
PurpleLake wrote: "host glibc exports no _gethtent symbol (nm -D libc.so.6), so the stated
private-helper-vs-public iterator comparison has no no-mock oracle and no safe code change
remains." The symbol claim is TRUE and irrelevant. The oracle is glibc's PUBLIC gethostent, which
glibc does export — verified: `nm -D /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6` -> gethostent@@GLIBC_2.2.5
and gethostent_r@@GLIBC_2.2.5 — and which is exactly the AF_INET view of /etc/hosts that
_gethtent is supposed to reproduce. A safe code change did remain, and it is two lines of rule.

ROOT CAUSE
crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/resolv_abi.rs, next_hosts_ipv4_entry: `addr_text.parse::<Ipv4Addr>()`
and `continue` on failure, so EVERY IPv6 line was dropped. glibc does not drop them all —
nss_files folds the two IPv6 forms that carry an IPv4 meaning into AF_INET entries and skips the
rest. On a stock Ubuntu /etc/hosts the `::1 ip6-localhost ip6-loopback` line is therefore an
AF_INET 127.0.0.1 entry in glibc and nothing at all in fl: 2 vs 3, exactly as recorded.

CONTRACT MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED (live glibc, bwrap --bind <synthetic hosts> /etc/hosts, ctypes):
  ::1 and 0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1  -> 127.0.0.1  af=AF_INET len=4   (IN6_IS_ADDR_LOOPBACK)
  ::ffff:1.2.3.4           -> 1.2.3.4                        (IN6_IS_ADDR_V4MAPPED)
  ::ffff:0102:0304         -> 1.2.3.4                        (same, hex spelling)
  ::1.2.3.4                -> SKIPPED   (v4-COMPATIBLE is NOT v4-mapped)
  ::0, ::ffff:0:9.10.11.12, 64:ff9b::13.14.15.16, fe80::1, 2001:db8::5 -> SKIPPED
  aliases preserved on the converted entries
Rule implemented is exactly V4MAPPED-or-LOOPBACK. `to_ipv4_mapped()` is used deliberately in
preference to `to_ipv4()`, because only the former excludes the v4-compatible form glibc skips.

title: perf: calloc always write_bytes(0, total) even for fresh kernel-zeroed mmap pages — skip the redundant zeroing for fresh-from-mmap blocks (glibc-style)
notes: LEVER (HIGH-VALUE, realistic: zeroed arrays/hash-tables/buffers): calloc (malloc_abi.rs ~1956) does std::ptr::write_bytes(ptr,0,total) on EVERY allocation, but large allocations served from fresh MAP_ANONYMOUS mmap are already kernel-zeroed — the memset is pure waste (a full extra pass over the buffer). glibc tracks zeroed pages and skips. DESIGN: add pipeline.allocate_zeroed(total) -> (ptr, already_zero) (or a fresh-mmap flag); calloc skips write_bytes when already_zero, else memsets. WHY TEST-CAPABLE TURN (not cargo-check-only): CORRECTNESS-CRITICAL — skipping the memset on a RECYCLED (non-zero) block hands the caller garbage in 'zeroed' memory -> silent data corruption in every calloc user; needs the malloc/calloc differential + a recycled-block stress test (alloc, write nonzero, free, calloc same class -> must be zero) to verify the fresh-vs-recycled distinction. No safe cargo-check subset (unlike realloc-shrink bd-tkcv3c, which was safe-by-construction). CLUSTER: with bd-tkcv3c (realloc in-place grow) + bd-wutxl6 (fwrite bypass) these 3 allocator/IO levers all need a test-capable (rch/batch) turn. NEGATIVE-EVIDENCE: rest of realistic surface saturated; 12 levers shipped this campaign (memory printf-scanf-perf-campaign).
close_reason: MEASURED REJECT (BlackThrush, frankenlibc-cc). Lever: route calloc through std::alloc::alloc_zeroed (new arena.allocate_zeroed/pipeline.allocate_zeroed) to skip the unconditional write_bytes(0,total) on fresh kernel-zeroed mmap pages. Controlled single-process new-vs-old + dlmopen glibc head-to-head on rch ovh-a (new bench calloc_glibc_bench): fl calloc(alloc_zeroed) vs fl malloc+write_bytes p50 256B 1043.4/1031.5 (1.011x), 4096 1060.5/1069.1 (0.992x), 65536 1676.6/1664.9 (1.007x), 262144 3476.7/3535.2 (0.983x), 1048576 13028.9/12522.4 (1.040x LOSS), 4194304 46155.7/46054.8 (1.002x). NEUTRAL band 0.98-1.04, slight loss at 1MiB -> no win. ROOT CAUSE: arena forces align=32 > Rust MIN_ALIGN(16) for its 24B fingerprint header, so System::alloc_zeroed NEVER forwards to libc calloc -- it does alloc+write_bytes identically to baseline, making the mmap-zeroed skip structurally unreachable. Confirmed: a working skip would make the new arm not touch pages -> far cheaper at 1-4MiB; instead new==old. glibc 1MiB p50 11792 (only ~6% under fl_old; fixed membrane overhead, not memset). Reverted all 3 source edits (malloc_abi/arena/ptr_validator); KEPT reusable calloc_glibc_bench harness. Retry predicate in tests/artifacts/perf/bd-7ak6cm-calloc-alloc-zeroed.md (only path = decouple header offset from layout align to align=16, a correctness-critical arena-contract change with ~<=6% >=1MiB-only ceiling). Validation: rustfmt --check bench, git diff --check, cargo check -p frankenlibc-abi and -p frankenlibc-membrane green (pre-existing f128 warnings only).

title: PORT: 16 NIS+ nis_* fail-safe libnsl stubs (error formatters + local queries + free no-ops)
description: Add 16 NIS+ (nis_*) fail-safe stubs to extend the libnsl parity work. NIS+ is even deader than NIS — sun deprecated it in the late 1990s — but binaries that link against it through libc must still resolve at link-edit. Provide the cheapest possible safe behavior. Error helpers (4): nis_perror writes "<label>: NIS+ error" to fd 2; nis_sperrno returns a static description string for the given nis_error code; nis_sperror returns a malloc-allocated "<label>: <msg>" string; nis_sperror_r writes that into a caller buffer. Logger (1): nis_lerror is a no-op (syslog target). Free helpers (7): nis_freeresult / nis_freenames / nis_free_object / nis_free_directory / nis_free_request / nis_freeservlist / nis_freetags are all no-ops because our query stubs never allocate any of those structures. Local queries (4): nis_local_directory / nis_local_host / nis_local_principal / nis_local_group all return a pointer to a static empty C string. Error codes use the standard NIS+ enum (NIS_NAMEUNREACHABLE = 5 etc). 16 functions total.

title: [bug][support-matrix] vsscanf/__isoc99_vsscanf/__isoc99_sscanf classified WrapsHostLibc but are native — vsscanf has zero fixture coverage, blocking the promotion
description:
Surfaced by bd-4habm0's scanner fix (1d5631b48). Before that fix these three rows validated only
because the scanner hallucinated host delegation out of a doc comment in stream_cell; with the
scanner comment-blind they report the truth:

  __isoc99_sscanf   WrapsHostLibc  "WrapsHostLibc but no host delegation detected"
  __isoc99_vsscanf  WrapsHostLibc  "WrapsHostLibc but no host delegation detected"
  vsscanf           WrapsHostLibc  "WrapsHostLibc but no host delegation detected"

GROUND TRUTH, read at HEAD (crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/stdio_abi.rs):
  vsscanf           -> runtime_policy gate, strict_c_str_len, scanf_core, raw va_list writes.
                       No host libc symbol on any path.
  __isoc99_vsscanf  -> `unsafe { vsscanf(s, format, ap) }`
  __isoc99_sscanf   -> takes addr_of_mut!(args), then `unsafe { vsscanf(s, format, ap) }`
The sibling `sscanf` — same scanf_core parse — is already classified Implemented, so the family is
internally inconsistent. These three rows overstate host dependency; support_matrix.json is stale.

WHY IT IS NOT A ONE-LINE MATRIX EDIT
WrapsHostLibc(2) -> Implemented(3) is a promotion, and the generator's
`reclassification_requires_conformance` policy demands strict AND hardened conformance evidence
per reclassified symbol. Measured from tests/conformance/symbol_fixture_coverage.v1.json:
  __isoc99_sscanf   covered=True   modes=[hardened, strict]  cases=2
  __isoc99_vsscanf  covered=True   modes=[hardened, strict]  cases=2
  vsscanf           covered=False  modes=[]                  cases=0
So two are promotable today and vsscanf is not. Promoting only the two would leave a wrapper
classified above the callee it delegates to, so bd-4habm0 deliberately promoted NONE and left
check_support_matrix_maintenance.sh RED on three honest rows rather than one false one.

DONE = vsscanf gets real strict+hardened conformance coverage (note it takes a va_list, which is
presumably why the fixture harness has never covered it — expect work in frankenlibc-fixture-exec,
not just a fixture JSON), then all three rows go to Implemented in support_matrix.json in one
change, and check_support_matrix_maintenance.sh exits 0. Do NOT regenerate the canonical report to
absorb the diff, and do NOT promote without the evidence the policy asks for.

title: PORT: pidfile_open + pidfile_write + pidfile_close + pidfile_remove + pidfile_fileno (FreeBSD libutil pidfile)
description: FreeBSD/libbsd pidfile(3) family — pidfile_open(path, mode, *otherpid) opens or creates a daemon PID file with an exclusive flock; if another process already holds the lock it returns NULL with errno=EEXIST and writes the locker pid to *otherpid (parsed from the file contents). pidfile_write writes the current pid as ASCII into the file. pidfile_close releases the lock without unlinking (for child-takeover patterns). pidfile_remove unlinks and closes (standard cleanup). pidfile_fileno returns the underlying fd. Used by sshd, mysqld, postgresql, ntpd, and basically every BSD/Linux daemon. Currently missing entirely from frankenlibc-abi. Ship: thin shims in stdlib_abi.rs over the just-landed flopen + pwrite + ftruncate + read + unlink, with a malloc"d struct pidfh storing fd + path so pidfile_remove can unlink without re-resolving the path.
