title: PORT: strtonum (OpenBSD bounded decimal parser)
description: OpenBSD strtonum(nptr, minval, maxval, errstr) parses nptr as a decimal long long integer constrained to [minval, maxval] and returns the value plus an opaque error category through *errstr (NULL on success, "invalid"/"too small"/"too large"/"out of range" on failure). Used by OpenBSD utilities (sshd, pf, bgpd) for safer numeric parsing than strtoll(3) — no errno fiddling, no overflow gotchas, range check baked in. Currently missing from frankenlibc-abi/stdlib_abi.rs. Ship: pure-safe core::stdlib::strtonum::parse returning Result<i64, StrtonumError> with Invalid/TooSmall/TooLarge/InvalidRange variants + thin abi shim that maps the error to OpenBSD-canonical static error strings.

title: Refine authoritative proof lanes with environment manifests and replayable host probes
description:
Supplemental refinement for bd-9vzzk. Authoritative mounted, xfstests, performance, and long-campaign lanes need a shared environment manifest so evidence can be replayed or rejected when host state drifts. A pass from an unknown worker, stale kernel/FUSE state, changed helper binary, or mismatched mount namespace should not upgrade public claims.

Scope: define an environment manifest consumed by authoritative lanes: lane id, environment kind, host/worker id, kernel, FUSE/fuser versions, mkfs/helper versions, cargo/toolchain, mount namespace, privilege model, filesystem tools, resource limits, git SHA, artifact schema version, probe timestamp, freshness TTL, and replay command.

Required proof before close:
1. Unit/schema tests reject environment manifests missing lane id, host/worker identity, kernel/FUSE details, helper versions where relevant, privilege model, resource limits, git SHA, timestamp, TTL, and replay command.
2. Unit tests cover stale manifest, host mismatch, worker mismatch, helper version mismatch, toolchain mismatch, privilege downgrade, missing /dev/fuse, changed mount namespace, resource-limit mismatch, and non-authoritative local run.
3. E2E/dry-run smoke emits manifests for local, host-skip, and fixture authoritative cases, then verifies readiness gates reject stale or mismatched manifests while preserving actionable remediation.

title: strtonum failure paths set errno
description: OpenBSD strtonum returns 0 on failure, stores the canonical errstr, and sets errno: EINVAL for invalid input or invalid min/max, ERANGE for too-small/too-large values. FrankenLibC currently returns the right errstr but leaves errno unchanged, so callers cannot distinguish failure through errno. Add focused regression coverage and set ABI errno on every failure path.
close_reason:
The errno writes were already on main (cf0a8f13a, stdlib_abi.rs strtonum sets EINVAL for invalid/NULL-nptr/inverted-range and ERANGE for out-of-range). The bead's other half -- 'add focused regression coverage' -- was missing: every one of the 13 pre-existing strtonum arms asserted the errstr channel ONLY, so nothing could fail if the errno half regressed. Gate added in 1297152c8.

EVIDENCE (remote via RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2, -j2, CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/tmp/rch_target_frankenlibc_greenglen):
  cargo test -j2 -p frankenlibc-abi --test stdlib_abi_test strtonum -> 18 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored.

GATE (crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/stdlib_abi_test.rs), six arms:
  - strtonum_invalid_input_sets_einval, strtonum_null_nptr_sets_einval, strtonum_inverted_range_sets_einval -> EINVAL;
  - strtonum_out_of_range_sets_erange -> ERANGE for both too-small and too-large. Note the deliberate contrast with the inverted-range arm: minval > maxval is a caller bug that OpenBSD reports as EINVAL, not ERANGE, even for a parseable number;
  - strtonum_sets_errno_even_with_null_errstr -> the case that motivated the bead. With errstr NULL there is no other failure channel, which is exactly the 'callers cannot distinguish failure' complaint;
  - strtonum_success_preserves_caller_errno -> OpenBSD saves errno on entry and restores it on success (ev[0].err = errno; ... errno = ev[error].err), so a successful parse is errno-transparent and must not leak ERANGE from its own internal conversion. Asserted with an ENOTTY sentinel.

NEGATIVE CASE (proved, not asserted): with set_abi_errno removed from the Err branch and the NULL-nptr early return, EXACTLY the new arms failed -- 5 of them, the errno-preservation arm correctly unaffected since it exercises the success path -- while ALL 13 pre-existing errstr arms stayed GREEN. That is the filed bug reproduced precisely: errstr channel intact, errno channel dead. Probe then removed; 'git diff --stat' on stdlib_abi.rs is now EMPTY, i.e. the source is byte-identical to HEAD.

NO REGRESSION: cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test stdlib_abi_test -> 401 passed / 12 failed. Same binary at clean HEAD via rch exec --base HEAD --clean-overlay --no-overlay -> 395 passed / 12 failed. The delta is exactly my 6 new tests; the 12 failures are unchanged and are all *_preserves_unprivileged_eperm_like_host (fsopen/fsmount/fspick/move_mount), which fail because the remote worker runs as ROOT and so does not get the unprivileged EPERM the tests expect. Pre-existing and environmental.

GATES: rustfmt --edition 2024 on the touched file: clean, and it rewrote only my own added lines (git diff --stat = 93 insertions, 0 deletions), so no other agent's formatting was disturbed. clippy -p frankenlibc-abi --all-targets -D warnings: zero findings in the touched file. ubs: exit 1 both before and after (verified against the HEAD version extracted to a scratch path) -- standard FFI/test finding class, no new class introduced.

SCOPE: test-only commit. No src change was needed, and I verified that claim by removing the errno writes and watching only the new arms fail. NOTE: strtonum is an OpenBSD function with no glibc counterpart, so there is no live-incumbent oracle available for it; the gate gates against the documented OpenBSD contract rather than a differential arm. source_commit=1c43977ee -> 1297152c8. Unrelated working-tree changes by other agents were not reverted or disturbed.

title: ffs-harness: ondisk_parse benches missing dx_hash latency floor across hash versions
description:
Finding (via /profiling-software-performance skill, sixth visit,
different target): `dx_hash` (crates/ffs-ondisk/src/ext4.rs:4720) is
the ext4 directory hash function called on every htree directory
lookup. It dispatches across 5 hash variants (LEGACY,
LEGACY_UNSIGNED, HALF_MD4, TEA, TEA_UNSIGNED) plus the half-md4
fallback for unknown versions. Each variant has different
performance characteristics — LEGACY is a simple multiply-add loop
(~10 cycles/byte); HALF_MD4 runs an MD4 round transform per 32-byte
chunk; TEA runs a Feistel round per chunk.

There is NO bench for any of these in the `ondisk` criterion gate.
A regression in any of them — accidentally swapping the LEGACY
multiplier, mis-aligning the MD4 chunk loop, or replacing TEA's
Feistel rounds with a slower abstraction — would silently slow
htree lookups without tripping any existing perf gate.

The proptest layer (bd-590tc) and fuzz coverage exist for
correctness; this bead adds the latency floor.

Acceptance: bench function in
crates/ffs-harness/benches/ondisk_parse.rs that exercises each
hash version on a representative directory-name workload (a fixed
set of 32 names of varying lengths). Registered in the existing
`ondisk` criterion_group!. Verified via
`rch exec -- cargo check -p ffs-harness --benches`.
notes: Shipped: bench_ext4_dx_hash function in crates/ffs-harness/benches/ondisk_parse.rs covering all 6 dx_hash version dispatches (LEGACY signed/unsigned, HALF_MD4 signed/unsigned, TEA signed/unsigned). Uses 32 representative directory names of varying lengths (4-67 bytes) to exercise both single-chunk and multi-chunk paths in HALF_MD4 (32-byte chunks) and TEA (16-byte chunks). Registered in the ondisk criterion_group!. Pairs with bd-590tc (dx_hash MR proptests for correctness). Verified via rch exec -- cargo check -p ffs-harness --benches (Finished in 57.64s).

title: sysconf has no RAW-integer-code differential gate — named-constant gate misses _SC_ codes the libc crate omits (config-table blind spot)
tempnam ignores TMPDIR env + dir-existence (glibc __path_search precedence)
close_reason:
FIXED + GATED. Commit 9ecf8e0b7.

BLOCKER COMMENT REFUTED BY READING THE CODE. It claimed 'superseded by d7d90fcc4 (tempnam honors TMPDIR and directory existence); current implementation performs glibc-style candidate selection before allocation'. At HEAD tempnam did none of that: dir==NULL hardcoded /tmp (Cow::Borrowed(b"/tmp")), TMPDIR was never read, no directory-existence check existed anywhere in the function, and the default prefix was 'tmp'. Second false 'superseded' claim today after bd-c7cs3h.

GROUND TRUTH (measured on live glibc 2.42 with a compiled C probe and two real fixture directories, not recalled) — the precedence is the OPPOSITE of the natural reading:
  TMPDIR unset,  dir=tdA           -> tdA
  TMPDIR unset,  dir=/nonexistent  -> /tmp     an unusable dir is SKIPPED
  TMPDIR=tdB,    dir=NULL          -> tdB
  TMPDIR=tdB,    dir=tdA           -> tdB      TMPDIR OUTRANKS the argument
  TMPDIR=bad,    dir=tdA           -> tdA
  TMPDIR=bad,    dir=NULL          -> /tmp
  pfx=NULL          -> 'file'   (NOT 'tmp')
  pfx=''            -> 'file'   (empty counts as absent)
  pfx='abcdefghij'  -> 'abcde'  (truncated to 5)

So FOUR divergences, of which the bead title names one:
  1. TMPDIR ignored entirely
  2. a non-existent dir argument used anyway instead of falling back
  3. default prefix 'tmp' instead of 'file' (and empty pfx not treated as absent)
  4. no ENOENT path when nothing is usable
(fl's existing 5-byte prefix truncation was already correct.)

IMPLEMENTATION (crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs):
- new tempnam_direxists(): stat + S_ISDIR, so a path that exists but is NOT a directory is rejected exactly like a missing one, matching glibc's direxists.
- new tempnam_path_search_dir(): glibc's __path_search(..., try_tmpdir=1) order — TMPDIR (via secure_getenv, as glibc does, so a set-user-ID program cannot be redirected by a hostile environment) if it names a real directory; else the caller's dir if it does; else /tmp; else None -> caller sets ENOENT and returns NULL. glibc's second fallback branch (P_tmpdir != "/tmp" then try "/tmp") is DEAD on Linux because the two are equal, so it is collapsed rather than transcribed.
- tempnam(): routes through the above and defaults an absent OR EMPTY prefix to 'file'.

GATE: crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/conformance_diff_tempnam.rs (new file; the only prior mention of tempnam in the test tree was in unistd_abi_test.rs, which did not cover directory selection).
- tempnam_directory_precedence_matches_glibc: all 8 rows of the matrix above vs LIVE glibc, using two created fixture directories and a path asserted not to exist.
- tempnam_prefix_defaults_and_truncation_match_glibc: NULL / empty / short / exactly-5 / over-length.
- tempnam_reports_enoent_when_no_directory_is_usable: TMPDIR and dir both unusable must still SUCCEED into /tmp (the fallback, not an error), which states the contract without requiring /tmp to be removed.
glibc reached by dlsym with assert_ne against fl's own address, so a release test build cannot compare fl to itself.

SCOPE, deliberately: the generated SUFFIX is not compared. tempnam guarantees only uniqueness, and fl's pid+counter suffix legitimately differs from glibc's six random characters; asserting it would make the gate fail for something that is not the contract (the bd-0qltjh lesson). The directory and prefix components are extracted from each returned path and compared.

NEGATIVE CASES chosen to separate the two plausible wrong readings: TMPDIR=bad + dir=tdA must yield tdA, so an implementation that ALWAYS prefers TMPDIR fails; and a 10-byte prefix must not start with 'abcdef', so an untruncated implementation fails while still satisfying starts_with. Each arm additionally asserts what the ORACLE produced, because an implementation ignoring both TMPDIR and dir and always answering /tmp would satisfy fl==glibc on several rows.

EVIDENCE (rch remote, source commit 9ecf8e0b7):
  cargo test -j2 --no-fail-fast -p frankenlibc-abi --test conformance_diff_tempnam -> 3 passed; 0 failed
  cargo clippy -j2 -p frankenlibc-abi --lib --test conformance_diff_tempnam -- -D warnings -> zero findings on touched files

Unrelated agent changes were not reverted.

title: [test-integrity] malloc_abi.rs unit tests can NEVER run — 'pub mod malloc_abi' is #[cfg(not(test))], so its #[cfg(test)] mod tests is excluded from the lib test binary
description:
FOUND 2026-07-25 (MagentaCondor, Lane B, while adding bd-ummyux regression tests).

crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/lib.rs:67-68

    #[cfg(not(test))]
    pub mod malloc_abi;

The gate is deliberate and correct -- the comment above it explains that malloc_abi defines
no_mangle malloc/free/memcpy/strlen that would shadow the system allocator inside the test binary
and cause infinite recursion or deadlock.

THE CONSEQUENCE NOBODY NOTICED: because the whole module is compiled out of the `--lib` test
target, the `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` INSIDE malloc_abi.rs is also compiled out. Those tests are
dead code. They have never executed, and `cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --lib` will report success
without running them.

CURRENTLY DEAD (malloc_abi.rs, ~L4725):
  - allocator_metrics_snapshot_jsonl_exports_dashboard_fields
  - malloc_stats_reset_for_harness_clears_exported_snapshot

EVIDENCE: `cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --lib -- --list` reports 203 tests and NONE are
`malloc_abi::tests::*`; filtering on `--lib bump` after adding two clearly-named bump tests to that
module ran 0 tests with "203 filtered out". Moving the same tests verbatim into
tests/malloc_abi_test.rs made them run and pass.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE TWO ORPHANS: this is a silent trap for every future contributor. Someone
adding a unit test to the allocator's own file gets a green run that proves nothing -- exactly the
"the bench never executed the code under test" failure class the campaign's V3 criterion exists to
catch, but in the test suite rather than the benchmark suite.

FIX OPTIONS (pick one, needs an owner decision):
  (a) Move the two orphaned tests to tests/malloc_abi_test.rs, which is where the working allocator
      tests already live, and delete the now-empty `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` from malloc_abi.rs.
  (b) Keep the module but add a compile-time tripwire so the mistake cannot recur silently, e.g. a
      `#[cfg(all(test, not(feature = "...")))] compile_error!("malloc_abi unit tests do not run; put
      them in tests/malloc_abi_test.rs")` inside the module.
  (a) is the smaller change; (b) is the one that prevents recurrence. Doing both is cheap.

AUDIT FOLLOW-ON: check whether any OTHER module in frankenlibc-abi is cfg-gated the same way and
carries a dead `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`. `grep -n "cfg(not(test))" crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/lib.rs`
is the starting point.

NOT FIXED HERE: bd-ummyux's regression tests were simply placed in tests/malloc_abi_test.rs instead,
so nothing is blocked on this. Filed so the trap gets closed deliberately rather than rediscovered.
notes:
FIXED 2026-07-26 (MagentaCondor, Lane B). Option (a)+(b) from the description, both.

(a) REHOMED the two orphaned tests to crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/malloc_abi_test.rs, where they
    link the real surface and actually run:
      - allocator_metrics_snapshot_jsonl_exports_dashboard_fields
      - malloc_stats_reset_for_harness_clears_exported_snapshot
    The first needed two private items (MallocStatsSnapshot, export_alloc_stats_snapshot_jsonl_from_
    snapshot). Rather than widen the public API with an internal record type, added a positional
    hook `malloc_stats_snapshot_jsonl_for_tests([usize; 7], bead, run, mode)` so the struct stays
    private. The second moved verbatim, plus the file's existing test_lock() since it mutates
    process-global stats and the integration suite runs tests in parallel (it did not need that
    lock before, because it never ran).
    The dead `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` block in malloc_abi.rs is replaced by a comment explaining
    why no unit tests may live there.

(b) TRIPWIRE: crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/malloc_abi_no_dead_unit_tests.rs, two tests.
      1. cfg_not_test_modules_contain_no_unit_tests -- fails if `#[cfg(test)]` reappears in any
         module listed in CFG_NOT_TEST_MODULES (currently src/malloc_abi.rs), with a message that
         explains the trap and points at the right file.
      2. lib_rs_still_gates_the_module_out_of_the_test_target -- fails if the `#[cfg(not(test))]`
         gate on `pub mod malloc_abi` disappears. Without this the first test would silently become
         vacuous: if the gate is ever removed, unit tests there WOULD run and the tripwire should be
         retired deliberately rather than left asserting nothing.

WHY A TRIPWIRE AND NOT JUST A COMMENT: the mistake produces no warning, no error, and a PASSING
`cargo test --lib` run. Nothing in the language catches it, so it needs an external check. This is
the same failure class as the perf campaign's V3 criterion ("the bench never executed the code under
test") but in the test suite, which is worse -- a green test run is precisely what people trust.

AUDIT DONE: `grep -n "cfg(not(test))" crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/lib.rs` -- malloc_abi is the only
module carrying that gate, so it is the only one that could hide dead unit tests. CFG_NOT_TEST_MODULES
is a list so the guard extends if another module is ever gated the same way.

NOTE: Agent Mail was unreachable ("Unable to connect") when this work started, so the edit surface
could not be reserved. git status was clean at the time (no peer mid-edit) and the only files touched
are malloc_abi.rs + the two test files.

title: P0: gcvt writes past tracked small output buffer
description:
[CRITICAL] The gcvt ABI wrapper constructs a mutable slice from the caller's raw buffer using ndigit + 32 bytes, capped at 512, without consulting malloc_abi::known_remaining(buf). A tracked caller allocation smaller than that assumed size can therefore be turned into an overlong &mut [u8] and written past before the core formatter truncates to that artificial slice size.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/stdlib_abi.rs:3218 accepts the raw caller buf pointer.
- crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/stdlib_abi.rs:3226-3228 assumes buf_size = ndigit.max(0) + 32 (min 512 cap) and calls from_raw_parts_mut(buf, buf_size).
- crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/stdlib_abi.rs:3229 passes that slice to frankenlibc_core::stdlib::gcvt, which writes rendered bytes plus a NUL up to the slice length.
- The module already imports known_remaining and uses it broadly for other stdlib pointer surfaces, but gcvt does not cap the writable slice by the tracked allocation.

Repro shape: p = malloc(1); call gcvt(123.456, 10, p). Expected hardened/TSM behavior is to cap to known_remaining(p) or reject safely. Actual code creates a 42-byte mutable slice from a 1-byte tracked allocation and may write beyond it.

Fix direction: compute tracked = known_remaining(buf as usize); choose a writable length bounded by tracked when present, and return buf after writing only within that length. Add an ABI regression using malloc-backed 1-byte and 2-byte buffers so the wrapper preserves the canary/neighbor bytes while still NUL-terminating where possible.
close_reason: fixed: gcvt caps malloc-tracked output buffers with known_remaining; validation: stdlib_abi_test gcvt, diff_gcvt_cases, cargo check/clippy -p frankenlibc-abi, UBS

title: [systemic] 914 of 1318 fixture arms name FL ITSELF as their oracle — an arm recorded from fl's own output cannot detect fl being wrong
description:
Measured 2026-08-15 over tests/conformance/fixtures/*.json:

  fixture cases carrying an oracle_source : 1318
    of which oracle_source starts 'FrankenLibC' :  914   (69%)

These arms were recorded by running fl and writing down what it printed. Their host_output is
'SKIP' with host_parity=true, so nothing ever compared them to a host. An arm like this is green
by construction on the day it is written and stays green no matter how wrong fl is; the only way
it ever goes red is if fl CHANGES -- which inverts the gate, because a fix looks like a regression.

FOUR CONFIRMED WRONG ARMS FOUND IN ONE SESSION, all four with oracle_source='FrankenLibC ...':
  freopen_null_path_class_{strict,hardened}     expected a NULL return; live glibc returns the
  freopen64_null_path_class_{strict,hardened}     SAME FILE* (POSIX null-path mode change)
  fcrypt_null_inputs_{strict,hardened}          expected NULL+EINVAL; live libxcrypt returns the
                                                  non-NULL token '*0' with EINVAL
  acct_privilege_denied_{strict,hardened}       pinned EPERM, unreachable as root (EFAULT)
  fsmount_permission_gate_{strict,hardened}     pinned EPERM, unreachable as root (EBADF)
Fixed in e2d1f63a7 and its follow-up. That is a 100% wrong rate among the arms in this class that
anything happened to execute -- which is the point: nobody had executed most of them.

THIS IS NOT A REQUEST TO REWRITE 914 ARMS. Most are probably right. The work is to make the class
VISIBLE and to convert the ones where a host oracle exists, highest-risk first:
  (a) arms pinning an errno CONSTANT for a call whose errno is privilege- or container-dependent
      (the acct/fsmount class) -- these are unpassable on the root CI workers and are the reason
      gates sit permanently red. Grep candidates: expected values matching _ERRNO_(EPERM|EACCES).
  (b) arms pinning a pointer/NULL-ness contract where glibc has a documented non-NULL behaviour
      (the freopen/fcrypt class).
  (c) arms for symbols glibc actually exports -- those can become real differentials in the same
      process, which is what the repo already does in conformance_diff_nice_eperm.rs.

The three fixes landed today all took the same shape and are worth copying: call the host (or the
raw syscall, where glibc has no wrapper) on the SAME input in the SAME process, and make the
expected token a parity verdict rather than a constant. That is privilege-independent, container-
independent, and strictly stronger than what it replaces.

DONE = (a) enumerated and converted or precondition-stated. Do NOT close this by reclassifying
oracle_source strings; the string is a symptom, the missing host comparison is the defect.

comments.text:
PROGRESS, not closed. Class (a) enumerated and found ALREADY CONVERTED; a stronger defect found in the same neighbourhood and fixed (commit BLOCKED on a lease, see bottom).

CLASS (a) ENUMERATION, method so nobody repeats it. oracle_source lives at cases[].inputs.oracle_source, NOT at case level — a case-level scan returns 0 and looks like a clean result, which is how I first mis-measured it. Corrected counts at HEAD: 1318 cases carry an oracle_source, 816 start with 'FrankenLibC' (the bead says 914; the delta is what e2d1f63a7 and its follow-ups already converted). Privilege-pinned arms corpus-wide, ANY oracle: 13 total. Every one of the acct/fsmount/fsopen/fspick arms now names a host or raw-syscall oracle and its expected token is a '..._MATCHES_HOST_...' parity verdict — i.e. class (a) is DONE. The 2 remaining fl-oracled hits my first grep flagged were false positives: the token 'EACCESS_NULL_RC_-1' contains the substring EACCES but the arm is eaccess(NULL) returning -1, not a privilege errno.

WHAT I FOUND INSTEAD, worse than the oracle_source symptom: crates/frankenlibc_conformance/src/lib.rs execute_execve_case never called execve at all — not fl's, not the host's. It read the fixture's own inputs.pathname, returned the literal "-1" when that string happened to be "/etc/passwd" and "NO_RETURN" otherwise, then wrapped it in non_host_execution (host_output SKIP, host_parity true by construction). Both spawn_exec_ops execve arms asserted a value the executor derived from their own input, so they passed identically whether fl's execve was correct, wrong, or deleted. execute_posix_spawn_case has the same shape (string-matches path.starts_with("/nonexistent")) and is NOT yet fixed — next lever.

Note also spawn_exec_ops_conformance_test.rs:396: the anti-SKIP guard exists but is scoped to case.function == "system", so for every other function a SKIP host_output satisfies the host_parity assertion vacuously. Generalising that guard is the cheap ratchet that would have caught this class; it belongs to this bead.

FIX (gated, uncommitted): both execve arms now execute. Non-executable path -> host execve and fl execve on the same args in the same process, compare rc AND errno, parity verdict; the passing token carries NO errno on purpose, since pinning it back in re-introduces the host-dependence the verdict removes. Executable path -> each library's execve runs in its own forked child (same fork/waitpid shape as the clone arm in that file); a child that RETURNS from execve exits 127, so a wrapper that fails to exec is a divergence, not a pass. Gate, harness 'cargo test -j 1 --no-fail-fast -p frankenlibc-harness --test spawn_exec_ops_conformance_test -- --test-threads=1': ok. 12 passed; 0 failed on worker hz1, replicated on worker hz2. The green is the non-vacuity proof — the fixture now demands the parity tokens, so the old stub's "-1"/"NO_RETURN" would fail.

Both files (that one and tests/conformance/fixtures/spawn_exec_ops.json, 5 lines) sit uncommitted in the working tree and MUST land together — the fixture alone turns the gate red. title: PoR for cryptographic durability audit (Graveyard Entry 11.11)
description:
# PoR for cryptographic durability audit (Graveyard Entry 11.11)

## GOAL
Implement Proofs of Retrievability (PoR) for cryptographic verification that stored data is intact and retrievable, without reading the entire dataset.

## BACKGROUND
From Alien CS Graveyard 11.11: PoR (Juels-Kaliski 2007, Shacham-Waters 2008) allows a verifier to challenge a storage system with random queries. The storage system responds with proofs that specific blocks exist and are correct. If the proofs verify, the entire dataset is retrievable with high probability.

## DESIGN
- Challenge: verifier sends random block indices + random coefficients
- Response: storage computes linear combination of challenged blocks weighted by coefficients
- Verification: verifier checks response against precomputed authenticators
- Authenticators: computed once at file creation, stored alongside data

## APPLICABILITY
- Future feature: useful for cloud/remote storage verification
- Complementary to RaptorQ: PoR proves data exists, RaptorQ repairs it if it doesn't
- Useful for auditing: periodic PoR challenges prove filesystem integrity without full scan

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] PoR authenticator generation at file creation
- [ ] Challenge-response protocol implemented
- [ ] Verification: false positive rate < 2^-128
- [ ] Benchmark: challenge/response time for 1GB file
acceptance_criteria: PoR authenticator generation at file creation time. Challenge-response protocol implemented with configurable challenge count. Verification: false positive rate below 2^-128. Authenticators stored alongside data in reserved metadata area. Benchmark: challenge/response time for 1GB file. Benchmark: authenticator generation time per MB. Unit tests: generate authenticators, challenge, verify for small files. Unit tests: corrupted block causes verification failure. Unit tests: uncorrupted file passes all challenges. Property test: random challenge sets always verify on intact data.

title: setjmp_abi tests::longjmp_entrypoint_terminates_with_enosys_payload_in_tests flakes under high parallelism
description:
## Repro

```bash
for i in {1..8}; do
  CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/rch_target_frankenlibc_cc cargo test \
    -p frankenlibc-abi --tests -- --test-threads=16 \
    | grep -E "FAILED|invalid size|signal:"
done
```

After ~3-4 iterations the unit test
`setjmp_abi::tests::longjmp_entrypoint_terminates_with_enosys_payload_in_tests`
asserts FAILED. Running with `--test-threads=1` does not reproduce.
Found while stress-testing the bd-wbqeo per-thread reentry refactor;
the failure is unrelated to that change (also reproduces against
prior commits — file history shows the test pattern is unchanged).

## Suspected cause

The setjmp/longjmp test uses a shared
`OnceLock<Mutex<HashMap<usize, JumpRegistryEntry>>>` keyed by env
pointer address (crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/setjmp_abi.rs:44). The
unit test creates a stack-local `marker: [u64; 16]` and uses its
address as the env_addr key. Two test functions running on different
worker threads get distinct stack addresses, but a single worker
thread that runs tests sequentially reuses the same stack frame
addresses across tests — the registry entry from a prior test
remains for that key and is overwritten by the next capture. The
new entry's bytes should match the new capture's mem_bytes, but
under contention or specific scheduling the read-back of mem_bytes
in restore_env compares against a stale or partially-updated entry,
returning EFAULT (22) instead of triggering the deferred
ENOSYS-panic path the test asserts.

The test then panics with errno=22 reason=`invalid_or_foreign_jump_context`
instead of errno=38 reason=`deferred_longjmp_transfer_backend`.

## Fix candidates

1. Test-only: each test should remove its registry entry on exit
   (RAII guard that calls `registry().lock().remove(&env_addr)`
   when the test scope ends).
2. Production: registry could key on (thread_id, env_addr) instead
   of just env_addr — this would handle both intentional cross-
   thread longjmp (illegal per POSIX, EINVAL is correct) and the
   stack-frame-reuse case across sequential tests on the same worker.
3. Test-only: serialize the setjmp tests with a #[serial] attribute
   or a shared TEST_LOCK Mutex so they don't race for stack address
   reuse.

## Severity

[MEDIUM] (P3) — test-only flake, doesn't affect production behavior.
But it does mask real failures by polluting CI noise. Suggest fix #1
(simplest) or #3 (most robust) as the swarm has time.
notes: Fixed in 6ee22896: RegistryEntryGuard RAII wrapper added to all six setjmp_abi unit tests. Validated by 12x stress with --test-threads=16: zero longjmp_entrypoint_terminates_with_enosys_payload_in_tests failures. Three OTHER unrelated flakes surfaced in same sweep — filed separately.

title: [perf][malloc] Swing-2 SUB-STEP B.1: drop the lock-prefixed CAS from allocator guard entry while the process is single-threaded
description:
LEVER. enter_allocator_reentry_guard() claims the per-thread slot with compare_exchange(0,1,AcqRel,Acquire) on EVERY malloc and EVERY free. The matched no-call-graph profile on bd-65p87u attributes 8.72 percent self to enter_allocator_reentry_guard with 95.18 percent of that frame on the locked CAS, and the per-crate GUARD_AB microbench reads 5.63-7.45 ns/call, i.e. two lock-prefixed RMWs per malloc/free pair against a deployed pair cost of 32.55 ns (malloc_st_probe, vmi1149989) / 68.386 ns (incumbent_coverage_ab --family malloc_free --fl-deepbind, hz2, ratio_median 12.385414 vs live glibc 5.507 ns).

CLAIM: the RMW is unnecessary while MULTI_THREADED is unlatched, and the contract it enforces is preserved exactly.

EQUIVALENCE ARGUMENT (this is the 'separate signal-reentrancy proof' bd-65p87u asks for):
allocator_depth lives in AllocatorReentrySlot, which is bound to exactly one live kernel tid by the slot.tid CAS; no second live thread can reach another thread's depth word. So the CAS never arbitrates between threads on this word -- its only remaining racer is an async signal handler on THIS thread. Against that racer a relaxed load + release store is equivalent:
  (a) handler lands before the load  -> it sees 0, enters, restores 0, we then see 0 and enter. Same as CAS.
  (b) handler lands after the store  -> it sees 1, takes bootstrap passthrough. Same as CAS.
  (c) handler lands INSIDE the load/store window (the only window the CAS does not have) -> it sees 0 and enters, but we have not yet touched segment_local (the store strictly precedes every access), and the handler restores 0 before returning. Its access nests strictly inside our pre-access window, so segment_local accesses remain sequenced, never overlapping -- which is the invariant the unsafe impl Sync comment states.
  (d) handler never returns (siglongjmp) -> depth is left at 1 and the thread falls to bootstrap passthrough forever, identically under both implementations.
The MULTI_THREADED gate is retained anyway, because under MT a recycled TCB/tid can alias slots (bd-35hjg.3.1) and the CAS is the cheaper thing to keep than a new aliasing proof.

NEGATIVE CASE a naive implementation fails: an unconditional store(1) that skips the zero-check lets a NESTED entry succeed. The gate asserts that with depth forced to 1 a second entry returns None (bootstrap passthrough) and that the depth word is restored to 0 on drop -- in BOTH the ST and the MT-latched state, so the new branch cannot be green only on the branch that was already covered.

DONE = the gate above passes with a non-zero counted pass line, all allocator conformance stays green, and the deployed ratio is re-measured with the SAME harness/worker as the banked baseline (incumbent_coverage_ab --family malloc_free --fl-deepbind on hz2, both A/A nulls inside tolerance). Report the ratio whichever way it moves; a null-failed or worse row gets ledgered as a rejection and reverted.
close_reason: Lever executed, gated, measured on a live incumbent, and REJECTED: ~0.8% fl-side change, vs-glibc ratio non-separating. Source reverted; evidence banked in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md 2026-08-15 (BlackThrush) and in the bead comment above, including the retry predicate that closes this sub-vein.

title: fix(poll): ppoll/pselect clobbered caller's timeout (kernel writeback not hidden)
description: ppoll and pselect passed the caller's timeout pointer straight to the kernel ppoll/pselect6 syscalls. The Linux kernel WRITES the remaining time back into that struct, but POSIX and glibc require these (unlike select) to leave the caller's timeout UNMODIFIED -- glibc hides the kernel behavior by passing a local copy. fl was clobbering the caller's timespec (e.g. zeroing it on timeout), corrupting any caller that reuses or inspects its timeout. title: ffs-mvcc: PersistentMvccStore lock-ordering invariant is undocumented and untested
description:
Finding (via /deadlock-finder-and-fixer skill, Class 1: classic
mutex deadlock prevention): `PersistentMvccStore` (crates/ffs-mvcc/
src/persist.rs:176) holds three `parking_lot::RwLock`s — `store`,
`wal`, and `stats` — and the production code paths consistently
acquire them in the order **store → wal → stats**:

  * `commit_with_options` (l. 404→422→437): store(W) → wal(W) → stats(W)
  * `checkpoint`          (l. 526→565):    store(R) → stats(W)
  * `truncate_wal`        (l. 589→599→628): store(R) → wal(W) → stats(W)

Pairwise the order is consistent everywhere. But:

  1. **No struct-level doc comment names the invariant.** A future
     contributor could introduce a function like `repack_wal` that
     acquires `wal.write()` before `store.write()` and instantly
     create an AB-BA deadlock with `commit_with_options`, which
     holds `store.write()` while waiting on `wal.write()`. The
     existing inline comments on `checkpoint`/`truncate_wal` explain
     WHY they hold `store` first, but there's no central pin.

  2. **No regression test exercises the lock ordering under
     contention.** All existing tests run commit, checkpoint, and
     truncate_wal serially. A future deadlock would only manifest
     under concurrent load and would silently regress the gate.

This is a Class 1 prevention finding (no existing deadlock — the
audit confirmed the order is currently consistent), but the lack of
a documented + tested invariant makes the code fragile to refactor.

Acceptance: a doc comment on `PersistentMvccStore` names the canonical
order **store → wal → stats** with rationale, and one unit test in
the `tests` module spawns concurrent commit + truncate_wal threads
with a watchdog timeout that fails if any thread hangs (proving the
order holds under contention).
notes: Shipped: struct-level doc on PersistentMvccStore documenting the canonical lock order store → wal → stats with a per-field rank annotation (rank 0/1/2) and a table of production callers showing compliance. Added lock_ordering_under_concurrent_commit_and_truncate regression test that spawns 2 concurrent workers exercising commit (store.W→wal.W→stats.W) and checkpoint+truncate_wal (store.R→{wal.W,stats.W}) with a 15s watchdog that panics on hang. Verified via rch exec -- cargo test -p ffs-mvcc --lib lock_ordering_under_concurrent_commit_and_truncate (passes in 0.16s).

title: error/error_at_line do not flush stdout before writing to stderr (glibc flush_stdout)
close_reason:
GATED (implementation was already present, ungated). Commit 59525fc5e.

The fflush(stdout) is in both error() and error_at_line() with bd-7zdmvd cited at the implementation. What was missing is any arm that could OBSERVE it: every existing test in conformance_diff_error_at_line.rs captures stderr alone, and on stderr a flushed and an unflushed stdout look identical. Third error-family bead in a row with shipped code and no failing-capable gate.

GROUND TRUTH (measured, not recalled) on live glibc 2.42, compiled C probe with stdout+stderr joined to one pipe (so stdout is fully buffered) and a marker written to stdout first, read with cat -A:
  error(0,0,"msg") -> 'MARKER' then './p3: msg'   <- flushed ahead of the diagnostic
  warnx("msg")     -> 'p3: msg' then 'MARKER'     <- err.h never flushes

GATE: crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/conformance_diff_error_at_line.rs
- error_flushes_buffered_stdout_before_the_diagnostic
- error_at_line_flushes_buffered_stdout_before_the_diagnostic
  Each joins fd 1 and fd 2 to one pipe, writes a marker to the impl's OWN stdout (glibc's via dlsym on the stdout global; fl's via io_internal_abi::native_stdio_stream_ptr(1)), calls the diagnostic, and compares transcripts byte for byte. Both impls' streams are flushed INSIDE the redirect window, so a non-flushing callee's marker still arrives -- after the message rather than before -- which is exactly the distinction under test and leaves no buffered residue for the next arm.
  Each also asserts what the ORACLE produced (glibc's transcript must START with the marker), not merely that the arms agree: if both impls stopped flushing, byte equality would still hold and the arm would be vacuous.
- warnx_does_not_flush_stdout_so_the_arms_above_can_fail: NEGATIVE CONTROL in the same harness. err.h's warnx writes to stderr without flushing stdout, so its marker must TRAIL the message in both impls. If it ever leads, the harness has stopped discriminating and the two arms above mean nothing.

title: Implement RaptorQ symbol refresh on dirty group flush
description:
# Implement RaptorQ symbol refresh on dirty group flush

## GOAL
Ensure repair symbols are regenerated when block groups are modified, as mandated by spec §0.4: "A block write that never triggers repair symbol refresh for its group is a spec-conformance bug."

## BACKGROUND
Currently repair symbols are generated at image creation. When blocks are modified:
1. Group becomes "stale" (symbols no longer match data)
2. Must regenerate before corruption can be recovered
3. Two modes: lazy (on next scrub) or eager (on fsync)

## TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS

### 1. Dirty Group Tracking
```rust
pub struct DirtyGroupTracker {
    dirty: BitVec,  // One bit per group
}

impl DirtyGroupTracker {
    pub fn mark_dirty(&mut self, group: GroupNumber);
    pub fn is_dirty(&self, group: GroupNumber) -> bool;
    pub fn clear(&mut self, group: GroupNumber);
    pub fn dirty_groups(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = GroupNumber>;
}
```

### 2. Refresh Triggers
- **Lazy**: Background scrub regenerates symbols for dirty groups
- **Eager (fsync)**: Regenerate immediately for committed groups
- **Configurable**: MountConfig.repair_refresh_policy

### 3. Refresh Flow
```rust
pub fn refresh_group_symbols(
    group: GroupNumber,
    device: &dyn BlockDevice,
    storage: &mut RepairGroupStorage,
    cx: &Cx,
) -> Result<()> {
    // 1. Read all blocks in group
    // 2. Regenerate RaptorQ symbols
    // 3. Write to repair storage slots
    // 4. Clear dirty flag
}
```

### 4. Budget Integration
- Refresh respects Cx budget
- Can be interrupted and resumed
- Progress tracked per-group

## TESTS
1. Unit: Dirty tracking set/clear
2. Integration: Write marks group dirty
3. Integration: Scrub refreshes dirty group
4. Integration: fsync refreshes if eager mode
5. E2E: Corruption after refresh -> recovery works

## LOGGING
- Mark dirty (trace): group number, cause
- Refresh start (debug): group, block count
- Refresh complete (info): group, duration, symbol count

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. Every modified group eventually refreshed
2. Lazy mode: refreshed within scrub interval
3. Eager mode: refreshed on fsync
4. Recovery works for refreshed groups
close_reason: Implemented dirty-group refresh APIs (mark/query/flush), aligned refresh logging, and added flush-path + tracker tests in ffs-repair pipeline; validated via rch cargo test/check/clippy and cargo fmt --check.

title: ffs-ondisk: Ext4Inode::extra_nsec/extra_epoch bit-pack helpers lack metamorphic relation tests
description:
Finding (via /testing-metamorphic skill, NEW target): crates/ffs-ondisk/src/ext4.rs:2725 has Ext4Inode::extra_nsec(extra) = extra >> 2 and extra_epoch(extra) = extra & 0x3 — the bit-pack helpers that decode the on-disk *_extra timestamp field used by every inode timestamp read on ext4 v6+ filesystems. The unit test  covers 4 fixed inputs but ZERO metamorphic-relation proptests pin the algebraic contract.

The bit-pack contract is critical: extra is a u32 split into [nsec:30][epoch:2]. The kernel uses bits [1:0] as epoch extension (adds 2^32 seconds to timestamps) and bits [31:2] as nanoseconds (max valid ~10^9). A regression that swapped the masks would silently corrupt every timestamp on every ext4 v6+ image — a high-leverage class of bug invisible to substring-style tests.

Untested algebraic laws:
  * MR1 — Bit-pack inverse: for any u32 x, (extra_nsec(x) << 2) | extra_epoch(x) == x
  * MR2 — Epoch bound: extra_epoch(x) ≤ 3 for all u32 x
  * MR3 — Nsec bound: extra_nsec(x) ≤ 0x3FFF_FFFF for all u32 x
  * MR4 — Disjoint fields: extra_nsec(epoch_only) == 0 when epoch_only & ~0x3 == 0; extra_epoch(nsec_only) == 0 when nsec_only & 0x3 == 0
  * MR5 — Determinism: same input always gives same output

Pairs with bd-bevt2 (feature flags), bd-jbilz (magic numbers + state flags), bd-k81lq (reserved inodes) — those pin SCALAR conformance; this pins the BIT-PACK ALGEBRA.

Acceptance: 5 proptest cases in the existing proptest! block at the end of crates/ffs-ondisk/src/ext4.rs.

title: inet_aton parse_bsd_part hex path accepts 0x+N due to Rust from_str_radix sign acceptance
description: Modes-of-reasoning correctness lens on crates/frankenlibc-core/src/inet/mod.rs:259-265. The hex branch of parse_bsd_part does u32::from_str_radix(rest, 16) where rest is the substring after `0x`/`0X`. Rust's u32::from_str_radix permits a leading '+' or '-' sign per its docs, so input `0x+1` parses as 1 — but glibc inet_aton (which strtoul-based libresolv parsers emulate) rejects it because strtoul reads the optional sign BEFORE the base prefix; once `0x` has already been consumed, '+' is not a valid hex digit and parsing terminates with zero digits consumed (failure). The decimal branch is safe (is_ascii_digit guard rejects '+'); the octal branch is safe (0..=7 guard rejects '+'). Only hex is affected, including `0X+`, `0x-`, `0x+abc`. Reproduce: parse_bsd_part("0x+1") returns Some(1); upstream behavior is None. Fix: after stripping the `0x`/`0X` prefix, validate every byte of `rest` is is_ascii_hexdigit before delegating to from_str_radix. Add unit tests for 0x+1, 0x-1, 0X+ABC, and ensure pre-existing valid inputs (0x7f.0.0.1) still parse.

PORT: complete BSD setmode X and copy-perm symbolic modes
description: Mock-code-finder discovery: crates/frankenlibc-core/src/stdlib/setmode.rs documents two unsupported BSD setmode/getmode symbolic-mode features: X conditional execute and u/g/o copy permissions used as perm operands. Today parse() rejects those inputs, which means ABI setmode() returns NULL/EINVAL for valid BSD chmod-style mode strings. Implement a clean safe-Rust extension that preserves the existing setmode bitbox ABI while supporting: (1) X adds execute bits only when current mode is a directory or any execute bit is already set; (2) u/g/o perm operands copy rwx bits from the referenced current-mode class into the target who class for +, -, and = operations. Add focused core unit tests and ABI tests covering file vs directory conditional X, existing-exec conditional X, copy u->g/o and g->u behavior, malformed input rejection, and existing supported cases. Validate with rustfmt, git diff --check, UBS on touched files, br dep cycles, and rch cargo test/check/clippy scoped to frankenlibc-core/frankenlibc-abi setmode surfaces.

title: 5 conformance divergences revealed by relighting glibc_internal_abi_test (isastream fd validation confirmed)
description:
bd-r71n1b relit crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/glibc_internal_abi_test.rs, which had not linked since the glibc 2.42 upgrade. It now runs: 264 passed, 5 FAILED, 24 ignored (commit 84bf6f296).

These 5 are PRE-EXISTING divergences the target could not report while dark. They are NOT caused by the dlvsym shim that relit it — three of them touch no compat symbol at all — and they are DETERMINISTIC, reproducing identically under --test-threads 1:

  inet6_opt_init_initializes_buffer
  isastream_matches_host_default_for_regular_and_invalid_fds
  obsolete_kernel_accounting_stubs_match_host_enosys
  profiling_frequency_and_profil_safe_defaults_are_stable
  res_hnok_rejects_invalid_hostnames

CONFIRMED DETAIL for one, measured against live glibc in the same process:
  isastream(-1):  fl = (rc 0, errno 0)   glibc = (rc -1, errno 9 EBADF)
fl's isastream does not validate the fd — it reports success for a bad descriptor. glibc returns -1/EBADF. (The fd=0 case passes; only the invalid fd diverges.)

One other panic payload was captured without its test name: 'assertion left == right failed, left: 255, right: 0'.

TO GET THE REMAINING DETAILS (the harness swallows per-test stdout in the batch run; run them singly):
  RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 env -u CARGO_TARGET_DIR rch exec -- \
    cargo test -j2 -p frankenlibc-abi --test glibc_internal_abi_test <name> -- --nocapture --test-threads 1
That is how the isastream detail above was obtained.

TREAT THIS AS A NEW BASELINE, NOT A REGRESSION LIST. These arms have not executed in weeks, so some may encode premises that drifted with glibc 2.42 rather than defects in fl — bd-cb59r9 hit exactly that (a deleted test asserted getdomainname(NULL) returns EFAULT when glibc actually SEGFAULTS). For each of the 5, MEASURE the host behaviour before deciding whether fl or the assertion is wrong, and say which in the closure.

DONE = each of the 5 is either fixed in fl with its arm green, or its assertion corrected against measured glibc 2.42 behaviour with the measurement cited. Splitting into per-symbol beads is fine and probably better; the requirement is that none is left silently red, because a permanently-red target is how this one went dark in the first place.

DO NOT relax an assertion to get green without a measurement showing the assertion was wrong.
close_reason: All 5 divergences resolved plus 2 more they concealed; 272/0 green on 0fe9f3fd3

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
2 of 5 RESOLVED in 339f7dac7. glibc_internal_abi_test: 264 -> 266 passed, 5 -> 3 failed.

They went in OPPOSITE directions, which is the point of measuring each one before deciding:

1. isastream — fl WAS WRONG. It ignored its argument and returned 0 for anything, including -1. Measured on live glibc 2.42 (dlvsym, since isastream is compat-only): isastream(-1) -> -1/EBADF, isastream(0) -> 0/0, isastream(1) -> 0/0. fl now fstats the fd and propagates the error, mirroring isfdtype next door.
   ITS TEST WAS ALSO WRONG: it asserted a flat (0, 0) for BOTH fds, i.e. it enshrined 'ignores the descriptor' as the contract. Now per-fd, and it asserts what the ORACLE produced rather than only fl == host — if both sides regressed to ignoring the fd, plain equality would still pass, which is how this survived.

2. res_hnok — THE TEST WAS WRONG, fl was right all along. It asserted 'bad_host.com' is rejected. Measured: res_hnok('bad_host.com') = 1 and res_hnok('good.example.com') = 1, while 'bad host' = 0, '-lead.com' = 0, 'a..b' = 0. glibc's res_hnok is a transport-level sanity check, not an RFC-1123 validator, and underscores are accepted. fl already agreed with the host on every case; only the expectation was wrong. Corrected against measurement and widened to cover accepted AND rejected forms — not relaxed to whatever passed.

So the 'treat this as a new baseline, not a regression list' warning in this bead's description was right: one of the first two was a genuine fl defect and the other was a stale assertion. Keep measuring per item.

REMAINING 3, with their measured diffs (left = fl, right = host):
  obsolete_kernel_accounting_stubs_match_host_enosys  glibc_internal_abi_test.rs:541
      fl=(-1, 38 ENOSYS)  host=(-1, 22 EINVAL)
      Line 541 is the ustat arm. Likely fl returns a blanket ENOSYS where the kernel rejects the
      dev argument with EINVAL first. Probe host ustat(0, NULL) before deciding which side is wrong.
  profiling_frequency_and_profil_safe_defaults_are_stable  glibc_internal_abi_test.rs:5750
      fl=(0, 0)  host=(0, 11 EAGAIN)
      Same return, different errno. Check whether glibc leaves a stale EAGAIN behind rather than
      setting it — if so the ARM is wrong for reading errno on a success path.
  inet6_opt_init_initializes_buffer  glibc_internal_abi_test.rs:2105
      left=255  right=0.  Single scalar, no host arm in the message; read the test to see which
      side 255 is.

Per-test detail command (the batch run swallows stdout):
  RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 env -u CARGO_TARGET_DIR rch exec -- \
    cargo test -j2 -p frankenlibc-abi --test glibc_internal_abi_test <name> -- --nocapture --test-threads 1

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
CLOSED on 0fe9f3fd3. glibc_internal_abi_test: 264 passed / 5 failed at relight (84f5f96/84fb...),
now 272 passed / 0 failed / 24 ignored, verified remotely:
  RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 env -u CARGO_TARGET_DIR rch exec -- cargo test -j2 -p frankenlibc-abi --test glibc_internal_abi_test

All 5 named divergences resolved, and the split was 3 fl defects to 2 stale assertions, which is why
the bead's own "measure each one before deciding" instruction was the load-bearing part:

  1. isastream          fl DEFECT (fixed 339f7dac7) - ignored its fd, returned 0 for -1
  2. res_hnok           TEST WRONG (fixed 339f7dac7) - glibc accepts underscores; fl always agreed
  3. ustat              fl DEFECT - blanket ENOSYS on a false "removed in Linux 4.18" premise.
                        Kernel probed directly: ustat(0,buf) = -1/EINVAL (no superblock for dev 0),
                        ustat(dev("/"),buf) = 0, ustat(dev("/"),NULL) = -1/EFAULT. Now issues
                        SYS_USTAT on x86_64; aarch64 genuinely lacks the syscall so ENOSYS stays.
  4. profil             TEST WRONG - it seeded the HOST errno with EAGAIN and CLEARED fl's, then
                        asserted they were equal, so it compared a survived sentinel against a zero
                        it had written itself. fl and glibc both leave errno alone.
  5. inet6_opt_init     TEST WRONG - asserted the call zeroes the first two header bytes. Measured
                        against live glibc 2.42: ip6h_nxt is left to the caller, ip6h_len comes from
                        the BUFFER length (extlen 8/16/64/2040 give 0/1/7/254), extlen 0/15/-8/2056
                        are rejected with no write, and a NULL extbuf returns 2 for any extlen.
                        fl already matched glibc on every one of those.

TWO MORE were hiding behind #3 and could not be seen while it failed early, which is the real lesson
of this bead - a red arm conceals its successors just as a dark target conceals everything:

  6. vtimes             fl DEFECT - ENOSYS, while glibc keeps a live getrusage wrapper returning 0.
                        Layout derived by measurement (0xAA-filled buffer): 10 words, of which
                        vm_ixrss and vm_maxrss are declared but NEVER assigned. The unit is 1/60 s,
                        not the 1/HZ the header claims: 84 successive carry points of vm_utime were
                        bracketed against getrusage and every one landed on k*1000000/60 us, which
                        rules out both the 16667- and the 16666-per-unit variants.
  7. sprofil            fl DEFECT - ENOSYS, while glibc succeeds and writes the sampling period
                        {0, 1000000/__profile_frequency()} = {0,10000} into tvp regardless of
                        profcnt. fl now matches. It still does not deliver samples and neither does
                        profil next door; that gap is bd-br5a1b, filed rather than papered over.

The new gates are differentials against the live host, not constants. ustat asserts the
kernel-zeroed struct tail and EINVAL on an unmounted device, which a stub cannot fake without
issuing the syscall. vtimes sandwiches each fl call between two host calls and requires every
monotone counter to land in that bracket - that is what pins the time unit, with no formula copied
into the test. sprofil asserts the period written to tvp, which a bare "return 0" fails.

NOT done here, filed instead: bd-br5a1b (profil/sprofil never deliver PC samples).

title: [perf][regression][resolv] getprotobyname_r went 1125 -> 3050 ns since 2026-07-10 while the same-invocation glibc arm held within 6%
description:
Found by bd-5ibpa3's live re-measurement (b60f88348). Not asserted there — that addendum reports
only what was measured; this bead is the follow-up the measurement points at.

THE NUMBERS, both from the same bench group (getprotobyname_r_tcp), same harness, host arm via
dlmopen(LM_ID_NEWLM, "libc.so.6") in the same invocation:

  2026-07-10 (fc181036f, bd-qds9jk, two passes)
     fl 1125.06 / 1124.32 ns      host_glibc 4475.76 / 4646.10 ns    -> 3.98x / 4.13x
  2026-08-08 (this session, 115 samples/arm, rch worker)
     fl 3050.616 ns               host_glibc 4202.232 ns             -> 1.37x
     A/A null arm 3231.263 ns (1.056 vs the fl arm; CIs disjoint, ~5.6% systematic)

WHY THIS IS A REGRESSION AND NOT A MACHINE DIFFERENCE
The host_glibc arm is the built-in control for machine speed, and it barely moved: 4475 -> 4202 ns,
about 6% — consistent with a different-but-comparable box. fl's arm moved 1125 -> 3050 ns, roughly
2.7x SLOWER, measured on that same box in that same invocation. A machine change moves both arms.
One arm moving 2.7x while the other holds within 6% does not.

The A/A null bounds the harness's own resolution at ~5.6%, which is nowhere near large enough to
account for a 2.7x move.

SCOPE / CAUTION
- The 2026-07-10 pass ran on an unknown worker; this one ran on an rch worker. The inference above
  rests on the glibc arm as the control, not on assuming identical hardware. If someone can pin
  both to the same worker, do that first — it would settle it outright.
- fc181036f's own profile said ~92% of this path's self time was allocator bookkeeping
  (malloc_abi::record_free_stats, record_alloc_stats, fallback_insert_sized_index, free). The
  allocator has been under active work since (bd-dcrhgl Swing-2 inline size header, bd-65p87u three
  locked RMW executions per pair). A regression in the shared malloc lane would show up exactly
  here, in an arm whose cost is dominated by it, while leaving the glibc arm untouched. That is a
  hypothesis to test, not a conclusion — start by re-profiling this arm and comparing the frame
  table against the one in fc181036f's commit message.

DONE = the 1125 -> 3050 ns move is either explained (with the explaining change named) or recovered,
with the getprotobyname_r_tcp group re-run under the same contract — live host arm in the same
invocation, A/A null arm reported, bootstrap median CIs — and the ledger updated next to the
2026-08-08 section. If it turns out to be a deliberate trade (e.g. the allocator lane bought
something bigger elsewhere), say so explicitly and record what was bought; do not simply restate
the old ratio.
close_reason:
FIXED. Source commit be12f2191 (fix + ledger), ledger section 2026-08-08 in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md.

CAUSE: e634aff2a AGAIN — the same Jun-26 silent deletion that took internal_fallocate_emulate
(bd-om1s58) and bd-qds9jk's bench hooks (bd-5ibpa3). It reverted bd-qds9jk's SHIPPED lever.
At HEAD, getprotobyname_r and getprotobynumber_r did `std::fs::read(PROTOCOLS_PATH)` plus a linear
re-parse ON EVERY CALL — the pre-index implementation bd-qds9jk replaced — while
`with_protocol_entry_by_name` / `with_protocol_entry_by_number` survived in resolv_abi.rs as DEAD
CODE. clippy had been saying so out loud: "function `with_protocol_entry_by_name` is never used".

IT WAS NOT ONLY PERF. The revert also dropped the `aliases: &[Vec<u8>]` argument from
fill_protoent_r, so p_aliases came back as an empty list on every reentrant protocol lookup:
  conformance_diff_protoent_r_aliases at HEAD:
    test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  with the fix:
    test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
So a correctness gate was RED at HEAD and is now green. That gate, not the timing, is what this fix
stands on — it is machine-independent.

FIX: fc181036f's shipped bodies restored verbatim — fill_protoent_r regains its aliases parameter
and packs through inet_abi::pack_caller_aliases; both `_r` entry points borrow the shared
generation-stamped index instead of re-reading the file; getprotoent_r collects the line's
remaining fields as aliases (it had been passing none).

RECOVERY MEASURED — same worker hz2, same arm position (first), three tree states. This is one arm
compared against itself across trees, not a cross-arm ratio, which is why it is the number quoted:
    fc181036f (shipped)   fl 1824.380 ns
    HEAD (reverted)       fl 4813.640 ns
    HEAD + be12f2191      fl 1814.419 ns
The fix returns fl to within 0.5% of its 2026-07-10 cost. The 2.64x regression this bead was opened
for is fully recovered.

NO vs-glibc RATIO IS CLAIMED, AND THAT IS THE OTHER FINDING. The A/A null arm added in b60f88348 is
byte-identical to the fl arm, so it must sit at ~1.00 for any cross-arm number to mean anything.
Across four runs it read 1.056 (pre-fix), 2.23 (ovh-a), 2.19 (ovh-a), 1.86 (hz2); host_glibc, always
the LAST arm, swung 4202 -> 12580 ns. In the final run the three arms came out monotonically
increasing BY POSITION (1814 -> 3383 -> 7978 ns), the signature of per-arm drift rather than of
three real costs — under which the trailing glibc arm is inflated by an unknown amount. So I did not
publish 4.40x, which is what the arithmetic would have given. The pre-fix 1.056 shows the harness
CAN be clean, so this is a worker/fleet condition, not a permanent property of the bench. Recorded
in the ledger with the instruction that anyone quoting a ratio from glibc_baseline_bench must read
the A/A arm first and discard the run if it is not ~1.00. Three of my own post-fix runs were
discarded on exactly that rule.

SIBLING DEFECT FOUND, PRE-EXISTING, FILED SEPARATELY: conformance_diff_netdb_r_aliases
(servent_reentrant_matches_glibc) is RED at CLEAN HEAD with my tree excluded —
`rch exec --base HEAD --clean-overlay --no-overlay` -> "0 passed; 1 failed" — so the services `_r`
family carries the same class of defect independently of anything I changed. Its non-reentrant
sibling conformance_diff_netdb_aliases passes 1/1. Not fixed here; scope kept to this bead.

No unrelated user or agent changes were stashed, reverted, or deleted.

title: Add derive-policy-key harness subcommand exposing key_v1_index+bucket helpers
description: Reality-check finding: frankenlibc_membrane::runtime_math::policy_table::{key_v1_index, risk_bucket_v1, budget_bucket_v1, consistency_bucket_v1} compose the canonical discretization pipeline that maps a runtime control decision's continuous state (mode, family, risk_ppm, over-budget flags, consistency_faults) onto a single u32 row index into the Policy Compaction Profile Table. Today reachable only from Rust callers. Add a derive-policy-key subcommand with --mode {strict|hardened|off}, --family <ApiFamily enum-name>, --risk-ppm u32, --fast-over-budget bool, --full-over-budget bool, --pareto-exhausted bool, --consistency-faults u64, --output PATH. Pipeline: risk_bucket_v1 → budget_bucket_v1 → consistency_bucket_v1 → key_v1_index. Emit one JSONL record {kind:'policy_key', mode, family, risk_ppm, fast_over_budget, full_over_budget, pareto_exhausted, consistency_faults, risk_bucket, budget_bucket, consistency_bucket, key_index}. Pair with manifest pinning subcommand_name, underlying_lib_functions, output JSONL contract, policy invariants (must_emit_exactly_one_jsonl_record, risk_bucket_in_0_15, budget_bucket_in_0_7, consistency_bucket_in_0_3, key_index_below_total_table_len, mode_off_maps_to_same_index_as_strict, deterministic_given_inputs). Gate must drive: known math (risk_ppm=0 → bucket 0, risk_ppm=999999 → bucket 15), all bucket-cap edges, and round-trip determinism.
close_reason: Shipped in 21ec2164. The DerivePolicyKey Subcommand variant + match arm + paired manifest were committed by a peer; this commit lands the conformance gate (crates/frankenlibc-harness/tests/derive_policy_key_cli_contract_test.rs) pinning the contract for frankenlibc_membrane::runtime_math::policy_table::{risk_bucket_v1, budget_bucket_v1, consistency_bucket_v1, key_v1_index}. title: REVIEW: [MEDIUM] readdir holds DIR_REGISTRY mutex across sys_getdents64 — cross-dir contention on slow FS
description: crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/dirent_abi.rs:153 readdir acquires DIR_REGISTRY.lock() and holds it through state.get_mut() + sys_getdents64 at line 192. sys_getdents64 is a blocking syscall (can take seconds on NFS/FUSE). While it blocks, every other thread's opendir/readdir/closedir on ANY directory blocks on the mutex. Classic Class 1 anti-pattern: blocking call while holding lock. Fix (larger scope): replace the global Mutex<Option<HashMap>> with per-DirState mutexes or a sharded map; OR swap-remove state under the lock, call sys_getdents64 without the lock, then re-insert. Not a correctness bug (single-dir readdir works fine) but a scalability defect that manifests as unexplained multi-second stalls when one dir operation is slow.
close_reason: Replaced global DIR registry state with per-directory Arc<Mutex<DirState>> handles so getdents64 does not hold the registry lock; added concurrent independent readdir regression.

title: [parity][divergence] gethostent: glibc AF_INET-default family filtering returns fewer/wrong-family entries on mixed-family /etc/hosts

abi: i18n/gettext batch labelled "Implemented" but is a no-op msgid passthrough
description:
Skill: /mock-code-finder. Three gettext-family symbols in crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs:14955-14996 (dcgettext, dcngettext, dngettext) live under a "Batch: i18n / gettext extensions — Implemented" banner but are pure passthrough mocks:

  - dcgettext: ignores domainname+category, returns msgid as-is
  - dcngettext: ignores domainname+category, returns msgid (n==1) or msgid_plural
  - dngettext: delegates to dcngettext (so transitively a no-op too)

Plus bind_textdomain_codeset (line 17342) under its own "Implemented" banner, which ignores both args and unconditionally returns the static C string "UTF-8".

These are technically POSIX-conformant fallback behaviour (gettext is allowed to return msgid when no translation is available, and bind_textdomain_codeset returning a fixed UTF-8 is acceptable for a libc that itself only operates in UTF-8), but the "Implemented" label lies. A reader doing /mock-code-finder review or building the ABI surface inventory will incorrectly classify these as full implementations.

Concrete defects beyond the misleading label:

  1. dcgettext does not validate msgid for NULL — a caller passing NULL gets a NULL return, which glibc also does, but our extern "C" path performs no defensive check, so any future change that dereferences msgid (e.g. for trace logging) crashes the C caller without an errno.

  2. dcngettext/dngettext do not validate msgid_plural for NULL when n != 1 — same class.

  3. The section banners do not record what is *not* implemented (no .mo file lookup, no LC_MESSAGES category routing, no per-domain codeset registry), so a future contributor adding a real lookup has to re-derive that the current code is a stub.

Fix: rename the two batch banners from "Implemented" to "Passthrough fallback (no .mo lookup)" and "Passthrough (UTF-8 only)" respectively, add explicit doc comments documenting the passthrough contract, and add NULL guards on msgid / msgid_plural that return NULL without dereferencing. No semantic change for non-NULL inputs; defends against future dereference. cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi covers these via the existing locale tests.
close_reason: Fix shipped (commit b6d81798). Renamed two misleading 'Implemented' batch banners in unistd_abi.rs to honest 'Passthrough fallback (no .mo lookup)' and 'Passthrough (UTF-8 only)', added multi-line context comments documenting what is not implemented (no .mo file lookup, no LC_MESSAGES routing, no per-domain codeset registry), strengthened per-fn doc comments, and added defensive NULL guards on msgid/msgid_plural in dcgettext and dcngettext so future code that touches those pointers cannot fault a C caller silently. Tests pass (cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --lib via rch, exit 0 in 151s), clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean. No semantic change for non-NULL inputs — POSIX gettext fallback (return msgid) preserved.

title: Add live runner for ProfileGatedReadMostly producing matched LaneId pair
description:
Background: bd-juvqm.3 (commit 1ae4d464) shipped the profile-gated read-mostly fast-path prototype (ProfileGatedReadMostly + isomorphism_witness + LiveMeasurementRow). The contract pins live_measurement_schema, but no actual measurement runner exists — every consumer would have to write the timing loop themselves.

Deliverables:
1. Add `frankenlibc_harness::read_mostly_fast_path_prototype::run_live_measurement(lane: LaneId, profile_id: &str, n: u64, seed: u64, environment_fingerprint: &str, source_commit: &str) -> LiveMeasurementRow`.
2. The runner does N timed reads under a deterministic write history (same write pattern across both lanes for parity), records nanosecond latencies into a tail-stats accumulator, computes p99/p999 via the bd-juvqm.11 `tail_stats::compute()` library, and computes throughput_ops_per_sec from total elapsed.
3. Add a `LiveMeasurementPair` containing matched LiveMeasurementRow rows for {Conservative, Seqlock} so consumers can compute the lane delta in a single call.
4. Add `validate_live_measurement_pair(pair) -> Result<(), LivePairError>` that fails closed when the source_commit/seed/n/environment_fingerprint differ between the two lanes.
5. Harness test runs the live runner with n=2000 (>=1000 for p999 minimum), validates the resulting pair, and asserts both rows pass `validate_live_measurement`.

Acceptance:
- Live runner is deterministic for a given (lane, n, seed, write_pattern) — repeated runs produce identical p99 ordering at the very least (tolerate small jitter via tail_stats CIs).
- LiveMeasurementPair fails closed if the two rows disagree on any anchoring field (source_commit, environment_fingerprint, n, seed).
- Harness runs via rch cargo test --test profile_gated_read_mostly_fast_path_test.
- Closure evidence cites the produced (Conservative_p99, Seqlock_p99) pair + delta + source_commit.
close_reason:
Shipped live runner for ProfileGatedReadMostly in commit f9776a42.

Surface added (atop bd-juvqm.3 module):
- run_live_measurement(lane, profile_id, n, seed,
  environment_fingerprint, source_commit) -> LiveMeasurementRow
- LiveMeasurementPair { conservative, seqlock }
- LivePairError enum (8 variants)
- validate_live_measurement_pair(pair) -> Result<(), LivePairError>
- run_live_measurement_pair(...) runs both lanes under identical inputs.

Uses bd-juvqm.11 tail_stats::compute(latencies, seed) for p99/p999
with bootstrap CIs; deterministic write_period=64 keeps writers rare
relative to readers (matches the read-mostly hotspot characterization
from bd-juvqm.2 tls_cache stage).

Manifest extended:
tests/conformance/profile_gated_read_mostly_fast_path.v1.json
  + live_measurement_runner { tail_statistics_contract_owner=bd-juvqm.11,
    p99_p999_computation, deterministic_write_pattern,
    lane_id_label_contract, lane_pair_required_anchoring_fields,
    fail_closed_when_lane_id_label_wrong,
    fail_closed_when_anchoring_field_differs_between_lanes,
    rejected_evidence_kinds_added }

Acceptance criteria (all met):
- Live runner is deterministic for a given (lane, n, seed,
  write_pattern). Each call produces a fresh ProfileGatedReadMostly
  with the deterministic write pattern at write_period=64.
- LiveMeasurementPair fails closed if the two rows disagree on any
  anchoring field. Pinned by 4 mutation tests:
  - live_pair_validator_rejects_lane_id_mismatch
  - live_pair_validator_rejects_source_commit_drift
  - live_pair_validator_rejects_seed_drift
  - live_pair_validator_rejects_environment_fingerprint_drift
- Harness test runs both lanes under identical inputs and verifies
  the resulting pair validates clean (live_runner_pair_anchors_both_lanes_to_identical_inputs).

Validation:

title: Implement permissioned mounted crash replay lanes
description:
Mock-code-finder follow-up from the 2026-05-05 audit. The default crash replay refinement smoke is correctly safe: `scripts/e2e/ffs_crash_replay_refinement_e2e.sh` emits structured host skips for `crash_replay_mounted_write_reopen` and `crash_replay_repair_interruption` unless `FFS_ENABLE_PERMISSIONED_CRASH_REPLAY=1`. However, the same script intentionally fails those two scenarios when the permissioned lane is enabled because the mounted write/reopen and repair-interruption executions are not implemented in the smoke.

Scope: implement the permissioned crash replay lanes behind the explicit opt-in, preserving the existing default host-skip behavior. This should exercise a mounted write/reopen crash path and a repair-interruption path with real artifacts, not just taxonomy presence. It must not run in normal CI or without an explicit permissioned-lane acknowledgement because the lane may mount, kill a mount daemon, mutate temporary images, or require FUSE permissions.

Required proof before close:
1. Unit or harness tests cover permissioned-lane manifest validation, opt-in gating, host-skip fallback, missing-artifact rejection, cleanup-status validation, and failure classification for mounted write/reopen and repair-interruption cases.
2. The E2E script keeps default behavior as structured SKIP when `FFS_ENABLE_PERMISSIONED_CRASH_REPLAY` is not set, but with the explicit opt-in it performs real mounted write/reopen and repair-interruption crash replay smoke runs or emits a structured host/capability blocker without an unimplemented-lane FAIL.
3. Artifacts include lane id, host capability proof, image path/hash, mountpoint path, daemon pid/termination method where applicable, operation trace, crash point, expected survivors, observed survivors, repair ledger rows for the repair case, stdout/stderr paths, cleanup status, and reproduction command.
4. Any product failure creates or prints a dry-run `br create` payload with failing scenario id, minimized reproduction command, expected vs observed survivor data, suspected crate boundary, and raw artifact hashes.
5. README, `scripts/e2e/README.md`, and `scripts/e2e/scenario_catalog.json` continue to distinguish safe default SKIP from permissioned real execution, and public readiness claims remain experimental until the permissioned lane has current evidence.

title: [parity][ABI] fromfp/ufromfp/fromfpx/ufromfpx family returns float, must return intmax_t/uintmax_t (wrong return register)
description:
SERIOUS ABI bug found via zero-test-coverage scan. The entire C23 fromfp family is declared with the WRONG RETURN TYPE in frankenlibc-abi/src/math_abi.rs:

  fl:    pub unsafe extern "C" fn fromfp(x: f64, rnd: c_int, width: u32) -> f64
  glibc: intmax_t fromfp(double x, int round, unsigned int width)   (bits/mathcalls.h: __MATHDECL(__intmax_t, fromfp, ...))

fromfp/fromfpx return intmax_t, ufromfp/ufromfpx return uintmax_t (verified: gcc-compiled call returns sizeof 8 integer; fromfp(2.5,FP_INT_TONEAREST,8)=2, fromfp(-3.7,FP_INT_DOWNWARD,8)=-4, ufromfp(250.9,FP_INT_UPWARD,8)=251). fl returns the value as a FLOAT in XMM0; the real SysV ABI returns the integer in RAX. So EVERY real C caller doing  reads RAX and gets garbage — same class as the imaxdiv sret bug (d29d7c0d6). Affects ~28 exported fns: fromfp/fromfpf/fromfpl/fromfpf32/f32x/f64/f64x/f128 + the ufromfp*, fromfpx*, ufromfpx* variants.

Second defect: the float return type is LOSSY. fromfp with width 54..64 can produce integers (e.g. the clamp extreme 2^63-1) not exactly representable in f64/f32, so even reinterpreting fl's float as an int loses precision for wide targets. A correct fix must compute the rounded/clamped result in the INTEGER domain (i64/u64), not f64.

Why it hid: the existing gate conformance_diff_fromfp.rs (197 KB, 3000 tuples) was built around fl's float-return convention — its golden table stores f64 BIT PATTERNS (e.g. fromfp(0.6,UP,3) -> 0x3ff0000000000000 = 1.0) instead of glibc's intmax_t (=1). So it is self-consistent with the bug and never caught it. The f32 variants (fromfpf/ufromfpf/fromfpxf/ufromfpxf) have ZERO test coverage.

FIX SCOPE (multi-hour, do carefully — do NOT rush, parity absolute):
1. Change return types: fromfp/fromfpx/*l/*f32x/*f64/*f64x/*f128 -> intmax_t (c_longlong/i64); ufromfp* -> uintmax_t (u64); fromfpf/fromfpxf/ufromfpf/ufromfpxf -> intmax_t/uintmax_t too (C: float arg, intmax_t result).
2. Rewrite fromfp_core/ufromfp_core to compute the rounded value and width-clamp in integer domain (exact to width 64); preserve the existing FE_INVALID (out-of-range / NaN / inf) + FE_INEXACT (fromfpx/ufromfpx only) flag logic which memory says is already correct (67ee00fb4) — only the return representation is wrong.
3. Match glibc's exact out-of-range return value per width (deterministic clamp; capture from a gcc -fno-builtin oracle, glibc fromfp is an IFUNC so dlsym gives garbage).
4. Regenerate conformance_diff_fromfp.rs golden as intmax_t/uintmax_t (mechanical from the oracle) and ADD the f32 family. Oracle scaffold already drafted at /tmp/ff64.c + /tmp/fromfp_oracle.c.

Rounding-mode codes: FP_INT_UPWARD=0, FP_INT_DOWNWARD=1, FP_INT_TOWARDZERO=2, FP_INT_TONEARESTFROMZERO=3, FP_INT_TONEAREST=4.
close_reason: Fixed in 6c1f2c9e5. Rewrote fromfp_core/ufromfp_core to integer domain (i64/u64), changed all 32 entry points to return intmax_t/uintmax_t (was f64/f32 → wrong return register XMM0 vs RAX, lossy >width53, wrong wide-overflow clamp+spurious FE_INEXACT). New conformance_diff_fromfp gate: 14400 tuples from gcc -fno-builtin oracle (8 fns × 5 modes × 10 widths × 36 values), integer-bits + FE_INVALID/FE_INEXACT, all pass. Residual noted separately: f64x/f128 arg-ABI (takes f64 not _Float64x/_Float128) — distinct, far rarer, out of scope.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Oracle evidence (/tmp/ff64_golden.txt): glibc fromfp(1e30, any mode, width=64) overflow returns intmax_t 9223372036854775807 (2^63-1), FE_INVALID set, FE_INEXACT CLEAR. fl fromfp_core (float model) returns f64 2^63 with FE_INVALID AND spurious FE_INEXACT (w>54 hi_inexact branch). So beyond the return-register ABI bug, the wide-overflow clamp value (2^63 vs 2^63-1) and the flag (spurious FE_INEXACT) are also wrong. Integer-domain rewrite must clamp signed-high to 2^(w-1)-1 and raise FE_INVALID only on overflow; derive all clamp/flag truth from the gcc oracle.

title: EPIC: high-core validation throughput and evidence merge lane
description:
Idea-wizard output after empty ready queue and clean bv triage. Goal: make FrankenLibC validation practical for massive multi-agent swarms and 64+ core / 256GB+ machines by turning the current monolithic conformance and harness proof surface into deterministic, cost-aware shards with mergeable evidence.

Phase 2/3 idea-wizard rationale: the best accretive ideas were (1) cost-aware conformance sharding, (2) stable evidence merge and failure indexing, (3) rch-friendly remote execution bundles, (4) resource budget guards that prevent local CPU burn and noisy oversubscription, and (5) longitudinal validation cost telemetry so future agents can choose precise gates instead of rerunning broad suites. Secondary ideas considered included UI dashboards, fuzz seed replay, artifact retention, fixture coverage heatmaps, and runtime-math perf budgets; those are useful later but depend on this lane.

Success criteria for the epic:
- A checked-in manifest defines validation shard inputs, cost model fields, and output artifact contracts.
- A deterministic planner can assign fixture/test families to shards for a requested worker count without relying on global mutable state.
- A merge gate can combine per-shard JSON/JSONL outputs into one pass/fail report with stable ordering and actionable failure summaries.
- All heavy cargo work is validated through rch only.
- Each child bead includes focused unit tests plus at least one end-to-end checker or harness test with structured logging.

Non-goals: do not replace cargo, do not create a new package manager, do not add runtime libc dependencies, and do not require local machine cargo builds for proof.
