title: [bug][crypt][CRITICAL] fl's crypt digests differ from libxcrypt for ALL implemented algorithms ($6$/$5$/$1$) — correct length and prefix, wrong content, so no real /etc/shadow hash verifies
description:
Found while fixing bd-r9ihvq (the crypt failure-token contract). That bead was about what crypt
returns on REJECTED settings; this is about what it returns on ACCEPTED ones, and it is far more
serious: fl's digests do not match libxcrypt for ANY implemented algorithm, so fl cannot verify a
single real password hash.

MEASURED, live libxcrypt (libcrypt.so.1) vs fl, same key "password", same settings, in the same
process (crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/conformance_diff_crypt_failure_token.rs prints these):

  crypt("password", "$6$saltsalt$")
    fl:        $6$saltsalt$5FWRm/r2DmdgEyxjgvf.WOSWP2T8dSoc5DDut4Knw4/1dv4Ofat0fIpxJx1DX0qSrP1U8NWhHMpS.fLjbIJyh/
    libxcrypt: $6$saltsalt$qFmFH.bQmmtXzyBY0s9v7Oicd2z4XSIecDzlB5KiA2/jctKu9YterLp8wwnSq.qc.eoxqOmSuNp2xS0ktL3nh/
  crypt("password", "$5$saltsalt$")
    fl:        $5$saltsalt$eNDfJrMCfjLMzuCV/JiON03OeRm37Pt6zOHgkQ4mtC.
    libxcrypt: $5$saltsalt$gOjOtoMpVhru2uyjeJSEc/JaLQWOXMNmlOnj6T4AtC.
  crypt("password", "$1$saltsalt$")
    fl:        $1$saltsalt$WhXxlbkySpa0jCDUPCNwK/
    libxcrypt: $1$saltsalt$qjXMvbEw8oaL.CzflDtaK/

ALL THREE differ. Note what is RIGHT, because it narrows the search a lot: the setting prefix is
echoed correctly, the output length is exactly right in every case ($6$ 86 chars, $5$ 43, $1$ 22),
and the alphabet is the correct crypt base64. So the framing, salt handling and encoding are fine —
the DIGEST itself is wrong. This is not a "not implemented" gap; it is a wrong implementation that
looks plausible.

WHY IT MATTERS: crypt's only real use is `strcmp(crypt(password, stored_hash), stored_hash)`. With
wrong digests that comparison NEVER matches, so under fl every /etc/shadow authentication fails
closed. Nothing in the tree caught it because, as far as I can tell, no gate ever compared an fl
digest against a live libxcrypt digest — the existing crypt tests in unistd_abi_test check shape and
self-consistency (fl vs fl), which a wrong-but-deterministic implementation satisfies perfectly.
That is the same "gate cannot fail for the defect it names" pattern as bd-44y7sl / bd-3vz1f8.

WHERE TO START:
  crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs -> crypt() dispatches to crypt_sha512 / crypt_sha256 /
  crypt_md5. Check those against the reference algorithms:
    $5$/$6$  Ulrich Drepper's SHA-crypt specification (the rounds=5000 default, the B/DP/DS
             sequences, and the very specific final permuted base64 ordering)
    $1$      the classic MD5-crypt construction
  The correct output length with wrong content most often means the digest LOOP is wrong (the 5000
  rounds and the alternating key/salt schedule) rather than the encoder. Test the intermediate
  values against the spec's published test vectors before touching the encoder.

DONE = a differential gate that compares fl's digest against LIVE libxcrypt byte-for-byte for
$1$/$5$/$6$ across several keys and salts (including the empty key, long keys >64 bytes, salts
shorter than 8 chars, and an explicit rounds= parameter), shown RED first, then green. The scaffolding
already exists: conformance_diff_crypt_failure_token.rs resolves libxcrypt via
dlopen("libcrypt.so.1") and has host_crypt/fl_crypt helpers ready to use; its
crypt_supported_algorithms_still_produce_real_hashes arm currently asserts SHAPE only and prints the
divergence, and should be tightened to equality as part of closing this.

RELATED: bd-c6ykz1 covers the algorithms fl does not implement at all (yescrypt $y$, bcrypt $2$,
scrypt $7$, gost-yescrypt $gy$). This bead is narrower and more urgent: the ones fl DOES claim to
implement are wrong.
close_reason:
FIXED. Source commit 890e5c313. fl's crypt is now byte-identical to live libxcrypt for every
algorithm it implements.

TWO INDEPENDENT DEFECTS, both required. The bead recorded the symptom (right length, right prefix,
right alphabet, wrong content, all three algorithms) and guessed the digest LOOP was at fault. That
guess was wrong in a useful way: the loops were correct, and the damage was entirely in step 6.

BUG 1 — the shared crypt-base64 encoder packed every 3-byte group BACKWARDS.
  Reference (glibc `b64_from_24bit(B2,B1,B0,N)` / FreeBSD `to64`): consume THREE bytes as
  w = (B2<<16)|(B1<<8)|B0, emit N characters least-significant-6-bits first.
  fl: accumulated ONE running little-endian bit stream across the entire input, i.e.
  w = (B0<<16)|(B1<<8)|B2 for each triple — exactly reversed.
  The transposition tables in md5/sha256/sha512 are written as TRIPLES precisely because the
  grouping is load-bearing; flattening them into a stream silently reversed all of it. One encoder,
  shared by all three algorithms, is why all three were wrong simultaneously — which is also why the
  bead's "all three differ" observation was the strongest clue available.
  Fix: encode() is group-based, big-endian within the group, with a short final group RIGHT-aligned
  so its last byte is B0. That right-alignment rule is what makes the md5 tail ([f11], 2 chars) and
  the sha256 tail (3 chars) land in glibc's order without special-casing.
  CONSEQUENCE THAT HAD TO BE HANDLED: sha256's tail array `[f[30], f[31]]` was correct ONLY against
  the reversed encoder. Fixing the encoder alone would have moved the bug rather than removed it, so
  it is flipped to `[f[31], f[30]]` to match Drepper's b64_from_24bit(0, alt_result[31],
  alt_result[30], 3).

BUG 2 — sha512's step-6 table was off by one from row 14 onward.
  Rows 14..20 used high indices 55,56,57,58,59,60,61 where the spec says 56,57,58,59,60,61,62.
  So `f[55]` was consumed TWICE and `f[62]` NEVER. This is provably wrong without any oracle: step 6
  is a permutation of digest bytes 0..=62, so every index must appear exactly once. That invariant
  is now a unit test, `transposition_table_is_a_permutation`, which reports duplicates and omissions
  by index and fails loudly on the old table. It is the cheapest possible gate for this bug class and
  needs no libxcrypt at all.
  This is what the remaining divergence looked like after Bug 1 was fixed — the first ~68 characters
  already matched, and only the tail was wrong:
    fl:        ...FwCNcPnIIddI6CaNL5OTSHau97TPJt/
    libxcrypt: ...FwCtq8lIIdpJ6CatVdOTSHKp97TPkt/

TWO FALSE COMMENTS CORRECTED IN PLACE. The sha512 module doc claimed the port "uses the correct
indices, so output now matches real glibc/libcrypt" — it did not match anything. An inline comment
claimed the table preserved "bug-for-bug compatibility (rows 14, 18, 19 differ from Drepper's
published spec by 1)" — the divergence was rows 14 THROUGH 20, and there was no compatibility to
preserve. Both now describe what is actually there, plus why the claim survived.

WHY IT SURVIVED, and this is the reusable part: every pre-existing crypt test compares fl against
fl — shape, determinism, salt truncation, different-keys-differ, and a "characterization" test that
explicitly pins whatever the code currently emits. A wrong-but-deterministic implementation
satisfies every one of them perfectly. Byte-equality against a live oracle is the only assertion
that could have failed, and it did not exist until bd-r9ihvq happened to add a success-path arm for
anti-vacuity reasons. Same family as bd-44y7sl / bd-3vz1f8 / bd-8omwj4, with far worse consequences.

GATES (compiled and executed, non-zero passed counts):
  conformance_diff_crypt_failure_token — the success arm is now BYTE-EQUALITY, over a matrix of
  4 keys x 8 settings ($1$/$5$/$6$, 2-char and 8-char salts, explicit rounds=1000, empty key,
  200-byte key), with an explicit guard that >= 20 (key, salt) pairs were actually compared so the
  matrix cannot silently go inert:
    test crypt_rejected_settings_match_libxcrypt_failure_token ... ok
    test crypt_failure_token_never_equals_the_setting ... ok
    test crypt_supported_algorithms_match_libxcrypt_byte_for_byte ... ok
    test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  frankenlibc-core --lib crypt: ok. 51 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 3163 filtered out
    (includes the new permutation invariant)

ONE EXISTING TEST WAS REPLACED, NOT ADJUSTED. `encode_packs_least_significant_first` asserted that
the first character of encode([0x01,0x00,0x00], 4) is '/', i.e. that 0x01 lands in the LOW 6 bits.
That is a faithful description of Bug 1, so adjusting its expected value would have been the
golden-regeneration reflex. It is replaced by
`encode_packs_group_big_endian_and_emits_lsb_first`, which states the reference rule, shows the
arithmetic for each expected character, and additionally pins the short-group right-alignment that
the md5 and sha256 tails depend on.

REGRESSION CHECK: unistd_abi_test 535 passed; 5 failed; 91 ignored — failure SET byte-identical to
the clean-HEAD baseline (abi_argp_parse_version x2, cuserid, kexec_load, mount_setattr), none
crypt-related, and that target's existing crypt arms still pass. fmt clean.

STILL OPEN, unchanged by this: bd-c6ykz1 covers the algorithms fl does not implement at all
(yescrypt $y$, bcrypt $2$, scrypt $7$, gost-yescrypt $gy$), for which fl now returns libxcrypt's
failure token rather than NULL (bd-r9ihvq). This bead was only about the ones fl does implement.

No unrelated user or agent changes were stashed, reverted, or deleted.

title: Add real EvidenceRingBuffer stress runner emitting structured report
description:
Background: bd-juvqm.7 (commit 8af10026) shipped the evidence-ring backpressure model (ModelRing + StressDriver + StressReport + validate_stress_report). The contract is testable on synthetic ring instances but no CLI driver runs the stress against the REAL `EvidenceRingBuffer` and emits a structured report that the conformance gate can consume.

Deliverables:
1. Add `frankenlibc_harness::evidence_ring_backpressure::run_real_ring_stress<const CAP: usize>(seed, drive_to_capacity_multiple) -> RealRingReport` that drives `frankenlibc_membrane::runtime_math::evidence::EvidenceRingBuffer<CAP>` past capacity and emits the same fields as `StressReport`.
2. Add a `RealRingReport` struct that mirrors `StressReport` but captures real-ring observations: total_pushed, snapshot_size, snapshot_first_seqno, snapshot_last_seqno, derived_loss (= total_pushed - snapshot_size), monotone_seqno (bool), source_commit.
3. Add a serializer `serialize_real_ring_report_jsonl()` that emits one line per stress run, suitable for `target/conformance/evidence_ring_backpressure.real.jsonl`.
4. Update `validate_stress_report` semantics so it accepts a `RealRingReport` shape too (loss_count = derived_loss, max_epoch derived from total_pushed/CAP).
5. Update tests/conformance/evidence_ring_backpressure_stress_contract.v1.json with a `real_ring_report_path` and `real_ring_required_fields` block.
6. Harness test that runs `run_real_ring_stress::<32>(seed=0xc0ffee, multiple=4)` and validates the resulting report passes the validator.

Acceptance:
- Real-ring report is deterministic for a given seed (the production ring's allocate_seqno is monotonic by construction).
- Validator rejects a derived_loss that does not match (total_pushed - snapshot_size).
- Harness runs via `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/projects/.cargo-target-frankenlibc-<agent>-<bead-short> rch cargo test -p frankenlibc-harness --test evidence_ring_backpressure_stress_contract_test`.
- Closure evidence cites the produced JSONL path + source_commit + report fields.
close_reason:
Shipped real EvidenceRingBuffer stress runner in commit 5267830e.

Surface added (atop the bd-juvqm.7 module):
- RealRingReport struct (12 fields).
- REAL_RING_REPORT_REQUIRED_FIELDS const (matches manifest).
- run_real_ring_stress::<CAP>(seed, multiple, source_commit).
- serialize_real_ring_report_jsonl(&RealRingReport) -> String.
- validate_real_ring_report(&RealRingReport) -> Vec<String>.

Manifest extended:
tests/conformance/evidence_ring_backpressure_stress_contract.v1.json
  + real_ring_report { report_path_template, required_fields (12),
    fail_closed_when_required_field_missing,
    fail_closed_when_derived_loss_inconsistent,
    fail_closed_when_seqno_non_monotone,
    fail_closed_when_source_commit_invalid,
    rejected_evidence_kinds_added }

Acceptance criteria (all met):
- Real-ring report is deterministic for a given seed: production
  EvidenceRingBuffer.allocate_seqno is monotonic by construction;
  payload byte derives from seed^i. The whole report PartialEq's
  byte-equal across two calls — pinned by
  run_real_ring_stress_is_deterministic_under_same_seed.
- Validator rejects derived_loss != total_pushed - snapshot_size —
  pinned by validate_real_ring_report_rejects_inconsistent_derived_loss.

title: [test-infra] 435 poison-intolerant serialization-lock acquires across 30 test files inflate one failure into many
description:
MEASURED, not theoretical. nss_cache_policy_test.rs reported 'test result: FAILED. 7 passed; 8 failed' on 2026-08-15 while carrying exactly ONE real divergence. The other 7 were phantoms: the real failure panicked while holding the file's TEST_LOCK, poisoning it, and the remaining tests acquired that mutex with .expect(), so each died on the poison instead of on its own behavior. passwd_getpwuid_finds_correct_user passed on its own under the SAME binary (1 passed; 14 filtered out) while failing in the full run — that isolation run is the discriminator. Fixed for that file in e0071d1be (bd-o0jhfu).

SURVEY at e0071d1be:
  rg -n '\\.lock\\(\\)\\.(expect\\(|unwrap\\(\\))' crates/*/tests/*.rs | wc -l   -> 435 sites, 30 files
  poison-TOLERANT (unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()))                       -> 214 sites
Highest-count files: conformance_diff_sigprocmask (10), pwd_abi_test (9), conformance_diff_getopt (6), resolv_abi_test (6), conformance_diff_err_h (5), conformance_diff_error_at_line (5), conformance_diff_fmtmsg (5).

DO NOT OVERSTATE THE BLAST RADIUS. A cascade needs (a) a poison-intolerant acquire on a SHARED static and (b) a test that actually fails while holding it. Most bd-aykfv1 rows are 0/1 or N/1 single-failure targets, where no cascade could have occurred. The cost this pattern imposes is on TRIAGE: a red target's failure count cannot be read as a defect count until the guards are poison-tolerant, and the 2026-08-15 case burned real time distinguishing 1 defect from 8.

WHY THE FIX IS NOT GATE-WEAKENING: poison-tolerance hides nothing. The real failure still reports, with its own assertion message. What disappears is the phantom count.

DONE = every serialization-lock acquire in crates/*/tests/*.rs is poison-tolerant, plus a re-run of any currently-red multi-test target so its failure count can be trusted. Not done by converting a subset and quoting the site count.
close_reason: Swept at c9d7b28d7 + 2b3ccb3d3. process_abi_test 43p/20f -> 62p/1f run alone, same command; 19 of 20 were phantoms. Scope and deliberate exclusions in comment.

title: [perf] regexec REG_NOSUB computed+discarded capture offsets instead of boolean DFA match
description: With REG_NOSUB, regexec reports only match/no-match (pmatch never filled), but regex_exec ran the full O(n*m) leftmost_start + run_from offset PikeVM search and then discarded the offsets. glibc uses a DFA boolean. fl already has an exact membership pass (any_match, lazy DFA for position-independent patterns) used as a prescan. Post-fix: nosub class patterns [0-9]+/[a-z]+ now fl/glibc 0.95-0.96 (fl matches/beats glibc; session-4 measured this path 1.54x SLOWER). Correctness: NEW conformance_diff_regex_nosub.rs (curated + 60k random ERE patterns vs live glibc, 0 boolean divergences); conformance_diff_regex 8 green (no regression). any_match has no false neg/pos so it equals execute().is_some().

title: [REALITY-CHECK] ScrubDaemon not wired to ffs mount path; README's 'automatic recovery / no separate fsck' is aspirational at runtime
description:
# Reality-check finding — vision→runtime integration gap

## Vision claim (README.md:35, :838)

> TL;DR table, RaptorQ self-healing row: 'Corruption detected by checksums triggers automatic recovery. Stale-window SLO monitoring. **No separate fsck pass. No downtime.**'
>
> Corruption Recovery section: 'The scrub pipeline (`ffs-repair::pipeline`) continuously monitors block integrity and orchestrates automatic recovery.'

## Reality (runtime code)

`ScrubDaemon` is implemented in `crates/ffs-repair/src/pipeline.rs:695+` with `run_once`, `run_until_cancelled`, backpressure-aware scheduling, and evidence-ledger integration — all tested (bd-15c.5, bd-15c.6, bd-15c.11 all closed). But it is never started by any mount-path code:

- `crates/ffs-fuse/` — zero references to `ScrubDaemon`, `RepairPipeline`, or `start_scrub_daemon`
- `crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs` — `ffs-repair` is not even a Cargo dependency of `ffs-core`
- `crates/ffs-cli/src/main.rs` mount dispatch at line 4160+ (`MountRuntimeMode::Standard` / `Managed` / `PerCore`) calls `mount_with_fuse` / `mount_managed` and returns — no daemon spawn

The 'automatic recovery' path is only exercised by the E2E test `e2e_survive_five_percent_random_block_corruption_with_daemon` inside `ffs-repair` itself, which instantiates the daemon directly in test scaffolding. There is no production call site that starts the daemon when a user runs `ffs mount`.

## Evidence

- `rg 'ScrubDaemon|start_scrub_daemon|RepairPipeline' crates/ffs-fuse/ crates/ffs-core/src/ crates/ffs-cli/` → zero matches
- `crates/ffs-fuse/Cargo.toml`, `crates/ffs-core/Cargo.toml`, `crates/ffs-block/Cargo.toml` → no `ffs-repair` dep
- `crates/ffs-cli/src/main.rs:4160-4180` mount dispatch: `mount_with_fuse(open_fs, mountpoint, read_write, allow_other, auto_unmount)?` — no repair/scrub setup

Additionally, the only read-path → repair hook in the codebase is the `RepairFlushLifecycle` trait (`crates/ffs-block/src/lib.rs:512`), which fires AFTER writes flush (to refresh stale symbols). There is NO 'checksum failed during FUSE read → invoke RaptorQ decode' hook; `decode_group` is only called from within `ffs-repair` itself.

## Why this is a real vision gap

The README's self-healing promise is a top-line differentiator ('automatic recovery', 'no separate fsck pass', 'no downtime'). At runtime, users mounting via `ffs mount` get zero of this — checksum failures surface as I/O errors with no repair attempt, and corruption is not scanned in the background.

The components all exist and are tested; they're just not integrated into the runtime mount path.

## Fix direction

1. Add `ffs-repair` as a workspace dependency of `ffs-core` (so mount-time wiring can construct the pipeline).
2. Extend `OpenOptions` / `MountOptions` with `self_heal: SelfHealConfig { enabled, interval, budget, ... }`.
3. On mount, construct `ScrubDaemon` and spawn it under asupersync `Cx` so it honors the mount's cancellation tree (not `Cx::for_testing()` like the flush daemon does).
4. Add a read-path callback (mirror of `RepairFlushLifecycle` but for reads): when a block read surfaces a checksum failure, invoke `decode_group` to attempt repair; if successful, write back the repaired block and log an evidence-ledger event.
5. CLI: add `--self-heal / --no-self-heal` flag to `ffs mount` (default: enabled for `--rw`, disabled for RO since reads to bad blocks on RO-mounted images can't be fixed in place).
6. Document the runtime behavior change in README — move 'no separate fsck pass' from TL;DR to 'when self-heal is enabled' scope.

## Acceptance

- `ffs mount --rw --self-heal` starts the scrub daemon against the mounted image.
- A bit-flipped block on the mounted image, read through the FUSE path, is transparently repaired (evidence-ledger entry + corrected bytes returned).
- E2E test extended to drive the corruption scenario through `ffs mount` (not just via the in-process ScrubDaemon test harness).
- README either (a) stops claiming automatic recovery in the default mount path, or (b) ships with self-heal on by default once the integration is proven safe.
close_reason: README+Limitations aligned with runtime reality in commit 7149da6: the TL;DR RaptorQ row now describes the CLI repair path that exists today (ffs repair / ffs fsck --repair) and explicitly defers background auto-scrub to V1.x; a new Limitations bullet documents that ScrubDaemon is implemented and tested via e2e_survive_five_percent_random_block_corruption_with_daemon but is not started by the ffs mount path. The full mount-path integration (new ffs-repair dep in ffs-core, SelfHealConfig on MountOptions, ScrubDaemon spawn under mount Cx, RepairReadLifecycle trait wiring on the read-path, --self-heal CLI flag) is tracked as follow-up feature bead bd-hoh5n with detailed acceptance criteria. Closing this reality-check finding: the vision-vs-reality mismatch is resolved on the doc side; the engineering work is captured in a separate, appropriately-scoped feature bead.

title: Fix TOCTOU in sharded MVCC prune and overflow in btrfs stripe calculations
close_reason:
Fixed 2 bug classes:
(1) CRITICAL TOCTOU in ShardedMvccStore::prune_safe() — watermark read and prune were not atomic; a snapshot could be registered at a commit_seq about to be pruned, causing data loss. Fix: hold active_snapshots write lock for the entire watermark-read-then-prune sequence.

title: fix(math): f128 libm functions have wrong arg-ABI (declare f64, proto _Float128) — 124 fns
description: All ~124 exported *f128 math functions (fabsf128, sqrtf128, cosf128, ceilf128, copysignf128, __isnanf128, __fpclassifyf128, ...) declare f64 params/returns but the C proto is _Float128 (128-bit xmm). fl reads the wrong register -> garbage for every call. Same class as strfromf128/strtof128 (fixed). SPLIT: (A) EXACT-operation fns are fixable BYTE-EXACT now via bit ops on the f128 (crate has #![feature(f128)], to_bits/from_bits): classification (isnan/isinf/signbit/finite/fpclassify/issignaling), fabs, copysign, and (with care) ceil/floor/trunc/round/rint/nextafter/fmax/fmin/fdim/frexp/ldexp/scalbn/modf/significand/logb/ilogb. (B) TRANSCENDENTAL/algebraic fns (sin/cos/exp/log/pow/sqrt-to-full/cbrt/gamma/bessel/erf/hypot/complex) need a full 113-bit quad-precision libm to be byte-exact — large separate effort; computing via f64-widen is only f64-precision (fails parity), so those remain the documented long-double=f64-class architectural limit until a quad libm exists. Fix (A) in batches with differential gates vs glibc; track (B) separately.
close_reason: Fixed the remaining wrong f128 ABI signatures in math_abi: exp2/exp2m1, lgamma/tgamma, Bessel j/y, clog10f128, and f128 _finite aliases now expose binary128 (or CFloat128Complex) ABI. The only f128-name f64-return hits left are intentional C23 narrowing functions. Validation: RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/projects/.rch-targets/frankenlibc-cod-b rch exec -- cargo check -p frankenlibc-abi passed on hz2; UBS on crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/math_abi.rs exit 0 with 0 critical findings; git diff --check clean.

comments.text:
INCIDENT: this bead's subject is FULLY REGRESSED at HEAD. Do not read its closure as current state.

Closed 2026-06-18 with a real, honest evidence line (cargo check passed, ubs clean). Eight days
later 517d0a233 "abi/math: C99 Annex G special values for complex exp/hyperbolic" (Jun 26 23:34)
removed 6914 lines from crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/math_abi.rs without saying so in its message, and
put every one of these functions back to the exact defect this bead fixed:

  exported fns with an f128 signature   135 at 517d0a233^   ->   0 at HEAD
  private f128 implementation helpers   115 deleted

  -pub unsafe extern "C" fn asinhf128(x: f128) -> f128 {   (real ldbl-128 port)
  +pub unsafe extern "C" fn asinhf128(x: f64) -> f64 { unsafe { asinh(x) } }

The symbol NAMES all survived - 1170 before, 1170 after - so nm, the version script and every
symbol-presence check still pass while the ABI is wrong and the precision is silently f64. That is
why nobody noticed for six weeks.

The closure's own validation could not have caught it either: `cargo check -p frankenlibc-abi`
without --all-targets does not build the 60 conformance_diff_f128_* gates, and those gates are
exactly what fails now. This is the same lesson as bd-r71n1b and bd-86hcwh - a check that cannot
execute the assertion is not evidence.

Restore is tracked as bd-ocwiw9 (P0) and its seven tranches; bd-8nrm2g is the one that relights
conformance_diff_f128_invhyp, the gate this bead's sibling bd-... family depended on. Leaving this
bead CLOSED rather than reopening it, so the live work has exactly one home; this comment exists so
that nobody cites the 2026-06-18 closure as the state of the tree.

See also bd-bldxfy and bd-cb59r9 - the two previously-known Jun-26 silent deletions (e634aff2a,
bd829b12f). This is the third and by far the largest.

THE ERROR: crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/stdio_abi.rs:8510 and :8526 reference $spec.alloc inside the scanf_write_values! macro; the macro expands 6 times, hence 6 x E0609 'no field alloc on type &Box<ScanSpec>'.

  3. the 5-line GNU 'm' parse block, positioned AFTER width and BEFORE the length modifier

PARSE ORDER VERIFIED AGAINST LIVE GLIBC 2.42 (ctypes sscanf probe, scratchpad/scanf_m_oracle.py) rather than taken on trust from the parent commit:
  sscanf('hello world', '%ms')     -> 1, 'hello'
  sscanf('hello world', '%m[a-z]') -> 1, 'hello'
  sscanf('hello world', '%mc')     -> 1, one byte, no NUL
  sscanf('hello world', '%4ms')    -> 1, 'hell'      => m follows the WIDTH
  sscanf('hello world', '%mls')    -> 1, wide 'hello' => m precedes the LENGTH modifier
  sscanf('hello world', '%lms')    -> 0               => m after the length modifier is not the
                                                         modifier; glibc assigns nothing
  sscanf('42', '%md')              -> 1, 42           => m on a non-string conversion is ignored,
                                                         not an error (abi only acts on alloc for
                                                         Char/String values, so this matches)
  sscanf('hello world', '%*ms')    -> 0               => suppression composes

title: [parity][bug][regex] deeper regexec divergences vs glibc: GNU mid-pattern ^/$ line-boundary anchors w/o REG_NEWLINE, BRE ^* literal-star, BRE quantifier/escape edges (\+ \? on empty), empty-group capture offsets [0,0] vs [-1,-1]
notes:
Found by regex_newline_eflags_differential_fuzz (live glibc oracle; the existing diff_regex_random_fuzz only varied {0,REG_EXTENDED}, eflags=0, single-line subjects). After fixing the [^...]+REG_NEWLINE bug (bd-vgnzud), these remain (concrete cases, cflags/eflags shown):
1. GNU mid-pattern anchor line-boundary: '$.' on '0b\n\na' cflags=1(ERE) eflags=0 → glibc matches [2,3] ($ matches before mid-string \n even WITHOUT REG_NEWLINE for a NON-terminal $), fl no-match. Same for '.^'. NOTE terminal 'a$' does NOT (probe-confirmed) → glibc distinguishes terminal vs non-terminal $/^.
2. BRE '^*' literal-star: '^*0' cflags=0 → glibc no-match (^ + literal '*' + 0), fl matches '0' (treats * as quantifying the ^ anchor). '*' after ^ (or at expr start) is a LITERAL in BRE.
3. BRE quantifier/escape on empty: '+*\+' cflags=0 → glibc empty-match [0,0], fl no-match. 'b*\+\|*c0' similar.
4. Empty-group capture offsets: '|()' → glibc group1=[0,0] (empty matched), fl [-1,-1]. '.()*a' → glibc group=[1,1], fl [-1,-1].
⚠️These are deep regex-engine semantics; each warrants careful per-class fix + the live fuzzer un-scoped incrementally. REG_NEWLINE=4 (NOT 8; 8 is REG_NOSUB — caught a fuzzer-flag bug).
close_reason: Items 1 (GNU mid-pattern ^/$ anchors), 2 (BRE ^* literal-star), 3 (BRE/ERE stacked quantifiers) all FIXED; item 4 (empty-group capture offsets) delegated to bd-1djvkw (single-level fixed, nested is glibc-idiosyncratic). Item 3 fix this commit.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Item 2 FIXED (BRE ^* literal-star): POSIX BRE — a * immediately following a leading zero-width anchor (^ at RE/subexpr/alt start, or GNU \< \> \b \B) is a LITERAL *, not a quantifier. Guard added in parse_quantified BRE branch: Some(b'*') if !matches!(atom, Ast::Anchor(_)) → leading anchor returns as-is, leaving * to parse as Literal('*') (a 2nd * then quantifies that literal, matching glibc ^**0). Proven by NEW regex_bre_anchor_star_differential_fuzz (live glibc, 188173 compared, 0 div). Remaining OPEN: item 1 (non-terminal anchor line-boundary), item 3 (BRE empty-match on + ?), item 4 (empty-group capture offsets [0,0] vs [-1,-1]).

A naive 'post-body split' fix regresses trailing-empty cases like ..(b*)+ (verified+reverted this session). Needs per-thread loop-progress tracking. title: Honor vis C-style and whitespace flags
description:
Discovery found crates/frankenlibc-core/src/stdio/vis.rs accepts VIS_SP, VIS_TAB, VIS_NL, and VIS_CSTYLE but documents that most non-octal libutil flags are ignored. NetBSD vis(3) specifies default passthrough for space/tab/newline, VIS_SP/VIS_TAB/VIS_NL to force encoding of those bytes, and VIS_CSTYLE to use C-style escapes for standard non-printable characters. Implement a focused parity slice for the existing core/ABI vis family without touching peer-owned fixture surfaces.

Expected implementation shape: update the core vis encoder to honor default whitespace passthrough, force-encode whitespace flags, C-style escapes including NUL ambiguity handling for nextc where available, and preserve VIS_OCTAL behavior; adapt ABI single-byte vis/svis paths to pass nextc through; add focused core and ABI tests for default whitespace passthrough, forced whitespace encoding, VIS_CSTYLE escapes, VIS_CSTYLE|VIS_OCTAL fallback, and VIS_OPTIONS env propagation.

Validation: rustfmt on touched files; git diff --check; rch cargo test -p frankenlibc-core stdio::vis::tests::; rch cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test stdio_abi_test vis; rch cargo check/clippy for frankenlibc-core and frankenlibc-abi; br no-db dep cycles.

title: EPIC: Dynamic System Constants — Replace hard-coded values with runtime queries
description:
FrankenLibC currently hard-codes several system-dependent constants (page size, stack limits, group counts, FD limits) that should be queried at runtime for cross-architecture correctness.

BACKGROUND: While FrankenLibC currently targets x86_64 Linux, these hard-coded values create latent bugs that will surface when porting to ARM64 (16KB/64KB pages), RISC-V, or systems with non-standard configurations. Even on x86_64, some values (like supplementary group count) can differ from defaults.

SCOPE: This epic covers all hard-coded constants identified in the comprehensive audit across malloc_abi.rs, unistd_abi.rs, glibc_internal_abi.rs, stdlib_abi.rs, pthread_abi.rs, and process_abi.rs.

ALREADY DONE: sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE) now queries AT_PAGESZ from /proc/self/auxv at runtime (cached). The mmap_alloc bootstrap path intentionally keeps 4096 as the minimum alignment (documented).

RATIONALE: AGENTS.md says "We want to do things the RIGHT way with NO TECH DEBT" — hard-coded system constants are textbook tech debt.
close_reason: Delivered: code + artifacts present.

title: Replace hard-coded 64-group limit with dynamic NGROUPS_MAX query
description:
FILE: crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/glibc_internal_abi.rs:4592
CURRENT: let mut groups = [0u32; 64]
PROBLEM: NGROUPS_MAX can be 65536 on modern Linux. Hard-coding 64 silently truncates group membership for users in >64 groups, breaking permission checks.
FIX: Use a two-pass approach — first call getgroups(0, NULL) to get count, then allocate dynamically. Or use sysconf(_SC_NGROUPS_MAX) to size the buffer.
IMPACT: Any program calling getgroups() or initgroups() for users in many groups will get truncated results.
CONSIDERATION: The Vec allocation here is fine since this isn't a bootstrap-critical path.

title: Replace hard-coded FD_SETSIZE=1024 with libc::FD_SETSIZE
description:
FILES: crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/rpc_abi.rs:2283-2287, glibc_internal_abi.rs:3074, fortify_abi.rs:1001
CURRENT: Hard-coded bounds check !(0..1024) and [u8; 128] arrays (128 = 1024/8).
PROBLEM: While glibc itself uses FD_SETSIZE=1024, using the constant name is better than magic numbers. More importantly, the fd_set TLS buffer in rpc_abi.rs is sized to exactly 128 bytes — should derive from libc::FD_SETSIZE / 8.
FIX: Replace magic number 1024 with libc::FD_SETSIZE constant. Replace 128-byte arrays with [u8; libc::FD_SETSIZE as usize / 8].
IMPACT: Medium — affects programs using select() with fd > 1024, though poll/epoll is preferred.

title: Increase CPU affinity mask from 128 bytes (1024 CPUs) to support larger systems
description:
FILE: crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs:1804
CURRENT: let mut mask = [0u8; 128] — supports max 1024 CPUs.
PROBLEM: Large servers can have >1024 logical CPUs (e.g., AMD EPYC with 256 cores + SMT = 512, multi-socket = 1024+). The mask should be sized to the actual system or use a reasonable upper bound.
FIX: Either use a larger static buffer (e.g., 512 bytes = 4096 CPUs) or dynamically query the kernel for the actual affinity mask size. The sched_getaffinity syscall returns the actual size used, so we could do a two-pass approach.
IMPACT: Low — only affects very large servers. Current 1024 CPU limit is sufficient for most systems.

title: Make default thread stack size configurable via environment variable
description:
FILES: crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/pthread_abi.rs:2488,2494
CURRENT: ATTR_DEFAULT_STACK_SIZE = 2 * 1024 * 1024 (2 MiB), ATTR_MIN_STACK_SIZE = 16384 (16 KiB)
CONTEXT: glibc uses a default of 8 MiB, musl uses 128 KiB. Our 2 MiB is a reasonable middle ground but differs from both.
FIX: Keep 2 MiB as default but allow override via FRANKENLIBC_THREAD_STACK_SIZE env var. The minimum should match PTHREAD_STACK_MIN from the system.
IMPACT: Low — 2 MiB works for most applications. Some embedded or memory-constrained scenarios might want smaller stacks.
CONSIDERATION: Don't read env var on every thread creation — cache it at init time.

title: Fix _SC_TTY_NAME_MAX from 32 to match system reality
description:
FILE: crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs:1924
CURRENT: _SC_TTY_NAME_MAX = 32
PROBLEM: While glibc returns 32 for this, some systems have longer TTY names (especially for pseudo-terminals with long paths like /dev/pts/XXX). The constant should match glibc's behavior for compatibility.
FIX: Keep 32 to match glibc behavior but add a comment documenting the rationale. This is actually correct for glibc compat.
IMPACT: Very low — TTY names are almost always < 32 chars.

title: PORT: radixsort/sradixsort (NetBSD libutil radix sort family)
description: Port the NetBSD libutil radixsort(3) family: radixsort(base,nmemb,table,endbyte) and sradixsort(base,nmemb,table,endbyte). Both sort an array of pointers to byte strings (terminated by endbyte) using an optional 256-entry translation table that remaps each input byte to a sort key. sradixsort guarantees stable order of equal keys; radixsort does not. Implementation: pure-safe core radix_sort(items: &[&[u8]], table: Option<&[u8;256]>) returning a permutation Vec<usize> using stable sort with per-position translated-byte comparison; abi shims that walk each pointer to find endbyte, build slices, sort, and rewrite the pointer array in place. Tests: identity table, reverse-order table, NULL table = byte order, embedded-bytes preserved at endbyte boundary, stability for sradixsort, length-difference ordering, NULL/zero edge cases.

title: Expand ext4 dir block checksum tests beyond round-trip + no-panic
description:
crates/ffs-ondisk/src/ext4.rs has stamp/verify_dir_block_checksum but the proptest coverage in the same file is limited to:

  - ext4_proptest_verify_dir_block_checksum_no_panic (negative)
  - ext4_proptest_verify_dir_block_checksum_short_rejects (negative)
  - ext4_proptest_dir_block_checksum_stamp_verify (round-trip)

None of these exercise the per-inode seed mixing — i.e. the kernel's defence against:
  - replaying a valid dir block under a different (ino, generation) tuple
  - using a stamp produced under one filesystem csum_seed on another filesystem instance
  - flipping a bit in the directory entry payload after a valid stamp

Apply the same four metamorphic relations the inode checksum harness now covers:
  - MR-INO: identical body, two different ino numbers → different stored checksums
  - MR-GEN: identical body+ino, different generation → different stored checksums
  - MR-SEED: identical body+ino+gen, different csum_seed → different stored checksums
  - MR-DETECT: single-bit flip in the covered region [0..bs-12] invalidates verification

Land them as proptests in crates/ffs-ondisk/src/ext4.rs alongside the existing ext4_proptest_dir_block_checksum_stamp_verify.

title: fuzz: pathname encoding edge cases (NUL, UTF-8, long, .. traversal, symlinks)
description:
## Scope
Add crates/frankenlibc-fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_pathname.rs targeting the pathname-parsing + canonicalization surface: realpath, canonicalize_file_name, basename/dirname, access/faccessat, stat/lstat/fstatat, readlink/readlinkat. These share a common pathname-bytes input channel and are the classic CVE surface (CVE-2018-1000001 realpath OOB, CVE-2016-1234 glibc glob).

## Archetype
1 + 3: Crash-detector on the impl + **differential** against libc for path operations that don't touch fs state (basename/dirname) and for the few that do (stat/readlink) over a pre-seeded tmpdir with a known symlink graph.

## Inputs
struct PathnameFuzzInput {
  op: u8,                 // 0=realpath, 1=basename, 2=dirname, 3=stat, 4=lstat, 5=readlink, 6=access
  bytes: Vec<u8>,         // arbitrary — rejected if it contains interior NUL (CString won't build)
  buf_size: u16,          // for readlink
  flags: i32,             // for faccessat etc.
}

## Invariants
- Never panic
- For basename/dirname: result string length <= original + some constant; bytes are a suffix/prefix of the input
- For realpath: if non-null, resolved path has no '//' or '/./' or trailing '/', all components are canonical
- For stat family: non-negative rc implies st_dev/st_ino written; errno on failure is in the documented set
- Host parity: our errno family matches libc for inert paths

## Seed corpus
- empty, '/', '.', '..', '/tmp', '/proc/self', '/dev/null', '/etc/passwd', '/////' (collapsing slashes), '../../../..', path with unicode (é, 中, emoji), path with high-bit bytes, path at NAME_MAX (255), path at PATH_MAX (4096)

## Expected bug classes
- PATH_MAX overflow, NAME_MAX overflow, NUL-embedded path, UTF-8 boundary split, symlink loop detection, '..' collapsing vs preserving, trailing-slash semantics, basename('') = '', dirname('/') = '/'

## Score
5 × 4 × /3 ≈ 6.7 — high (path CVEs are a historical goldmine).
close_reason: Added seeded pathname fuzz coverage, canonical path assertions, and host return/errno parity checks for basename, dirname, stat/lstat, access, fstatat, readlink/readlinkat, and faccessat.

title: ffs-harness: render_remediation_markdown lacks golden-snapshot pinning
description:
Finding (via /testing-golden-artifacts skill, second visit, different
target): `render_remediation_markdown` (crates/ffs-harness/src/
remediation_catalog.rs:336) produces a markdown table representation
of the remediation catalog (loaded from
DEFAULT_REMEDIATION_CATALOG_JSON, deterministic across runs). The
existing test `render_markdown_includes_all_entries` (l. 619) only
checks substring presence:

  for entry in &catalog.entries {
      assert!(markdown.contains(&entry.id));
      assert!(markdown.contains(&entry.outcome_class));
  }

Substring-only assertions tolerate silent drift in:
  * the title format `# Remediation Catalog \`{catalog_id}\` (bead {bead_id})`
  * the blank line between title and table
  * the table header row (`| ID | Outcome | Feature State | ...`)
  * the alignment separator row (`|----|---------|...`)
  * the exact cell field order and the `|`-escape rule for the
    `immediate_action` column (`entry.immediate_action.replace('|', "\\|")`)
  * field ordering: `id | outcome_class | feature_state | data_safety_severity | mutation_status | owning_bead | immediate_action`

A regression that swapped two columns or dropped the alignment row
would not trip the substring tests but would break every downstream
markdown renderer / docs pipeline that consumes this output.

Acceptance: an insta golden snapshot test pins the EXACT bytes of
`render_remediation_markdown(&default_catalog)`, stored under
crates/ffs-harness/src/snapshots/ following the existing
benchmark_taxonomy + perf_comparison snapshot pattern.
notes: Shipped: render_remediation_markdown_default_catalog_snapshot insta golden snapshot in crates/ffs-harness/src/remediation_catalog.rs + .snap fixture under crates/ffs-harness/src/snapshots/. Pins title format, blank line, table header, alignment row, per-row cell field order, and the \| escape rule for immediate_action. Used a self-removing probe test to capture the exact output bytes from the rch worker, then pre-wrote the .snap fixture so the snapshot test passes on first run. Verified via rch exec -- cargo test -p ffs-harness --lib render_remediation_markdown_default_catalog_snapshot.

title: Refine xfstests failure triage with minimized repro and duplicate suppression
description:
Supplemental refinement for bd-rchk3.4. Converting xfstests failures into fix beads needs a strict triage contract so product bugs become narrow, claimable work while environment/harness/scope failures do not pollute the product backlog. Duplicate suppression and minimized repros should be explicit before real failure rows are processed.

Scope: define a triage extractor that consumes immutable xfstests baseline artifacts and produces dry-run bead payloads with failing test id, flavor, command, normalized outcome, expected behavior, actual behavior, suspected crate boundary, minimized repro or minimization status, duplicate key, labels, dependencies, and validation command.

Required proof before close:
1. Unit tests cover product failure extraction, host failure exclusion, harness failure exclusion, unsupported-scope exclusion, duplicate failure merging, stale raw-artifact rejection, missing command rejection, missing expected/actual rejection, and suspected-boundary vocabulary.
2. Unit tests verify every product bead payload includes xfstests id, filesystem flavor, exact command, normalized errno/output where relevant, raw log refs, minimized repro command or explicit non-minimized follow-up, proposed validation command, owner label, and dependency rationale.
3. E2E/dry-run smoke processes fixture baseline results and emits proposed br commands without creating live beads, then verifies duplicate suppression and disposition counts.
4. Logs include baseline id, failure row id, classification, duplicate key, proposed bead title/id placeholder, raw artifact hash, minimization status, output path, and reproduction command.
5. Live bead creation from xfstests failures must remain disabled until dry-run output is reviewed and every non-product row has an explicit environment/harness/scope disposition.
close_reason: Completed dry-run xfstests failure triage extractor with immutable raw refs, duplicate suppression, CLI/script artifacts, and validation evidence: RCH xfstests unit tests 33/33, RCH clippy clean, plan-mode E2E emitted live=false proposed=0 excluded=17, fmt/bash/git-diff/jq/cycle checks clean, UBS exit 0.

title: memmove fortify overflow abort coverage
description: __memmove_chk has overlap/pass-through coverage but no direct fork-isolated overflow-abort regression. Add a child-process test proving len > destlen aborts before copying.
close_reason:
ALREADY SATISFIED — closing on run tests matched to this bead's contract.

COVERING TESTS: memmove_chk_overflow_aborts_child_process for the abort contract, and
memmove_chk_overlapping for the property that distinguishes memmove from memcpy — overlapping
regions must still copy correctly rather than abort.

EVIDENCE. crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/fortify_abi_test.rs, run just now:
  cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test fortify_abi_test
  -> test result: ok. 152 passed; 0 failed; 0 IGNORED; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
Zero ignored matters here: a sibling bead last round nearly closed on a suite that reported 24
ignored, where the arm in question could have been one of them.

WHY THE ABORT ARMS CANNOT PASS VACUOUSLY — I checked the harness rather than trusting the test
names. assert_child_sigabrt forks, and if the child RETURNS NORMALLY it calls _exit(127); the parent
then asserts WIFSIGNALED(status) and WTERMSIG(status) == SIGABRT. So a fortify wrapper that failed to
abort would exit 127, WIFSIGNALED would be false, and the assertion would fail. The sentinel exit is
what makes these real tests rather than 'we called it and nothing happened'.

NOT CITED BY BEAD ID. None of the eight fortify beads is named anywhere in the test tree, so the
bead->gate mapping that settled earlier batches returned NONE for all of them. Coverage was
established by matching each bead's CONTRACT to a named executing test instead. Bead-ID citation is
a convenience, not the definition of coverage — and its absence is not evidence of absence.

No code change was needed or made for this bead.

title: [bug] atanhf drifts 251 ULP vs glibc at tiny |x| (~1.9e-12) — RED gate math_special_differential_probe
description: math_special_differential_probe::f32_trig_inverse_cbrt_passthroughs_within_4_ulp_of_glibc FAILS: 'atanhf drifted 251 ULP vs glibc at x=-1.9116941e-12' (probe line 488). atanh(x)~=x for tiny x so this should be near-exact; 251 ULP means the tiny-|x| branch (|x|<0.5 f64 path) is wrong. NOT caused by the remainder change (float.rs, separate fn/file) — reproduces at HEAD. Likely regressed by a recent float32.rs change (2f2393f19 'classify f32 from exponent bits' is top of that file's history and touches classification, which selects atanhf's branch). Unrelated to perf; flagging as a shipped correctness regression on main. Owner of 2f2393f19 (bd-a3vxfu) should verify.
close_reason:
CLOSED ON THE BEAD'S OWN NAMED PROBE, now green for the first time. It took two fixes, not one: the atanhf fix this bead was filed for (landed earlier in 72125d717) plus log1pf, which the probe only reached once atanhf stopped failing.

  cargo test -p frankenlibc-core --test math_special_differential_probe   (rch worker)
    test atanhf_tiny_inputs_match_glibc_bits ... ok
    test log1pf_tiny_inputs_match_glibc_bits_and_inexact_flag ... ok
    test f32_trig_inverse_cbrt_passthroughs_within_4_ulp_of_glibc ... ok      <- the named RED gate
    test result: ok. 6 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored
Run against the exact committed tree at d3857dcac. Non-zero passed count, and the immediately
preceding run of the same command on the same worker reported 4 passed / 1 failed with
'log1pf drifted 548 ULP vs glibc at x=-8.282635e-14', so before and after are both measured.

WHY THE GATE STAYED RED AFTER THE atanhf FIX: this probe asserts and stops at the first drift, so
it could only ever report one symbol at a time. atanhf going green exposed log1pf, same file, same
tiny-|x| defect class. Anyone re-running it should expect that pattern rather than assume the first
green assertion means the family is clean.

log1pf ROOT CAUSE (shipped d3857dcac): it computed log(1.0 + f64::from(x)) under a written comment
claiming 1+x is 'EXACT for an f32 x'. False -- exact only for |x| >= 2^-29; below that the sum's
rounding error swamps a result of size |x|. Fixed by returning x for |x| < 2^-24, where x is
already the correctly rounded result. Threshold measured against glibc 2.42, not just derived:
81,600 sampled f32 values below 2^-24 all return x, 4,000 in [2^-23,2^-22) none do.

RESIDUAL, filed as bd-onysf5 and deliberately NOT closed here: the atanhf fast path returns the
right value but raises no FE_INEXACT, where glibc raises it for every nonzero tiny input. log1pf's
new branch does raise it (and the new gate pins both value and flag, on both sides of the
threshold); atanhf's does not, and atanhf_tiny_inputs_match_glibc_bits compares to_bits() only, so
nothing catches it. Its 2^-12 threshold is separately validated: 68,400 samples below it all return
x, and [2^-12,2^-11) already differs in 58% of samples, so that branch is value-correct.

title: [parity][feature][regex] implement REG_STARTEND exec flag (sub-buffer match, embedded NUL, offset rebasing)
description: fl regexec ignored REG_STARTEND (always read the NUL-terminated C string). Implemented in the ABI regexec wrapper: when eflags has REG_STARTEND, the match region is string[pmatch[0].rm_so..rm_eo] — embedded NULs allowed, no terminator. Semantics (probed vs host glibc + pinned by NEW regex_startend_differential_fuzz, 200k 0-div): offsets returned relative to string (rm_so re-added); the string logically ends at rm_eo so $ anchors there; ^ anchors at the true buffer start so rm_so>0 forces NOTBOL UNLESS REG_NEWLINE and buf[rm_so-1]=='\n' (a \n-induced BOL matches even under caller NOTBOL); uses the binary-safe regex_exec_bytes (no NUL truncation). Also fixed: glibc's '.' never matches a NUL byte (only reachable via the byte/STARTEND path; the C-string path truncates at NUL so it is a no-op there) — fixed AnyChar in both VMs. Added pub CompiledRegex::newline_mode() getter + pub const REG_STARTEND=4. NOTE the fuzzer uses well-formed anchors only; non-terminal $/^ mid-pattern is the separate bd-aedwrn quirk.

title: [RED SWEEP] 28 of 610 conformance_diff gates FAIL when actually executed; most untracked. Triage each for root/container dependence
description:
METHOD (reproducible): 'cargo test --all-targets' cannot surface these, and neither can 'cargo check --all-targets --keep-going' — check COMPILES a test target but never RUNS it, and 'cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --no-fail-fast' aborts at the first target that fails to LINK (cargo test has no --keep-going on this toolchain). What works:
  cargo build --tests -p frankenlibc-abi --keep-going
  then execute each target binary in target/debug/deps directly
Locate the binaries in the SAME invocation that built them — an ls/find in a later invocation can hand you a stale artifact (see the note on bd-hdb4c3).

RESULT on an rch worker, 610 conformance_diff binaries executed, 28 RED, 3 produced no result line:
  cfbaud (0/2)                     clock_getcpuclockid (0/1)      dn_comp (1/1)
  error_at_line (11/1)             exact_unary_flags (0/1)        fdopen (1/1)
  fmtmsg (3/1)                     gamma_signgam (0/1)            getdate (0/1)
  getgrouplist_overflow (0/1)      getopt_fuzz (0/1)              getpt (0/1)
  memmove (0/1)                    nearbyint_flags (0/1)          nextup_canon (0/1)
  nice_eperm (0/1)                 pathconf (0/2)                 payload (0/1)
  posix_madvise (0/1)              privileged_syscalls (0/1)      psignal (0/1)
  ptrace_peek (0/1)                ptsname (0/1)                  sched_affinity_zerofill (0/1)
  sysconf (0/1)                    sysconf_raw (0/1)              sysconf_values (1/2)
  tsearch (0/1)
(passed/failed). cfbaud is FIXED at 906493e47 (bd-lmhxt4); the other 27 stand.

DO NOT ASSUME ALL 27 ARE fl DEFECTS. The sweep ran as ROOT in a container. nice_eperm, privileged_syscalls, ptrace_peek, getpt, getgrouplist_overflow, pathconf, sysconf* and getdate are all plausibly environment-dependent — an EPERM arm cannot fail the way it is written when the process is root, and getdate needs DATEMSK. Each needs triage into: (a) real fl divergence, (b) arm whose premise assumes a non-root or differently-configured host, (c) flake. Only (a) is a defect; (b) is a defect in the ARM and should be fixed to state its precondition or skip loudly rather than fail.

Searching .beads/issues.jsonl for these names found open beads only for getcpuclockid (bd-4atx9e, bd-d3tvn3) and error_at_line (bd-m70eq2) and fdopen (bd-28e4u6). The rest were untracked.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN ANY ONE ROW: cfbaud was two shipped fixes composing into a function that did nothing, and the gate that proved it had been sitting red. A gate nobody runs is worth less than no gate, because it is counted as coverage.

DONE = every row above triaged to (a)/(b)/(c) with its own bead or fix, and a documented way to run this sweep that a future agent will actually use. Do NOT close this by re-running the sweep and reporting a number.

    getpt                    O_NOCTTY|O_CLOEXEC re-added           was 8c2658f6d
    nice_eperm               EACCES not remapped to EPERM          was ab7ff020b
    ptrace_peek              PEEK returned 0 instead of the word   was 9c7d75949
    ptsname                  EINVAL not mapped to ENOTTY; buflen   was 9dc0343e8
    getgrouplist_overflow    buffer untouched on overflow          was b851e0bda
  and, found the same way but split out for size:
    getdate                  156-line POSIX default-fill machinery was e5ffb3532+636c72c28  -> bd-3kslha
    sysconf/sysconf_raw/sysconf_values + pathconf  20 POSIX keys   was b5ae82d1a+e2a577d08  -> bd-d3cav6

posix_madvise is not a conformance nit — POSIX_MADV_DONTNEED == MADV_DONTNEED == 4 on Linux and the
kernel form is destructive, so fl was silently zero-filling live pages. The gate read back 0 where
glibc read back 0xdeadbeef.

THE TRIAGE METHOD, which costs about 30 seconds per row and needs no build:
  1. git log --oneline --all -- crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/conformance_diff_<row>*.rs
     The GATE file usually survived the deletion (that is why the row is red rather than dark), so
     its history names the fix commit that shipped with it.
  2. git show <fix-sha> -- 'crates/*/src/*'   -> take a distinctive added line
  3. rg -qF '<that line>' crates/*/src        -> absent means the fix is gone at HEAD
  4. git log -S '<that line>' -- <file>       -> names the adding AND deleting commit
Step 3 has false positives (56745ef4a reformatted the whole tree), so CONFIRM BY READING the
function at HEAD, and confirm the intended behaviour with a live host oracle before restoring. I did
that for every row: fmax/fmin +-0 via libm.so.6, clock_getcpuclockid(0)->0xfffffffa,
getpt FD_CLOEXEC==0, nice(-1)->EPERM as uid 1000, ptsname_r(master,0)->ERANGE and
ptsname_r(non-master)->ENOTTY.

This also revises the bead's own framing. It says 'neither red means fl is broken nor red means the
gate is stale generalises'. On this batch, 10 of 10 red rows were fl defects — but a THIRD category
the bead does not name turned out to be the real one: fl-was-fixed-and-un-fixed. Checking that
first is cheaper than either of the other two triages, and on this evidence it is where the mass is.

Rows still unswept at HEAD: error_at_line (11/1), fdopen (1/1), privileged_syscalls, and the
root/container-dependent set (getgrouplist_overflow now passes as uid 1000, so the bead's suspicion
that it was environment-dependent was wrong — it was a real defect all along).

MEASUREMENT HYGIENE for this sweep's triage, from bd-9ri7g1 (closed at 2b3ccb3d3): until c9d7b28d7, 18 ABI/core test files acquired their shared serialization guard with .expect()/.unwrap(). comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
CORRECTION to my comment earlier today. I wrote that locale_abi_test's 5 failures are 'the worker's LANG=C.UTF-8 leaking into an assertion that expects "C"' and filed them as category (b), an arm-premise defect. THAT WAS WRONG, and it is decision-relevant: it would have sent triage at the arm instead of the implementation.

Two checks refute it. (1) setlocale_set_c_locale passes an explicit "C" — its result cannot depend on LANG at all. (2) Run ALONE it still fails: 'test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed; 51 filtered out' (worker hz2, harness cargo test -j 1 -p frankenlibc-abi --test locale_abi_test setlocale_set_c_locale -- --test-threads=1 --exact), so it is not cross-test interference either.

Real cause, now filed as bd-1kxrmz: fl ships exactly ONE locale and aliases the C locale onto it (C_LOCALE_NAME="C.UTF-8", C_LOCALE_CODESET="UTF-8", setlocale returns that name for the NULL query and for "C"/"POSIX"/""). Live glibc 2.42 returns "C" for both "C" and "POSIX" with CODESET=ANSI_X3.4-1968, and "C.UTF-8"/UTF-8 only when C.UTF-8 was actually selected. Both libraries are self-consistent; they ship different locales. That is a design decision with a codeset consequence, not an arm defect, so it is NOT category (b) and must not be closed by rewriting the arms without recording the choice.

Method note for the rest of this sweep: 'run the arm ALONE' is the cheap discriminator and it separates all three of your categories — passes alone + fails in target = phantom/interference; fails alone = real; fails only under a particular env/uid = (b). It cost one run here and overturned my own conclusion.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
THE SWEEP THIS BEAD ASKED FOR NOW RUNS AS A PLAIN cargo test. bd-5wckql cleared five compile/link aborts of five different kinds; before that, 'cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi' produced ZERO result lines, which is why this bead's METHOD section had to build test binaries individually and execute them by hand.

OBSERVED, worker vmi1149989, harness 'RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 env -u CARGO_TARGET_DIR rch exec -- cargo test -j 1 --no-fail-fast -p frankenlibc-abi -- --test-threads=1', 1619s:
  1078 targets, 6770 tests passed, 43 failed, 29 RED targets.

So the METHOD section can be replaced: no more 'cargo build --tests --keep-going then run the binaries in the same invocation'. The plain command works and reports every target, which also removes the stale-artifact hazard that method carried.

RED TARGETS, 29. Thirteen are gitignored zz_probe_*/zz_scratch_* throwaway probes (mostly 0 passed) — diagnostic probes that assert divergences on purpose, not product defects; see bd-blnp4u. The 16 real ones, with failing test counts:
  unittests 2 | basename_dirname_differential_probe 2 | conformance_diff_catopen 1 | conformance_diff_crypt_gensalt 1 | conformance_diff_langinfo 2 | conformance_diff_math 2 | conformance_diff_nl_langinfo 1 | conformance_diff_nl_langinfo_l 1 | conformance_diff_res_mkquery 1 | getopt_long_differential_fuzz 1 | locale_abi_test 5 | nl_langinfo_scan_differential_fuzz 1 | pwd_abi_test 1 | resolv_abi_test 7 | resource_abi_test 1 | swscanf_int_differential_fuzz 1

CROSS-REFERENCE WITH THIS BEAD'S ORIGINAL 27: almost none of them are the same rows. That list was produced by executing conformance_diff binaries directly as ROOT in a container; this one is the whole crate. Do not merge the two lists — re-triage against this run, which is reproducible with one command.

Five of the red targets (langinfo, nl_langinfo, nl_langinfo_l, nl_langinfo_scan, locale_abi_test — about 10 of the 30 real failures) are very likely ONE cause, bd-1kxrmz: fl aliases the C locale onto C.UTF-8, so setlocale(LC_ALL,"C") returns "C.UTF-8" and CODESET is UTF-8 rather than ANSI_X3.4-1968. Also correcting my earlier comment on this bead: I first classified locale_abi_test's 5 failures as category (b) environment-dependence (worker LANG=C.UTF-8). That was WRONG — setlocale(LC_ALL,"C") cannot depend on LANG, and the arm fails run alone. It is category (a), a real divergence.

title: Guard fuzz minimization scripts against accidental local cargo-fuzz execution

title: getmntent/getmntent_r do not unescape \040 \011 \012 \134 in mount-table fields (glibc does)
description:
TWO GATES ARE CURRENTLY RED ON MAIN because fl's getmntent path returns mount-table fields with glibc's octal escapes still literal:

  crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/conformance_diff_getmntent.rs::getmntent_matches_glibc
  crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/conformance_diff_mntent_escape.rs::getmntent_r_decode_matches_glibc

MEASURED (rch remote, live host glibc oracle in the same invocation):
  fl    = ('tmpfs', '/tmp\\040dir', 'tmpfs', 'rw,size=1G', 0, 0)
  glibc = ('tmpfs', '/tmp dir',      'tmpfs', 'rw,size=1G', 0, 0)

glibc's getmntent_r unescapes exactly four sequences per string field -- \040 space, \011 tab, \012 newline, \134 backslash -- so a mount point may contain whitespace. fl leaves them literal.

VERIFIED PRE-EXISTING, NOT caused by any working-tree change: reproduced at clean HEAD with
  rch exec --base HEAD --clean-overlay --no-overlay -- cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test conformance_diff_getmntent
which yields the identical assertion byte for byte.

THE DECODER ALREADY EXISTS AND IS UNUSED ON THIS PATH: frankenlibc-core/src/mntent/parse.rs::unescape_mntent_field implements precisely those four mappings, documents that any other byte (including a backslash followed by a non-matching triplet such as \054) is copied verbatim to match glibc 2.42, and is evidently reached by the ENCODE direction -- conformance_diff_mntent_escape::addmntent_encode_matches_glibc PASSES. So this is very likely a wiring gap in getmntent_r rather than a missing algorithm.

DONE = both named tests above go green with no relaxation of their assertions, and the round trip addmntent -> getmntent_r is asserted to be identity for a field containing a space, a tab, a newline and a backslash. Keep a negative case: a backslash followed by a non-matching octal triplet (\054) must survive VERBATIM, since that is where a naive 'decode all octal escapes' implementation diverges from glibc.

Related: bd-35m9c7 asks for a getmntent static-buffer differential gate; conformance_diff_getmntent.rs now exists, so that bead should be re-checked against it.
close_reason:
FIXED + GATED. Commit f068a0eeb. Two gates that were RED on main are now green.

DEFECT: glibc's getmntent_r decodes \040 space, \011 tab, \012 newline and \134 backslash in every string field so a mount point may contain whitespace; fl packed the raw field.
  fl    = ('tmpfs', '/tmp\\040dir', 'tmpfs', 'rw,size=1G', 0, 0)
  glibc = ('tmpfs', '/tmp dir',      'tmpfs', 'rw,size=1G', 0, 0)

ROOT CAUSE was a WIRING GAP, not a missing algorithm — the bead's guess was right. frankenlibc-core/src/mntent/parse.rs::unescape_mntent_field implements exactly those four mappings and documents that anything else (including a backslash before a non-matching triplet such as \054) is copied verbatim. It was never called from getmntent_r; rg showed its only callers were its own unit tests in parse.rs. The ENCODE direction did go through the escape layer, which is why addmntent_encode_matches_glibc passed the whole time while decode was broken — a one-directional gate pair hid it.

FIX (crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs::getmntent_r): the field packer now decodes straight into the caller's buffer. Unescaping only ever shrinks, so the existing 'needed' bound computed from raw field lengths stays a valid upper bound and no scratch allocation is required. getmntent (static-buffer variant) delegates to getmntent_r, so one change fixes both entry points.

EVIDENCE (rch remote, source commit f068a0eeb):
  cargo test -j2 --no-fail-fast -p frankenlibc-abi --test conformance_diff_getmntent --test conformance_diff_mntent_escape --test conformance_diff_hasmntopt
    getmntent_matches_glibc ................... ok   (was FAILED)
    getmntent_r_decode_matches_glibc .......... ok   (was FAILED)
    addmntent_encode_matches_glibc ............ ok
    addmntent_getmntent_r_round_trip_is_identity  ok  (new)
    hasmntopt_matches_glibc / _value_option_is_found ... ok
  cargo clippy -j2 -p frankenlibc-abi --lib --test conformance_diff_mntent_escape -- -D warnings -> zero findings on touched files.

NEGATIVE CASES: the pre-existing decode arm already feeds a literal \054 that must stay three characters (a naive 'decode every octal escape' implementation diverges from glibc there) and is a live differential via dlsym, so no assertion needed relaxing.

NEW ARM added per this bead's DONE criteria: addmntent_getmntent_r_round_trip_is_identity. The two existing arms each pin ONE direction against glibc, so a SYMMETRIC defect -- escaping and unescaping the same wrong set -- would satisfy both while corrupting any caller that writes a table and reads it back. It round-trips a record containing a space, a tab, a newline, a backslash and a literal \054, and also asserts the ON-DISK line really contains \040 and \012, so the round trip cannot pass by the writer having emitted raw bytes and the reader echoing them.

PROVENANCE: found by replaying the mntent family's gates while closing bd-emgdrv, not by reading a spec. VERIFIED PRE-EXISTING rather than introduced by this session's work: rch exec --base HEAD --clean-overlay --no-overlay -- cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test conformance_diff_getmntent reproduced the identical assertion byte for byte.

FOLLOW-UP left open, not folded in: bd-35m9c7 asks for a getmntent static-buffer differential gate and describes the surface as 'only fl-internal'; conformance_diff_getmntent.rs now exists and is a live differential, so that bead should be re-checked against it rather than implemented from scratch.

Unrelated agent changes were not reverted.

title: perf: fgetc/fputc double-lock the main stdio registry mutex per char (registry_contains_stream + registry().lock())
description: fgetc (and siblings) call registry_contains_stream(id) [registry().lock() #1, for host-delegation routing] then later registry().lock() #2 for the actual read, for fl-registered streams (the common fmemopen/fopen case) — TWO acquisitions of the same global mutex per char. Collapse to one: acquire once, get_mut; if None, drop + host-delegate. CAUTION: host path currently runs BEFORE decide() (skips it); naive collapse would make host streams pay decide() and could change host-delegation ordering or hold the lock across decide() (deadlock risk). title: ffs-ondisk: Ext4{Compat,Incompat,RoCompat}Features lack kernel-conformance test for 40 feature bits
description:
Finding (via /testing-conformance-harnesses skill, eighth visit,
different target): the three ext4 feature-flag wrapper structs in
crates/ffs-ondisk/src/ext4.rs declare 40 feature-bit constants in
total:

  * `Ext4CompatFeatures` (l. 148-196): 10 flags (DIR_PREALLOC=0x1
    .. ORPHAN_FILE=0x1000)
  * `Ext4IncompatFeatures` (l. 210-...): 16 flags (COMPRESSION=0x1
    .. CASEFOLD=0x20000)
  * `Ext4RoCompatFeatures` (l. 327-...): 14 flags (SPARSE_SUPER=0x1
    .. ORPHAN_PRESENT=0x10000)

Each mirrors a kernel macro from `fs/ext4/ext4.h` (EXT4_FEATURE_*).
The flags control mount eligibility:
  * COMPAT bits: advisory; unknown bits are safe to ignore.
  * INCOMPAT bits: unknown bits MUST cause mount failure.
  * RO_COMPAT bits: unknown bits cause read-only mount.

There is **no kernel-conformance test** pinning the 40 values. A
regression that swapped, e.g., FILETYPE (0x2) and EXTENTS (0x40)
would silently mis-classify every ext4 image. A regression in BIT64
(0x80) would silently fail to recognize 64-bit field layout.

Pairs with bd-tyeic (27 EXT4_*_FL inode flags), bd-k81lq (reserved
inodes), bd-343v3 (file types), bd-khzn4 (btrfs tree objectids),
bd-f0q7n (btrfs item keys), bd-xhswi (btrfs csum types), bd-vnfhb
(POSIX S_IS predicates).

Acceptance: kernel-conformance unit test pinning all 40 feature
flag constants to their canonical kernel macro values, plus the
structural invariant that each flag is a single power-of-2 bit and
no two flags within the same set share a bit.

title: Add gate for exp2/exp10/pow10 (+f32) special cases (+/-inf,+/-0,NaN,exact,over/underflow) vs glibc — uncovered

CLOSED. Commit 6aefa6fb0. Gate conformance_diff_exp_base_special: FAILED -> 'test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out'.

THIS ONE CLOSED BY FIXING THE GATE, NOT THE IMPLEMENTATION, and that needs justifying because
weakening a gate to land a change is a named forbidden pattern. The justification and the required
evidence:

The gate was RED on exactly one argument — exp10(0.5): fl=3.162277660168379 glibc=3.1622776601683795,
1 ULP. It demanded bit-equality for every entry of a shared CASES array. 0.5 is an ORDINARY
argument, and two independent things say it should never have been held to 0 ULP:
  1. THIS BEAD'S OWN SCOPE is special cases — +/-inf, +/-0, NaN, exact integer powers, overflow,
     underflow. All of those passed before and still pass. 0.5 reached past the bead's scope only
     because one array feeds both the special and the ordinary checks.
  2. THE REPO PUBLISHES A 4-ULP TRANSCENDENTAL CONTRACT. exp10's fast path documents it in so many
     words ('within 4 ULP of glibc on [-50,50]') with u<=4 unit tests beside it in core float.rs;
     erf/erfc carry the same contract in special.rs; and two sibling gates are NAMED
     exp2_f64_within_4_ulps_vs_glibc and exp2f_within_4_ulps_vs_glibc. A 0-ULP demand here
     contradicts the published contract and would force withdrawing a deliberately-accepted
     0.6x-glibc accuracy/speed trade.

The gate now applies both standards, selected by a PREDICATE ON THE ARGUMENT — non-finite and every
finite integer stay bit-for-bit; finite non-integers get sign and finiteness pinned exactly plus
<=4 ULP. A predicate, not an exemption list: naming the failing arguments would have turned it green
without meaning anything. pow10==exp10 stays bit-exact for all arguments (an fl-internal identity,
unrelated to matching glibc).

WIN/LOSE SPLIT, MEASURED rather than argued. Setting MAX_ULP to 0 makes the ULP arm equivalent to
bit-equality, so its failures ARE the set the tolerance admits:
  MAX_ULP = 0 -> 1 passed; 1 failed. Sole failure: exp10(0.5), 1 ULP.
  MAX_ULP = 4 -> 2 passed; 0 failed.
exp2, exp2f and exp10f hit 0 ULP on every case, so three of the four functions never touch the
tolerance. The change admits exactly one 1-ULP argument and nothing else. That measurement and the
instruction to repeat it before raising the constant are recorded at the constant itself.

NO implementation changed — exp10's fast path stands and its documented contract is now what the
gate actually checks.

ESCALATED FIRST, not decided unilaterally: this was a collision between two in-repo standards
(published 4-ULP transcendental contract vs newer bit-exact differential gates) affecting several
shipped perf kernels, so I put the options to the user and implemented the one chosen rather than
picking for them.

title: xdr_string/xdr_bytes/xdr_array DECODE allocate from attacker-supplied length BEFORE stream-bounds check
description:
## Reproduction

Found by fuzz_xdr (~10s of fuzzing) on a 16-byte stream:

```
Scenario {
  initial_op_mode: 1,        // XDR_DECODE
  buf_init: [253],           // 1 byte (resized to 16 in fuzz harness)
  buf_size_lie: 1828716579,  // (clamped to 16, doesn't matter)
  ops: [WrapstringDecode],
}
```

The first 4 bytes of the stream decode as the u32 length (RFC 4506 §4.11
big-endian). With `buf_init=[253]` resized to 16, the first 4 bytes are
`fd 00 00 00`, decoded as length = 0xfd000000 ≈ 4.24 GB. xdr_string
allocates a 4.24 GB buffer via `libc::malloc` and only THEN passes it to
xdr_opaque, where xgb finally notices the stream only has 12 bytes
remaining and returns XDR_FALSE.

libFuzzer reports `oom-...` artifact and exit 71 (SIGOUT).

## Defect

In `crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/rpc_abi.rs`:

- `xdr_string` (line ~1119): reads u32 size, validates `size <= maxsize`,
  malloc(size+1) — `maxsize` is `c_uint::MAX` for callers using
  `xdr_wrapstring`, so any 32-bit attacker length passes.
- `xdr_bytes` (line ~1061): same pattern; malloc(size) with maxsize check
  only.
- `xdr_array` (line ~1204): malloc(count * elsize) with `count <=
  maxsize` and overflow check, but the element-count cap is also caller-
  supplied via maxsize.

The `maxsize` is the spec-level upper bound on the value, not the
wire-level upper bound on what can actually fit in the remaining
stream. Even with a sane caller-supplied maxsize, xdr_string lets an
attacker request `min(maxsize, 4GB)` of memory from a stream that
contains only a few bytes.

This is direct CVE-class:
- CVE-2017-17807 (rpcbind: xdr_array len * elsize OOM/DoS)
- CVE-2020-25645 (sunrpc xdr_bytes: malloc before bounds check)
- CVE-2022-23219 (sunrpc xdrmem_create + xdr_opaque length lie)

## Fix

In `xdr_string`, `xdr_bytes`, and `xdr_array` DECODE branches, BEFORE
calling libc::malloc, query the remaining stream bytes via the
xdr_inline / x_getpostn / x_handy field and reject any decoded
length whose payload (size + padding) cannot fit. This is defense-
in-depth on top of the existing maxsize check — a malicious caller
that passes `maxsize=u32::MAX` (which `xdr_wrapstring` does
unconditionally per the glibc spec contract) still cannot trigger
OOM if the decoded length exceeds remaining stream bytes.

Implementation note: `Xdr::x_handy` for xdrmem streams stores the
remaining unread byte count. For xdrrec/xdrstdio streams the check
is harder (streaming source), but for those streams the wire
protocol is record-framed and `xdrrec_eof` / record-length checks
already provide some bounding.

## Severity

[HIGH] (P2). Pre-auth DoS for any service that exposes XDR-parsed
input from untrusted peers (RPC, NFS, NIS+, LDAP-over-XDR
deployments). Mitigation by caller-supplied maxsize is incomplete
because xdr_wrapstring (and any spec-following caller) passes
maxsize=u32::MAX.
notes: Fixed in f7581b5e: (1) xdrmem_remaining_bytes + xdr_padded_len helpers added; xdr_string/xdr_bytes/xdr_array DECODE paths now reject decoded lengths whose padded payload exceeds remaining xdrmem stream BEFORE libc::malloc, blocking the 4 GiB attacker-supplied length DoS vector. (2) xdr_array now rejects elsize=0 with c!=0, closing the 1-byte malloc + per-element 4-byte write heap-buffer-overflow. Verified: 85/85 xdr_abi_test pass, fuzz_xdr 1.6M runs in 91s (~17k exec/s) with no crashes. Found via fuzz_xdr in <60s.

title: ffs-mvcc: ShardedMvccStore lock-ordering invariant is undocumented and untested
description:
Finding (via /deadlock-finder-and-fixer skill, second visit, different
target): `ShardedMvccStore` (crates/ffs-mvcc/src/sharded.rs:115)
holds five `parking_lot::RwLock`s — `shards: Vec<RwLock<MvccShard>>`,
`active_snapshots`, `conflict_policy`, `contention_metrics`, plus
`publication_gate.wait_lock: Mutex<()>` for the publication ordering.
Static audit confirms the canonical implicit lock order:

  active_snapshots (rank 0) → shards (rank 1) → contention_metrics (rank 2)

Production callers comply:

  * `commit` / `commit_ssi`: shards.W (via lock_shards) → preflight_fcw_locked → contention_metrics.W (briefly) → drop shards. No active_snapshots touch.
  * `prune_safe`: active_snapshots.W → prune_versions_older_than → shards.W per shard. No contention_metrics touch.
  * `register_snapshot` / `release_snapshot` / `watermark` / `active_snapshot_count`: active_snapshots only (leaf).
  * `set_conflict_policy` / `effective_policy`: conflict_policy only (leaf).

The order is consistent — no AB-BA in production. But:

  1. **No struct-level doc comment names the invariant.** A future
     contributor adding e.g. a `gc_with_metrics` function that took
     `contention_metrics.write()` BEFORE `active_snapshots.write()`
     would silently introduce a deadlock against `prune_safe`, which
     holds `active_snapshots.write()` while waiting on shard locks
     (which `commit` holds while waiting on `contention_metrics.write()`).

  2. **No regression test exercises the lock ordering under
     contention.** The existing tests in this crate run commit,
     prune, and snapshot ops sequentially. A future deadlock would
     only manifest under concurrent load and would silently regress
     the gate.

Pairs with bd-7zd94 (PersistentMvccStore lock-ordering doc + test);
this one covers the sharded store's larger lock graph.

Acceptance: a doc comment on `ShardedMvccStore` names the canonical
order with rationale, per-field rank annotations, and a table of
production callers showing compliance. One unit test in the `tests`
module spawns concurrent commit + prune_safe + register/release
threads with a watchdog timeout that fails on hang.
notes: Shipped: struct-level doc on ShardedMvccStore documenting the canonical lock order active_snapshots → shards → contention_metrics with per-field rank annotations (rank 0/1/2 + leaf for conflict_policy) and a table of production callers showing compliance. Added lock_ordering_under_concurrent_commit_prune_and_register regression test with 3 concurrent workers (64 commits, 32 prune_safe calls, 64 register/release_snapshot pairs) guarded by a 15s watchdog that panics with bd-bky2f tag on hang.
