title: [AUDIT] Two Jun-26 commits silently deleted ~1300 lines of unrelated work; 2 casualties found, more likely
description:
MEASURED, NOT SUSPECTED. Two commits nine seconds apart, same author, both describing narrow unrelated work, each cut far more than they claim:

  e634aff2a  2026-06-26 23:34:16  'stdlib/wordexp: full ${...} parameter expansion'
             3 files, +568 / -3449.  unistd_abi.rs: 29374 -> 27195 lines.
  bd829b12f  2026-06-26 23:34:25  'stdlib/random: glibc-exact System V random types'
             4 files, +61 / -447.   stdlib_abi_test.rs: 9907 -> 9581 lines.

Line counts (git show <ref>:<file> | wc -l):
  unistd_abi.rs       e634aff2a~1=29374  e634aff2a=27195  HEAD=28064   still ~1310 BELOW the pre-commit peak
  stdlib_abi_test.rs  bd829b12f~1=9907   bd829b12f=9581   HEAD=9726    still ~181 BELOW

Shape is consistent with a bad merge/rebase that reverted those files to an older revision rather than an intentional edit. Roughly 869 and 145 lines have been re-added since by other work, so the deletions were never noticed as such.

TWO CASUALTIES CONFIRMED SO FAR, both found only because a bead pointed at the behaviour:
1. bd-c7cs3h — the setlogmask priority filter in syslog_send, added by dc6bdb4e0 (Jun 18), deleted by e634aff2a. Six weeks with syslog ignoring setlogmask entirely. Restored + gated in 10d408aa1.
2. bd-egk49q — every errno assertion for humanize_number's failure paths, added by 239d43855, deleted by bd829b12f. The errno MAPPING in stdlib_abi.rs survived, so the contract held while the coverage did not. Restored in 251b24190.

In both cases the bead had been marked 'BLOCKER: superseded by <sha>' by the 2026-08-04 comment sweep, against code or tests that no longer existed.

WHY THIS IS P1: anything else those commits dropped is currently unimplemented or ungated with no bead tracking it, and the two found so far were both real behavioural regressions in shipped functions. The deletions are invisible to every existing gate by construction — a deleted test cannot fail.

METHOD (concrete, no guessing required):
  git diff e634aff2a..e634aff2a~1 -- crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs > /tmp/lost_unistd.diff
  git diff bd829b12f..bd829b12f~1 -- crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/stdlib_abi_test.rs > /tmp/lost_stdlib_tests.diff
(note the reversed range: this yields what was REMOVED as additions)
For each removed item, check whether an equivalent exists at HEAD by NAME:
  - removed 'fn <name>' / '#[test] fn <name>' -> rg '<name>' at HEAD
  - removed behaviour with a bead id in a comment -> br show that bead
Anything absent at HEAD is either (a) legitimately superseded by a later rewrite — record which commit, or (b) a lost regression — restore it and gate it.
Also check the other two files e634aff2a touched: crates/frankenlibc-core/src/stdlib/wordexp.rs went 700 lines lighter, and wordexp_differential_fuzz.rs changed; wordexp itself may have lost coverage.

DONE = a per-item disposition for every removed function/test in those two diffs (superseded-by-<sha> or restored-in-<sha>), and a bead filed for each real regression found. Report the count both ways — restoring nothing is a valid outcome IF every item is accounted for by name.

Related: bd-c7cs3h, bd-egk49q. The 'superseded by <sha>' comment sweep of 2026-08-04 is unreliable and must not be used to close anything here without re-reading the source.

AUDIT COMPLETE. Per-item disposition for both diffs below. Net: the source-code deletion was almost entirely re-implemented; the TEST deletion was not, and is the real unrepaired loss.

METHOD: git diff <sha>..<sha>~1 -- <file> (reversed range, so removals appear as additions), extract every removed 'fn <name>', then check each against HEAD by name, and for source helpers check the PUBLIC FUNCTION they served rather than the helper itself.

=== e634aff2a — crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs (29374 -> 27195 lines) ===
44 removed fn names; 34 absent at HEAD by name (10 recur). Disposition: ALL 34 SUPERSEDED, no further regression found.
Every public entry point they served exists at HEAD, re-implemented with different internals — verified for getopt, getopt_long, argp_parse, getdate, fmtmsg, cuserid, pkey_alloc, pkey_set, rseq, sem_wait, strfmon, fallocate, pathconf, fpathconf, getprotobyname_r. title: PORT: humanize_number (NetBSD/FreeBSD libutil byte-count formatter)
description: NetBSD libutil humanize_number(buf, len, bytes, suffix, scale, flags) renders an int64 byte count into a human-readable string in buf, like "1.5K" or "32 MiB". Companion to dehumanize_number (just shipped). Six-prefix table (space K M G T P E) divided by 1024 by default or 1000 when HN_DIVISOR_1000 is set; switches to IEC prefixes (Ki Mi Gi …) when HN_IEC_PREFIXES is set. HN_AUTOSCALE picks the largest scale where the value still fits in three digits; HN_GETSCALE returns the auto-scale value without writing. HN_DECIMAL adds a single fractional digit when the integer part is < 10. HN_NOSPACE/HN_B control the spacing and trailing "B". Used by df(1), du(1), ls -h, and many BSD/Linux utilities. Ship: pure-safe core::stdlib::humanize_number with a HumanizeFlags bitmask + auto-scale algorithm + thin abi shim that maps the C int "scale" parameter to either a numeric scale or one of the special HN_AUTOSCALE/HN_GETSCALE sentinels.

title: [test-infra] 273 gitignored zz_*.rs probes under crates/*/tests are compiled by cargo — any broken one silently re-breaks the whole abi suite
description:
STRUCTURAL cause behind bd-5wckql, which took five fixes to clear because each abort hid the next.

.gitignore:218 excludes '**/tests/zz_*.rs'. There are 273 such probe files under crates/*/tests, against 1876 tracked test files. cargo compiles EVERY .rs in tests/ as its own test target regardless of gitignore, so one uncompilable throwaway probe aborts 'cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi' before a single target executes — while being invisible to git status, git log, git blame and code review. tests/zz_scratch_divmin.rs had been broken since 2026-06-14 and nobody could see it.

The convention itself is reasonable (throwaway probes should not be committed). Its interaction with cargo's test autodiscovery is not.

OPTIONS, none of which I should pick unilaterally because they all change a shared workflow:
  (a) Move probes out of tests/ into a directory cargo does not autodiscover (e.g. crates/frankenlibc-abi/probes/ driven by an explicit [[test]] or a small runner). Path change breaks everyone's muscle memory and any tooling that greps tests/zz_*.
  (b) autotests = false in Cargo.toml plus explicit [[test]] entries for the 1876 tracked targets. Correct and fully mechanical, but an enormous manifest, and AGENTS.md forbids generating it with a script.
  (c) A CI/pre-commit check that builds every tests/*.rs and refuses a broken probe. Keeps the convention, catches the breakage at the author instead of at whoever next runs the suite.
  (d) Do nothing and accept periodic re-breakage, with the static extern-audit from bd-5wckql as the detector.

RECOMMENDATION: (c). It preserves the convention, puts the cost on the probe's author, and needs no path migration.

DO NOT 'fix' this by deleting the 273 probes. Rule 1, and several encode real investigations.

Detector available now, no build required: parse every 'unsafe extern "C"' block under crates/*/tests, resolve each declared symbol (honouring #[link_name]) against the real exports of libc/libm/libpthread/librt/libdl/libutil, and flag anything only another library provides. That found the last two link aborts statically after four had been found the slow way, one 27-minute suite run at a time.

title: [perf][membrane] cheap fast-path for runtime_policy::decide on tiny untracked-default-mode calls (1.4-2x tax)
description: The single biggest remaining vs-glibc perf gap is the per-call membrane decision: runtime_policy::decide runs on EVERY string/stdlib ABI call. On tiny inputs it dominates, costing ~1.4-2x vs glibc (measured: atoi 1.45x@short, memcmp(16) 2.02x, strcmp/strcasecmp small, strpbrk short-string 3.9x). The membrane decide() (frankenlibc-membrane/src/runtime_math/mod.rs:1383) already has a nominal-pointer fast-path + cached atomics, but the common case (untracked pointer, default SafetyLevel, healing off) still pays the full decision aggregation. decide() is proof-gated by structural invariant tests (mod.rs ~8005-8170: cached-atomics-only/no-mutex, Allow-final-else, no-transcendental-on-strict-fast-path), so this needs the membrane architect, NOT a solo edit. Proposal: a branch-predicted ultra-fast Allow for {untracked & default-mode & healing-off & aligned} that still feeds the telemetry counters, gated by the existing structural-invariant tests + a differential that the decision stream is unchanged for tracked/hardened pointers. This single lever would close the residual tax across the ENTIRE ABI surface (everything else is now at parity). Target: tiny-input string/stdlib calls 1.4-2x -> ~1.05x.

title: Verify every claim gate has both positive and negative tests
description: For every claim-control gate in README, FEATURE_PARITY, support_matrix, replacement_levels, semantic overlay, release notes, performance budgets, compatibility reports, and user workload docs, require both positive tests proving allowed advancement and negative tests proving missing, stale, contradictory, or prose-only evidence blocks advancement. 2. Inventory every claim gate and classify it by source artifact, generated artifact, user-visible claim type, replacement level, runtime mode, oracle kind, and owner bead.
3. For each gate, add or specify positive tests for valid evidence advancement and negative tests for missing artifact, stale artifact, contradictory artifact, wrong source commit, insufficient replacement level, skipped runtime mode, unsupported workload, and prose-only advancement.

title: [bug][stdio] fopencookie streams are write-through; glibc buffers them, so fwrite return codes and the timing of hook calls diverge
description:
Split out of bd-zpmf99 at the point where that bead's own scope ended. NOT about NULL hooks — it applies to every cookie stream.

OBSERVATION (live glibc 2.42 vs fl, all-NULL cookie_io_functions_t, mode "w"):
  glibc: fwrite(data,1,5,f) -> 5, ferror=0     then fflush(f) -> -1, ferror=1
  fl:    fwrite(data,1,5,f) -> 0, ferror=1     then fflush(f) ->  0, ferror=1
Both agree on the END state (ferror set, errno untouched) — that half is gated by conformance_diff_fopencookie. They disagree on WHEN.

MECHANISM: glibc gives a cookie stream a normal fully-buffered FILE, so fwrite copies into the buffer and returns the full count; the write hook is not called until the buffer is flushed. fl calls the write hook synchronously from fwrite, so a hook that reports a short write (0 here, because the hook is NULL) is visible in fwrite's OWN return value.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE RETURN CODE: a caller that writes a record and checks fwrite's return sees success under glibc and failure under fl for the same stream and the same hook. Worse for real cookies, the hook is invoked at different points, so a hook with side effects (counting calls, chunking, compressing) observes a different call pattern — sizes and counts, not just timing.

NOT YET ESTABLISHED: whether fl's cookie streams honour setvbuf at all, and whether _IONBF makes glibc match fl. That is the first thing to check, because if fl is simply always _IONBF the fix may be to respect the stream's buffering mode rather than to special-case cookie writes.

DONE = a differential gate over a NON-NULL write hook that records (call count, byte counts) plus fwrite/fflush return codes, green against glibc for the default buffering mode and for an explicit setvbuf(_IOFBF)/_IONBF. Do not close this by asserting only the end state — conformance_diff_fopencookie already does that, and it is precisely what this bead is NOT about.

title: profil/sprofil accept and report the sampling period but never deliver PC samples
description:
fl's profil() is a 'success no-op' (crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/glibc_internal_abi.rs) and sprofil() now mirrors it: both return glibc's success contract, and sprofil writes the correct sampling period into tvp ({0, 1000000/__profile_frequency()} = {0,10000}, measured against live glibc 2.42), but neither arms a SIGPROF/setitimer sampling engine, so the caller's histogram buffer is never written.

This is a REPORTED gap, not a hidden one: it was surfaced while resolving bd-86hcwh, where sprofil's blanket ENOSYS was a measured divergence from glibc (host returns 0). Fixing the return contract was correct and is covered by a differential gate; delivering actual samples is the separate, larger piece of work tracked here.

DONE = profil(buf, bufsiz, offset, scale) installs a periodic sampler that increments the correct bucket of the caller's buffer for the sampled PC, with a gate that burns CPU in a known code range and asserts the corresponding bucket is non-zero while a bucket outside the range stays zero. sprofil extends the same engine to multiple regions.

Note glibc segfaults on sprofil(NULL, profcnt>0, ...) — it dereferences profp without checking — so the enable path cannot be gated as a plain fl-vs-host equality; assert fl's own sampling behaviour instead.

title: EPIC: Flat Combining for Contended State [Score 6.0, section 14.2]
description:
Implement flat combining for sequentially batching operations under contention. When multiple threads contend on shared state (e.g., global allocation statistics, arena rebalancing counters, evidence ledger writes), flat combining designates one thread as the 'combiner' that executes all pending operations sequentially, eliminating lock contention. How it works: (1) Each thread publishes its pending operation to a per-thread slot in a shared publication list. (2) One thread acquires the combiner lock. (3) The combiner scans all publication slots, collects pending operations, and executes them all sequentially. (4) The combiner writes results back to each thread's slot. (5) Other threads spin-wait on their slot until the result appears. Benefits: (a) Sequential execution eliminates all synchronization within the combined batch. (b) Cache locality — the combiner's working set stays hot. (c) Throughput scales better than lock-based approaches under high contention because the combiner amortizes lock acquisition cost across N operations. Target applications in FrankenLibC: global allocation statistics (malloc_stats/mallinfo), arena rebalancing decisions, evidence ledger batch writes, and TSM validation pipeline under burst load.

## Success Criteria
See `acceptance_criteria` field.

**Alien CS Reference:** Section 14.2 of graveyard (Score 6.0). Flat combining from Hendler, Hendler & Shavit (2010 SPAA). Publication list pattern for sequential batching under contention.

- Future applications: arena rebalancing, evidence ledger batch writes, TSM pipeline burst handling.

title: Implement flat-combining lock for global allocation stats
description:
Implement the flat-combining primitive and apply it to global allocation statistics. Core data structure: FlatCombiner<T, Op> where T is the shared state and Op is the operation enum. Components: (1) PublicationList — array of cache-line-aligned slots, one per thread. Each slot contains: operation (Option<Op>), result (Option<Result>), active flag, age counter. (2) CombinerLock — a simple test-and-set lock. Only the combiner holds it. (3) combine() method — acquires lock, scans publication list, executes all pending ops on shared state T, writes results back, releases lock. (4) apply(op: Op) -> Result — publish op to thread's slot, try to become combiner. If successful, run combine(). If not, spin-wait on slot until result appears. First application: global allocation statistics (total_allocated, total_freed, active_allocations, peak_usage, per-size-class counts). Currently protected by a Mutex<AllocStats>. Under 32-thread workload, this mutex is a top-5 contention point. Flat combining should reduce contention by 10-50x for stat-heavy workloads (e.g., mallinfo called frequently).

## Acceptance Criteria
See `acceptance_criteria` field.
design:
**Alien CS Reference:** Section 14.2 of graveyard (Score 6.0). Flat combining from Hendler, Hendler, & Shavit (2010 SPAA). Publication list pattern from Herlihy (2008).

**Rust Implementation Guidance:**
- FlatCombiner<T, Op, R>: generic over shared state T, operation enum Op, and result type R.
- PublicationSlot: #[repr(align(128))] to span 2 cache lines (avoid false sharing on adjacent slot writes).
- Slot layout: op: AtomicPtr<Op>, result: UnsafeCell<MaybeUninit<R>>, active: AtomicBool, age: AtomicU32.
- CombinerLock: AtomicBool with try_lock() returning CombinerGuard.
- combine() scans slots, collects ops into local Vec (bounded by MAX_THREADS), executes sequentially on T, writes results back.
- apply() publishes op, tries to become combiner. If not combiner, spin_loop() on result slot with bounded spins before park().
- Thread slot assignment: thread_local! with lazy init, index from AtomicUsize::fetch_add.

title: Benchmark: flat combining vs lock under high contention
description:
Benchmark flat combining against mutex-based locking for global allocation statistics under various contention levels. Test matrix: (1) Thread counts: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64. (2) Operation mix: read-only (mallinfo), write-only (allocation tracking), mixed (realistic: 80% writes, 20% reads). (3) Batch sizes: 1, 10, 100, 1000 operations per thread between yield points. (4) Baselines: Mutex<AllocStats>, RwLock<AllocStats>, atomic counters (for comparison). Metrics: (a) Throughput (ops/sec aggregate). (b) Latency distribution (p50/p95/p99). (c) Combiner scan overhead (how much time spent scanning publication list). (d) Fairness (variance in per-thread throughput). (e) Cache behavior (L1/L2/L3 miss rates via perf). Expected: flat combining wins decisively at >= 8 threads for write-heavy workloads. For read-only at low thread counts, the overhead of the publication list may make simple locking faster. Document the crossover point. Generate structured JSON results + gnuplot-compatible data files for CI tracking.

title: printf executor DSL cannot express int* output args (%n)
description:
Split off from bd-qij6l. The remaining sprintf %n case `sprintf_n_with_args` (format `%d%n`, args `[123]`) cannot be exercised by the in-process conformance executor because the fixture DSL has no way to express an `int*` output parameter. The executor therefore binds no storage for %n and the case remains tracked as a known impl gap in crates/frankenlibc-harness/tests/printf_conformance_conformance_test.rs KNOWN_IMPL_GAPS.

## Fix direction
One of:
1. Extend the fixture DSL (inputs.args) to allow a typed `{"intptr_out": ...}` element that the executor materializes as a real `int` cell and whose post-call value is captured in `expected_n_value`.
2. Delete `sprintf_n_with_args` from printf_conformance.json (%n with conversions is not meaningfully testable when host glibc refuses it under FORTIFY anyway).

## Out of scope
The two no-arg %n cases (`sprintf_n_count_zero`, `sprintf_n_count_mid`) were already addressed by bd-qij6l: they now run in mode=hardened and no longer need host parity.
notes:
Closed by cc-libc. Resolved by deleting the sprintf_n_with_args fixture entirely. Rationale: host glibc refuses %n under FORTIFY, so a meaningful parity test is impossible regardless of DSL; and the no-arg %n cases (sprintf_n_count_zero/mid, covered by bd-qij6l) already exercise our impl's %n dispatch. Extending the fixture DSL with an intptr_out type would touch ~6 variadic dispatch branches in run_impl_snprintf — not justified for one hardened-only conversion-interaction case. If we ever need pointer-out coverage, the DSL extension can be done properly as its own scope.

Validation: cargo test -p frankenlibc-harness --test printf_conformance_conformance_test -> 14 passed, 0 failed.

syslog/vsyslog ignore the setlogmask priority mask (messages never filtered)
close_reason:
FIXED (regression restored) + GATED, with a measured red-run. Commit 10d408aa1.

THE BLOCKER COMMENT WAS REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT. It claimed 'superseded by dc6bdb4e0 (syslog honors setlogmask) with differential gate 3376bed21; current syslog/vsyslog path filters via SYSLOG_MASK'. At HEAD both halves were false:
- SYSLOG_MASK had exactly TWO readers and both were inside setlogmask() itself (rg -n SYSLOG_MASK crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs -> lines 15551/15573/15575 only). Nothing in syslog(), vsyslog(), or syslog_send() consulted it. The original bug, verbatim.
- 3376bed21 is bd-22qdtd's gate, not this bead's. It exercises the setlogmask set/query round-trip and NEVER CALLS syslog(), so a stored-but-never-read mask passes it perfectly.

ROOT CAUSE: a SILENT REGRESSION, not an unimplemented feature. dc6bdb4e0 (2026-06-18) added the check at the top of syslog_send. e634aff2a (2026-06-26) DELETED it -- a commit titled 'stdlib/wordexp: full ${...} parameter expansion (default/alt/length)' that had nothing to do with syslog. Traced with: git log -S 'SYSLOG_MASK.load' -- crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs, then git show e634aff2a for the removed hunk. With no arm covering the behaviour it went unnoticed for six weeks, and the bead sat 'superseded' against code that no longer existed.

FIX (crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs::syslog_send): restored at its original site -- in syslog_send so syslog and vsyslog share it exactly as glibc's both funnel through __vsyslog_internal, and before the state lock and any I/O so a filtered message does not even open the socket. Rule: (1 << (priority & 0x07)) & mask == 0 -> return, i.e. glibc's (LOG_MASK(LOG_PRI(pri)) & LogMask) == 0.

GATE: crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/conformance_diff_syslog_mask.rs (new file; no syslog gate existed). openlog with LOG_PERROR makes both impls echo to stderr, so 'was it emitted' is observable on a captured fd 2 with no syslog daemon involved. Compares WHICH priorities produced output rather than the bytes of the line -- line formatting is a separate concern and asserting it here would make the gate fail for reasons that are not the bug it guards (the lesson from bd-0qltjh earlier this session). glibc reached through extern decls with a dlsym assert_ne against fl's own addresses, so a release test build cannot silently compare fl to itself.
  syslog_honors_log_upto_err
  syslog_honors_a_single_priority_mask            non-contiguous masks; catches an impl treating the mask as a <= threshold, which LOG_UPTO alone cannot distinguish
  a_filtered_message_is_dropped_not_merely_unprinted   the mask gates the message, not just the LOG_PERROR echo
  syslog_emits_every_priority_under_the_default_mask   NEGATIVE CONTROL: all bits set -> nothing filtered, so an impl dropping everything (or a blind capture) still fails
  setlogmask_round_trip_still_matches_glibc       bd-22qdtd's property, kept alongside so the relationship is visible
Each differential arm also asserts what the ORACLE produced, not merely that the arms agree: if BOTH impls stopped filtering -- the exact state guarded against -- equality alone would still hold.

EVIDENCE (rch remote, source commit 10d408aa1):
  GREEN: cargo test -j2 -p frankenlibc-abi --test conformance_diff_syslog_mask -> 5 passed; 0 failed
  clippy -j2 -p frankenlibc-abi --lib --test conformance_diff_syslog_mask -- -D warnings -> zero findings on touched files

  RED-RUN (proves the gate is not vacuous). Ran the SAME committed gate against a copy with only the filter deleted, in a throwaway detached worktree at /data/projects/.worktrees/frankenlibc-redrun-bd-c7cs3h so the shared tree was never left broken (verified: main tree kept both SYSLOG_MASK.load readers throughout):
    test result: FAILED. 2 passed; 3 failed.
    syslog_honors_log_upto_err            FAILED  fl=[T,T,T,T,T,T,T,T] glibc=[T,T,T,T,F,F,F,F]
    syslog_honors_a_single_priority_mask  FAILED  fl=[T,T,T,T,T,T,T,T] glibc=[F,F,F,F,F,F,F,T]
    a_filtered_message_is_dropped_not_merely_unprinted  FAILED
    syslog_emits_every_priority_under_the_default_mask  passed  (correct: nothing should be filtered under an all-bits mask)
    setlogmask_round_trip_still_matches_glibc           passed  <- EMPIRICAL CONFIRMATION that bd-22qdtd's gate is blind to this regression, which is why six weeks passed
  Note: rch refuses project paths outside /data/projects ('input resolves outside canonical root'), so the worktree had to live under /data/projects/.worktrees/ rather than in the session scratchpad.

CLEANUP OWED: the throwaway worktree /data/projects/.worktrees/frankenlibc-redrun-bd-c7cs3h still exists and contains a DELIBERATELY BROKEN syslog_send. It carries a WHAT_IS_THIS.txt saying so. title: fuzz: no dedicated fuzz target for ext4 casefold key/collide/diagnostics
description:
Finding (via /testing-fuzzing skill, NEW target): fuzz/fuzz_targets/ has 47 targets but NONE dedicated to the ext4 casefold collision contract — ext4_casefold_key, ext4_casefold_names_collide, ext4_casefold_name_diagnostics. fuzz_ext4_checksums covers casefold tangentially via lookup_in_dir_block_casefold (it constructs a single fixed search key b"Test_File" and asserts determinism for that key against block-shaped input), but the casefold *function itself* — the byte-level fold — never receives arbitrary fuzzed input.

The casefold fold has UTF-8/ASCII-fallback branching, multi-codepoint sharp-s expansion (ß/ẞ -> 'ss'), and produces a Vec<u8> that the directory-lookup path treats as the canonical comparison key. A bug in any branch would silently mis-classify directory entries on case-folded ext4 filesystems.

The newly-shipped bd-6rsow proptest verifies the equivalence-relation laws on 32 random byte sequences. A dedicated fuzz target lifts that to >1M iterations with libfuzzer corpus learning across mutations of multi-byte UTF-8 boundaries, ASCII edge cases, and byte sequences that look almost-but-not-quite UTF-8.

Acceptance: new fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_ext4_casefold.rs that, for arbitrary byte input, asserts:
  * ext4_casefold_key(name) never panics
  * ext4_casefold_names_collide(name, name) is reflexive
  * ext4_casefold_key(ext4_casefold_key(name)) == ext4_casefold_key(name) (idempotence)
  * ext4_casefold_name_diagnostics(name).folded_key == ext4_casefold_key(name)
  * ext4_casefold_name_diagnostics(name).source_len == name.len()
  * Symmetry on a split-input pair: collide(a, b) == collide(b, a)
Plus a [[bin]] entry in fuzz/Cargo.toml so cargo-fuzz can drive it.
close_reason: done

title: [MOCK-FINDER] btrfs_ino_lookup only supports root objectid; non-root returns ENOENT with 'not implemented yet' comment
description:
# Mock-finder audit finding

`FsOps::btrfs_ino_lookup` at crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:16062-16082 only returns a path for `objectid == BTRFS_FIRST_FREE_OBJECTID (256)` and falls through to `Err(FfsError::Io(libc::ENOENT))` for every other inode, with the comment: `// Full back-reference walking not implemented yet.`

## Context

The prior bead bd-jfsga ('add BTRFS_IOC_INO_LOOKUP ioctl support') was closed 2026-04-21 as 'done' with acceptance criterion 'BTRFS_IOC_INO_LOOKUP returns correct path for known inodes'. The current implementation satisfies that criterion only for the single well-known root objectid; every other known inode returns ENOENT indistinguishable from 'inode does not exist'. Callers (btrfs-progs, user scripts) cannot tell the difference between 'this inode genuinely doesn't exist' and 'this file doesn't implement lookup for non-root inodes'.

## Evidence

- Backend: crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:16062-16082
- FUSE dispatcher wiring: crates/ffs-fuse/src/lib.rs:2100-2125 (correctly routes the ioctl)
- Comment verbatim: 'Full back-reference walking not implemented yet.'

## Why this is a real stub, not an intentional scope limit

Unlike write-participating MMP (crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:6531) and e2compr lzv1/lzrw3a/bzip2 (6989, 7955), which surface a bespoke `UnsupportedFeature` error with a clear scope message, this path returns a generic ENOENT that masks the limitation from callers and from conformance tools.

## Fix direction

Walk the btrfs INODE_REF / INODE_EXTREF back-references chain from the target objectid up to the tree root, assembling path components in reverse. Reference implementation: fs/btrfs/ioctl.c::btrfs_search_path_in_tree in Linux v6.19. For v1 scope, supporting only same-subvolume paths (no cross-subvolume) is acceptable if documented.

## Acceptance

- Non-root objectid that exists in the subvolume tree returns its reconstructed path.
- Non-existent objectid returns a structured NotFound / FfsError that the FUSE layer maps to ENOENT (current behavior preserved for truly-missing inodes).
- Unit + mounted-path test that resolves a file created at runtime and asserts the returned path matches.
- If cross-subvolume resolution is out of scope, emit `UnsupportedFeature('cross-subvolume btrfs_ino_lookup not implemented')` with a distinct errno mapping instead of ENOENT.
close_reason: Implemented in commit f70dcca. btrfs_ino_lookup (crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:16051) now walks INODE_REF back-references from the target objectid up to the subvolume root, assembling a /-separated path with trailing / before the terminating NUL (matches fs/btrfs/ioctl.c::btrfs_search_path_in_tree). Algorithm extracted as pure helper btrfs_build_path_from_inode_refs for unit-testability; 6 new tests cover subvolume root, single hop, multi-hop a/b/c/, missing back-ref → NotFound, cycle → Corruption, and hard-link first-wins determinism. Cross-subvolume (ROOT_REF) remains out-of-V1-scope but now returns UnsupportedFeature with a clear message rather than silent ENOENT. All 6 new tests + existing ffs-core suite pass via rch; workspace clippy green.

title: [HIGH] build_btrfs_readdir_image still computes invalid tree_block_csum after explicit stamping
description:
# Review finding

The current `build_btrfs_readdir_image()` fixture already writes explicit CRC32C values into both synthetic tree blocks, but `rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/rch_target_frankenfs_cod cargo test --workspace --all-targets` still fails the six btrfs directory-walk tests with `Format("invalid field: tree_block_csum (CRC32C checksum mismatch)")`.

## Evidence
- Builder already stamps both blocks: `crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:23225-23378`.
- It computes `csum_root` and `csum_fs` over `image[tree + 0x20 .. tree + nodesize]` and writes them to bytes `0..4`.
- After `br-bd-o5114 repair btrfs default-root smoke fixture`, the remaining red frontier is exactly:
  - `walk_btrfs_dir_entry_items_includes_dir_index_items`
  - `btrfs_readdir_mixed_types`
  - `btrfs_readdir_empty_directory_returns_dot_dotdot`
  - `btrfs_readdir_sorted_by_index`
  - `btrfs_readdir_offset_pagination`
  - `btrfs_readdir_special_characters_in_names`
- All six still fail on the same checksum mismatch, so the root cause is no longer "missing stamp calls".

## Why this is high severity
This keeps the full workspace test gate red and shows the older broad review bead is now under-specified. The next implementation pass needs to debug the actual checksum semantics, not just add stamp writes.

## Expected fix direction
Audit the exact checksum window, node header fields, and final byte mutations for the 16 KiB synthetic readdir fixture. Verify the bytes being hashed match what the parser later validates.
close_reason: Already shipped; targeted btrfs readdir repros now pass

title: poll fortify nfds byte-count overflow abort
description: __poll_chk and __ppoll_chk compute nfds*sizeof(pollfd) with a hard-coded unchecked multiply. In debug builds an overflowing nfds can panic instead of taking the fortify abort path, and in optimized builds it can wrap before delegating. Replace the guard with checked size_of::<pollfd>() math and add fork-isolated overflow coverage for both wrappers.
close_reason:
ALREADY FIXED AND FULLY COVERED — verified, not assumed. No code change was needed and none was
made. Unlike the last four beads in this queue, this one's coverage has no missing half.

BOTH HALVES OF THE BEAD'S REQUEST ARE PRESENT AT HEAD, read directly from the source
(bd-02gcfy discipline — the bead's own text asserts the defect is live, and it is not):

1. "Replace the guard with checked size_of::<pollfd>() math"
   crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/fortify_abi.rs:1173
     fn checked_pollfd_bytes(nfds: NfdsT) -> usize {
         let Some(bytes) = (nfds as usize).checked_mul(core::mem::size_of::<libc::pollfd>())
             else { unsafe { __chk_fail() } };
         bytes
     }
   No hard-coded multiplier, no unchecked multiply, and size_of::<pollfd>() rather than a literal.
   BOTH wrappers call it before delegating: __poll_chk (1181) and __ppoll_chk (1194).

2. "add fork-isolated overflow coverage for both wrappers"
   crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/fortify_abi_test.rs has all six arms, three per wrapper:
     poll_chk_safe / poll_chk_nfds_over_real_buffer / poll_chk_nfds_byte_count_overflow
     ppoll_chk_safe / ppoll_chk_nfds_over_real_buffer / ppoll_chk_nfds_byte_count_overflow
   all through assert_child_sigabrt (fork + waitpid + WIFSIGNALED/WTERMSIG == SIGABRT).

THE OVERFLOW ARM DISCRIMINATES THE EXACT DEFECT, which is the check I make before closing on a
green gate rather than after (see bd-44y7sl, bd-3vz1f8, bd-8omwj4 — three gates in this same queue
that passed for the wrong reason). It passes
    overflowing_nfds = usize::MAX / size_of::<pollfd>() + 1     (= 2^61 on x86_64)
    fdslen           = usize::MAX
With the checked multiply, 2^61 * 8 overflows -> None -> __chk_fail -> SIGABRT, and the test passes.
With the UNCHECKED multiply the bead describes, the product wraps and the guard compares
`wrapped <= usize::MAX`, which never fires, so no abort happens, the child falls through to
_exit(127), WIFSIGNALED is false and the test FAILS. Choosing fdslen = usize::MAX is what makes it
discriminating: any smaller value would abort on the ordinary size comparison and mask the overflow.

IT ALSO DISTINGUISHES ABORT FROM PANIC, which is the other half of the bead's concern ("in debug
builds an overflowing nfds can panic instead of taking the fortify abort path"). These tests run in
a debug build. A Rust panic would unwind out of the closure and reach _exit(127), giving
WIFSIGNALED == false; only a real abort gives WTERMSIG == SIGABRT. The arms pass with SIGABRT, so
the abort path is positively confirmed rather than merely "did not crash differently".

GATE OBSERVED COMPILING AND EXECUTING, whole target, no name filter:
  RCH_ENV_ALLOWLIST=CARGO_TARGET_DIR RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec -- \
    cargo test -j 2 -p frankenlibc-abi --test fortify_abi_test
  test poll_chk_safe ... ok
  test poll_chk_nfds_over_real_buffer_aborts_child_process ... ok
  test poll_chk_nfds_byte_count_overflow_aborts_child_process ... ok
  test ppoll_chk_safe ... ok
  test ppoll_chk_nfds_over_real_buffer_aborts_child_process ... ok
  test ppoll_chk_nfds_byte_count_overflow_aborts_child_process ... ok
  test result: ok. 152 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 10.32s

No unrelated user or agent changes were stashed, reverted, or deleted.

title: Printf DISC-001: Implement banker's rounding (round-half-to-even)

title: PORT: strpct/strspct (NetBSD libutil percentage formatters)
description: Port the NetBSD libutil percentage formatters: char *strpct(char *buf, size_t bufsize, uintmax_t num, uintmax_t denom, size_t precision) and char *strspct(char *buf, size_t bufsize, intmax_t num, intmax_t denom, size_t precision). Each renders 100 * num / denom into buf rounded to `precision` fractional digits, returning buf. denom == 0 yields "0" (or "0.0..0" for precision > 0) per NetBSD convention. strspct preserves the sign of (num * denom). Used by df/iostat/etc for "% Used" columns. Implementation: pure-safe core helper format_percent that does the integer math + rounding without floats; abi shims that snprintf the result into the bounded buffer with truncation guarded. Tests: zero/non-zero precision, denom=0, exact integers, halfway-rounding, signed strspct sign handling, undersized buffer, NULL buf returns NULL.

title: ffs-mvcc: WalWriter::append_commit + rollback_failed_append have implicit append-only reasoning mode
description:
Finding (via /modes-of-reasoning-project-analysis skill, third
visit, different target): `WalWriter::append_commit`
(crates/ffs-mvcc/src/wal_writer.rs:310) has inline `// ── D1 ──`,
`// ── D8 ──`, etc. dividers naming individual invariants
(strict monotonicity, sentinel rejection, backpressure, etc.) but
**no function-level doc block** that names the OVERARCHING
reasoning mode the function implements:

  **Append-only with strict-monotonic sequence check, plus
  atomic-rollback on any failure between encoded-write and synced
  state.**

The partner helper `rollback_failed_append` (l. 627) reverts THREE
state pieces on failure but is private with no doc:

  1. `write_pos` — reset to the pre-append offset
  2. file length — truncated via `set_len(write_offset)` (best-
     effort, ignored result)
  3. `appends_since_sync` — restored to pre-append value

There is also an INLINE rollback path inside `append_commit` for
verify failure (l. 411-412) that resets only `write_pos` and
truncates the file — NOT `appends_since_sync`, because the
`increment_pending_sync_count` happens AFTER verify (l. 419). This
is intentional but easy to miss — a future contributor moving the
verify check after the increment, or adding new pre-sync state,
might forget to reset it on verify failure.

Same shape as bd-gqswx (in-memory commit_internal +
rollback_in_memory_commit) and bd-3ydm6 (is_reserved_inode
fail-closed): a critical reasoning mode applied without naming.

Acceptance: function-level doc blocks on `append_commit` and
`rollback_failed_append` naming the **append-only with
strict-monotonic sequence check + atomic-rollback** mode, listing
the three state pieces the rollback covers, and explicitly calling
out the two-rollback-paths invariant (the inline verify-failure
rollback is sufficient because the sync counter has not been
incremented yet; any new pre-sync state added between verify and
sync MUST be reset on verify failure too). NO behavioural change.
notes: Shipped: function-level doc blocks on WalWriter::append_commit and rollback_failed_append in crates/ffs-mvcc/src/wal_writer.rs naming the append-only + strict-monotonic + atomic-rollback reasoning mode. Documents the three state pieces rollback_failed_append covers (write_pos, file length, appends_since_sync) and explicitly calls out the two-rollback-paths invariant: (1) verify-failure inline rollback only resets write_pos and file length because the sync counter has NOT been incremented yet; (2) post-counter sync-failure delegates to rollback_failed_append. Any new failure path or reordering that puts the increment before verify MUST update both rollback paths to keep the WAL invariant. Pure documentation diff — no behavioural change. Pairs with bd-gqswx (in-memory commit_internal atomic-or-rollback) and bd-3ydm6 (fail-closed reasoning). Verified via rch exec -- cargo check -p ffs-mvcc --lib (Finished in 33.27s).

title: REVIEW: [HIGH] pthread_cond_wait/timedwait clobbers RECURSIVE/ERRORCHECK mutex owner without ownership check
description:
In crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/pthread_abi.rs lines 2541-2554 (pthread_cond_wait) and 2775-2788 (pthread_cond_timedwait), for PTHREAD_MUTEX_RECURSIVE_TYPE and PTHREAD_MUTEX_ERRORCHECK_TYPE the code unconditionally clears the mutex owner (owner.store(MUTEX_NO_OWNER)) and zeros the recursive lock count (count.swap(0)), without first verifying that the calling thread is actually the owner.

If thread A holds a recursive mutex with count=N and thread B incorrectly invokes pthread_cond_wait on that same mutex (a POSIX violation, but glibc detects it for ERRORCHECK), the current code:
1. Saves count (which belongs to A) into thread B's stack-local saved_count
2. Stores NO_OWNER, destroying A's ownership record
3. Resets count to 0, destroying A's recursion depth
4. Waits on the condvar
5. On wake, claims ownership for thread B and restores A's saved count to thread B

This effectively allows thread B to silently steal the mutex. POSIX mandates EPERM for pthread_cond_wait with an unlocked or non-owned ERRORCHECK mutex.

Repro: Two threads, mutex_init with PTHREAD_MUTEX_ERRORCHECK; thread A locks; thread B calls pthread_cond_wait without locking; expect EPERM, observe owner state corruption.

Fix: Before saving/clearing owner, read current owner via owner.load(Acquire) and compare to core_self_tid(). If mismatch and type is ERRORCHECK, return EPERM. For RECURSIVE, also return EPERM (POSIX says behavior is undefined, but EPERM is safer than corruption).
close_reason: Fixed: commit 64fb99b2 added owner verification in pthread_cond_wait/timedwait for RECURSIVE/ERRORCHECK; returns EPERM for non-owner. Regression test added.

title: [bug][resolv] fl public gethostent emits AF_INET6 entries; glibc's gethostent returns an AF_INET-only view (7 vs 3 on a stock /etc/hosts)
description:
Found while fixing bd-79p18u (98975eb0b). That bead was about the PRIVATE helper `_gethtent`; this
is the same class of defect in the PUBLIC POSIX entrypoint, and it is larger.

MEASURED, live glibc via ctypes over this machine's real /etc/hosts (2 IPv4 lines + 5 IPv6 lines):
  glibc gethostent yielded 3 entries, ALL af=AF_INET(2), h_length=4:
    name=localhost      addrs=['127.0.0.1']
    name=thinkstation1  addrs=['127.0.1.1']
    name=ip6-localhost  addrs=['127.0.0.1']  aliases=['ip6-loopback']   <- the ::1 line, converted
  It returned NO AF_INET6 entry, and skipped fe00::0 / ff00::0 / ff02::1 / ff02::2 entirely.

fl's public gethostent (crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs, host_iter_next at ~18562) calls
parse_addr_binary(addr_str) and emits whatever family that returns, including AF_INET6, setting
h_addrtype/h_length accordingly. On this /etc/hosts it would therefore yield 7 entries (2 IPv4 +
5 IPv6) where glibc yields 3, with different h_addrtype values — a caller iterating gethostent and
assuming glibc's AF_INET view gets extra entries with 16-byte addresses.

NOTE ON PROVENANCE: bd-79p18u carried a blocker comment asserting that because "public gethostent
already parses both AF_INET and AF_INET6 in unistd_abi.rs ... no safe code change remains". That
same fact is the defect here, not a reason to stand down.

DO NOT FIX BLIND — MEASURE FIRST. glibc's family behaviour for the hosts iterator interacts with
RES_USE_INET6 and with sethostent/gethostent_r, and the AF_INET view above is what an unconfigured
process sees. Before changing fl, characterise glibc under: default; after res_init with
RES_USE_INET6 set; and via gethostent_r. Use the recipe that worked for bd-79p18u — a synthetic
/etc/hosts bind-mounted with `bwrap --dev-bind / / --bind <file> /etc/hosts` and a ctypes drain —
so the input is controlled rather than whatever the host happens to have.

DONE = fl's public gethostent reproduces glibc's observable entry sequence (count, order, h_name,
h_aliases, h_addrtype, h_length, address bytes) on a controlled /etc/hosts covering plain IPv4,
::1, ::ffff:a.b.c.d, ::a.b.c.d, and ordinary global/link-local IPv6, gated by a live in-process A/B
in the style of resolv_abi_test.rs::gethtent_matches_glibc_gethostent_af_inet_view (in a test build
fl is not no_mangle, so a declared extern gethostent binds to host glibc). The gate must be shown
RED against the current implementation before it is called green.
close_reason:
FIXED. Source commit fbeb967c5. The bead (which I filed while closing bd-79p18u) was correct, and
the divergence was larger than the private-helper one that led to it.

ORACLE MEASURED FIRST, exactly as the bead demanded — it explicitly said "DO NOT FIX BLIND —
MEASURE FIRST" and named three configurations to characterise. All three are now settled:

1. DEFAULT gethostent, over a bind-mounted synthetic hosts file
   (bwrap --dev-bind / / --bind <file> /etc/hosts + a ctypes drain):
     ::1 and 0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1  -> 127.0.0.1  af=AF_INET len=4   (IN6_IS_ADDR_LOOPBACK)
     ::ffff:1.2.3.4           -> 1.2.3.4                        (IN6_IS_ADDR_V4MAPPED)
     ::ffff:0102:0304         -> 1.2.3.4                        (same, hex spelling)
     ::1.2.3.4                -> SKIPPED   (v4-COMPATIBLE is NOT v4-mapped)
     ::0, ::ffff:0:9.10.11.12, 64:ff9b::13.14.15.16, fe80::1, 2001:db8::5 -> SKIPPED
     aliases preserved on converted entries
2. gethostent_r on the same file: BYTE-IDENTICAL to gethostent, entry for entry. So one rule serves
   both entry points and no separate reentrant contract is needed.
3. RES_USE_INET6: MOOT. It was removed from glibc in 2.25, so there is no supported way to make the
   public iterator return AF_INET6 at all. That closes the bead's open question rather than leaving
   it as a caveat — the AF_INET view is not a default, it is the only behaviour.

DEFECT CONFIRMED LIVE at clean HEAD by the new gate, not inferred:
  gethostent entry count diverged: fl=5 glibc=3
    fl:    [("hetzner2",2,4,..), ("localhost",2,4,..), ("localhost",10,16,..),
            ("ip6-allnodes",10,16,..), ("ip6-allrouters",10,16,..)]
    glibc: [("hetzner2",2,4,..), ("localhost",2,4,..), ("localhost",2,4,..)]
Three AF_INET6 entries (af=10, h_length=16) that glibc never emits. A caller iterating gethostent
and assuming glibc's AF_INET view would read 16-byte addresses out of a 4-byte contract.

FIX: crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs — the shared shim both iterators use now implements
glibc's AF_INET view and is RENAMED parse_addr_binary -> hosts_line_af_inet_addr, documenting that
it never yields AF_INET6. The old name is what invited the bug: it read as a generic address parser
while both of its callers were the hosts iterator, so "return whatever family you parsed" looked
right. That is the same failure shape as sys_fchmodat's flags parameter in bd-f29d1s — a signature
that lied about its contract — and renaming it is the durable half of the fix.

Both call sites updated: host_iter_next (gethostent) and gethostent_r. `to_ipv4_mapped` is used
rather than `to_ipv4` because only the former excludes the v4-compatible form glibc skips.

GATE — two arms appended to resolv_abi_test.rs, both holding RESOLVER_ENV_LOCK (the lesson from
bd-5zait2: fl honours the process-wide hosts override that sibling tests install, glibc does not):
  public_gethostent_matches_glibc_af_inet_view — full sequence diff (name, h_addrtype, h_length,
      address bytes) against live glibc, PLUS the oracle's positive fact asserted separately (every
      glibc entry is AF_INET with h_length 4), so a joint regression to AF_INET6 still fails rather
      than passing because both sides moved together.
  public_gethostent_agrees_with_gethtent — pins the public iterator against _gethtent. The two
      implement the same rule in different files and had already drifted apart once; this makes the
      drift a test failure instead of a discovery.

  WITH THE FIX:
    cargo test -j 2 -p frankenlibc-abi --test resolv_abi_test -- public_gethostent
    test public_gethostent_agrees_with_gethtent ... ok
    test public_gethostent_matches_glibc_af_inet_view ... ok
    test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 219 filtered out
  CONTROL — clean HEAD, tests overlaid, fix EXCLUDED
  (rch exec --base HEAD --clean-overlay -o crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/resolv_abi_test.rs):
    test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 2 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 219 filtered out

WHOLE TARGET, no name filter: 188 passed; 2 failed. The 2 are the pre-existing
nss_files_gethostbyname_uses_hosts_backend and nss_files_gethostbyname4_uses_gaih_addrtuple_backend
pair, identical to the clean-HEAD baseline and untouched. fmt clean.

No unrelated user or agent changes were stashed, reverted, or deleted.

title: EPIC: Implement real DNS resolution for getaddrinfo
description:
getaddrinfo() currently only resolves:
1. Numeric IP addresses (127.0.0.1, ::1)
2. Hostnames found in /etc/hosts

It does NOT perform actual DNS queries. This means programs like wget, curl (for non-localhost URLs), dig, nslookup, and any network client that resolves hostnames will fail.

OPTIONS:
A) Delegate to host libc's getaddrinfo for non-numeric, non-/etc/hosts hostnames
B) Implement a minimal DNS stub resolver (send UDP query to nameserver from /etc/resolv.conf)
C) Both: try our resolver first, fall back to host

Option A is fastest to implement and most reliable. Option B gives us full independence from host libc.

ALREADY DONE: /etc/hosts lookup works, numeric IP parsing works, freeaddrinfo correctly frees our Box-allocated structures.
close_reason: Already implemented. getaddrinfo has a full native DNS stub resolver: udp_dns_query() sends A/AAAA queries to /etc/resolv.conf nameservers via SYS_socket/SYS_sendto/SYS_recvfrom with configurable timeout/retry. ResolverConfig parses nameservers, search domains, ndots. Resolution chain: numeric -> /etc/hosts -> DNS -> repair fallback. 46 resolv tests pass. Previously verified when closing bd-zh1y.7 and bd-1y7.

title: Add host libc delegation for DNS-requiring getaddrinfo calls
description:
When getaddrinfo receives a hostname that:
1. Is NOT a numeric IP address
2. Is NOT found in /etc/hosts

Delegate to the host libc's getaddrinfo via our ELF resolver. The host's getaddrinfo will perform the actual DNS query.

IMPLEMENTATION:
1. resolve_host_symbol_raw("getaddrinfo") to get host's function pointer
2. Call host_getaddrinfo(node, service, hints, res) 
3. Return the host's result directly (the addrinfo structs are heap-allocated by the host)
4. In freeaddrinfo, detect whether the addrinfo was allocated by us (Box) or host (malloc) and free accordingly

TRICKY PART: freeaddrinfo must distinguish our Box-allocated addrinfos from host-malloc-allocated ones. Could use a sentinel field or check if the pointer is in our Box allocation range.

title: Add GitHub Actions CI workflow for fmt/check/clippy/test gates
description:
## What
Create .github/workflows/ci.yml that runs all quality gates on every push to main and on PRs.

## Why
Currently all gates (cargo fmt --check, cargo check --workspace --all-targets, cargo clippy
--workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace) run manually. Regressions
can be committed undetected. CI automation is the single highest-leverage improvement.

## Implementation Plan

### Step 1: Create .github/workflows/ci.yml
- Trigger: push to main, pull_request to main
- OS: ubuntu-latest (FUSE-dependent; no macOS/Windows)
- Rust: install via dtolnay/rust-toolchain@nightly (per rust-toolchain.toml)
- System deps: apt-get install libfuse3-dev fuse3 (for fuser crate)
- Cache: actions/cache for ~/.cargo/registry, ~/.cargo/git, target/

### Step 2: Define CI jobs
Job 1 — fmt-check:
  cargo fmt --check

Job 2 — check-clippy:
  cargo check --workspace --all-targets
  cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

Job 3 — test:
  cargo test --workspace
  cargo test --workspace --all-features (separate step, catches feature-gated issues)

Job 4 — test-e2e (optional, needs privileged):
  Only if /dev/fuse available
  cargo test -p ffs-harness --test fuse_e2e -- --test-threads=1

### Step 3: Add CI status badge to README.md
Replace or add alongside existing badges:
  [![CI](https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/frankenfs/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](...)

### Step 4: Verify CI works
- Create a test branch, push it, verify Actions run
- Intentionally break something (add a clippy warning), verify CI catches it
- Fix and verify green

## Considerations
- rust-toolchain.toml pins nightly — CI must respect this (dtolnay/rust-toolchain reads it)
- E2E FUSE tests skip gracefully when /dev/fuse unavailable (tested: fuse_e2e.rs line 225)
- Build time estimate: ~2min check+clippy, ~1min tests (from rch timings)
- asupersync has no special CI requirements (pure Rust, no system deps beyond FUSE)
- Cargo.lock should be committed for reproducible CI builds
- Consider: actions/cache key should include rust-toolchain.toml hash for cache invalidation

## Test Plan
- Push to a test branch and verify all 4 jobs run
- Verify FUSE E2E tests either run (if privileged) or skip (if not) without failing
- Verify cache hits on second push reduce build time
- Verify intentional failure (e.g., add unused variable) is caught by clippy job

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] .github/workflows/ci.yml exists and is valid YAML
- [ ] CI runs on every push to main and on PRs
- [ ] All 4 gates (fmt, check, clippy, test) are separate jobs
- [ ] README badge shows CI status
- [ ] E2E tests skip gracefully when FUSE unavailable
- [ ] Cache configured for cargo artifacts
- [ ] Verified: CI catches intentional failures

description: glibc_baseline_math/powf_irrational (base in [0.5,2.5), exp 1.337): fl 1615ns/batch vs glibc 589 = 2.73x slower (WORST math gap). ROOT CAUSE: fl powf_medium decomposes into exp2f(y*log2f(x)) = TWO f32 libm transcendentals (~25ns), while glibc powf is a single FUSED routine (~9ns). Decomposition is fundamentally ~2.5x slower regardless of precision. ATTEMPTS REJECTED 2026-06-05: (1) f64-kernel decompose super::exp2(y*super::log2(x)) — REGRESSED to 37ns (f64 transcendentals cost MORE per-call than f32 siblings); (2) f32 logf*LOG2_E reroute (logf cheaper than log2f) — FAILED 4-ULP parity, powf(2.1247,-2.8547) off by >4 ULP (f32 lacks precision headroom for the extra multiply). CONCLUSION: only a FUSED minimax powf closes this — a single-pass polynomial approx of x^y over a reduced domain (range-reduce base mantissa + exponent split, evaluate combined log2/exp2 minimax with f64 intermediate, round once). Alien-artifact class: needs offline minimax coefficient generation (Remez/Sollya-style) with a 4-ULP-vs-glibc proof obligation. Same wall as pow_irrational bd-2g7oyh.116 (1.89x) and log2 bd-e4jb7k residual. Parent perf epic bd-2g7oyh.

title: getdomainname null pointer host-errno parity
description: getdomainname has an ABI null-pointer guard but no differential coverage. Add a no-mock host comparison proving NULL+nonzero length returns -1 and EFAULT like glibc.
close_reason:
Gate added in 34c7203e6. The ABI null guard already existed; the bead asked only for differential coverage. THE BEAD'S PREMISE IS REFUTED and that is the main finding.

REFUTED PREMISE (measured, not recalled): the bead asked for a gate proving getdomainname(NULL, len>0) returns -1 and EFAULT 'like glibc'. Live glibc 2.42 on this host does NOT do that -- it has no null guard and SEGFAULTS. Measured two independent ways:
  (a) ctypes probe on thinkstation1, each case in its own subprocess: getdomainname(NULL, 64) -> exit -11 (SIGSEGV); getdomainname(NULL, 0) -> rc=0 errno=0 (len 0 means nothing is copied, so the null is never dereferenced).
  (b) reproduced independently on the remote worker by the committed gate itself, which forks a child and requires SIGSEGV.
So fl's -1/EFAULT is a deliberate TSM hardening divergence, NOT parity, and the gate says so rather than asserting a conformance claim that does not exist.

ALSO MEASURED, and more useful than the NULL case: glibc's Linux getdomainname truncates like strncpy and writes a terminator ONLY if it fits. With domainname='(none)' (len 6): len=1 -> '(' with no NUL; len=3 -> '(no' with no NUL; len=6 -> '(none)' with NO NUL; len=7 -> '(none)\0'. There is no EINVAL for a short buffer (the generic non-Linux glibc implementation does return EINVAL there, which is what makes this worth pinning). fl already matches this exactly.

EVIDENCE (remote via RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2, -j2, CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/tmp/rch_target_frankenlibc_greenglen):
  cargo test -j2 -p frankenlibc-abi --test conformance_diff_getdomainname -> 3 passed; 0 failed.

GATE (crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/conformance_diff_getdomainname.rs), glibc reached by dlsym and asserted distinct from fl's entry point:
  - getdomainname_matches_glibc_across_buffer_lengths: compares rc, errno, and the WHOLE 512-byte poisoned (0xAA) buffer, so an over-write past len is caught as well as a missing terminator, over lengths straddling strlen(domain) (0,1,2,dl-1,dl,dl+1,dl+8,512). Lengths are derived from the host's actual domainname at runtime, not hardcoded.
  - getdomainname_exact_fit_is_not_nul_terminated_like_glibc: pins the len==strlen(domain) case separately, because a 'helpful' implementation that always terminates would still pass a looser sweep on other sizes.
  - getdomainname_null_is_a_deliberate_hardening_divergence: asserts fl returns -1/EFAULT, and MEASURES glibc's side in a forked child (RLIMIT_CORE 0 so no core file is dropped in the tree) requiring death by SIGSEGV. If glibc ever grows a null guard this arm fails and tells the next reader to convert it into a parity assertion.

NEGATIVE CASE (proved, not asserted): with fl changed to always NUL-terminate -- the realistic 'helpful' bug -- BOTH parity arms failed (at len=1, fl wrote 0x00 where glibc wrote '(' = 0x28) while the hardening arm correctly stayed GREEN, since it does not exercise the copy path. Probe then removed; unistd_abi.rs is byte-identical to HEAD (it does not appear in git status).

GATES: rustfmt --edition 2024: clean. clippy -p frankenlibc-abi --all-targets -D warnings: zero findings in the new file.

SCOPE: test-only commit; no src change, because the implementation was already correct on every defined input and I verified that by breaking it and watching the gate fail. source_commit=1297152c8 -> 34c7203e6. Unrelated working-tree changes by other agents were not reverted or disturbed.

title: Left-Right Sync for complex metadata reads (section 14.3)
description:
Implement Left-Right synchronization for wait-free reads of complex metadata structures in FrankenLibC. Left-Right maintains two copies of the data structure (left and right). Readers always access one copy wait-free (no locks, no atomics on the read path). Writers update the inactive copy, then toggle the active pointer, then wait for readers to drain from the old copy before updating it too. Compared to RCU (bd-3aof), Left-Right provides: (a) Wait-free reads (not just lock-free). (b) Works for non-RCU-friendly data structures (those requiring consistent snapshots of multiple fields). Application to FrankenLibC: (1) Allocator configuration — the allocator's configuration (size-class table, arena count, thread-to-arena mapping) is a complex multi-field structure that must be read consistently. Left-Right provides atomic snapshot reads without locks. (2) TSM policy table — the TSM's decision policy (state machine transitions, threshold parameters) may be updated at runtime (e.g., when switching from strict to hardened mode). Left-Right ensures readers always see a consistent policy snapshot. (3) Symbol dispatch table — the IFUNC-like dispatch table mapping symbols to implementations. Updated when CPU features change (e.g., AVX-512 becomes available after cpuid check). Implementation: LeftRight<T> wrapper with read() -> &T (wait-free) and write(|t: &mut T| ...) (serialized, may block briefly).

## Acceptance Criteria
See `acceptance_criteria` field.
design:
**Alien CS Reference:** Section 14.3 of graveyard. Left-Right from Ramalhete & Correia (2015). Wait-free reads with consistent snapshots for multi-field structures.

**Rust Implementation Guidance:**
- LeftRight<T: Clone>: maintains two copies (left: Box<T>, right: Box<T>) with version_index: AtomicBool.
- read() -> ReadGuard<T>: returns reference to active copy. No atomic RMW on read path (single atomic load of version_index).
- ReadGuard registers in per-reader arrival/departure counters (2 counters, one per version).
- write(|t: &mut T| ...) -> (): acquires writer mutex, updates inactive copy, toggles version_index, waits for readers on old version to drain, updates other copy.
- Reader drain: spin on reader counter for old version until zero. Bounded wait if readers are well-behaved.
- T: Clone required to synchronize the two copies after toggle.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria
1. LeftRight<T> compiles and passes miri for basic read/write cycle.
2. Read path is wait-free: no CAS, no RMW (verified by cargo asm inspection).
3. Consistent snapshot: multi-field read always sees consistent state (test with 2-field struct updated atomically).
4. 16-reader + 1-writer stress test: 1M operations, TSan clean.
5. Read latency <3ns at p99 (compare with RCU at <2ns and RwLock at ~15ns).
6. Writer latency <1us including reader drain wait at p99 under 16-reader load.
7. No starvation: writer completes within bounded time even with continuous readers.

### Mandatory Verification Gate
- Comprehensive unit tests are required for all touched logic: positive, negative, adversarial, and regression.
- Deterministic e2e scripts are required for all externally visible behavior in strict and hardened mode where relevant.
- Structured logs are mandatory for unit/e2e runs with fields: `trace_id`, `mode`, `api_family`, `symbol`, `decision_path`, `healing_action`, `errno`, `latency_ns`, `artifact_refs`.
- Closure evidence must include exact test commands, expected outputs/thresholds, and representative failure signatures.
- CI must persist logs, diffs, and reports with deterministic naming and retention for replay/triage.
- Tooling contract: deterministic orchestration/traceability uses `/dp/asupersync`, and deterministic diff/snapshot/TUI evidence uses `/dp/frankentui`.
notes:
**Logging Requirements:**
- tracing::trace!(target: left_right, operation=read, version, reader_count) per read (disabled in release).
- tracing::debug!(target: left_right, operation=write, version_toggled, drain_wait_ns) per write.
- tracing::warn!(target: left_right, slow_drain, drain_wait_ns, remaining_readers) if drain exceeds 100us.

### Mandatory Test/E2E Logging Checklist
- Test command set is documented in bead notes before closure (unit + e2e + perf where applicable).
- Expected output and pass/fail thresholds are documented per command.
- Failure triage snippets are documented (top failure classes + where to inspect artifacts).
- Evidence index entry links logs, parity diffs, and benchmark/proof artifacts.
- Overload behavior logging is required when applicable: pressure signal, degradation mode, selected policy, guard decision, rollback trigger.

Verified with rch exec cargo test -p frankenlibc-membrane left_right -- --nocapture, rch exec cargo check --workspace --all-targets, and rch exec cargo clippy -p frankenlibc-membrane --all-targets -- -D warnings. title: feat(dlfcn): standalone stubs for dlopen/dlsym/dlclose
description:
For standalone mode (no host glibc), the dlfcn functions need minimal implementations:
1. dlopen: Return NULL with ENOSYS for actual .so loading (standalone doesn't support dynamic loading)

4. dladdr: Lookup address in main program ELF
5. dl_iterate_phdr: Iterate only over main program PHDRs
6. dlvsym: Same as dlsym (version ignored in standalone)

This provides functional stubs that allow programs to gracefully handle missing dynamic loading.
Unblocks 6 of the 204 WrapsHostLibc symbols.

title: PORT: inet_net_pton + inet_net_ntop (BIND/libresolv CIDR codec)
description: BIND/libresolv inet_net_pton(af, src, dst, size) parses CIDR-like network-address strings ("192.168.0/24", "10/8") into the dst byte buffer, returning the prefix length in bits, or -1 with errno on error. Thin abi shims in glibc_internal_abi.rs since libresolv exports them.

title: Convert D1 queue head to tier-A incumbent ratios (nl_langinfo, fpclassify, fpclassifyf, tdelete, memrchr)
description:
Pre-registered before any timing. Converts the head of the D1 queue published by the 2026-07-31 incumbent-coverage audit, whose headline was that ZERO of 246 held claims carry a machine-checkable same-invocation incumbent ratio.

WHY THESE SYMBOLS. The audit ranked unsupported claims by exposure in public, user-facing docs, because an unsupported claim a user might act on is worse than one buried in a ledger. These are the queue head:
  L381  strict nl_langinfo reads the immutable C-locale table directly  -- README.md, CHANGELOG.md
  L815  fpclassify classifies f64 from exponent and fraction bits      -- README.md, RELEASE_READINESS_SCORECARD.md
  L776  fpclassifyf classifies f32 from exponent and fraction bits     -- CHANGELOG.md
  L1144 tdelete removes the redundant lookup walk                      -- CHANGELOG.md
  L16509 memrchr 512B fold tier                                        -- ledger only, included because it is a string scanner and shares the harness cheaply
Every one currently rests on a self-speedup or on no comparison at all. None has ever been measured against glibc.

WHAT IS AND IS NOT BEING CLAIMED. This run attaches an incumbent ratio; it does not defend the original claims. The original rows asserted our code got faster than our previous code, and that may well be true and is not under test. The question here is the only one the campaign counts: is the deployed FrankenLibC symbol faster than the live glibc symbol, in the same process, on the same input.

EXPECTATION, registered so the result cannot be reinterpreted afterwards. The base rate is poor: strfmon and wordexp were predicted wins and measured 2-4x LOSSES, and wctype was predicted a win and lost at the head of glibc's table. Prior expectation for this batch is therefore MIXED, and specifically:
  E1 fpclassify/fpclassifyf are pure bit inspection on both sides with no locale, no allocation and no string. glibc's is a handful of instructions. PREDICT parity or a LOSS, not a win. A win here would need explaining, not celebrating.
  E2 nl_langinfo is a table index on both sides after glibc's hoisting. PREDICT parity or small LOSS by the same reasoning that refuted strfmon.
  E3 tdelete and memrchr are the only two where a real algorithmic difference exists, so they are the only two where a win is plausible.
Any row that lands opposite its registered expectation is reported as such rather than quietly absorbed.

CONTRACT, unchanged and non-negotiable. Live glibc linked directly and called in the same invocation as the strict FrankenLibC object loaded by explicit dlopen RTLD_NOW|RTLD_LOCAL; benchmark ELF and both serving objects self-report SHA-256 from inside the process; every symbol pair asserted to distinct addresses and distinct serving objects; conformance precedes timing for every claimed symbol; per-arm A/A controls on every row; corrected null gate with the median clause; ACTUAL OBSERVED thread count from /proc/self/task; CV telemetry only; artifacts built from a pinned commit with no working tree, and if the rch clean-overlay path is used its retrieved artifact set is checked for staleness first, because that path silently returned a six-week-old FrankenLibC object in the strfloor run.

BUFFER PROVENANCE REQUIREMENT, inherited from strfloor and now mandatory for any string-taking symbol: inputs must be allocated through FrankenLibC's own malloc for at least one arm, because the strfloor run showed the allocation-registry probe costs +2.415 ns only when it HITS, and a harness that allocates its inputs with the incumbent's allocator cannot see that cost at all. memrchr rows must therefore carry both provenances.

title: [RED] sysconf 20-key + pathconf/_PC_2_SYMLINKS fixes deleted by e634aff2a — 5 conformance_diff rows red (sysconf, sysconf_raw, sysconf_values, pathconf x2)
description:
Same deletion class as bd-tnqpnn and bd-3kslha. Found by the same mechanical sweep; one deleted fix accounts for THREE of the bd-aykfv1 red rows, which is why the row list looked bigger than the defect list.

SYSCONF. b5ae82d1a 'fix(sysconf): return glibc values for 20 POSIX feature/limit keys (were -1+EINVAL)'
is gone at HEAD. Two independent confirmations:
    grep -n '_SC_JOB_CONTROL|_SC_BC_BASE_MAX' crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs -> no matches
    line 2555 reads 'libc::_SC_THREADS => 1,' which is the PRE-FIX value; the fix changed it to
    200809 (_SC_THREADS reports the _POSIX_THREADS version, not a boolean)
Deleting commit:
    git log --oneline -S 'libc::_SC_JOB_CONTROL => 1,' -- crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs
      e634aff2a  stdlib/wordexp: full ${...} parameter expansion
      b5ae82d1a  fix(sysconf): ...
The 20 keys fell back to the EINVAL default, i.e. sysconf returns -1 for keys glibc answers with a
definite constant (_SC_JOB_CONTROL, _SC_SAVED_IDS, the _SC_BC_* quartet, _SC_COLL_WEIGHTS_MAX,
_SC_EXPR_NEST_MAX, _SC_2_C_BIND/_C_DEV/_LOCALEDEF/_SW_DEV, ...). Accounts for the sysconf (0/1),
sysconf_raw (0/1) and sysconf_values (1/2) rows together.

PATHCONF. e2a577d08 'fix(pathconf): return glibc values for _PC_2_SYMLINKS + statvfs-derived record
limits' is gone by the same commit:
    grep -n '_PC_2_SYMLINKS' crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs -> no matches
    git log --oneline -S 'libc::_PC_2_SYMLINKS => Some(1),' -> e634aff2a, e2a577d08
d2a979696 'fix(fpathconf): statvfs-derived record limits via fstatfs (parity with pathconf)' probes
as 3-of-4 missing by the same method — CONFIRM BY READING fpathconf at HEAD before restoring, the
probe has false positives from the 56745ef4a tree-wide reformat.

METHOD NOTE for whoever takes this: restore from the original commit rather than retyping, and
re-derive each constant from a LIVE host oracle before trusting the restored literal —
ctypes sysconf(name)/pathconf(path,name) against libc.so.6 gives the values this host actually
reports, and the gate compares against that host, not against the commit.

NEGATIVE CASE: a naive restore that adds the 20 keys but leaves _SC_THREADS => 1 will still pass any
test that only checks 'not -1'. The gate must assert the VALUE 200809 for _SC_THREADS specifically.

DONE = conformance_diff_sysconf, conformance_diff_sysconf_raw, conformance_diff_sysconf_values and
conformance_diff_pathconf all green with non-zero passed counts.

title: [flaky] pthread_abi_test timing tests fail under parallel test-binary load
description:
Found while regression-checking the semaphore restoration (d4b77a016). NOT caused by that change --
proven with a like-for-like control, which is the point of this bead.

SYMPTOM. Running pthread_abi_test alongside other test binaries produces failures in timeout-shaped
tests, and the SET OF FAILURES VARIES between runs:
  with 3 sibling binaries : kill_sig_zero_to_live_thread,
                            mutex_timedlock_future_deadline_times_out_before_unlock,
                            timedjoin_np_succeeds_before_deadline   -> 203 passed; 3 failed
  alone, run 1            : getaffinity_np_live_thread              -> 205 passed; 1 failed
  alone, run 2            : (none)                                  -> 206 passed; 0 failed

THE CONTROL THAT SETTLED IT. My first baseline ran pthread_abi_test ALONE and came back 206 passed,
which made the change look guilty. That comparison was invalid: the overlay run had three sibling
binaries competing for CPU and the baseline had none. Re-running the CLEAN-HEAD baseline under the
IDENTICAL four-binary invocation reproduced exactly the same three failures, 203 passed; 3 failed.
Same tests, same count, no overlay. Load, not code.

Worth generalising: when a suite contains timing assertions, a baseline must reproduce the overlay
run's CONCURRENCY, not just its commit. Comparing a loaded run against an unloaded one will
manufacture a regression that is not there, or hide one that is.

WHY IT MATTERS: these are deadline tests (mutex_timedlock future deadline, timedjoin before
deadline, and a signal delivery race). On a busy worker the thread under test does not get scheduled
inside the window, so the deadline expires first. They are correctness tests whose oracle is wall
clock, which makes them unreliable on shared hardware -- the same fleet-shaped problem as bd-30sv83
(root) and bd-dy9dqc (timezone), here as CPU contention.

DONE = pthread_abi_test green across at least 3 consecutive runs under parallel load with other test
binaries. Likely approaches: widen the deadlines substantially (they appear tuned for an idle
machine), or gate the timing-sensitive arms behind a serialisation lock so they do not run
concurrently with the rest of the suite. Do NOT simply delete the assertions -- the wake/timeout
paths they cover are real contracts.

--- UPDATE 2026-08-09 (PlumStork, 619f37306) ---
PARTIAL FIX LANDED, BEAD STAYS OPEN. The bead's diagnosis ('deadline tests whose oracle is wall clock') was right for exactly ONE arm and wrong for the rest.

Only mutex_timedlock_future_deadline_times_out_before_unlock had a wall-clock upper bound (elapsed < 150ms against a 200ms hold). It now asserts the CAUSAL fact it was approximating: the holder sets an 'unlocked' flag after releasing, and the arm asserts ETIMEDOUT arrived while the mutex was still held, plus a load-safe lower bound that it waited out its own 50ms deadline. Hold widened to 2s. Nothing deleted or relaxed.

The other arms were not deadline tests at all. Six '..._live_thread' arms used sleep(20ms) after pthread_create as a stand-in for a handshake; the failures read 'left: 3, right: 0', i.e. ESRCH. cancellable_thread now signals readiness through arg and wait_until_running blocks on it (1ms poll, 30s runtime budget, assertion unchanged). sigqueue's real handshake was capped at 100x1ms and got the same treatment.

Note the bead's own list of failing tests was never stable, and that is explained: on this host the observed set was sigqueue/setname/getaffinity/getcpuclockid/thread_create_join/condvar_wait_errorcheck, varying per run. It was never the three tests the bead names.

WHAT IS LEFT, measured over 12 consecutive loaded runs post-fix (64-core worker, 4 concurrent sibling binaries):
  2  getcpuclockid_returns_valid_clock_for_live_thread   -> split to bd-4atx9e
  2  getaffinity_np_live_thread                          -> split to bd-4atx9e
  1  sigqueue_live_thread_preserves_queued_value         -> split to bd-4atx9e
  1  thread_create_join                                  -> still this bead
  1  condvar_wait_errorcheck_without_lock_returns_eperm  -> still this bead
kill_sig_zero_to_live_thread and setname_getname_np_live_thread failed ZERO times in those 12 runs, having failed regularly before.

bd-4atx9e is the important half: with a real handshake in place, an ESRCH from getaffinity_np/getcpuclockid/sigqueue for a thread that has already executed user code is an fl defect, not scheduling. This bead should NOT be closed by widening timeouts on those arms.

DONE for this bead is unchanged (3 consecutive green runs under parallel load) and now additionally requires bd-4atx9e.

title: REVIEW: [HIGH] futex_wait_timed panics (debug) / wraps to effectively-infinite timeout (release) on i64 subtraction overflow when deadline.tv_sec < 0
description:
Location: crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/pthread_abi.rs:1101-1104 (futex_wait_timed).

Current code:
    let deadline = unsafe { &*abstime };
    let mut rel = libc::timespec {
        tv_sec: deadline.tv_sec - now.tv_sec,
        tv_nsec: deadline.tv_nsec - now.tv_nsec,
    };

Defect:
- `absolute_timespec_valid` at line 1075 only checks `tv_nsec` in [0, 1e9); it does NOT check tv_sec >= 0 nor that deadline is after now.
- `deadline.tv_sec - now.tv_sec` is an unchecked i64 subtraction.
- In debug builds: `i64::MIN - 1_700_000_000` PANICS with 'attempt to subtract with overflow', aborting the process.
- In release builds: the subtraction silently wraps to a huge positive value (~9.2e18), defeating the subsequent `rel.tv_sec < 0` check and handing the kernel a timespec that corresponds to ~3e11 years — the call then blocks effectively forever instead of returning ETIMEDOUT.

Reachability: Every pthread_cond_timedwait / pthread_cond_clockwait / sem_timedwait / pthread_mutex_timedlock that eventually routes through futex_wait_timed. An adversarial or buggy caller passing tv_sec=i64::MIN (or any extreme negative) aborts the process in debug mode or loses the timeout contract in release.

Severity: HIGH. Exported libc surface, crashes from user input on common code paths.

Fix plan:
- Use i64::checked_sub for the tv_sec subtraction. Treat overflow or a deadline in the past (rel.tv_sec < 0 after carry) uniformly as ETIMEDOUT.
- Also tighten absolute_timespec_valid to reject tv_sec < 0 so the invariant is visible at the API boundary.
- Add a regression test: pthread_cond_timedwait with tv_sec=-1 must return ETIMEDOUT (not hang, not crash).
close_reason: Fixed: crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/pthread_abi.rs absolute_timespec_valid now rejects tv_sec < 0 in addition to out-of-range tv_nsec, and futex_wait_timed uses i64::checked_sub on the deadline-minus-now arithmetic so an extreme tv_sec (including i64::MIN) produces ETIMEDOUT instead of panicking (debug) or wrapping to a ~9.2e18-second effectively-infinite timeout (release). Added two regression tests in crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/pthread_abi_test.rs: cond_timedwait_rejects_negative_tv_sec (tv_sec = -1 and i64::MIN) and cond_timedwait_rejects_out_of_range_tv_nsec (tv_nsec in {-1, 1_000_000_000, i64::MAX}). Run: rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/rch_target_libc_review cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test pthread_abi_test -> 183/0 passed in 0.27s.
