title: [perf][malloc] Swing-2: inline size header + framing reduction (deployed malloc/free 8.05x -> target ~5x)
description:
MEASURED CONTEXT (BlackThrush 2026-07-02, all in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md + docs/perf_next_architectural_swings.md):
Deployed malloc/free is ~8.05x glibc (fl ~37ns vs glibc ~4.6ns) after the lean-stats win (20901156e took it from 9.5x). The remaining ~32ns overhead decomposes (per-crate microbench examples/malloc_sizetrack_ab.rs + fallback_*_for_bench / reentry_guard_enter_exit_for_bench / record_alloc_free_stats_for_bench hooks):
  - native malloc+free ~5ns (= glibc floor, irreducible)
  - FALLBACK hash table insert+lookup+remove ~11.6ns  <-- THIS SWING
  - reentry guard enter+exit ~4ns x2 ~8ns (safety-critical: post-CAS is_runtime_ready/in_policy_reentry_context/pthread-reentry checks catch cross-subsystem reentry; NOT safely removable)
  - stats recorder ~9ns (DONE, lean path)

SUB-STEP A (inline size header, replaces the FALLBACK table ~11.6ns -> ~0.7ns, 16x, measured):
  fl malloc delegates to native_libc_malloc; store [magic:u64, size:usize] in a 16-byte header before the returned ptr (16B preserves MALLOC_ALIGNMENT). free reads magic at ptr-16 -> native_free(ptr-16); foreign (host-malloc'd) ptrs have no magic -> native_free(ptr).
  CRITICAL SAFETY (why the naive header + why NOT a page-radix): known_remaining() has 395 call sites and is invoked with ARBITRARY pointers (stack/static/interior), so reading ptr[-16] blindly is UB. Guard: (1) publish_fallback_range [min,max] heap-range check so the header is read ONLY when min_heap+16<=ptr<=max_heap (mapped => no fault); (2) strong 8-byte magic so an interior read (in-heap, mapped) is rejected. Residual ~2^-64 interior-false-accept yields a garbage bound = no worse than glibc (which bounds nothing, trusts NUL) => does not regress the strict-mode safety contract. A page-radix (ptr>>PAGE_SHIFT) DOES NOT WORK here: fallback_key is the exact byte address and many different-sized allocs share one 4KiB page (host-delegated), so a page slot cannot hold per-alloc sizes.

SUB-STEP B (framing): after A, remaining is the ~8ns reentry guard (safety, harder) + native floor. Evaluate a single-threaded (!MULTI_THREADED) non-atomic stats path (attempted, was below bench noise ~2ns -> only worth it bundled with A's re-measure).

CONSTRAINTS: touches the membrane safety contract -> membrane-owner review. Conformance-heavy: malloc/calloc/realloc/aligned_alloc/valloc/reallocarray/free/posix_memalign + overflow + foreign-ptr adoption + double-free. Shadow-run rollback: keep FALLBACK table behind a cfg flag; populate BOTH + assert agreement across the full conformance suite before switching reads to the header.
ENTRY BENCH (already in tree): examples/malloc_sizetrack_ab.rs proves header 0.71ns vs table 11.55ns.
SUCCESS: deployed MALLOC_FREE fl/glibc 8.05x -> ~5-6x (A removes ~10ns); all allocator gates green (malloc_abi_test 55 incl HTM+mallinfo, aligned_alloc/reallocarray/valloc/realloc_shrink/malloc_edges).
notes:
2026-07-04 BlackThrush surface: fresh per-crate rch run on vmi1149989 (AGENT_NAME=BlackThrush CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/projects/.rch-targets/frankenlibc-dcrhgl-baseline rch exec -- cargo run --release -p frankenlibc-bench --example malloc_sizetrack_ab --features abi-bench) measured SIZETRACK_AB table=19.59ns header=0.63ns header/table=0.032 table_saves=18.96ns/op; GUARD_AB=5.63ns/call; STATS_AB=16.78ns/alloc+free-pair. No code shipped: min/max allocation envelope plus magic does not prove addr-16 is mapped for arbitrary known_remaining pointers, so the naive inline-header production switch can fault before the magic check. Retry only with a no-fault exact-membership/page-residency/shadow-agreement guard; current fallback table remains source of truth.

2026-07-10 cod_fl measured safe-guard sublever: local deployed malloc_st_probe perf stat stayed fl 38.30-40.43ns vs glibc 4.57-4.82ns (8.30-8.48x), flamegraph ranked free 13.20% and enter_allocator_reentry_guard 11.25% with fallback table/stats visible. Deployed on the SAME worker (examples/malloc_st_probe, vmi1149989): fl=32.55ns glibc=3.34ns at sz=64.

THE COMPONENTS DO NOT FIT INSIDE THE DEPLOYED COST. Summing them: table 17.99 + reentry guard ~11.4 (5.69/call over malloc and free) + stats 15.51 + native floor ~3.3 = ~48 ns/pair, against a MEASURED deployed fl of 32.55 ns/pair on that same worker. The parts exceed the whole by ~50%, so at least one component is substantially over-attributed when timed in its own loop -- isolation gives each one its own cache and branch behaviour and no overlap with the rest.

CONSEQUENCE, and this is the point: 'table is 17.25ns, remove it and fl drops 17.25ns' is NOT a supported inference. If it were true the table would be 55% of fl's entire deployed cost and sub-step A alone would land ~4.6x, comfortably past this bead's 5-6x line. That projection is exactly as unreliable as the arithmetic that produced it. Neither this bead's original ~33ns budget nor my earlier ~63ns reading survives contact with a same-worker decomposition.

ALSO REFUTED, quietly, by SIZETRACK_GUARDED_HEADER_AB: the 'currently provable safe transition' -- prove exact-start membership via the table, THEN read the header -- costs 18.14ns against the table's 17.99ns, i.e. it saves NOTHING (guarded_tax +0.15ns). It cannot be an intermediate step; it is strictly worse than the status quo. The header only pays if the table lookup is REMOVED from the path, which is precisely the part that needs the safety argument.

MORE PROMISING THAN THE HEADER, on these numbers: SEGMENT_BITMAP at 0.99ns and SEGMENT_SIZECLASS at 1.92ns are within noise of the header's 0.74ns while requiring NO user-memory dereference at all -- ownership derived from the pointer address alone. That sidesteps the whole known_remaining()/arbitrary-pointer fault-surface argument that forced the magic-plus-range guard in sub-step A. If a segment scheme is viable for host-delegated allocations, it is the better primitive.

METHOD CAVEAT on these rows: malloc_sizetrack_ab does not self-report its ELF SHA-256, unlike malloc_st_probe. The rows are same-invocation A/B against each other, which is what makes the table-vs-header comparison legitimate, but they carry less provenance than the deployed rows above.

NEXT STEP I RECOMMEND, replacing 'implement sub-step A': the bead's own shadow-run plan is the only thing that answers this -- populate BOTH table and header behind a cfg flag, assert agreement across the conformance suite, then measure DEPLOYED malloc/free with reads switched. That is a deployed-ratio experiment, not a microbench projection, and after today it is the only evidence that would justify the safety argument.

title: fortify __wctomb_chk ignores MB_LEN_MAX object-size guard
description: glibc fortify routes wctomb through __wctomb_chk when the destination object is smaller than MB_LEN_MAX (16), but FrankenLibC's __wctomb_chk ignores buflen and delegates directly. Add the MB_LEN_MAX guard and abort regression coverage.
close_reason:
DONE at 05bd899b9 — but NOT the way the bead prescribed, because the prescription was wrong.

EVIDENCE:
  cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test fortify_abi_test wctomb
  test result: ok. 4 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 152 filtered out
  cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test fortify_abi_test
  test result: ok. 156 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out

THE BEAD'S PRESCRIPTION WAS THE BUG. It says 'Add the MB_LEN_MAX guard'. Someone did, and that IS the defect: glibc's __wctomb_chk compares buflen against MB_CUR_MAX. MB_LEN_MAX (16) is what the FORTIFY header macro compares the object SIZE against when deciding whether to route the call to __wctomb_chk at all — a different constant at a different layer. Note the fix and a gate were both already at HEAD, so on a comment sweep this would have looked done twice over.

ORACLE — the host's own __wctomb_chk, called directly, one process per row:
  C locale     MB_CUR_MAX=1  buflen 1, 5, 6, 15, 16 -> none abort
  C.UTF-8      MB_CUR_MAX=6  buflen 1, 5 abort; 6, 15, 16 return
  en_US.UTF-8  MB_CUR_MAX=6  same as C.UTF-8
fl used 'buflen < 16' and therefore aborted for EVERY buflen in 1..=15 in every locale. That is the damaging direction for a fortify check: it kills correct programs. The pre-existing arm wctomb_chk_short_buffer_aborts_child_process (buflen=1) passes either way, so it never noticed.

FIX: consult __ctype_get_mb_cur_max() instead of the literal 16. FORTIFY_MB_LEN_MAX is removed rather than left dangling, with a comment in its place recording why the two constants are not interchangeable — the confusion is the whole bug.

GATE: differential against the HOST's __wctomb_chk over buflen in {1,5,6,7,15,16}, fork-isolated per case via a new child_aborted() helper that REPORTS whether the child took SIGABRT instead of asserting it, so an abort is comparable data rather than a dead harness. Plus a reference arm asserting the host's own boundary (5 aborts, 6 and 15 do not), so fl and glibc cannot pass by agreeing on a wrong answer. Mutation-tested: restoring the 16 bound fails with 'buflen=6: fl aborted=true, host aborted=false'.

SCOPE SPLIT, DECLARED. The arm runs under C.UTF-8, where fl and the host now agree exactly. The C-locale row still diverges because fl's __ctype_get_mb_cur_max is hardcoded to 6 and ignores setlocale — filed as bd-w7nxne with the full table and a warning that some of the other hardcoded 6s in the multibyte paths are encoder BUFFER sizes where 6 is correct and must not be changed. Asserting the C-locale row here would fail for that reason rather than this one.

NO REGRESSION: fortify_abi_test 156 passed; cargo check -p frankenlibc-abi --all-targets --keep-going shows the same 4 pre-existing failing targets as the established baseline.

title: PORT: fchmodat2 + eventfd2 + 4 rt_sig* (rt_sigprocmask/queueinfo/suspend/tgsigqueueinfo)
description: Add 6 more Linux libc syscall wrappers. (1) fchmodat2(dirfd, pathname, mode, flags) -> int (Linux 6.6+, SYS_fchmodat2=452) — like fchmodat but accepts AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW + AT_EMPTY_PATH flags. (2) eventfd2(initval, flags) -> int (SYS_eventfd2=290) — kernel-name variant of eventfd that accepts flags directly; some sandboxes/seccomp policies trace this name explicitly. (3) rt_sigprocmask(how, *set, *oldset, sigsetsize) -> int (SYS_rt_sigprocmask=14). (4) rt_sigqueueinfo(tgid, sig, *uinfo) -> int (SYS_rt_sigqueueinfo=129) — send a siginfo_t to a thread group. (5) rt_sigsuspend(*mask, sigsetsize) -> int (SYS_rt_sigsuspend=130). (6) rt_tgsigqueueinfo(tgid, tid, sig, *uinfo) -> int (SYS_rt_tgsigqueueinfo=297) — send a siginfo_t to a specific thread. Skip rt_sigaction (kernel struct layout differs from libc) and rt_sigreturn (kernel signal-trampoline; never callable from user code). Forward via libc::syscall + raw_syscall_with_errno bridge; NULL-pointer guards return EFAULT where applicable.

Every deployed ABI call pays a fixed ~25-30ns membrane entrypoint tax (strlen 64B 31ns vs glibc 2.5ns; strchr 64B 5.8x; same root as malloc 256B 54x). Decomposition (runtime_policy.rs): (1) entrypoint_scope(symbol) = next_trace_seq atomic fetch_add + ffi_pcc_certificate_index_for_symbol which is a match-on-symbol-str doing several str comparisons per call whose result is CONSTANT per static str so recomputed wastefully + with_trace_context TLS write; (2) known_remaining(s) lookup; (3) alloc adds decide/observe + signal_critical_section + allocator_stage_context. NO single dominant piece. RULED OUT this session as non-levers (measured neutral): the string SIMD-dispatch certify (bd-strlen-dead-dispatch-certify, cheap) and the scan width for strlen (folded neutral). The scan WIDTH for strchr WAS a lever (bd-4rxozm, 14x to 1.2x). So the residual deployed gap is the entrypoint tax = a FOUNDATIONAL refactor: precompute pcc_index at call sites (pass u8 const not symbol str), make entrypoint_scope a no-op when tracing has no subscriber, batch/defer known_remaining. High breadth (every ABI call) but soundness/observability-sensitive and membrane-core. Not attempted unilaterally.

title: Track A: Implement _IO_iter_* native stream iteration over NativeStreamRegistry
description:
## Goal
Replace 4 stub _IO_iter_* functions in io_internal_abi.rs (lines 1430-1457) with real implementations that iterate over the NativeStreamRegistry.

## Current State
All 4 functions return null, making the stream list appear empty:
- _IO_iter_begin() -> null (should return first occupied slot index)
- _IO_iter_end() -> null (should return sentinel past last slot)
- _IO_iter_file(iter) -> null (should return FILE* for the slot)
- _IO_iter_next(iter) -> null (should advance to next occupied slot)

## Why This Matters
glibc atexit/fflush-all path may walk _IO_list via these iterators. If the list is empty, exit-time flushing of native streams is silently skipped by any code using glibc's _IO_iter API. Our native fflush(NULL) works via NativeStreamRegistry.flush_all(), but external code (atexit handlers in host glibc) that walks _IO_list via iterators would miss our streams.

## Design
Use slot-index-as-opaque-pointer encoding:
- _IO_iter_begin: Lock registry, find first OCCUPIED slot (index 0..255), return (index+1) cast to *mut c_void. Return null if no occupied slots. We use index+1 so that 0 (stdin at slot 0) is distinguishable from null.
- _IO_iter_end: Return (STREAM_REGISTRY_CAPACITY+1) cast to *mut c_void as sentinel. This is 257, always > any valid encoded slot.
- _IO_iter_file: Decode (iter as usize - 1) to get slot index, call registry.get(index), return &NativeFile as *mut c_void. Return null if index is invalid or slot is empty.
- _IO_iter_next: Decode current slot index from iter, scan forward for next OCCUPIED slot, return encoded index or end sentinel.

### Thread Safety
The registry is behind a Mutex. Each iterator call acquires and releases the lock independently. This means the iteration is NOT atomic — streams could be added/removed between calls. This matches glibc behavior (glibc's _IO_iter functions are also not atomic without _IO_list_all_lock held externally).

### Implementation Helpers
Add to NativeStreamRegistry:
- first_occupied() -> Option<usize>: scan slots[0..] for first SLOT_OCCUPIED
- next_occupied(after: usize) -> Option<usize>: scan slots[after+1..] for next SLOT_OCCUPIED

## Files Changed
- crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/io_internal_abi.rs: Replace 4 function bodies, add 2 helpers to NativeStreamRegistry

## Unit Tests (in tests/io_internal_native_file_test.rs)
- test iter_begin_returns_first_stream: Register 0 extra streams -> begin iterates over stdin/stdout/stderr (3 entries)
- test iter_begin_end_empty_after_unregister: Unregister all stdio, begin == end (no streams)
- test iter_file_returns_valid_native_file: iter_file on valid iterator returns non-null with correct fd
- test iter_file_on_end_returns_null: iter_file on end sentinel returns null
- test iter_next_advances_to_next_occupied: skip empty slots correctly
- test iter_next_at_end_returns_end: advancing past last stream returns end sentinel
- test iter_full_traversal_count: register 5 streams, iterate begin->next->next...->end, count matches open_count()
- test iter_survives_concurrent_unregister: unregister a stream during iteration, no crash

## e2e Test Script: scripts/check_io_iter_native.sh
Build and run a focused Rust test binary that:
1. Opens 10 files via our native fopen (if available) or memfd_create
2. Walks _IO_iter_begin -> _IO_iter_next until _IO_iter_end
3. Counts entries and verifies >= 10
4. Emits structured JSONL trace per step

## Structured Logging
Each function emits: trace_id, api_family=io_internal, symbol=_IO_iter_begin|end|file|next, slot_index, result_ptr, latency_ns

## Acceptance Criteria
- All 4 _IO_iter_* functions return real iterators over NativeStreamRegistry
- 8+ unit tests pass covering positive, negative, edge, and concurrency cases
- e2e script passes
- cargo clippy clean
- LD_PRELOAD smoke suite (58 passes) not regressed
close_reason: Implemented _IO_iter_begin/end/file/next over NativeStreamRegistry using slot-index-as-opaque-pointer encoding. Added first_occupied()/next_occupied() helpers. 8 new integration tests: begin returns first stream, end is constant sentinel, file returns valid NativeFile, file on end/null returns null, next past end stays at end, full traversal visits all streams, traversal after unregister skips freed slots. All 40 io_internal tests pass. Clippy clean.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Implementation note: NativeStreamRegistry already has get() and open_count(). Use slot index as opaque pointer (usize cast to *mut c_void). Sentinel for _IO_iter_end = STREAM_REGISTRY_CAPACITY (256). Lock registry mutex during scan. Consider exposing first_occupied()/next_occupied() helpers on NativeStreamRegistry.

title: [HIGH] build_btrfs_image fixture no longer stamps root-tree tree_block_csum
description:
# Review finding

`build_btrfs_image()` is still constructing a synthetic btrfs root-tree leaf without stamping its `tree_block_csum` field.

## Evidence
- Builder: `crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:22119-22204`
- It writes a leaf header and item payload at `root_logical = 0x4000`, but never calls the existing test CRC helper used elsewhere (`stamp_btrfs_test_tree_block_crc32c` at `crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:22283-22287`).
- The workspace test rerun still fails all `build_btrfs_image()` consumers with `Format("invalid field: tree_block_csum (CRC32C checksum mismatch)")`:
  - `open_fs_from_btrfs_image`
  - `open_fs_btrfs_debug_format`
  - `open_fs_btrfs_superblock_accessor`
  - `open_fs_btrfs_walk_root_tree`

## Why this is high severity
This builder underpins the basic btrfs open/root-tree smoke tests. Right now those tests are red because the fixture no longer satisfies the parser’s checksum contract.

## Repro
`rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/rch_target_frankenfs_cod cargo test --workspace --all-targets`

## Expected fix direction
Stamp the synthetic root-tree block checksum after finalizing the leaf contents, and confirm the minimal open/root-tree tests go green independently of the larger readdir fixture family.
close_reason: Fixed: build_btrfs_image at crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:22185 now stamps CRC32C on both root-tree leaf and fs-tree leaf at lines 22298-22301 (csum = crc32c(&image[leaf+0x20..leaf+nodesize])). All cited consumers (open_fs_from_btrfs_image, open_fs_btrfs_debug_format, open_fs_btrfs_superblock_accessor, open_fs_btrfs_walk_root_tree) pass under rch workspace run.

  -> test strfry_preserves_pointer_length_nul_and_byte_multiset ... ok
     test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored; 0 measured; 629 filtered out

THE 1 IGNORED IS NOT THIS BEAD'S. The filtered run also lists
strfry_rejects_tracked_unterminated_string as 'ignored, requires real hardened mode bounds checking
(bd-q3snos)'. That is a DIFFERENT contract — hardened-mode bounds rejection — owned by bd-q3snos, not
by this bead's permutation-invariant contract. I am flagging it rather than letting a nonzero ignored
count sit unexplained in the evidence, because an ignored test adjacent to the one you are citing is
exactly how a closure quietly becomes false.

Run filtered deliberately: unistd_abi_test carries 5 pre-existing failures (argp x2, cuserid,
kexec_load, mount_setattr, baseline-confirmed earlier this session), so a whole-suite result would
have been unusable as evidence here.

DISCOVERY-METHOD CORRECTION, and it revises what I said one round ago. After the fortify and
syscall batches I reported that bead-ID citation 'found nothing again' and implied it is unreliable.
That was an over-generalisation from two clusters. In THIS cluster it works: conformance_diff_getmntent
and conformance_diff_feholdupdate both name their bead, and fgetspent/putspent/stdbit cite theirs in
the doc comment. Bead-ID citation should stay the FIRST check; it succeeds whenever the gate's author
recorded it, and fails only where they did not. My own function-name heuristic in this round was the
weaker tool — it picked unistd_abi_test.rs over the dedicated conformance_diff_getmntent.rs.

THESE BEADS ALSO NEEDED A SHARPER BAR THAN THE EARLIER BATCHES. Each says 'only fl-internal coverage',
which is a different claim from 'uncovered': a test existing is not enough, it has to compare against
a LIVE host oracle. I verified that rather than assuming, and every gate cited below carries an
unsafe extern "C" host-oracle block (in a debug build fl's no_mangle is off, so those symbols resolve
to glibc). A gate that only asserted fl's own expected values would not have satisfied these beads —
as conformance_diff_stdbit's own comment puts it, an fl-internal test 'cannot catch a spec
MISUNDERSTANDING'.

title: [HIGH] rpc_abi_test parallel race: free(): invalid size SIGABRT at --test-threads>=4 (locally reproducible bd-ye0f4 sibling)
description:
## Symptom

cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test rpc_abi_test under default cargo
parallelism aborts with free(): invalid size:

    running 35 tests
    RPC: Success
    RPC: Timed out
    RPC: Unknown error
    free(): invalid size
    error: test failed, to rerun pass -p frankenlibc-abi --test rpc_abi_test
    process didn't exit successfully: .../rpc_abi_test-... (signal: 6, SIGABRT)

The 3 RPC lines come from clnt_perrno_does_not_crash, which runs
early. Abort fires AFTER those lines, meaning another parallel-
running test is the culprit, not clnt_perrno itself.

## Bisection (LOCAL — unlike bd-ye0f4 which only reproduced on rch)

    --test-threads=1: 35 passed, 0 failed
    --test-threads=2: 35 passed, 0 failed
    --test-threads=4: SIGABRT with free(): invalid size
    --test-threads=8: SIGABRT with free(): invalid size (default)

Locally reproducible on a 64-core x86_64 host at HEAD 17431c7a —
threshold is exactly at --test-threads=4. This is the first
locally-reproducible sample of the bd-ye0f4 cluster's
'free(): invalid size' signature. Previous cluster beads (bd-g2bd5,
bd-ye0f4) only reproduced under rch remote execution with the
identical glibc error.

## Why this matters

The bd-ye0f4 cluster has been cycling fix→regress since
2026-04-22 across a581f0ac, e289f838, b04d7238 (all partial TLS
dtor scoping fixes). Every round left the race live. Root cause
has been elusive because nobody could reproduce it locally — only
on rch workers with specific worker scheduling. This rpc_abi_test
sample is a deterministic local reproducer: same
'free(): invalid size' glibc detection, pinpoints the race at the
4+ thread boundary, and runs every time.

## Diagnosis candidates

clnt_perrno_does_not_crash routes through crate::unistd_abi::write.
write() fans into runtime_policy::decide (complex state machine
with potentially-racy internal globals) and runtime_policy::observe
(recording validations). Other tests in the same binary exercise
rpc_thread_createerr, rpc_thread_svc_*, rpc_thread_tls_* — thread-
local getters that allocate buffers.

The most likely explanation: one test's thread-local RPC state is
freed by another thread's teardown (thread-local cross-allocator
free), or runtime_policy has a per-thread AtomicI32 / RefCell that
gets torn-down by one test while another test is mid-decide.

## Fix direction

1. Re-run with RUST_BACKTRACE=1 MALLOC_CHECK_=3 (already tried, no
   extra info — glibc's native free() abort is silent). Next level:
   compile with RUSTFLAGS='-Zsanitizer=address' (nightly) and rerun
   the 4-thread test to get an ASan stack trace pointing at the
   freeing site and the allocating site.
2. Audit all thread-locals in crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/rpc_abi.rs
   and crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/runtime_policy.rs for allocation
   Drop impls that could free pointers allocated by a different
   thread's allocator. rpc_abi.rs has SPERRNO_BUF and
   SPCREATEERR_BUF (Cell<[u8; N]>) which are inline arrays — safe.
   But __rpc_thread_createerr, __rpc_thread_svc_fdset,
   __rpc_thread_svc_max_pollfd, __rpc_thread_svc_pollfd return
   pointers into allocations — those are the likely culprits.
3. Check the 3+ rpc_thread_* tests: if they allocate in one test
   thread and the Drop fires on the next test thread (pthread-local
   rebinding), we get cross-allocator free.

## Validation

cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test rpc_abi_test -- --test-threads=2
  -> 35 passed, 0 failed.
cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test rpc_abi_test -- --test-threads=4
  -> SIGABRT, free(): invalid size.

No commit changes needed to repro. Provides the long-awaited local
sample for the bd-ye0f4 cluster.
notes:
## ROOT-CAUSE FIX by cc-libc (2026-04-22)

Bisected by running rpc_abi_test with progressively narrower test-name filters at --test-threads=4. Convergence:

    cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test rpc_abi_test 'host2netname_' -- --test-threads=2  -> SIGABRT free(): invalid size
    cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test rpc_abi_test host2netname_creates_valid_name -- --test-threads=4  -> 1/1 pass
    cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test rpc_abi_test host2netname_null_defaults     -- --test-threads=4  -> 1/1 pass

Either test alone passes; the two together at N>=2 abort. They share no test-side state — but they BOTH allocate via host2netname() and BOTH free via libc::free().

The actual bug at crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/rpc_abi.rs:2874:

    let buf = unsafe { crate::malloc_abi::raw_alloc(name.len()) } as *mut c_char;

host2netname allocates through OUR internal arena (raw_alloc), but the test releases the buffer via libc::free (host glibc's free). In debug builds (test context, no LD_PRELOAD), libc::free binds at link time to glibc's free — which sees a chunk header from our arena, interprets it as a glibc chunk-size field, gets nonsense, and aborts with 'free(): invalid size'.

The race is just chunk-layout entropy: with 1 thread the same allocator context is reused so chunks happen to look fine; with 2+ threads the arena's per-thread chunk metadata diverges from glibc's expectations and the free hits a bad size word deterministically.

## Fix

Change host2netname to allocate via libc::malloc instead of our internal raw_alloc. POSIX defines host2netname as 'returns a buffer the caller must free()' — that means the caller's free() (glibc's in non-preload context, our interposed one in preload context) must match the alloc. libc::malloc satisfies both: in preload context it IS our interposed malloc, in non-preload context it's glibc's, and either way it pairs correctly with libc::free.

## Validation

cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test rpc_abi_test (default parallelism) -> 35 passed, 0 failed (was SIGABRT). All thread counts 1..8 now pass.

## Wider implication for the bd-ye0f4 cluster

30+ other call sites use the same `crate::malloc_abi::raw_alloc` pattern and return the buffer to the caller (inet_abi.rs, dirent_abi.rs, stdlib_abi.rs, more in rpc_abi.rs, wchar_abi.rs, unistd_abi.rs, string_abi.rs). Each is a candidate sibling failure. Every test that exercises one of those entrypoints AND frees with libc::free is a potential next bd-dqqh1. Filed as an umbrella bead for systematic audit.
close_reason: Fixed: host2netname now uses libc::malloc instead of internal raw_alloc; alloc/free pair consistent with caller libc::free in both LD_PRELOAD and non-preload contexts.

title: fuzz: printf/snprintf format-string adversarial invariants (width/precision/specifier chaos)
description:
## Scope
Add crates/frankenlibc-fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_printf_adversarial.rs covering format-string **security** properties beyond what fuzz_printf already does. fuzz_printf focuses on correctness of well-formed specifiers with structured args; this target covers **attacker-controlled format strings**: huge widths/precisions, positional-arg reordering, %n refusal, bracket-bomb '%*.*' chains, and buffer-exhaustion safety.

## Archetype
1 crash-detector + invariant (security contract):
- snprintf with huge width (1M) must not OOM or overrun dst buffer
- %n must either be honored with a valid ptr OR return -1 / refuse — never crash or write to garbage
- positional '%99$d' with missing args must return an error rather than reading OOB stack

## Inputs
struct PrintfAdversarialFuzzInput {
  format: Vec<u8>,           // arbitrary bytes — fuzzer can generate '%' + junk
  int_args: [i32; 8],        // padded arg vector
  str_args: [Option<Vec<u8>>; 4],
  dst_size: u16,
}

## Invariants
- Return value <= dst_size - 1 (or -1)
- Written bytes fit in dst_size (guard-byte sentinel check)
- Determinism on repeated calls with identical args
- No panic on ANY format byte sequence (including partial '%' at NUL, unknown specifier, repeated length modifiers)

## Expected bug classes (per CVE history)
- glibc CVE-2023-25139: %n within width-modifier chains
- glibc CVE-2010-0296: formatted-printing stack exhaustion for deeply nested positional refs
- Integer overflow in computed width (we widened i32 width to c_int during bd-0u5fm but the WIDTH field inside pattern '%2147483648d' is still parsed — test with decimal-string widths that overflow usize)
- Off-by-one in our own buffer-truncation path

## Relation to existing work
bd-m40be (fnmatch), bd-7rxtm (strftime), bd-luc3d (length-modifier ABI) already found format-parser bugs via fuzzing. This target fills the final gap: the printf pipeline itself, beyond the structured-fixture-case harness.

## Score
5 × 4 × /2 ≈ 10 — CVE-class severity (format-string attacks remain a top-10 web-server vector).
notes:
Closed by cc-libc.

Delivered crates/frankenlibc-fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_printf_adversarial.rs with 8 archetypes covering the CVE classes listed in the bead:

- adv_parser_panic: arbitrary-byte inputs to parse_format_string / parse_format_spec (termination + bounded-segment invariant).
- adv_huge_dynamic_width: %*d with attacker-chosen width int.
- adv_bracket_bomb: %*.*d chaining width and precision magnitudes.
- adv_bracket_bomb_string: %*.*s variant with attacker-supplied string.
- adv_percent_n_refusal: %n under hardened mode — must be honored (count==2) or refused (rc<0 or count==-1), never write to garbage.
- adv_overflow_width_literal: integer-overflow widths encoded as compile-time literals (%2147483648d, %99999999999d, %.99999999999d, %9999999999.9999999999d) so we never pass attacker-controlled formats to a C variadic call.
- adv_positional_out_of_range: %99$d with only one arg — must not read past supplied varargs.
- adv_percent_storm: pure-% format string — parser stress.

All archetypes use 64-byte GUARD_BYTE sentinels on both sides of the destination buffer; each call asserts the guards are untouched after return. Hardened mode is set once globally via sync::Once.

Safety: the target never passes an attacker-controlled format to a variadic C call (that would be UB at the language level). Attacker chaos lands in the numeric args, in the Rust parser entrypoints, or in a fixed set of compile-time format literals.

Wired into crates/frankenlibc-fuzz/Cargo.toml as `fuzz_printf_adversarial` bin.

Validation: cargo check --bin fuzz_printf_adversarial clean (13s on vmi1149989); cargo clippy --bin fuzz_printf_adversarial --no-deps -- -D warnings clean (local fallback because remote worker lacks nightly-2026-04-13).

title: Fix JBD2 replay incomplete transaction accounting
description: ReplayStats::incomplete_transactions currently subtracts committed sequence count from pending transaction count. That undercounts when orphan commit blocks coexist with incomplete pending descriptors because the counts can cancel out even though the pending sequence was never committed. Count pending sequence IDs that are absent from the committed set instead, and add a regression test.

title: PORT: mergesort + heapsort (BSD libc sort variants)
description: BSD libc mergesort(base, nmemb, size, compar) and heapsort(base, nmemb, size, compar) — sort variants of qsort with the same signature except they return int (0 on success, -1 with errno on failure). mergesort is STABLE (preserves input order for equal elements); heapsort is NOT stable but uses no auxiliary storage. Both are ~50 years old, present in libbsd 0.0/0.3, used by mtree, ls -t, sort -s, and any tool that needs stability without writing its own merge sort. Currently missing entirely from frankenlibc-abi. Ship: pure-safe core::stdlib::sort::{mergesort, heapsort} that operate on byte slices via index permutation (so the existing qsort comparator-callback infrastructure works unchanged) + abi shims that return 0/-1 with ENOMEM on alloc failure (mergesort) or EINVAL on bad inputs.
close_reason: shipped: core::stdlib::sort {mergesort (stable, copy-out + timsort), heapsort (in-place max-heap)} + stdlib_abi shims with EINVAL/ENOMEM mapping; 13+9 tests; clippy-clean; rch-built

title: [HIGH] fuzz gap: signal/socket/fortify/setjmp/mmap/dlfcn/pthread/c11threads ABI modules are unfuzzed (mmap now partially covered by fuzz_mmap)
description:
## Motivation

/testing-fuzzing skill discovery pass on crates/frankenlibc-abi/src enumerated 3646 `pub unsafe extern "C" fn` symbols across 38 modules and cross-referenced against the 30 fuzz bins registered in crates/frankenlibc-fuzz/Cargo.toml. The CVE-class gap is concentrated in 8 modules that currently have **no** fuzz target:

| Priority | Module | Symbols | CVE class |
|---------|--------|---------|----------|
| 1 | mmap | 11 | memory-safety (UAF / OOB / W^X bypass) — **covered by fuzz_mmap in same PR** |
| 2 | signal | 29 | handler setup races, async-signal-safety, privilege escalation |
| 3 | socket | 18 | network attack surface, kernel ABI complexity |
| 4 | fortify | 79 | `__*_chk` overflow-detection wrappers — if broken, they silently fail to protect |
| 5 | setjmp | 12 | control-flow integrity, sigsetjmp edge cases |
| 6 | dlfcn | 7 | dlopen/dlsym attack surface |
| 7 | pthread | 141 | concurrency (mutex/cond/rwlock/barrier) — best done as TSan campaign |
| 8 | c11threads | 21 | C11 threading (thrd_/mtx_/cnd_) — same pattern as pthread |

## Status of priority-1 (mmap)

Delivered in the same push: `crates/frankenlibc-fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_mmap.rs` — stateful harness with a live-mapping arena, 7 ops (Map/Unmap/Protect/Sync/Advise/Remap/MarkStaleInPlace), guard-byte sentinels on writable mappings, alignment invariant on mmap/mremap return addresses, and the use-after-unmap contract (every op on a Stale slot must return -1 / MAP_FAILED). The harness intentionally exercises PROT_EXEC / RWX requests against the hardened-mode membrane to cover the expected refuse-or-clamp path. Registered as `fuzz_mmap` bin. Validation: cargo build + cargo clippy --no-deps -- -D warnings both clean.

## Fix direction for the remaining 7

Each should follow the pattern already established by the 5 fuzz targets cc-libc shipped earlier this session (fuzz_printf_adversarial, fuzz_pathname, fuzz_env, fuzz_sched, fuzz_pidfd_timer):

- Stateful archetype with a handle table where applicable (signal → signal handler slots; socket → sockfds; pthread → thread / mutex / cond handles; setjmp → jmp_buf storage slots).
- Return-code contract + lifecycle invariant (stale handle → must fail).
- Direct syscall differential where possible (signal, socket via libc::syscall). For pthread/c11threads, use a BTreeMap / counter shadow model because the ABI deviates from raw syscall shape.
- Safety bounds: signal restricted to {0, SIGWINCH, SIGURG} the way fuzz_pidfd_timer does; socket in PF_LOCAL with SOCK_DGRAM + AT_EMPTY_PATH style so no real network traffic.
- TSan-specific campaign for pthread/c11threads; run with `RUSTFLAGS=-Zsanitizer=thread`.

## Score priority

Per /testing-fuzzing skill, score = (untrusted-input) * (complexity) * (unsafe/native) * (prior CVEs). The mmap surface scores highest because of 40+ years of mmap/munmap/mprotect CVEs (CVE-2017-1000405 ptrace race, CVE-2016-5195 'Dirty COW' mprotect interaction, CVE-2023-40283 vma-use-after-free). Signal is second (CVE-2020-14386 af_packet, CVE-2021-44733 tee), fortify third (CVE-2023-4911 'Looney Tunables' via __stack_chk_* interaction).

## Exit criteria

One child bead per remaining module, each:
- Delivers a fuzz target in crates/frankenlibc-fuzz/fuzz_targets/
- Registers it in crates/frankenlibc-fuzz/Cargo.toml
- Achieves ≥1000 exec/s (skill Hard Rule 1) or, for stateful harnesses, ≥100 exec/s
- Cargo clippy --no-deps -- -D warnings clean
- Seed corpus committed (exclude artifacts per existing .gitignore)
notes: Fuzz coverage delivered for all 8 priority modules + 4 pthread sub-targets: fuzz_mmap, fuzz_signal, fuzz_socket, fuzz_fortify, fuzz_setjmp, fuzz_dlfcn, fuzz_pthread_mutex, fuzz_pthread_cond, fuzz_pthread_keys, fuzz_pthread_rwlock, fuzz_pthread_sync_misc, fuzz_c11threads. All 12 sources present + registered in crates/frankenlibc-fuzz/Cargo.toml. Verified via rch full build (exit 0, 62s remote) + fuzz_signal 30s smoke (2.4M runs, ~77k exec/s, 0 crashes). fuzz_xdr added later in this session covers the 9th high-CVE surface (SunRPC XDR) — found and fixed bd-bhqcn, bd-lc5ss, bd-xpgak in that target.

title: [test-env] Two more environment-dependent REDs: ctime_r assumes a UTC host, glob errfunc assumes non-root
description:
Two gates RED at clean HEAD, neither caused by an fl defect. Both are the same shape as bd-30sv83
(privilege) -- a gate that encodes an assumption about the MACHINE rather than about fl.

1. conformance_diff_gmtime::ctime_r_matches_glibc -- assumed a UTC host.
   ctime is asctime(localtime(t)), so glibc's answer depends on the machine timezone. fl is UTC-only
   BY DESIGN: time_abi's tzset documents that the TZ environment variable is not consulted and all
   conversions assume UTC, and core stamps tm_gmtoff = 0. On the rch fleet (UTC-5) glibc returned
   'Wed Dec 31 19:00:00 1969' for epoch 0 against fl's 'Thu Jan  1 00:00:00 1970'. Green on a UTC dev
   box, red on the fleet.
   FIXED by pinning TZ=UTC + tzset() before the comparison. That CONTROLS the variable rather than
   dropping the assertion: the gate still pins the entire asctime rendering (day/month names,
   zero-padding, the two-space day, trailing newline, 26-byte buffer contract), which is the part fl
   actually implements. The gate's header claimed 'gmtime is fully deterministic (UTC, no
   timezone)', which is true of gmtime and NOT of ctime_r -- the author generalised across the two
   functions in one file.

2. conformance_diff_fnmatch_glob::diff_glob_errfunc_directory_error_paths -- assumed non-root.
   It chmods a directory 0o000 and expects glob to report the failure through errfunc. Root ignores
   permission bits, so no error occurs: the callback is never called, errno stays 0, no epath is
   recorded, and every case returns GLOB_NOMATCH instead of GLOB_ABORTED.
   FIXED by splitting the assertions. fl-vs-glibc comparison on rc, callback_calls, errno and epath
   now runs ALWAYS and is never skipped; only the premise assertions (rc == expected, calls == 1,
   errno != 0, epath contains 'blocked') are guarded on geteuid() != 0. As root both impls agree, so
   the comparison half still has teeth.

title: PORT: statmount/listmount + finit_module + quotactl_fd + map_shadow_stack + bpf + kexec_load + kexec_file_load (8 modern Linux syscalls)
description: Add 8 modern Linux libc syscall wrappers, all forwarding via libc::syscall + raw_syscall_with_errno{,_long} bridges. (1) statmount(*req, *out, bufsize, flags) -> int (Linux 6.8+, syscall 457) — query a single mount by ID into struct statmount. (2) listmount(*req, *out, count, flags) -> int (Linux 6.8+, syscall 458) — enumerate child mount IDs into a buffer. (3) finit_module(fd, *args, flags) -> int (SYS_finit_module=313) — load a kernel module from an open file descriptor. (4) quotactl_fd(fd, cmd, id, *addr) -> int (Linux 5.14+, SYS_quotactl_fd=443) — like quotactl but takes an open fd instead of a block-device path. (5) map_shadow_stack(addr, size, flags) -> long (Linux 6.6+, syscall 453) — allocate a CET shadow stack on x86_64. (6) bpf(cmd, *attr, size) -> int (SYS_bpf=321) — universal BPF interface. (7) kexec_load(entry, nr_segments, *segments, flags) -> long (SYS_kexec_load=246) — load a new kernel image for kexec reboot. (8) kexec_file_load(kernel_fd, initrd_fd, cmdline_len, *cmdline, flags) -> long (SYS_kexec_file_load=320) — same but from open fds. NULL-pointer guards where applicable; opaque pointers for kernel structs whose layouts are version-specific.
close_reason: shipped: 8 modern Linux syscall wrappers (statmount, listmount, finit_module, quotactl_fd, map_shadow_stack, bpf, kexec_load, kexec_file_load) + 10 abi tests covering NULL guards + privilege/kernel fallbacks

title: PORT: dehumanize_number (NetBSD human-readable size parser)

title: pow gap is log2-bound: fl log2 1.47x slower than glibc (11.8 vs 8.0ns); need 4-ULP table log2 at ~8ns (exp2 already faster)
notes: PROBED f64-table log2 (LilacDeer): m∈[1,2), centered table z_i=1+(i+0.5)/N, invc=1/z_i, logc=log2(z_i) f64, degree-8 Taylor poly for log2(1+r). RESULT: 176519 ULP @ 0.99999, 461M ULP near-1 — CATASTROPHIC near x∈[0.5,2)∩near-1. ROOT CAUSE (confirmed): result=e+logc[i]+poly; when log2(x)→0 (x near 1) the e+logc[i] terms are O(1) and cancel, so logc's 0.5-ULP f64 rounding (~1e-16 abs) becomes ~1e-16/ULP(tiny result) = thousands of ULP. f64 table is fine for |e|>=1 (x<0.5 or x>=2, result>=~1) but USELESS on [0.5,2) which IS the common/benched range. NEEDS: logc stored as dd (hi+lo) + dd-FINALIZATION at runtime: (rhi,rlo)=two_sum(e, logc_hi+poly); result=rhi+(rlo+logc_lo+poly_lo). logc_lo generated offline via dd ln (atanh series, ~63 terms for z near 2, OFFLINE so speed irrelevant) / dd ln2. Poly degree ~5-7 with dd table. Runtime ~15-20 ops ~10ns. EMBED N=64 table = 192 consts (or N=16, deg-10 poly, 48 consts). This is a dedicated multi-hour artifact; same dd generator unblocks tgamma/powf. The shipped reroute (ln*LOG2_E, 1.15x) stays as the current impl + the near-1 fallback for the table.

title: fuzz: no dedicated fuzz target for ext4_chksum (CRC32c) algebraic-laws contract
description:
Finding (via /testing-fuzzing skill, NEW target): fuzz/fuzz_targets has 50 targets and ext4_chksum is referenced in 2 (fuzz_ext4_checksums.rs, fuzz_ext4_htree_mmp.rs) but ONLY as a helper to validate other parsers. There is NO dedicated libfuzzer target that pumps random (seed, data) pairs through ext4_chksum and asserts the algebraic-law contract.

ext4_chksum is the CRC32c-based checksum function used by every metadata block (group desc, inode, extent block, dir block, MMP, fast-commit). The proptest layer pins:
  * ext4_proptest_chksum_deterministic — same input → same output
  * ext4_proptest_chksum_empty_data_varies — chksum(seed, &[]) == seed
  * ext4_proptest_chksum_collision_resistance — different inputs yield different outputs (with high probability)
  * ext4_proptest_chksum_incremental — seed-then-append equals direct compute

A libfuzzer target lifts these algebraic laws to >1M iterations/session with corpus learning across input lengths, byte-pattern boundaries, and sign-bit transitions. A regression to a slower-but-correct implementation would slip past unit tests; a regression to a wrong-polynomial CRC variant would fail the algebraic law immediately.

Acceptance: new fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_ext4_chksum.rs that, for an arbitrary (seed, data) split from libfuzzer input, asserts:
  * MR-1 — Determinism: chksum(s, d) called twice gives same result
  * MR-2 — Empty-data identity: chksum(s, &[]) == s
  * MR-3 — Incremental composition: chksum(chksum(s, &d[..k]), &d[k..]) == chksum(s, &d) for all valid k
  * MR-4 — Never panics: implicit
Plus a [[bin]] entry in fuzz/Cargo.toml.
close_reason: done

title: [parity][bug] open_memstream *sizeloc reports full content length, not min(length, position)
description: Found by NEW open_memstream_differential_test (live glibc). POSIX: after fflush/fclose, *sizeloc = the SMALLER of the buffer content length and the current file position. fl reported the full content length, so after a BACKWARD seek + write, fl over-reported. e.g. write 'abc', seek to 6 + 'X' (hole filled with NUL, len 7), then seek to 1 + 'Z' (position 2): glibc *sizeloc=2, fl=7 (buffer bytes were identical 'aZc\0\0\0X\0' + NUL terminator at the max extent 7). Fix: sync_memstream_to_caller sets *size_loc = content_len.min(stream.offset()), keeping the buffer copy (full content + NUL at max extent). FOLLOW-UP: open_wmemstream (wchar_abi sync_open_wmemstream_to_caller) has the analogous size_loc=wchars.len() bug, but fl stores UTF-8 + glibc wide fseek interprets the offset as a WIDE-CHAR position vs fl's byte offset — needs separate characterization (only manifests on backward seek of a wide stream; forward-only is a no-op). stdio_abi_test(255) green.
close_reason: done

Implementation: thin abi shim implementing standard binary search via the existing memory layout helpers; compar invoked with (key, mid_elem, thunk). title: Refine mounted write matrix with namespace atomicity and fsyncdir durability proofs
description:
Supplemental refinement for bd-rchk0.3.2.1. The mounted write matrix covers operation classes and no-partial-mutation cases, but users also need namespace durability evidence: create, rename, link, unlink, rmdir, symlink, and xattr updates must survive reopen according to explicit fsync/fsyncdir boundaries, and rejected operations must not leave split-brain parent/child state.

Scope: define namespace atomicity and directory durability scenarios for ext4 and btrfs mounted paths. The scenarios should distinguish data fsync, parent directory fsync, file close, unmount, forced reopen, unsupported operation rejection, and host capability skips. They should check both visible namespace state and underlying image/reopen state.

Required proof before close:
1. Unit/schema tests reject mounted write scenarios missing parent directory id, child inode/path id, namespace operation kind, fsync/fsyncdir boundary, expected survivor set, expected link count, reopen expectation, and no-partial-mutation checks.
2. Unit tests cover rename overwrite, rename no-overwrite, cross-directory rename, link count update, symlink target persistence, unlink after open handle, rmdir non-empty rejection, xattr namespace update, and unsupported fallocate no-op/refusal classification.
3. E2E mounted smoke covers at least one ext4 and one btrfs namespace scenario in the permissioned lane, plus a dry-run or fixture lane for missing capability.
4. Logs include scenario id, filesystem flavor, mount options, operation sequence, fsync/fsyncdir calls, pre/post directory entries, link counts, xattr keys, image hashes, reopen observations, cleanup status, artifact paths, and reproduction command.
5. Readiness gates cannot count mounted rw namespace coverage if only status-code checks ran without reopen and parent-directory durability proof.

close_reason:
FIXED (coverage restored) + GATED. Commit 251b24190.

The blocker comment said 'superseded by 239d43855; stdlib_abi.rs:7575 maps invalid inputs to EINVAL and core failures to errno, with focused humanize_number failure tests in stdlib_abi_test.rs'. HALF true, and the false half was the part that matters:
- The MAPPING survives. stdlib_abi.rs::humanize_number sets EINVAL for a NULL buffer, zero length, an unreadable suffix and an invalid scale, and ERANGE for BufferTooSmall.
- The TESTS DO NOT. 239d43855 added errno assertions for every failure path; bd829b12f (2026-06-26 23:34:25, 'stdlib/random: glibc-exact System V random types') deleted 332 lines from stdlib_abi_test.rs and took them with it. What remained were three tests asserting nothing but rc == -1, and humanize_invalid_scale_returns_minus_one_with_errno was gone entirely. So the contract held while the coverage did not — which is precisely why nobody noticed.

Traced with: git log -S 'humanize_invalid_scale_returns_minus_one_with_errno' -- crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/stdlib_abi_test.rs, which names the adding and the deleting commit in one command.

RESTORED + EXTENDED (crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/stdlib_abi_test.rs):
  humanize_null_buf_returns_minus_one          -> now asserts EINVAL (was rc only)
  humanize_zero_len_returns_minus_one          -> now asserts EINVAL (was rc only)
  humanize_buffer_too_small_returns_minus_one  -> now asserts ERANGE (was rc only)
  humanize_invalid_scale_returns_minus_one_with_errno  -> restored, asserts EINVAL
  humanize_valid_call_succeeds_without_touching_errno  -> NEW NEGATIVE CONTROL
Each failure test clears errno to 0 first, so a stale value cannot satisfy the assertion. ERANGE vs EINVAL is the distinction these assertions exist to hold — an implementation collapsing both to EINVAL passes on rc alone.

NEGATIVE CONTROL, added because the four arms above are all failure paths: a well-formed call in the same shape must SUCCEED (n > 0) and leave errno at 0. Without it, an implementation that failed everything, or set EINVAL unconditionally, would satisfy every assertion above.

NO DIFFERENTIAL ARM, deliberately, and this is a scope statement not an omission: humanize_number is NetBSD/FreeBSD libutil, not glibc. There is no host oracle to compare against on this fleet, so the contract is asserted directly against the documented BSD behaviour rather than against a live incumbent. Every other bead I closed today used a live glibc arm; this one cannot, and says so.

title: abi tests: synchronous_gai_wrappers flakes under --test-threads=16 (fmemopen/tmpfile fixed)
description:
## Symptom

Three additional unit tests flake intermittently under high
parallelism (--test-threads=16, ~25% combined hit rate across 12
sweep iterations), distinct from bd-7v4oe (closed):

| Test | Hit rate (12 sweeps) | File |
|------|---------------------|------|
| `synchronous_gai_wrappers_match_host_degenerate_contracts` | 3/12 (25%) | DNS/network |
| `tmpfile_closes_without_leaking_named_tmp_entries` | 1/12 (~8%) | filesystem |
| `fmemopen_write_creates_stream` | 1/12 (~8%) | stdio |

The bd-7v4oe fix (registry RAII guard) verified its own target
flake is gone in this same sweep — these are separate races.

## Likely categories

1. **synchronous_gai_wrappers** — touches `getaddrinfo` and friends
   which read /etc/resolv.conf, /etc/hosts, etc. Under parallelism
   the host glibc resolver may serialize on shared file descriptors
   or DNS cache state, producing different EAI_* codes than
   "degenerate" baseline. Fix candidate: serialize the test (or
   subset) with a shared lock.
2. **tmpfile_closes_without_leaking_named_tmp_entries** — POSIX
   `tmpfile()` creates an unlinked file in /tmp. Under parallel
   pressure the directory enumeration check may see entries from
   other in-flight `tmpfile()` calls. Fix candidate: use a unique
   subdirectory or accept transient races in the leak count check.
3. **fmemopen_write_creates_stream** — fmemopen builds a memory-
   backed FILE*. Could share registry state with other stream
   tests. Fix candidate: same RAII registry-cleanup pattern as
   bd-7v4oe.

## Severity

[MEDIUM] (P3) — test-only flakes that don't affect production
behavior. Worth fixing because they pollute CI and mask real
regressions in stress sweeps. The bd-7v4oe pattern (RAII cleanup
guards) likely applies to (3); (1) and (2) need targeted analysis
of the host syscall surface they exercise.
notes:
Partial fix: fmemopen flake closed in dd82f863 (STREAM_REGISTRY_PROBE_LOCK), tmpfile flake closed in 18baf908 (drop racy redundant /tmp enumeration). synchronous_gai_wrappers flake remains open — needs cross-test DNS state serialization across multiple test binaries (host glibc gai async queue shares state across all in-process callers). Reproduces only when running --tests (multiple binaries), not within unistd_abi_test alone. 10/10 isolated runs pass.

Fully fixed: three-part fix in this cycle.
1. GAI_TEST_LOCK (31f5b9f2): intra-binary serialization across 16 gai_*/getaddrinfo_a tests. Single-pass parity now stable.
2. GaicbShape struct size (9d4bd2f5): test's GaicbShape was 32 bytes but glibc's struct gaicb is 56 (adds __return + __unused[5]). host_gai_error reads __return — with the short struct it read uninitialized stack past the boundary, producing divergent host-vs-abi results under parallel pressure. Real ABI-correctness bug surfaced by the flake.
3. xdr_reference calloc (fd7c7cba): bonus fix. Stress uncovered a SIGABRT / misaligned-pointer deref in xdr_reference_depth_limit regression test; root cause was libc::malloc leaving inner pointer fields uninitialized for recursive procs. Switched to libc::calloc (mirrors glibc xdr_reference's malloc+memset idiom).
Verified: 5/5 xdr_abi_test --test-threads=16 iters pass; earlier gai 7/8 iters had zero gai failures (xdr SIGSEGV was the #3 bug, now also fixed). Full abi 8x stress in flight.

title: [MAINT] FuseInodeLocks.table grows unboundedly — every accessed inode allocates a FuseInodeLock that is never evicted
description:
# Maintainability / resource finding from modes-of-reasoning pass

## Finding

`FuseInodeLocks` at crates/ffs-fuse/src/lib.rs:703-737 stores a `Mutex<BTreeMap<InodeNumber, Arc<FuseInodeLock>>>`. Every FUSE mutation operation (create/mkdir/unlink/rmdir/rename/setattr) calls `acquire()`, which does `table.entry(ino).or_insert_with(...)` — inserting a new entry on first encounter and never evicting.

For a long-running FUSE mount that touches many inodes, the table grows monotonically. With ~80 bytes per entry (key + Arc + FuseInodeLock fields), a mount that accesses a million inodes parks ~80 MB of never-freed locks.

## Evidence

- Storage: crates/ffs-fuse/src/lib.rs:705 `table: Mutex<BTreeMap<InodeNumber, Arc<FuseInodeLock>>>`
- Insertion: line 727 `table.entry(ino).or_insert_with(|| Arc::new(FuseInodeLock::default()))`
- No `remove` call anywhere — confirmed via `rg 'table\.\(remove\|clear\|retain\)' crates/ffs-fuse/`
- No TTL, no LRU eviction, no drop-on-last-guard hook

## Why this wasn't caught earlier

Not a deadlock (inspected in /deadlock-finder pass, out of that skill's scope). Not a correctness bug. Pure resource accumulation that only matters for long-running mounts. Relevant as soon as FrankenFS targets real production workloads.

## Fix directions

1. **Drop-on-last-guard cleanup.** When `FuseInodeGuard::drop` runs, check if the `Arc<FuseInodeLock>` strong_count is 1 (we hold the last ref). If so, remove the entry from the table. Race-safe because `acquire()` holds the table mutex during insert, so we can hold it during the last-guard removal check.
2. **Epoch-based GC.** Periodically scan the table and evict entries whose `Arc` strong_count is 1 (no active guard) AND that haven't been acquired in N seconds.
3. **Cap-based eviction.** Soft cap the table size; evict idle entries LRU when the cap is exceeded.

Option 1 is cleanest and matches the natural lifecycle (entries exist only when a guard is live).

## Acceptance

- A stress test creating/unlinking 100K inodes shows FuseInodeLocks.table stays bounded (approximately proportional to concurrent guards, not to total inodes-ever-accessed).
- No regression in the sorted-ino total-order guarantee (the crate's only concurrency invariant). /deadlock-finder sweep remains CLEAN.
- Unit test: acquire+drop a single inode's guard, assert the table is empty afterward.

## Severity rationale

P3 (low) — not exploitable, not correctness, not currently a production concern (FrankenFS mounts are short-lived in V1.x). But it is a real resource leak that will matter when V2+ targets longer-running deployments. Worth tracking so it doesn't get lost.
close_reason: Reconciled stale JSONL row: FuseInodeLocks leak fix already implemented and closure is present in commit 776fe07.

title: [parity][bug][realpath] userspace resolver: file followed by '.' must be ENOTDIR (dropped CurDir lost the dir requirement)
description:
Found by NEW realpath_differential_fuzz (live host realpath() over a rich symlink tree). The PRIMARY resolver (fl::realpath, /proc-based) is correct; the pure-userspace fallback realpath_resolve_userspace diverged: a non-directory final target followed by a '.' (or '/.', '/./' chains) resolved OK in fl but glibc returns ENOTDIR (errno 20). e.g. 'lnk_file/.', 'lnk_abs//.', 'd/f/.', 'to_sub/g/./'.

ROOT CAUSE: collect() used Path::components(), which NORMALIZES '.' away (except a leading one), so a trailing/middle '.' was dropped before the loop's non-directory check ('if !queue.is_empty() return ENOTDIR') could fire. ('..' was preserved as ParentDir, so 'file/..' already gave ENOTDIR correctly.)

FIX (stdlib_abi.rs realpath_resolve_userspace): split raw path bytes on '/' (preserving '.' and '..' as real components) instead of Path::components(); handle '.' in the loop as a path no-op that, by remaining in the queue, makes a preceding file trip the ENOTDIR check. Also switched the input/cwd/symlink-target collection + is_absolute checks to byte-based. 40k differential-fuzz 0-div (primary + fallback).
close_reason: Fixed: byte-based component split preserves '.' so file-then-'.' trips ENOTDIR. 40k differential-fuzz 0-div (primary+fallback), probe+conformance pass.

title: ffs-mvcc: wal_throughput benches missing checkpoint + truncate_wal latency floors
description:
Finding (via /profiling-software-performance skill, fifth visit,
different target): the wal_throughput criterion bench file
(crates/ffs-mvcc/benches/wal_throughput.rs) is comprehensive — 14
benches covering commit throughput, SSI overhead, EBR memory,
RCU/RwLock/Mutex read scaling, write amplification, MVCC contention,
sharded MVCC, pruning, coalesced append. But TWO operations on the
PersistentMvccStore persistence path have NO bench coverage:

  1. `PersistentMvccStore::checkpoint(path)` — writes a snapshot
     of the version chains to disk via temp-file + atomic rename.
     Cost scales with version count and version-chain length.

  2. `PersistentMvccStore::truncate_wal()` — rewrites the WAL header
     and truncates the file to header_size after a successful
     checkpoint. Cost is dominated by the file_set_len + sync_all.

Both are on the operator-facing maintenance path. A regression that
made checkpoint quadratic in version count, or truncate_wal slower
because of an extra fsync, would silently degrade the maintenance
window cost without tripping any existing bench gate.

Acceptance: 2 new bench functions in
crates/ffs-mvcc/benches/wal_throughput.rs registered in the
existing `wal_benches` criterion_group!, each priming the store
with a deterministic workload before invoking the operation under
test. Verified via `rch exec -- cargo check -p ffs-mvcc --benches`.
notes: Shipped: 2 new criterion bench functions in crates/ffs-mvcc/benches/wal_throughput.rs covering bench_checkpoint_throughput (PersistentMvccStore::checkpoint with 256 blocks × 8 versions seed) and bench_truncate_wal_throughput (PersistentMvccStore::truncate_wal after a fresh checkpoint horizon, 64 commits seed). Both use iter_batched with SmallInput so the seed isn't measured. Registered in the wal_benches criterion_group!. Verified via rch exec -- cargo check -p ffs-mvcc --benches (Finished in 48.76s). Pairs with bd-7zd94 (PersistentMvccStore lock-ordering doc + test, which exercises commit/checkpoint/truncate_wal under contention) — that test pins correctness; this bench pins latency floor.

title: error_at_line ignores error_one_per_line (no same-file/line suppression; over-counts error_message_count)
close_reason:
GATED (implementation was already present, ungated). Commit 757ad815a.

The blocker comment was right that ERR_AT_LINE_STATE already suppresses repeated file+line calls and skips the error_message_count bump, and that bd-enxo3y is cited at the implementation. What was missing is that NOTHING EXERCISED IT: conformance_diff_error_at_line.rs's own header says the suppression is 'left off (default 0) so each call prints', so every arm in the file ran the unsuppressed path. Per the shipped-but-ungated pattern, this bead closes on a gate that could actually fail, not on the code being present.

GATE: crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/conformance_diff_error_at_line.rs
- error_at_line_honors_error_one_per_line_like_glibc: sets error_one_per_line in BOTH impls (fl's global directly, glibc's via dlsym) and runs an 8-step file/line sequence end-to-end through each, comparing transcripts plus per-step error_message_count deltas. Steps cover every branch of glibc's condition: pointer-equal repeat, strcmp-equal repeat via a DISTINCT CString with equal bytes (glibc short-circuits on pointer equality first, so a single reused CString would never reach the strcmp branch), line-differs, file-differs, NULL-vs-name, and both-NULL. Each impl keeps its own statics, so each sequence is primed with a location no step uses -- otherwise step 0 could be suppressed by whatever a previously-run arm left behind.
- error_at_line_repeats_when_error_one_per_line_is_clear: NEGATIVE CONTROL. Same sequence with the flag clear must print every time. Without it, an implementation that suppressed unconditionally -- or one that never printed at all -- would satisfy the suppression assertions.
- Both also assert the property by name (exactly steps 1/5/7 suppressed; suppressed steps print nothing AND do not count; printed steps do count) so a regression reads as the bug rather than as one opaque transcript diff.

EVIDENCE (rch remote, worker vmi1227854, source commit 757ad815a):
  cargo test -j2 -p frankenlibc-abi --test conformance_diff_error_at_line
    -> test result: ok. 9 passed; 0 failed. (4 arms before this bead and bd-ul4pyl)
  cargo clippy -j2 -p frankenlibc-abi --lib --test conformance_diff_error_at_line -- -D warnings
    -> zero findings on any file touched.

DEFECT FOUND BY THIS GATE, filed and fixed separately as bd-0qltjh: the NULL-filename steps were the first calls in the repo to reach error_at_line with file_name == NULL, and they failed on FORMATTING, not suppression -- fl printed 'PROG:msg' where glibc prints 'PROG: msg'. Fixed in the same commit; without that fix these arms stay red.

PRE-EXISTING, NOT CAUSED BY THIS BEAD: the 12 stdlib_abi_test fsmount/fsopen/fspick/move_mount failures (root-vs-unprivileged on rch workers), verified pre-existing by clean-HEAD baseline replay while closing bd-ul4pyl. Unrelated agent changes were not reverted.

Integrate FrankenLibC with franken_kernel suite substrate: adopt canonical Cx capability context, TraceId, DecisionId, PolicyId, SchemaVersion types. All TSM decisions must flow through Cx. All evidence records must use canonical IDs. Must not fork franken_kernel schema. ADOPTION WEDGE: FrankenLibC must function standalone without franken_kernel (fallback to local types).

## Acceptance Criteria
See `acceptance_criteria` field.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria
Implementation must preserve all existing functionality and claims while adding deterministic verification coverage.

### Mandatory Verification Gate
- Comprehensive unit tests are required for all touched logic: positive, negative, adversarial, and regression.
- Deterministic e2e scripts are required for all externally visible behavior in strict and hardened mode where relevant.
- Structured logs are mandatory for unit/e2e runs with fields: `trace_id`, `mode`, `api_family`, `symbol`, `decision_path`, `healing_action`, `errno`, `latency_ns`, `artifact_refs`.
- Closure evidence must include exact test commands, expected outputs/thresholds, and representative failure signatures.
- CI must persist logs, diffs, and reports with deterministic naming and retention for replay/triage.
- Tooling contract: deterministic orchestration/traceability uses `/dp/asupersync`, and deterministic diff/snapshot/TUI evidence uses `/dp/frankentui`.
notes:
### Mandatory Test/E2E Logging Checklist
- Test command set is documented in bead notes before closure (unit + e2e + perf where applicable).
- Expected output and pass/fail thresholds are documented per command.
- Failure triage snippets are documented (top failure classes + where to inspect artifacts).
- Evidence index entry links logs, parity diffs, and benchmark/proof artifacts.
- Overload behavior logging is required when applicable: pressure signal, degradation mode, selected policy, guard decision, rollback trigger.

title: [bug][math] nearbyint/nearbyintf raise FE_INEXACT; that flag suppression is the whole point of the function
description:
conformance_diff_nearbyint_flags was RED at HEAD (sweep bd-aykfv1), untracked. Values were all correct; only the flag diverged.

  nearbyint(0.5)   fl 0x0000000000000000 flags 0x20   glibc same value, flags 0x0
  nearbyint(-0.5)  fl 0x8000000000000000 flags 0x20   glibc same value, flags 0x0
  nearbyint(1.5)   fl 0x4000000000000000 flags 0x20   glibc same value, flags 0x0
  (same for nearbyintf)

CAUSE: core's nearbyint was literally 'libm::rint(x)'. Suppressing FE_INEXACT is the ENTIRE difference between nearbyint and rint (IEEE 754 roundToIntegralExact vs roundToIntegralNearest). The doc comment above it already read 'Round to nearest integer without raising inexact exception' — the contract was stated correctly and the body contradicted it.

FIXED at the commit citing this bead: math_abi::nearbyint/nearbyintf now wrap the call in suppress_inexact(), which reads MXCSR before and after and puts the inexact bit back. Only that bit is restored; any other exception the call legitimately raises is untouched. This is what glibc's hardware roundsd does with its suppress-precision-exception bit.

A WRONG FIRST ATTEMPT, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT REPEATED. I first did what the round family does (bd-i5cj3w) and rounded by bit manipulation, which raises no flag at all. That fixed the flags and BROKE THE VALUES: nearbyint must honour the CURRENT rounding mode, and a hand-rolled ties-to-even is only right under FE_TONEAREST. The gate caught it immediately under FE_DOWNWARD (m0x400):
  nearbyint(1.5)  bit-manip 2.0   host 1.0
  nearbyint(-0.5) bit-manip -0.0  host -1.0
round can use bit manipulation because its tie rule is fixed; nearbyint cannot. The distinction is now recorded in both function comments.

ALSO NOTE: suppress_inexact is #[cfg(not(test))] with a pass-through twin, because lib.rs gates fenv_abi #[cfg(not(test))] and the module does not exist during 'cargo test --lib'. The flag behaviour is observed by the integration gate, which links the real library. FIX: math_abi::nearbyint/nearbyintf wrap the call in suppress_inexact(), reading MXCSR before and after and restoring only the inexact bit. Any other exception the call legitimately raises is left alone. That is what glibc's hardware roundsd does with its suppress-precision-exception bit.

TWO MISTAKES I MADE AND CAUGHT, both now documented in the source so the next person does not repeat them:

1. WRONG REMEDY. I first copied the round family's approach (bd-i5cj3w) and rounded by bit manipulation, which raises no flag at all. It fixed the flags and BROKE THE VALUES: nearbyint must honour the CURRENT rounding mode, and a hand-rolled ties-to-even is only right under FE_TONEAREST. The gate caught it immediately under FE_DOWNWARD (m0x400) — bit-manip gave nearbyint(1.5)=2.0 and nearbyint(-0.5)=-0.0 where the host gives 1.0 and -1.0. round may use bit manipulation because its tie rule is FIXED; nearbyint may not. Both function comments now say so.

2. NEW BROKEN TARGET. My first suppress_inexact called fenv_abi unconditionally, but lib.rs gates that module #[cfg(not(test))], so it does not exist during 'cargo test --lib'. That added a FIFTH failing target to the --all-targets check. Worth noting the check is what caught it — the integration gate was green throughout.

THE CONTRACT WAS ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN AND IGNORED: the doc comment above core's nearbyint read 'Round to nearest integer without raising inexact exception' while the body was 'libm::rint(x)'. That is the third time in this sweep a comment stated the right rule and the code did the opposite (see also psignal bd-3k2orn and dn_comp bd-50his3).

title: [parity][bug] basename SYMBOL was POSIX but glibc bare basename is GNU; dirname dropped leading-slashslash prefix
description: Found by NEW basename_dirname_differential_fuzz (200k vs live glibc). Bug 1: fl exported the bare basename symbol with XPG-POSIX semantics (strips trailing slashes, empty yields dot, slash yields slash), but glibc bare basename SYMBOL is the GNU variant (string.h under _GNU_SOURCE): component after the LAST slash, no strip, no buffer modify, trailing-slash paths yield empty. POSIX one is __xpg_basename (compile-time redirect from libgen.h), which fl already exports right. So _GNU_SOURCE programs calling basename got wrong POSIX semantics. Bug 2: dirname collapsed a leading two-slash PREFIX (dirname of slashslash-ccc gave slash but glibc gives slashslash; POSIX network-root: a run of EXACTLY two leading slashes is preserved, 1 or 3-plus collapse to one). FIXED both: stdlib_abi basename rewritten to GNU; dirname_range in core preserves the two-slash prefix. conformance_diff_libgen updated (it linked __xpg_basename as oracle, encoding the bug). 200k fuzz 0-div.
close_reason: done

title: feat(iconv): add ISO-2022-CN-EXT stateful codec (ISO-IR-165 G1 + CNS planes 3-7 via G3/SS3)
description:
Last charset from the coverage probe (bd-zz8w41) that fl rejects. ISO-2022-CN-EXT/ISO2022CNEXT extends the existing ISO-2022-CN (iso2022cn_decode/convert at mod.rs ~21343/~21196) per RFC 1922.

ADDS over ISO-2022-CN:
 (1) G1 designator ESC $ ) E -> ISO-IR-165 (CCITT extended GB2312, a superset). fl has NO ISO-IR-165 table and glibc does NOT expose ISO-IR-165 standalone (iconv -f ISO-IR-165 errors), so the table must be GENERATED THROUGH ISO-2022-CN-EXT itself: for each 2-byte cell c0c1 in 0x21..0x7E, feed glibc 'ESC $ ) E  0x0E  c0 c1  0x0F' and record the UCS-4 output. Build iso_ir_165_tables.rs (decode + reverse encode) the same way the EBCDIC/JISX tables were swept.
 (2) G3 via SS3 = ESC O (0x1B 0x4F) for CNS 11643 planes 3-7, designated ESC $ + I/J/K/L/M (planes 3,4,5,6,7). Existing ISO-2022-CN already does plane2 via SS2 (ESC N) routed through decode_euctw([0x8E,0xA2,...]); planes 3-7 route through decode_euctw([0x8F, 0x8E?, plane-byte, ...]) — VERIFY decode_euctw (mod.rs ~18279) supports planes 3-7 (SS3 0x8F + plane designator 0xA3..0xA7); if not, extend it.

STATE additions: a G3 plane register (which CNS plane is designated to G3) alongside the existing iso2022cn_in_g1/out_g1. Encode side: prefer GB2312, then ISO-IR-165, then CNS planes per glibc's selection order (check glibc iso-2022-cn-ext.c precedence).

GATE: model on conformance_diff_iconv_iso2022cn.rs — dlsym live glibc, exhaustive designator/SS2/SS3 sequences + random round-trips, byte-exact both directions incl flush/SI-reset.

This is a focused-session task (table generation + stateful G3 + designators), deliberately NOT rushed at an hour-tail to preserve absolute parity.

ISO-IR-165 table generated through glibc's own decoder (8388 decode cells + 8294 asymmetric lazy-stay encode domain). Reproduces glibc's exact stateful quirks: SO requires prior announcement (no default G1); active-set captured at SO (designator-while-shifted is announcement-only); SS2 consumes ESC N before decode while SS3 doesn't consume ESC O; encode escape-minimizing TO_LOOP selection (primary SO set by ann, then CNS-2, other SO sets, CNS-3..7) incl. glibc's IR-165-primary shifted/unshifted comparison bug; flush emits SI when any announcement active; newline clears encode announcements but not decode. title: Idea-wizard: FrankenLibC swarm-scale evidence and remote proof hardening

Scope

ffs-btrfs: BTRFS_ITEM_* item-key constants lack kernel-conformance pinning
description:
Finding (via /testing-conformance-harnesses skill, fifth visit,
different target): crates/ffs-btrfs/src/lib.rs declares 15
`pub const BTRFS_ITEM_*` u8 constants for the on-disk item-key
type field (inode_item, dir_item, dir_index, inode_ref, xattr_item,
extent_data, root_item, extent_item, metadata_item, block_group_item,
dev_item, chunk, free_space_info/extent/bitmap). Each one mirrors a
specific kernel macro from `fs/btrfs/btrfs_tree.h`, and the read-only
VFS path dispatches on these values (e.g., `entry.key.item_type ==
BTRFS_ITEM_ROOT_ITEM`).

But there is **no kernel-conformance test** pinning the values to
their canonical kernel macros. A regression that swapped, e.g.,
BTRFS_ITEM_DIR_ITEM (84) and BTRFS_ITEM_DIR_INDEX (96) would
silently mis-route every btrfs directory iteration: dir_index
entries would be parsed as dir_item entries (different key.offset
semantics: hash vs sequence-counter) and vice versa.

Pairs with bd-khzn4 (just-landed BTRFS_*_TREE_OBJECTID kernel
conformance test). Same shape as bd-k81lq (ext4 reserved-inode
constants) and bd-343v3 (ext4 file-type constants).

Acceptance: a kernel-conformance unit test in the existing tests
module of crates/ffs-btrfs/src/lib.rs that pins each of the 15
constants to its kernel-macro value, plus a strict-monotonic
sortedness invariant across the contiguous reserved range and a
boundary check that BTRFS_ITEM_FREE_SPACE_BITMAP (200) sits below
BTRFS_ITEM_DEV_ITEM (216) which is below BTRFS_ITEM_CHUNK (228).
notes: Shipped: kernel-conformance unit test btrfs_item_key_constants_match_kernel_header in crates/ffs-btrfs/src/lib.rs. title: lchmod follows symlinks: uses classic fchmodat syscall that drops AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW (chmods target)
close_reason:
FIXED — and the bug was LIVE. Source commit 166faf14f.

THE BLOCKER COMMENT ON THIS BEAD IS WRONG. It said: "superseded by e7e4e5765 (lchmod no longer
follows symlinks), with real host-glibc filesystem gate 246fbdcf3; current lchmod routes
AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW through fchmodat." Every clause is literally true and the conclusion is false.
lchmod DOES delegate to fchmodat with AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW, and fchmodat DID pass it to
syscall::sys_fchmodat — but the classic `fchmodat(2)` SYSCALL takes only THREE arguments. There is
no flags register. The kernel discarded the fourth argument and chmod'd the symlink's TARGET. This
is the fifth instance of the class AGENTS.md warns about (bd-02gcfy: 4 of the first 7 audited were
wrong), and it is the exact shape bd-cb59r9 named — the function survived while the rule inside it
died, one level below where the comment looked.

MEASURED AT HEAD, BEFORE ANY CHANGE:
  syscall(SYS_fchmodat, AT_FDCWD, <symlink>, 0707, AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW)
     -> rc=0, symlink TARGET mode 0644 -> 0707       (flag silently dropped)
  glibc lchmod(<symlink>, 0777)
     -> rc=-1 ENOTSUP, target unchanged at 0644      (correct behaviour)
And through fl's own entrypoints, via the new gate run against clean HEAD:
  fl  lchmod(symlink, 0777) -> rc=0,  errno=0,  target mode 0777
  glibc same call           -> rc=-1, errno=95 (ENOTSUP), target mode 0644
So fl was silently making symlink targets world-writable-ish (0777) on every lchmod. That is a
security-relevant divergence in ordinary application code, not a test-only problem.

FULL glibc CONTRACT MEASURED on a real filesystem (temp dir, real file + real symlink) and now
reproduced exactly:
  regular file, flags=0                 -> 0, mode applied
  regular file, AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW     -> 0, mode applied      <- must NOT over-reject
  symlink,      flags=0                 -> 0, TARGET modified (follows; correct)
  symlink,      AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW     -> -1 ENOTSUP, nothing modified
  any other flag bits                   -> -1 EINVAL, nothing modified

FIX (two parts):
1. crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs fchmodat now routes flag-bearing calls to the
   `fchmodat2(2)` syscall, which has a real flags argument and implements all five rows above
   natively. flags==0 stays on the classic syscall (universally available, identical in effect).
2. crates/frankenlibc-core/src/syscall/mod.rs sys_fchmodat's `flags: i32` parameter is REMOVED and
   the call switched to syscall3. That parameter is the whole reason this survived review: it made
   every call site LOOK correct while doing nothing. The signature can no longer lie. Its only
   other caller (chmod, which passed 0) is updated.

DIVERGENCE STATED, NOT HIDDEN: on pre-6.6 kernels without fchmodat2, this returns ENOTSUP where
glibc reaches "regular file + AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW" through /proc/self/fd and succeeds. I chose to
fail CLOSED rather than fall back to the flagless syscall (which would silently follow the symlink
again — the very defect) and rather than lstat-then-chmod (racy in precisely the security-sensitive
case). The test host runs 6.17, so the fchmodat2 path is the one exercised.

GATE: new crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/conformance_diff_fchmodat_nofollow.rs. No mocks — each case
builds a real file (0644) and a real symlink in a temp dir, runs glibc and fl on byte-identical
trees, and compares the return contract AND the resulting on-disk mode. Three arms: the five-case
fchmodat matrix, an lchmod differential, and a standalone invariant
(fchmodat_nofollow_never_touches_the_symlink_target) that does NOT depend on fl==glibc, so a joint
regression still fails. The "regular file + NOFOLLOW must SUCCEED" row is load-bearing in the other
direction: a fix that rejected every flag-bearing call would satisfy the symlink rows and be just as
wrong.

  WITH THE FIX:
    cargo test -j 2 -p frankenlibc-abi --test conformance_diff_fchmodat_nofollow
    test fchmodat_symlink_nofollow_matches_glibc ... ok
    test fchmodat_nofollow_never_touches_the_symlink_target ... ok
    test lchmod_matches_glibc_and_spares_the_target ... ok
    test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  CONTROL — clean HEAD, gate overlaid but fix EXCLUDED
  (rch exec --base HEAD --clean-overlay -o crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/conformance_diff_fchmodat_nofollow.rs):
    test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 3 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
    "fchmodat(AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW) on a symlink modified its TARGET (0644 -> 0707); the flag was dropped"
    "lchmod(symlink): fl=(rc=0,errno=0,mode=0777) glibc=(rc=-1,errno=95,mode=0644)"

REGRESSION CHECKS: glibc_internal_abi_test 272 passed; 0 failed; 24 ignored.
cargo check -p frankenlibc-core -p frankenlibc-abi --all-targets --keep-going gives the SAME broken
target set as clean HEAD (math_survey, qsort_radix_vs_stdlib_bench, nss_cache_policy_test — all
pre-existing dark bench-hook targets). One extra name appeared only in my run,
zz_scratch_divmin, which is a GITIGNORED scratch file (.gitignore:218 `**/tests/zz_*.rs`) present in
the rch-synced working tree but absent from the git baseline; its errors are CDiv/CLdiv missing
Debug/PartialEq, unrelated to this change, and it never reaches CI. fmt clean.

The cited gate 246fbdcf3 was not the protection the comment implied: nothing in the tree compared
the symlink target's mode before and after, which is why a flag that was never delivered looked
fine for months. That comparison is now the gate's core assertion.

No unrelated user or agent changes were stashed, reverted, or deleted.
