title: Refine xfstests preflight with remediation safety and no-auto-install guarantees
description:
Supplemental refinement for bd-rchk3.1.1. The xfstests prerequisite preflight should help operators fix missing host capability, but it must not auto-install packages, mutate host mount state, or imply a lane is authoritative before the operator has provisioned it. This bead turns preflight remediation into explicit, safe guidance.

Scope: define preflight remediation output for missing packages, helper binaries, FUSE permission, mount namespace support, scratch/test directories, dpkg lock state, RCH worker mismatch, and unsupported local hosts. Remediation may print commands or links, but default validation must be read-only and side-effect free.

Required proof before close:
1. Unit/script tests cover remediation classification for missing headers/libs, missing xfstests helpers, missing mkfs helpers, /dev/fuse absence, fusermount permission failure, dpkg lock, non-root mount denial, unavailable scratch/test roots, RCH worker mismatch, and intentionally unsupported local lane.
2. Tests prove preflight does not run package installation, does not mount/unmount real filesystems, does not create persistent host directories outside controlled temp paths, and does not mark remediation as complete without a fresh follow-up probe.
3. E2E/dry-run smoke uses fixture host states to emit remediation manifests and verifies every blocking item has user-action text, risk level, authoritative-lane impact, and reproduction command.
4. Logs include preflight id, probe version, host/kernel, worker id if any, prerequisite id, observed value, classification, remediation text id, side-effect policy, output paths, cleanup status, and reproduction command.
5. xfstests coverage claims remain blocked or host-skipped until a fresh side-effect-free preflight proves the prerequisites are present in the intended authoritative lane.
close_reason: Completed xfstests remediation safety refinement: preflight rows now include preflight/probe ids, observed values, safe guidance with no package-manager/install/mount/persistent-path authority, fresh-follow-up-probe claim state, and fixture coverage for missing tooling, permission denial, dpkg lock, worker mismatch, and unsupported local lanes

title: feat(iconv): ISO-2022-CN/JP/JP-2/JP-3 stateful codecs + UTF-7-IMAP
description: Stateful escape-sequence codecs fl rejects (ISO-2022-JP/CN-EXT are in PHASE1_EXCLUDED_CODEC_FAMILIES): ISO-2022-CN, ISO-2022-JP-2, ISO-2022-JP-3, ISO-2022-JP (excluded), and UTF-7-IMAP (modified base64 UTF-7 per RFC 3501, '&' shift not '+'). notes: ISO-2022-JP-3 SCOPED + de-risked (cc, 2026-06-16): now BUILDABLE next turn. SHIFT_JISX0213 (1127ed119) + EUC-JISX0213 (c68881ced) shipped this turn (byte-exact), so the JIS X 0213 plane tables EXIST (eucjisx0213_tables::EUCJX_P1/P2/P1_MULTI). Multi-cp combining via EUCJX_P1_MULTI. ENCODE PRIORITY (probe-verified): ASCII>JIS-Roman(¥/‾)>JIS X 0208(emit ESC$B, use encode_eucjp codeset1 ku-ten)>0213 plane1(emit ESC$(O — the 2000 designator! — use EUCJX_ENC 2-byte ku-ten)>plane2(emit ESC$(P, EUCJX_ENC 3-byte 0x8F form ku-ten); combining seqs munch→ESC$(O. 日本→ESC$B (0208 preferred); か゚→ESC$(O 2477; U+20089→ESC$(P 2121. Build = model decode on iso2022jp_decode (escape 3/4-byte lookahead + literal-ESC recovery) + the iso2022jp2-style encode priority. title: [bug][RED][stdio] funopen stream reads back 0 bytes after write+fseek: funopen_round_trips_write_seek_read fails at clean HEAD
description:
RED at clean HEAD, found while gating bd-xmlbtg. Untracked until now.

  cargo test -j2 -p frankenlibc-abi --test stdio_abi_test -- --exact funopen_round_trips_write_seek_read

FAILS ALONE, so it is not cross-test interference:
  test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 300 filtered out
  panicked at crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/stdio_abi_test.rs:6381
  assertion `left == right` failed
    left: 0
   right: 10

Confirmed pre-existing on a CLEAN baseline (rch exec --base HEAD --clean-overlay --no-overlay,
worker vmi1156319), and reproduced on worker hz1 with the working tree, so it is neither a
working-tree artifact nor worker-specific.

THE SEQUENCE, from the test body:
  funopen(state, read, write, seek, close)   -> stream
  fwrite("funopen-rw", 1, 10, stream)        -> 10   (ok)
  fseek(stream, 0, SEEK_SET)                 -> 0    (ok)
  fread(out, 1, 10, stream)                  -> 0    <-- SHOULD BE 10
So the write and the seek both report success and the read returns end-of-data immediately. The
bytes are in the caller's cookie state (the test's final assertions check `s.data == payload` after
fclose), so the defect is in the READ path of a funopen/BSD-cookie stream after a seek, not in the
write path.

LIKELY SHAPE, unverified: either the seek does not reach the cookie's seek callback (so the cookie
is still positioned at EOF when the read runs), or the buffered read path short-circuits on a stale
end-of-data flag set by the preceding write and never calls the cookie read callback at all. Check
whether fseek on a cookie stream clears the EOF/read-buffer state the way it does for fd streams,
and whether the write is flushed to the cookie before the seek.

NEGATIVE CASE any fix must pass: the existing arm already encodes it -- fread must return 10 and the
bytes must equal the payload. Do NOT relax it to accept a short read. Add a companion case that
writes, seeks to a NON-zero offset, and reads, so a fix that only special-cases offset 0 fails.

RELATED: fopencookie has its own open bead (bd-bpac6v, write-through vs buffered). funopen and
fopencookie share the cookie-stream machinery in stdio_abi.rs (is_cookie_stream / flush_cookie_stream
/ cookie_stream_close), so check whether one fix covers both before doing them separately.
close_reason: Fixed in 74b49032a: cookie writes are buffered, and fseek repositioned without flushing them, so the cookie was empty when the read ran. The pre-existing arm (RED at clean HEAD on vmi1156319 and RED alone) is now green, plus a new non-zero-offset companion so a rewind-only fix would fail. hz1: whole stdio_abi_test file 259 passed / 0 failed, up from 257 passed / 1 failed.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FIXED AND CLOSED: commit 74b49032a, worker hz1.

ROOT CAUSE. Cookie writes are BUFFERED -- fputs/fwrite on a cookie stream go through cookie_buffer_write into the stream's pending buffer, not straight to the caller's write callback. The cookie branch of fseek then repositioned WITHOUT flushing that buffer. So at the moment of the read the caller's write callback had never run, the cookie was still empty, and fread correctly reported 0 bytes.

THIS BEAD'S GUESS WAS CLOSE BUT NOT RIGHT. I wrote 'either the seek does not reach the cookie seek callback, or the read short-circuits on a stale EOF flag'. It was neither: the seek callback runs fine and no EOF flag is involved. The missing step was the flush BEFORE the seek. Worth recording because the symptom (read returns 0 immediately) points at the read path, and the defect is in the write path.

WHY IT SURVIVED THIS LONG: fclose flushes, so the arm's final assertion state.data == payload passed. The contents were always right at the end; only the intermediate read return value was wrong. An arm that checked contents only, without checking the read count, would still be green today.

FIX: flush_cookie_stream under the cell lock before cookie_stream_seek, reporting EIO if the flush fails rather than seeking anyway. glibc flushes output before repositioning, and C requires this seek between a write and a read on the same stream.

GATE, both directions:
  funopen_round_trips_write_seek_read -- the pre-existing arm, RED at clean HEAD (vmi1156319, --base HEAD --clean-overlay --no-overlay, and RED run alone) -- now green.
  funopen_reads_back_from_a_nonzero_offset_after_write -- NEW, added per this bead's own instruction: seeks to offset 4 rather than 0 so a fix that only special-cases rewind fails, and asserts the bytes are the payload's tail rather than just counting them.
  worker hz1, cargo test -j2 -p frankenlibc-abi --test stdio_abi_test: funopen filter 4 passed / 0 failed; whole file 259 passed / 0 failed / 44 ignored, up from 257 passed / 1 failed.

RELATED, unchanged: bd-bpac6v describes fopencookie streams as write-through. That is not what the code does -- cookie_buffer_write buffers and flush_cookie_stream drains -- so whoever takes bd-bpac6v should re-verify its premise against the source before acting on it.

title: [FUZZ-GAP] extend fuzz_mvcc_operations to cover commit_ssi, commit_fcw_prechecked, stage_write_with_proof, SafeMerge policy
description:
# Fuzz coverage gap — MVCC advanced commit paths

## Current coverage

`fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_mvcc_operations.rs` exercises:
- `MvccStore::begin`
- `Transaction::stage_write` (plain)
- `MvccStore::commit` (generic)
- `MvccStore::current_snapshot` + `read_visible`
- `MvccStore::prune_safe`

## Gap

The README's signature claim is that FrankenFS has 'adaptive conflict policy (Strict/SafeMerge/Adaptive with expected-loss decision model).' The *policy selection* lives on these APIs, which are not exercised by the current fuzz harness:

- `Transaction::stage_write_with_proof(block, bytes, proof)` — line 324 of ffs-mvcc/src/lib.rs. Carries the `MergeProof` that SafeMerge relies on. No fuzz driver produces proofs or feeds them through commit.
- `MvccStore::commit_ssi(txn)` — line 1528. Serializable-snapshot-isolation commit path.
- `MvccStore::commit_fcw_prechecked(txn)` — line 1478. Strict first-committer-wins with caller-supplied pre-check.
- `MvccStore::resolved_writes_for_commit(txn)` — line 1500. Drives the conflict-resolution arbiter that selects Strict vs SafeMerge.
- `MvccStore::commit_with_cow_allocator(...)` / `commit_ssi_with_cow_allocator(...)` — COW-integrated commits.
- `MvccStore::set_conflict_policy(ConflictPolicy::{Strict, SafeMerge, Adaptive})` + `adaptive_config` — policy switches.

## Why this matters

The README documents a 120-writer stress test proving 'SafeMerge achieved 9.5x lower expected loss than Strict' — this is one of the project's signature differentiators. But the fuzz suite currently only drives the plain `commit` path; adversarial inputs to the SSI / FCW-pre-checked / merge-proof paths would surface policy-selection edge cases (e.g., conflict detection misses, merge-proof-shaped corrupt inputs, adaptive-policy thrashing under pathological interleavings).

## Scope

Extend `fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_mvcc_operations.rs` (or split into a new `fuzz_mvcc_commit_policies.rs` if the harness grows) to:

1. Randomly flip `ConflictPolicy` on the store during the sequence.
2. Generate occasional `MergeProof` values (valid + malformed) and call `stage_write_with_proof`.
3. Route commits through `commit` / `commit_ssi` / `commit_fcw_prechecked` according to a fuzz-chosen arm.
4. After each commit, invariants:
   - Commit seq strictly monotonic on success.
   - `read_visible(block, snapshot_before_commit)` never sees post-commit bytes.
   - `read_visible(block, snapshot_after_commit)` sees post-commit bytes for visible blocks.
   - Adaptive policy decision remains consistent with `effective_policy()` reporting.
5. Seed corpus: single-writer, two-writer conflict on same block, non-overlapping concurrent writes, merge-proof with wrong seq, prune-between-commits sequence.

## Acceptance

- Target drives `commit`, `commit_ssi`, `commit_fcw_prechecked` with frequency proportional to a fuzzable selector byte.
- Policy toggles exercised (`Strict` / `SafeMerge` / `Adaptive`).
- `stage_write_with_proof` called at least in one branch.
- Invariant assertions use `assert!`; all assertions hold on current implementation (regression baseline).
- Exec/s ≥ 500 (stateful harness floor per /testing-fuzzing skill rules).
close_reason: Implemented in commit fec9579: fuzz_mvcc_operations extended to drive commit_ssi/commit_fcw_prechecked/stage_write_with_proof with I1-I4 invariants + seed_policy_commit_paths corpus.

title: Add differential gate for fgetpwent (parse passwd entries from caller FILE*) vs glibc — only fl-internal
[bug][crypt] fl $1$/$5$/$6$ hashes diverge byte-for-byte from host libxcrypt
description:
conformance_diff_crypt.rs's header says fl's modern-method crypt output 'DIVERGE byte-for-byte from
host libcrypt on every input' and calls it 'a serious cross-compatibility issue (passwords hashed by
glibc do not validate under fl, and vice versa)'. The header states the gap was 'filed as bead'. I
searched the open beads for crypt and found bd-c6ykz1 (MISSING schemes: yescrypt/bcrypt/scrypt),
bd-c1gtzh (crypt_r has no gate), bd-iu39zz (crypt_checksalt classification), bd-wa0cpo (crypt_gensalt
has no gate) — none of which is this. So the claim appears to be wrong and the gap was untracked.
Filing it so it is not carried indefinitely by a comment.

STATUS: the divergence is captured by report_crypt_divergences_against_host in that file, which is
#[ignore]d with the reason 'fl crypt hashes diverge from glibc — known parity gap'. Run with
--ignored to dump the full diff.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A NORMAL PARITY BEAD: crypt output is PERSISTED. A hash written into
/etc/shadow by glibc will not validate under fl and vice versa, so this is not a transient
formatting difference — it is a data-compatibility break for anything that stores password hashes.
The three affected methods ($1$ MD5, $5$ SHA-256, $6$ SHA-512) are the ones actually in use on
existing systems.

CONTEXT FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT: until cbf91fd06 this whole gate did not even LINK on the rch fleet
(#[link(name = "crypt")] needs the libcrypt.so dev symlink, which the workers lack), so the two
smoke arms were not running either. That is fixed; the ignored differential arm is the remaining
work.

DONE = report_crypt_divergences_against_host un-ignored and green, i.e. fl's $1$/$5$/$6$ output
byte-identical to host libxcrypt, with a quoted non-zero passed count. Do NOT close this by widening
the comparison — the whole point is byte-for-byte equality of a persisted credential.
close_reason:
DONE. report_crypt_divergences_against_host un-ignored (now crypt_matches_host_libxcrypt_byte_for_byte) and GREEN at 3a6071f7c.

EVIDENCE (rch remote, at HEAD):
  cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test conformance_diff_crypt
  test crypt_matches_host_libxcrypt_byte_for_byte ... ok
  test fl_crypt_rejects_malformed_rounds_fields ... ok
  test result: ok. 4 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  cargo test -p frankenlibc-core --lib crypt::
  test result: ok. 60 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 3163 filtered out

PREMISE CORRECTED. The bead (quoting the file header) said fl's $1$/$5$/$6$ output 'DIVERGE byte-for-byte from host libcrypt on every input'. Running the ignored arm at HEAD refuted that: 13 of 15 cases were ALREADY byte-identical, and the 2 that were not differed only in the setting PREFIX, never in the digest:
  fl:    $5$saltsaltsalt$/N7c7rmQ...        (rounds= dropped)
  glibc: $5$rounds=5000$saltsaltsalt$/N7c7rmQ...
The digest/transposition/base64 work had already been fixed under bd-9n50f2; only the header was stale.

TWO DEFECTS FIXED (1a8260f2e, 3a6071f7c):
1. rounds= echo. fl re-emitted the prefix when rounds != 5000; libxcrypt re-emits it whenever the INPUT setting carried one, so $5$rounds=5000$s$ round-trips with its prefix. parse_crypt_salt now returns ShaCryptSetting{rounds, rounds_custom, salt}.
2. rounds= validation. fl CLAMPED out-of-range counts into [1000,999999999] and fell back to 5000 for unparseable fields, so a malformed setting still minted a hash the host will never reproduce. Live libxcrypt REJECTS every deviation with *0/EINVAL. Probed on this host (key=password):
  rounds=1000$x$ / =1001 / =4999   -> accepted, errno=0
  rounds=999$x$                    -> *0 errno=22 (below min)
  rounds=1000000000$x$             -> *0 errno=22 (above max)
  rounds=0500$x$                   -> *0 errno=22 (leading zero)
  rounds=+5000 / = 5000 / =-1 / =abc / =$ -> *0 errno=22
  rounds=99999999999999999999999$x$ -> *0 errno=22 (overflow)
  rounds=5000x$ / =12345 / =5000    -> *0 errno=22 (no closing $)
All 14 now in the differential set; each is byte-identical to the host.

SCOPE NOT WIDENED. The comparison is still exact CStr byte equality over the whole returned string. crypt_diff_coverage_report used to ASSERT divergences were non-empty — a lock that would have failed on the fix; it now only reports.

FLAKE FOUND AND FIXED. crypt(3) returns STATIC storage; two libtest threads walking the case table reported '10 of 30 diverge' on a build whose real count was zero. Host calls are now serialized under a mutex; 3 consecutive full runs green.

ALSO ADDED: known-answer vectors in core::crypt::{md5,sha256,sha512} captured from live libcrypt.so.1, so a digest/transposition/base64 regression fails in-crate without needing the host present.

PRE-EXISTING, NOT MINE: conformance_diff_crypt_gensalt still fails to LINK (undefined symbol crypt_gensalt) — that is bd-wa0cpo's dark gate. cargo check -p frankenlibc-core -p frankenlibc-abi --all-targets --keep-going has the SAME 4 failing targets with and without this change (math_survey, qsort_radix_vs_stdlib_bench, nss_cache_policy_test, zz_scratch_divmin), verified by stashing.

title: [RED] sscanf %mc returns 0 where glibc returns -1 (EOF/no-conversion)
description:
conformance_diff_scanf_malloc::scanf_m_modifier_matches_glibc is RED at clean HEAD (verified with
--base HEAD --clean-overlay --no-overlay; unrelated to e861f2893).

  sscanf('ab', '%5mc') [%mc]: fl=(0, [])  glibc=(-1, [])

glibc returns -1 (EOF / no conversion performed) while fl returns 0. The distinction matters: a
caller loop of the form 'while (sscanf(...) > 0)' behaves the same, but code testing '== EOF' to
distinguish input exhaustion from a matching failure sees the wrong answer. Both allocate nothing,
so this is a return-value contract bug, not a memory bug.

Worth checking the width interaction while here: the directive is '%5mc' -- a width WITH %m -- so
whether the divergence is about %mc generally or specifically about a width applied to it should be
established before fixing.

DONE = that gate green with a quoted non-zero passed count.
close_reason:
FIXED, but this bead's PREMISE WAS WRONG and the correction matters more than the fix. Commit f7dfb955d. Gate conformance_diff_scanf_malloc: FAILED -> 'test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out'.

WHAT I FILED: 'sscanf(ab, %5mc): fl=(0,[]) glibc=(-1,[])', described as a return-value contract bug
where glibc reports EOF and fl reports 0.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE: glibc returns 1 having read 'ab'. Its %Nc reads what IS available and
succeeds. fl's NARROW path demanded the full width and failed the conversion — that was the defect.
The '-1' in this bead came from my misreading an earlier truncated failure line, and I wrote it into
the bead without re-deriving it.

CONSEQUENCE OF TRUSTING MY OWN NOTE: I implemented the bead as written first, teaching the engine to
report EOF on a short %c read. That moved fl from 0 to -1 while glibc was returning 1 — a wrong fix
built on a wrong premise. The gate rejected it immediately, which is the only reason it did not
land. That attempt is reverted and is not in the commit.

WHAT SETTLED IT was the gate's own header: 'fl had no m modifier ... and its narrow %Nc required the
full width to be present (failing where glibc reads what is available)'. The correct contract was
written in the file I was already looking at. Reading the harness before theorising would have
skipped the wrong fix entirely — the same lesson as bd-vxrku8, where I trusted a stale COMMENT over
a measurement. Here I trusted a stale NOTE OF MY OWN, which is worse, because a bead I wrote reads
as authoritative to me.

THE REAL DEFECT, now fixed: scan_char's two halves disagreed. The WIDE branch already clamped to the
available input, and its comment says so; the narrow branch required the full width. Both now clamp,
and only a total absence of input is a failure. That also answers this bead's own open question —
the divergence was about width generally, not about %m: %5c and %5mc share the path.

NO REGRESSION: sscanf_char_differential_fuzz 1 passed; conformance_diff_swscanf 3 passed (the wide
path this now matches); conformance_diff_scanf_scanset 1 passed; conformance_diff_scanf_hexfloat 1
passed; sscanf_float_edge_differential_test 1 passed; sscanf_differential_fuzz 1 passed;
sscanf_scanset_differential_fuzz 1 passed; conformance_diff_strtod_edges 1 passed. fmt clean.

title: [bug][math] setpayload family truncates non-integer payloads, accepts NaN, and skips the +0.0 write on failure
description:
conformance_diff_payload was RED at HEAD (sweep bd-aykfv1), untracked. 30 divergences.

  setpayload(1.5)   fl ret0 res=0x7ff8000000000001   glibc ret1 res=0x0000000000000000
  setpayload(42.7)  fl ret0 res=0x7ff800000000002a   glibc ret1 res=0x0000000000000000
  setpayload(qNaN)  fl ret0 res=0x7ff8000000000000   glibc ret1 res=0x0000000000000000
  setpayload(-1.0)  fl ret1 res=UNTOUCHED            glibc ret1 res=0x0000000000000000

THREE DEFECTS, all four impls (setpayload/setpayloadf/setpayloadsig/setpayloadsigf), all from one line — 'let p = payload as u64' followed by testing p:
  1. The cast TRUNCATES. 1.5 became payload 1 and 42.7 became 42, both returning SUCCESS, so a caller silently got a NaN it never asked for.
  2. The cast SATURATES a NaN to 0, which then passed the range check, so a NaN payload was accepted outright.
  3. On failure fl returned without touching *res. glibc writes +0.0 on every failing path.
Additionally '-0.0' slipped through, because 'payload < 0.0' is false for it.

GROUND TRUTH from the host — valid iff a NON-NEGATIVE INTEGER strictly below 2^51 (2^22 for f32), with -0.0 rejected despite comparing equal to zero:
  setpayload(0.0)    ret 0  res 0x7ff8000000000000
  setpayload(1.0)    ret 0  res 0x7ff8000000000001
  setpayload(42.0)   ret 0  res 0x7ff800000000002a
  setpayload(2^51-1) ret 0  res 0x7fffffffffffffff
  setpayload(1.5 / 42.7 / -1.0 / -0.0 / 2^51 / inf / nan) ret 1  res 0x0000000000000000

FIXED at the commit citing this bead: one shared payload_value_f64/f32 validator — sign bit clear, finite, integral, in range — used by all four impls, with the +0.0 write on every failure path. The *sig* variants additionally require a non-zero payload, since with the quiet bit clear a zero mantissa is an infinity rather than a NaN.

Integrality is checked through core's trunc rather than f64::trunc: the latter lowers to the 'trunc' symbol, which in the shipped libc.so is fl's own — the self-interposition hazard documented on core's log2f.
close_reason:
DONE at 37514f38b.

EVIDENCE:
  cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test conformance_diff_payload
  test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out   (30 divergences before)
  cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test conformance_diff_nextup_canon
  test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test conformance_diff_math_exact
  test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test math_abi_test
  test result: ok. 118 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  cargo check -p frankenlibc-abi -p frankenlibc-core --all-targets --keep-going: same 4 pre-existing failing targets as the baseline.

THREE DEFECTS FROM ONE LINE. All four impls read 'let p = payload as u64' and then tested p, which meant:
  - the cast TRUNCATED a non-integer, so setpayload(1.5) returned SUCCESS with payload 1 and setpayload(42.7) with payload 42 — a caller silently received a NaN it never requested;
  - the cast SATURATED a NaN to 0, which then passed the range check, so a NaN payload was accepted outright;
  - and every failure path returned without touching *res, where glibc writes +0.0.
'-0.0' also slipped through because 'payload < 0.0' is false for it. The lesson is narrow and reusable: validating a float by casting it to an integer and checking the integer discards exactly the information that makes the input invalid.

GROUND TRUTH taken from the host before any change — valid iff a non-negative INTEGER strictly below 2^51 (2^22 for f32), -0.0 rejected despite comparing equal to zero, +0.0 written on every failure. The full table is in the source next to the validator.

FIX: one shared payload_value_f64/f32 (sign bit clear, finite, integral, in range) used by all four impls, with the +0.0 write on each failure path. The *sig* variants additionally require a non-zero payload, because with the quiet bit clear a zero mantissa is an infinity rather than a NaN — a rule the old code happened to have right and which is preserved explicitly rather than by accident.

AVOIDED A KNOWN TRAP: integrality is checked via core's trunc, not f64::trunc. The latter lowers to the 'trunc' symbol, which in the shipped libc.so is fl's own — the self-interposition hazard documented on core's log2f. Writing the check the obvious way would have been correct in the test binary and recursive in the shipped library.

No new gate: conformance_diff_payload already encoded the host's answers across the whole family and was red before, green after.

bytes; we can parse them once and reuse the resulting Ext4GroupDesc
for the encode bench.

`bench_ext4_group_desc_write_64` to ondisk_parse.rs, register them in

title: printf: %e/%E produces wrong digits at high precision (mantissa recomputed with FP error)
description: printf.rs format_e computes mantissa = value / 10.powi(exp) then formats that errored mantissa, so %.17e of 123456789.0 gave 1.23456788999999989e+08 vs glibc 1.23456789000000000e+08. Propagates into %g/%G e-style. Fix: use Rust's correctly-rounded {:.Ne} formatting and translate the exponent to C's e+dd form. Differential-tested against host glibc.
close_reason: Rewrote printf.rs format_e to use Rust's correctly-rounded {:.Ne} formatting instead of value/10^exp, fixing wrong digits past ~15 sig figs (%.17e of 123456789.0 now 1.23456789000000000e+08). conformance_diff_stdio_printf 7/7 pass; new test test_e_high_precision_exact_digits.

title: fix(ptrace): PEEK requests returned 0/faulted instead of the peeked word
description: ptrace's PEEKTEXT/PEEKDATA/PEEKUSER (requests 1-3) were broken: the Linux ptrace syscall writes the peeked word via the data pointer and returns 0, but the C API expects the word as the RETURN value. fl passed the caller's data (NULL for PEEK) straight to the syscall (kernel writes to NULL -> EFAULT) and returned the syscall result (0). glibc redirects data to a local, returns that word, and clears errno (word may be -1). Fixed to mirror glibc. Gate conformance_diff_ptrace_peek (fork self-tracing child, PEEKDATA a known global via fl vs glibc, graceful skip if ptrace restricted).
close_reason: Shipped: ptrace PEEKTEXT/DATA/USER now redirect data to a local and return the peeked word (errno cleared), matching glibc — was passing caller NULL data through (EFAULT) and returning 0. Gate conformance_diff_ptrace_peek (fork+TRACEME+PEEKDATA differential vs live glibc).

title: fuzz: no dedicated fuzz target for ext4 *_extra timestamp bit-pack contract
description:
Finding (via /testing-fuzzing skill, NEW target): fuzz/fuzz_targets has 49 targets but NONE dedicated to the Ext4Inode::extra_nsec / extra_epoch bit-pack contract. The newly-shipped bd-834zk proptest (32 cases) pins the [nsec:30][epoch:2] u32 layout; a libfuzzer target lifts that to >1M iterations/session with corpus learning across mask-edge u32 values, sign-bit boundaries, and pathological bit patterns.

The bit-pack helpers are on the hot path for every inode timestamp read on ext4 v6+ filesystems. A regression that swapped the masks (epoch ⇔ nsec) would silently corrupt every timestamp on every ext4 image — invisible to substring tests.

Acceptance: new fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_ext4_extra_bit_pack.rs that, for arbitrary u32 input, asserts:
  * MR1 — Bit-pack inverse: (extra_nsec(x) << 2) | extra_epoch(x) == x
  * MR2 — Epoch bound: extra_epoch(x) ≤ 3
  * MR3 — Nsec bound: extra_nsec(x) ≤ 0x3FFFFFFF
  * MR4 — Disjoint encoding: extra_nsec(epoch_only) == 0 and extra_epoch(nsec_only) == 0
  * MR5 — Never panics on any u32
Plus a [[bin]] entry in fuzz/Cargo.toml.

title: PORT: unvis (NetBSD vis(3) streaming byte decoder)
description: NetBSD vis(3) streaming decoder unvis(*cp, c, *astate, flag) — single-byte state-machine inverse of vis(3). Caller feeds bytes one at a time; the function returns UNVIS_VALID (1) when *cp holds a fully decoded byte, UNVIS_VALIDPUSH (2) when *cp is decoded AND the current input byte should be re-fed, UNVIS_NOCHAR (3) for partial sequences, UNVIS_SYNBAD (-1) for malformed input. The opaque *astate carries decoder state across calls. Used by mtree, BSD pkg tools, and anything needing a streaming decoder rather than the all-at-once strunvis. Currently missing entirely from frankenlibc-abi. Ship: pure-safe core::stdio::vis::UnvisDecoder state machine + thin abi shim that maps the i32 state cell to/from the typed enum.

title: perf: fused single-pass f32 powf kernel to beat glibc (general path still ~3.9x slower after f64 exp/ln route)
description: Follow-up to bd-z8p3mx. The general powf path now routes through exp(y*ln(x)) in f64 (fl's fast f64 exp/log), measured 1.4-1.6x faster than the prior libm::powf fallback (powf_glibc_bench on ovh-a: general_big_e fl 30.85ns vs fl_old 44.77ns vs glibc 7.89ns). But fl is STILL ~3.9x slower than glibc because exp(y*ln(x)) is TWO f64 transcendentals (~15ns each) for one f32 result, vs glibc's single FUSED f32 powf kernel (~8ns: table-based log + reduce + table-based exp with double-double precision). The f64 intermediate is required for general-range accuracy (rounding y*log2(x) to f32 before a fast f32 exp2f exceeds 4 ULP for large |y*log2 x| — which is why powf_medium_fast_path is bounded to base[0.5,2.5)/exp[-3,3]). LEVER: port a fused single-pass f32 powf (glibc __ieee754_powf / e_powf, or the Arm-optimized __v_powf with 2^7-entry log+exp tables + a double-precision reduction) so one pass produces the f32 result. Same kernel also closes the medium_ref residual (fl 18.64ns vs glibc 7.82ns, the existing exp2f/log2f medium path). Must hold <=4 ULP vs glibc (gate conformance_diff_powf_general already covers the general domain; extend with the medium box). Big swing, accuracy-critical. bench: powf_glibc_bench (reuse). Evidence: tests/artifacts/perf/bd-z8p3mx-powf-general-f64-route.md.

title: perf: port ARM fused f64 pow/exp/log kernels for the general case (f64 pow general still = libm::pow)
description: Extend the proven f32 fused-kernel recipe (bd-z8p3mx + bd-fused-f32-exp-log-kernels, ALL CLOSED: powf/exp2f/log2f/expf/logf now glibc-class bit-exact, 4 WINs + powf near-parity) to the DOUBLE-precision family. frankenlibc-core/src/math/exp.rs: f64 pow (line ~992) has a pow_profile_exp_1_337 overfit + small-int fast paths then defers GENERAL case to libm::pow; f64 exp2 = libm::exp2 (pure); f64 log2 uses log2_kernel (already fast, beats glibc per bd-e4jb7k). RECIPE (memory powf-fused-kernel-and-math-overfit): curl raw ARM optimized-routines math/pow.c + exp.c + log.c + their _data.c (pow uses __pow_log_data 128-entry table + __exp_data 128-entry table; LARGER than f32, ~256+ doubles + polys). Faithful wrapping arith; guard to normal domain, defer overflow/underflow/special to libm for FE/errno; keep correctly-rounded int-exponent fast path ahead. f64 pow needs hi/lo (double-double) log + the exp with the same. Validate LOCALLY vs host glibc 2.42 (model conformance_diff_powf_general -> a f64 version), measure on rch (reuse powf_glibc_bench pattern with f64 arms). EFFORT: larger than f32 (bigger tables, double-double arithmetic in pow) but HIGH VALUE (f64 pow/exp/log are hot). Expect general f64 pow LOSS->parity bit-exact. Order: pow first (highest use), then exp2/exp10 if libm-backed. GOTCHA: pow.c uses TOINT_INTRINSICS variants -- use the portable (non-TOINT) branch like the f32 ports.

title: conformance_diff_c23_narrow: 4 of 6 double-rounding witnesses are INERT (cannot fail) — construct real ones for fmul/fdiv/fsqrt
description:
conformance_diff_c23_narrow carries a hand-constructed 'double-rounding witness' per op. Measured 2026-08-06 against live glibc AND against the naive expression each witness exists to discriminate:

  fadd  witness  DISCRIMINATES
  ffma  witness  DISCRIMINATES
  fsub  witness  INERT   glibc 0x3f800000 == naive 0x3f800000
  fmul  witness  INERT   glibc 0x3f800001 == naive 0x3f800001
  fdiv  witness  INERT   glibc 0x3eaaaaab == naive 0x3eaaaaab
  fsqrt witness  INERT   glibc 0x3fb504f3 == naive 0x3fb504f3

Four of six produce the same bits whether the implementation single-rounds or double-rounds, so they cannot fail. This is not hypothetical: nine narrowing entry points (faddl fdiv fdivl fmul fmull fsqrt fsqrtl fsub fsubl) sat as plain double-rounding casts for six weeks with this gate green, and only fadd and ffma — the two with discriminating witnesses — were ever caught.

A replacement fsub witness has landed in 2a4119b5d:
  fsub(1 + 2^-24, -2^-60)   glibc 0x3f800001   naive 0x3f800000

DONE = discriminating witnesses for fmul, fdiv and fsqrt, each accompanied by the measured glibc bits AND the measured naive-double-rounding bits so the reader can see it can fail. Then verify by construction: temporarily revert the op to '(x OP y) as f32', watch the gate go RED, restore.

They must be CONSTRUCTED, not sampled: 400k random probes found none, because double rounding only bites when the f64 result lands exactly on an f32 midpoint (a 25-significant-bit value), which is measure-zero under random sampling. Build inputs whose exact result falls strictly between an f32 midpoint m and m + 2^-53 relative, so f64 rounds down to m (an f32 tie, resolved to even) while the exact value rounds up.

GENERAL RULE this is an instance of: a test named for a property must be shown capable of failing that property. Same family as bd-1l9rlp (a gate that passes on zero tests).
close_reason:
FIXED. Source commit b367a3cf7. All three inert witnesses replaced with constructed, discriminating
ones, each verified by construction exactly as this bead demanded.

THE WITNESSES, with the measured glibc bits AND the measured naive-double-rounding bits, which is
what the bead asked for so the reader can see they can fail. In all three the target f32 midpoint is
m = 1 + 2^-24 (halfway between 1.0 and 1+2^-23), glibc gives 0x3f800001, naive gives 0x3f800000:

  fmul   x = 0x3ff000000fffffff  (1 + 2^-24 - 2^-52)
         y = 0x3ff0000000000001  (1 + 2^-52)
         exact = m + 2^-76 - 2^-104   (inside the band, above m)
  fdiv   x = 0x3ff0000010800002
         y = 0x3ff0000000800001
  fsqrt  x = 0x3ff0000020000011      (just above m^2, so sqrt lands just above m)

METHOD — constructed, not sampled, per the bead's instruction. Double rounding differs from single
rounding only when the exact result lies strictly between an f32 midpoint m and m + ulp_f64(m)/2:
rounding to f64 then lands exactly ON m, which is an f32 tie resolved to the EVEN neighbour (1.0),
while correctly rounding the exact value goes up (1+2^-23). Derived with exact rational arithmetic
(Python Fractions, round-half-to-even implemented at both 24 and 53 bits) and then CONFIRMED against
live glibc via libm.so.6 — glibc returned the correctly-rounded value in every case, so the
witnesses are anchored to the oracle and not merely to my own rounding code.

WHY fdiv WAS THE HARD ONE, recorded because it explains why the original fdiv(1, 3) was inert and
why a naive search fails. For y near 1, y*m sits just ABOVE an f64 grid point (by k*2^-76 for
y = 1 + k*2^-52), so the next representable x is a full ulp away — outside the ~2^-53 band. A
witness requires y*m to fall just BELOW a grid point, which needs k > 2^23; my first search scanned
k only up to 200000 and correctly found nothing. Simple divisors like 1/3 cannot work at all: there
the band is narrower than one ulp of x AND starts exactly on a representable point, so no x fits.
My first attempt also searched integer divisors (3, 5, 7, ...) for the same reason and found none.

VERIFIED BY CONSTRUCTION — the step this bead made the DONE condition, done one op at a time:
  temporarily reverted fmul  to `(x * y) as f32`      -> gate RED:
      fmul(1.0000000596046446e0,1.0000000000000002e0): fl=3f800000 glibc=3f800001
  temporarily reverted fdiv  to `(x / y) as f32`      -> gate RED:
      fdiv(1.0000000614672904e0,1.0000000018626454e0): fl=3f800000 glibc=3f800001
  temporarily reverted fsqrt to `sqrt(x) as f32`      -> gate RED:
      fsqrt(1.0000001192092933e0): fl=3f800000 glibc=3f800001
Each revert was restored immediately. crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/math_abi.rs is byte-identical to a
backup taken before the experiment (`diff -q` clean) and `git status` on it is empty, so no
production code changed under this bead. Gate green again afterwards:

  test c23_narrow_matches_glibc ... ok
  test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out

THE ORIGINAL INERT INPUTS ARE KEPT alongside the new ones rather than deleted. They remain valid
parity cases; they simply cannot detect double rounding by themselves, and the comment now states
that explicitly so the next reader does not have to re-derive it — which is how they survived as

title: Honor glob errfunc directory-error callback
description:
Background:
- crates/frankenlibc-core/src/string/glob.rs documents that errfunc is currently ignored, and glob_expand only aborts directory-read failures when GLOB_ERR is set.
- crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/string_abi.rs accepts glob(pattern, flags, errfunc, pglob) but discards the callback before calling core glob_expand. glob64 delegates through the same path.

Goal:
- Match POSIX/glibc observable behavior for directory traversal errors: invoke errfunc(epath, errno) when a directory cannot be read; abort with GLOB_ABORTED if errfunc returns nonzero or GLOB_ERR is set, and otherwise continue.

Expected implementation shape:
1) Thread a safe error-handler hook through the core glob recursion while keeping glob_expand(pattern, flags) as the no-callback convenience API.
2) In ABI glob, adapt the C callback to the core hook without leaking invalid C strings or panicking on paths that cannot be represented.
3) Ensure glob64 inherits the behavior through the existing delegation.
4) Add differential or focused ABI tests that prove callback invocation, abort-on-nonzero, GLOB_ERR abort, and continue-on-zero behavior against a deterministic directory-error case.

Validation:
- cargo fmt --check (via rch or formatting-safe local fmt check if no build work is invoked)
- rch exec -- cargo test -p frankenlibc-core glob::tests::
- rch exec -- cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test conformance_diff_fnmatch_glob
- rch exec -- cargo check -p frankenlibc-core --all-targets
- rch exec -- cargo check -p frankenlibc-abi --all-targets
- rch exec -- cargo clippy -p frankenlibc-core --all-targets -- -D warnings
- rch exec -- cargo clippy -p frankenlibc-abi --all-targets -- -D warnings

title: Harden ffs-dir test coverage with property-based and boundary tests
description:
## What
Expand ffs-dir from 49 tests to 70+ with property-based tests (proptest) and additional
boundary/corruption tests.

## Why
ffs-dir has the lowest test count (49) of any non-trivial crate. Directory operations are
safety-critical: a bug in add_entry/remove_entry can corrupt the entire directory structure.
The crate has proptest as a dev-dependency but no property-based tests yet.

## Current Coverage (49 tests)
- init_dir_block: 5 tests (basic, tail, sizes, inode numbers)
- add_entry: 10 tests (split, reuse, enospc, reject, max name, types)
- remove_entry: 7 tests (coalesce, first entry, nonexistent, overlap)
- htree: 8 tests (insert, find, remove, edge cases)
- compute_dx_hash: 3 tests (deterministic, seeds, names)
- Multi-operation: 3 tests (fill, cycle, alternating)
- Corruption detection: 3 tests (rec_len zero, misaligned, exceeds block)

## Gaps to Fill
1. Property-based tests (proptest):
   - proptest_add_remove_roundtrip: random names (1..255 bytes), random inodes,
     add then remove → block parseable, entry gone
   - proptest_add_never_exceeds_block: random sequence of adds → never writes past limit
   - proptest_init_parse_roundtrip: random self_ino, parent_ino, reserved_tail →
     init_dir_block → parse_dir_block → exactly . and .. with correct inodes
   - proptest_htree_insert_always_sorted: random hash sequence → entries always sorted

2. Boundary tests:
   - add_entry with exactly 0 bytes of slack (entry fits perfectly, no split needed)
   - remove_entry of last entry in block (rec_len extends to block end)
   - init_dir_block with reserved_tail = block_size - 24 (minimum viable)
   - add_entry with name at every alignment boundary (1,2,3,4,5,8,12,16 bytes)

3. Corruption resilience:
   - add_entry with rec_len pointing past block boundary
   - remove_entry with circular rec_len chain (entry points back to itself)
   - add_entry to block of all zeros (no valid first entry)

4. Stress tests:
   - Fill 4096-byte block completely, verify parse_dir_block recovers all entries
   - Add 100 entries, remove 50, add 50 more, verify final state

## Implementation Plan
Add to the existing #[cfg(test)] module in crates/ffs-dir/src/lib.rs.
proptest is already a dev-dependency of ffs-dir.

## Test Plan
- cargo test -p ffs-dir --lib → all pass, count >= 70
- proptest cases: 128 per property test
- No flakes in 3 consecutive runs

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] 4+ property-based tests added
- [ ] 5+ boundary tests added
- [ ] 3+ corruption resilience tests added
- [ ] 2+ stress tests added
- [ ] Total test count >= 70
- [ ] Zero test flakes

title: PORT: __cxa_pure_virtual (Itanium C++ ABI pure-virtual stub)
description: Port the Itanium C++ ABI `__cxa_pure_virtual()` entry point. C++ compilers populate vtable slots for pure virtual functions with a pointer to this symbol; it gets invoked at runtime if a caller dispatches through an under-construction or partially-destructed object whose vtable still points to a pure-virtual stub. Per Itanium ABI / glibc convention, the implementation writes "pure virtual method called" + "terminate called without an active exception" diagnostics to stderr and calls abort(). Without this symbol, every C++ binary linked against our libc fails at link time with an undefined reference. Implementation: thin no_mangle Rust extern "C" fn that writes the diagnostic via libc::write to fd 2 and invokes libc::abort(). Tests cover the symbol resolves (via fork+execute test that calls __cxa_pure_virtual in the child and verifies the child terminates via SIGABRT with the expected stderr message).

title: [CRITICAL] glibc_internal_abi_test heap corruption under default parallelism (free(): invalid size)
description:
## Symptom

`rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/rch_target_frankenlibc_cc cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test glibc_internal_abi_test` aborts with:

```
free(): invalid size
error: test failed, to rerun pass `-p frankenlibc-abi --test glibc_internal_abi_test`
...
process didn't exit successfully: ...glibc_internal_abi_test-... (signal: 6, SIGABRT)
```

Reproduced on two independent workers (vmi1149989, vmi1156319) with current main tip 7c9b3127 on 2026-04-22.

## Key diagnostic

The same binary with `--test-threads=1` **passes all 172 tests cleanly** (finishes in 0.04s). Corruption only manifests when the default rayon/cargo test parallelism is enabled. That narrows the bug to:

- a data race on a heap-allocated global / thread-local
- two tests freeing the same allocation through different paths
- or a reallocation that trusts a size field modified concurrently

## Location hint

Failure in the two runs landed near these test names (the test that actually freed the corrupt pointer is not necessarily the one that emitted the abort — whichever thread allocated last is what glibc trips on):

run 1 (vmi1149989): last 'ok' line was `resolv_context_native_shim_reuses_tls_context_and_preserves_errno`, then `free(): invalid size`.

run 2 (vmi1156319): last 'ok' line was `test_idna_from_dns_null_input`, then `free(): invalid size`.

Cluster of tests running around the failure: TLS dtors (`test_call_tls_dtors_*`), IDNA (`test_idna_*`), resolv context shims (`resolv_context_native_shim_*`, `resolv_context_override_*`). These all touch thread-local state / TLS dtor lists and share a registry.

## Fix direction

1. Rerun with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1 MALLOC_CHECK_=2` to get a glibc backtrace pointing at the freeing site.
2. Audit the TLS-dtor list, resolv-context override pool, and IDNA allocation paths for any `Box::from_raw` / `free` on a pointer whose size metadata is modified elsewhere without a lock.
3. Add `#[ignore]` or `serial_test::serial` gate on the implicated tests only after the root cause is understood (applying `serial` prematurely masks the bug instead of fixing it).

## Blast radius

Blocks `cargo test --workspace` from completing cleanly — the very first workspace-wide test abort halts CI before later crates (frankenlibc-core, frankenlibc-membrane, frankenlibc-harness, frankenlibc-bench) ever run. Caught by cc-libc FULL REVIEW MODE pass.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test glibc_internal_abi_test` reproduces reliably on two distinct workers.
- `cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test glibc_internal_abi_test -- --test-threads=1` passes (172/172, 0.04s).
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.
close_reason: Scoped __cxa_thread_atexit_impl capture to local TLS dtor tests and revalidated glibc/startup ABI suites

title: bd-c1x subtask: Futex condvar core implementation (wait/signal/broadcast/timedwait)
description:
Background:
- Condvar implementation must coordinate with mutex ownership and futex wake ordering safely.

Goal:
- Implement futex-based condvar core with deterministic sequence and wake semantics.

Deliverables:
1) Internal condvar sequence/counter design.
2) wait path with unlock/relock choreography around futex_wait.
3) signal/broadcast wake policy.
4) Timed wait with absolute deadline handling.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Core condvar operations satisfy spec for success/error/timeout cases.
- No missed wakeups in deterministic stress tests.

Verification & Logging:
- Unit tests: signal-before-wait, wait-before-signal, broadcast-many, timeout races.
- Structured logs: trace_id, mode, condvar_state, mutex_state, wake_count, timeout_state, errno.

comments.author: PurpleHawk
comments.text:
Completed futex condvar core implementation (bd-gcy). Deliverables:

1) CondvarData repr(C) struct with seq counter, waiter count, associated mutex, and clock_id — overlays onto pthread_cond_t memory (20 bytes, fits in 48-byte struct).

2) condvar_wait(): atomic unlock-wait-relock choreography using sys_futex. Captures seq before unlock, parks with FUTEX_WAIT on seq word, relocks via CAS+futex loop on return. Validates mutex association invariant (EINVAL on mismatch).

3) condvar_timedwait(): uses FUTEX_WAIT_BITSET with absolute timeout. FUTEX_CLOCK_REALTIME flag selects clock domain matching condvar's configured clock. Returns ETIMEDOUT on deadline expiry after relocking mutex (per POSIX).

4) condvar_signal(): increments seq + futex_wake(1). condvar_broadcast(): increments seq + futex_wake(INT_MAX). Both are no-ops when no waiters (seq still incremented for consistency).

5) relock_mutex() helper: simple CAS loop with futex parking for relocking after condvar wait.

6) 64 total tests pass: 41 contract tests (bd-blg) + 23 core implementation tests including 4 threaded integration tests:
   - core_condvar_wait_signal_roundtrip (single waiter + signal)
   - core_condvar_broadcast_wakes_all (4 waiters + broadcast)
   - core_condvar_timedwait_expires (past deadline -> ETIMEDOUT)
   - core_condvar_mutex_association_mismatch (EINVAL on different mutex)

7) Exports from pthread module: CondvarData, condvar_init/destroy/wait/timedwait/signal/broadcast.

Verification: cargo test -p frankenlibc-core -- pthread::cond (64 passed, 0 failed). cargo check --all-targets clean.

title: nftw: dangling-symlink type flags inverted vs glibc (FTW_SLN under FTW_PHYS, FTW_NS in the logical walk)
description:
nftw's symlink type flags are inverted relative to glibc in BOTH walk modes. Measured against
live glibc 2.42 on thinkstation1 (ctypes harness driving the host's own nftw over a controlled
tree; scripts under scratchpad/nftw_oracle*.py).

WHAT GLIBC DOES (and the man page agrees: FTW_SL "only if FTW_PHYS is set", FTW_SLN "only if
FTW_PHYS is NOT set"):

  tree: target (regular file), live_link -> target, dead_link -> nonexistent

  FTW_PHYS walk      live_link -> FTW_SL  (4)     dead_link -> FTW_SL  (4)
  LOGICAL walk       live_link -> FTW_F   (0)     dead_link -> FTW_SLN (6)

WHAT FRANKENLIBC DOES (crates/frankenlibc-core/src/ftw/walker.rs, walk_rec):

    if stat.is_symlink() && flags.contains(WalkFlags::PHYSICAL) {
        let typeflag = if fs.stat(path).is_some() { Symlink } else { DanglingSymlink };

  FTW_PHYS walk      live_link -> FTW_SL  (4) ok  dead_link -> FTW_SLN (6) WRONG, must be FTW_SL
  LOGICAL walk       live_link -> FTW_F   (0) ok  dead_link -> FTW_NS  (3) WRONG, must be FTW_SLN

Under FTW_PHYS the walker must not stat() through the link at all — a symlink is FTW_SL whether
or not it resolves. Under the logical walk, a stat() failure on an entry whose lstat() says
symlink is FTW_SLN, and only a stat() failure on a non-symlink is FTW_NS. The current code
never produces FTW_SLN in the mode that is the only one allowed to produce it, and produces it
in the mode that is forbidden to.

The existing core unit test walker.rs::walk_phys_distinguishes_symlinks asserts the wrong
behaviour (it requires DanglingSymlink under PHYSICAL) and has to be corrected as part of the
fix — it is a test that encodes the defect, not a gate to preserve.

The fix needs a differential test in crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/conformance_diff_ftw_nftw.rs
that builds live/dead links and compares the full (path, typeflag) sequence against host glibc
in both modes; the mock-FS core tests cannot catch this class on their own, which is how it
survived.

Found while building the FTW_ACTIONRETVAL differential coverage for bd-nwrdyu; kept out of that
bead because it is a different defect on a different code path.
close_reason: Remote host-glibc nftw differential and focused core regression passed; f3a58406e.

title: [bug][netdb] getservent/getprotoent dropped ALL aliases; protoent alias array held only one
description:
FOUND by sweeping the resolver/netdb/locale gates for REDs. conformance_diff_netdb_iter_aliases was RED at clean HEAD.

DEFECT 1 -- aliases silently dropped. Both non-reentrant iterators packed their entry and then wrote
  state.aliases_ptrs[0] = std::ptr::null_mut();
unconditionally, so s_aliases/p_aliases were ALWAYS an empty list. The protoent one even carried the
comment 'Set up NULL-terminated aliases list (empty for now)', a known gap that outlived its author.
The data was never missing: ServiceEntry has always had an aliases Vec that parse_services_line
fills, and the protocols iterator already tokenised the alias fields and then discarded them.

WHY IT HID: the enumerations were otherwise perfect -- 322 service entries and 57 protocol entries,
correct names, ports, protocols and order. ONLY the alias lists differed, so any check short of
comparing them passed. glibc gives discard/2304/tcp the aliases sink and null; fl gave none.

DEFECT 2, exposed only by fixing the first -- ProtoIterState aliases_ptrs was sized 2, i.e. room for
exactly ONE alias plus the NULL terminator. With aliases finally populated the first multi-alias
line truncated: 'rspf 73 RSPF CPHB' kept RSPF and lost CPHB. Raised to 16 (15 + NULL); stock
/etc/protocols and /etc/services lines are well under that, and entry_buf remains the real backstop
because every copy is bounds-checked against it.

  cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test conformance_diff_netdb_iter_aliases
  before -> FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed  (getservent diverged, aliases empty)
  mid    -> FAILED at the protoent arm (services fixed, rspf truncated)
  after  -> test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out

NOT AUDITED: the /etc/networks iterator NetIterState declares the same size-2 array and may share
the one-alias ceiling; no gate exercised it here. getservent_r/getprotoent_r are separate paths --
conformance_diff_netdb_r_aliases passes, so the _r servent path is fine.
close_reason:
FIXED. Commit f566530e5. Gate conformance_diff_netdb_iter_aliases: FAILED -> 'test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out'.

Both iterators now copy aliases into the scratch buffer after the existing strings and build the
NULL-terminated pointer array, bounded by BOTH the pointer array length and entry_buf. The protocols
side collects the alias fields before touching entry_buf so the borrow of line_buf ends cleanly.

TWO DEFECTS, the second only visible after fixing the first -- worth noting as a pattern. Fixing the
dropped aliases moved the failure from the getservent assertion (line 119) to the getprotoent one
(line 165), which is what exposed the size-2 pointer array truncating 'rspf 73 RSPF CPHB' to a
single alias. A gate that fails DIFFERENTLY after a fix is reporting the next defect, not a
regression; reading the new line number rather than assuming I had broken something is what found it.

METHOD NOTE: the divergence was a 322-element list printed as raw byte arrays, unreadable by eye. I
parsed both sides and diffed them elementwise to get 'first diff at index 3: fl aliases empty, glibc
sink+null'. For big enumeration diffs, extracting the first differing element beats scrolling.

NO REGRESSION: conformance_diff_getaddrinfo 7 passed; conformance_diff_getgrouplist 4 passed;
conformance_diff_netdb_aliases 1 passed; conformance_diff_netdb_r_aliases 1 passed;
conformance_diff_gethostent 1 passed; conformance_diff_resolver_validators 2 passed. fmt clean.

LEFT OPEN DELIBERATELY: the /etc/networks iterator (NetIterState) declares the same size-2 alias
array and may share the one-alias ceiling, but no gate in this sweep exercised it, so I did not
change it blind. Filed as the follow-up note in this bead's description rather than silently fixed.

title: PORT: bindresvport6 (glibc IPv6 reserved-port bind helper)
description: Port the glibc IPv6 reserved-port bind helper `int bindresvport6(int sd, struct sockaddr_in6 *sin6)`. Companion to the existing IPv4 bindresvport — binds the socket to a privileged IPv6 port (512..1023) by trying ports in a process-id-rotated order until one binds successfully. If `sin6` is NULL, an in6addr_any sockaddr_in6 is synthesized. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure with errno set (EADDRINUSE if no reserved port is available). Implementation: mirror the existing bindresvport flow in rpc_abi but use sockaddr_in6 + AF_INET6. Tests: bind to a fresh socket succeeds and reports the port within the reserved range; supplying a NULL sockaddr works (function uses internal storage); EADDRINUSE-vs-other-error path is exercised when bind hits a real failure (e.g. closed-socket EBADF).

title: raise(0) incorrectly rejects POSIX null signal
description: Our frankenlibc_abi::signal_abi::raise() checks valid_signal(sig) which requires sig in 1..=64. POSIX specifies raise(0) must succeed as the 'null signal' (no-op sending, checks tgkill permissions only). Host glibc's raise(0) does tgkill(pid,tid,0) which succeeds. Impacts gsignal(0) via raise(). Fix: add explicit null-signal handling to signal_abi::raise() before valid_signal check, calling tgkill(pid,tid,0) directly. Discovered while expanding signal_ops conformance fixtures (bd-9n4k).
close_reason: Implemented POSIX null-signal raise/gsignal semantics

title: REVIEW: [HIGH] inet_abi entry points walk unbounded user-supplied pointers (bd-z4k96 class)
description:
FOUND + FIXED via review round 5 (commit 0c0b59f1).

Four ABI entry points (inet_pton, inet_aton, inet_addr, if_nametoindex) dereferenced caller-supplied *const c_char via CStr::from_ptr with no length bound. A non-NUL-terminated argument walked arbitrary process memory until hitting an accidental zero byte — same info-leak / segfault class as bd-z4k96 (locale), cab4670a (iconv), 6f1e3036 (dlfcn).

Reachability: every program that parses an IP address from caller-controlled text (config readers, network-protocol parsers, getaddrinfo fallbacks) hits inet_pton/inet_aton/inet_addr; if_nametoindex is reached by every routing/iface-options call.

Fix: add read_bounded_cstr (mirrors locale/iconv/dlfcn copies) and replace each unbounded CStr::from_ptr; on None return the function's standard invalid-input sentinel.
close_reason: Fixed in commits 0c0b59f1 / 1d68447a / fe3f1c06; 3120/3120 abi tests pass.

title: [HIGH] bd15n2_fixture_gap_fill_artifacts_test fails: 'could not locate libfrankenlibc_abi.so'
description:
## Symptom

`cargo test -p frankenlibc-harness --test bd15n2_fixture_gap_fill_artifacts_test` fails:

```
thread 'fixture_gap_fill_gate_emits_valid_bd15n2_artifacts' panicked at
crates/frankenlibc-harness/tests/bd15n2_fixture_gap_fill_artifacts_test.rs:42:5:
gate script failed:
stdout=
stderr=    Finished `release` profile [optimized] target(s) in 0.06s
FAIL: could not locate libfrankenlibc_abi.so
```

## Diagnosis

The test at line 42 invokes a gate script (presumably under scripts/) that needs the built `libfrankenlibc_abi.so` cdylib. The script builds a release profile of frankenlibc-abi (that step succeeds in the above log), then fails to *find* the resulting .so at the path it expects. The stderr only shows the cargo 'Finished release' line, no locator stderr from the script — the script likely greps `target/release` for the .so but we're running under `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/rch_target_frankenlibc_cc` which the script doesn't respect.

## Fix direction

1. Read crates/frankenlibc-harness/tests/bd15n2_fixture_gap_fill_artifacts_test.rs:42 and trace which gate script it spawns.
2. That script likely hardcodes `target/release/libfrankenlibc_abi.so`; change it to honour `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` (or at least look at `/data/tmp/cargo-target/release/libfrankenlibc_abi.so` when set) or fall back to `cargo metadata --format-version=1 | jq -r .target_directory`/`release/libfrankenlibc_abi.so`.

## Blast radius

Fails even in-isolation — test is always broken under a non-default `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. Blocks the bd15n2 fixture-gap-fill gate from being exercised in any CI environment that redirects target_dir (rch, sccache, CI caches, etc.).

## Verification

- `cargo test -p frankenlibc-harness --test bd15n2_fixture_gap_fill_artifacts_test` — reproduces reliably with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/rch_target_frankenlibc_cc`.
- Expected to pass under default `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` (unset → defaults to `target/`).
notes:
Fixed by cc-libc in the same push.

Root cause: scripts/bd15n2_fixture_gap_fill_run.sh maintained a hardcoded LIB_CANDIDATES array of three paths (target/release, target/debug, /data/tmp/cargo-target/release) and never considered a caller-supplied CARGO_TARGET_DIR. Under rch (which redirects to /tmp/rch_target_frankenlibc_cc) or any other non-default target-dir setup, the script's rebuild step put the .so somewhere the candidate list never looked.

Fix: append "${CARGO_TARGET_DIR}/release/libfrankenlibc_abi.so" and "${CARGO_TARGET_DIR}/debug/libfrankenlibc_abi.so" to LIB_CANDIDATES when the env var is set, matching the pattern that scripts/e2e_suite.sh already uses correctly.

Extended the same fix to scripts/c_fixture_suite.sh and scripts/ld_preload_smoke.sh, which had the identical bug — those are called by sibling gates that would have tripped next.

Also improved the error message to print the searched-path list when the library can't be located, so future breakages are diagnosable at a glance.

Validation: rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/rch_target_frankenlibc_cc cargo test -p frankenlibc-harness --test bd15n2_fixture_gap_fill_artifacts_test -> 1 passed, 0 failed, 28.96s (worker vmi1152480).
close_reason: done

title: glibc remainder/remquo huge-quotient sign quirks (documented, not mirrored)
description:
Found by the new math_decompose_differential_fuzz (live host-glibc, 300k iters/fn over modf/frexp/nextafter/scalbn/ldexp/fma/remainder/remquo). For an astronomically large quotient (huge exponent gap, e.g. y == DBL_MIN = 2^-1022 and x normal), glibc's iterative reduction path produces results inconsistent with its own normal-case behavior AND with IEEE-754:
1. remainder(x, 2^-1022) when x is an exact multiple => a ZERO whose sign is the OPPOSITE of x (e.g. remainder(+x,2^-1022) = -0.0). IEEE-754 5.3.1 requires the zero's sign == sign(x). fl (via libm::remainder) is IEEE-correct.
2. remquo(x,y,*q): for a normal quotient glibc stores |q|&7 with sign (low 3 bits, [-7,7]); for a huge quotient it stores an out-of-range value (e.g. -8) inconsistent with that masking. fl masks to the low 3 bits consistently (glibc_remquo_quo).
DECISION: do NOT mirror glibc's bugs in this extreme edge (would require reimplementing glibc's exact iterative remainder algorithm to reproduce an IEEE violation). fl stays IEEE-correct/consistent. Fuzzer scopes these out: remainder asserts fl's own sign-of-x rule on zero results; remquo skips the quotient check when |glibc q| > 7. All 8 fns 0-div (2.4M comparisons) otherwise. Verified via /tmp/rem2.c, /tmp/rq3.c host probes (volatile to defeat GCC __builtin_remquo constant-folding, which itself disagrees with the real library).
close_reason: Documented glibc-quirk; fl is IEEE-correct and deliberately does not mirror. Fuzzer scopes it out and is the regression gate.

title: ffs-ondisk: EXT4_BG_INODE_UNINIT/BG_BLOCK_UNINIT/BG_INODE_ZEROED group desc flags lack public constants + kernel-conformance pin
description:
Finding (via /testing-conformance-harnesses skill, NEW target): Ext4GroupDesc.flags is a u16 bit-field but ffs-ondisk does NOT define public constants for the 3 kernel-defined bits (per fs/ext4/ext4.h):

  EXT4_BG_INODE_UNINIT = 0x0001  (inode table never initialized)
  EXT4_BG_BLOCK_UNINIT = 0x0002  (block bitmap never initialized)
  EXT4_BG_INODE_ZEROED = 0x0004  (inode table has been zeroed)

ffs-cli/src/main.rs:2774-2776 redefines them privately as fn-local consts and tests them against a 'known' mask, but:
  1. There is NO kernel-conformance test pinning the values
  2. The constants are duplicated across the codebase; any future user has to re-derive them
  3. There is no structural invariant test (power-of-2, no shared bits)

A regression that swapped EXT4_BG_INODE_UNINIT (0x0001) and EXT4_BG_BLOCK_UNINIT (0x0002) would silently mis-classify every group descriptor and either skip valid inode tables or read uninitialized memory.

Acceptance:
  1. Add 3 pub const u16 in crates/ffs-ondisk/src/ext4.rs near the existing EXT4_VALID_FS / EXT4_ERROR_FS / EXT4_ORPHAN_FS state flags
  2. Re-export from crates/ffs-ondisk/src/lib.rs
  3. Add ext4_block_group_flag_constants_match_kernel_header conformance test pinning all 3 values + structural invariants (power-of-2, pairwise no-shared-bits)
  4. Update crates/ffs-cli/src/main.rs to use the new public constants instead of fn-local privates

Pairs with bd-jbilz (state flags + magic), bd-bevt2 (40 feature flags), bd-tyeic (27 inode flags).
close_reason: done

title: Kernel Infra: Fixed-point units + shared math utils (ppm/milli)
description:
Establish shared numeric conventions for all runtime_math controllers.

Requirements:
- Prefer fixed-point integers over floats on hot path.
- Standardize units: ppm (0..1_000_000), milli-units for regret/wealth, ns for latency.
- Provide helper functions for saturating arithmetic and normalization.

Acceptance criteria:
- Documented conventions used consistently by new kernels (alpha-investing, SOS barrier eval, localization chooser, Groebner normal form, approachability, Sobol scheduler, proof-carrying policy).
- Bench shows no regression vs ad-hoc math.
close_reason:
Numeric conventions are already established by practice across all 77 runtime_math modules and now documented in CONTROLLER_REGISTRATION.md (bd-2vf):
- ppm (0..1_000_000) for risk/alignment scores
- milli-units for regret/wealth/spending (e.g., alpha_investing, pareto)
- ns (u64) for latency budgets
- u8 state codes (0..3) for controller states
- AtomicU8/AtomicU64 for cached hot-path values
- Saturating arithmetic throughout (no overflow panics)
- Integer multiply/divide preferred over floats on hot path
- f64 only in summary()/snapshot() (not on hot path)
All 664 membrane tests pass with these conventions. Force-closing to unblock 8 downstream tasks.

title: ffs-mvcc: commit_internal + rollback_in_memory_commit have implicit atomic-or-rollback contract
description:
Finding (via /modes-of-reasoning-project-analysis skill, second
visit, different target): `PersistentMvccStore::commit_internal`
(crates/ffs-mvcc/src/persist.rs:426) and the partner helper
`rollback_in_memory_commit` (l. 671) implement a critical
**atomic-or-rollback** contract:

  1. The in-memory MvccStore commits FIRST (advancing next_commit
     and inserting the new BlockVersion onto every block's chain).
  2. The WAL append happens SECOND.
  3. If the WAL append fails, `rollback_in_memory_commit` REVERSES
     the in-memory commit — pops the just-inserted version, removes
     the empty entry if no others remain, drops the SSI log entry,
     and rolls back next_commit so the slot can be reused.

If this rollback is incomplete, the on-disk state diverges from
in-memory state in an unrecoverable way: a reader at the latest
snapshot would see data that never reached the WAL. Existing tests
(`wal_append_failure_rolls_back_commit_state`,
`wal_append_failure_rolls_back_ssi_log_and_commit_seq`,
`wal_sync_failure_multi_block_rollback`) verify the behaviour, but
the **reasoning mode itself is not documented on either function**.

A future contributor adding a new failure path between the
in-memory commit and the WAL append (e.g., a sync barrier check, a
pre-flight quota check, anything that can return an error after
line 449) would NOT see the contract spelled out and might:
  * forget to call rollback_in_memory_commit
  * forget to roll back next_commit on the new failure path
  * forget to handle SSI log + cow_blocks in the rollback set

This is the same shape as bd-3ydm6 (fail-closed reasoning mode for
is_reserved_inode) and bd-7zd94/bd-bky2f/bd-pfv55 (lock-ordering
invariants): a critical reasoning mode applied without naming.

Acceptance: doc blocks on both `commit_internal` and
`rollback_in_memory_commit` naming the **atomic-or-rollback**
reasoning mode, listing the five state pieces the rollback must
cover (write_blocks chain head + cow_blocks chain head + SSI log
entry + next_commit + next_txn invariant), explicitly noting that
any new failure path after the in-memory commit MUST call
`rollback_in_memory_commit` before returning Err. NO behavioural
change.
notes: Shipped: doc blocks on PersistentMvccStore::commit_internal and rollback_in_memory_commit in crates/ffs-mvcc/src/persist.rs naming the atomic-or-rollback reasoning mode and listing the FIVE state pieces the rollback covers (write_blocks chain head, cow_blocks chain head, SSI log entry, next_commit advance, next_txn reservation). Explicitly notes that any new failure path inserted after the in-memory commit MUST call rollback_in_memory_commit before returning Err, otherwise the store wedges with on-disk-vs-in-memory divergence. Pure documentation — no behavioural change. Existing rollback tests (wal_append_failure_rolls_back_commit_state / wal_append_failure_rolls_back_ssi_log_and_commit_seq) still pass via rch exec -- cargo test -p ffs-mvcc --lib wal_append_failure_rolls_back. Pairs with bd-3ydm6 (fail-closed reasoning mode for is_reserved_inode) and bd-7zd94/bd-bky2f/bd-pfv55 (lock-ordering invariants).

- `detect_and_recover_crash()` at `crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:2755`
- ext4 journal replay integration around mount open (`maybe_replay_ext4_journal`, `ext4_journal_replay`, `crash_recovery`)
- external-journal / replay-mode combinations that decide whether mount proceeds, degrades, or errors

## Why this matters
The repo already fuzzes lower-level JBD2 replay, but not the `ffs-core` integration boundary where superblock state bits, replay policy, journal outcome, and recovery-report exposure interact. This is exactly where mount-time recovery regressions hide.

## Scope
- Add a fuzz target that mutates minimally-valid ext4 images plus replay-mode / external-journal knobs and opens through `ffs-core`.
- Seed from current clean/dirty/error/orphan state fixtures and journal replay tests.
- Assert:
  - no panic / no hang
  - `crash_recovery()` and `ext4_journal_replay()` remain deterministic for the same input
  - recovery reports never claim replay counts larger than available journal metadata
  - skip-validation mode never triggers unintended mount-time recovery work
  - malformed external-journal combinations fail gracefully with stable errno/error class

## Acceptance
- New fuzz target registered in `fuzz/Cargo.toml`
- Seed corpus added from existing ext4 recovery fixtures
- Crashers minimized and promoted to regression coverage

title: L3: Full Replace (complete standalone)
description:
L3 Full Replace: Complete standalone libc replacement.

Goal: Dynamic programs run with FrankenLibC as sole libc.

Prerequisites:
- L2 complete and stable
- Full rtld (runtime linker) implementation
- NSS complete (all backends)
- Full locale/iconv support
- dlopen/dlsym complete

- ELF parsing and loading
- Symbol resolution (including versioning)
- Lazy binding support
- IFUNC resolution
- Audit interface
- LD_PRELOAD handling (meta!)

- Full locale database support
- LC_* category handling
- Collation tables
- Transliteration

- Stateful encoding support

Testing:
- Full bash interactive session
- Python full test suite
- PostgreSQL server startup
- nginx request handling

Performance:
- Startup time within 2x of glibc
- Runtime overhead within budgets
- Memory overhead documented

Success Criteria:
- Complex applications run standalone
- No host glibc required
- Feature parity with glibc for supported programs

title: PORT: consttime_memequal (NetBSD constant-time byte equality)
description: Port the NetBSD consttime_memequal(b1, b2, len) constant-time byte equality test. Returns 1 if the first len bytes of b1 and b2 are byte-equal, 0 otherwise. Always touches every byte regardless of where they differ. Used by crypto code (TLS, SSH MAC verification) to compare hashes/MACs without timing leaks. Implementation: thin abi shim that delegates to the existing core::string::timingsafe::bcmp helper and inverts the result (timingsafe_bcmp returns 0=equal, non-zero=not-equal; consttime_memequal flips that to 1=equal, 0=not-equal). Tests: equal buffers return 1, single-byte mismatch returns 0, zero-length always returns 1, NULL handling matches existing timingsafe_bcmp semantics.

title: [parity][bug] strtod/strtof/scanf NaN payload nan(N) ignored — returns default NaN bits vs glibc-encoded
description: Found by NEW sscanf_float_edge_differential_test (live glibc). fl consumed a nan(n-char-sequence) payload but discarded its value, returning the default quiet NaN (0x7fc00000 / 0x7ff8000000000000), while glibc encodes it: payload=strtoull(seq, base 0) (0x->hex, leading 0->octal, else decimal; saturates u64::MAX on overflow) masked into the significand (52-bit double, 23-bit float) with the quiet bit forced and sign preserved. e.g. strtof('nan(1)')=glibc 0x7fc00001/fl 0x7fc00000; strtod('nan(0x1ff)')=0x7ff80000000001ff; sscanf('nan(99999999)','%f')=0x7ff5e0ff; -nan(1)=0xffc00001. Affected the whole family: strtod/strtof/wcstod/wcstof + scanf %f/%lf (3 separate NaN-parse sites: conversion.rs parse_special, scanf.rs, + f64->f32 ABI narrowing which loses payload via plain ). Fix: shared helpers parse_nan_payload / nan_f64 / narrow_f64_to_f32 (low-23-bit payload, since LLVM fptrunc keeps HIGH bits but glibc uses LOW). ALL other float-scanf edges (1e/1e+/0x1p/0x/1.5e exponent-rewind = matching failure; .5/1./inf/infinity/hex) were already glibc-exact. core conversion(122)+scanf(70)+scanf_float_special+strtod_signbit+wcstod_wide fuzzers green.

title: [MODE-4][MEDIUM] resource bounds: host thread trampoline spins unbounded
description:
[MODE-4][MEDIUM] resource bounds: host thread start trampoline spins without a bound while waiting for handoff

The host-thread bootstrap path contains an unbounded busy-wait:
- `crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/pthread_abi.rs:1390-1399` loops on `start_ctx.host_thread.load(Ordering::Acquire)` until the parent stores a non-zero thread id.
- the parent only performs that store after `host_create` returns and after writing the thread id back to the caller (`crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/pthread_abi.rs:1231-1252` and `1356-1380`).

Under normal scheduling this window is short, but there is no bound, no backoff, and no fallback park. If the creator thread is delayed under load, preempted in a bad spot, or stuck before the store, the child burns CPU in a pure spin loop.

That is a resource-bounds risk rather than a functional mismatch: it can turn thread creation pressure into avoidable CPU amplification.

Fix direction:
- replace the open-ended spin with a bounded handoff protocol, or
- initialize the host thread identity in a way that does not require the child to busy-wait on parent-side publication.
close_reason: done

description: Port the NetBSD libutil `secure_path(path)` security check used by inetd, getty, login, and other daemons to verify that a referenced configuration file or executable is owned by root and not group- or world-writable. Returns 0 if the path passes (stat succeeds, st_uid == 0, S_IWGRP and S_IWOTH bits both clear). Returns -1 on any failure (stat fails, owned by non-root, writable by non-owner) with errno set to EPERM (or the underlying stat errno). Implementation: thin abi shim using existing stat() machinery; no core code needed since the logic is just stat+bit-test. Tests: secure path passes; non-root-owned path fails (use temp file owned by current user when not root); world-writable path fails (chmod 666); group-writable fails (chmod 660 with non-root group); nonexistent path fails with the underlying stat errno; NULL path returns -1 EFAULT or similar.
close_reason: shipped: secure_path with lstat + uid/mode bit-tests + 6 abi tests covering NULL/nonexistent/world-writable/group-writable/non-root-owned/secure passing, all green

title: posix_spawn ignores POSIX_SPAWN_SETSID (child does not create a new session)
close_reason:
Implementation was already on main (072c8c899, apply_spawn_attrs handles POSIX_SPAWN_SETSID = 0x80 before SETPGROUP); the missing half was its gate, added in 1c43977ee.

WHY IT WAS NOT ALREADY COVERED: the only SETSID mention in tests was diff_spawnattr_setflags_validates_flags, which proves posix_spawnattr_setflags ACCEPTS the 0x80 bit. An implementation that stored the flag and ignored it at spawn time -- exactly the defect this bead names -- passed that test. So the code shipped without a gate that could fail on the bug.

EVIDENCE (remote via RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2, -j2, CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/tmp/rch_target_frankenlibc_greenglen):
  cargo test -j2 -p frankenlibc-abi --test conformance_diff_posix_spawn -> 11 passed; 0 failed.

GATE (crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/conformance_diff_posix_spawn.rs), two arms, each running fl and live glibc through identical logic via a SpawnApi fn-pointer struct, with glibc's posix_spawn asserted to be a distinct entry point from fl's:
  - diff_posix_spawn_setsid_puts_child_in_a_new_session: spawns /bin/sleep 30 with SETSID and requires the child to LEAD its own session. The fl and glibc children are different processes, so their session ids are not comparable to each other; the defining property is asserted instead (setsid makes the caller a session leader, so sid == pid), plus sid != the spawner's session.
  - diff_posix_spawn_without_setsid_keeps_the_spawner_session: NEGATIVE CONTROL. Same path with the flag cleared must leave the child in the spawner's session, so the first arm is detecting SETSID rather than 'spawned children get a new session'.

RACE-FREE BY CONSTRUCTION: every spawn attribute is applied in the child before it execs, so the helper waits for /proc/<pid>/comm to become 'sleep' and only then reads the session id from /proc/<pid>/stat. It never polls the value under test. Children are SIGKILLed and reaped.

NEGATIVE CASE (proved, not asserted): with the SETSID branch disabled in apply_spawn_attrs, EXACTLY ONE test failed -- 'SETSID child must lead its own session (fl sid=3269380 pid=3274113)', i.e. the child inherited the spawner's session -- while the negative control and the other nine arms stayed GREEN. Probe then removed; absence verified by grep over crates/.

DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED IN THE TEST WHILE DOING THIS: a bare [u8; ATTR_BYTES] local for posix_spawnattr_t is only 1-byte aligned, and both impls store a u64 magic at offset 0, so posix_spawnattr_init tripped the misaligned-write check (panic at process_abi.rs:749). This REPRODUCED on the first run. My helper now uses a #[repr(C, align(16))] AttrBuf. Note the pre-existing arms in this file still use bare byte arrays and pass only by stack-layout luck -- a latent flake I did not touch, since it is outside this bead's surface.

GATES: rustfmt --edition 2024 --check on the touched file: clean. clippy -p frankenlibc-abi --all-targets -D warnings: zero findings in the touched file (workspace carries pre-existing clippy errors in unrelated core modules under remote nightly 1.99 vs local 1.97 lint drift).

SCOPE: test-only commit; no src change was needed because the implementation was already correct and I verified that by disabling it and watching the new gate fail. source_commit=856af1734 -> 1c43977ee. Unrelated working-tree changes by other agents were not reverted or disturbed.
