title: [perf][stdio] per-FILE stream state (Arc<Mutex<StdioStream>> registry): MT fd-stream fgetc measured 53.9x behind glibc on sound instrument
description: Successor to bd-n7dpzr with a VALID measurement (its 07-11 kill was fmemopen-only — that workload never takes the registry lock per byte; fd streams DO). FGETC_FD_AB phase of examples/stdio_fread_mem_mt_ab.rs (persistent threads, barrier rounds, FILE* opened once, per-thread /dev/shm file, verify_fd byte+EOF+rewind gate vs dlmopen glibc): 1t fl 195.6us vs glibc 49.8us per 4096-byte drain = 3.93x (single_threaded==false, i.e. the any-program-with-one-spawned-thread state); 8t fl 3007.6us vs glibc 55.8us = 53.9x — glibc degrades 1.12x 1t->8t (per-FILE locks), fl 15.4x (ONE global registry mutex per fgetc). DESIGN (from cc-stdio-mt-2026-07-11 scoping + this evidence): registry value type -> Arc<parking_lot::Mutex<StdioStream>>; ~60 id-scoped sites transform to short-map-probe-then-per-stream-lock; 4 sorted_stream_ids sites lock in index order; TLS (FILE*,gen)->Arc cache for fgetc/fgets/fread/fputc/fputs/fwrite hot paths (MT-safe, unlike the ST *mut write cache); blocking flush then holds only its own stream's lock (fixes the hold-registry-across-sys_write hazard). ATOMIC refactor — do not commit a broken partial. Gates: stdio_abi_test 256 + conformance_diff_stdio_* + FGETC_FD_AB two-binary A/B with FREAD/FGETS_MEM arms as null controls. Evidence: ledger cc-fd-mt-survey-2026-07-22.
close_reason: SHIPPED 2026-07-22 (MagentaCondor): per-FILE Arc<Mutex<StdioStream>> registry + MT-safe TLS cell cache. fd-stream MT fgetc 63.3x→2.75x vs glibc (8t 3.78ms→154.6us/drain=24.4x, DISJOINT 0.041 cand/base); 1t 0.80. Global registry-mutex convoy eliminated (fl 1t→8t scaling 1.25x vs glibc 1.17x). Conformance: stdio_abi_test 256/0 + 8 differentials + verify_fd/gets byte-identity; full 788-target crate suite 742 pass / 28 fail with all 28 proven pre-existing by same-worker lever-vs-HEAD per-binary comparison (zero regressions). title: Add indirect block pointer write support for e2compr beyond direct range
description:
BACKGROUND: The e2compr compressed write path (write_ext4_compressed_cluster, write_ext4_uncompressed_cluster) uses set_indirect_block_ptr to write block pointers in the inode's i_block array. This function currently rejects logical_block >= 12 because entries 12-14 are the single/double/triple indirect pointers, and overwriting them with data block pointers would corrupt the indirect addressing table.

CURRENT LIMITATION: With the smallest cluster size (4 blocks, shift=2) and 4K block size, only clusters at logical blocks 0-3, 4-7, and 8-11 can be written — files up to 48KB. Cluster shift 3 (8 blocks) limits to 32KB. Larger files cannot be compressed at all.

THE READ PATH ALREADY WORKS: resolve_indirect_block handles single/double/triple indirect lookups for reading. The write side needs the inverse operation.

IMPLEMENTATION PLAN:
1. Add write_indirect_block_ptr(cx, scope, inode, alloc, logical_block, phys) that mirrors resolve_indirect_block but writes:
   - For logical_block < 12: direct write to inode.extent_bytes (existing code).
   - For 12 <= logical_block < 12 + ptrs_per_block: allocate or read the single-indirect block (i_block[12]), write the pointer at the correct offset within it.
   - For double-indirect range: allocate/read i_block[13] -> intermediate block -> write pointer.
   - For triple-indirect range: three-level allocation/read.
2. Intermediate blocks must be allocated on first use (when i_block[12/13/14] is 0).
3. Allocated intermediate blocks must be freed when the last pointer in them becomes 0 (during cluster freeing).
4. Update set_indirect_block_ptr callers to use the new function.
5. Add tests for files that span into the indirect range.

COMPLEXITY: Medium-high. The read path is ~120 lines; the write path will be ~200 lines due to allocation of intermediate blocks. Must correctly handle:
- First write to a new indirect level (allocate the intermediate block).
- Overwrite of existing pointers (read-modify-write the intermediate block).
- Freeing of intermediate blocks when all their pointers become 0.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Compressed write works for files up to at least 1MB (requires single-indirect support).
- Compressed read/write roundtrip test for a file spanning into indirect block range.
- set_indirect_block_ptr error at lb >= 12 is removed.
- No block leaks: freed clusters also free their intermediate block pointers if they become empty.
close_reason: All subtasks complete: single-indirect (bd-z15u, commit 18cd3d7) and double/triple indirect (bd-pv9l, commit 06a4288). e2compr can now compress files of any size.

title: EPIC: V1.1 Post-Parity Hardening and Operationalization
description:
# EPIC: V1.1 Post-Parity Hardening and Operationalization

## Context
Tracked V1 parity is complete (75/75), but FrankenFS is explicitly still early-stage and experimental for mount/write operations. The project now needs a rigorous post-parity program focused on production-grade correctness confidence, failure containment, observability, and predictable performance under stress.

This epic converts that post-parity intent into an executable dependency graph that is:
- granular enough for independent agent execution,
- explicit about acceptance gates,
- self-contained (no need to reopen planning docs during execution).

## Why this exists
Parity completion proves breadth of implemented behavior, not necessarily depth of operational hardening. Remaining risk lives in:
- durability under crash/fault scenarios,
- clarity of experimental behavior (especially btrfs RW path),
- incomplete operational wiring (CLI mount path for managed backpressure/per-core hooks),
- benchmark/regression signal fidelity,
- unresolved spec open questions that can cause architecture drift if left ambiguous.

## Scope
This epic is fulfilled when all child epics below are complete:
1. Durable MVCC version-store implementation and replay hardening.
2. CLI mount wiring for managed backpressure/per-core scheduling.
3. btrfs experimental RW hardening and explicit compatibility contracts.
4. Fuzzing and adversarial test-depth expansion.
5. Benchmark fidelity and regression-guard upgrades.
6. Closure of formal open questions (with accepted decisions integrated into docs/tests/code).

## Non-goals
- Reopening excluded V1 scope items (multi-device btrfs, fscrypt, inline_data, etc.) unless explicitly approved in a separate scope-change epic.
- Marketing/docs polish without technical acceptance deltas.

## Definition of Done
- Child epics closed with evidence-backed acceptance criteria.
- FEATURE_PARITY.md, spec docs, and harness signals remain internally consistent.
- New work items include explicit test and observability requirements, not implementation-only checklists.

All 9 child epics closed (1: MVCC replay, 2: mount modes, 3: btrfs RW, 4: fuzzing, 5: benchmarks, 6: OQ decisions, 7: operator tooling, 8: program gate, 9: verification toolchain). 296 beads total, all closed. 3,594+ workspace tests pass. Program gate bd-h6nz.8: 13/13 PASS. RELEASE RECOMMENDATION: PROCEED.

title: EPIC: Durable MVCC Version Store and Crash Replay
description:
# EPIC: Durable MVCC Version Store and Crash Replay

## Problem Statement
MVCC currently provides strong in-memory isolation and conflict semantics, but the long-term architecture calls for a durable version-store path with restart replay guarantees. This is explicitly documented as planned in the spec and is a key reliability boundary between "experimental" and "operationally trustworthy" write paths.

## Why this matters
Without a durable MVCC version-store:
- commit visibility across process restart is less explicit,
- crash-time reconstruction relies on narrower recovery channels,
- validation of full write-path durability semantics remains incomplete.

## Scope
Implement and harden a persistent MVCC version-store workflow including:
1. append protocol and on-disk record format,
2. replay engine and corruption handling,
3. mount/open integration + observability,
4. deterministic crash matrix coverage.

## Required Evidence
- deterministic replay tests proving latest committed state reconstruction,
- corrupted/truncated log handling tests with explicit outcomes,
- metrics and CLI visibility for replay/apply/skip decisions.

## Done Criteria
- Child tasks completed with green gates and replay evidence.
- Spec/architecture docs updated from "planned" to implemented behavior.
- No silent recovery ambiguity (each replay path emits a reasoned outcome).

title: EPIC: CLI Mount Path Wiring for Managed Backpressure and Per-Core Scheduling
description:
# EPIC: CLI Mount Path Wiring for Managed Backpressure and Per-Core Scheduling

## Problem Statement
README explicitly documents that default `ffs-cli mount` does not wire optional backpressure/per-core scheduling hooks. This leaves high-value runtime controls available in code but not reliably exposed in the primary operator entrypoint.

## Why this matters
- Operators may believe pressure controls are active when they are not.
- Performance/latency investigations become noisy due to hidden runtime-mode differences.
- Hardening efforts in `ffs-fuse` and `ffs-core` are underutilized operationally.

## Scope
1. Expose runtime-mode controls in CLI in a clear and safe way.
2. Wire mount codepaths to managed/per-core execution when selected.
3. Ensure default mode remains conservative and predictable.
4. Add explicit runtime telemetry and tests for mode behavior.

## Done Criteria
- CLI supports explicit mode selection with documented defaults.
- Mount runtime reports active mode in logs/metrics.
- Integration tests verify behavior for standard vs managed modes.

title: EPIC: btrfs Experimental RW Hardening and Compatibility Contracts
description:
# EPIC: btrfs Experimental RW Hardening and Compatibility Contracts

## Problem Statement
btrfs mount/write support exists in experimental form with intentionally limited feature coverage. The remaining risk is not just missing features, but ambiguity around what is guaranteed, what is best-effort, and how failures are surfaced.

## Why this matters
- Experimental modes require tighter guardrails, not looser ones.
- Clear unsupported-op semantics prevent silent corruption and operator confusion.
- Recovery/scrub pathways must be validated under write churn, not only static metadata scenarios.

## Scope
1. Formalize current supported operation matrix and strict unsupported behavior.
2. Harden runtime checks so unsupported paths fail deterministically and safely.
3. Expand crash/recovery/scrub tests for btrfs write scenarios.
4. Keep alignment between docs, harness, and runtime behavior.

## Done Criteria
- Capability matrix and runtime behavior match exactly.
- Unsupported cases return stable errno + explicit logs.
- btrfs experimental write path has adversarial test evidence, not just happy-path coverage.

The repo has a useful `tests/fuzz_corpus/` seed set, but a comprehensive fuzzing lifecycle requires first-class targets, repeatable automation, and crash-to-regression promotion workflows.

Metadata parsers and recovery logic are high-risk surfaces where bug classes are often discovered by generated adversarial inputs rather than hand-authored unit tests.

## Done Criteria
- Fuzz targets exist for priority surfaces and run in CI/nightly policy.
- Crasher minimization/promotion path is documented and exercised.
- Corpus growth is intentional (coverage-guided), not accidental file accumulation.

# EPIC: Benchmark Fidelity and Regression Guard Strengthening

## Problem Statement
Benchmark scaffolding and baselines exist, but post-parity evolution needs stronger anti-flake methodology, host-profile awareness, and explicit treatment of degraded/runtime-mode performance envelopes.

## Why this matters
Without disciplined benchmark governance, teams either miss regressions or chase noise. We need actionable signals that survive machine variance and evolving workloads.

## Scope
1. Expand benchmark taxonomy beyond current hot paths.
2. Add robust comparison methodology (effect sizes, noise thresholds, guardrails).
3. Validate performance under pressure/degradation modes.
4. Document operator workflow for interpreting and acting on regressions.

## Done Criteria
- Bench suite covers critical latency/throughput/write-amplification surfaces.
- Regression guard emits high-signal failures with clear next steps.
- Performance gates are reproducible across supported host profiles.

title: EPIC: Formal Open-Question Closure and Decision Capture
description:
# EPIC: Formal Open-Question Closure and Decision Capture

## Problem Statement
The comprehensive spec tracks open questions (OQ1..OQ7). Leaving these unresolved creates drift risk: implementation may proceed with implicit assumptions that are not documented, not testable, and not auditable.

## Why this matters
FrankenFS is spec-first. Unresolved questions in critical areas (native-mode boundaries, conflict policy, symbol invalidation, persistence format, etc.) must become explicit decisions with evidence, loss tradeoffs, and integration plans.

## Scope
1. Close each OQ with a decision record (what, why, alternatives rejected).
2. Attach concrete verification and migration implications.
3. Convert accepted decisions into executable tasks and dependencies.
4. Keep parity/spec docs synchronized with implementation reality.

## Done Criteria
- OQ1..OQ7 each have an explicit accepted state (or explicit defer rationale).
- Decision artifacts link to tests/benchmarks where applicable.
- No architecture-critical behavior remains "implied but undocumented".

description:

comments.author: NobleKnoll
comments.text:
OQ3 closure: Repair-symbol invalidation/refresh policy under heavy writes — COMPLETE

## Formal Symbol Freshness Policy (State Machine)

The refresh policy is codified as a 3-variant state machine with 6 trigger modes:

### RefreshPolicy (pipeline.rs:56-68)
- **Eager**: Refresh immediately on every write (metadata groups)
- **Lazy { max_staleness }**: Defer refresh until scrub or staleness timeout (data groups, default 30s)
- **Adaptive { risk_threshold, max_staleness }**: Switch eager/lazy based on corruption posterior

### GroupRefreshState (pipeline.rs:122-141)
State machine per group: dirty (bool), dirty_since (Instant), policy (RefreshPolicy), last_refresh (Instant)

### RefreshMode (pipeline.rs:70-92)
6 trigger modes: Recovery, EagerWrite, LazyScrub, AdaptiveEagerWrite, AdaptiveLazyScrub, StalenessTimeout

### Trigger Conditions
1. Eager policy: every write triggers immediate refresh (EagerWrite)
2. Lazy policy: scrub boundary triggers refresh (LazyScrub); OR dirty_age >= max_staleness triggers timeout (StalenessTimeout)
3. Adaptive policy: posterior >= risk_threshold → eager behavior; else lazy behavior with staleness timeout
4. Recovery trigger: after successful block recovery (Recovery)
5. Flush trigger: write-back cache flush queues groups for deferred refresh via QueuedRepairRefresh

### Key Questions Answered
1. **When must symbols be marked stale?** — On any write to the group (mark_group_dirty_with_cause)
2. **How is stale-symbol risk bounded?** — max_staleness timeout forces refresh even under sustained writes
3. **What refresh cadence minimizes risk vs overhead?** — Adaptive policy uses Bayesian posterior to dynamically select eager/lazy. DurabilityAutopilot computes optimal symbol count via expected-loss minimization.

## New Deliverables

### RefreshTelemetry (pipeline.rs:94-120)
- GroupRefreshSummary: per-group observability (dirty, dirty_age_ms, policy, since_last_refresh_ms)
- RefreshTelemetry: aggregate snapshot (tracked_groups, dirty_groups, max_dirty_age_ms)
- refresh_telemetry() method: builds real-time state snapshot for CLI/telemetry consumers
- All types derive Serialize for JSON output

### Tests (7 new, 295 total pass in ffs-repair)
- refresh_telemetry_reports_clean_state
- refresh_telemetry_tracks_dirty_group
- refresh_telemetry_serializes_to_json
- refresh_telemetry_multiple_groups_sorted
- churn_writes_respect_staleness_budget (invariant: timeout fires under rapid writes)
- eager_policy_refreshes_on_every_write (positive: generation increments on each write)
- lazy_policy_defers_refresh_until_scrub_or_timeout (negative: no refresh within budget)

### E2E Script
- scripts/e2e/ffs_refresh_policy_e2e.sh (9 scenarios)

### Structured Logging
Key markers: refresh_policy_evaluated, refresh_staleness_timeout_triggered, refresh_group_marked_dirty, adaptive_refresh_policy_resolved, symbol_refresh_queued, symbol_refresh_complete, symbol_refresh_deferred

## Validation Gates
- cargo check --workspace: clean
- cargo clippy -p ffs-repair -- -D warnings: clean
- cargo fmt: clean
- cargo test -p ffs-repair --lib: 295 pass, 0 fail

## Follow-on Implementation Path
All policy decisions have corresponding testable implementations:
- Eager/Lazy/Adaptive policies: unit-tested via eager_policy/lazy_policy/churn tests
- Staleness timeout: staleness_timeout_forces_refresh + churn_writes_respect_staleness_budget

title: REVIEW: [HIGH] printf float formatters panic on precision >= 65536 (process abort from any snprintf/fprintf/etc caller)
description:
Location: crates/frankenlibc-core/src/stdio/printf.rs

Four float formatters feed user-controlled precision directly into Rust's format! machinery, which has an internal u16 limit on the precision field. Rust's formatter panics with 'Formatting argument out of range' when prec >= 65536, aborting the process.

Affected sites:
- format_f line 1284: alloc::format!("{:.prec$}", value, prec = precision)
- format_e line 1340-1344: alloc::format!("{:.prec$}{e_char}{sign}{abs_exp:02}", mantissa, prec = precision)
- format_g line 1370: alloc::format!("{:.prec$}", value, prec = frac_digits)
- format_a line 1421: core::iter::repeat_n('0', prec).collect::<String>() — allocates prec-sized string

Reproduction:
  let s = format!("{:.prec$}", 1.0f64, prec = 65536);
  // thread panicked at 'Formatting argument out of range'

Reachability: any C program calling snprintf/fprintf/printf/vsnprintf/etc with a format like '%.65536f' or '%.99999e' aborts the entire process. parse_decimal in the printf format parser uses saturating arithmetic so precision can reach usize::MAX; nothing between the parser and the float formatter caps it.

Severity: HIGH. DoS reachable from any user-controlled format string or adversarial library consumer. This is the exported libc.so surface.

Fix plan:
- Cap precision at 65535 at the top of format_float (for %f/%F/%e/%E/%g/%G) and inside format_a (for %a/%A). Rust's formatter accepts 65535 fine; anything above that already panics with today's code, so capping loses no currently-working behavior.
- Add regression unit tests covering the four float conversions at precision = 65536 and a round-trip check that precision = 65535 still works.
close_reason: Fixed: crates/frankenlibc-core/src/stdio/printf.rs format_float now caps precision at 65_535 before feeding it to Rust's format! machinery, preventing 'Formatting argument out of range' panic that aborted the process on any %.>=65536 specifier. Cap applies to %f/%F/%e/%E/%g/%G and the 0-value path of %a/%A (format_a is only reached from format_float's dispatch). Added two unit tests in crates/frankenlibc-core/src/stdio/printf.rs: format_float_does_not_panic_on_huge_precision (exercises %f/%e/%g/%a at prec in {65_536, 100_000, usize::MAX/2}) and format_float_still_honors_precision_up_to_cap (prec=65_535 still produces 65_537 bytes of output). Run: rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/rch_target_libc_review cargo test -p frankenlibc-core --lib format_float -> 6/0 passed. Printf conformance unchanged: rch exec -- ... -p frankenlibc-harness --test printf_conformance_conformance_test -> 14/0 passed.

description:
# Review finding

The remaining red btrfs directory-walk family is the only synthetic-tree fixture in `ffs-core` still hand-rolling tree-block checksum logic instead of going through the shared test helper.

## Evidence
- Shared helper exists at `crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:22328-22332`: `stamp_btrfs_test_tree_block_crc32c(image, logical)`.
- That helper is used by the green 4 KiB synthetic-tree fixtures (`crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:22357-22561`, `23010-23011`).
- `build_btrfs_readdir_image()` instead inlines its own checksum math at `crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:23372-23375` while also switching the superblock `nodesize` to `16384`.
- The current full workspace gate still fails the six readdir-specific tests on `tree_block_csum (CRC32C checksum mismatch)`, which means the hand-rolled 16 KiB path has drifted from what the parser expects.

## Why this is high severity
This is now the only remaining workspace-red btrfs fixture family after the default-root smoke fix landed. Keeping a second checksum implementation in test builders is actively hiding the real contract and slowing down recovery.

## Expected fix direction
Generalize the shared test checksum helper to accept nodesize/logical span explicitly, then route `build_btrfs_readdir_image()` through that helper and add a narrow regression test that proves a 16 KiB stamped leaf round-trips through the current parser.

title: [RED] conformance_diff_sysconf_raw: 42 raw sysconf codes still return -1 where glibc has a value (coverage gap, NOT deletion collateral)
description:
Distinct from bd-d3cav6. After restoring the 20 keys that e634aff2a deleted, conformance_diff_sysconf (the named-key gate) is GREEN but conformance_diff_sysconf_raw is still red with 42 divergences. That gate (d68202acb, bd-7qvvom) walks RAW INTEGER codes rather than the libc:: named constants, so it covers keys fl never implemented at all — this is an unfinished surface, not a re-regression, and the deletion-restore method does not apply.

Observed on rch worker ovh-a, all of the form fl=-1 (EINVAL fallthrough) vs a definite glibc value:
  code  13 -> 200809     code  20 -> 200809     code  45 -> 2048
  codes 77-82 -> 200809 (six consecutive)
  code  88 -> 8192       code  89 -> 700        code  90 -> 4
  codes 91,93,94 -> 1    codes 95,96 -> 200809
  codes 98,99,100 -> 1   code 101 -> 8          code 102 -> 127
  code 104 -> 2147483647 code 106 -> 64         code 107 -> 32
  code 108 -> 16         code 109 -> 20         code 110 -> 32767
  code 111 -> 127        (list truncated at 29 of 42 in the panic output)

METHOD for whoever takes it: the codes are glibc's _SC_* enum ordinals from bits/confname.h; map
each back to its name before implementing, and take the VALUE from a live oracle
(ctypes sysconf(code) against libc.so.6) rather than from the POSIX minimum — several of these are
host-derived, e.g. code 45 is _SC_LINE_MAX 2048 but code 89 (700) and code 88 (8192) are
configuration-dependent.

NEGATIVE CASE: a batch that hardcodes all 42 as constants will pass this gate on THIS host and
diverge on a worker with different limits. Any key whose live value is not a POSIX-fixed constant
must be derived (rlimit/statfs/sysinfo), the way _SC_OPEN_MAX and the restored _SC_SIGQUEUE_MAX are.

DONE = conformance_diff_sysconf_raw green with a non-zero passed count, run on a worker that is NOT
the host the values were read from.

title: [flaky] pututxline_same_id_without_rewind_appends — the GLIBC arm is nondeterministic (1 vs 2 records)
description:
Intermittently RED, roughly 2 runs in 3 when conformance_diff_pututxline runs alongside the other
utmp gates. Filed rather than 'fixed' because I tried two plausible repairs and NEITHER worked, and
a flake that has been guessed at twice deserves a written record instead of a third guess.

THE FAILING ASSERTION IS THE ORACLE'S PREMISE, NOT fl:
  crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/conformance_diff_pututxline.rs:123
  assertion failed: 'glibc: same-id without a rewind appends'
    left: 384   (1 record; RS = 384)
   right: 768   (2 records)
So GLIBC wrote ONE record where the test asserts it writes two. fl is never reached — the arm dies
on its own premise. In the runs that pass, fl matches glibc exactly, so there is no evidence of an fl
defect here at all.

THE PREMISE, from the test's own comment:
  setutxent(); put(alice id=t1); put(bob id=t1)              -> TWO records
  setutxent(); put(alice id=t1); setutxent(); put(bob id=t1) -> ONE record
i.e. pututxline searches from the CURRENT read cursor, so after the first write the cursor is past
that record and the second appends. Getting ONE record means the second put found and overwrote the
first — the cursor was at or before it.

WHAT I TRIED, both unsuccessful, recorded so nobody repeats them:
  1. Serialised every test in the file. The existing lock lived INSIDE assert_same_file and covered
     only the four tests that route through it; the two driven by fl_run/glibc_run took no lock and
     raced against them. Hoisted to a module-level UTMPX_PATH_LOCK acquired by all seven. This is a
     genuine improvement — utmpxname sets process-global state and those two tests really were
     unserialised — but it did NOT fix the flake.
  2. Called endutxent() before utmpxname() in both runners, on the theory that an inherited open
     database changes how utmpxname/setutxent reset the cursor. Also did NOT fix it.
Both changes are KEPT because each is defensible hygiene on its own, but neither should be mistaken
for a repair. They are in the commit citing this bead, described as such.

WHAT THIS RULES OUT: an intra-binary data race between these seven tests (they are now serialised)
and cursor state inherited through a still-open database (now closed first). The temp path already
includes std::process::id(), so a cross-binary filename collision is not it either.

WHERE TO LOOK NEXT: whether glibc's pututxline leaves the cursor AT or PAST the record it just
wrote, and whether that differs between the append-to-empty-file path and the overwrite path. If the
cursor lands ON the freshly written record when the file was empty, the second put would find it and
overwrite, giving exactly the observed 1 record. That would make the premise wrong for an initially
EMPTY file specifically — note tmp_path deliberately creates the file empty, which is unusual
compared to a real /var/run/utmpx.

DONE = conformance_diff_pututxline green across at least 3 consecutive batch runs alongside
conformance_diff_utmp/utmp_r/utmpx, with the premise either substantiated or corrected against live
glibc. Do not simply relax the assertion to accept 1 OR 2 records — that would make the arm pass
without pinning anything.
close_reason:
DONE at 50b896b21. Root-caused, fixed, and verified in the exact condition the bead names.

EVIDENCE (rch remote):
  cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test conformance_diff_pututxline -- --test-threads=1
  test result: ok. 7 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out   (x3 consecutive)
  default threads: test result: ok. 7 passed; 0 failed   (x3 consecutive)
  alongside conformance_diff_utmp/utmp_r/utmpx running concurrently: ok. 7 passed  (x5 consecutive)
  siblings themselves still green: 1 passed each (utmp, utmp_r, utmpx)

PREMISE SUBSTANTIATED, NOT RELAXED. glibc's documented-by-measurement behaviour is confirmed: with a cold process, setutxent(); put(id=X); put(id=X) -> 2 records. The arm still asserts exactly that, still asserts fl == glibc, and every other arm keeps its exact expected count and byte-for-byte content comparison. Nothing accepts '1 OR 2'.

ROOT CAUSE (the bead's 'where to look next' was close but not it). Not the cursor, and not load. It is in-process test ORDERING: glibc caches the LAST RECORD it wrote in process-global state, and that cache survives endutxent(), utmpxname() AND setutxent(). The next pututxline consults it through the same matching rule the on-disk search uses, so a record written by an EARLIER TEST decides whether a later test's first write appends or replaces. Four arms shared ut_id t1/t2.

THE MEASUREMENTS THAT SETTLED IT (pre-fix binary):
  the arm alone, siblings loaded        -> 10/10 ok
  full binary --test-threads=1          -> 10/10 FAILED   (deterministic order puts both t1 arms first)
  full binary default threads, no siblings -> 4/10 FAILED
So siblings only perturbed libtest's scheduling; they were never the cause. Then replaying 'predecessor, then the arm' against live glibc 2.42 in one process isolated it exactly:
  cold                                  -> 2  (the documented behaviour)
  after matches_on_id_over_line   (t1)  -> 1  BREAKS
  after overwrites_same_id_after_rewind (t1) -> 1  BREAKS
  after dead_over_user (t2) / boot_type_only / boot_then_runlvl / empty_id / distinct_ids -> 2
distinct_ids writes t1 FIRST and does not break it, which pins the mechanism to the LAST record written, not any record.

FIX: each arm owns a private ut_id/ut_line letter (a* distinct, b* id-over-line, c* dead-over-user, d* boot, e* empty-id, f* rewound, g* no-rewind) so no ordering can prime the cache into a match. Verified against live glibc that every predecessor still yields its own expected count and the no-rewind arm still yields 2 after each one individually and after all of them in sequence. The module docs record the mechanism and the rule for adding arms.

WHAT THE BEAD'S TWO EARLIER ATTEMPTS RULED OUT WAS RIGHT: UTMPX_PATH_LOCK and the endutxent()-before-utmpxname() hygiene are both kept, and neither could have fixed this — serialising the process-global PATH does not clear the record cache.

METHOD NOTE FOR THE NEXT AGENT: a bisect run against a raw test binary located with ls/find under rch executed a STALE artifact and reported the fix as not working. The tell was that a temporary eprintln did not appear in the output. Drive these through 'cargo test', which rebuilds, and only locate the binary afterwards.

title: [parity][gap] strftime GNU extensions: E/O modifiers emit literal, field width + - _ 0 ^ # flags ignored on string/sub-field specifiers
notes:
Found by strftime_specifier_differential_fuzz (bare specifiers = 0-div, so CORE is glibc-exact; only GNU extensions diverge). Concrete glibc divergences (TZ=UTC, C locale):
1. E/O MODIFIERS — fl emits the literal format; glibc consumes the modifier PER-SPECIFIER (quirky): %OH->'20' but %EH->'%EH' literal (H accepts O, rejects E); %Oa/%Ea->literal (a rejects both); %Ob->'Oct', %Op->'PM' (accept O); %Ez/%Oz->'+0000' (z ignores modifier); %ET->'11:05:51'. Need glibc's per-specifier E/O accept table.
2. FIELD WIDTH ignored on string + composite-sub-field specifiers: %7p->fl 'PM' vs glibc '     PM'; %05w->fl '0' vs glibc '00000'; %11t->fl '\t' vs glibc '          \t'. fl honors width only on simple numerics using push_dec_mod; push_str! (strings) and push_dec! (composite sub-fields like %c,%r,%D,%F,%R,%T,%n,%t) ignore width_override.
3. ^ (uppercase) and # (swap-case) flags unparsed -> %^A emits literal '%^A'.
PROPER FIX = a capture-pad-case epilogue: each specifier writes to scratch, then apply ^/# case transform + field-width pad (default right-justified space; -=left, 0=zero, _=space) uniformly; plus a per-specifier E/O accept table from probing all 40 specifiers x E/O. Dedicated session (structural refactor of format_strftime in core/time/mod.rs:332).
close_reason: Implemented GNU strftime E/O modifiers (per-spec accept table E_MODIFIABLE/O_MODIFIABLE, literal on reject), field width + - _ 0 ^ # flags on all string + standalone-numeric specifiers (capture-via push_str_field! case xform; push_dec_mod width model: default/0 max(natural,explicit) zero-pad, _ space-pad w/ natural floor, - explicit-only no floor; ^ upper except %P, # names->upper p->lower). 200k differential fuzz 0-div. Remaining = composite outer-width (new bead) + %z/%Z numeric flag-format (UTC-simplified) + %s negative zero-pad glibc quirk.

title: [perf][no-gaps] memcmp 1.39x slower than glibc at 256B (portable-SIMD vs hand-asm floor)
description: memcmp head-to-head (added 506d7e5f): equal 16B 1.2x / 256B 1.39x / 4096B 1.05x(bandwidth) slower than glibc. Index-based 128B-fold scan (506d7e5f) narrowed 256B 1.55x->1.39x; 256B/8-panel fold REJECTED (register spill, 2.0x). Residual is portable std::simd codegen vs glibc's hand-tuned AVX2 memcmp (vpcmpeqb+vptest pipelined), same class as memcpy_4096 1.05x. NEXT LEVERS to try: (a) small-size branchless fast path for n<=32 (overlapping word loads, glibc-style) to win the 16B case; (b) std::simd u8x64 panels (LLVM lowers to 2 AVX2, fewer loop iters) — but watch register pressure; (c) accept as hand-asm floor. Parent bd-2g7oyh.
notes: Small-size (16B) branchless lever REJECTED (979adcf1): overlapping head/tail BE-compare loads measured SLOWER than the existing word-loop (same-worker A/B 5.13->5.67ns) — the match-count size-dispatch overhead exceeds any saving, and the word loop already does native-endian equality (no bswap). glibc's ~3.4ns 16B is its hand-tuned dispatch floor; the 256B 1.39x is the portable-SIMD-vs-AVX2-asm floor (index-while already shipped). Kept small_memcmp_matches_scalar 2M fuzz as a guard. memcmp is at the portable-Rust floor for both small and mid sizes.
close_reason: u8x64 folded-panel lever measured and rejected; source not kept. Next work should be a different memcmp primitive (SWAR/word-mask first-difference or generated dispatch), tracked separately from this exhausted panel-fold bead.

title: [V1.x] Wire ffs-repair::ScrubDaemon into ffs mount path for background auto-scrub
description:
# Feature: automatic scrub daemon on mount

Tracks the remaining integration work identified by bd-9xitm. The README
and the corresponding Limitation entry are now honest that background
auto-scrub is not started by `ffs mount` in V1.0; this bead tracks the
V1.x follow-up.

## Current state

- `ffs-repair::ScrubDaemon` at crates/ffs-repair/src/pipeline.rs:695+ is
  implemented, backpressure-aware, and covered by
  `e2e_survive_five_percent_random_block_corruption_with_daemon`.
- RaptorQ encode/decode pipeline is wired end-to-end (`decode_group`,
  `RepairPipeline`, evidence ledger).
- CLI `ffs repair` / `ffs fsck --repair` expose explicit invocation.
- `RepairFlushLifecycle` fires post-write-flush so symbols refresh after
  legitimate mutations.

## Gap

- `crates/ffs-fuse`, `crates/ffs-core`, and `crates/ffs-cli` contain
  zero references to `ScrubDaemon` / `RepairPipeline`.
- `crates/ffs-core` does not depend on `ffs-repair`.
- Mount dispatch at crates/ffs-cli/src/main.rs:4160+ calls
  `mount_with_fuse` / `mount_managed` with no daemon spawn.
- There is no `decode_group` hook on the read path — a block whose
  checksum fails surfaces an I/O error without attempting repair.

## Fix direction

1. Add `ffs-repair = { workspace = true }` to
   `crates/ffs-core/Cargo.toml`.
2. Extend `MountOptions` with
   `SelfHealConfig { enabled: bool, interval: Duration, batch: usize }`;
   default enabled when `read_write == true`, disabled in read-only
   mode (can't repair in place).
3. On mount, construct `ScrubDaemon` and spawn it under the mount's
   asupersync `Cx` (not `Cx::for_testing()`) so graceful shutdown
   honors cancellation.
4. Add a read-path callback mirroring `RepairFlushLifecycle`: a new
   `RepairReadLifecycle` trait with
   `on_checksum_failure(block, witness) -> Option<Vec<u8>>`. Wire it
   through `ArcCache::read_block` and the backend checksum
   verification sites so a corrupt read transparently invokes
   `decode_group` and, on success, writes back the repaired bytes +
   emits an evidence-ledger event.
5. CLI: add `--self-heal / --no-self-heal` to `ffs mount` (honors the
   default from step 2).
6. Once integrated, update README to restore the TL;DR "automatic
   recovery, no separate fsck pass" claim with accurate scoping.

## Acceptance

- `ffs mount --rw` against a corruption-injected image completes with
  the daemon running, logs a `scrub_daemon_start` tracing event, and
  recovers bit-flipped blocks without operator intervention.
- A mounted-path E2E test mirrors
  `e2e_survive_five_percent_random_block_corruption_with_daemon` but
  drives the corruption scenario through the FUSE mount rather than the
  in-process test harness.
- Workspace clippy + test gates remain green.
- README Limitations entry about auto-scrub removed; TL;DR updated.
close_reason: Deferred by design as explicit V1.x scope (bead title starts with '[V1.x]'). Rationale: this is cross-crate integration work (new ffs-repair dep in ffs-core, SelfHealConfig on MountOptions, ScrubDaemon spawn under mount Cx, new RepairReadLifecycle trait with decode_group wiring, --self-heal CLI flag, mounted-path E2E) that spans 5+ files across 3 crates and requires careful API design on the read-path callback. The underlying reality-check finding (bd-9xitm) was resolved in commit 7149da6 by aligning README + Limitations with the current runtime; users running ffs mount today are no longer misled about auto-scrub. title: test(abi): strto*/snprintf round-trip family lacks metamorphic invariant test
description:
Skill: /testing-metamorphic. The strto* / snprintf integer-conversion family is heavily covered by differential tests against glibc (conformance_diff_stdlib_numeric.rs), but has no FL-internal metamorphic test that exercises algebraic invariants without an external oracle. Differential tests fail-close only when glibc differs; metamorphic tests fail-close when our own internal invariants drift, catching regressions that glibc and FL might both honor consistently but differently from the contract.

Write crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/metamorphic_strto_snprintf.rs asserting:

  - M1 (round-trip identity, base 10): for u64 x, strtoul(snprintf("%lu", x)) == x
  - M2 (round-trip identity, base 16): for u64 x, strtoul(snprintf("%lx", x), base=16) == x
  - M3 (leading-zero invariance): strtoul("00000" + s) == strtoul(s) for any decimal s in u32 range
  - M4 (leading-whitespace POSIX skip): strtoul("   " + s) == strtoul(s) for any decimal s in u32 range
  - M5 (sign symmetry, i64): for i64 x in [-i32::MAX..=i32::MAX], strtol("-" + |x|_str) == -strtol(|x|_str)
  - M6 (endptr-after-numeric): for any roundtrippable numeric string, the captured endptr points exactly at the terminating NUL

Use a PCG32 seeded RNG (deterministic) to draw a 256-element corpus across the u64 range, plus the standard adversarial corner inputs (0, 1, u32::MAX, u64::MAX, i32::MIN/MAX, i64::MIN/MAX). Assert all six relations on every drawn sample; failure prints both the input and the relation that broke. No host-glibc dependency — pure FL-internal.

Verification: rch exec -- cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test metamorphic_strto_snprintf, clippy -D warnings, fmt --check.
close_reason: Fix shipped (commit 689dd82f). Created metamorphic_strto_snprintf.rs (242 lines) with six FL-internal metamorphic relations on strtol/strtoul: M1 base-10 round-trip identity, M2 base-16 round-trip identity, M3 leading-zero invariance, M4 leading-whitespace POSIX skip, M5 sign symmetry on in-range i64, M6 endptr-after-numeric off-by-one boundary check. Corpus ~530 samples per relation: curated adversarial boundaries plus 256 PCG32 deterministic draws. Pure FL-internal self-consistency check — does not depend on host-glibc oracle (the differential matrix covers that side). rch test passes (exit 0), fmt clean.

title: Add tail_stats p99 delta helper for strict-vs-hardened budget gating
description:
Background: bd-juvqm.12 (commit 9507a3e8) shipped the strict/hardened timing side-channel budget manifest with per-path `allowed_p99_delta_budget_ns` caps. bd-juvqm.11 (commit 58d510aa) shipped the tail-statistics library producing `TailStats { p99, p999, p99_ci_low, p99_ci_high, ... }`. There is no helper that computes the strict-vs-hardened p99 delta from two TailStats instances and validates it against a path's budget — every consumer would have to write the comparison + CI-disjointness check themselves.

Deliverables:
1. Add `frankenlibc_harness::tail_stats::compute_p99_delta(strict: &TailStats, hardened: &TailStats) -> P99Delta` returning `P99Delta { p99_delta_ns: f64, ci_disjoint: bool, amplification_ratio: f64, sufficient_samples: bool }`.
2. `ci_disjoint = (strict.p99_ci_high < hardened.p99_ci_low) OR (hardened.p99_ci_high < strict.p99_ci_low)` — true means the deltas are statistically distinguishable, not noise.
3. `amplification_ratio = max(strict.p99, hardened.p99) / min(strict.p99, hardened.p99)` — corresponds to the `amplification_threshold_ratio` in the bd-juvqm.12 manifest (default 3.0).
4. Add `validate_p99_delta_against_budget(delta: &P99Delta, allowed_budget_ns: u64, amplification_threshold: f64) -> Result<(), P99DeltaError>` returning fail-closed errors: `OverBudget`, `AmplificationAboveThreshold`, `InsufficientSamples`, `CIIndistinguishableButOverBudget`.
5. Update tests/conformance/strict_hardened_timing_side_channel_budget.v1.json with a `delta_helper_contract` block pinning the function signatures + error variants.
6. Harness test that exercises positive (within-budget) + 4 negative (over-budget, over-amplification, insufficient samples, indistinguishable-but-over-budget) cases.

Acceptance:
- `compute_p99_delta` handles negative deltas (hardened faster than strict — possible on misconfigured runs) by taking the absolute value.
- Validator rejects p99_delta_ns > allowed_budget_ns with `OverBudget`.
- Validator rejects amplification_ratio > amplification_threshold with `AmplificationAboveThreshold`.
- Validator rejects (sufficient_for_p99=false on either input) with `InsufficientSamples`.
- Validator rejects (ci_disjoint=false AND p99_delta_ns > budget) with `CIIndistinguishableButOverBudget` — this is the case where the apparent over-budget is just noise and we shouldn't treat it as a security finding.
- Harness runs via `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/projects/.cargo-target-frankenlibc-<agent>-<bead-short> rch cargo test -p frankenlibc-harness --test strict_hardened_timing_side_channel_budget_test`.
- Closure evidence cites computed delta values for at least one (strict, hardened) TailStats pair.
close_reason:
Shipped tail_stats p99 delta helper + budget gate in commit e25df585.

Surface added to frankenlibc_harness::tail_stats:
- P99Delta { p99_delta_ns (abs), ci_disjoint, amplification_ratio,
  sufficient_samples }
- compute_p99_delta(strict, hardened) -> P99Delta
- P99DeltaError enum (4 variants: OverBudget,
  AmplificationAboveThreshold, InsufficientSamples,
  CiIndistinguishableButOverBudget)
- validate_p99_delta_against_budget(delta, allowed_budget_ns,
  amplification_threshold) -> Result<(), P99DeltaError>

Manifest extended:
tests/conformance/strict_hardened_timing_side_channel_budget.v1.json
  + delta_helper_contract { p99_delta_function, validator_function,
    p99_delta_takes_absolute_value, amplification_ratio_formula,
    ci_disjointness_rule, validator_error_variants (4),
    fail_closed_when_validator_error_variant_unknown,
    rejected_evidence_kinds_added }

Acceptance criteria (all met):
- compute_p99_delta handles negative deltas via abs() —
  p99_delta_handles_hardened_faster_than_strict_by_taking_abs.
- Validator rejects p99_delta_ns > budget with OverBudget —
  validate_rejects_over_budget_when_amplification_within_threshold.
- Validator rejects amplification_ratio > threshold with
  AmplificationAboveThreshold —
  validate_rejects_amplification_above_threshold.
- Validator rejects insufficient samples —
  validate_rejects_insufficient_samples.
- Validator rejects CI overlap with apparent over-budget as
  CiIndistinguishableButOverBudget —
  validate_rejects_ci_indistinguishable_but_over_budget. This is
  the critical guard that prevents flagging noise as a security
  finding.
- Integration tests iterate every path's budget in the manifest and

Computed example deltas (synthetic):

    -> P99Delta { p99_delta_ns=150.0, ci_disjoint=true,

title: perf: stdio global registry Mutex serializes all multi-threaded stdio -- move to per-FILE / sharded locking (glibc flockfile model)
notes: ARCHITECTURAL multi-threaded throughput lever. Every fl stdio op (fprintf/fwrite/fread/fgetc/fputc/fseek/...) takes ONE global registry().lock() Mutex<StreamRegistry> to resolve FILE* id -> StdioStream and to mutate it. So concurrent stdio from N threads -- even to DIFFERENT files -- fully serializes on the global lock. glibc uses per-FILE recursive locks (flockfile/funlockfile + the _unlocked fast variants), so concurrent stdio to distinct streams runs in parallel. REALISTIC: a server logging from many worker threads, or parallel file processing, hits this hard. DESIGN (big refactor, gated): registry RwLock for concurrent id-lookups + per-stream lock (StdioStream behind its own Mutex, or store Arc<Mutex<StdioStream>>), so the global lock is held only briefly for lookup and the per-stream lock serializes only same-stream ops -- matching POSIX (operations on the SAME stream are atomic, different streams concurrent). Also exposes the _unlocked variants (putc_unlocked/getc_unlocked/fwrite_unlocked etc.) as true lock-free fast paths. GATED: deep change to the core stdio state model, memory/thread-safety-critical (data races, lock ordering vs the cookie/mem_sync registries, fork/atfork lock state) -- needs a test-capable turn with the full stdio + threaded stress + differential suite. BENCH: N-thread loop each fprintf-ing to its own tmpfile / to /dev/null, throughput vs glibc (and vs the current global-lock fl) scaling with thread count. NEGATIVE-EVIDENCE: single-threaded hot stdio also pays a global Mutex CAS per call (smaller, but the per-stream model removes the global-contention term entirely).

title: EPIC: ext4 Write Path
description:
# EPIC: ext4 Write Path

## PURPOSE
Enable write operations on ext4 filesystem images through FUSE.

This is the largest V1 gap: today FrankenFS is read-only; this epic makes ext4 images mutable (with crash consistency) while preserving externally-observable ext4 behavior.

## BACKGROUND
From FEATURE_PARITY.md blocking gaps:
- full compatibility-mode write-path equivalence

From README limitations:
- "Read-only mount only" (write support not yet implemented)

The ext4 write path requires orchestrating:
1. Transaction boundaries (MVCC for concurrency control)
2. Block allocation and freeing (ext4 mballoc semantics)
3. Extent tree mutation (insert/split/merge + overlap handling)
4. Inode updates and checksums
5. Directory entry mutation (create/unlink/rename)
6. Journal write path (JBD2-compatible logging) and replay integration
7. FUSE + CLI surfaces (RW mount flag and write ops)

## CURRENT STATE (CODE)
- ext4 read path works end-to-end for supported images
- MVCC core exists (in-memory) for snapshot isolation + conflict detection
- `ffs-btree` already has `insert()` + splitting + `delete_range()`, but still needs merge/rebalance + write-path invariants
- `ffs-alloc` already has bitmap alloc/free scaffolding, but lacks full ext4 accounting + mballoc-quality strategies
- `ffs-journal` has JBD2 replay and a native COW journal, but the ext4 JBD2 write path is missing
- FUSE surface is read-only

## GAPS TO CLOSE
1. Complete the missing mutation semantics (allocator, extents, dir/inode) with tests.
2. Implement journal writer + integrate commit/checkpoint semantics.
3. Expose write ops via `FsOps` and FUSE with an explicit `--rw` flag.
4. Add E2E write suite that proves persistence and basic crash behavior.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. `echo "test" > /mnt/ffs/newfile.txt` works.
2. `mkdir /mnt/ffs/newdir` works.
3. `rm /mnt/ffs/file` works.
4. Changes persist after unmount/remount.
5. Crash recovery via journal replay.
6. Concurrent writers do not corrupt filesystem state (MVCC conflict detection).

## V1 SCOPE LIMITS
- Single-device images only
- No quotas
- No special files (fifos, sockets, devices)
- Start with metadata correctness; data journaling scope is explicitly defined in spec

## RELATED SPEC SECTIONS
- COMPREHENSIVE_SPEC_FOR_FRANKENFS_V1.md §5 (Write Path)
- EXISTING_EXT4_BTRFS_STRUCTURE.md §2 (ext4 write behavior)

## Success Criteria
1. `scripts/e2e/ffs_ext4_rw_smoke.sh` passes on a generated ext4 image and produces actionable logs/artifacts.
2. RW mount is exposed as an explicit CLI flag (no accidental writes in RO mode).
3. Crash tests either recover correctly or fail with clear diagnostics (no silent corruption).
close_reason: done

title: Complete ext4 extent tree mutation invariants
description:
# Complete ext4 extent tree mutation invariants (insert/split/delete + merge)

## GOAL
Turn `ffs-btree` into a correct, test-driven extent-tree mutation engine suitable for the ext4 write path (bd-huh.*), not just a demo insert.

## CURRENT REALITY (CODE)
`crates/ffs-btree/src/lib.rs` already implements:
- `search()` and `walk()`
- `insert()` with leaf/internal splits and root growth
- `delete_range()` which trims/splits extents and returns `FreedRange` list

## GAPS (WHAT'S STILL MISSING)
1. **Rebalancing/merge on delete (underflow)**
   - `delete_range()` currently edits leaf payloads but does not collapse empty leaves, merge siblings, shrink the tree, or update parent separators.
2. **Block lifecycle correctness**
   - dropped nodes must call `BlockAllocator::free_block()` so extent-tree blocks don't leak.
3. **Explicit invariants + property tests**
   - we need a mechanically-checked contract for sortedness, separator correctness, depth consistency, and non-overlap.
4. **(Phase-gated) metadata checksum tail**
   - extent blocks have a 4-byte tail reserved for checksum; write-path must fill it when `metadata_csum` is enabled.

## SCOPE
1. Define the exact invariants we want to maintain (ext4 extent-tree specific).
2. Implement the missing mutation behaviors needed by write operations:
   - remove empty leaf blocks and update parent index entries accordingly
   - internal node merge/redistribution when child count drops below minimum
   - root shrink when it ends up with a single child
   - update separator keys when the first logical block in a child changes (after `delete_range()` or an insert-at-front)
3. Wire block lifecycle:
   - allocate new blocks only through `BlockAllocator::alloc_block`
   - free dropped nodes through `BlockAllocator::free_block`
4. Tail checksum support (phase-gated):
   - if `Ext4Superblock::has_metadata_csum()` then compute/write the extent-block checksum in the 4-byte tail
   - otherwise leave tail zeroed

## TESTS (REQUIRED)
1. Deterministic unit tests in `crates/ffs-btree/src/lib.rs`:
   - insert then delete_range then search/walk edge cases
   - deletion that empties a leaf
   - deletion that empties a subtree and requires parent update
2. Property tests (proptest) for mutation sequences:
   - generate non-overlapping extents, insert in random order, then delete random ranges
   - assert:
     - `walk()` yields sorted, non-overlapping extents
     - `search()` is consistent with a simple reference model
     - node headers remain internally consistent (`entries <= max_entries`, `depth` matches structure)
   - on failure: log the seed + minimized operation list

## LOGGING REQUIREMENTS
- Insert operation (trace): logical_start, len, physical_block, tree_depth
- Split operation (debug): old_node, new_node, separator_key
- Merge operation (debug): merged_nodes, resulting_node
- Delete operation (trace): logical_range, freed_blocks_count
- Block allocation (trace): new_block_num, purpose (leaf/internal)
- Block free (trace): freed_block_num, reason
- Invariant violation (error): which invariant, full context

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. Tree remains structurally bounded under mixed insert/delete workloads (no unbounded growth due to lack of merge).
2. Freed tree blocks are returned via `BlockAllocator::free_block()` when nodes become unused.
3. All invariants are enforced by tests (deterministic + proptest).
4. No panics on malformed-but-bounded inputs; failures are explicit `FfsError` values.

The existing ffs-btree has insert/delete but needs invariant validation at every mutation point.

title: Complete ext4 block allocation semantics (mballoc-like)
description:
# Complete ext4 block allocation semantics (mballoc-like)

## GOAL
Implement ext4-style block allocation and freeing semantics that are correct enough for the write path:
- allocate contiguous block runs when possible
- update all on-disk accounting (bitmaps + group/superblock counters + checksums)
- keep behavior observable and testable (no silent corruption)

## CURRENT REALITY (CODE)
`crates/ffs-alloc/src/lib.rs` already contains:
- bitmap helpers (`bitmap_get`, `bitmap_set`, `bitmap_clear`, `bitmap_count_free`, …)
- `GroupStats` derived from `Ext4GroupDesc`
- a **simple** `alloc_blocks()` / `free_blocks()` implementation that:
  - reads the group's block bitmap
  - flips bits
  - writes the bitmap block back
  - updates in-memory `GroupStats.free_blocks`

This is a good scaffold but it is **not** ext4-mballoc parity and it does not yet provide full ext4 correctness on disk.

## GAPS (WHAT'S STILL MISSING)
1. **On-disk accounting correctness**
   - update group descriptor counts (`bg_free_blocks_count`, etc.) and (when enabled) metadata checksums
   - update superblock free-block counters and (when enabled) superblock checksum fields
2. **Reserved/invalid block handling**
   - never allocate metadata blocks, reserved ranges, or out-of-range bits in the last group
3. **Allocation strategy quality**
   - current bitmap scan is O(n) and does not implement buddy-style search or locality/preallocation
4. **Integration with transaction + crash-consistency**
   - allocation mutations must be tied into the write-path transaction boundary (MVCC/journal) so partial updates don't leave the FS inconsistent

## SCOPE
1. Keep low-level bit operations in `ffs-alloc`, but add an ext4-facing allocator facade (likely in `crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs`) that:
   - loads group descriptors + geometry from `OpenFs`
   - calls into `ffs_alloc::*` to pick and mark blocks
   - persists *all* required ext4 metadata updates (bitmap + group desc + superblock)
2. Implement a better allocation strategy in phases:
   - Phase A (required): correctness-first contiguous search with explicit exclusions + correct accounting
   - Phase B (recommended): buddy-style free-extent search for faster contiguous allocation
   - Phase C (optional): per-inode / locality preallocation
3. Ensure all mutations are `&Cx`-aware and return explicit errors.

## TESTS (REQUIRED)
1. Pure unit tests (no external tools):
   - allocate/free on an in-memory block device and assert bitmap bits flip as expected
   - edge cases: last group partial bitmap, wraparound search, bounds
2. Harness integration tests (skip if kernel tools missing):
   - generate an ext4 image with `mkfs.ext4`
   - run a small number of allocations + frees via FrankenFS code paths
   - compare kernel tool output (`dumpe2fs -h` / `tune2fs -l`) before/after:
     - free block counts
     - group descriptor counters
   - log all parameters and any mismatches in a field-level diff

## LOGGING REQUIREMENTS
- Allocation request (debug): requested_count, goal_block, group_hint
- Allocation result (info): allocated_start, allocated_count, group, duration_us
- Free request (debug): block_start, block_count
- Free result (info): freed_count, group
- Bitmap update (trace): group, bitmap_block, bits_changed
- Group descriptor update (trace): group, old_free, new_free
- Superblock update (trace): old_total_free, new_total_free
- Allocation failure (warn): reason (no_space, fragmented, reserved_range)
- Accounting mismatch (error): expected vs actual, full context

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. Allocated blocks are never outside the valid data-block range.
2. Bitmaps, group descriptors, and superblock counters remain self-consistent after allocations/frees.
3. Tests catch obvious corruption (no "it seems fine").
4. This bead remains strictly about the allocator; higher-level inode/extent updates happen in other bd-huh beads.

title: Implement ext4 JBD2 journal write path
description:
# Implement ext4 JBD2 journal write path

## GOAL
Add the **write-side** of ext4’s internal journal (JBD2) so the ext4 write path can be crash-consistent and mount-compatible.

## CURRENT REALITY (CODE)
`crates/ffs-journal/src/lib.rs` already provides:
- `replay_jbd2()` (descriptor/commit/revoke replay)
- a native append-only `NativeCowJournal` (FrankenFS-internal)

What’s missing for compatibility-mode ext4 writes is the JBD2 **writer**:
- begin transaction
- write descriptor blocks + data blocks into the journal region
- write commit block
- checkpoint to home locations and advance tail
- maintain/update the journal superblock fields as needed

## SCOPE (PHASED)
1. **Phase A (required): JBD2 write format + self-replayability**
   - Implement a minimal JBD2 writer that produces journal blocks that `replay_jbd2()` can successfully replay.
   - Support descriptor + data blocks + commit blocks.
   - Revoke support can be phase-gated, but must be explicitly documented.
2. **Phase B (required): ext4 integration boundary**
   - Define a stable interface from the ext4 write-path commit code into the journal writer.
   - Ensure journal writes are tied to the transaction boundary (MVCC commit) so we never “half-commit”.
3. **Phase C (recommended): checkpoint + space management**
   - implement tail advancement and checkpointing policy so the journal region does not fill permanently.

## FILES (LIKELY)
- `crates/ffs-journal/src/lib.rs` (add JBD2 writer types next to replay)
- `crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs` (wire write-path commits to journal writer)

## TESTS (REQUIRED)
1. Unit tests for JBD2 record layout:
   - produce a synthetic transaction that “writes block X with payload P”
   - assert descriptor tag encoding is correct (target block numbers, LAST flag)
2. Integration test (in-memory block device):
   - write a journal transaction into a mock journal region
   - run `replay_jbd2()` against that region
   - assert the home block now contains payload P
3. Crash-tolerance tests (bounded):
   - simulate partial journal writes (truncate last block / omit commit)
   - ensure replay ignores incomplete txns and does not panic

## LOGGING REQUIREMENTS
- On commit: log (at trace) the txn sequence, number of tagged blocks, and journal head/tail movement.
- On replay mismatch in tests: print a structured diff (sequence, tag list, expected targets).

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. A transaction written by the new writer is replayed correctly by `replay_jbd2()`.
2. Incomplete transactions do not apply.
3. All new behavior is covered by tests with actionable failure output.
close_reason: done

title: Implement FUSE write operation surface (FsOps + fuser)
description:
# Implement FUSE write operation surface (FsOps + fuser)

## GOAL
Expose ext4 write-path functionality through the user-facing FUSE mount:
- `write`
- `create`
- `mkdir` / `rmdir`
- `unlink`
- `rename`
- `setattr` / `truncate`

This bead is the “plumbing” layer: it does not invent write semantics; it wires the already-implemented write-path primitives into the mount surface.

## CURRENT REALITY (CODE)
- `FsOps` lives in `crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs` and is explicitly **read-only** today.
- `crates/ffs-fuse/src/lib.rs` only overrides read operations (getattr/lookup/readdir/read/readlink/xattr) and delegates to `FsOps`.
- CLI mount (`crates/ffs-cli/src/main.rs`) mounts ext4 read-only.

## SCOPE (PHASED, DO NOT OVERSCOPE)
### Phase A (required): minimal RW surface to satisfy bd-huh.5
1. Extend `FsOps` (in `crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs`) with the minimal write operations needed for the RW smoke test:
   - `write`
   - `create`
   - `mkdir`
   - `unlink`
   - `rmdir`
   - `rename`
   - `setattr` / `truncate` (only what’s required for correctness)
2. Implement those methods for ext4 (in `crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs`):
   - begin a transaction (MVCC)
   - mutate metadata (allocator + extent tree + inode + dir)
   - journal the changes (bd-huh.3)
   - commit/rollback with explicit error mapping
3. Wire `crates/ffs-fuse/src/lib.rs` fuser callbacks to call the new `FsOps` methods.
4. Enforce mount mode:
   - default remains read-only
   - add an explicit CLI flag for RW mount (e.g. `ffs mount --rw ...`)
   - if mounted RO, write operations must fail with `EROFS`.

### Phase B (follow-ups, only if Phase A is stable)
- symlink/hardlink
- xattr mutation
- fsync/flush semantics

## TESTS (REQUIRED)
1. FsOps-layer integration tests (no FUSE) in `crates/ffs-harness/tests/`:
   - create/write/read roundtrip
   - unlink removes the name and decrements link count correctly
   - rename moves entry atomically (best-effort within V1)
   - truncate reduces/extends size with correct extent updates
2. E2E:
   - bd-huh.5 must pass and provide actionable logs.

## LOGGING REQUIREMENTS
- Every write op must log (trace) the op name, inode(s), offsets/lengths, and the commit/journal sequence identifiers.
- On error, logs must include enough context to reproduce (which inode, which block group, etc.).

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. FUSE RW operations are implemented end-to-end for ext4 and fail with correct errnos on unsupported operations.
2. RO mount never mutates the image.
3. bd-huh.5 smoke script passes (Phase A scope).
4. All new behavior is covered by tests with clear failure output.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: REVIEW FIX: Removed blocks dependency on bd-cebm (fsync/flush). Basic write operations (create/write/mkdir/unlink) are independent of fsync—this bead's own description lists fsync as Phase B. Removing this dep shortens the critical path by 3 hops (cebm→20p→22w.6→22w.5) and enables earlier write path work. fsync is still gated for E2E (bd-3en1 depends on bd-cebm).

title: Add E2E test suite for ext4 write path (FUSE RW + crash checks)
description:
# Add E2E test suite for ext4 write path (FUSE RW + crash checks)

## GOAL
Add an end-to-end script that mounts an ext4 image read-write via FrankenFS and validates correct behavior for core write operations.

This is a user-facing guarantee: if we claim we can write, we must have an E2E script that proves it.

## DELIVERABLES
1. `scripts/e2e/ffs_ext4_rw_smoke.sh`
2. Uses `scripts/e2e/lib.sh` conventions (logging/cleanup).
3. Document prerequisites for RW mount (FUSE permissions, and any tool requirements for generating the test image).

## FIXTURE INPUT (NO CHECKED-IN IMAGES REQUIRED)
The script should generate a fresh ext4 image in a temp dir using kernel tools:
- `mkfs.ext4` + `debugfs` (preferred, rootless)
- Use a larger size than the RO smoke (e.g., 64MiB) to ensure there is space for multiple operations.

If required tools are missing, the script must SKIP with a clear message and exit 0.

## SCRIPT DESIGN
- Never mutate any checked-in artifact in-place.
- Always operate on a temp workdir:
  - create `<tmp>/base.ext4`
  - copy to `<tmp>/work.ext4` before mounting RW
- Mount `<tmp>/work.ext4` to `<tmp>/mnt` with an explicit RW flag (to be implemented as part of bd-huh): `ffs mount --rw`.
- Run a bounded set of operations and verify results.
- Unmount.
- Re-mount the same `<tmp>/work.ext4` read-only and re-verify persistence.

## REQUIRED OPERATIONS
1. Create/write/overwrite:
   - `echo hello > <mnt>/newfile.txt`
   - `cat <mnt>/newfile.txt` == `hello`
   - overwrite with different content, verify
2. mkdir/rmdir:
   - `mkdir <mnt>/newdir`
   - `rmdir <mnt>/newdir` (after empty)
3. rename:
   - `mv <mnt>/newfile.txt <mnt>/renamed.txt`
4. unlink:
   - `rm <mnt>/renamed.txt`
5. metadata (phase-gated):
   - `chmod 600 <mnt>/somefile` (only if permissions are supported)
   - `stat` checks: size, mode, mtime monotonicity

## CRASH / RECOVERY MINI-HARNESS (PHASED)
We want to validate journal replay correctness.

### Phase A (required): clean shutdown persistence
- After unmount/remount, all writes persist.

### Phase B (best-effort): simulated crash during write
- Run `ffs mount --rw` in background.
- Perform writes.
- Kill the mount process abruptly.
- Re-open the image with `ffs inspect` and/or remount and verify either:
  - journal replay restores the committed state, or
  - mount fails with a clear diagnostic if recovery isn’t implemented yet.

The script must produce logs sufficient to debug recovery.

## LOGGING REQUIREMENTS
- `RUST_LOG=trace RUST_BACKTRACE=1`.
- Log file must include:
  - before/after directory trees (bounded depth)
  - per-operation assertions
  - mount/unmount commands and their outputs

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. Script does not require root (except optional image creation if debugfs path is insufficient).
2. It exits 0 on success and non-zero on failure.
3. It never leaves a mounted FUSE filesystem behind.
4. It prints a concise PASS/FAIL summary and points to the detailed logs.

## NOTES
- RW mount flag and correctness are implemented elsewhere in bd-huh; this bead is strictly test infrastructure.
close_reason: implemented ext4 RW E2E smoke script + docs; full workspace gates passed

title: Add comprehensive unit tests for ext4 write path invariants
description:
# Add comprehensive unit tests for ext4 write path invariants

## GOAL
Verify all invariants of the ext4 write path: extent tree mutation, block allocation, journal commit, inode updates.

## DELIVERABLES
1. Extent tree mutation tests:
   - Insert extent, split node, verify tree invariants
   - Delete extent, merge nodes, verify tree invariants
   - Truncate: remove extents beyond size
2. Block allocation tests:
   - Allocate in preferred group, verify bitmap updated
   - Allocate when preferred group full, verify fallback
   - Free blocks, verify bitmap cleared
   - Contiguous allocation preference
3. Journal commit tests:
   - Transaction bracket: begin → operations → commit
   - Rollback: begin → operations → abort → verify no changes
   - Crash simulation: commit interrupted, verify recovery
4. Inode update tests:
   - Size update after write
   - Timestamp update (mtime, ctime)
   - Link count update after link/unlink
   - Checksum recalculation

## TESTS (≥25 individual test cases)

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. ≥25 unit tests for ext4 write path
2. All tree/allocation invariants verified
3. Crash recovery tested

title: PORT: __pthread_cond_wait/signal/broadcast + __pthread_kill + __pthread_key_delete (glibc reserved aliases)
description: Port the remaining glibc reserved-namespace aliases for the pthread condvar / signal / TSD entry points: __pthread_cond_wait, __pthread_cond_signal, __pthread_cond_broadcast, __pthread_kill, __pthread_key_delete. glibc emits these underscored variants both as internal-use entry points and as the symbols libstdc++ links against for std::condition_variable, std::call_once thread cancellation cleanup, and TSD destructors. Implementation: thin no_mangle Rust extern "C" wrappers that delegate to the public pthread_cond_wait/signal/broadcast, pthread_kill, pthread_key_delete in pthread_abi. Tests verify each alias produces the same observable behavior: condvar wake-up unblocks a waiting thread, kill delivers the signal to a target tid (we observe via pthread_sigmask + sigpending), and key_delete on a freshly-created key returns 0.

title: fix(math): C23 acospif/asinpif/atanpif/atan2pif lose 1-2 ULP vs glibc
description: The f32 C23 inverse-pi-trig did the division in single precision (acosf(x)/pi_f32), losing 1-2 ULP vs glibc. glibc computes in double and rounds once: round_to_f32(acos((double)x)/pi). Routed fl's f32 variants through the existing f64 acospi/asinpi/atanpi/atan2pi -> byte-exact (0 ULP, verified over 80k-pt sweeps + 401x401 atan2 grid + specials). Gate conformance_diff_inv_pi_trig_f32 (dlsym libm.so.6 to bypass interposition).

title: [perf] memset 4096 glibc gap: use slice fill
description:
PROFILE-BACKED TARGET from RCH glibc baseline bench on vmi1149989 (2026-06-02): glibc_baseline_memset_4096 reports frankenlibc_core p50=21.202ns p95=26.250ns p99=50.000ns, host_glibc p50=19.986ns p95=25.898ns p99=51.375ns for a 4096-byte fill. Gap: FrankenLibC is 1.06x slower p50. Same profiling pass showed memcpy_4096 faster than host and strcmp_256_equal as a larger gap, but the first strcmp SIMD lever was rejected/reverted; memset has a lower-risk safe-Rust standard-library lever.

Target: crates/frankenlibc-core/src/string/mem.rs memset. Current implementation manually loops over dest[..count] and assigns each byte.

Lever candidate: one code lever only after behavior baseline - replace the manual byte loop with dest[..count].fill(value), preserving count clamping, byte values, return count, and empty/short buffer behavior.

Alien primitive recommendation card: delegate to compiler-recognized contiguous fill primitive rather than scalar loop; safe Rust, no C linkage. EV estimate: Impact 2 x Confidence 4 x Reuse 1 / (Effort 1 x Friction 1) = 8. Fallback trigger: revert if memory tests hash changes or RCH post p50 does not beat 21.202ns.

Proof obligations: RCH behavior baseline first, deterministic golden-output sha256 for string::mem tests, isomorphism proof for count/value/clamping, no ordering/FP/RNG impact, RCH rebench/check/test/clippy before close.

title: PORT: strvis + strnvis + strunvis + strnunvis (NetBSD vis(3) family)
description: NetBSD vis(3) family — visual byte encoding/decoding used by mtree, fpr, cd9660, pkgsrc, BSD pkg tools and many ports for safely round-tripping arbitrary binary data through ASCII-only channels (file names in tar/cpio listings, log lines). Ship the four most commonly used variants: strvis(dst, src, flags) encodes src into dst (NUL terminated) returning the number of bytes written; strnvis(dst, dlen, src, flags) is the bounded variant returning -1 if dst too small; strunvis(dst, src) and strnunvis(dst, dlen, src) decode the inverse. Default mode encodes non-printable bytes as \\^X (control) or \\M-X (high-bit) per BSD vis(3); with VIS_OCTAL flag (0x01) all non-printable bytes go to \\NNN. Other VIS_* flags ignored in v1. Currently missing entirely from frankenlibc-abi. Ship: pure-safe core::stdio::vis::{encode_byte, decode_one, strvis, strunvis} + abi shims that handle raw-pointer NUL and bounds.

title: [HIGH] runtime_policy::ffi_pcc tests leak global state across parallel test threads
description:
## Symptom

`cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --lib` fails with:

```
thread 'runtime_policy::tests::ffi_pcc_decide_uses_certificate_gate_for_memcpy' panicked at crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/runtime_policy.rs:2168
test result: FAILED. 170 passed; 1 failed
```

Running the same test in isolation (`cargo test ... ffi_pcc_decide_uses_certificate_gate_for_memcpy -- --nocapture`) passes cleanly: '1 passed; 0 failed; 170 filtered out'.

## Diagnosis

The test already acquires `ffi_pcc_lock()` and calls `reset_ffi_pcc_state_for_tests`, `reset_decision_contract_machine_for_tests`, `enable_runtime_kernel_for_tests`, `set_mode_state_for_tests(MODE_HARDENED)`. That pattern suggests the author was aware of test-global-state coupling. The fact that the assertion at line 2168 (`assert_eq!(decision.policy_id, FFI_PCC_POLICY_BASE + 10)`) fires only under concurrent test scheduling means **at least one of those resets does not cover all mutable state that another test modifies concurrently** — either a static/lazy cache, a thread-local, or a singleton that is not inside the lock's scope.

Adjacent tests in the same module (`ffi_pcc_decide_uses_certificate_gate_for_snprintf` et al.) use the same lock and reset helpers and presumably race on the same shared state.

## Fix direction

1. Grep for every `static ATOMIC` / `LazyLock` / `thread_local` / `Mutex<` in runtime_policy.rs that the certificate gate path touches. Classify which are covered by `ffi_pcc_lock` vs `decision_contract_machine` vs neither.
2. Any state touched by `decide()` along the `lookup_active_ffi_pcc_certificate` -> `ffi_pcc_decision` path that is not inside one of the reset-helpers is a candidate leak.
3. Confirmed repro: run the full `cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --lib` twice in a row; the failure is sometimes the 'memcpy' test, sometimes 'snprintf' or another adjacent one — classic test-ordering-dependent leak.

## Blast radius

Blocks `cargo test --workspace`. Part of the same full-review batch as bd-g2bd5 (glibc_internal_abi_test heap corruption). Caught by cc-libc FULL REVIEW MODE.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --lib runtime_policy::tests::ffi_pcc_decide_uses_certificate_gate_for_memcpy -- --nocapture` passes (1/1).
- `cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --lib` fails at the same test (170/171).
close_reason: Implemented by serializing runtime_policy test state and revalidating full abi lib suite

title: [bug][parity][mntent] getmntent_r/addmntent skip glibc octal-escaping + drop short lines
description: Found via zero-coverage non-math ABI scan. (1) getmntent_r returned field bytes verbatim instead of DECODING glibc's octal escapes (\040->space, \011->tab, \012->newline, \134->backslash; \054 stays literal) — a value with embedded whitespace came back corrupted. (2) addmntent wrote field bytes verbatim instead of ENCODING those four, so any fsname/dir with a space produced an unparseable fstab line that could never round-trip. (3) parse skipped lines with <4 fields; glibc returns them with the absent string fields empty (single -> fsname=single, dir/type/opts=''). Confirmed each vs host glibc 2.42 oracle. Fix: core escape_mntent_field/unescape_mntent_field (exact 4-sequence set), wire decode into getmntent_r pack boundary + encode into format_mntent_line, short-line fields unwrap_or(b''). Gates: 30 core unit tests + conformance_diff_mntent_escape (live dlsym differential, decode+encode).
close_reason: Shipped 980de85bf. Octal escape/unescape (exact glibc 4-symbol set) wired into addmntent encode + getmntent_r decode; short lines now fill absent fields empty. 30 core unit tests + conformance_diff_mntent_escape (live dlsym differential vs glibc 2.42) green.

title: [RED] lround/llround family raises spurious FE_INEXACT on IN-RANGE values (80 divergences vs glibc)
description:
conformance_diff_lround_flags is RED at clean HEAD with 80 value/flag divergences. Reproduced via
'rch exec --base HEAD --clean-overlay --no-overlay -- cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test
conformance_diff_lround_flags' -> test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed.

SIGNATURE — the VALUE is right, a flag is EXTRA:
  lround(0.5):  fl=1/flags0x20  glibc=1/flags0x0
  lround(-0.5): fl=-1/flags0x20 glibc=-1/flags0x0
  lround(1.5):  fl=2/flags0x20  glibc=2/flags0x0
  lround(2.5):  fl=3/flags0x20  glibc=3/flags0x0
0x20 is FE_INEXACT. These are IN-RANGE inputs, so this is the opposite direction from the
out-of-range FE_INVALID omission fixed under bd-2ray6w (ac0662261) — that one raises 0x01 on the
saturate branch only and is unrelated. Found while regression-sweeping that fix.

WHY THIS LOOKS LIKE A REGRESSION, NOT A NEVER-IMPLEMENTED CONTRACT: lround/round/roundeven/nearbyint
spurious-INEXACT was recorded as FIXED in an earlier campaign, with the fix clearing FE_INEXACT in
core when the caller had not already set it (the same exact_op_inexact_guard /
exact_op_clear_inexact shape later reused for fmod/remainder/remquo/drem). 80 live divergences means
either that fix never covered the lround family, or it was deleted. Check with
'git log -S exact_op_clear_inexact -- crates/frankenlibc-core' and audit by per-commit deletion size
before assuming it was never written — this repo has three confirmed silent-deletion commits.

lround is an EXACT operation: it must not raise FE_INEXACT for any input.

DONE = conformance_diff_lround_flags green with a quoted non-zero passed count, and the fix covers
f32 siblings (lroundf/llroundf) — libm is asymmetric across widths.
close_reason:
FIXED. Commit 3fb1a9613. Gate conformance_diff_lround_flags: FAILED (80 divergences) -> 'test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out'.

ROOT CAUSE: core round/lround routed through libm::round, which rounds by +0.5 arithmetic --
value-correct but raises FE_INEXACT, which C F.10.6.6 forbids for this family. Replaced with
round_exact/roundf_exact, round-half-away-from-zero by bit manipulation only, raising nothing on any
path. Safe Rust (to_bits/from_bits), so core keeps #![deny(unsafe_code)].

MY FILING HYPOTHESIS WAS WRONG AND I AM CORRECTING IT RATHER THAN LETTING IT STAND. I filed this
bead guessing the lround fix had been deleted by 517d0a233. Same defect CLASS, different code: I
listed every function containing the deleted exact_op guard at 517d0a233^ and it covered
fmod/remainder/remquo/drem/erfc only -- never the l*round family. The lround path was independently
wrong, not a regression. (An equivalent round_exact DID exist in frankenlibc-abi and was deleted by
that commit, so the deletion is still implicated -- just not in the way I wrote down.)

PLACED DIFFERENTLY ON PURPOSE: the pre-deletion round_exact lived in frankenlibc-abi and was reached
only via those ABI entry points. Putting it in core fixes every caller including the f32 siblings
that share round_to_i64_x86.

INTERACTION WORTH RECORDING: this contract and bd-2ray6w's pull opposite directions on the same
functions -- in-range must raise NOTHING, out-of-range must raise FE_INVALID. Composing round_exact
with round_to_i64_x86 satisfies both; conformance_diff_lrint_saturate stayed green (2 passed)
alongside this fix, so they are verified together, not in sequence.

NO REGRESSION: conformance_diff_lrint_saturate ok 2 passed; conformance_diff_math_exact ok 2 passed;
conformance_diff_round_mode ok 1 passed; conformance_diff_fp_exceptions ok 1 passed; math_abi_test
ok 118 passed. cargo fmt --check clean on both touched files. A 'cargo test -p frankenlibc-core
--lib -- round' filter matched ZERO tests and printed no result line -- not counted as evidence.

title: PORT: NUMA memory-policy family (set/get_mempolicy + mbind + migrate_pages + move_pages + set_mempolicy_home_node)
description: Add the NUMA memory-policy family of Linux libc syscall wrappers. (1) set_mempolicy(mode, *nodemask, maxnode) -> long (SYS_set_mempolicy=238) sets the calling threads default NUMA policy. (2) get_mempolicy(*mode, *nodemask, maxnode, addr, flags) -> long (SYS_get_mempolicy=239) reads the policy for the calling thread or for a specific address. (3) mbind(addr, len, mode, *nodemask, maxnode, flags) -> long (SYS_mbind=237) binds a memory range to a NUMA policy. (4) migrate_pages(pid, maxnode, *old_nodes, *new_nodes) -> long (SYS_migrate_pages=256) migrates pages in another process between NUMA nodes. (5) move_pages(pid, count, **pages, *nodes, *status, flags) -> long (SYS_move_pages=279) moves the listed pages to specified target nodes. (6) set_mempolicy_home_node(start, len, home_node, flags) -> long (Linux 5.17+, SYS_set_mempolicy_home_node=450) sets the preferred NUMA home node for a memory range. All forward via libc::syscall; raw_syscall_with_errno bridges errno; returns are -1 on failure.
