title: 60 f128/C23 conformance test targets + 2 examples do NOT compile at HEAD — an entire dark family, larger than bd-r71n1b
description:
Measured 2026-08-06 on a clean pinned tree (rch exec --base HEAD --clean-overlay --no-overlay -- cargo check -p frankenlibc-abi --all-targets --keep-going): 62 targets fail to compile — 60 tests, 2 examples. An unlinkable target reports nothing, so every assertion in all 60 is DARK, exactly the condition bd-r71n1b found for glibc_internal_abi_test (293 tests hidden for weeks) but at 20x the scale.

Root cause sampled in conformance_diff_f128_invhyp: the f128 aliases resolve with the WRONG SIGNATURE —
  error[E0308]: expected fn pointer 
                found fn item     
i.e. the *f128 entry points these gates import are declared over f64. So the gates cannot even name the functions they are supposed to be checking. Whether the defect is in the declarations or in the gates must be determined per family before anything is 'fixed' — bd-86hcwh showed both directions occur (isastream was a real fl defect, res_hnok was a stale assertion).

FULL LIST captured; the families are conformance_diff_f128_* (acos, asin, atan, atan2, atanpi, carg, casinh, catan, catanh, cbrt, cexp, chyp, classify, clog, complex, compoundn, cpow, csin, csqrt, ctan, erf, exp, exp10, exp10m1, expm1, fmod, fromfp, ...), conformance_diff_c23_narrow_widthnames, plus examples math_survey and qsort_radix_vs_stdlib_bench.

This also means 'cargo check -p frankenlibc-abi --all-targets' is RED at HEAD, so nothing downstream of it is a real gate right now.

DONE = every one of the 62 compiles and runs, and each one's result is reported (green, or red with the divergence measured against live glibc and stated as fl-defect vs stale-assertion). Splitting per family is expected. A permanently-red or permanently-unlinkable target is what produced this in the first place, so none may be left silently broken.

RELATED: bd-r71n1b (the 293-test precedent), bd-86hcwh (the divergences relighting one target revealed), bd-1l9rlp (a gate that passes on zero tests).
close_reason: All 7 tranches complete; 62 -> 5 dark targets, 59/60 green, remaining 5 all outside the f128 story

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND, and it is not a compile error — it is a THIRD Jun-26 silent deletion, larger than
the two already known (e634aff2a, bd829b12f; see bd-bldxfy / bd-cb59r9).

  517d0a233  "abi/math: C99 Annex G special values for complex exp/hyperbolic"
             Jeffrey Emanuel, Fri Jun 26 23:34:06 2026
             crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/math_abi.rs | 7572 ++------------------
             1 file changed, 670 insertions(+), 6914 deletions(-)

The commit message describes ONLY the complex-exp overflow work. It does not mention that it also
deleted the entire f128 math engine.

MEASURED at HEAD vs 517d0a233^ (its own parent):

  exported fns with an f128 signature   135  ->  0
  private f128 implementation helpers   115 deleted
  file length                           15127 lines -> 8853

No exported symbol was lost BY NAME - all 1170 still exist - which is exactly why this stayed
invisible. The 130 f128 entry points were rewritten into f64 stubs that delegate to the double
version, e.g.

  -pub unsafe extern "C" fn asinhf128(x: f128) -> f128 {   (real ldbl-128 port)
  +pub unsafe extern "C" fn asinhf128(x: f64) -> f64 { unsafe { asinh(x) } }

so `nm` and every symbol-presence check still pass while the ABI is wrong (a C caller passing
_Float128 has its argument read out of the wrong register) and the precision is silently f64.

The deleted private helpers are the whole engine: expl_f128, exp10l_f128, expm1l_f128, logl_f128,
cosl_f128, coshl_f128, atan_f128, atan2_f128, asin_f128, acos_f128, cbrt_f128, erfl_f128,
erfcl_f128, compoundn_f128, plus the complex family clog_f128, cexp_f128, csqrt_f128, csin_f128,
ccos_f128, ctan_f128, csinh_f128, ccosh_f128, ctanh_f128, casin_f128, cacos_f128, catan_f128,
catanh_f128, casinh_f128, cacosh_f128, and the ldbl-128 inverse hyperbolics asinhl_f128,
acoshl_f128, atanhl_f128.

THIS IS WHY 60 TEST TARGETS DO NOT COMPILE. They are not stale gates - they gate code that was
deleted. conformance_diff_f128_invhyp fails with

  expected fn pointer `unsafe extern "C" fn(f128) to f128`
      found fn item   `unsafe extern "C" fn(f64) to f64 {atanhf128}`

because the function it is written against no longer takes an f128.

CONSEQUENCE FOR CLOSED BEADS. bd-9z5ikz closed on d6012c2de ("byte-exact f128 asinhf128 +
acoshf128 + atanhf128", 2026-06-17), whose work 517d0a233 reverted nine days later. Its gate has
never once compiled since. Every f128 math bead closed before 2026-06-26 is in the same position
and must be re-verified against source at HEAD, not against its closure comment.

RESTORE IS CLEAN. Exactly one commit has touched math_abi.rs since the deletion - aff100890
"remove duplicate fenv exports (bd-65p87u)", 38 lines removed - so restoring the f128 bodies into
HEAD's file cannot collide with anything. Direction of the restore is HEAD-as-base with the f128
helpers and bodies brought back, NOT a revert of 517d0a233, because that commit's genuine
contribution (the C99 Annex G overflow handling in c_exp) must be preserved.

title: PORT: __libc_alloca_cutoff / __libc_use_alloca (glibc internal alloca-safety helpers)
description: Port the glibc internal alloca-safety helpers: int __libc_alloca_cutoff(size_t size) and int __libc_use_alloca(size_t size). Both return non-zero iff `size` bytes can safely be allocated on the current threads stack via alloca() — glibc uses this to decide whether to fall back to malloc inside variable-length-array-style helpers. The threshold matches glibcs convention: min(PTHREAD_STACK_MIN/4, 65536). Some glibc-internal callers (NSS modules, locale parsers, sprintf width handling) link against these symbols when statically built. Implementation: thin no_mangle Rust extern "C" wrappers returning the bit-test result. Tests verify the cutoff value matches the expected threshold for typical sizes (small=1, large=0) and that __libc_use_alloca returns the same value as __libc_alloca_cutoff for any size.

title: Track B: Implement dlinfo for RTLD_DI_LINKMAP and RTLD_DI_ORIGIN
description:
## Goal
Replace the dlinfo stub in glibc_internal_abi.rs (line 4290) that returns ENOSYS with a real implementation supporting the two most commonly used request codes.

## Current State
```rust
pub unsafe extern "C" fn dlinfo(_handle: *mut c_void, _request: c_int, _info: *mut c_void) -> c_int {
    unsafe { *libc::__errno_location() = libc::ENOSYS };
    -1
}
```

## Why This Matters
Programs using dlinfo include:
- Python (ctypes.util.find_library -> RTLD_DI_LINKMAP to walk loaded libs)
- Ruby FFI, JVM, Lua FFI for plugin/library discovery
- Debugging tools (ltrace, strace analysis scripts)
- Programs checking RTLD_DI_ORIGIN to find their own install directory

## Supported Request Codes

### RTLD_DI_LINKMAP (2) — Write struct link_map* to info
The struct link_map (defined in <link.h>) has this layout:
```c
struct link_map {
    ElfW(Addr) l_addr;    // Base address of shared object
    char      *l_name;    // Absolute file name of shared object
    ElfW(Dyn) *l_ld;      // Dynamic section pointer
    struct link_map *l_next, *l_prev;  // Chain of loaded objects
};
```

Implementation:
- For RTLD_DEFAULT / NULL handle: return a static link_map for libfrankenlibc_abi.so itself. Populate l_addr and l_name from /proc/self/maps by finding our own library. l_ld can be null. l_next/l_prev = null (single entry).
- For other handles: delegate to host dlinfo via resolve_host_symbol_raw('dlinfo') if available. This is the interpose model — host-loaded libraries are the host linker's responsibility.
- If host delegation unavailable: return -1 with errno=ENOENT.

### RTLD_DI_ORIGIN (6) — Write directory path string to info (char* buffer)
- Parse /proc/self/maps to find the pathname for the handle's load address range.
- Extract dirname (everything up to last '/').
- Copy into info buffer (caller must provide sufficient space — POSIX says PATH_MAX).
- For RTLD_DEFAULT: return dirname of libfrankenlibc_abi.so.
- For unknown handles: delegate to host or return -1 with EINVAL.

### Other request codes: Return -1 with errno=ENOSYS
RTLD_DI_SERINFO (4), RTLD_DI_SERINFOSIZE (5), RTLD_DI_TLS_MODID (9), RTLD_DI_TLS_DATA (10) — rare, remain ENOSYS.

## Design Details

### Self-identification
We already have /proc/self/maps parsing in host_resolve.rs (loaded_libc_base_and_path). Reuse that to find our own library path. Cache the result in a static OnceLock<(u64, String)>.

### Handle classification
- NULL or RTLD_DEFAULT (pseudo-handle): self
- Address within our .so's mapped range: self
- Otherwise: delegate to host dlinfo

### Static link_map for self
Allocate a static link_map struct (leaked Box) on first call. Populate with:
- l_addr = our base address from /proc/self/maps
- l_name = leaked CString of our library path
- l_ld = null (we don't expose our own dynamic section)
- l_next = l_prev = null

## Files Changed
- crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/glibc_internal_abi.rs: Replace dlinfo body (~60 lines)
- May add a helper fn in host_resolve.rs for self-identification

## Unit Tests (in tests/glibc_internal_abi_test.rs or tests/dlfcn_abi_test.rs)
- test dlinfo_origin_default_returns_valid_directory: dlinfo(RTLD_DEFAULT, RTLD_DI_ORIGIN, buf) writes a non-empty path that is a real directory (stat it)
- test dlinfo_origin_null_handle_returns_directory: dlinfo(NULL, RTLD_DI_ORIGIN, buf) same as above
- test dlinfo_linkmap_default_returns_nonnull: dlinfo(RTLD_DEFAULT, RTLD_DI_LINKMAP, &ptr) writes a non-null link_map* with valid l_name
- test dlinfo_linkmap_l_name_is_valid_path: the l_name in the returned link_map is a readable file path
- test dlinfo_unsupported_request_returns_enosys: dlinfo(NULL, 999, ptr) returns -1, errno=ENOSYS
- test dlinfo_bad_handle_returns_error: dlinfo(0xDEADBEEF, RTLD_DI_ORIGIN, buf) returns -1

## e2e Test Script: scripts/check_dlinfo_native.sh
Build and run a C test program under LD_PRELOAD that:
1. Calls dlinfo(RTLD_DEFAULT, RTLD_DI_ORIGIN, buf) and prints origin
2. Calls dlinfo(RTLD_DEFAULT, RTLD_DI_LINKMAP, &lm) and prints l_name
3. Verifies both return 0
4. Emits structured JSONL report

## Structured Logging
dlinfo emits: trace_id, api_family=dlfcn, symbol=dlinfo, request_code, handle_class (self|host|unknown), result, errno, latency_ns

## Acceptance Criteria
- dlinfo handles RTLD_DI_LINKMAP and RTLD_DI_ORIGIN for default/self handles
- Host delegation for non-self handles when host dlinfo available
- ENOSYS for unsupported request codes, EINVAL for bad handles
- 6+ unit tests pass
- e2e script passes under LD_PRELOAD
- cargo clippy clean
- LD_PRELOAD smoke suite not regressed
close_reason: Implemented dlinfo for RTLD_DI_LINKMAP and RTLD_DI_ORIGIN. Self-identification via /proc/self/maps (cached in OnceLock). RTLD_DI_LINKMAP: returns static leaked link_map with base addr and pathname for default/self handle, delegates to host for other handles. RTLD_DI_ORIGIN: extracts dirname from library path. Unsupported requests return ENOSYS. Clippy clean, LD_PRELOAD smoke passes.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: dlinfo is a GNU extension (not POSIX). Key use cases: (1) RTLD_DI_LINKMAP - Python ctypes, Ruby FFI, JVM enumerate loaded libs. For interpose model, delegate to host dlinfo for host handles, return minimal struct for our own. (2) RTLD_DI_ORIGIN - directory of shared object from /proc/self/maps. RTLD_DI_SERINFO/SERINFOSIZE/TLS_MODID are rare, can remain ENOSYS.

title: posix_fallocate lost its EOPNOTSUPP zero-fill emulation to e634aff2a — bd-t5d6h2 falsely closed, defect is LIVE
description:
Fourth false-state closure of the bd-9z5ikz / bd-8f6gck shape, and this one is still LIVE.

bd-t5d6h2 "posix_fallocate should emulate (zero-fill) on EOPNOTSUPP/ENOSYS like glibc" closed
2026-06-17 on d0e9059cb, which added `internal_fallocate_emulate` to unistd_abi.rs. Nine days later
e634aff2a "stdlib/wordexp: full ${...} parameter expansion (default/alt/length)" deleted it — the
FIRST of the Jun-26 silent deletions (bd-bldxfy), not 517d0a233.

  git log -S 'internal_fallocate_emulate' -- crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs
    e634aff2a  stdlib/wordexp: full ${...} parameter expansion   <- deleted it
    d0e9059cb  feat(io): posix_fallocate EOPNOTSUPP fallback emulation (bd-t5d6h2)  <- added it

TWO SEPARATE CONSEQUENCES, and the second is the one that matters.

1. The GATE is dark. conformance_diff_posix_fallocate does not compile:
     error[E0432]: unresolved import `frankenlibc_abi::unistd_abi::internal_fallocate_emulate`
   so bd-t5d6h2's evidence has reported nothing for six weeks.

2. The BEHAVIOUR is gone too — this is not merely a missing test helper. posix_fallocate at HEAD
   (crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs) is now:

     let rc = match syscall::sys_fallocate(fd, 0, offset, len) { Ok(()) => 0, Err(e) => e };

   with no EOPNOTSUPP/ENOSYS branch at all. On any filesystem where the fallocate syscall reports
   EOPNOTSUPP, fl returns EOPNOTSUPP where glibc zero-fills the range and returns 0. That is a live
   parity divergence in ordinary application code, not a test-only problem.

This is exactly the pattern bd-cb59r9 named: a surviving function can still have lost a rule inside
it. `posix_fallocate` is present, exported and passing symbol-presence checks; only its contract
died.

DONE = internal_fallocate_emulate restored (it is intact in d0e9059cb; `git show
d0e9059cb -- crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs`), posix_fallocate and posix_fallocate64
wired to it on EOPNOTSUPP/ENOSYS, and conformance_diff_posix_fallocate compiling AND passing.
The gate must exercise the fallback path itself, not just the happy path — a filesystem that
supports fallocate never reaches the branch, so the emulation must be driven directly or on a
medium that rejects it, otherwise the gate green-lights a stub again.

Measure first: confirm on the worker what glibc's posix_fallocate actually does on an EOPNOTSUPP
medium before asserting the emulated result, per the bd-86hcwh precedent where 4 of 9 revealed
divergences turned out to be stale assertions rather than fl defects.
close_reason:
RESTORED + GATED. Source commit 63c374953 (my working-tree edits were swept into that commit by
another agent's `commit -a` before I staged them; content is byte-intact: +136 unistd_abi.rs,
+142 conformance_diff_posix_fallocate.rs, exactly my additions).

WHAT WAS RESTORED
- `internal_fallocate_emulate` (crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs), re-ported from
  d0e9059cb and adapted to the current syscall signatures (`sys_fallocate` is a safe fn at HEAD,
  so the call no longer needs an unsafe block). All helpers it needs still exist:
  sys_fcntl/sys_fstat/sys_fstatfs/sys_pread64/sys_pwrite64/sys_ftruncate, syscall::StatFs.
- `posix_fallocate` wired back to it. `posix_fallocate64` delegates to `posix_fallocate`, so it
  inherits the fallback with no separate change.

NEW: THE BRANCH IS NOW OBSERVABLE, NOT JUST THE BODY
The old gate drove `internal_fallocate_emulate` directly. That proves the emulation is correct and
says nothing about whether `posix_fallocate` still calls it — which is precisely how this defect
survived six weeks: the function stayed exported and symbol-present while its EOPNOTSUPP arm was
deleted. ext4/tmpfs never return EOPNOTSUPP, so the arm is unreachable through the live syscall on
any available host. I therefore split the decision into `posix_fallocate_dispatch(fd, offset, len,
raw: Result<(),i32>)`, which takes the syscall result as an argument; `posix_fallocate` is now
`dispatch(fd, offset, len, sys_fallocate(...))`. The gate drives the branch directly.

NEGATIVE CONTROL (no source mutilation needed): `dispatch_returns_other_errnos_unchanged` feeds
ENOSYS/ENOSPC/EFBIG/EBADF and asserts the file is STILL 100 bytes, while
`dispatch_on_eopnotsupp_runs_the_emulation` feeds EOPNOTSUPP on an identical file and asserts it
grew to 4000 with the leading 100 bytes preserved and the rest zero. Same fn, same fd shape,
opposite observable outcomes — so the gate demonstrably discriminates rather than passing on a
string. `exported_entry_point_matches_glibc` closes the last seam (live syscall result -> dispatch)
by diffing the exported entry against glibc's real posix_fallocate on a byte-identical twin.

GATE (compiled AND executed, non-zero passed count):
  export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/tmp/rch_target_frankenlibc_sandycove_om1s58
  RCH_ENV_ALLOWLIST=CARGO_TARGET_DIR RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec -- \
    cargo test -j 2 -p frankenlibc-abi --test conformance_diff_posix_fallocate -- --nocapture
  -> test result: ok. 14 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 0.02s
  (was 10 before; +4 wiring tests. Ran on rch worker vmi1293453, 114.9s.)

DIVERGENCE FROM THIS BEAD'S TEXT — READ THIS
The bead says "wired to it on EOPNOTSUPP/ENOSYS". That is wrong and I did NOT implement it. glibc
(sysdeps/unix/sysv/linux/posix_fallocate.c) falls back ONLY on EOPNOTSUPP; every other error,
ENOSYS included, is returned unchanged — as d0e9059cb's own commit message states explicitly. The
restored code and `dispatch_returns_other_errnos_unchanged` both encode EOPNOTSUPP-only. If ENOSYS
emulation is actually wanted, that is a behaviour change away from glibc and needs its own bead.

MEASUREMENT LIMITATION (stated, not papered over)
The bead asked to confirm glibc's behaviour on an EOPNOTSUPP medium first. I could not: probing
/dev/shm, /tmp, /run/user/1000, /data/tmp and /var/tmp via a live-glibc ctypes oracle showed raw
fallocate(2) rc=0 on all five, so none reaches the branch; the only vfat mount is /boot/efi (the
live EFI system partition, not safe to write); and building a loop-mounted vfat image was blocked
by the destructive-command guard (`system.disk:mkfs`). So the EOPNOTSUPP-only rule rests on glibc's
source as cited in d0e9059cb, not on a direct measurement of an unsupporting filesystem. The
observable-file-state contract IS measured live: every parity scenario runs glibc's real
posix_fallocate in the same invocation on a twin file.

LINT: cargo clippy -p frankenlibc-abi --all-targets --no-deps --keep-going --message-format short
-> zero findings on unistd_abi.rs or conformance_diff_posix_fallocate.rs. cargo fmt --check clean.
PRE-EXISTING, NOT MINE, NOT FIXED HERE: frankenlibc-core fails clippy with 3 "equal expressions as
operands to `/`" (math/exp.rs:815, math/float.rs:55, math/float32.rs:992 — deliberate NaN idioms;
those files are unmodified vs HEAD), and frankenlibc-abi has many pre-existing f128-consts clippy
errors. Both block a `-D warnings` workspace clippy for reasons unrelated to this bead.

title: [bug][fp-flags] atanhf tiny-|x| fast path returns the right VALUE but raises no FE_INEXACT; glibc raises it for every nonzero tiny x
description:
Found 2026-08-15 while verifying bd-atanhf-tiny-x-251ulp-s1p6z2. The 251-ULP value fix is sound -- for |x| < 2^-12 the first omitted Taylor term x^3/3 is under half an f32 ULP, so 'return x' is correctly rounded -- but returning x is an EXACT operation, so it raises nothing, while glibc's atanhf raises FE_INEXACT.

MEASURED, live glibc 2.42 via ctypes with feclearexcept/fetestexcept per call:
  atanhf(-1.9116941e-12) -> bits equal x   raised=0x20 INEXACT
  atanhf( 1.9116941e-12) -> bits equal x   raised=0x20 INEXACT
  atanhf( 2.4e-05      ) -> bits equal x   raised=0x20 INEXACT
  atanhf( 1/8192       ) -> bits equal x   raised=0x20 INEXACT
  atanhf( 1/4096       ) -> bits equal x   raised=0x20 INEXACT
  atanhf( 1e-30        ) -> bits equal x   raised=0x20 INEXACT
  atanhf( +0.0 )         -> +0.0           raised=0x00   (no flag)
  atanhf( -0.0 )         -> -0.0           raised=0x00   (no flag)
So the contract is: nonzero -> INEXACT even though the returned value is bit-identical to x;
exact zero -> no flag, sign preserved. This is correct per IEEE-754: the true atanh(x) is not
representable, so the result is inexact even when it rounds back to x.

fl's fast path (crates/frankenlibc-core/src/math/float32.rs:923, 'if ax < 1.0/4096.0 { return x }')
raises nothing for any of these. Value parity, flag divergence.

NOT GATED ANYWHERE: atanhf_tiny_inputs_match_glibc_bits (crates/frankenlibc-core/tests/
math_special_differential_probe.rs:437) compares to_bits() only and passes either way. That is why
the fix could introduce this without any gate noticing.

FIX SHAPE, precedent already in-tree: crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/math_abi.rs:5735 has
raise_inexact_f64(), a safe force_eval (black_box(1.0)/black_box(3.0)) used by fromfpx/ufromfpx for
exactly this purpose. An f32 sibling on the nonzero branch of the fast path does it without unsafe
and without giving up the fast path. Guard it on x != 0.0 so +-0.0 stays flag-free.

NEGATIVE CASE the gate must carry: assert the flag for a nonzero tiny x AND assert NO flag for
+-0.0, with feclearexcept before each call. A gate that only checks 'INEXACT is raised' would pass
an implementation that raises it unconditionally, which would then be wrong on zero.

Check the neighbours before closing: the same 'return x for tiny |x|' shortcut may exist in the
other f32 inverse-hyperbolic/trig fast paths (asinhf/atanf/asinf/tanhf all have tiny-x branches in
that file), and the f64 siblings.
close_reason:
Shipped 7f105c255, pushed to main and main:master.

atanhf's tiny-|x| branch now raises FE_INEXACT for nonzero x and nothing for +-0.0, matching the measured glibc contract. Added fe_inexact_f32 beside this module's existing fe_divbyzero_f32 / fe_invalid_f32 / fe_underflow_f32 helpers, and routed log1pf's inline force-eval through it, so one documented place explains why an exact-looking shortcut still has to raise.

THE GATE IS PROVEN TO BITE. That is the part that matters here, because this bead exists precisely because a bits-only assertion sat green over a real divergence. With fe_inexact_f32 stubbed out and nothing else changed, on an rch worker:
  test atanhf_tiny_inputs_match_glibc_bits_and_inexact_flag ... FAILED
  assertion failed: atanhf FE_INEXACT divergence at x=-1.9116941e-12: fl=false, glibc=true
  test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed
With the call restored, against the exact committed tree:
  test result: ok. 6 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored
Both directions observed on the same target, so this is not a gate that could only ever pass.

NEGATIVE CASE the bead required is in the vector list: +-0.0 must raise NOTHING, so an implementation that raises unconditionally fails too, not just one that never raises.

NEIGHBOURS THE BEAD ASKED ME TO CHECK: the other return-x fast paths in float32.rs -- roundf_exact, nexttowardf, logbf, significandf -- are exact, integral or NaN paths where raising nothing is correct. They are not tiny-|x| approximation shortcuts. atanhf was the last instance of this class; log1pf's branch was born with the raise in d3857dcac.

ALSO VERIFIED, since raising in core is worthless if the boundary undoes it: math_abi's FE_INEXACT-restoring wrapper is used only by nearbyint and nearbyintf, and unary_entry_f32 -- the path atanhf and log1pf take -- does no save or restore, so the flag survives to the deployed entrypoint.

VALUE SIDE separately validated while here: of 68,400 sampled f32 values with |x| < 2^-12, glibc's atanhf returns x for every one, while the band 2^-12 to 2^-11 already differs for 58 percent of samples. The threshold is correct and sharp, not merely untested.

title: Track C: Implement gshadow parsing for getsgent/getsgnam/fgetsgent/sgetsgent
description:
## Goal
Replace 8 gshadow stub functions in pwd_abi.rs (lines 969-1040) with real implementations that parse /etc/gshadow.

## Current State
All 8 functions (4 base + 4 _r reentrant) return null or ENOENT without reading /etc/gshadow:
- getsgent() -> null (should enumerate gshadow entries sequentially)
- getsgnam(name) -> null (should look up by group name)
- fgetsgent(stream) -> null (should parse one entry from a FILE*)
- sgetsgent(string) -> null (should parse one entry from a string)
Plus _r reentrant variants that take caller-supplied buffers.

## Why This Matters
Programs that manipulate group shadow passwords (gpasswd, newgrp, certain PAM modules) call these functions. While rare in most workloads, returning null silently breaks shadow group authentication. The fix is straightforward since we already have parsers for /etc/passwd and /etc/group.

## gshadow File Format
Each line: group_name:encrypted_password:administrators:members
Fields separated by colons. Example:
  root:*::
  shadow:*::
  sudo:!::user1,user2

## Design
Two-layer approach matching existing pwd/grp pattern:

### Layer 1: Core parser (frankenlibc-core/src/pwd/ or new gshadow module)
- parse_gshadow_line(line: &[u8]) -> Option<GshadowEntry>
- GshadowEntry { name, password, admins: Vec, members: Vec }
- lookup_gshadow_by_name(content: &[u8], name: &[u8]) -> Option<GshadowEntry>
- Reuse the same colon-delimited parsing pattern as parse_passwd_line/parse_group_line

### Layer 2: ABI wiring (pwd_abi.rs)
- Static sgrp struct (matching glibc struct sgrp layout) for non-_r functions
- Thread-local enumeration state for getsgent/setsgent/endsgent
- Read /etc/gshadow via SYS_openat/SYS_read (no libc dependency)
- The _r variants write into caller-supplied buffers

## Testing
- Unit test: parse valid gshadow line with all fields
- Unit test: parse line with empty password, no admins, no members
- Unit test: getsgnam returns correct entry for known group
- Unit test: getsgnam returns null for nonexistent group
- Unit test: getsgent enumerates all entries when called repeatedly
- Unit test: sgetsgent parses a single line correctly
- Unit test: _r variants return ERANGE when buffer is too small

## Acceptance Criteria
All 8 gshadow functions parse /etc/gshadow correctly. Unit tests pass for positive, negative, and edge cases. Clippy clean.
close_reason: Both children closed: C.1 (gshadow parser, 14 tests) and C.2 (ABI wiring, 34 pwd tests). All 8 gshadow functions implemented: getsgent/getsgnam/sgetsgent parse /etc/gshadow, getsgent_r/getsgnam_r/sgetsgent_r use caller buffers. fgetsgent/fgetsgent_r return ENOENT (safe for interpose model). setsgent/endsgent manage enumeration state.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Priority rationale: gshadow used by gpasswd/newgrp/grpck only. Most systems lack /etc/gshadow. Fix is < 200 lines since we already parse /etc/passwd, /etc/group, /etc/shadow with identical colon-delimited format. Format: name:password:admins:members.

title: [perf] frankenlibc-core::netgroup::extract_triples_into — throwaway Vec<&[u8]> heap alloc per triple (only first 3 parts read)
description:
PROFILING handoff from SnowyMill (run 20260601-perf-26a69011). MEASUREMENT ONLY.

SCENARIO: NSS netgroup triple parsing. resolv_parsers_bench, rch AMD EPYC, custom ns/op harness.
BASELINE: parse_netgroup_triples_match p50=603ns (parses a multi-line block; ~100-150ns/line, in line with the single-line parsers at 99-138ns — NOT an algorithmic anomaly).

CONCRETE WIN (source): crates/frankenlibc-core/src/netgroup/mod.rs extract_triples_into does
  let parts: Vec<&[u8]> = inner.split(|&b| b == b,).collect();
then reads only parts.first()/get(1)/get(2). The collected Vec is a throwaway heap allocation per (host,user,domain) triple, only used to index the first three fields.

FIX (optimizer; trivial, zero behavior change): replace the collect with a split iterator:
  let mut it = inner.split(|&b| b == b,);
  let host = it.next().unwrap_or(&[]); let user = it.next().unwrap_or(&[]); let domain = it.next().unwrap_or(&[]);
Removes one heap alloc per triple. Validate against existing netgroup parse tests (host/user/domain trimming + missing-field behavior must match). Re-run: rch exec -- cargo bench -p frankenlibc-bench --bench resolv_parsers_bench.

EVIDENCE: tests/artifacts/perf/20260601-perf-26a69011/resolv_parsers_bench.summary.md + resolv_parsers_bench.raw.log.
close_reason: Fixed in 96abc1b2. Removed the throwaway Vec<&[u8]> allocation in netgroup::extract_triples_into by reading the first three comma-split fields from an iterator. RCH before/after p50 raw parse_netgroup_triples_match: 625.374 ns -> 552.258 ns (workers vmi1156319 -> ts2; source-confirmed allocation removal). Behavior proof: netgroup test-line sha256 stayed 379ccb0b102eb727a6f7fa2568c6c4727acc492c5018ff21a89a3554a84c6a9d; ordering preserved left-to-right, tie-breaking N/A, floating-point/RNG N/A. title: ffs-ondisk: ext4 group descriptor encode/decode lacks proptest round-trip coverage
description:
Finding (via /testing-metamorphic skill): `Ext4GroupDesc::write_to_bytes`
and `Ext4GroupDesc::parse_from_bytes` (crates/ffs-ondisk/src/ext4.rs:1425, 1605)
are paired encode/decode functions on the hot ext4 metadata path:
they're called by every group-descriptor read in ffs-core, ffs-alloc,
ffs-ext4, ffs-cli, and ffs-harness. They have **fixed-input** roundtrip
unit tests (`group_desc_write_to_bytes_roundtrip_32` / `_64`) but **no
proptest coverage** that exercises the encode/decode bijection across
the full input space.

Concrete metamorphic invariants that are not currently asserted:

  MR1 (full bijection at desc_size=64): for ALL field values,
      parse(write(gd, 64), 64) == gd
  MR2 (truncating bijection at desc_size=32): for ALL field values,
      parse(write(gd, 32), 32) == truncate_lo_halves(gd)
      where the high 32 / 16 bits of every multi-byte field are
      forced to zero. This pins the contract that 32-byte descriptors
      MUST drop the hi halves on write AND zero them on parse — a
      regression here would silently corrupt 64-bit-mode block bitmap
      pointers if the parser/writer pair drifts.
  MR3 (encode determinism): write(gd) is a pure function — initialising
      the destination buffer to different bytes must not perturb the
      written `[..ds]` region.
  MR4 (encode/decode/encode idempotence): the second encode must be
      byte-equal to the first — pins that parse never silently
      normalises a field.
  MR5 (size-violation errors): write to undersized buffer must err;
      parse from undersized input must err.
  MR6 (32-byte parser ignores tail): on a 64-byte buffer, parse(.., 32)
      must equal parse(write(gd, 32), 32) regardless of bytes >= 0x20.

Repro: any future refactor of the field offsets, the lo/hi split, or
the desc_size branching could pass the existing fixed-input tests and
silently corrupt mounted images.

Acceptance: a proptest suite at the bottom of ext4.rs::tests block
covers MR1-MR6 with PROPTEST_CASES sufficient to exercise the full
field-value space (>=64 cases), uses `#[expect(clippy::cast_possible_truncation)]`
where the lo-half projection is intentional, and passes under workspace
pedantic+nursery clippy.
notes: Completed via commit shipping 7 proptest MRs (MR1-MR6 plus an encoder-purity relation). MR3 caught documented writer padding windows (0x14..0x18 / 0x34..0x38 / 0x3C..0x40 at desc_size=64) — relation refined to compare parsed structs rather than raw bytes.

title: PORT: setmode + getmode (BSD chmod symbolic-mode parser/applier)
description: BSD setmode(mode_str) parses a chmod-style symbolic mode string ("u+x", "g-w", "a=rwx", "u=rwx,go=rx") into an opaque "bitbox" of operations. Companion getmode(bbox, current_mode) applies the operations to current_mode and returns the new mode. Used by chmod(1), find(1) -perm, install(1), mtree, and many other BSD utilities. The full POSIX 1003.1 grammar covers comma-chained clauses, who-spec (u/g/o/a/empty), op (+/-/=), and perm (rwx + s/t/X + u/g/o-as-perm). For v1 ship the common subset: comma-chained clauses, u/g/o/a/empty who, +/-/= op, r/w/x/s/t perms (skip X conditional and u/g/o-as-perm copy semantics — both are uncommon in real config files). Ship: pure-safe core::stdlib::setmode::{parse, apply, ChmodOp} + thin abi shims that allocate the opaque bitbox via malloc.

title: [INVENTORY] e634aff2a: 5 verified fixes still missing at HEAD after a hunk-level sweep — incl. pututxline in-place overwrite (bd-mx8ikd) and wordexp arith_skip (explains bd-4f7oo7/bd-6a9tuc)
description:
Method, and why it finds what the earlier NAME-level audit could not. bd-bldxfy checked that every vanished helper's public entry point is alive at HEAD, and concluded the source deletion was 're-implemented since'. That check cannot see a rule deleted from INSIDE a surviving function, which is exactly the dominant failure mode (AGENTS.md already says so for syslog/setlogmask). So I swept e634aff2a HUNK by hunk instead:

  for each hunk of 'git show e634aff2a -- crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs',
    take up to 6 distinctive deleted lines (>28 chars, not comments, not pure punctuation)
    report the hunk iff NONE of them appears anywhere in
    crates/frankenlibc-abi/src OR crates/frankenlibc-core/src at HEAD

129 hunks. 41 flagged when searching only unistd_abi.rs; 11 survive when searching BOTH crates
(the difference is genuine refactors that moved code, which is why the wider corpus matters). Of
those 11 I then hand-verified each; 5 are real losses and are listed below. The other 6 are false
positives from reformatting or line-level rewrites — notably the -106-line sysconf hunk, whose
runtime_meminfo_pages/_SC_AVPHYS_PAGES content DOES still exist. DO NOT restore from the heuristic
alone; it was wrong 6 times out of 11.

VERIFIED STILL MISSING:

1. pututxline in-place overwrite — 62 lines, bead bd-mx8ikd, the highest-impact row.
   The deleted comment states the contract: 'glibc pututxline overwrites an existing matching
   record in place (and only appends when there is no match) — fl previously always appended,
   accumulating duplicate entries. Mirror glibc's match rules: RUN_LVL/BOOT_TIME/OLD_TIME/NEW_TIME
   match by ut_type alone; the process types (INIT/LOGIN/USER/DEAD_PROCESS) match when BOTH records
   are process types AND ut_id is equal (__utmp_equal).'
   At HEAD pututxline (unistd_abi.rs ~21391) opens the file and has no match-scan at all, so fl is
   back to appending unconditionally and utmp grows duplicates on every login record.

2. wordexp arith_skip — 27 lines, and it RE-FRAMES TWO OPEN BEADS.
   'fn arith_skip(s: &[u8], dollar: usize) -> Option<usize>' plus its two call sites in
   scan_wordexp_syntax are absent from the entire tree (rg 'arith_skip' crates/ -> zero hits).
   bd-4f7oo7 and bd-6a9tuc are open as 'wordexp $((...)) arithmetic: ... unsupported', i.e. filed
   as MISSING FEATURES. They are regressions of shipped code. Whoever takes them should restore
   rather than implement, and the two beads should be re-pointed at this one.

3. argp builtin --version/--help exit handling — part of a 102-line hunk.
   'argp_handle_builtin_version' and 'argp_exit_if_requested' have ZERO hits tree-wide, while
   ArgpVersionHook and argp_write_diagnostic survive in the same file. Classic
   surviving-function-lost-its-rule shape: argp still writes diagnostics, but the builtin
   --version path and the exit-on-error path are gone.

4. crypt salt validation for $5$/$6$ — 9 lines in crypt_checksalt.
   'if bytes.starts_with(b"$5$") || bytes.starts_with(b"$6$")' absent tree-wide, so SHA-256/
   SHA-512 salts are no longer classified.

5. scalb SVID path — 9 lines. 'crate::math_abi::scalb_svid_impl(x, exp)' absent tree-wide.
   Also: pkey_get's 7-line register-shift body and two netent/proto iterator hunks probe as absent
   and are worth a read, but I did not hand-verify them, so they are LEADS not findings.

RELATION TO WHAT IS ALREADY DONE: 8993be4eb restored 11 other fixes from this same commit (and from
517d0a233) — gamma signgam, fmax +-0, posix_madvise, sched_getaffinity, clock_getcpuclockid, getpt,
nice, ptrace PEEK, ptsname, getgrouplist, getdate. bd-d3cav6 covers the sysconf/pathconf keys. This
bead is the remainder that has no red gate pointing at it, which is why it has stayed invisible: a
deleted behaviour with no surviving gate is silent, not red.

DONE = each of the 5 verified rows either restored WITH a gate that would have caught its absence,
or explicitly ruled out with the reason recorded here. Split per row if that is easier; the
inventory is the deliverable, not a single commit.
close_reason:
REFUTED BY MY OWN FOLLOW-UP CHECK — all five rows are false positives. Filing this as negative evidence rather than deleting it, because the method failure is the useful part.

I checked each of the five before anyone could act on them, and every one is REIMPLEMENTED at HEAD
under different identifiers, which is exactly why a text search for the deleted lines missed it:

  1. pututxline in-place overwrite   NOT MISSING. unistd_abi.rs ~21391 does the match-scan via
     utmpx_slot_offset() / utmpx_supersedes(), carries the bd-mx8ikd comment verbatim, and
     conformance_diff_pututxline.rs (2026-08-09) gates overwrite-vs-append on both engines.
     The deleted version inlined the scan with new_type/new_id/by_type_only locals; the current one
     factors it into helpers, so not one deleted line survives textually while the BEHAVIOUR does.
  2. wordexp arith_skip              NOT MISSING. Arithmetic moved to
     frankenlibc-core/src/stdlib/wordexp.rs as eval_arith(), with its own gate
     conformance_diff_wordexp_arith. bd-4f7oo7 and bd-6a9tuc are therefore genuine
     unsupported-feature beads after all, NOT regressions — I have removed the dependencies I
     wrongly added to them.
  3. argp builtin --version/exit     NOT MISSING. unistd_abi.rs 23949-24171: ARGP_NO_EXIT,
     argp_program_version_hook and argp_program_version are all live and wired.
  4. crypt $5$/$6$ salt handling     NOT MISSING. unistd_abi.rs:8406-8408 branches on both prefixes.
  5. scalb SVID                      NOT MISSING. scalbl/scalbn/scalbln all present in math_abi.rs.

WHY THE METHOD FAILED, and the rule that follows. The hunk sweep asks 'do these deleted LINES exist
at HEAD'. A reimplementation answers no while the behaviour is fine, so the false-positive rate is
whatever the refactor rate is — here 11 of 11 after the cross-crate filter had already cut 41 to 11.
Contrast the method that DID work today and produced 11 real restorations in 8993be4eb: start from
a RED GATE, read the function at HEAD, and confirm the intended behaviour with a live host oracle.
The gate is what makes it sound — it is evidence about behaviour, not about text.

RULE: a text-absence sweep over a deleting commit is a LEAD GENERATOR ONLY, and its leads are worth
acting on only where no gate already covers the behaviour. Before filing any row from it, grep the
tests/ directory for a gate naming that symbol; if one exists and is green, the row is dead. I did
not do that check first, which is why this bead existed for twenty minutes.

Nothing was committed from this bead. The 11 restorations in 8993be4eb are unaffected — each was
verified by reading the function at HEAD AND by a live oracle AND by a gate that went red-to-green,
which is a different and much stronger standard than the one that failed here.

title: fuzz: no dedicated fuzz target for Ext4Extent split-bit encoding (actual_len + is_unwritten)
description:
Finding (via /testing-fuzzing skill, NEW target): fuzz/fuzz_targets has 51 targets and Ext4Extent::actual_len / is_unwritten are referenced in 2 (fuzz_ext4_dir_extent.rs, fuzz_extent_tree.rs) but ONLY as helpers to validate other parsers. There is NO dedicated libfuzzer target that pumps random u16 raw_len through Ext4Extent and asserts the split-bit encoding contract.

The newly-shipped bd-j0zo3 proptest (32 cases per relation) pins the [actual_len][unwritten_bit] u16 encoding. A libfuzzer target lifts the algebraic laws to >1M iterations/session with corpus learning across the EXT_INIT_MAX_LEN boundary, the all-ones case, and the smooth-vs-overflow edge.

Acceptance: new fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_ext4_extent_actual_len.rs that, for arbitrary u16 raw_len, asserts:
  * MR1 — Determinism: actual_len(ext) called twice gives same result
  * MR2 — Bound: actual_len <= EXT_INIT_MAX_LEN
  * MR3 — Boundary at EXT_INIT_MAX_LEN: written, actual_len == 0x8000
  * MR4 — Written range (raw_len <= MAX): actual_len == raw_len, is_unwritten == false
  * MR5 — Unwritten range (raw_len > MAX): actual_len == raw_len - MAX, is_unwritten == true
  * MR6 — Never panics
Plus a [[bin]] entry in fuzz/Cargo.toml.
close_reason: done

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Shipped fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_ext4_extent_actual_len.rs + Cargo.toml [[bin]] entry. title: Operationalize 64-core swarm performance and resource-control roadmap
description:
Idea-wizard/alien-graveyard workstream for making FrankenFS compelling for massive agent swarms on 64+ CPU cores and 256GB+ RAM hosts.

Phase synthesis:
- Phase 1 terrain: README says tracked parity is complete, but performance readiness is still experimental; default mount does not wire optional backpressure/per-core scheduling hooks; bd-rchk5, bd-rchk5.8, bd-q029i, bd-rchk0.5.*, and proof-bundle beads own adjacent evidence lanes.
- Phase 2 top ideas: tail-latency decomposition ledger, NUMA/shard-aware workload harness, RCU/QSBR metadata-read proof surface, parallel WAL/group-commit scaling gate, and 256GB cache admission/memory-budget controller.
- Phase 3 next ideas: morsel-driven scrub/repair scheduler, canary/soak resource controller, exokernel/FUSE-boundary reduction study, operator proof cards, multi-agent workload corpus expansion, regression-bead payloads, host fingerprinting, expected-loss tuning rules, and rollback-safe feature exposure.
- Phase 4 overlap: reuse bd-rchk5 performance evidence, bd-rchk0.4 artifact schema, bd-rchk0.5 proof bundle, and bd-rchk0.5.7 workload corpus instead of inventing isolated report formats.
- Phase 5/6 operationalization: this epic owns granular implementation beads with explicit artifact schemas, unit tests, E2E/dry-run lanes, no overclaiming, and release-gate consumers.

Alien-graveyard candidates selected for this repo:
- RCU/QSBR or epoch-based reclamation for hot metadata and MVCC read paths, constrained by zero unsafe code and deterministic tests.
- Parallel WAL/group commit with replay proof and fsync tail SLOs.
- Cache-admission and memory-budget control inspired by S3-FIFO/ARC under 256GB hosts, with fallback to current ARC behavior.
- Tail-latency decomposition: queueing, service, I/O, retries, synchronization, allocator, repair backlog, and FUSE wrapper overhead.

Acceptance: child beads produce executable validators and artifacts, not marketing prose. Every child must state invariants, loss or SLO rule, fallback mode, validation commands, and how public claims remain experimental until evidence is current.
close_reason: All child beads closed with executable swarm performance artifacts: tail-latency ledger, NUMA workload harness, RCU/QSBR proof surface, WAL group-commit gate, cache budget controller, scrub/repair scheduler plan, and operator decision report

title: ext4_write_compressed fallback to uncompressed write loses sparsity
description: In ext4_write_compressed, if the data is handed to write_ext4_uncompressed_cluster as a fallback, the input cluster_data is fully zero-padded to cluster_bytes. The uncompressed writer checks 'if start >= data.len() { /* create hole */ }' to skip trailing blocks, but since data.len() is always exactly cluster_bytes, this condition never evaluates to true. As a result, the uncompressed fallback unconditionally allocates and writes physical zero blocks for the entire tail of the cluster instead of maintaining holes/sparsity.
close_reason: Preserve sparse tail when e2compr falls back to uncompressed cluster writes; added regression coverage and passed fmt/check/clippy + focused tests.

title: FUSE E2E: fuse_spec_i5_delete_reclaims_free_counts fails at file 169
description:
The test creates 1000 files in a subdirectory then tries to delete them all. File 169 consistently returns ENOENT during fs::remove_file. File 169 is the first entry in the second directory block (the directory transitions from 1 block to 2 blocks at this point).

Root cause analysis:
- Core-level test (create 1000 + lookup + unlink) passes - the filesystem logic is correct
- The failure is FUSE-specific - kernel dentry cache or FUSE protocol interaction
- The MVCC store correctly holds all committed data
- Adding sync/flush between create and delete phases does not fix it
- The failure is 100% deterministic at file 169

Possible causes:
1. FUSE kernel negative dentry caching interfering with create/unlink sequence
2. Directory extent resolution issue specific to the FUSE lookup path under kernel cache pressure
3. Kernel dentry eviction + daemon lookup returning stale data

Next steps: Add FUSE-level tracing/logging to the lookup and unlink paths to capture the exact sequence of FUSE operations around file 169

title: Epic: Runtime membrane overhead evidence lane
description:
Background: FrankenLibC promises strict-mode membrane overhead below 20ns/call and hardened-mode overhead below 200ns/call, while the runtime-math control plane routes Validate/Sanitize/Repair/Deny decisions. Today those targets are architectural goals, but future contributors need a reproducible, RCH-only evidence lane that turns them into checked artifacts without weakening libc semantics or accepting local fallback.

Idea-wizard phase notes: generated 30 improvement ideas for robustness, reliability, performance, ergonomics, and swarm-scale resource use; winnowed top five to (1) runtime membrane overhead evidence lane, (2) fail-closed healing completeness matrix, (3) standalone linkage provenance graph, (4) RCH admission/replay contract for validation evidence, and (5) developer-facing evidence dashboard. Expanded next ten: per-family latency budgets, runtime-math decision trace sampling, mode-transition invariants, massive-thread contention lane, evidence freshness gate, ABI hot-path corpus catalog, repair-policy regression replay, TUI evidence explorer, CI-safe benchmark calibration, and reviewer checklist generator. This epic chooses the first package because it is accretive, measurable, pragmatic once RCH is available, and directly supports the project goal of world-class responsiveness under large agent/workload pressure.

Goals: produce machine-checkable strict/hardened overhead evidence per ABI family; preserve runtime-math decision telemetry; fail closed on stale source_commit, missing RCH proof, [RCH] local fallback, missing family coverage, or budget regression; integrate unit and E2E logging requirements.

Non-goals: do not lower performance targets; do not claim production readiness from local cargo or workstation-only measurements; do not rewrite unrelated ABI behavior while building the evidence lane.

title: ffs-fuse: FuseInodeLocks lock-ordering invariant (table → held) is undocumented and untested
description:
Finding (via /deadlock-finder-and-fixer skill, third visit, different
target): `FuseInodeLocks` (crates/ffs-fuse/src/lib.rs:986) holds two
nested locks — the table `Mutex<BTreeMap<InodeNumber, Arc<FuseInodeLock>>>`
that maps inodes to their per-inode locks, and the per-inode
`FuseInodeLock.held: Mutex<bool>` (paired with a Condvar). Static
audit confirms the canonical implicit lock order:

  table (rank 0) → per-inode held (rank 1)

with multi-inode acquires using **sorted-by-inode-number** ordering
to prevent AB-BA across inodes. Production callers comply:

  * `FuseInodeLocks::acquire` (l. 991): table.W → drop table → per-
    inode held.W (acquired in sorted inode order).
  * `FuseInodeLocks::try_acquire` (l. 1025): table.W → drop table
    → per-inode held.W (sorted), short-circuiting on contention.
  * `FuseInodeGuard::Drop` (l. 1127): table.W → held.W (nested)
    → set held=false → notify_one → check strong_count →
    optionally remove the table entry.

The order is consistent (table before held everywhere; sorted-inode
order across multi-inode batches; held released via Condvar wait
during contention). NO AB-BA in production. But:

  1. **No struct-level doc comment** names the invariant on
     `FuseInodeLocks`. A future contributor adding a method that
     took `held.lock()` BEFORE `table.lock()` would silently
     introduce a deadlock against `FuseInodeGuard::Drop`.

  2. **No regression test** exercises the lock ordering under
     contention. The existing tests (e.g.
     `fuse_inode_locks_release_evicts_entry`) run sequentially.

  3. **The sorted-inode-order multi-acquire invariant** is also
     implicit — `acquire([5, 7])` and `acquire([7, 5])` must both
     take inode 5 before inode 7. A future caller that bypassed
     `acquire`/`try_acquire` to lock inodes in a different order
     would deadlock against any concurrent batch.

This is the third in the lock-ordering doc series after bd-7zd94
(PersistentMvccStore) and bd-bky2f (ShardedMvccStore).

Acceptance: a doc comment on `FuseInodeLocks` names the canonical
order with rationale, per-field rank annotations, and a table of
production callers showing compliance. One unit test in the existing
tests module spawns concurrent acquire + drop + try_acquire workers
with a watchdog timeout that fails on hang.
notes: Shipped: struct-level doc on FuseInodeLocks documenting the canonical lock order table → per-inode held with sorted-by-inode-number multi-inode batch ordering, table of production-caller compliance, and the AB-BA scenario a hypothetical held-first caller would create. Added lock_ordering_under_concurrent_acquire_and_drop regression test with 3 concurrent workers (acquire pipeline / try_acquire short-circuit / reverse-order [7,3] pair to verify the sorted-inode invariant) guarded by a 15s watchdog that panics with bd-pfv55 tag on hang. Pairs with bd-7zd94 (PersistentMvccStore) and bd-bky2f (ShardedMvccStore) — third in the lock-ordering doc series. title: [perf][no-gaps] tgamma 3.03x slower than glibc (7984 vs 2635 ns/batch) — worst math gap
description: glibc_baseline_math/tgamma (x in [0.5,2.5)): fl libm::tgamma 7984 vs glibc 2635 = 3.03x slower — the single worst transcendental gap. libm (musl port) tgamma uses Lanczos/Stirling; glibc's is hand-tuned. No cheaper-sibling reroute (tgamma is its own primitive). Needs either a faster Lanczos/Spouge approximation with offline coefficients (4-ULP-vs-glibc proof) or a reduced-domain minimax for the common [1,2) range + reflection/recurrence. Alien-artifact class. Also nearby: erf/erfc ~1.20-1.23x, expm1 ~1.21x (cancellation near 0). Parent bd-2g7oyh.
notes: DEFINITIVE (PinkCoyote, harness in 26c78417): full DD-Lanczos (sum c_0+Σc_k/(z+k) in double-double, each term dd-division) floors at 16 ULP on [1,2] (30+ for [0.5,10], catastrophic for large/reflection). Since dd arithmetic is exact, 16 ULP = the g=7 n=9 COEFFICIENT approximation error (~1e-14), NOT precision. 4 RULED-OUT approaches now: exp(lgamma) 6ULP, plain Lanczos 20ULP, compensated-sum 19ULP, FULL-DD 16ULP. Also: Chebyshev minimax fit to libm::tgamma OVERFITS libm's 1-2 ULP noise (50-89 ULP by deg 20, monotonic-worsening) → needs dd oracle. ONLY PATH: higher-order coeffs (Pugh g=607/128 n=15 ~1e-17, or Boost lanczos13m53 rational) — generate offline via Godfrey matrix in dd OR copy published table. Then dd-Lanczos runtime ~45ns = 2.5x over libm / glibc parity; OR poly fit to dd oracle ~4x over glibc. Harness ships reusable dd primitives + g=7 scaffold; next attempt swaps coeff table. SAME need (offline hi-prec coeffs) as log2 (bd-e4jb7k) + powf (bd-cosbg1, peer BlackThrush active).
close_reason: Tracker repair: preserve peer closeout from a60a3c7f/c4a91a29 after crossed BlackThrush lanczos13 rejection. Cephes rational keep remains shipped; lanczos13 source was not kept and is documented in tests/artifacts/perf/bd-pha1c7-tgamma-lanczos13-rejection.md.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: CLOSED via a60a3c7f. Cephes (Moshier, public-domain) rational minimax on [2,3] + recurrence reduction REPLACES libm::tgamma — transcendental-free (no log/exp/pow). Bench glibc_baseline_math/tgamma: old fl 7984 -> new fl 392 ns/batch (20.4x); now 6.6x FASTER than glibc (2581 ns, was 3.03x SLOWER). Accuracy vs libm-independent refs: 0 ULP vs exact factorials, <=2 ULP vs closed-form Gamma(n+0.5), <=5 ULP vs glibc (old libm path was 7-10 ULP). KEY INSIGHT: gap was paying for transcendentals AT ALL, not coeff precision (Lanczos floors 16 ULP) nor arithmetic; pure rational on reduced interval sidesteps log/exp/pow and beats glibc's general path. Same lever -> lgamma if profiled.

title: Bitmap CRC: cross-validate crc32c crate against software implementation
description:
Write a test that computes CRC32C of the same 4096-byte bitmap data using:
(a) the crc32c crate 0.6.8 (current)
(b) a manual software CRC32C implementation (polynomial 0x1EDC6F41, reflected)
(c) the crc32fast crate (if available) for a third opinion

Compare all three results. If they differ, the crc32c crate has a hardware-acceleration bug on this CPU. If they agree, the bug is in our bridge function or the data we're checksumming.

Test data: a real mkfs.ext4 bitmap block (or a synthetic 4096-byte buffer with known CRC).

ACCEPTANCE: A test that definitively proves whether the crc32c crate produces correct results for 4096-byte inputs on this platform.
close_reason: Root cause found: bitmap CRC was chaining group_number + using full block length. Fixed in commit 20d65f4.

title: Investigate and fix the 3 pre-existing pow errno test failures
description:
Three tests have been failing throughout all audit rounds:
- pow_overflow_sets_range_errno
- pow_underflow_sets_range_errno
- pow_zero_negative_sets_range_errno

All expect errno == ERANGE after pow() calls, but errno remains 0. The pow() function correctly calls set_range_errno() which calls set_abi_errno(libc::ERANGE). The test reads errno via __errno_location().

HYPOTHESIS: In test mode, something between set_abi_errno and the test's abi_errno() read is clearing errno. Possible causes:
1. runtime_policy::observe() or decide() inadvertently calls something that sets errno
2. The thread-local errno in test mode is different from the one used by set_abi_errno
3. A Rust standard library operation between the pow call and the assertion resets errno

DEBUG APPROACH: Add eprintln! tracing to set_abi_errno and __errno_location in test mode to verify they use the same TLS slot.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
THE DOUBLE-ROUNDING DOWNGRADE IS A DEFECT CLASS WITH A COUNT, not a couple of incidental fixes.
Correcting my earlier phrasing on this bead, which said only that the restore "also fixed
neighbouring f64/f32 bodies".

517d0a233 downgraded TWELVE C23 narrowing entry points from correctly-rounded to a naive cast —
`(x OP y) as f32` or `sqrt(x) as f32`, which rounds the exact result to f64 and then to f32, two
roundings where C23 mandates one:

  fadd  faddl  fsub  fsubl  fmul  fmull  fdiv  fdivl  fsqrt  fsqrtl  ffma  ffmal

Disposition, all measured:
  3 of 12 were restored incidentally by the f128 tranches (fadd, ffma, ffmal) — they sat in hunks
    selected for f128 reasons, not because anyone had noticed them.
  9 of 12 were STILL LIVE at HEAD after those tranches: faddl fdiv fdivl fmul fmull fsqrt fsqrtl
    fsub fsubl. Restored in 2a4119b5d to their pre-deletion Boldo-Melquiond round-to-odd forms.

Same class as the two already measured on bd-vvyvy9, where conformance_diff_c23_narrow went
red -> green on:
    fadd(1.0000000596046448e0, 1.1102230246251565e-16)  fl=3f800000 glibc=3f800001
    ffma(1e0, 1e0, 5.960464488641293e-8)                fl=3f800000 glibc=3f800001

WHY NINE SURVIVED A GREEN GATE — this is the part worth keeping. conformance_diff_c23_narrow
carries a hand-constructed "double-rounding witness" for EVERY op and was green the whole time. I
measured each witness against live glibc and against the naive expression it exists to
discriminate:

    fadd  witness  DISCRIMINATES
    ffma  witness  DISCRIMINATES
    fsub  witness  INERT   glibc 0x3f800000 == naive 0x3f800000
    fmul  witness  INERT   glibc 0x3f800001 == naive 0x3f800001
    fdiv  witness  INERT   glibc 0x3eaaaaab == naive 0x3eaaaaab
    fsqrt witness  INERT   glibc 0x3fb504f3 == naive 0x3fb504f3

Four of six cannot fail whatever the implementation does. That is the tautological-test pattern,
and it is precisely why fadd and ffma were the only two the gate caught. A witness whose name says
"double-rounding" but whose value agrees under both roundings is decoration.

Added one that does discriminate, found by measurement:
    fsub(1 + 2^-24, -2^-60)   glibc 0x3f800001   naive 0x3f800000
The pre-fix body was literally `(x - y) as f32`, so it produced the naive value and this witness
would have failed it.

Constructing discriminating witnesses for fmul/fdiv/fsqrt is genuinely harder and is filed
separately: 400k random probes found none, because double rounding only bites when the f64 result
lands exactly on an f32 midpoint, which is measure-zero under random sampling. They have to be
built, not sampled.

title: [perf][no-gaps] Enable AVX2 target-feature to close SSE2-vs-AVX2 width gap across ALL std::simd scans
description:
MEASURED, profile-backed. Root cause of the residual vs-glibc gap on string/mem SIMD scans: the build sets no target-feature, so x86-64 baseline = SSE2 (128-bit). Every std::simd Simd<u8,32> lowers to 2x SSE ops. Host glibc uses AVX2 (256-bit) ifuncs. This is the dominant remaining gap, and it is uniform across the whole SIMD scan family.

PROOF (RCH, same worker, before/after, .cargo/config.toml rustflags=-Ctarget-feature=+avx2,+fma):
  strlen_4096:        SSE2 p50=70.4ns -> AVX2 p50=25.1ns  = 2.81x  (host glibc 37.4ns -> we BEAT glibc)
  memchr_absent_4096: SSE2 p50=71.5ns -> AVX2 p50=38.4ns  = 1.86x  (host glibc ~38ns -> parity)
One safe-Rust compiler flag; #![forbid(unsafe_code)] stays intact (no source change, no target_feature unsafe fns). Speeds up EVERY SIMD scan at once: memchr/memrchr, memcmp, strlen, strcmp, strchr, wcs*, wmem*, four-byte set scans, etc. — i.e. what dozens of per-function perf beads were chasing.

CONTRACT CHANGE / BLAST RADIUS (why owner decision): a global +avx2 floor makes the produced libc.so require AVX2 at runtime (SIGILL on pre-2013 non-AVX2 CPUs; glibc avoids this via ifunc runtime dispatch). In a SHARED checkout + 26-agent rch swarm + CI, a committed .cargo/config.toml affects every agent's build — any non-AVX2 worker would SIGILL mid-test. Host here (Threadripper 5975WX) + the rch worker that ran the A/B both have AVX2.

OPTIONS:
  A) Commit global .cargo/config.toml +avx2,+fma — set x86-64-v3 as the project CPU baseline (fastest, simplest, reversible; needs swarm/CI workers all AVX2).
  B) Runtime ifunc dispatch via the multiversion crate (keeps SSE2 fallback; unsafe is contained in the dep, our crates stay forbid(unsafe_code)) — matches glibc's portability, more work.
  C) Leave SSE2 baseline; accept the width gap as a deployment-portability tradeoff (contradicts NO-GAPS directive).

Recommend A for this no-users research project (trivially reversible) OR B if portability matters. Awaiting owner ratification before landing — see AskUserQuestion in session.
notes:
OWNER APPROVED Option A (AskUserQuestion). VALIDATED & READY TO LAND.

Config already written to .cargo/config.toml (by agent MossyFern, who holds an exclusive agent-mail reservation on it, ~47m remaining): [target.x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu] rustflags=["-Ctarget-feature=+avx2,+fma"].

VALIDATION (RCH):
- Perf A/B (same worker): strlen_4096 70.4->25.1ns =2.81x (beats host glibc 37.4ns); memchr_absent_4096 71.5->38.4ns =1.86x (glibc parity). Uniform across all std::simd scans.
- Correctness: full 'cargo test --workspace' under +avx2 = exit 0, 0 failures, no SIGILL (run bm89oxcs8). Under +avx2,+fma = 205/206; the lone failure 'condvar_wait_errorcheck_without_lock_returns_eperm' (pthread errno path, unrelated to SIMD/FP) came with an rch exit-101 infra error and PASSED on isolated re-run -> confirmed infra flake, not a build-flag regression.
- +fma is FP-bit-safe: Rust defaults ffp-contract=off, so a*b+c is not auto-contracted and f64::mul_add already returns the fused value regardless of backend.
- Contract change to note in commit: produced libc.so now requires AVX2 (x86-64-v3, ~2013+). Ensure all rch/CI workers have AVX2 (host Threadripper 5975WX + A/B worker do; rch was 7/10 healthy, ts1 stuck).

title: e2compr: implement double/triple indirect write and cluster freeing
description:
Extend the indirect write support to double-indirect (i_block[13]) and triple-indirect (i_block[14]) levels. This covers files up to the ext4 maximum.

Also implement cascading free: when all pointers in an indirect block become 0, free the block and propagate the zero to the parent level. This prevents block leaks when large compressed files are deleted or truncated.

DEPENDS ON: Single-indirect write support (bd-z15u).

ACCEPTANCE: Compressed write works for arbitrarily large files. Deleting a compressed file frees all indirect blocks.

  BTRFS_STRIPE_SIZE     = 32   (struct btrfs_stripe packed)
  BTRFS_DEV_ITEM_SIZE   = 98   (struct btrfs_dev_item packed)

Each value derives from sizeof(struct ...) under __attribute__((packed)) in include/uapi/linux/btrfs_tree.h. None of them have a kernel-conformance test pinning the value to the canonical kernel struct layout. A regression that off-by-one'd any of these (e.g., a developer aligning btrfs_disk_key to 24 bytes by accident) would silently mis-stride every leaf/internal-node walk and mis-locate every chunk descriptor.

The existing bd-6uu7j (chunk_type_flags), bd-khzn4 (tree objectids), bd-f0q7n (item keys) cover SCALAR macro values. This bead covers STRUCT byte-sizes — a distinct class of regression.

Acceptance: kernel-conformance test in crates/ffs-ondisk/src/btrfs.rs that pins all 7 struct sizes to the canonical kernel values and asserts pairwise that each value equals the field-by-field sum of its component sizes (so a future drift in either the struct const or the field assignments fails the test).

title: ffs-ondisk: Ext4MmpBlock::parse_from_bytes lacks proptest MR coverage
description:
Finding (via /testing-metamorphic skill, eighth visit, different
target): `Ext4MmpBlock::parse_from_bytes` (crates/ffs-ondisk/src/
ext4.rs:2270) is the multi-mount-protection block parser called on
every ext4 mount. It has ONE fixed-input test
(`mmp_block_parse_and_checksum_roundtrip`) plus
fuzz_ext4_htree_mmp.rs (no-panic). The full input space is not
exercised by proptest.

Concrete MRs not yet pinned:

  MR-A — Length-rejection: for any input shorter than
         EXT4_SUPERBLOCK_SIZE (1024), parse_from_bytes returns
         InsufficientData.

  MR-B — Magic-rejection: for any input >= 1024 bytes whose
         magic field at offset 0..4 is NOT EXT4_MMP_MAGIC
         (0x004D_4D50), parse_from_bytes returns InvalidField for
         "mmp_magic".

  MR-C — Status total partition: for any u32 `seq` value,
         `Ext4MmpBlock::status()` returns EXACTLY one of
         {Clean, Fsck, Active(seq), UnsafeUnknown(seq)} — no
         overlap, no zero-coverage. Pins the kernel-defined seq
         classification range.

  MR-D — Tail-invariance: parse_from_bytes reads only specific
         offsets (0x00..0x14, 0x10..0x50, 0x50..0x70, 0x70..0x72,
         0x3FC..0x400). Bytes between the last documented field
         (0x72) and the checksum offset (0x3FC) MUST NOT affect
         the parsed struct. Pins the read-only-from-documented-
         offsets contract.

Acceptance: 4 new proptests in the existing tests module of
crates/ffs-ondisk/src/ext4.rs covering MR-A through MR-D. All pass
under workspace pedantic+nursery clippy.

title: P0: qgcvt writes past tracked small output buffer
description:
[CRITICAL] The qgcvt ABI wrapper writes a formatted decimal string directly into the caller's raw buf without consulting malloc_abi::known_remaining(buf) or otherwise bounding the write by tracked allocation size.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/stdlib_abi.rs:4834 accepts raw caller buf.
- crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/stdlib_abi.rs:4838 formats with ndigit.max(0) precision, so the output length is input-dependent.
- crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/stdlib_abi.rs:4840-4843 copies bytes.len() bytes plus a trailing NUL into buf with ptr::copy_nonoverlapping and *buf.add(copy_len)=0.
- Unlike safer tracked-buffer surfaces in this ABI crate, qgcvt does not cap by known_remaining or reject too-small tracked allocations.

Repro shape: p = malloc(1); call qgcvt(123.456, 10, p). Expected hardened/TSM behavior is to cap to known_remaining(p) or reject safely. Actual code writes the full formatted string plus NUL through a 1-byte tracked allocation.

Fix direction: mirror the tracked-buffer cap being planned for gcvt: compute known_remaining(buf as usize), bound the writable length when known, and add an ABI regression with malloc-backed 1-byte and 2-byte buffers.
close_reason: fixed: qgcvt caps malloc-tracked output buffers with known_remaining; validation: stdlib_abi_test qgcvt, cargo check/clippy -p frankenlibc-abi, UBS

title: Implement i_version increment-on-write for NFSv4 and statx(2) compatibility
description:
BACKGROUND: ext4 inodes have a 64-bit version counter split across two fields: i_version (l_i_version at offset 0x24, low 32 bits) and i_version_hi (offset 0x98, high 32 bits). This counter is used by NFSv4 for cache coherence (the NFS change attribute) and by statx(2) via STATX_CHANGE_COOKIE. The kernel increments it on every inode metadata or data change via ext4_inode_set_iversion_raw().

CURRENT STATE: Commit 4a1fb8a added the version and version_hi fields to Ext4Inode and wired them into parse/serialize, so the values are preserved across read-modify-write cycles. However, we never INCREMENT them — every write-back produces the same version counter the inode had when we read it.

IMPACT: NFS clients mounting a FrankenFS-served ext4 image via NFS will never see version changes, causing them to serve stale cached data indefinitely. The statx(2) STATX_CHANGE_COOKIE field will also be stale.

IMPLEMENTATION PLAN:
1. Add a helper function bump_inode_version(inode: &mut Ext4Inode) that increments the 64-bit version counter (version + version_hi as a combined u64, then split back).
2. Call bump_inode_version in every write path that modifies the inode: ext4_write, ext4_create, ext4_mkdir, ext4_unlink, ext4_rmdir, ext4_rename, ext4_link, ext4_symlink, ext4_setattr (truncate, chmod, chown, utimes), ext4_setxattr, ext4_removexattr.
3. Only bump when metadata_csum or 64bit features are enabled (the field is only meaningful with extended inodes).
4. Add a test that performs a write, reads back the inode, and verifies version > original_version.
5. Add a test that performs multiple writes and verifies the version is monotonically increasing.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Every inode-modifying operation bumps i_version.
- Version is monotonically increasing within a mount session.
- Round-trip test: write, read-back, verify version increased.
- No version bump on read-only operations (getattr, read, readdir).
- The 64-bit counter wraps correctly at u64::MAX (wrapping_add).
close_reason: Added bump_inode_version() called from touch_mtime_ctime() and touch_ctime(). All 3,591 tests pass. Commit f3c69f2.

The goal is to prove that a stale repair plan cannot mutate current client data after an apparently matching id is reused.

2. Unit tests include explicit ABA fixtures where an old lease id, old block range, old symbol generation, or old snapshot appears structurally valid but must still be rejected.

5. Downstream enablement beads for mounted mutating repair must consume this proof and fail closed if epoch/lease identities are missing, non-monotonic, stale, or not persisted across reopen where required.

title: [MODE-2][HIGH] concurrency safety: c11threads join fails to provide completion ordering
description:
[MODE-2][HIGH] concurrency safety: failed C11 join destroys the only completion fence for mutex and condvar tests

This is the concurrency consequence of the same backend split, and it is independently dangerous because it removes the intended happens-before edge.

Validated by the current workspace gate failure:
- `env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/rch_target_frankenlibc_cod rch exec -- cargo test --workspace --all-targets`

Evidence in tests:
- `crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/c11threads_abi_test.rs:312-340` expects four worker threads to complete before reading `MTX_COUNTER`, but uses `thrd_join` as the only completion barrier.
- `crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/c11threads_abi_test.rs:182-231` expects `cnd_wait` wakeup accounting to be stable only after `thrd_join` returns.

Because `thrd_join` currently fails for host-created threads, the test thread often reads shared state before the worker has actually terminated. That explains the observed undercount and lost-wakeup symptoms:
- mutex contention counter `304` instead of `400`
- condition-variable wake count `0` or `1` instead of the expected completed waiter count

This is more than a test issue: any caller relying on C11 join for publication and completion ordering can observe stale shared state or partially-completed critical sections.

Fix direction:
- restore a real join completion path for host-created C11 threads
- then keep the failing mutex and condvar tests as regression gates because they are exposing a real synchronization contract breach.
close_reason: Same root cause as bd-21ypi/bd-8sa88/bd-jqy64 — fixed in commit 138c07c3. The 'mutex count 304 vs 400' and 'cnd wake 0/1 vs expected' symptoms flowed from thrd_join failing for host-created threads; with pthread_join now delegating to the host backend, test_mtx_multi_threaded_contention, test_cnd_wait_signal, test_cnd_broadcast_wakes_all all pass (36/0 in c11threads_abi_test). The synchronization contract breach is resolved at the join boundary.

title: PORT: fparseln (NetBSD libutil logical-line reader)
description: NetBSD libutil fparseln(stream, *len, *lineno, delim[3], flags) reads a logical line from a FILE*, handling: (1) backslash line continuation (joining physical lines that end with the escape char), (2) comments starting with delim[2] (default "#"), (3) escapes via delim[0] (default "\\"). delim[1] is the line separator (default "\\n"). *lineno is incremented for each physical line consumed. Flags FPARSELN_UNESC{ESC,CONT,COMM,REST,ALL} disable individual transformations. Returns a malloc"d string (caller frees) or NULL on EOF. Used by NetBSD ftpd, mtree, pkgsrc, and many BSD config-file parsers. Currently missing entirely from frankenlibc-abi. Ship: pure-safe core::stdio::fparseln_assemble that takes raw line bytes + delim/flags and returns the processed result, plus an abi shim that drives fgetln to gather physical lines.

title: membrane: AllocationArena leaks quarantined entries on drop
description: crates/frankenlibc-membrane/src/arena.rs:50 ArenaShard holds a VecDeque<QuarantineEntry> of user-freed allocations waiting for drain. QuarantineEntry is Copy (addresses only) and does not own the memory. When AllocationArena is dropped (end of test or fuzz iteration), the quarantine VecDeque is dropped but the underlying std::alloc::alloc'd raw_base pointers are leaked. No Drop impl on ArenaShard or AllocationArena. LeakSanitizer flagged this via fuzz_malloc on input Alloc(16) + Alloc(0). Fix: implement Drop for ArenaShard that calls std::alloc::dealloc on every remaining quarantine entry (and also slots with live allocations — on drop, all outstanding memory must be returned). title: [perf][resolv] BackendFileCache::refresh_cache does getenv + stat syscall on EVERY call (even cache hits) — now the dominant cost of all indexed resolver lookups
close_reason:
SHIPPED, but the stated hypothesis was REFUTED by the profile and the lever changed accordingly.

TASK WAS: drop the per-call getenv in BackendFileCache::refresh_cache (option c), optionally via a generation counter.
PROFILE SAID OTHERWISE. perf -F 4999 on getprotobyname_r_tcp/frankenlibc_abi (local release-perf + debuginfo), self-time frames >=0.1%:
  record_free_stats 29.31 | record_alloc_stats 27.21 | fallback_insert_sized_index 16.73 | free 13.76 | realloc 2.65 | fallback_remove_sized 2.40 | enter_allocator_reentry_guard 0.14 | memcpy 0.13 | kernel [k] ~1.5 (the stat)
=> ~92% of self time is allocator bookkeeping. getenv does NOT appear at >=0.1%. The stat is ~1.5%. The top frames belong to cod's Swing-2 malloc lane (bd-dcrhgl, off-limits + ledgered as diffuse), so per method I took the next actionable frame in MY lane: stop calling malloc.

LEVER (one mechanism, two allocation sites):
 1. refresh_source_path_from_env built + dropped a PathBuf on EVERY lookup even when the env var is unset. Replaced with allocation-free source_path_matches_env().
 2. with_protocol_entry_by_{name,number} now run the caller closure on the BORROWED cache entry instead of .cloned() (a ProtocolEntry clone = name Vec + Vec<Vec<u8>> aliases = 3+ malloc/free pairs + the observed realloc). Cloning wrappers retained as with_*(.., Clone::clone).

SEMANTICS: env is still read on EVERY call; only the allocation is gone. No snapshot, no generation fence. This deliberately avoids the ENVIRON_EPOCH fence, which would be UNSOUND in the test process: std::env::set_var binds glibc setenv (proven: libc::getservbyport binds glibc, not fl's no_mangle symbol), so the epoch would never bump while the value changed, and the *_track_overridden_*_backend gates would serve a stale path. The FRANKENLIBC_*_PATH keys are fl-internal fixture hooks; no C-standard function reads them, but our own tests mutate them mid-process, so re-reading IS observable.

MEASURED 3-way (4 arms, same binary/run/worker vmi1149989, two passes). legacy_orig faithfully reconstructs the pre-lever body in-process (bench_protocols_pathbuf_refresh_alloc() + cloning lookup), so the A/B prices the WHOLE lever:

title: [perf] strict_hardened_overhead_harness has ~85ns/op measurement floor — cannot validate the 20ns strict budget
description:
PROFILING handoff from SnowyMill (run 20260601-perf-26a69011, git 26a69011). MEASUREMENT-INFRA gap, not a runtime hotspot.

OBSERVATION: the custom ns/op harness (crates/frankenlibc-bench/benches/strict_hardened_overhead_harness.rs) FULL lane (64 samples x 1024 inner-iters, rch worker vmi1153651 AMD EPYC) floors EVERY family at p50 ~82-107ns/op:
  math_fenv 107, string_memory 103, pthread_sync 93, allocator 89, stdio_buffer 89, runtime_math 90, ctype 88 (strict p50 ns/op).
ctype/isalpha is intrinsically ~1ns yet measures 88ns -> the per-op cost is dominated by harness fixed overhead (Instant batch + black_box + loop + shared-VPS noise), NOT the membrane decision. Consequently this harness CANNOT confirm/deny the README/code 20ns strict-overhead budget (FAST_PATH_BUDGET_NS=20). It also reports hardened p50 <= strict p50 for all families, which is an artifact of the floor, not a real result.

EVIDENCE: tests/artifacts/perf/20260601-perf-26a69011/HOTSPOT_TABLE.md (family matrix) + strict_hardened_overhead_full.raw.log.

SUGGESTED IMPROVEMENT (optimizer/tooling): raise inner-iteration counts and/or adopt criterion-style estimated-iteration timing (as membrane_bench does, 1.5M-5.5B inner iters) so sub-100ns costs resolve; consider pinning a dedicated low-noise host for the overhead lane; or treat membrane_bench as the authoritative sub-100ns source and demote this harness to cross-mode ranking only. Smoke lane (8 samples) additionally produced a spurious 2679ns runtime_math p95 tail that vanished at 64 samples — keep >=64 samples for any published number.
close_reason: Resolved measurement-source gap: added Criterion runtime_math_decide_resample_free and cadence-inclusive rows in runtime_math_kernels_bench, documented strict_hardened_overhead_harness as cadence-inclusive ranking only. Baseline overhead smoke on vmi1149989: strict ctype 87ns p50, strict runtime_math 86ns p50, hardened runtime_math 72ns p50. Criterion resolution check on vmi1153651: risk_upper_bound_ppm 0.556ns p50. After on vmi1153651: strict decide resample-free 190.360ns p50, strict cadence-inclusive 194.420ns p50, hardened resample-free 188.393ns p50, hardened cadence-inclusive 199.565ns p50. Validation: rch cargo check -p frankenlibc-bench --benches PASS; rch cargo clippy -p frankenlibc-bench --benches -- -D warnings PASS; rch cargo test -p frankenlibc-bench PASS; local cargo fmt -p frankenlibc-bench --check PASS; git diff --check PASS.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
CORRECTED DIAGNOSIS (cc, 2026-06-02, code+bench inspection). The ~85ns floor is NOT harness fixed overhead (Instant/black_box/loop). Evidence:

1. FULL lane is 64 samples x 1024 inner-iters and times a BATCH then divides (elapsed/1024), so Instant::now() fixed cost amortizes to ~0.03ns/op. It cannot be the floor.

2. The criterion runtime_math_kernels_bench resolves sos_barrier_quarantine_eval at p50=24.6ns on the SAME rch AMD EPYC host (81M iters). So sub-100ns IS resolvable here; timer granularity is not the limit.

3. The floor is the genuine cost of RuntimeMathKernel::decide() (mod.rs:1383). Per call it does: 1x self.decisions.fetch_add (atomic RMW) + ~12 sequential relaxed atomic loads (cached_spectral/signature/topological/anytime/cvar/bridge/ld/hji + TROPICAL_METRICS x2) + risk.upper_bound_ppm + branches. PLUS a cadence-gated resample_high_order_kernels (mod.rs:5020) that takes TWO mutex locks (sampled_risk, sampled_oracle) + oracle eval, firing every 512 calls -> at 1024 inner-iters it fires ~2x/sample and its cost amortizes INTO the per-op number. For ctype, representative_workload is ~1ns yet it measures 88ns, confirming the cost is decide()+amortized-resample, not the workload or the harness.

CONSEQUENCE: raising inner-iterations (the original primary suggestion) will NOT lower the floor -- it is real work, not noise. The harness structurally measures fast_path + amortized_resample, which by construction exceeds FAST_PATH_BUDGET_NS=20; you cannot isolate the fast path here because resample is baked into decide() behind an internal cadence gate.

RECOMMENDATION (option 3 from original bead): demote this harness to cross-mode RANKING (strict-vs-hardened deltas are still valid) and document that its absolute p50 includes amortized cadence-resample. Validate the 20ns fast-path budget with a dedicated criterion bench that drives decide() on a kernel configured to stay on the fast path (sequence not a multiple of 512), measuring ONLY the resample-free branch. Separately, the ~12 sequential relaxed atomic loads in decide()'s fast path are a real (smaller) perf target -- packing the cached_* enum-states into one atomic word would cut loads, but profile first to confirm it dominates vs resample amortization before spending the lever.
