title: [flaky] wait4_no_child_echild arm returns RC_0 under parallel libtest — an unreaped fork from a sibling fixture case
description:
Observed 2026-08-15 on an rch worker while fixing bd-ssm0dr.

  process_spawn_wait_tail_fixture_cases_match_execute_fixture_case ... FAILED   (whole-suite run)
    fixture expected_output mismatch for wait4_no_child_echild_hardened (hardened)
      actual=WAIT4_NO_CHILD_RC_0   expected=WAIT4_NO_CHILD_RC_-1_ERRNO_ECHILD

  process_spawn_wait_tail_fixture_cases_match_execute_fixture_case ... ok       (run ALONE)
    test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 172 filtered out

The arm asserts 'this process has no children', which is a property of the whole PROCESS, not of
the case. Sibling fixture cases in the same binary fork (process_spawn_exit_actual calls
libc::fork), and libtest runs them on parallel threads, so a live unreaped child from another case
makes wait4(WNOHANG) return 0 instead of failing with ECHILD. It is order/timing dependent: an
earlier run of the same suite had this gate GREEN and a different pair red.

NOT the same defect as bd-ssm0dr (privilege-dependent errno constants). This one is a
shared-process-state assumption, and it is why the red SET moved between two runs of the same
command -- which is exactly the trap that inflates red counts (see the poison-cascade note on
bd-9ri7g1: run the target ALONE before believing the count).

FIX SHAPE: make the arm own its precondition instead of assuming it. Either reap first
(waitpid(-1, .., WNOHANG) in a loop until ECHILD before the measured call), or run the measured
wait4 in a forked child that provably has no children of its own. Prefer the reap loop -- forking
inside an fl test arm has its own deadlock history.

NEGATIVE CASE: the fixed arm must still fail if wait4 returns 0 or -1 with an errno other than
ECHILD after the reap loop has drained; a 'tolerate RC_0' relaxation is the wrong fix and would
make the row prove nothing.
close_reason: Fixed by f9a0e8e38 after 8bcae16e8 proved insufficient: popen forks inside fl, so the first lock never saw its child. Measured on hz1 by looping the built conformance binary -- 5 failures in 25 iterations before, 0 in 30 after (P~0.1% under the null). Assertion never relaxed; the arm still requires RC_-1_ERRNO_ECHILD. The unrelated SIGSEGV seen in those iterations stays open on bd-u2daxd.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
Correction to my own fix-shape note, after reading the arm (crates/frankenlibc_conformance/src/lib.rs:29411): a reap loop is NOT sufficient on its own.

The observed value was RC_0, and under WNOHANG that means 'children exist but none have changed
state' -- i.e. a sibling's child is still ALIVE, not merely unreaped. waitpid(WNOHANG) cannot
remove a live child, so draining zombies leaves the race intact.

What actually fixes it is making 'this process has no children' true for the duration of the
measured call: serialize this arm against every fork-using arm in the same binary (they are in the
same module -- process_spawn_exit_actual and friends call libc::fork), with the forking arms
holding the lock until they have reaped. A dedicated mutex around 'fork + reap' and around this
one measured wait4 is enough; libtest's parallelism is the only thing creating the overlap.

Do not 'fix' it by tolerating RC_0 -- that makes the row prove nothing, which is the trap this
bead exists to avoid.

title: _IO_adjust_column / _IO_adjust_wcolumn diverge from glibc — wrong column-counter algorithm
description:
## Defect

Both `_IO_adjust_column` (`crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/io_internal_abi.rs:2055`)
and `_IO_adjust_wcolumn` (line 2091) implement their own tab-aware
column tracker:

```rust
for i in 0..count as usize {
    let byte = ...;
    match byte {
        b'\n' | b'\r' => c = 0,
        b'\t' => c = (c + 8) & !7,
        _ => c += 1,
    }
}
```

The actual glibc implementation (sunrpc-adjacent — `libio/genops.c`) is:

```c
int _IO_adjust_column (unsigned start, const char *line, int count) {
    const char *ptr = line + count;
    while (ptr > line)
        if (*--ptr == '\n')
            return line + count - ptr - 1;
    return start + count;
}
```

The semantics is: **find the position past the last newline in the
buffer, OR add `count` to `start` if no newline.** Tabs are NOT
expanded; carriage returns are NOT zeroed; the function never iterates
forward through every byte.

This is an ABI behavioral divergence. Any consumer (e.g. older glibc-
linked C++ stream code, certain pretty-printers in third-party
libraries) that calls `_IO_adjust_column` to know "how far am I from
the last newline" gets a different answer from us than from real
glibc, especially when the buffer contains tabs or carriage returns.

Additional smaller defects in the current code:
- `c + 8` and `c += 1` arithmetic on `c: u32` panics in debug mode
  for adversarial column values near `u32::MAX` (theoretical only —
  caller would need to seed `col` near INT_MAX which is implausible).
- `c as c_int` at the end can return a negative result when `c >
  i32::MAX`.

## Fix

Rewrite both helpers to mirror glibc's "scan back from end for last
newline" algorithm. Keep the membrane policy gate intact. The wide
variant scans backward over `i32` wide-chars looking for `0x0A`.

## Severity

[HIGH] (P2). Pure correctness divergence — no memory-safety
exploit, but breaks ABI compatibility for third-party libraries that
depend on the documented glibc semantics. Pretty-printer column
counters, indent trackers, and any consumer that mixes
_IO_adjust_column results with raw text-position arithmetic will
silently produce wrong layouts.
notes: Fixed in fb6e5ed2: _IO_adjust_column and _IO_adjust_wcolumn rewritten to match glibc libio/genops.c — backward scan for last newline, returns either (count - newline_pos - 1) or (start + count). Tabs and CR no longer special-cased. Saturating arithmetic eliminates the debug-mode overflow panics in the old tab-expansion path. 6 regression tests pin glibc semantics. Verified 52/52 io_internal_native_file_test pass + clippy clean.

title: [iconv][utf-7] support shift sequences split across multiple iconv() calls (partial-buffer state)
description: fl's UTF-7 codec (d93b5a3a4) handles single-call (complete-buffer) conversions byte-exactly vs glibc, but does NOT support a Modified-Base64 shift sequence split across multiple iconv() calls. The dedicated utf7_convert path in frankenlibc-core/src/iconv/mod.rs treats each call's input as complete: for a UTF-7 SOURCE it decodes whole units (a +...- run atomically), and for a UTF-7 TARGET it builds the whole output in one shot (E2BIG with in_consumed=0 if it doesn't fit). Real-world callers usually convert a whole string in one call (or use a generous buffer), so this is a rare edge. To fully match glibc's streaming contract: add per-descriptor UTF-7 shift state (in_shift, bit accumulator, pending high surrogate for decode; in_shift + pending bits for encode) to IconvDescriptor (like from_bom_pending), thread it through utf7_convert so a partial trailing shift returns EINVAL with the right in_consumed and resumes on the next call, and flush pending encode bits + closing '-' on the inbuf=NULL call. Low priority (rare usage); the single-call path is already exact and gated (conformance_diff_iconv_utf7).
close_reason: done

title: Bitmap CRC: verify kernel bitmap pre-processing before checksumming
description:
Read the Linux kernel source for ext4_block_bitmap_csum_set() and ext4_block_bitmap_csum_verify() to determine:
(a) Whether the kernel zeroes unused tail bits in the bitmap before checksumming. For a group with fewer blocks than blocks_per_group, the tail bits may be set to 1 (indicating 'used') by mkfs but the kernel may ignore/zero them before CRC.
(b) Whether the kernel checksums exactly block_size bytes or clusters_per_group/8 bytes. Our code checksums the full block.
(c) Whether the kernel XORs or masks any fields in the group descriptor before storing the checksum.

SPECIFIC FILES TO CHECK:
- fs/ext4/balloc.c: ext4_block_bitmap_csum_set(), ext4_block_bitmap_csum_verify()
- fs/ext4/bitmap.c: ext4_bitmap_csum()
- include/linux/ext4.h: struct ext4_group_desc layout

ACCEPTANCE: Document the exact kernel pre-processing steps. If any differ from our implementation, fix our code.
close_reason: Kernel source confirmed: no group number in bitmap CRC, length is clusters_per_group/8 for blocks and inodes_per_group/8 for inodes. Fixed in commit 20d65f4.

title: [bug][getopt] fl permutes argv EAGERLY; glibc defers the exchange to the final -1 — 1709/8000 fuzz cases diverge on optind
description:
conformance_diff_getopt_fuzz was RED at HEAD (sweep bd-aykfv1), untracked. 1709 of 8000 fuzz cases diverge — 21%.

FIRST CASE: opts="abcd:" argv=[prog, -c, -b, bar, -c]
  host steps: ret 'c' optind 2; ret 'b' optind 3; ret 'c' optind 5
  fl   steps: ret 'c' optind 2; ret 'b' optind 3; ret 'c' optind 4

ROOT CAUSE, established with a live trace of glibc rather than inferred:
  ret='c' optind=2   argv=[prog -c -b bar -c]   unchanged
  ret='b' optind=3   argv=[prog -c -b bar -c]   unchanged
  ret='c' optind=5   argv=[prog -c -b bar -c]   STILL unchanged, optind ran PAST the operand
  ret=-1  optind=4   argv=[prog -c -b -c bar]   permuted ONCE, optind reset to first_nonopt

glibc scans IN PLACE, remembering the operand run as first_nonopt/last_nonopt and letting optind run ahead over it; it calls exchange() to rotate operands to the tail only when it is about to return -1, and only then sets optind = first_nonopt so the caller finds the operands.

fl (crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs, parse_getopt_short, the rotate_right block) permutes EAGERLY: whenever argv[optind] is an operand it locates the next option element, rotates that option — plus its separate argument — in front of the operand run immediately, and steps from the rotated array. optind therefore tracks a DIFFERENT array than glibc's at every intermediate step.

CONSEQUENCES, both observable:
  1. optind differs at every step after the first skipped operand. That is what the gate catches.
  2. argv itself differs MID-SCAN. glibc leaves argv untouched until the final call; fl has already rotated it. A caller that inspects argv between getopt() calls — or that stops early without draining to -1 — sees a different array under fl. The final argv agrees, which is why the gate's end-state argv comparison passes and only the step trace fails.

FIX SHAPE: adopt glibc's model — track first_nonopt/last_nonopt, leave argv alone while scanning, let optind advance past operands, and perform a single exchange() rotation when returning -1, setting optind = first_nonopt. This replaces the incremental rotate_right block; it is a structural change, not a bookkeeping tweak, which is why it is filed rather than patched in passing.

DO NOT try to fix this by adjusting optind alone. The two models agree on the final argv and the option sequence and disagree on the intermediate state of BOTH optind and argv; only reproducing the deferred-exchange structure makes the step traces match.

DONE = conformance_diff_getopt_fuzz green (it drives 8000 randomized cases against live glibc, so it is a sufficient oracle), with getopt_abi_test and the getopt_long gates still green.
close_reason:
DONE at cba2420be. Diagnosed last turn, implemented this turn.

EVIDENCE:
  cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test conformance_diff_getopt_fuzz
  test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out   (was 1709/8000 diverging)
  cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test conformance_diff_getopt
  test result: ok. 7 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  cargo test -p frankenlibc-core --lib getopt
  test result: ok. 42 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 3182 filtered out

FIX: adopted glibc's model wholesale, as this bead insisted. GETOPT_FIRST_NONOPT/GETOPT_LAST_NONOPT statics; scan in place letting optind run past the operand run; a single getopt_exchange() (glibc's exchange()) mirrored onto the real argv pointer array; optind set back to first_nonopt on the -1 path. The clamp at the top means a caller restarting with optind = 1 resets the bounds implicitly, which is how glibc's own restart works rather than a special case.

TWO STEPS, EACH MEASURED: the core deferred-exchange took 1709 -> 305. The residual 305 were all inputs where the only thing before  is an operand, e.g. [prog, '-', '--', ...] — glibc has a dedicated  block that rotates the preceding operands in front of the separator and jumps optind to the end. Adding it took 305 -> 0. I did not guess that from the first fix being 'mostly right'; the gate named the remaining class.

THE BEAD'S OWN WARNING HELD. It said not to attempt an optind-only tweak because both models agree on the final argv and the option sequence. That is exactly why the 49 curated assertions (conformance_diff_getopt 7 + core getopt 42) passed before AND after — they never inspect optind at a step where an operand has been skipped, the single state the models disagree in. Only the 8000-case fuzz gate could confirm this, and a green conformance_diff_getopt would have been meaningless as evidence.

SECOND OBSERVABLE, now also fixed: argv mid-scan. glibc leaves argv untouched until the final call; fl had already rotated it. A caller inspecting argv between getopt() calls, or stopping before draining to -1, saw a different array. The gate's end-state comparison could never have caught that on its own.

REGRESSION CHECK: unistd_abi_test is 539 passed / 1 failed. That failure is crypt_checksalt_classifies_known_prefixes, verified pre-existing by stashing this change and re-running the arm alone (FAILED both ways), filed as bd-premb7 — note it disagrees with conformance_diff_crypt_checksalt, which is green, so two gates for one behaviour contradict each other.

comments.text:
SURROUNDING COVERAGE, measured while filing (PlumStork): the eager-permutation model does NOT break the narrower getopt gates, which is why it survived.

  conformance_diff_getopt          test result: ok. 7 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  cargo test -p frankenlibc-core --lib getopt
  test result: ok. 42 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 3182 filtered out
  conformance_diff_getopt_fuzz     test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed  (1709/8000 cases)

So 49 curated getopt assertions pass while 21% of randomized cases diverge. The curated ones evidently never inspect optind at a step where an operand has already been skipped — that is the exact state the two models disagree in. title: towupper/towlower: simple-vs-full case mapping table gaps vs glibc (bd-2g7oyh.150)
notes:
Single-char towupper/towlower (crates/frankenlibc-core/src/string/wchar.rs) use Rust std char::to_uppercase/to_lowercase (FULL mapping) as a proxy for glibc's SIMPLE case mapping. They diverge where a code point has a simple mapping that Rust's full mapping expands to multiple chars:
- towupper: U+1F80..U+1FAF Greek-with-ypogegrammeni have simple uppercase to the prosgegrammeni forms (U+1F80->U+1F88, etc.); we return UNCHANGED, glibc maps them. ~48 chars.
- Unicode-version table mismatch: Medefaidrin U+16E40.. and newer Latin extended where glibc's Unicode version differs from bundled Rust std tables.
Fix: compile glibc's exact SimpleUppercase/SimpleLowercase columns into a lookup, replacing the to_uppercase/to_lowercase proxy for affected ranges.
Already handled (commit 8a56581d): U+0130 special-cased to 'i'; all base+combining full expansions return unchanged. Parent bd-2g7oyh.
close_reason: Closed by 1aa36d77: full-codepoint sweep vs glibc found 83 divergences (27 Greek simple-uppercase override + 56 Unicode-version-skew no-ops); sweep now 0 divergences, guarded by diff_towupper_towlower_full_codepoint_sweep

title: Refine readiness reporting with cross-lane event envelope and correlation ids
description:
Supplemental refinement for bd-un9xt and bd-rchk0.4.3. The readiness report can only aggregate evidence reliably if every lane emits a compatible structured event envelope. Today the planning beads list many lane-specific log fields; this bead makes the shared minimum explicit so cross-lane reporting, proof bundles, release gates, and follow-up creation do not invent incompatible schemas.

Scope: define a versioned event envelope with report id, run id, lane id, scenario id, artifact id, parent correlation id, classification, severity, timestamps, git SHA, host/capability fingerprint, raw-log references, controlling evidence, remediation id, and reproduction command. Lane-specific payloads may extend the envelope but cannot omit the shared fields.

Required proof before close:
1. Unit/schema tests reject events missing envelope version, run id, lane id, scenario id or explicit aggregate marker, classification, severity, timestamp, artifact path/hash, raw-log reference, and reproduction command.
2. Unit tests cover correlation across mounted matrix, xfstests, repair confidence, crash replay, fuzz smoke, performance, proof bundle, and release-gate events, including duplicate ids, stale schema versions, clock-skew tolerance, and missing parent events.
3. E2E smoke aggregates fixture events from at least four lanes and proves the readiness report preserves correlation ids from raw lane artifact to human summary row and machine-readable output.
4. Logs include envelope version, event count, lane ids, rejected event diagnostics, correlation graph summary, output paths, and reproduction command.
5. Future lane beads may add fields, but public readiness claims cannot consume lane artifacts that fail this shared envelope validator.

title: atfork runners hold Mutex across user callbacks — self-deadlock on re-entrant pthread_atfork
description: run_atfork_prepare/parent/child in crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/pthread_abi.rs:4350-4385 hold ATFORK_HANDLERS.lock() across arbitrary user-callback invocation. A prepare/parent/child handler that transitively calls pthread_atfork (common in lazy-init library paths) re-locks a non-recursive std::sync::Mutex on the same thread -> deadlock. Concrete interleaving: T1 fork() -> run_atfork_prepare() holds lock -> calls H1 -> H1 init'd some library L2 that registers its own handler via pthread_atfork -> pthread_atfork tries ATFORK_HANDLERS.lock() -> self-deadlock. Class 1 (classic mutex deadlock). Fix: snapshot handlers (Vec<AtforkHandlers> with derive(Clone, Copy)), drop guard, iterate snapshot. Affects: unistd_abi.rs:5415/5432/5434 fork interposer and process_abi.rs:139/156/159 fork interposer.

title: pthread_mutex_consistent returns 0 for non-robust/not-owner-died mutex (glibc: EINVAL) — needs robust-mutex state tracking
close_reason: Fixed (commit a2aa126a5): pthread_mutex_consistent returned 0; glibc returns EINVAL unless the mutex is robust+owner-died (inconsistent), which fl can never produce. Return EINVAL to match for all reachable mutexes; _np alias delegates. Gate conformance_diff_mutex_consistent 2/2 vs glibc. NOT architectural after all. Residual (separate): fl rejects robust mutex init.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: BLOCKED (architectural): glibc pthread_mutex_consistent returns EINVAL unless the mutex is robust AND in EOWNERDEAD state, then clears it. fl's native mutex doesn't track robust/owner-died state (pthread_abi.rs ~5682), so it returns 0 unconditionally. Faithful fix needs recording the robust attr in the mutex word at init + owner-died tracking on lock acquisition — a real robust-mutex implementation. Deferred to a focused robust-mutex session. Found via stub-tell comment sweep alongside bd-cykuni.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: RESOLVED not-blocked: the fix does NOT need robust-mutex state tracking. Since fl never makes a mutex inconsistent (lock never returns EOWNERDEAD; init rejects robust attrs with EINVAL), glibc's pthread_mutex_consistent returns EINVAL for EVERY mutex fl can construct. So returning EINVAL unconditionally is correct parity. NOTE residual: fl pthread_mutex_init rejecting robust attrs (EINVAL where glibc accepts) is a separate robust-mutex limitation, left for a future focused session.

title: [RED] acct_privilege_denied_strict expects EPERM but gets EFAULT as root — one arm-premise defect reddening TWO fixture gates
description:
Found 2026-08-15 while landing bd-741gtz's arm corrections. Two frankenlibc_conformance gates are red and BOTH fail on the same single case:

  process_spawn_wave01_fixture_cases_match_execute_fixture_case          FAILED
  unistd_process_filesystem_wave12_fixture_cases_match_execute_...       FAILED

  fixture expected_output mismatch for acct_privilege_denied_strict (strict)
    left:  symbol=acct;mode=strict;expected=ACCT_BAD_PATH_RC_-1_ERRNO_EPERM;actual=ACCT_BAD_PATH_RC_-1_ERRNO_EFAULT;failure_signature=mismatch
    right: symbol=acct;mode=strict;expected=ACCT_BAD_PATH_RC_-1_ERRNO_EPERM;actual=ACCT_BAD_PATH_RC_-1_ERRNO_EPERM;failure_signature=none

CATEGORY (b) in bd-aykfv1's taxonomy: the ARM assumes a non-root process. acct(2) checks
CAP_SYS_PACCT first, so an unprivileged caller gets EPERM before the kernel ever looks at the
path; as root that check passes and the bad path surfaces as EFAULT. rch workers run as ROOT,
so the arm cannot pass where it is actually executed. That makes it permanently red on the
fleet, which is the worst state for a gate -- counted as coverage, never green.

FIX SHAPE (do not just flip EPERM to EFAULT): the arm should state its precondition. Either
skip loudly when geteuid()==0, or split into two arms keyed on privilege, so the row proves
something on both kinds of host instead of encoding one of them.

NEGATIVE CASE: whatever replaces it must still fail if acct() returns 0, or returns -1 with
an errno that is neither EPERM (unprivileged) nor EFAULT (privileged, bad path) -- a naive
'accept any -1' arm would pass on a stub that never implemented acct at all.

Verify first with the live oracle before writing the arm; do not take this description on
trust (see bd-02gcfy). Both as root and as an unprivileged user:
  python3 -c "import ctypes,ctypes.util; l=ctypes.CDLL(ctypes.util.find_library('c'),use_errno=True); print(l.acct(b'/nonexistent/x'), ctypes.get_errno())"
close_reason:
Shipped c752df380 (pushed to main and main:master).

SCOPE CORRECTION vs this bead's own title: it was not one defect reddening two gates. It was TWO
distinct privilege-pinned defects of the same class -- acct (process_spawn_wave01) and fsmount
(unistd_process_filesystem_wave12) -- plus a third, unrelated flake (bd-ry1dg5). And fsmount was
hiding two more: the fixture gate asserts case-by-case and ABORTS at the first mismatch, so
fsopen/fspick were never evaluated. Fixing fsmount alone would have exposed them on the next run,
so all four symbols moved together.

MEASURED BOTH SIDES (not taken from the man page):
  euid 1000, raw syscalls on this host:
    fsmount(-1,0,0) fsopen(NULL,0) fspick(AT_FDCWD,NULL,0) -> all rc=-1 errno=1 EPERM
  root (rch worker): fsmount(-1,0,0) -> rc=-1 EBADF
Confirms the mechanism the bead asserted: the capability check (CAP_SYS_ADMIN / CAP_SYS_PACCT)
runs BEFORE argument validation, so unprivileged callers never reach the invalid fd/pointer. No
errno constant is portable across the two hosts.

FIX SHAPE DELIVERED, as the bead required -- the arm no longer encodes one kind of host: each calls
the host (libc::acct; the raw syscall for the mount API, which glibc does not wrap) on the SAME
input in the SAME process and expects a parity verdict. Strictly stronger than the constant it
replaces.

NEGATIVE CASES the bead demanded, all live in the new tokens: a wrapper that returns 0//a valid fd
fails (fl_fd >= 0 or rc mismatch), and one that returns -1 with an errno the kernel did not just
report fails (fl_errno != host_errno). A naive 'accept any -1' arm would pass a stub that never
implemented the call; this does not.

GATE OBSERVED COMPILING AND EXECUTING on an rch worker (root -- the environment where the old arms
were unpassable), against the exact committed tree:
  cargo test -p frankenlibc_conformance --lib fixture_cases_match_execute_fixture_case -- --test-threads=1
  test result: ok. 85 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 88 filtered out
Measured before and after: 83 passed/2 failed at the start of this work, 84/1 after the acct half,
85/0 now.

FL's errno slot, so using it for a host arm reports a freshly-reset 0 and looks exactly like an
fl-vs-kernel divergence; and regenerating the conformance golden with the prebuilt Aug-14 harness

title: Bound ext4 info group expansion before allocation

title: Isolate the string-taking membrane floor by buffer provenance (wctype vs strtol), vs live glibc
description:
Pre-registered before any timing exists. Discharges an obligation created by the 2026-07-30 wctype row, and attacks the priority-2 population (344 positive ledger rows, only 16 carrying a same-invocation incumbent).

THE OBLIGATION. The wctype mechanism test measured a flat ~11.173 ns floor on FrankenLibC wctype against a glibc walk starting at 5.755 ns, and named bounded_cstr_bytes -> known_remaining as the STRUCTURAL SUSPECT while explicitly recording that the attribution was NOT isolated. This run isolates it, without editing library source, so the thing measured is the deployed object.

WHY THE OBVIOUS READING IS ALREADY IN DOUBT. strtol carries a deployed stdlib_membrane_fastpath bypass that skips decide() and known_remaining entirely, and its in-tree comment records ~12 ns against glibc ~6 ns. So a symbol that does NOT pay known_remaining still sits at ~12 ns, which is roughly where wctype sits WITH it. Either known_remaining is not the dominant floor term, or the two floors have different causes. That is the question.

THE LEVER: BUFFER PROVENANCE, no source edit required. known_remaining is bump_mmap_remaining -> segment_remaining -> fallback_remaining and every one is address-keyed. bump_mmap_remaining early-outs on an atomic flag; segment_remaining consults the segment table; fallback_remaining early-outs when the address is outside [FALLBACK_ALLOC_MIN_ADDR, FALLBACK_ALLOC_MAX_ADDR] but when the address IS in range it TAKES A LOCK and probes up to 1024 slots. So if that chain is the floor, the same function on the same bytes must cost different amounts depending only on where the buffer came from. If it is not the floor, provenance cannot matter.

DISCRIMINATING PAIR, opposite predictions in one invocation:
  wctype  reads its argument with bounded_cstr_bytes, calling known_remaining unconditionally => PREDICT provenance-SENSITIVE.
  strtol  carries the stdlib_membrane_fastpath bypass => PREDICT provenance-INSENSITIVE.
Because the two predictions are opposite, "provenance matters" cannot be a property of the harness.

THE LOAD-BEARING CONTROL. Buffers of different provenance sit at different addresses and therefore differ in cache set, page and TLB behaviour REGARDLESS of any registry. glibc has no allocation registry, so glibc's own spread across the same four buffers measures exactly that placement artifact. The registered discriminator is therefore NOT "FrankenLibC varies" but "FrankenLibC varies MORE THAN GLIBC DOES ON THE SAME BUFFERS", by a factor fixed in advance at 2.0.

FOUR PROVENANCES, identical bytes: stack; static (object data segment); glibc_heap (CString from the benchmark's glibc malloc); fl_heap (allocated by dlsym'd FrankenLibC malloc, so it is registered in the very tables known_remaining consults).

PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTIONS.
P1  fl wctype provenance spread (max/min over the four buffers) exceeds glibc wctype provenance spread by at least 2x.
P2  fl strtol provenance spread does NOT exceed glibc strtol spread by 2x.
P3  every row carries an fl/glibc incumbent ratio, because a self-speedup is maintenance and only an incumbent ratio is a campaign result.

REFUTATION AND ITS CONSEQUENCE. P1 failing refutes known_remaining as the wctype floor term and OBLIGES a correction to the 2026-07-30 ledger row, which named it as the suspect. That correction will be made if it is earned.

CONTRACT. Live glibc linked directly and called in the same invocation as the strict FrankenLibC object loaded by explicit dlopen RTLD_NOW|RTLD_LOCAL; benchmark ELF and both serving objects self-report SHA-256 from inside the process; both symbol pairs asserted to distinct addresses and distinct serving objects; buffer addresses printed per provenance; conformance precedes timing (recognition for wctype, value AND endptr offset for strtol across 15 inputs x 4 bases); per-arm A/A controls on every row; corrected null gate with the median clause (effect CI excludes 1.0, effect deviation exceeds 2x the larger null half-width, each null MEDIAN within 2% of 1.0); ACTUAL OBSERVED thread count read from /proc/self/task at measurement time, never the requested count; CV telemetry only; built via rch exec --base <sha> --clean-overlay so a co-tenant agent's working-tree edits cannot enter the binary.
notes: RESULT: REFUTED, and it corrects the 2026-07-30 wctype row as pre-committed. threadripperje, glibc 2.42, admitted first attempt, pre/post guards clear at max busy 0.140/0.141, threads_observed=1 read from /proc/self/task. All 8 rows decidable, every null median within 0.3% of 1.0. STRFLOOR_PREDICTION verdict=REFUTED p1_wctype_provenance_sensitive=false p2_strtol_provenance_insensitive=true wctype_fl_spread=1.2432 wctype_glibc_spread=1.0053 strtol_fl_spread=1.0009 strtol_glibc_spread=1.0006. P1 FAILED: three of four wctype provenances are indistinguishable (stack 9.938, static 9.928, glibc_heap 9.928 ns), so for an untracked pointer all three probes early-out and known_remaining is free to measurement resolution. The structural suspect named in the wctype row is WITHDRAWN. strtol independently proves the string read is cheap: it reads a C string and completes the whole call in 5.295 ns. BUT THE REGISTRY IS NOT FREE ON A HIT, AND THE HIT IS THE DEPLOYED CASE: fl_heap costs 12.343 ns vs 9.928, a 1.2433x / +2.415 ns penalty on a buffer FrankenLibC itself allocated. In a real program the strings handed to libc come from that program's malloc, which in a deployed FrankenLibC is ours, so the 12.343 column is realistic and the 9.93 columns are an artifact of a benchmark holding foreign memory. Invisible to any harness that allocates inputs with the incumbent's allocator. P2 CONFIRMED tightly: strtol spread 1.0009 vs glibc 1.0006, four rows agreeing to four decimals. TWO TIER-A INCUMBENT RATIOS PRODUCED (today's coverage audit found zero in the whole ledger): wctype 0.2346-0.2926x and strtol 0.615626x, i.e. 1.62x faster than live glibc, both with the full INCUMBENT_OBJECT/INCUMBENT_LINKAGE/kind=fl_glibc bundle. DO NOT GENERALISE strtol: one input (12345, base 10), one host; the in-tree comment records strtol(42) at ~12 ns vs glibc ~6 ns and the standing note claims a 1.08-1.47x short-input LOSS. Neither reproduced nor refuted here; flagged NEEDS ITS OWN SWEEP over length and base. Conformance 68 comparisons pass before timing. Compile check green under rch exec --base cb7665a02 --clean-overlay --no-overlay, but that path retrieved a STALE Jul-10 libfrankenlibc_abi.so, so measured artifacts were built from git archive of the pinned commit cb7665a027c97e6799585635f485e7c20b3c5c97 on the measurement host; exported harness hash 092576ff0eb749bc678eaa652b9611ee9f530dafc1ed69ea763b975f9476aa3d matches git show. Bench ELF 87bab99e1fd4ee0846d6283cf85453d92a729ce78103771ba74a315cacf524cf, Build ID b0e2339d1808e43973a53d26b278853293b2bfd7; FL SO c82c12819b07c33bf9f7c42ddd33e284ca5ecc04ae623a4676fde8f33e80b408; glibc 6791cc9bdc08295aafcfae01a7d66d788ee5577cbe94db00ace5f1ee04ef2b09. Log SHA-256 7e33603b3d4629665d760bdcb844696fab8e86756835f6aa6782161d08d1cb9a.
close_reason: Pre-registered isolation ran under the full contract and REFUTED known_remaining as the string floor: the probe chain is free on a miss. Correction to the 2026-07-30 wctype row applied as pre-committed. Produced the ledger's first two tier-A same-invocation incumbent ratios, and a new finding in the uncomfortable direction -- the registry costs +2.415 ns precisely on buffers FrankenLibC allocated, i.e. the deployed case.

title: perf: deployed strlen/strnlen run an expensive per-call Clifford certification whose result is discarded (dead dispatch)
description: MEASURED + code-traced (BlackThrush, strlen_glibc_bench): deployed string_abi::strlen is ~2.1x slower than glibc at 256K and ~35x at 1K. ROOT CAUSE (a removable one): the common strlen path (string_abi.rs ~2232, !heals && rem.is_none()) calls select_string_simd_dispatch(SimdStringOperation::Strlen, s, s, 64) then passes dispatch.lane_bytes to raw_lane_strlen_bytes(s, _lane_bytes) -- which IGNORES lane_bytes and calls scan_c_string(s, None) unconditionally. select_string_simd_dispatch -> try_simd_dispatch_candidate (len_hint 64 >= Strlen/Avx2 threshold 64, so it proceeds) -> certify_simd_string_operation: an EXPENSIVE Clifford-isomorphism proof (SimdCliffordProfile reference+candidate, CliffordController, observations) run EVERY call and then thrown away. strlen uses NO certified hand-tuned intrinsic (it uses scan_c_string's safe portable_simd), so there is nothing to certify -- the dispatch+certify is vestigial (likely copied from memcpy/memcmp which DO use certified intrinsics). LEVER: skip select_string_simd_dispatch in the strlen (and strnlen via raw_lane_strnlen_bytes -> scan_c_string) paths, calling scan_c_string directly. Expected: removes the per-call certification overhead with ZERO behavior change (lane_bytes was discarded; conformance_diff_strlen/strlen_simd/strnlen_simd will stay green). CAUTION/why-not-done-here: this is the membrane certification/proof-carrying-code system -- verify the proof-ledger/observability contract does not REQUIRE a strlen certification record (it shouldn't, since no unsafe intrinsic is dispatched), and coordinate (foundational area, likely peer-touched). If the observability is wanted, gate the certify behind the Trace mode / do it once, not per call. Benefits every deployed strlen/strnlen call. Same dead-dispatch pattern may exist for other scan_c_string-backed ops -- audit. bench: strlen_glibc_bench (committed). Related architectural: bd-deployed-malloc-membrane-50x (per-call membrane overhead).
close_reason: MEASURED NEUTRAL (BlackThrush). My hypothesis was WRONG: the per-call select_string_simd_dispatch + Clifford certification is CHEAP, not the strlen bottleneck. Tested removing the dead dispatch (raw_lane_strlen_bytes(s,0) directly) -- behavior-neutral (all strlen conformance gates green, dispatch-label test unaffected) but PERF NEUTRAL: strlen_glibc_bench candidate vs dispatch-present baseline identical at p50 (64B 31.7 vs 31.9ns, 1K 288.1 vs 288.5, 16K 548 vs 569; within noise, same glibc control). REASON the certify is cheap: is_x86_feature_detected is std-cached, and certify_simd_string_operation for the fixed len_hint=64 is nearly free. So the deployed strlen per-call overhead (~30ns at 64B vs glibc 2.5ns) is elsewhere -- entrypoint_scope("strlen") tracing-span creation + known_remaining lookup -- NOT the dispatch. Reverted (no perf gain + removing it drops the observability log). The lane_bytes IS provably discarded (dead value), so removing the dispatch is valid code-hygiene if someone wants it, but it is NOT a perf lever. The real deployed-strlen overhead is the membrane entrypoint machinery (entrypoint_scope/known_remaining), same architectural class as bd-deployed-malloc-membrane-50x.

title: strtol family: invalid-base ordering/endptr + SWAR-hex control-byte over-consumption vs glibc
description:
Found by NEW strtol_family_differential_fuzz (250k cases x4 fns = 1M, fl vs glibc __isoc23_strtol/strtoul/strtoll/strtoull — the C23 oracle fl's plain symbols deliberately mirror, per the open scanf-%i bead bd-2g7oyh.203). TWO real fl bugs fixed:

1) INVALID BASE ordering + endptr. glibc validates the base BEFORE inspecting the string: an invalid base (not 0, outside 2..=36) returns 0 + EINVAL with nothing consumed and leaves *endptr UNTOUCHED (never writes it). fl checked the base only AFTER prefix parsing, so empty/sign-only input (e.g. strtol("  -", 37)) hit an early Success return and wrote *endptr=nptr; and the abi's InvalidBase path wrongly wrote *endptr=NULL instead of leaving it untouched. Fix: base-first check at the top of strtol_impl + strtoul_impl (conversion.rs); abi strtol/strtoul/strtoimax/strtoumax no longer touch *endptr on EINVAL (stdlib_abi.rs, 4 sites). Covers signed (strtoll/strtoimax->strtol_impl) and unsigned (strtoull/strtoumax->strtoul_impl).

2) SWAR HEX over-consumption (the serious one — hot path, pre-existing). parse_eight_hex lowercases via word|0x20, which folds CONTROL bytes 0x10..=0x19 onto '0'..='9' (e.g. 0x17|0x20=='7'); the re-encode validity check compared against the already-folded lw rather than the original byte, so it accepted them. Result: a hex string containing a control byte 0x10-0x19 in an 8-byte-aligned window was parsed PAST the non-hex byte (scalar loop correctly stops there) producing a wrong value + endptr (e.g. strtol of bytes '7','0','5','0','0','C','b',0x17,... base16 -> fl consumed 10 vs glibc 7). Fix: reject any byte < 0x30 up front via the bytes-less-than-n SWAR hack (all valid hex >= 0x30; exact). The 'exhaustive' unit test swar_parse_eight_hex_matches_scalar only spot-checked a few gap chars and MISSED 0x10-0x19 — strengthened to sweep all 256 byte values per lane.

Decimal SWAR (is_eight_digits) is NOT affected: it checks c&0xF0==0x30, which 0x10-0x19 fail. WIDE wcstol/wcstoul (wcstol_impl, separate scalar impl) likely share bug #1 (base ordering) — NOT covered here (no wide fuzzer); follow-up. PROBE TRAP noted: GCC redirects strtol->__isoc23_strtol in C and constant-folds literal calls, so host C probes of 0b/raw-vs-c23 disagree with the actually-linked symbol — used argv + .symver to get ground truth. Regression: core conversion 96, conformance_diff_stdlib_numeric 31, stdlib_abi 405, isoc_abi 38, metamorphic_strto 6 all green; fuzzer 1M 0-div.
close_reason: Fixed: base-first validation + endptr-untouched on EINVAL (strtol_impl/strtoul_impl + 4 abi sites); SWAR parse_eight_hex rejects bytes <0x30 (control 0x10-0x19 over-consumption); exhaustive SWAR test strengthened. New strtol_family_differential_fuzz 1M 0-div.

title: fuzz: read/write/pread/pwrite buffer + count validation
description:
## Scope
Add crates/frankenlibc-fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_read_write.rs targeting frankenlibc_abi::unistd_abi::{read,write,pread,pwrite,readv,writev}. Focus on buffer-bound validation + short-read/short-write semantics + errno correctness for invalid fd/len/buf.

## Archetype
1 + 3: Crash-detector + **differential** against libc for matched calls, using a seeded pipe pair and /dev/zero / /dev/null fds as deterministic backends.

## Inputs
struct ReadWriteFuzzInput {
  op: u8,                 // 0=read, 1=write, 2=pread, 3=pwrite, 4=readv, 5=writev
  fd_selector: u8,        // 0=/dev/zero, 1=/dev/null, 2=pipe-read-end, 3=pipe-write-end, 4=closed-fd, 5=-1
  buf_len: u16,           // 0..=32768
  buf_offset: u8,         // shift within a larger allocation (exercises decide's address checks)
  poison_ptr: bool,       // NULL or address we can catch
  offset: i64,            // for pread/pwrite
  iovec_count: u8,        // 0..=8 for readv/writev
}

## Invariants
- No panic on any input
- rc is a non-negative byte count OR -1 with errno in {EBADF, EFAULT, EINVAL, EIO, EAGAIN, EINTR, EPIPE, ENOSPC, ESPIPE, EOVERFLOW}
- Host parity for the /dev/zero, /dev/null, closed-fd cases: ours matches libc::read/write bit-for-bit
- readv/writev total byte count equals the sum of per-iovec byte counts
- Buffer is not read/written past requested len (ASAN + explicit sentinel check before and after)

## Expected bug classes
- Off-by-one in iovec loop, iov_len overflow, fd validation bypass, membrane decision mismatches for cross-page buffers, missing EINTR retry, sign handling for large counts (SSIZE_MAX), ESPIPE not mapped for pread/pwrite on pipes

## Sentinel pattern
Allocate 2*buf_len + 2 pages, place guard bytes (0xAA) before and after the requested window; after the call assert guard bytes unchanged.

## Score
5 × 5 × /2 ≈ 12.5 — tied with bd-o4yda for priority.
close_reason: fuzz_read_write harness committed and green: 16.3M execs / 108K exec/s in 151s. Covers read, write, pread, pwrite, readv, writev against 5 deterministic fd backends (/dev/zero, /dev/null, pipe read, pipe write, closed fd, wild fd). Sentinel-byte guards before/after every buffer window catch any over-count write. Differential parity against libc for non-pipe backends. Two harness-side bugs fixed during bring-up (count > buf_size overrun, buf_offset into post-pad). Zero real impl bugs under the invariant set — the read/write wrapper is solid. Committed 4e263808.

title: Fix br dotted reality-check bead mutation and import loss
description:
During the 2026-05-02 plan-space review, br could read reality-check dotted IDs from JSONL but could not safely mutate several of them. Examples:

- `br --no-db show bd-rchk0.5.6 --json` succeeds.
- `br --no-db update bd-rchk0.5.6 ...` fails with `ISSUE_NOT_FOUND`.
- Fresh temp-DB import from `.beads/issues.jsonl` lists `bd-rchk0.5.6`, but `br show bd-rchk0.5.6 --db <temp>` fails.
- Temp-DB flush refuses to export because the imported DB has 1385 issues while JSONL has 1386, with the missing issue reported as `bd-rchk0.5.6`.
- Project `br doctor --json` still reports DB/JSONL count mismatch (`db`: 1286, `jsonl`: 1386), and `br sync --import-only --json` times out before repairing it.

Root-cause hypothesis: ID-prefix or dotted-child handling is losing or shadowing a parent issue such as `bd-rchk0.5.6` when sibling/child IDs such as `bd-rchk0.5.6.1` also exist. This blocks safe plan-space maintenance because `br update`/`br dep add` cannot revise the affected beads without risking a stale or lossy export.

Required proof before close:
1. Unit tests cover exact lookup, update, dependency add, import, export, and no-db mutation for parent/child dotted IDs including `bd-rchk0.5.6` and `bd-rchk0.5.6.1`, plus nearby IDs such as `bd-rchk0.5.10` and `bd-rchk0.5.10.1`.
2. Regression tests prove JSONL import into a fresh DB preserves the full issue count and that flush refuses no valid record after no-op import, update, and dependency operations.
3. E2E script starts from a copied fixture JSONL, runs `br list`, `br show`, `br update`, `br dep add`, `br dep cycles`, `br sync --import-only`, and `br sync --flush-only`, then verifies issue count, exact IDs, dependency graph, and JSONL parseability.
4. Logs preserve command lines, DB path, JSONL path, before/after counts, failing ID if any, stdout/stderr, exit codes, and reproduction command; no test relies on `--force` export.
5. After the fix, the reality-check plan beads can be revised through normal `br` commands without direct JSONL editing, stale DB loss, or child-ID shadowing.
close_reason: Completed br dotted-ID roundtrip validation: current br 0.2.3 preserves bd-rchk0.5.6 and bd-rchk0.5.6.1 through exact no-db lookup, no-db parent update, no-db dependency add, fresh DB import, DB update, flush-only export, zero dependency cycles, count-preserving post-flush lookup, command transcript, and reproducible artifact scripts/e2e/validate_br_dotted_id_roundtrip.sh. title: btrfs core: resolve named subvolume and snapshot mount selections
description:
Survey finding: `FEATURE_PARITY.md` and `README.md` both claim btrfs subvolume mount support, but `OpenFs::from_device` still hardcodes `BTRFS_FS_TREE_OBJECTID` and the operator-facing CLI rejects `--subvol/--snapshot`. This bead owns the core selection logic in `ffs-core`.

Scope:
- Extend `OpenOptions` with an explicit btrfs mount selection contract (default root, named subvolume, named snapshot, and optionally numeric objectid if that simplifies diagnostics).
- Walk the root tree and resolve the requested selection to the mounted `subvol_objectid` plus `subvol_root_dirid`.
- Return deterministic `FfsError` variants for missing selections, ambiguous names, and selection/type mismatches.
- Keep default-root behavior unchanged when no selection is requested.

Acceptance:
- `OpenFs::open_with_options` can mount a non-default subvolume/snapshot without post-open mutation hacks.
- Synthetic and/or kernel-reference tests prove correct resolution for default root, named subvolume, named snapshot, and missing target cases.
- Structured diagnostics include the requested selector and resolved objectid/root dirid.

title: fix(sched): nice() must report permission failure as EPERM, not raw EACCES
description: nice() surfaced the kernel setpriority's EACCES on a permission failure. POSIX specifies nice() fails with EPERM, and glibc remaps EACCES->EPERM. Verified on host (uid 1000, nice=-4): raw setpriority(-20)->EACCES(13), glibc nice(-20)->EPERM(1); fl returned EACCES. Fixed: map EACCES->EPERM in nice()'s setpriority error branch. Gate conformance_diff_nice_eperm (glibc vs fl nice(-40) rc+errno; exercises the permission path on non-root, gracefully skips remap assertion when privileged).
close_reason: Shipped: nice() maps EACCES->EPERM (POSIX/glibc); gate conformance_diff_nice_eperm (verified on non-root host: raw EACCES vs glibc EPERM).

title: ffs-cli: wire btrfs --subvol and --snapshot mount flags to OpenOptions
description:
Survey finding: `ffs-cli` advertises `--subvol`/`--snapshot` on `mount`, but `validate_btrfs_mount_selection()` hard-rejects both flags even though the underlying codebase already has internal btrfs subvolume context machinery. This bead owns the operator-facing CLI plumbing.

Scope:
- Remove the unconditional rejection path in `crates/ffs-cli/src/main.rs`.
- Thread the requested selection into `OpenOptions` and preserve all existing ext4 behavior.
- Emit structured startup/rejection logs that show requested selector, resolved selection type, and failure class.
- Replace the current `mount_rejects_subvol_flag` / `mount_rejects_snapshot_flag` tests with positive routing tests and deterministic failure diagnostics for nonexistent selectors.

Acceptance:
- `ffs mount ... --subvol <name>` and `ffs mount ... --snapshot <name>` reach `OpenFs::open_with_options` instead of bailing in argument validation.
- Missing selectors fail with clear, stable user-facing errors.
- CLI tests cover default-root, explicit subvolume, explicit snapshot, and nonexistent selection cases.

title: add operator-facing coverage and parity evidence for btrfs subvolume/snapshot mount
description:
Survey finding: current conformance only proves the default btrfs root-alias path, while docs/parity wording imply user-selectable subvolume mount support. This bead closes that evidence gap after the core and CLI work land.

Scope:
- Add harness and/or FUSE E2E coverage that mounts a non-default btrfs subvolume and snapshot through the real CLI/operator path.
- Assert mounted-root `getattr`/`lookup`/`readdir`/`read` behavior is scoped to the selected tree, not the default root.

title: ffs-ondisk: parse_dev_item lacks proptest coverage despite 5 fixed-input tests
description:
Finding (via /testing-metamorphic skill, third visit, different
target): `parse_dev_item` (crates/ffs-ondisk/src/btrfs.rs:1074) is
a pure deterministic 98-byte BtrfsDevItem parser on the btrfs
multi-device probe path. It has FIVE fixed-input tests
(parse_dev_item_valid, _rejects_bytes_used_above_total,
_rejects_zero_devid, _rejects_zero_total_bytes, _too_short) but
ZERO proptests. The bd-7mj5d / bd-9er6s / bd-590tc style metamorphic
relations are not exercised:

  MR-1 (No-panic over arbitrary bytes): for any input of any length
       in [0, 256], parse_dev_item must return either Ok or a structured
       ParseError — never panic. This is the basic robustness contract
       that the existing fuzz target enforces but the proptest layer
       does not.

  MR-2 (Tail-invariance): the parser only reads bytes 0..98. For any
       valid input of length 98, appending arbitrary suffix bytes
       MUST yield the same parse result. A regression that
       accidentally hashed or dispatched on tail bytes would slip
       past the existing tests.

  MR-3 (Field round-trip / byte-offset contract): given valid
       devid/total_bytes/bytes_used/io_*/dev_*/uuid/fsid values, the
       parser returns those exact values from the documented offsets
       (devid@0, total_bytes@8, bytes_used@16, io_align@24, io_width@28,
       sector_size@32, dev_type@36, generation@44, start_offset@52,
       dev_group@60, seek_speed@64, bandwidth@65, uuid@66..82,
       fsid@82..98). Any drift in the offset table would silently
       corrupt every btrfs multi-device read.

Acceptance: 3 new proptests added to the existing
`proptest!` block (l. 3037) with shared ProptestConfig.
notes: Shipped: 3 new btrfs proptest MRs in crates/ffs-ondisk/src/btrfs.rs. MR-1 (no-panic over arbitrary 0..=256 byte inputs); MR-2 (tail-invariance — bytes >= 98 must not affect parse output); MR-3 (field-offset contract — every documented field offset returns the expected value across the input space, pins the 98-byte layout). All 8 parse_dev_item tests (5 existing fixed-input + 3 new proptests) pass via rch exec -- cargo test -p ffs-ondisk --lib parse_dev_item.

title: [parity][bug] swprintf/vswprintf empty the buffer on truncation instead of writing glibc's truncated prefix
description: Found by NEW swprintf_truncation_differential_fuzz (live glibc, exact dest-buffer compare). glibc swprintf returns -1 when the result+NUL exceeds n (correct in fl), BUT on truncation it STILL writes the truncated prefix (min(n-1,produced) wide chars) followed by a NUL — exactly like the success path — rather than emptying the buffer. fl's swprintf/vswprintf wrote only *s=0 (an empty string) on truncation, so e.g. swprintf(buf,3,'hello') gave ['h',0... no, [0]] vs glibc ['h','e',0]. Return value (-1) was already correct; only the truncated buffer diverged (same class as wcsxfrm bd-yc71xq). Fixed: call narrow_to_wide_buf (which writes min(n-1,produced)+NUL, no-ops for null/n==0) on the truncation path too, then return -1. POSIX leaves the buffer unspecified once the function errors, but glibc is deterministic and the narrow snprintf path writes the prefix. 0-div across hello/int/neg/char/hex/str/%% cases x n in 0..len+2.
close_reason: done

title: feat(io): posix_fallocate should emulate (zero-fill) on EOPNOTSUPP/ENOSYS like glibc
description: posix_fallocate calls sys_fallocate(fd,0,offset,len) and returns its errno directly. glibc's posix_fallocate, when fallocate returns EOPNOTSUPP or ENOSYS (filesystems without fallocate support), FALLS BACK to a generic emulation: fstat for st_blksize, then for each block in [offset,offset+len) pread one byte and, if it's a hole, pwrite a 0 to force allocation (extending the file to offset+len, preserving existing data, never shrinking). fl returns EOPNOTSUPP instead -> divergence on unsupported FS. Implement glibc's posix_fallocate fallback (sysdeps/posix/posix_fallocate.c). NOTE: needs a fallocate-unsupported FS to differential-test (ext4/tmpfs support it), so the gate likely needs a crafted mount or to mock the EOPNOTSUPP path; deferred as focused-session work. Same return-contract (errno-direct, not -1) already correct.
close_reason: Verified at HEAD, not assumed: internal_fallocate_emulate + posix_fallocate_dispatch are live and faithful to glibc (EOPNOTSUPP-only fallback), and the named gate conformance_diff_posix_fallocate was observed compiling and executing 14 passed / 0 failed on RCH worker vmi1153651. Bead title's ENOSYS half is a premise error, corrected in the comment.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: REOPENED 2026-08-06. This bead's fix (d0e9059cb) was deleted by e634aff2a nine days later — the first Jun-26 silent deletion (bd-bldxfy). Both halves are gone: internal_fallocate_emulate no longer exists, so conformance_diff_posix_fallocate cannot compile and has reported nothing since; and posix_fallocate itself now returns the raw syscall error with NO EOPNOTSUPP/ENOSYS branch, so the emulation this bead delivered is not running in production either. Live parity divergence vs glibc, tracked with full evidence in bd-om1s58.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
VERIFIED DONE AT HEAD, closed on the three-step rule (source read, gate opened, gate observed executing) rather than on a comment.

1. SOURCE AT HEAD. crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs:12493 internal_fallocate_emulate exists and is faithful to sysdeps/posix/posix_fallocate.c: EINVAL on negative offset/len, EFBIG on off_t overflow, EBADF for O_APPEND descriptors and for fstat failure, ESPIPE for FIFOs, ENODEV for non-regular files, ftruncate-only for len==0 that extends, block stride from fstatfs capped at 4096 with a 512 fallback for f_bsize==0, first probe at offset+(len-1)%increment, pread-before-pwrite so an already-allocated non-zero byte is skipped and existing data is never clobbered, errno-direct return. Iteration count matches glibc's (len-1)/increment+1. posix_fallocate:12629 routes the raw syscall through posix_fallocate_dispatch:12597, which emulates on EOPNOTSUPP and returns every other errno verbatim.

2. TITLE PREMISE CORRECTED. This bead (and bd-om1s58) says the fallback covers EOPNOTSUPP *and ENOSYS*. glibc's Linux posix_fallocate falls back ONLY on EOPNOTSUPP; ENOSYS is returned to the caller. fl matches glibc, and the gate pins that distinction explicitly (dispatch_returns_other_errnos_unchanged iterates ENOSYS/ENOSPC/EFBIG/EBADF and asserts the file is untouched). Do not 'fix' fl to emulate on ENOSYS -- that would be the divergence.

3. GATE OBSERVED COMPILING AND EXECUTING, non-zero pass count. RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 env -u CARGO_TARGET_DIR rch exec -- cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test conformance_diff_posix_fallocate on RCH worker vmi1153651: 'test result: ok. 14 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out'. This answers the bead's REOPENED note directly -- the target is no longer dark and internal_fallocate_emulate is no longer missing.

4. THE GATE CAN FAIL. dispatch_on_eopnotsupp_runs_the_emulation drives the EOPNOTSUPP branch directly and asserts file length 4000, the leading 100 bytes still 0x42, and the remainder zero -- so a reverted or no-op emulation fails it. exported_entry_point_matches_glibc runs live libc::posix_fallocate against fl's exported symbol on identically built files and compares rc and bytes. The remaining 12 cover empty/leading-data extension, offset beyond EOF, sparse holes, zero-length noop vs truncate-extend, unaligned offset+len, and multi-block extension.

title: Refine remediation catalog with data-safety severity and dead-end prevention
description:
Supplemental refinement for bd-rchk0.5.12. A remediation catalog can still fail users if entries say what happened but not whether their data is safe, whether mutation occurred, what command to run next, or who owns the unresolved state. This bead adds data-safety severity and dead-end prevention as hard catalog requirements.

Scope: define remediation entries around user decision-making: data-safety impact, mutation status, confidence state, immediate next command, safe retry policy, escalation path, owning bead/subsystem, docs target, and release-gate effect. Every fail/skip/warn/error state should either have a concrete action or an explicit non-goal rationale.

Required proof before close:
1. Unit/schema tests reject remediation rows missing data-safety severity, mutation status, operator action, safe retry policy, owning bead/subsystem, docs target, reproduction command, artifact requirements, or release-gate effect.
2. Unit tests cover product failure, host capability skip, unsupported operation, stale artifact, security refusal, unsafe repair refusal, low-confidence repair, noisy performance, missing proof lane, inconclusive oracle conflict, and pass-with-experimental-caveat entries.
3. E2E smoke feeds fixture outcomes through the catalog and proves JSON, CLI/TUI text, proof-bundle summary, and release-gate output all contain the same remediation id and no dead-end fail/skip/warn state.
4. Logs include outcome code, remediation id, data-safety severity, mutation status, action command or explicit non-goal, owner/bead, source artifact hash, docs target, output paths, and reproduction command.
5. Release gates must fail closed if any user-visible failure, skip, security refusal, unsupported feature, stale evidence, or unsafe repair state lacks a remediation entry with concrete next action or explicit non-goal rationale.

title: Add differential gate for mempcpy + rawmemchr (return-end / unbounded-search) vs glibc
fix(io): dup2(fd,fd) on aarch64 returned EINVAL via dup3 routing (must return fd)
description: On arches without a native dup2 syscall (aarch64), sys_dup2 routes through dup3(oldfd,newfd,0). dup3 returns EINVAL when oldfd==newfd, but POSIX dup2(fd,fd) must return fd unchanged when fd is valid (EBADF if not). glibc special-cases equal fds: validate the fd via fcntl(F_GETFL) and return newfd or -1. fl lacked this, so dup2(fd,fd) would wrongly EINVAL on aarch64. x86_64 uses native SYS_dup2 (already correct), so this is aarch64-only. Fixed arch-independently in fl::dup2 by mirroring glibc's equal-fd fcntl special-case before the syscall. Gate conformance_diff_dup2_samefd validates the contract + fl's new fcntl path on x86_64 vs host dup2 (valid->fd, closed->EBADF, never EINVAL).
close_reason: Shipped: dup2(fd,fd) now mirrors glibc's fcntl-validate special-case (aarch64 dup3 routing returned EINVAL); gate conformance_diff_dup2_samefd.

title: C.1: Implement gshadow line parser in frankenlibc-core
description:
## Goal
Add a gshadow line parser to frankenlibc-core, following the exact pattern of the existing /etc/passwd parser in crates/frankenlibc-core/src/pwd/mod.rs.

## Reference: Existing Pattern
The passwd parser at pwd/mod.rs uses:
- `pub struct Passwd { pw_name: Vec<u8>, pw_passwd: Vec<u8>, ... }`
- `pub fn parse_passwd_line(line: &[u8]) -> Option<Passwd>` — splits on colons, validates field count
- `pub fn lookup_by_name(content: &[u8], name: &[u8]) -> Option<Passwd>` — iterates lines, matches name

The gshadow parser should follow this EXACT pattern for consistency.

## gshadow File Format (/etc/gshadow)
Each line: `group_name:encrypted_password:administrators:members`
- group_name: non-empty, no colons (same as /etc/group name field)
- encrypted_password: may be empty (""), or "!" (locked), or "*" (no password)
- administrators: comma-separated usernames (may be empty — no admins)
- members: comma-separated usernames (may be empty — no members)

Example lines:
  root:*::
  shadow:!::
  sudo:!::alice,bob
  dev:x:alice:alice,bob,charlie

## Implementation

### File: crates/frankenlibc-core/src/pwd/gshadow.rs (NEW FILE)
Add `pub mod gshadow;` to crates/frankenlibc-core/src/pwd/mod.rs.

### Struct
```rust
pub struct Gshadow {
    pub sg_namp: Vec<u8>,    // group name
    pub sg_passwd: Vec<u8>,  // encrypted password
    pub sg_adm: Vec<u8>,     // raw comma-separated admin list
    pub sg_mem: Vec<u8>,     // raw comma-separated member list
}
```

### Functions
```rust
pub fn parse_gshadow_line(line: &[u8]) -> Option<Gshadow>
pub fn lookup_gshadow_by_name(content: &[u8], name: &[u8]) -> Option<Gshadow>
```

### Parsing Logic
1. Skip empty lines and lines starting with #
2. Split on b':' — must have exactly 4 fields
3. Field 0 (name) must be non-empty
4. Fields 1-3 may be empty
5. Return Gshadow with owned Vec<u8> copies

## Inline Tests (#[cfg(test)])
- parse_valid_full_line: `sudo:!:admin1,admin2:user1,user2` -> all 4 fields correct
- parse_minimal_line: `root:*::` -> password="*", admins="", members=""
- parse_empty_password: `grp:::` -> password is empty
- parse_locked_password: `grp:!::` -> password is "!"
- parse_with_admins_and_members: `dev:x:alice:alice,bob` -> admins="alice", members="alice,bob"
- reject_too_few_fields: `root:*:` (3 colons needed, only 2) -> None
- reject_empty_name: `:*::` -> None
- reject_comment_line: `# comment` -> None
- reject_empty_line: "" -> None
- lookup_finds_entry: content with 3 lines, lookup "sudo" finds correct one
- lookup_returns_none_for_missing: lookup "nonexistent" returns None
- lookup_is_case_sensitive: "ROOT" does not match "root"

## Acceptance Criteria
Parser handles all gshadow field combinations. 12 inline tests pass. cargo clippy clean.
close_reason: Implemented gshadow parser in frankenlibc-core/src/pwd/gshadow.rs. Struct Gshadow with sg_namp/sg_passwd/sg_adm/sg_mem fields. parse_gshadow_line() handles comments, blank lines, field validation. lookup_gshadow_by_name() scans content for case-sensitive name match. 14 inline tests pass covering: valid full/minimal lines, empty/locked password, admin+member lists, reject malformed, lookup hit/miss/case sensitivity.

title: getopt: no argument permutation (glibc default) and +/- optstring prefix modes unhandled
description: frankenlibc getopt is unconditionally POSIX-strict (see unistd_abi.rs:2816 comment): it stops at the first non-option argument and never permutes. glibc's DEFAULT mode permutes argv so options after non-options are still found -- getopt([prog,-a,file,-b],ab) in glibc returns a then b (optind=3, file moved to tail); frankenlibc returns only a then -1. Also the leading + (stop/POSIXLY_CORRECT) and - (RETURN_IN_ORDER, non-options returned as arg of option \1) optstring prefixes are not handled -- getopt_arg_mode treats + and - as ordinary option chars. Verified by host-glibc C probes. Core step_short (getopt/state.rs) takes immutable &[&[u8]] and StepOutcome has no RETURN_IN_ORDER variant; fixing needs first_nonopt/last_nonopt tracking + an argv exchange/permute step (most naturally in the abi layer which owns the real char** argv), plus +/- prefix detection.
close_reason: Implemented glibc-default argument permutation for getopt: parse_getopt_short now rotates the next option element (with its separate argument) ahead of any run of operands, mirroring the rotation onto the caller's real argv pointer array; a leading '+' optstring flag or POSIXLY_CORRECT forces POSIX-strict ordering; the '+'/'-' flag byte is stripped so it is never treated as a selectable option; bsd_getopt simplified to a passthrough. C-probe verified vs host glibc; conformance_diff_getopt updated+passing (5), unistd_abi_test 604 pass. Residual '-' RETURN_IN_ORDER \1 mode and opterr diagnostics tracked in bd-j< new follow-up>.

title: [parity][bug] wcscasecmp/wcsncasecmp return ±1 sign instead of glibc folded-codepoint difference
description: Found by NEW wcscasecmp_differential_fuzz (400k vs live glibc). glibc's case-insensitive WIDE compares return the actual difference of the ASCII-case-folded code points (towlower(c1) minus towlower(c2)) via wint_t arithmetic — e.g. wcscasecmp of U+00C0 vs U+00E0 is -32, of two empty-vs-Gbreve is -304 — NOT a bare +/-1 sign. (Contrast the NON-case wide compares wcscmp/wcsncmp/wmemcmp, which glibc DOES return as +/-1.) fl returned only the sign for wcscasecmp/wcsncasecmp. The narrow strcasecmp already returned the difference; only the wide case-fold variants were wrong. Fixed the production ABI impls (wchar_abi: a.wrapping_sub(b) as i32) plus the core wide.rs functions + their cfg(test) oracle + property-test reference + regenerated the golden corpus sha256. 400k fuzz 0-div incl accented/Greek/circled/fullwidth letters the C locale does not fold.
close_reason: done

title: scan_wordexp_syntax misses bad characters inside parameter expansion
description: `scan_wordexp_syntax` in `unistd_abi.rs` skips all character validation when `parameter_brace_depth > 0`. This means unquoted bad characters (like `|`, `&`, `;`) inside a brace expansion (e.g. `${foo|bar}`) will go undetected, and `wordexp` will return `0` instead of `WRDE_BADCHAR`, breaking parity with glibc.
close_reason: Fixed missing bad character detection inside brace expansion in scan_wordexp_syntax.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: BTRFS TRANSACTION MODEL: btrfs transactions group multiple COW tree updates into an atomic unit. Key concepts: (1) transaction handle (acquire on begin, release on end), (2) delayed items (buffered in memory until transaction commit), (3) transaction commit writes all dirty trees atomically. Our MVCC layer maps naturally onto this: MVCC transaction ≈ btrfs transaction.

description:
RED at clean HEAD, untracked until now. Found while regression-checking bd-ym6gw0.

  RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 env -u CARGO_TARGET_DIR rch exec --base HEAD --clean-overlay --no-overlay \
    -- cargo test -j2 -p frankenlibc-abi --test resolv_abi_test

worker hz2: test result: FAILED. 186 passed; 7 failed; 31 ignored. The identical set fails with a
working tree too, so it is neither a working-tree artifact nor an interaction with other changes.

THE SEVEN:
  ns_sprintrrf_formats_a_record
  ns_sprintrrf_formats_aaaa_record
  ns_sprintrrf_formats_mx_record
  ns_sprintrrf_formats_txt_record_with_quoting
  ns_sprintrrf_falls_back_to_rfc3597_for_unknown_type
  ns_sprintrrf_unsupported_known_type_uses_generic_type_number
  ns_sprintrr_wraps_sprintrrf_via_handle_and_rr

They all fail the same way, and it is NOT an assertion mismatch:

  frankenlibc: runtime kernel panic (fallback)
  frankenlibc: panic location: crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/resolv_abi_test.rs:4197

Line 4197 is `assert!(n > 0)` immediately after the ns_sprintrrf call, so the formatter returns a
NON-POSITIVE length for every record type tried -- A, AAAA, MX, TXT, an unknown type, and a known
but unsupported type -- and the wrapper ns_sprintrr fails with it. That pattern (every type, zero
length) says the entry point is failing before any per-type formatting runs, not that one record
type is formatted wrongly.

FIRST THING TO CHECK: whether ns_sprintrrf is a stub or returns an error unconditionally, and
whether the six sibling arms are simply inheriting one broken entry point. If it is a stub, this is
a missing-implementation bead, not a formatting bug, and it should be retitled as such.

NEGATIVE CASE any fix must pass: the arms already encode it -- a positive return length AND the
rendered text containing " IN A " and "127.0.0.1" for the A record, so returning a non-empty
placeholder string would still fail. Do not weaken them to `n >= 0`.

CONTEXT: these arms are in the 31-ignored / 186-passed resolv_abi_test file, so the suite is red as
a whole and has been; anything gating on this file's exit status is currently gating on a known red.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
PREMISE OF THIS BEAD CORRECTED, 4 of 7 arms fixed, 3 remain on a REAL divergence (c1cd5ce11).

MY FILING WAS WRONG. I wrote 'the formatter returns a non-positive length for every record type'. It does not: it returns correct text. The seven arms asserted a format nobody had measured -- single spaces and no trailing dot -- while both fl AND glibc emit tabs with a dot-terminated owner name. Live glibc 2.42 via libresolv.so.2:
  b'foo.com.\t\t1H IN A\t\t127.0.0.1'
which is byte-identical to what fl produced. So four arms (A, AAAA, TXT, the ns_sprintrr wrapper) were red purely against an invented oracle and are now green, compared against the live host at runtime via dlopen/dlsym. resolv_abi_test on hz2: 190 passed / 3 failed / 31 ignored, from 186 / 7 / 31.

THE 3 REMAINING ARE GENUINE: fl renders unknown and unsupported-known rdata as compact uppercase hex where glibc uses BIND's hex dump.
  fl     \# 3 010203
  glibc  \# 3 (\t; unknown RR type 999\n\t01 02 03 )\t\t\t\t\t; ...

MEASURED FORMAT, probed directly against libresolv.so.2 at lengths 0/1/3/8/16/24/40 so the wrapping rule is known rather than guessed:
  len=0   \# 0\t; unknown RR type 999                     (no parens at all)
  len=1   \# 1 (\t; comment \n\t01 )\t\t\t\t\t\t; .
  len=3   \# 3 (\t; comment \n\t01 02 03 )\t\t\t\t\t; ...
  len=8   ... 08 )\t\t\t; ........
  len=16  ... 0f 10 ; ................        <-- NOTE: NO closing paren emitted
  len=24  full 16-byte line + ASCII, then \n\t + remaining 8 + ) + tabs + ASCII
So: lowercase hex, space separated, 16 bytes per line, an ASCII column after each line (dots for non-printables), closing paren on the final PARTIAL line with tab padding before the trailing comment. The len%16==0 case appears to drop the paren entirely, which looks like a BIND quirk and must be reproduced, not corrected.

UNEXPLAINED, AND WHOEVER TAKES THIS SHOULD RESOLVE IT FIRST: the type token differs by context. My standalone ctypes probe got '0S IN 999' while the SAME glibc call inside the test binary got '0S IN TYPE999'. Until that is understood, do not hardcode either spelling -- the differential comparison is safe because both sides run in the same process, but a hand-written expectation would be wrong in one of the two contexts. That is the same trap this bead already fell into once.

The MX arm fails for the same generic-rendering reason.

title: perf: realloc always alloc+copy+free even when the new size fits the old block's size class — add an in-place fast-path (no copy for grow/shrink within class)
notes: LEVER (HIGH-VALUE, realistic: Vec/string/buffer growth loops): realloc (malloc_abi.rs ~2204) unconditionally pipeline.allocate(size) + copy_nonoverlapping(min(old,new)) + free(old), even when size maps to the SAME allocator size class as old_size (the block already has capacity). Add in-place: after old_size=slot.user_size, if size_class_index(size)==size_class_index(old_size) -> return ptr unchanged (no alloc/copy/free), update the slot's logical user_size to size. size_class_index() already exists (core/malloc/size_class.rs:102). BENCH: realloc-grow loop (push N items doubling) vs original; expect ~no allocs in steady state. WHY TEST-CAPABLE TURN (not cargo-check-only): (1) needs an arena slot user_size mutation API (none public today -> arena surgery); (2) CORRECTNESS-CRITICAL — an in-place GROW that fails to update user_size makes a later realloc copy too few bytes -> silent data loss; a wrong capacity bound -> heap overflow (memory corruption, worse than conformance-RED). Must run the malloc/realloc differential + stress tests, not just cargo check. size-class equality is the safe conservative bound (both sizes <= class capacity which the block has). NEGATIVE-EVIDENCE: rest of realistic surface saturated (see memory printf-scanf-perf-campaign: printf/scanf/tokenize/mb-wc/getline/fgets/calendar/string-mem/strtod all optimized; 11 levers shipped).

fix(inet): setsourcefilter/getsourcefilter used SOL_SOCKET instead of protocol level for MCAST_MSFILTER
description: bd-8bpt3a follow-up. The AF-independent setsourcefilter/getsourcefilter passed MCAST_MSFILTER at SOL_SOCKET, but that option lives at the protocol level (SOL_IP/SOL_IPV6/...). glibc selects the level via __get_sol(family,grouplen) over a 7-protocol sol_map (size-match required, family-match wins, else first size-match, else -1->EINVAL). fl's wrong level yields ENOPROTOOPT(92) where glibc returns EINVAL(22). Fixed: added mcast_get_sol mirroring glibc's table+order (verified struct sizes in=16/in6=28/ax25=16/ipx=16/at=16/rose=28/ll=20) + sol==-1 EINVAL early-return, applied to both fns. (IPv4-specific get/setipv4sourcefilter already correctly used IPPROTO_IP.) Gate conformance_diff_sourcefilter compares rc AND errno vs live glibc.
close_reason: Shipped c131ba2e5: setsourcefilter/getsourcefilter now select the protocol socket level via mcast_get_sol (glibc __get_sol replica, 7-protocol table) instead of SOL_SOCKET — old code yielded ENOPROTOOPT(92) where glibc returns EINVAL(22). title: [bug][parity][abi][f128] strfromf128/strfromf64x wrong arg-ABI (param declared f64, proto _Float128/_Float64x)
description: glibc_internal_abi.rs ~707/698: declared param f64 but C prototype is _Float128/_Float64x. _Float128 is passed in all 128 bits of xmm0; fl reads only low 64 as a double -> garbage (strfromf128('%.40g',1.0Q/3.0Q) -> 1.19e103 vs glibc 0.333...). _Float64x (80-bit) is stack-passed; fl reads stale xmm0. Same class as the documented long-double/f128 architectural limitation (fl uses f64 for long double; cannot represent _Float128 in safe Rust). NO f64-shaped quick fix -> needs a real f128 formatter, mirrors the strtof128/f128-math residual. NOTE strfromf32/strfromf32x are CORRECT (_Float32x==double, _Float32 widens to double in xmm0). title: PORT: getbsize (BSD libutil block-size header)
description: BSD libutil getbsize(headerlenp, blocksizep) reads the BLOCKSIZE environment variable (parsing optional k/K/m/M/g/G suffix as 1024-multiplier), clamps the block size to [512, 1<<30], and returns a pointer to static storage containing the matching header string ("512-blocks", "1K-blocks", "1M-blocks", "1G-blocks"). Used by df(1), du(1), ls(1) and other BSD utilities to render block counts in user-friendly units. Currently missing entirely from frankenlibc-abi. Ship: pure-safe core::stdlib::getbsize::resolve_blocksize parsing the env-var byte slice + format header bytes, plus a thin abi shim in stdlib_abi.rs that reads getenv("BLOCKSIZE"), calls into core, and stores the result in a OnceLock<[u8; 32]> static buffer for the static-pointer return.

title: ffs-types: 27 EXT4_*_FL inode-flag constants lack kernel-conformance test
description:
Finding (via /testing-conformance-harnesses skill, seventh visit,
different target): crates/ffs-types/src/lib.rs declares 27
`pub const EXT4_*_FL: u32` inode-flag constants
(EXT4_SECRM_FL=0x1, EXT4_UNRM_FL=0x2, ..., EXT4_CASEFOLD_FL=0x40000000)
each mirroring a kernel macro from `fs/ext4/ext4.h`. The flags
control inode behaviour (immutable, append-only, journal-data,
extents-on, htree-index, casefold, etc.) and are read by every
ext4 inode parsing path.

There is **no kernel-conformance test** pinning the values to
their canonical kernel macros. A regression that swapped, e.g.,
EXT4_INDEX_FL (0x1000) and EXT4_EXTENTS_FL (0x80000) would silently
treat htree-indexed directories as extent-tree-using files and
vice-versa — both fatal misclassifications.

Pairs with bd-k81lq (ext4 reserved-inode constants), bd-343v3 (ext4
file-type constants), bd-khzn4 (btrfs tree objectids), bd-f0q7n
(btrfs item keys), bd-xhswi (btrfs csum-type constants).

Acceptance: kernel-conformance unit test pinning all 27
EXT4_*_FL constants to their canonical kernel macro values. Plus
TWO invariants: (1) each flag is a distinct power-of-2 bit (single
bit set), and (2) no two flags share a bit (pairwise AND is zero).
A regression that accidentally renumbered a flag onto another
flag's bit would fail the second invariant.
notes: Shipped: kernel-conformance unit test ext4_inode_flag_constants_match_kernel_header in crates/ffs-types/src/lib.rs's tests module. Pins all 27 EXT4_*_FL u32 constants (SECRM through CASEFOLD) to their canonical kernel macro values, plus two structural invariants: (1) every flag is a single power-of-2 bit (is_power_of_two), (2) no two flags share a bit (pairwise AND is zero), plus cross-check that OR of all 27 flags has exactly 27 bits set. Pairs with bd-k81lq / bd-343v3 / bd-khzn4 / bd-f0q7n / bd-xhswi / bd-vnfhb. Verified via rch exec -- cargo test -p ffs-types --lib ext4_inode_flag_constants_match_kernel_header.

title: PORT: __dso_handle (Itanium C++ ABI per-DSO handle)
description: Port the Itanium C++ ABI `__dso_handle` global symbol. It is a `void *` defined per-DSO that callers (notably `__cxa_atexit(func, arg, dso_handle)`) use as a unique handle identifying the dynamic shared object. Standard convention: define it as a pointer that holds its own address (so the address is unique per-DSO and stable across linkage). Without it, C++ programs linking against our libc fail at static-init time when the compiler emits `__cxa_atexit(..., &__dso_handle)`. Implementation: single line — `pub static __dso_handle: ... = ...` exported as a no_mangle symbol. Tests verify the symbol resolves and __cxa_atexit accepts &__dso_handle as the dso_handle argument.

title: [RED][flaky] frankenlibc_conformance --lib is unstable under parallel libtest: 2 of 5 runs red with two different manifestations, green single-threaded
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-15 (BlackThrush), after bd-0ftdgt fixed the one DETERMINISTIC crash in this suite.
Harness in every row: cargo test -j2 -p frankenlibc_conformance --lib, via
RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 env -u CARGO_TARGET_DIR rch exec.

  worker        threads   result
  vmi1227854    default   test result: ok. 173 passed; 0 failed
  vmi1149989    default   test result: ok. 173 passed; 0 failed
  vmi1149989    default   test result: FAILED. 172 passed; 1 failed
                          -> implementation::tests::process_ops_fixture_cases_match_execute_fixture_case
  hz2           default   SIGSEGV after 122 of 173 tests reported, no summary line
  vmi1227854    default   test result: ok. 173 passed; 0 failed
  hz1           1         test result: ok. 173 passed; 0 failed   (all 173 reported)

So: 3 of 5 default-threaded runs green, 2 red with TWO DIFFERENT manifestations, on three different
workers; and the single-threaded run is green. The instability is PARALLELISM-INDUCED, not
ordering-induced and not worker-specific.

WHY THIS IS FILED SEPARATELY FROM bd-0ftdgt. That bead's defect was deterministic and is genuinely
closed: fcloseall unregistered the standard streams, wave02-then-wave06 reproduced it every time,
and it is fixed and gated. This is a DIFFERENT crash -- it survives that fix, it is intermittent, and
it does not reproduce single-threaded. Do not re-close bd-0ftdgt's reproducer expecting this to go
away with it.

WHAT IS NOT YET KNOWN, stated plainly: the failure TEXT for the process_ops row was lost, because
that run was captured through a grep filter instead of to a full log. Which fixture case mismatched,
and which test was in flight during the hz2 SIGSEGV, are both still unidentified. libtest interleaves
parallel threads, so the last reported 'ok' does not name the culprit.

NEXT STEP, cheap and decisive for the FAILED half: re-run the default-threaded suite to a FULL log
(no grep filter in the pipeline) until process_ops fails again, then read its assertion. For the
SIGSEGV half, the same log narrows the candidate set to the tests that had not yet reported.

THE CLASS. These fixture arms share one process and mutate global state: environment variables,
current working directory, stdout/stderr redirection, signal dispositions, locale, and child
processes. bd-ry1dg5 closed the child-process half of that (a fork/reap lock landed in 8bcae16e8)
and it did NOT make these rows green, which is direct evidence that at least one other shared-state
axis is live. Treat each axis as its own lever rather than adding one blanket lock.

DO NOT 'fix' this by forcing --test-threads=1 in CI. That hides the defect rather than removing it,
and it would also hide the next one; the suite is supposed to be safe under parallel libtest.

comments.text:
