THE ASSERTION-MISMATCH HALF IS CLOSED. Root cause was child-lifecycle overlap: popen forks INSIDE fl, so the fork/reap lock landed in 8bcae16e8 never saw its child. A live popen child made the no-child arms report RC_0, and a wait(-1) arm reaping popen's child made pclose report -1. Extending the lock to popen/pclose/system/fork/_Fork/vfork/forkpty/execve closed it. Measured on worker hz1, harness = looping the built conformance test binary (~17s per whole-suite run, built by RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 env -u CARGO_TARGET_DIR rch exec -- cargo test -j2 -p frankenlibc_conformance --lib):
  before: 5 failures in 25 iterations, named as wait4_no_child RC_0, waitid_no_child RC_0, pclose STATUS_-1
  after:  0 failures in 30 iterations
That also explains the earlier process_ops row from the rch runs -- same class.

THE SIGSEGV HALF SURVIVES. One SIGSEGV in those 30 post-fix iterations (iteration 7 of the second batch), plus an rch run on hz1 that ended 'signal: 11, SIGSEGV' with no summary line. So it is real, it is roughly 1-in-30 on hz1, and it is NOT the child-lifecycle race.

THIS BEAD NOW MEANS ONLY THE SIGSEGV. Renaming it in spirit: everything above the line is done.

WHAT MAKES THE NEXT STEP CHEAP, and it is the method that cracked the other half: do not re-roll rch jobs. Loop the prebuilt binary over ssh on a worker (about 17s per iteration versus about 5 minutes per rch job) until it segfaults, with the loop capturing FULL output per iteration rather than a grep filter. Then the set of tests that had not yet reported bounds the culprit. Candidate axes, none yet ruled out: the signal_async arms install process-wide handlers while siblings run; the setjmp/longjmp arms unwind across frames; the fortify arms deliberately smash memory in children and one of them running in the parent would look exactly like this.

DO NOT force --test-threads=1 to make it green -- the single-threaded run already passes, which is the whole point.

title: [HIGH] open_fs_btrfs_walk_root_tree smoke assertions are stale against default-root mount semantics
description:
# Review finding

The `build_btrfs_image()` smoke suite is failing early today on missing default-root resolution, but the test body behind `open_fs_btrfs_walk_root_tree` is also stale against the current mount contract. It still asserts that the walked root tree contains exactly one item with `objectid=256` and an 8-byte dummy payload.

## Evidence
- Failing suite today: `tests::open_fs_btrfs_walk_root_tree` is in the red set from `cargo test --workspace --all-targets`, but it currently aborts before its assertions because `OpenFs::from_device(..., OpenOptions::default())` cannot resolve a default-root `ROOT_ITEM`.
- Test assertions: `crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:22736-22748` expect `items.len() == 1`, `items[0].key.objectid == 256`, `item_type == 132`, and dummy payload bytes.
- Current selection logic opens btrfs under `BtrfsMountSelection::DefaultRoot` when no selector is supplied: `crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:2395-2428`. Any fixture fix that adds the missing default-root `ROOT_ITEM` for objectid 5 or otherwise models current semantics will likely invalidate the old single-item/objectid-256 expectation unless the test explicitly opens a non-default selection.

## Why this is high severity
This is a likely second workspace-red failure masked by the earlier `NotFound` abort. If the fixture is repaired without aligning this test, the gate will still stay red.

## Repro
Current gate: `rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/rch_target_frankenfs_cod cargo test --workspace --all-targets`

## Expected fix direction
Either:
- make the smoke test open an explicit non-default/root-tree-focused selection and keep the current objectid-256 assertions, or
- update the fixture and assertions to reflect the default-root mount contract and the resulting walked root-tree inventory.
Do not stop at making `OpenFs::from_device()` succeed; prove the post-open root-tree assertions still match the intended contract.

title: Refine deterministic fuzz smoke with seed provenance minimization and quarantine policy
description:
Supplemental refinement for bd-rchk7.4. A deterministic fuzz smoke gate is useful only if seed provenance, minimization, timeout handling, and quarantine rules are explicit. Otherwise the smoke gate can become flaky, silently drop hard seeds, or accept error-class drift without a reproducible follow-up.

Scope: define a seed manifest with source, provenance, parser surface, expected classification, minimization status, timeout budget, resource budget, quarantine state, owning bead, and corpus checksum. The smoke gate should be bounded but strict about panic, hang, timeout, and unexpected classification drift.

Required proof before close:
1. Unit/schema tests reject seed rows missing seed id, source/provenance, target parser, corpus checksum, expected classification, timeout budget, resource budget, minimization status, quarantine status, and owning bead for quarantined seeds.
2. Unit tests cover panic classification, timeout classification, resource-cap classification, expected error drift, minimized seed replay, non-minimized seed follow-up requirement, duplicate seed ids, stale corpus checksum, and quarantine expiry.
3. E2E smoke runs a fixed seed subset, emits deterministic pass/fail/skip/error artifacts, and proves every failure has a minimized replay command or a follow-up/quarantine entry with owner and expiry.
4. Logs include corpus version, seed id, seed hash, provenance, parser target, expected classification, observed classification, duration, resource counters where available, minimization status, quarantine id, artifact paths, and reproduction command.
5. Release gates and corpus docs cannot count fuzz smoke as healthy if any high-risk parser seed is missing provenance, silently quarantined, timed out without owner, or changed classification without a linked bead.
close_reason: Implemented fuzz-smoke seed provenance, minimization, resource budget, quarantine policy, and rch-safe E2E report capture; validated with rch fuzz-smoke command, E2E smoke, targeted check/clippy, json validation, diff-check, and UBS.

title: bench(core): /etc-db parsers lack runtime-cost benchmark coverage

  * parse_services_line on a typical /etc/services row
  * parse_protocols_line on a typical /etc/protocols row
  * parse_networks_line on a typical /etc/networks row
  * parse_aliases_line on a typical /etc/aliases row
  * parse_netgroup_triples on a 6-line content blob with one matching group

Register in Cargo.toml. Run via `rch exec -- cargo bench -p frankenlibc-bench --bench resolv_parsers_bench` to produce one batch of RESOLV_PARSERS_BENCH rows. No host-glibc dependency. clippy + fmt clean.

title: REVIEW: [HIGH] arc4random_buf silently returns with partially-uninitialized buffer on getrandom short read (nbytes > 256)
description:
Location: crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs:3663-3665

Current code:
    pub unsafe extern "C" fn arc4random_buf(buf: *mut c_void, nbytes: usize) {
        let _ = unsafe { syscall::sys_getrandom(buf as *mut u8, nbytes, 0) };
    }

Defect:
- Linux getrandom(2) 'will never return fewer bytes than requested' for size <= 256 when flags=0, but CAN return a short read for sizes > 256 (man 2 getrandom: 'when reading from /dev/urandom a request of 512 bytes may return fewer if interrupted by a signal').
- arc4random_buf discards the return value and does not loop until nbytes bytes have been written.
- BSD contract: arc4random_buf() never fails; the full buffer must be filled with cryptographically strong random bytes. Our impl leaves the tail uninitialized on a short read, silently handing the caller stack/heap garbage in place of entropy.
- Also: if sys_getrandom returns Err(e), we silently return without filling anything, so buf keeps its prior contents — an app relying on arc4random_buf for a session key or nonce gets deterministic bytes instead of randomness.

Severity: HIGH. Security-relevant: any libc consumer using arc4random_buf for cryptographic material over 256 bytes (session secrets, long keys, nonces for bulk encryption) can receive insufficient entropy. The same pattern affects arc4random at line 3655-3658 where the 4-byte read result is discarded, but on modern kernels a 4-byte read cannot short-read in practice.

Fix plan:
- Loop on partial reads until nbytes bytes are written or the call returns Err with a non-retriable errno.
- Treat EINTR and short reads identically (advance the pointer by bytes-read and keep going).
- Add a regression test that requests a 1_024-byte buffer, asserts the full range is written (no trailing zeros region), and a 0-byte request is a no-op.
close_reason: Fixed: crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs arc4random_buf now loops on partial reads until nbytes bytes have been written, retrying on EINTR and breaking on persistent errors rather than discarding sys_getrandom's return value. null/zero-size inputs are explicit no-ops. Three regression tests added in crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/unistd_abi_test.rs: arc4random_buf_fills_entire_buffer_past_256_bytes (1 KiB sentinel test that detects any trailing >=16-byte window of un-overwritten 0xA5), arc4random_buf_zero_size_is_noop, arc4random_buf_null_pointer_is_noop. Run: rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/rch_target_libc_review cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test unistd_abi_test arc4random -> 3/0 passed in 0.00s. aio_suspend regression tests still pass (4/0). (The 4-byte arc4random path cannot short-read on modern kernels so its call-site is unchanged.)

title: long double ABI: strtold/strtold_l/wcstold (and long-double family) return f64 in XMM0, not 80-bit long double in ST(0) — real C callers read the wrong register. Unfixable in safe Rust (no f80); needs inline asm/naked fn. Known-limitation tracking.
notes: FACET (cc, ABI-audit): the C23 _Float64x NARROWING functions f64x{add,sub,mul,div,fma,sqrt}f128 are also affected — declared (f64,f64)->f64 with a trivial f64 impl, but C23 takes two _Float128 (args should be f128, not f64) and returns _Float64x (80-bit long double). Doubly-wrong ABI (args + return) + stub impl. Unrepresentable in safe Rust (same root): even fixing the f128 args can't fix the _Float64x return register. f32x* siblings are CORRECT (_Float32x=f64, args f128). Unfixable without inline asm / an f80 type.

title: [bug][malloc] bump_alloc mmap-exhaustion fallback returns a headerless pointer that free() hands to glibc — heap corruption + VMA leak (likely root cause of bd-ummyux)
description:
ROOT-CAUSE ANALYSIS (cc_fl / MagentaCondor, 2026-07-25, code-read; NOT yet reproduced under instrumentation).

THE DEFECT. malloc_abi.rs `bump_alloc` (~L1249) reserves from the 256 MiB static BUMP_HEAP and
returns `header.add(BUMP_HEADER_WORDS)` -- i.e. base+16, with BUMP_MAGIC + requested size written
into the 16-byte header immediately before the user pointer. On exhaustion it does:

    if new_pos > BUMP_SIZE {
        // Static bump heap exhausted -- fall back to mmap.
        return unsafe { mmap_alloc(total) };
    }

`mmap_alloc` returns the RAW mmap base as the USER pointer. No BUMP_MAGIC header is written, and
the address is outside the BUMP_HEAP range. Therefore for such a pointer:
  - `is_bump_ptr(p)` == false (range check fails immediately, ~L1337)
  - `bump_allocation_size(p)` == None  => `malloc_usable_size` is wrong
  - `free(p)` falls through the segment check, the is_bump_ptr check, and then either hits the
    fallback table (bootstrap_malloc_passthrough DOES `fallback_insert_sized` it) or `check_ownership`,
    and in BOTH cases ends at `native_libc_free_with_slot(p)` == host glibc free() on an
    mmap(MAP_ANONYMOUS) pointer that glibc never allocated.

That is heap corruption with exactly the "free(): invalid pointer" / "realloc(): invalid pointer"
abort signature already banked in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md as a criterion-analysis hazard.

SECOND DEFECT, SAME FAMILY. The sibling `bump_alloc_aligned` (~L1277) does NOT fall back to mmap --
on the same exhaustion condition it returns `std::ptr::null_mut()` (L1288). So the two bump entry
points disagree about what exhaustion means.

WHY THIS IS THE LIKELY bd-ummyux ROOT CAUSE (NULL at 2048 B under 8-thread fmemopen churn).
The bump heap is monotonic -- BUMP_POS only ever advances, nothing is ever reclaimed. In an
abi-bench binary fl's malloc is interposed process-wide, so every Rust-side Vec/String/thread
allocation can enter our malloc, and any that arrives while the slot's native reentry guard is held
takes `bump_alloc`. Sustained 8-thread churn therefore walks BUMP_POS to 256 MiB. After that EVERY
such allocation becomes its own page-rounded `mmap` that is never `munmap`ed (free cannot recognise
it), so the process VMA count climbs monotonically. At `vm.max_map_count` (65530 default) mmap
starts failing, `mmap_alloc` returns NULL (L1332), `malloc` returns NULL, and Rust's
`handle_alloc_error` aborts with exactly "memory allocation of 2048 bytes failed", exit=134.
This fits every observed property of bd-ummyux: intermittent (7/12 then 1/6 -- depends on how far
BUMP_POS got), abi-bench-specific (interposition), and multi-thread-specific (churn rate).

CHEAP VERIFICATION (do this before fixing -- the analysis is code-read only):
  1. Add two `AtomicUsize` counters: bump_mmap_fallback_hits, and expose BUMP_POS. Print both from
     an atexit/Drop in the probe.
  2. Re-run the stdio_mt_contention 8t fmemopen churn phase on vmi1152480 (the banked repro,
     /data/tmp/fread_ab/base, b_2.err holds the signature).
  3. Predicted: BUMP_POS saturates at ~256 MiB and bump_mmap_fallback_hits is large and rising at
     the moment of the abort; `wc -l /proc/<pid>/maps` climbs toward 65530.
  If BUMP_POS is nowhere near 256 MiB at abort, this hypothesis is WRONG and the NULL comes from
  somewhere else -- say so in the ledger and re-open.

FIX SKETCH (do not ship without the verification above):
  - Give the mmap fallback the same 16-byte BUMP_MAGIC-style header (a distinct MMAP_MAGIC), record
    the mapped length, and teach free()/malloc_usable_size()/realloc() to recognise it and
    `munmap` instead of handing it to glibc. That closes both the corruption and the VMA leak.
  - Make `bump_alloc_aligned` use the same fallback rather than returning NULL.

RELATED: bd-ummyux (the NULL/SIGABRT symptom), and the deployed-allocator lane bd-dcrhgl.
Reserved surface note: malloc_abi.rs is historically cod's file; this is filed as analysis for the
owner rather than edited in place.
notes:
HANDED OFF to SwiftCastle 2026-07-26 03:40Z. My chunk-extension fix (race-fixed, 63/0/1 green) is
uncommitted in the working tree; SwiftCastle is replacing it with the reclaiming mmap-ownership record
this bead originally specified (free/realloc/usable_size + munmap), because that is bounded by
SIMULTANEOUS LIVE overflow allocations whereas chunk extension is bounded by CUMULATIVE churn — only
the former closes bd-ummyux's acceptance target.

WHAT MUST SURVIVE ANY REDESIGN (the actual bug):
 1. is_bump_ptr is the load-bearing predicate. native_libc_free, native_libc_free_with_slot,
    native_libc_realloc (via bump_allocation_size), free, malloc_usable_size and mcheck ALL key on it
    to decide 'ours, never hand to host'. An overflow pointer it does not recognise reaches host
    glibc free()/realloc() — the banked 'free(): invalid pointer' / 'realloc(): invalid pointer' aborts.
 2. bump_alloc_aligned had the mirror defect (NULL on exhaustion where its sibling returned an
    unmanaged mmap). Keep the two paths unified.
 3. Claim-before-publish: any slot-publication step needs a three-state flag (EMPTY/BUSY/live). The
    first version published by CAS-ing base LAST, which let two threads stage metadata into one slot
    and the CAS loser munmap its own region — live base paired with unmapped metadata. Caught by
    SwiftCastle in review.
 4. Keep a diagnostics counter equivalent to malloc_bump_overflow_stats(): the root cause is a CODE
    READ, never reproduced. A churn run that aborts with chunks_mapped==0 REFUTES it and bd-ummyux
    must be reopened against another cause. Do not close bd-ummyux on the invalid-free fix alone.

The 8-thread contract completed 5,120 live/release lifecycles with zero failures and created==released, while lifecycle/realloc tests pin exact ownership, header, size, alignment, copy-before-release, and munmap retirement. No benchmark was run in Lane B. Reopen if any overflow test fails, a valid overflow pointer reaches host free/realloc, or created-minus-released grows after quiescence.

description:
fl's error() and error_at_line() print 'unknown' as the program-name prefix where glibc prints argv[0].

MEASURED 2026-08-04 on a remote worker, and reproduced at clean HEAD via 'rch exec --base HEAD --clean-overlay --no-overlay', so it is NOT caused by any working-tree change:

  fl    = "unknown:parse.c:12: syntax error\n"
  glibc = "<abs path to test binary>:parse.c:12: syntax error\n"

This is the sole reason crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/conformance_diff_error_at_line.rs::error_at_line_matches_glibc is RED, and it has been red at HEAD for as long as the baseline shows. Every case in that test fails on the prefix alone; the file:line, message, and strerror suffix all match.

glibc initialises program_invocation_name / program_invocation_short_name from argv[0] during startup (csu), and error.c uses it via __progname. fl's error path falls back to the literal "unknown", so either the startup capture is not populating the global or error() is not reading it.

WHY IT IS FILED SEPARATELY: found while gating bd-xqg5il (error_print_progname hook). That bead's arms are about the hook and pass; this defect is about the fallback prefix used when NO hook is set. bd-xqg5il's negative control therefore asserts the hook properties (no HOOK prefix, line ends ': boom') rather than byte equality with glibc, and cites this bead for why.

DONE = error_at_line_matches_glibc goes GREEN with no change to its assertions.
close_reason:
FIXED + GATED. error()/error_at_line() now print program_invocation_name (the full argv[0]) instead of the literal "unknown". Commit 3c58516fd.

ROOT CAUSE was TWO defects, not one. The bead suspected either "startup capture is not populating the global" or "error() is not reading it"; it was both:
1. WRONG GLOBAL. glibc's error.c does `#define program_name program_invocation_name` and prints the FULL argv[0]. fl read program_invocation_short_name -- the BASENAME that warn/err use. Confirmed against live glibc 2.42 with a compiled C probe: a binary at <dir>/probe prints "<dir>/probe:parse.c:12: syntax error" while its program_invocation_short_name is "probe". So even with the global populated, fl would have printed the wrong string.
2. UNPOPULATED. startup_abi::init_program_name only runs from fl's own CRT startup, which does not run under rlib tests or interpose-style loading, so the global is null and the fallback fired.

IMPLEMENTATION
- crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/err_abi.rs: new pub(crate) get_progname_full(), placed beside the existing get_progname() so the fallback POLICY has one home rather than two copies. Ladder: published program_invocation_name (capped scan), else /proc/self/cmdline argv[0], else "?". /proc/self/comm is deliberately NOT in this ladder -- Linux truncates it to TASK_COMM_LEN, so it would produce a plausible-looking WRONG full name where the basename ladder can tolerate it.
- crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/stdlib_abi.rs: error() and error_at_line() both route through get_program_name_for_error(); the old get_program_short_name() helper and its now-unused AtomicOrdering import are gone.

GATE (crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/conformance_diff_error_at_line.rs)
- error_at_line_matches_glibc is GREEN with NO change to its assertions. That was this bead's stated DONE condition. error_matches_glibc likewise.
- CONTROL RESTORED, NOT WEAKENED: error_without_hook_still_prints_the_default_prefix was deliberately property-based rather than byte-for-byte, with an in-code comment naming bd-ul4pyl as the reason ("fl resolves its program name to unknown ... would swamp this control with an unrelated diff"). With the defect fixed that reason is gone, so it now asserts byte equality with glibc IN ADDITION to the two hook properties -- strictly stronger, and the property assertions are kept so a regression still reports WHICH half moved. Its comment was also factually wrong after the fix and is corrected.
- TWO NEW ARMS name the specific value against glibc's own globals read live by dlsym, so a regression reads as "we printed the basename" instead of two long paths differing somewhere:
    error_prefix_is_the_full_argv0_not_its_basename
    error_at_line_prefix_is_the_full_argv0_not_its_basename
  Each guards its own discriminator FIRST (asserts program_invocation_name != program_invocation_short_name, i.e. argv[0] has a directory component -- otherwise the arm could not tell the bug from the fix), then rejects BOTH pre-fix shapes: the basename prefix and the literal "unknown:".

EVIDENCE (rch remote, worker vmi1227854, source commit 3c58516fd):
  cargo test -j2 -p frankenlibc-abi --test conformance_diff_error_at_line --test conformance_diff_error --test err_abi_test
    -> conformance_diff_error_at_line: 6 passed; 0 failed  (was 4 arms, 1 of them RED)
    -> conformance_diff_error:         1 passed; 0 failed
    -> err_abi_test:                  39 passed; 0 failed; 3 ignored  (warn/err basename path unaffected)
  cargo clippy -j2 -p frankenlibc-abi --lib --test conformance_diff_error_at_line -- -D warnings
    -> zero findings on any file this bead touched.

NEGATIVE RESULT WORTH KEEPING: the natural place for a unit test of get_progname_full is an inline #[cfg(test)] module in err_abi.rs. It CANNOT WORK -- lib.rs declares `#[cfg(not(test))] pub mod err_abi;`, so the module is excluded from the lib's own test build and anything gated on `test` there is never compiled. I wrote such a test, it silently did not appear (201 lib tests, none matching), and I replaced it with integration coverage. A comment in err_abi.rs now records this. NOTE: efun_abi.rs has an inline #[cfg(test)] block under the same #[cfg(not(test))] declaration, so that one is dead too -- filed separately as bd-0z7a1y.

PRE-EXISTING, NOT CAUSED BY THIS BEAD: stdlib_abi_test has 12 failures (fsmount/fsopen/fspick/move_mount *_preserves_unprivileged_eperm_like_host). VERIFIED pre-existing by baseline replay at clean HEAD via `rch exec --base HEAD --clean-overlay --no-overlay -- cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test stdlib_abi_test`: identical failure SET, same 12 names, 401 passed / 12 failed / 67 ignored on both sides -- the only diff in the two logs is the elapsed-time line. Cause is environmental: these arms expect unprivileged EPERM but rch workers run as root, so the mount syscalls return EINVAL (22). Untouched.

Unrelated working-tree changes by other agents were not reverted.

title: EPIC: New runtime_math kernels (FDR, SOS, localization, Groebner, approachability, Sobol, proof-carrying policy)
description:
Goal: add new alien-artifact kernels that compile down to tiny deterministic guards/dispatch, without blowing hot-path budgets.

Kernels in scope:
- alpha-investing / sequential FDR controller (controls false escalations under many monitors).
- SOS-derived barrier certificates (offline synthesis; runtime polynomial eval).
- Atiyah-Bott localization fixed-point policy chooser (offline fixed points; runtime selection).
- Groebner-basis normal-form canonicalization of violation signatures (offline basis; runtime reduction table).
- Blackwell approachability controller for multi-objective (latency, risk, coverage) set convergence.
- Sobol low-discrepancy probe scheduler (deterministic coverage acceleration).
- Proof-carrying policy tables (offline synth; runtime table lookup + hash/cert checks).

Non-negotiable:
- Each kernel must specify hot-path cost, update cadence, cached state surface, and a test strategy.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## Epic Notes: New runtime_math Kernels (How They Serve libc)

### Purpose
runtime_math is the control plane for the membrane: it decides when to stay fast vs go deep, and when to repair vs deny. New kernels are allowed only if they compile to **small deterministic runtime artifacts** (tables, tiny evaluators) with *explicit* overhead.

### Reverse Core Map Anchoring (Surface -> Failure Class -> Math -> Runtime Artifact)
These kernels must tie to concrete libc pressure points:
- **Hot string/memory kernels** -> overlap/alignment/dispatch faults -> localization + proof-carrying tables -> certified dispatch tables
- **Allocator** -> temporal/provenance corruption + contention regimes -> approachability + SOS barrier -> admissibility guard + multi-objective controller
- **Loader/symbol/IFUNC** -> compatibility drift -> Groebner normal forms + localization -> canonical “violation signatures” + resolver table witnesses
- **Conformance monitoring (many tests, many monitors)** -> multiple-testing false escalations -> alpha-investing FDR -> controller that caps false alarms across families
- **Harness probe selection** -> coverage gaps -> Sobol -> deterministic low-discrepancy probe schedules under budget

### Branch-Diversity Reminder (Project Rule)
Major milestones must include at least:
- conformal statistics: already in-tree (`conformal`, `eprocess`) + this epic adds FDR
- algebraic topology: already in-tree (`cohomology`, `persistence`)
- abstract algebra: this epic adds Groebner
- Grothendieck-Serre methods: already in-tree (`higher_topos`) + localization is in the same “geometry/localization” vein

### Runtime Cost Discipline (Non-Negotiable)
For each kernel we require:
- hot-path invocation budget (ns/op) and cadence (per call vs per epoch)
- cached state surface (what lives in `RuntimeKernelSnapshot`)
- deterministic arithmetic (fixed-point if possible; no heavy transcendentals)
- tests that show behavior invariants and that perf gates remain within budget

### Deliverable Shape
Each kernel follows the same pipeline:
1. Design bead: math contract + loss model + artifact format + invariants
2. Implement bead: tiny runtime evaluator/controller (no heavy machinery)
3. Integrate bead: wire into `RuntimeMathKernel::decide/observe` with versioned snapshot fields
4. Tests/perf bead: microbench + property tests + regression thresholds

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: CobaltCompass: All 9 blockers now CLOSED. Epic complete: alpha-investing FDR, SOS barriers, localization chooser, Groebner normal form, approachability, Sobol, proof-carrying policy tables all integrated with tests and perf validation. 809 membrane tests pass.

title: Refine bd-rchk0.4.3 with actionable failure taxonomy and report contracts

Supplemental refinement for bd-rchk0.4.3. The one-command readiness report should not only count pass/fail/skip/error rows; it must explain what a user should do next, and it must preserve enough evidence to distinguish product bugs from host or harness limitations. This bead uses an explicit dependency instead of a dotted child id until bd-suf84 is fixed.

Required proof before close:
1. Unit/schema tests validate failure taxonomy values for product_failure, host_capability_skip, authoritative_lane_unavailable, harness_failure, unsupported_by_scope, stale_artifact, missing_artifact, noisy_measurement, security_refusal, unsafe_repair_refusal, and pass_with_experimental_caveat.
2. Aggregator tests cover mixed artifacts from xfstests, FUSE capability, mounted write matrix, repair confidence, writeback-cache gate, fuzz smoke, performance runs, proof bundles, and release gates.
3. E2E smoke builds a fixture artifact directory with at least one pass, fail, skip, error, stale, and unsupported record, then emits JSON plus human text whose rows link raw logs, remediation ids, owning beads, and reproduction commands.
4. Logs include report id, input artifact paths/hashes, schema versions, git SHA, host fingerprint, classification decision, controlling artifact, missing-field diagnostics, stale-artifact diagnostics, output paths, and cleanup status.
5. The report must fail closed for missing required lanes and must not permit README/FEATURE_PARITY status upgrades from aggregate counts alone without release-gate approval.

title: ffs-extent: ExtentCache lacks proptest MR coverage of insert/lookup/invalidate invariants
description:
Finding (via /testing-metamorphic skill, fourth visit, different
target): `ExtentCache` (crates/ffs-extent/src/lib.rs:1094-1276) is
the per-inode extent mapping cache. It has 13 fixed-input tests
(cache_hit_after_insert, cache_invalidate_range_removes_overlapping,
cache_invalidate_all_bumps_generation, cache_hit_rate_calculation,
cache_eviction_at_capacity, cache_stats_reset, etc.) but ZERO
proptests exercising the invariants over the full input space.

Concrete metamorphic relations missing:

  MR-1 (Insert/lookup roundtrip): after `insert(ns, m)` for a single-
       block mapping, `lookup(ns, m.logical_start)` returns Some(m'.)
       with the same physical_start and unwritten flag.

  MR-2 (Invalidate-range removes overlapping): after
       `invalidate_range(ns, start, count)`, lookups for any logical
       block in `[start, start+count)` return None — the cache
       generation bump removes the entry from the visible set.

  MR-3 (Invalidate-all clears every namespace): after `invalidate_all()`,
       every previously-inserted mapping returns None on lookup,
       across every namespace, regardless of insert ordering.

  MR-4 (Stats monotonicity): hits and misses only ever increase
       between `reset_stats()` calls; never decrease.

  MR-5 (reset_stats preserves entries): after `reset_stats()`, hit
       counters return to zero but cached entries are still
       lookup-visible.

Acceptance: 5 new proptests covering MR-1 through MR-5 in
crates/ffs-extent/src/lib.rs's existing tests module, using the
ExtentCache::with_capacity API. The proptests should bound input
sizes to keep test time low (capacity in 1..=64, mapping count in
0..=32, namespaces in 1..=8).
notes: Shipped: 5 new ExtentCache MR proptests in crates/ffs-extent/src/lib.rs's proptest! block. MR-1 (insert/lookup roundtrip), MR-2 (invalidate_range removes overlapping entries), MR-3 (invalidate_all clears every namespace), MR-4 (stats monotonicity — hits/misses never decrease), MR-5 (reset_stats preserves cached entries). All 5 pass via rch exec -- cargo test -p ffs-extent --lib proptest_extent_cache. Type fix during writing: ExtentMapping.count is u32 not u64; invalidate_range takes count: u64 (extended via u64::from).

title: PORT: err_set_exit (BSD libutil pre-exit hook)
description: Port the BSD libutil `err_set_exit(void (*func)(int))` setter that registers a callback invoked by err()/errx()/errc()/verr()/verrx()/verrc() immediately before they call exit(). The hook receives the exit code that err is about to use. Used by daemons/utilities to release locks, flush logs, or close PID files when a fatal error path is taken. Implementation: add a Mutex-protected global cell holding Option<unsafe extern "C" fn(c_int)> in err_abi; expose a setter that swaps and returns the previous value; modify each of the 6 fatal exit sites (err, verr, errx, verrx, errc, verrc) to invoke the hook before sys_exit_group. Tests cover the cell-management contract (set/get/swap), invocation order via a fork-based test that sets a hook writing to a shared pipe before calling errx (parent reads the pipe to confirm hook fired before exit).

title: wordexp: fl refuses ALL command substitution with WRDE_CMDSUB even without WRDE_NOCMD, so $(cmd) and $(($(cmd)+1)) diverge from glibc
description:
MEASURED on live glibc 2.42 (ctypes wordexp oracle, found while gating bd-6a9tuc/bd-4f7oo7):

  flags=0    $(($(echo 41)+1))   glibc rc=0 ['42']   fl rc=4 WRDE_CMDSUB
  flags=0    $((`echo 41`+1))    glibc rc=0 ['42']   fl rc=4 WRDE_CMDSUB
  NOCMD      both                  glibc rc=4          fl rc=4        <- this half is CORRECT

fl's wordexp_impl (crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs, the syntax_scan.has_command_substitution branch) returns WRDE_CMDSUB unconditionally with the comment 'For safety, reject command substitution entirely in our implementation. A full implementation would fork /bin/sh -c'. So the NOCMD half of the contract is right and the DEFAULT half is wrong: without WRDE_NOCMD, POSIX and glibc both require the substitution to be performed.

WHY THIS IS FILED AND NOT FIXED IN PASSING: implementing it means executing a shell (glibc forks /bin/sh -c). That is a deliberate security posture decision, not a parity bug fix, and it interacts with the membrane's process-spawn policy. It needs an owner who decides whether fl executes shells at all, and if so under what runtime_policy gate. Do NOT quietly turn it on to make a differential go green.

NEGATIVE CASE any implementation must pass: with WRDE_NOCMD set, $(echo hi), `echo hi`, x$(echo hi)y and "$(echo hi)" must still all return WRDE_CMDSUB and must NOT execute anything -- conformance_diff_wordexp_arith already asserts exactly that against the oracle, so it will catch an implementation that forgets the flag.

SCOPE NOTE: conformance_diff_wordexp_arith deliberately carries NO command-substitution-inside-arithmetic arm, so that gate stays honest about what it covers. Add the arms as part of fixing this bead.

title: [parity][strptime] %s fills tm via UTC, glibc uses localtime (TZ-dependent divergence)
description: strptime("%s") parses an epoch-seconds value and breaks it down into struct tm. fl computes the tm fields in UTC (time_abi.rs ~line 1551, comment 'Convert epoch to tm (UTC)'). glibc uses localtime_r, so the broken-down fields are in the system local timezone. Under a non-UTC TZ they diverge: e.g. strptime("1234567890","%s") on a UTC-5 host gives glibc tm_hour=18 (local) vs fl tm_hour=23 (UTC), and tm_wday/tm_yday can shift across a day boundary. Found by a differential probe of strptime directives (the %p/%j bugs from the same probe were fixed in dd2b76057). Fix: route the %s handler through fl's localtime_r (which is TZ-aware) instead of the inline UTC breakdown, so tm + tm_isdst/tm_gmtoff/tm_zone match glibc. RISK: introduces TZ-dependency + relies on fl localtime parity; %s is a GNU extension (rare). Under TZ=UTC (common CI) the current code already matches, which is why no existing gate caught it. P4.
close_reason: NOT A BUG — architectural. fl is a UTC-only libc by explicit design: localtime_r is documented 'Identical to gmtime_r since we only support UTC' (time_abi.rs:441), hardcoding tm_gmtoff=0 / tm_zone=UTC. strptime %s computing UTC is therefore CONSISTENT with fl's own localtime; routing it through localtime_r would not change the result. The glibc divergence is the project-wide UTC-only choice (affects localtime/mktime/strftime-local/strptime-%s uniformly), not a %s-specific bug, and matching glibc would require a full TZ database — out of scope. Under TZ=UTC (common CI) fl matches glibc, which is why no gate flagged it. Same class as the deliberate-divergence precedents.

title: PORT: crypt_r/rn/ra + crypt_gensalt/_r/_rn/_ra + xcrypt_r/_gensalt/_gensalt_r
description: Add the remaining libcrypt re-entrant + gensalt API to close the libcrypt parity gap. Our existing crypt() supports MD5/SHA-256/SHA-512 already; build on it. (1) crypt_r(key, salt, *data) -> *mut c_char: call crypt(), copy the result string into data->output (which sits at offset 0 of struct crypt_data per glibc and libxcrypt), return data as *mut c_char. (2) crypt_rn(key, salt, *data, size) -> *mut c_char: like crypt_r with explicit size; refuse if size < result length. (3) crypt_ra(key, salt, **data, *size) -> *mut c_char: auto-allocating version; if *data NULL or *size too small, malloc 384 bytes (CRYPT_OUTPUT_SIZE). (4) crypt_gensalt(prefix, count, *rbytes, nrbytes) -> *mut c_char: generate a salt string for the requested algorithm (default $6$ when prefix is NULL/empty) using rbytes as a random source; return pointer to a static thread-local buffer. (5) crypt_gensalt_r(prefix, count, *rbytes, nrbytes, *output, output_size) -> *mut c_char: same into caller buffer. (6) crypt_gensalt_rn(...) -> alias of _r. (7) crypt_gensalt_ra(prefix, count, *rbytes, nrbytes) -> *mut c_char: malloc + format. (8)/(9)/(10) xcrypt_r / xcrypt_gensalt / xcrypt_gensalt_r — aliases.
close_reason: shipped: 10 libcrypt entries (crypt_r/rn/ra; crypt_gensalt/_r/_rn/_ra; xcrypt_r/_gensalt/_gensalt_r) building on existing crypt() + 10 abi tests including round-trip via gensalt → crypt

title: PORT: 25 libuuid functions (RFC 4122/v1/v3/v4/v5/v6/v7 UUID handling)
description: Add 25 libuuid functions to close the libuuid.so.1 surface gap (DCE 1.1 / RFC 4122 / draft-ietf-uuidrev-rfc4122bis UUID handling). UUIDs are 16-byte structs; the API is pure-safe except for time/RNG entries which use getrandom + gettimeofday. (1) uuid_clear/uuid_copy/uuid_compare/uuid_is_null/uuid_variant/uuid_type — pure byte ops. (2) uuid_parse/uuid_parse_range/uuid_unparse{,_lower,_upper}/uuid_get_template — text<->bytes. (3) uuid_generate{,_random} — v4 from getrandom. (4) uuid_generate_time{,_safe,_cont,_v6,_v7} — v1/v6/v7 from gettimeofday + getrandom (RFC 4122 §4.5 random node-id). (5) uuid_generate_md5/uuid_generate_sha1 — v3/v5 namespace UUIDs via md-5 / sha2 crates. (6) uuid_time/uuid_time64 — extract v1 timestamp. (7) __uuid_generate_random/__uuid_generate_time/__uuid_generate_time_cont — internal-namespace aliases.
close_reason: withdrawn: project hooks gate libuuid out of scope (libuuid is util-linux's separate libuuid.so.1, not part of glibc's libc.so.6 — frankenlibc-abi only promises the libc surface). Keeping uuid_abi out of the crate per the explicit policy comment auto-injected on the test file.

title: syscall: typed statfs veneer
[bug][parity][time] asctime/ctime return NULL for year>=10000; out-of-range wday/mon wrap instead of '???'
description: Found via zero-coverage non-math scan, confirmed vs glibc 2.42. (1) Non-reentrant asctime/ctime delegated to asctime_r/ctime_r which cap at the 26-byte contract buffer and return NULL+EOVERFLOW for year>=10000. glibc's non-reentrant form uses a WIDER static buffer and succeeds (asctime(y10000)='Wed Jan  2 03:04:05 10000', up to 62-char strings), bounded only by tm_year+1900 overflowing int. asctime_r/ctime_r correctly still cap at 26. (2) format_asctime used tm_wday.rem_euclid(7)/tm_mon.rem_euclid(12) -> always in-bounds so the '???' fallback never fired; glibc prints '???' for out-of-range wday(8)/mon(13). Fix: core format_asctime_full (no 26 cap) + bounds-check wday/mon -> '???' + tm_year.checked_add(1900) overflow->NULL; non-r asctime/ctime use 64-byte buffer + format_asctime_full. Gate conformance_diff_asctime_range (dlsym); asctime_r_differential_fuzz still green.
close_reason: Shipped. format_asctime_full + ??? bounds-check + year-overflow guard; non-r uses 64B buffer. Gate conformance_diff_asctime_range green, asctime_r fuzz unchanged.

title: PORT: 14 NIS / yp_* fail-safe libnsl stubs
description: Add 14 fail-safe NIS / yp_* stubs (libnsl parity). NIS (Yellow Pages) is dead infrastructure; modern Linux systems do not run ypbind. These wrappers exist so binaries that statically reference yp_* through libc do not fail at link time, and graceful YPERR_NODOM (= 12, local NIS domain not set) is returned at runtime. (1) yp_get_default_domain(**outdomain): write NULL, return YPERR_NODOM. (2) yp_bind(*dom): return YPERR_DOMAIN. (3) yp_unbind(*dom): no-op. (4) yp_match / yp_first / yp_next / yp_all / yp_master / yp_order / yp_maplist / yp_update: zero out outputs, return YPERR_DOMAIN. (5) yperr_string(err) and ypbinderr_string(err): return static "(no such NIS error)" or known descriptions. (6) ypprot_err(code): convert ypbind protocol error code to YPERR_* (we just return YPERR_YPBIND).
close_reason: shipped: 14 NIS yp_* + yperr_string + ypbinderr_string + ypprot_err fail-safe stubs + 14 abi tests covering YPERR_* codes and output-zeroing semantics

title: [bug][parity][strfmon] NaN renders 'NaN' (loses sign); duplicate (/+ flags accepted
description: Found via zero-coverage non-math scan, confirmed vs glibc 2.42 (C locale). (1) render_value -> format_fixed -> format!('{x:.prec}') prints NaN as 'NaN'; negative=value<0.0 is false for NaN so sign dropped. glibc renders 'nan' lowercase with leading '-' iff signbit (%n -nan -> -nan; %(n -nan -> -nan not parenthesized). (2) parse_spec flag loop allowed repeated '+'/'(' (re-set bool); glibc rejects a repeated '+' or '(' with -1/EINVAL (duplicate =/^/!/- are allowed). Fix: NaN early-return in render_value (sign by is_sign_negative + 'nan', field-width via caller); return None on second '+'/'('. Gate conformance_diff_strfmon_nan_flags. Left/right-prec interaction with NaN is glibc-internal-width, not pinned.
close_reason: Shipped. NaN early-return (sign+nan) + duplicate +/( rejection. Gate conformance_diff_strfmon_nan_flags green; existing strfmon gates unchanged.

title: PORT: warnc + vwarnc + errc + verrc (BSD err.h explicit-code variants)
description: BSD/NetBSD <err.h> extensions warnc(code, fmt, ...), vwarnc(code, fmt, ap), errc(eval, code, fmt, ...), verrc(eval, code, fmt, ap) take an explicit errno code instead of consulting the global *__errno_location(). Useful when the caller has already preserved errno or wants to report a different code than the one currently set. Currently err_abi.rs ships warn/vwarn/warnx/vwarnx/err/verr/errx/verrx but is missing the explicit-code variants. Implement as 4 thin shims that call write_err_message with an overridden errno (refactor saved_errno injection) — no new core module needed since byte-level format_err_message in core already accepts the errno-text as a parameter.

title: External journal: compute journal segments from external device geometry
description:
When replaying an external journal, we need to compute JournalSegment entries. For an internal journal, segments come from the journal inode's extent tree. For an external journal, the entire device is the journal:
- JBD2 superblock occupies block 0.
- Journal blocks span from block s_first_log_block to block s_maxlen.
- Each journal block = one filesystem block (block size from JBD2 superblock).

Implement a function external_journal_segments(jbd2_sb: &Jbd2Superblock) -> Vec<JournalSegment> that produces the segment list for an external journal device.

ACCEPTANCE: Function correctly computes segments. Test with a synthetic JBD2 superblock.
close_reason: Added Jbd2Superblock::external_journal_segment() that computes JournalSegment from first_log_block and max_len. Commit 7a8ede4.

This bead defines the calibration corpus and statistical output required by the repair confidence lab.

Required proof before close:

2. The corpus includes recoverable single-block corruption, recoverable multi-block corruption within symbol budget, unrecoverable corruption beyond budget, stale symbols, insufficient symbols, ledger tamper, wrong-image ledger, hostile path, and verification-failure cases.
3. E2E/harness smoke runs a bounded calibration subset and emits per-case JSON plus aggregate confidence summary without requiring the long campaign by default.

title: feat(iconv): combining-multibyte SBCS codecs (T.61, ISO-6937, ANSI_X3.110, NAPLPS)
description: glibc supports T.61/T.61-8BIT, ISO_6937/ISO_6937-2, ANSI_X3.110(ISO-IR-99), CSA_T500, NAPLPS(CSISO99NAPLPS), ISO-IR-90/103/156 — fl rejects all. These are 8-bit sets where certain bytes (0xC1-0xCF in ISO-6937/T.61) are COMBINING-DIACRITIC PREFIXES: decode reads prefix byte + following letter byte -> a precomposed codepoint (2-byte decode), and encode decomposes precomposed cps -> prefix+letter (2-byte encode). codec_char flags DEC_MULTIBYTE_LEAD. Needs a stateful/2-byte decode path (model on a dedicated whole-buffer branch) + multi-byte encode (encode_sbcs_mb exists). Generate accent-prefix tables from host glibc. Niche.
close_reason: Done 4342ef520: ISO_6937/ISO_6937-2/T.61/ANSI_X3.110 via 2-byte-DBCS infra (combining-prefix leads 0xC1-0xCF decode to 1 precomposed cp). Gate conformance_diff_iconv_iso6937. 278 codecs.

scalb was not an approximation of scalb; it was a different function -- x * (2.0).powf(exp) in
unistd_abi.rs for scalb/scalbf, and a bare scalbn(x, y as i32) for scalbl in math_abi.rs.

TWO DEFECTS, as diagnosed on this bead:
1. 2.0.powf(1024) overflows to +inf, so scalb(0, 1024) computed 0 * inf = NaN and raised a spurious
   FE_INVALID where glibc returns 0 silently.
2. A NON-INTEGRAL exponent -- the defining SVID behaviour -- was not a domain error at all.
   glibc: NaN + FE_INVALID + EDOM(33). fl returned a finite value with no flag.

Implemented glibc's __ieee754_scalb kernel plus the w_scalb errno wrapper as ONE shared helper pair
in math_abi.rs, called by all three widths so they cannot drift, exactly as the spec on this bead
called for. Evaluation ORDER is load-bearing and follows glibc: a NaN x propagates through x*n
without a domain error; n == +inf routes through x*n, which is what makes scalb(0, +inf) an invalid
NaN; n == -inf yields a signed zero except that inf/inf is an invalid NaN; only then does
non-integrality become the domain error. The domain NaN comes from 0.0/0.0 under black_box, which
produces the value and raises the flag in one operation and cannot be folded away.

the identical bug. glibc's *_finite aliases ARE __ieee754_scalb -- the same kernel minus errno -- so
they owed the same non-integral domain error. Routed to the errno-free helper. The gate exercises
only scalb/scalbf/scalbl, so these two are correct-by-construction from a verified helper rather

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
DIAGNOSED, NOT YET FIXED. Releasing to open with a full spec so the next agent starts from the
semantics rather than from the symptom. 535 divergences, TWO distinct defects, three entry points.

WHERE THE CODE ACTUALLY LIVES (not where you would look):
  scalb, scalbf  -> crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs:26840 and :26845
  scalbl         -> crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/math_abi.rs:6237
scalb/scalbf are in unistd_abi.rs, not math_abi.rs.

WHAT THEY ARE NOW — not an approximation of scalb, a different function entirely:
  pub unsafe extern "C" fn scalb(x: f64, exp: f64) -> f64 { x * (2.0f64).powf(exp) }
  pub unsafe extern "C" fn scalbf(x: f32, exp: f32) -> f32 { x * (2.0f32).powf(exp) }
  pub unsafe extern "C" fn scalbl(x: f64, y: f64) -> f64 { scalbn(x, y as i32) }

DEFECT 1 — spurious NaN/FE_INVALID where glibc is exact and silent:
  scalbf(0, 1023): fl bits=ffc00000 inv=true, glibc bits=00000000 inv=false
  scalb(0, 1024):  fl bits=fff8000000000000 inv=true, glibc bits=0 inv=false
Mechanism: 2.0.powf(1024) overflows to +inf, then 0 * inf = NaN and raises FE_INVALID. The powf
formulation is the bug; scalb(0, n) is 0 for every integral n.

DEFECT 2 — missing domain error on a NON-INTEGRAL exponent, the whole point of SVID scalb:
  scalb(0, 2.5):  fl bits=0 inv=false errno=0, glibc bits=fff8000000000000 inv=true errno=33
  same for 0.5, -2.5, 0.9, and across scalbf/scalbl.
errno 33 is EDOM. glibc's __ieee754_scalb returns (fn-fn)/(fn-fn) -- a 0/0 NaN that raises
FE_INVALID naturally -- and w_scalb's wrapper sets EDOM.

TARGET SEMANTICS (glibc __ieee754_scalb + w_scalb), in evaluation order:
  1. x NaN or fn NaN            -> x * fn  (NaN propagates, no domain error)
  2. fn == +inf                 -> x == 0 ? invalid NaN : x * fn
  3. fn == -inf                 -> x infinite ? invalid NaN : signed zero
  4. fn not integral            -> invalid NaN + EDOM        <- defect 2
  5. otherwise                  -> scalbn(x, fn clamped to +/-65000 as i32)   <- defect 1 disappears
     with ERANGE on overflow/underflow per the wrapper.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTE: put ONE shared helper in math_abi.rs as pub(crate) and have unistd_abi.rs call
it, so the three widths cannot drift. set_domain_errno()/set_range_errno() already exist in
math_abi.rs (they wrap set_abi_errno with libc::EDOM/ERANGE). Do NOT relocate the scalb/scalbf
definitions out of unistd_abi.rs -- they carry #[cfg_attr(not(debug_assertions), unsafe(no_mangle))]
and moving them risks a duplicate exported symbol.

DO NOT STUB THESE. scalb is the obsolete SVID spelling but glibc still implements it, and this repo
already has three confirmed false 'obsolete -> ENOSYS' stubs.

The gate is the oracle and already enumerates every case, so iterate against it:
  cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test conformance_diff_scalb -- --nocapture
It compares bits, FE_INVALID and errno for all three widths.

DONE = that gate green with a quoted non-zero passed count.

title: add ffs-core fuzz target for ext4 orphan-recovery mount path
description:
Apply /testing-fuzzing to the ext4 orphan-recovery mount path in `crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs`.

## Target surface
- `OpenFs::from_device(...)` on ext4 images that advertise orphan recovery work
- `maybe_recover_ext4_orphans()` at `crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:2803`
- `collect_ext4_orphan_list_lenient()` at `crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:2943`
- `clear_ext4_orphan_state()` at `crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:3000`

## Why this matters
This path walks attacker-controlled inode chains (`s_last_orphan` + inode `dtime` links), tolerates cycles/out-of-range heads, mutates allocator state, and clears superblock state on success. It is classic fuzz material: bounded traversal, corrupt pointers, unreadable inodes, and stateful mutation in one mount-time recovery path.

## Scope
- Add a dedicated `fuzz` target that feeds adversarial ext4-like images into `OpenFs::from_device` / recovery helpers.
- Seed from existing orphan-recovery unit fixtures and mutate:
  - `s_last_orphan`
  - orphan flag bits
  - inode table pointers
  - `dtime` links (cycles, out-of-range, self-loop, deep chain)
  - extent/inode metadata for linked orphans
- Assert:
  - no panic / no hang
  - traversal remains bounded
  - deterministic outcome for identical input
  - if recovery returns stats, `processed() <= scanned` and counts remain internally consistent
  - clearing orphan state never writes past image bounds

## Acceptance
- New fuzz target registered in `fuzz/Cargo.toml`
- Seed corpus checked in
- Crashers minimized and promoted to regression tests

title: Perf: Per-kernel microbench suite (criterion groups + thresholds)
description:
Add a criterion microbench suite that measures *per-kernel* costs, not just end-to-end decide().

## Why
End-to-end `decide()` can hide regressions. Per-kernel benches let us pin blame when a new kernel or refactor shifts cost.

## Bench Design
- Criterion group per kernel (or per family of kernels).
- Measure:
  - `decide` contributions (hot modules)
  - cadence update costs (epoch modules)
- Report ns/op and p95/p99 where applicable.

## Dependency
- Must reuse the baseline harness from `bd-d5l` and regression thresholds from `bd-242`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A new kernel cannot land without adding/adjusting its microbench.
- Thresholds catch >X% regressions (configurable) in CI.

title: Wire LiveMeasurementPair → P99Delta bridge: run_live_measurement_pair_with_p99_delta
description:
Background: bd-hp41p (commit e25df585) shipped tail_stats::compute_p99_delta(strict, hardened) -> P99Delta and validate_p99_delta_against_budget(...) -> Result<(), P99DeltaError>. bd-juvqm.3 (commit 1ae4d464) and bd-8b70o (commit f9776a42) shipped run_live_measurement_pair which internally calls tail_stats::compute() but DROPS the resulting TailStats — keeping only p99_ns / p999_ns as u64 on each LiveMeasurementRow. To classify a lane-pair's p99 as within/over budget today, callers would have to re-drive both lanes through drive_one_lane all over again to re-derive TailStats with their CI bands — wasteful and racy.

Deliverables:
1. Add `run_live_measurement_pair_with_p99_delta(profile_id, n, seed, environment_fingerprint, source_commit) -> Result<(LiveMeasurementPair, P99Delta), LiveMeasurementError>` to read_mostly_fast_path_prototype. Internally drives both lanes ONCE, computes TailStats for each lane, builds LiveMeasurementRow rows from them, AND returns the P99Delta computed from the two TailStats so the caller can pass it to validate_p99_delta_against_budget without re-running.
2. Add `run_live_measurement_pair_with_p99_delta_and_detected_fingerprint(profile_id, n, seed, source_commit) -> Result<(LiveMeasurementPair, P99Delta), LiveMeasurementError>` mirroring bd-gxgr5's default-fingerprint convenience pattern.
3. New conformance manifest tests/conformance/live_measurement_pair_p99_delta_bridge.v1.json pinning the bridge function paths, the underlying compute_p99_delta path, the underlying validator path, and the policy that the bridge MUST NOT call drive_one_lane more than once per lane.
4. Harness test that:
   - asserts the manifest function paths match the lib surface (compile-time function-pointer checks);
   - drives a small (n>=5_000) pair, asserts the returned P99Delta matches what compute_p99_delta would have produced from the underlying TailStats, AND that the LiveMeasurementPair's p99_ns floor for both lanes is consistent with the P99Delta's p99_delta_ns;
   - asserts validate_p99_delta_against_budget on the returned delta with an absurdly generous budget passes, and with budget=0 returns OverBudget or CiIndistinguishableButOverBudget;
   - asserts the wrapper's environment_fingerprint propagates to both rows.

Acceptance:
- Single drive per lane: no double-driving; bridge cost ≤ 1× the underlying pair cost (asserted by walltime ratio in test).
- LiveMeasurementPair fields are bit-identical to what run_live_measurement_pair would have produced for the same inputs.
- P99Delta is bit-identical to compute_p99_delta(strict_tail_stats, hardened_tail_stats).
- Lib const + manifest enums match — drift fails closed.
- Lib + integration tests green; clippy clean on -D warnings.
- Closure cites a sample (n, seed, p99_delta_ns, amplification_ratio, ci_disjoint) tuple.

title: ffs-types: missing kernel S_IS* predicates over POSIX file-mode constants
description:
Finding (via /porting-to-rust skill, fourth visit, different target):
crates/ffs-types/src/lib.rs declares the 7 POSIX file-mode constants
(S_IFMT + S_IFIFO/CHR/DIR/BLK/REG/LNK/SOCK) but does NOT export the
seven kernel-canonical predicates that are macros in `<sys/stat.h>`:

  #define S_ISREG(m)  (((m) & S_IFMT) == S_IFREG)
  #define S_ISDIR(m)  (((m) & S_IFMT) == S_IFDIR)
  #define S_ISLNK(m)  (((m) & S_IFMT) == S_IFLNK)
  #define S_ISCHR(m)  (((m) & S_IFMT) == S_IFCHR)
  #define S_ISBLK(m)  (((m) & S_IFMT) == S_IFBLK)
  #define S_ISFIFO(m) (((m) & S_IFMT) == S_IFIFO)
  #define S_ISSOCK(m) (((m) & S_IFMT) == S_IFSOCK)

Production callers (ffs-ondisk/src/ext4.rs:2395, ffs-core/src/
lib.rs:9401) inline the `(mode & S_IFMT) == S_IFREG` pattern. This is:

  * Error-prone — each callsite reimplements the mask + compare. A
    typo (e.g., `& S_IFREG` instead of `& S_IFMT`) silently produces
    a wrong predicate that compiles cleanly.
  * Hard to grep — code reviewers can't search for `is_regular_file`
    or `S_ISREG` to audit which paths classify file kinds.
  * Inconsistent with the bd-3ydm6 pattern where `is_reserved_inode`
    is exposed as a named pub const fn.

Acceptance: 7 named pub-const-fn predicates added to
crates/ffs-types/src/lib.rs (one per S_IS* macro), each carrying
a doc comment naming the POSIX header counterpart. Plus a kernel-
conformance unit test pinning each predicate against the 7 mode
constants AND verifying mutually-exclusive classification (every
mode satisfies exactly ONE S_IS* predicate, not two).
notes: Shipped: 7 named pub-const-fn POSIX file-mode predicates in crates/ffs-types/src/lib.rs (is_regular_file / is_directory / is_symlink / is_character_device / is_block_device / is_fifo / is_socket), each carrying a doc comment naming the kernel S_IS* macro counterpart. Kernel-conformance unit test posix_file_mode_predicates_match_kernel_macros pins each predicate against its S_IF* constant, verifies the S_IFMT mask honors permission/sticky bits, and proves mutually-exclusive classification (every mode satisfies EXACTLY ONE predicate, not zero, not two). Pairs with bd-3ydm6 (is_reserved_inode), bd-k81lq (reserved-inode constants), bd-343v3 (file-type constants). Verified via rch exec -- cargo test -p ffs-types --lib posix_file_mode_predicates_match_kernel_macros.

title: D.1: (SUPERSEDED) — folded into parent bd-9dq5
description:
## Goal
Implement the request-tracking infrastructure for async DNS and the gai_error/gai_cancel functions.

## Design

### Request Registry
A global mutex-protected HashMap<usize, AsyncDnsRequest> maps gaicb pointer addresses to request state. The gaicb struct (defined by POSIX) contains:
- ar_name: hostname to resolve
- ar_service: service name/port
- ar_request: hints (addrinfo struct)
- ar_result: output addrinfo list (written on completion)

### gai_error(req: *mut gaicb) -> c_int
1. Look up req address in registry
2. If not found: return EAI_SYSTEM (unknown request)
3. Return state: EAI_INPROGRESS (still running), 0 (completed successfully), EAI_CANCELLED, or the error code from getaddrinfo

### gai_cancel(req: *mut gaicb) -> c_int
1. Look up req in registry
2. If not found: return EAI_NOCANCEL
3. If already completed: return EAI_ALLDONE
4. If in progress: set CANCELLED flag, return EAI_CANCELLED (or EAI_NOTCANCELED if thread already started resolution)

### State Constants
- EAI_INPROGRESS = -100 (glibc value)
- EAI_CANCELLED = -101
- EAI_ALLDONE = -103
- EAI_NOTCANCELED = -102

## Implementation
File: crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs (near existing gai_* functions)
- Add AsyncDnsRequest struct
- Add static ASYNC_DNS_REGISTRY: LazyLock<Mutex<HashMap<usize, AsyncDnsRequest>>>
- Replace gai_error body
- Replace gai_cancel body

## Testing
- gai_error on unknown request returns EAI_SYSTEM
- gai_cancel on unknown request returns EAI_NOCANCEL
- Register a fake completed request, gai_error returns 0
- Register a fake in-progress request, gai_cancel returns EAI_CANCELLED

## Acceptance Criteria
State machine is correct. Registry tracks requests. Tests pass.
close_reason: Superseded: Track D redesigned as synchronous-only. No request registry or futex wait needed. All logic fits in parent bd-9dq5.

title: External journal: wire replay through external device ByteDevice
description:
Wire the external journal replay path:
1. Open the external journal image as a FileByteDevice.
2. Read journal blocks from the external device.
3. Feed them to replay_jbd2_segments (existing function) with the DATA device as the write target.
4. After successful replay, clear needs_recovery on the data device.

The key insight: journal blocks are READ from the external device, but replayed blocks are WRITTEN to the data device. The existing replay infrastructure accepts a BlockDevice for writes — just pass the data device's block adapter.

DEPENDS ON: Journal segment computation (bd-vdk6).

ACCEPTANCE: A test with a synthetic data FS + dirty external journal verifies that replay writes land on the data device and needs_recovery is cleared.
close_reason: Already implemented by concurrent agent: ExternalJournalReplayAdapter reads journal blocks from external device, writes replayed blocks to data device. UUID/block-size validation, JBD2 replay, superblock re-read after replay. Test open_fs_replays_external_journal_transaction passes.

title: [f128-restore T1] primitives + shared tables (scalbn/cbrt/atan/atan2/asin/acos_f128) — unblocks every other tranche
description:
Pre-deletion anchors in math_abi_pre.rs: scalbn_f128 8558, cbrt_f128 8601, atan_f128 8838, atan2_f128 8902, asin_f128 8996, acos_f128 9152, neval_f128 10097, deval_f128 10107. Also restore add_exp_field_f128 and the f128 sqrt primitive.

This tranche owns the SHARED static tables (LOGB_P/Q/R/S, LOG_TBL_F128, EXPL_TABLE, T_EXPL_ARG1/2, T_EXPL_RES1/2, the polynomial coefficient blocks). Every other tranche references them, so this one lands first and the rest depend on it.

Gates relit here: conformance_diff_f128_atan, _atan2, _asin, _acos, _cbrt, _atanpi.

RESTORE RECIPE (identical for every tranche; parent bd-ocwiw9 has the root cause).

The deleted source is intact in git. Get the pre-deletion file once:

  git show 517d0a233^:crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/math_abi.rs > /tmp/math_abi_pre.rs

DIRECTION: HEAD's math_abi.rs is the BASE. Bring the f128 helpers and bodies back INTO it. Do NOT
revert 517d0a233 - that commit also added real work (C99 Annex G overflow handling in c_exp,
zero-imaginary special-casing, and errno paths for logb/fdim/nextafter/lround on f64/f32) which must
survive. Only one other commit has touched the file since (aff100890, -38 duplicate fenv exports),
so there is nothing else to collide with.

PER TRANCHE:
 1. Copy the named private helpers verbatim from the pre-deletion file, plus any static table they
    reference (EXPL_TABLE, LOG_TBL_F128, T_EXPL_ARG1/2, T_EXPL_RES1/2, LOGB_P/Q/R/S, ...). The
    tables are the reason a family cannot be restored alone - resolve the closure before editing.
 2. Change the tranche's exported entry points back from the f64 stub to the f128 signature and
    body. At HEAD they read e.g.
        pub unsafe extern "C" fn asinhf128(x: f64) -> f64 { unsafe { asinh(x) } }
    and must return to
        pub unsafe extern "C" fn asinhf128(x: f128) -> f128 { ... }
 3. Relight the tranche's conformance_diff_f128_* gates. They already exist and are already written
    against the f128 signature - that is WHY they do not compile today. Do not rewrite a gate to
    match the stub.
 4. Run them. A gate that now compiles and FAILS is a result, not a setback: report the divergence
    measured against live glibc and say whether fl or the assertion is wrong (bd-86hcwh precedent -
    that ratio came out 5 fl-defects to 4 stale assertions).

DONE for a tranche = its helpers restored, its entry points f128 again, its gates compiling AND
running, with each gate's outcome stated. Leaving a gate red and silent is what created this.

MANDATORY CHECK before closing any tranche: confirm no OTHER f128 entry point still carries an f64
signature within the families you claimed, with
  grep -nE 'fn [a-z0-9_]+f128\(.*f64' crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/math_abi.rs
The count must fall by exactly the number you restored; at HEAD today it is 130.

title: tzset leaves tzname[0]=NULL (glibc always sets it non-NULL); populate UTC timezone globals
close_reason:
GATED (implementation was already present, ungated). Commit 147b4cd5f.

The blocker comment is accurate about the SOURCE: crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/time_abi.rs::tzset publishes tzname/__tzname[0..1] = 'UTC', timezone/__timezone = 0, daylight/__daylight = 0, and cites bd-vxpc1y. Fix 8daab4a96 is intact at HEAD (unlike bd-c7cs3h earlier this session, where the analogous claim was false and the fix had been silently deleted).

What was missing is any arm that could FAIL on the original bug. Verified with rg over crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/: 'tzset' appears in a dozen files purely as SETUP before a strftime/mktime/getdate comparison, and 'tzname' appears exactly once — as part of the NAME of conformance_diff_strptime_tzname.rs::strptime_tzname_matches_glibc, which never reads the global. Nothing asserted the globals. Fourth bead this session with that shape.

GATE: crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/conformance_diff_tzset_globals.rs (new file; no tzset gate existed).
- tzset_publishes_utc_globals_like_glibc: byte-for-byte vs LIVE glibc under TZ=UTC on the 4-tuple (tzname[0], tzname[1], timezone, daylight). Also asserts what the ORACLE produced ('UTC', 0, 0) — if BOTH impls stopped publishing anything meaningful, equality alone would still pass. glibc reached by dlsym with assert_ne against fl's own tzset address, so a release test build cannot compare fl to itself.
- tzset_always_leaves_tzname_zero_a_readable_string: the property the bead is actually about, asserted independently of TZ over {UTC, America/New_York, empty, unset} — after tzset(), tzname[0] must be dereferenceable and non-empty. Deliberately includes a zone fl does not implement: the requirement is a VALID STRING, not the right zone, so an unsupported zone must still not yield NULL.
- tzset_keeps_the_underscored_aliases_in_step: fl publishes tzname/timezone/daylight and the __-prefixed aliases as SEPARATE statics (glibc_internal_abi.rs:5035-5041), not as aliases of one another, so a fix touching only the public set would leave __tzname[0] NULL — the same segfault, one symbol over. Nothing else covered this.

SCOPE, stated deliberately: this gate does NOT compare the two implementations under an arbitrary TZ. fl is UTC-only by design, so glibc reports EST for America/New_York where fl reports UTC; that divergence is a known design limitation, not this bead, and asserting it here would make the gate fail for a reason it does not own (the lesson from bd-0qltjh earlier this session, where a NULL-filename formatting defect made the error_one_per_line arms fail for the wrong reason).

EVIDENCE (rch remote, source commit 147b4cd5f):
  cargo test -j2 --no-fail-fast -p frankenlibc-abi --test conformance_diff_tzset_globals
    tzset_publishes_utc_globals_like_glibc ............. ok
    tzset_always_leaves_tzname_zero_a_readable_string ... ok
    tzset_keeps_the_underscored_aliases_in_step ........ ok
    test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed.
  cargo clippy -j2 -p frankenlibc-abi --test conformance_diff_tzset_globals -- -D warnings -> zero findings.
  ubs on the new file: 0 critical.

SENSITIVITY — DEDUCTIVE, NOT MEASURED, and flagged as such: I did not run the worktree red-run used for bd-c7cs3h. The pre-fix state is not a subtle behaviour but the STATIC INITIALIZER itself — glibc_internal_abi.rs:5039-5041 declare tzname/__tzname as [null_mut(), null_mut()] — and the gate's cstr() helper asserts non-NULL before doing anything else, so with tzset()'s body removed all three arms panic on the first field. If a reviewer wants it measured, the recipe is in the bd-c7cs3h closure.

BUILD NOTE for anyone touching these globals from a test: Rust 2024 rejects a shared reference to a mutable static, and assert_eq! takes references, so the scalar comparisons read through &raw const into locals first. Array indexing of the tzname statics was fine; only the timezone/daylight scalars needed it.

Unrelated agent changes were not reverted.

title: [bug][netdb] getnetbyaddr and getnetbyaddr_r ignored the address-family argument
description:
conformance_diff_getnetbyaddr_type was RED at clean HEAD, found while following up the netdb alias
work (bd-ghlqqo).

DEFECT. Both entry points took the address family as an ignored parameter, literally named _type,
and matched on n_net alone. glibc's files backend matches when
    n_net == net AND (type == AF_UNSPEC || n_addrtype == type)
and fl stamps every /etc/networks entry with n_addrtype = AF_INET, so a query for any other family
must find nothing. fl answered link-local for AF_INET6 and for a bogus type 99 where glibc returns
NULL.

I GOT THE RULE WRONG ON THE FIRST ATTEMPT, and the gate caught it. I wrote the guard from the gate's
own header comment, which asserted that a query with 'AF_INET6, an arbitrary integer, 0' finds
nothing. That is wrong about 0: AF_UNSPEC is a WILDCARD. Live glibc returns link-local for
getnetbyaddr(0xa9fe0000, 0), so rejecting AF_UNSPEC swapped one divergence for another. The header
has been corrected in the same change, since a stale comment that reads like a spec is how the next
person makes the same mistake.

I also nearly missed it: my first grep of the failure output filtered for the _r arm and hid the
non-_r mismatch at type=0. Both arms were failing identically. Grep the whole mismatch list, not the
part you expect.

COVERAGE GAP THIS EXPOSED. getnetbyaddr_r had no live coverage at all. The pre-existing tests in
unistd_abi_test that touch it are ALL #[ignore]d for bd-q3snos:
  cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test unistd_abi_test -- getnetby getnetent
  -> test result: ok. 0 passed; 0 failed; 6 IGNORED; 0 measured; 625 filtered out
A zero-passed result is not evidence. The gate was therefore extended with a reentrant arm driving
getnetbyaddr_r over the same (net, type) matrix, so the _r fix is proven rather than assumed.

  cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test conformance_diff_getnetbyaddr_type
  before -> FAILED (AF_INET6 and type=99 matched when glibc returns NULL)
  after  -> test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
close_reason:
FIXED. Commit 7d8ecf956. Gate conformance_diff_getnetbyaddr_type: FAILED -> 'test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out'.

Correct rule implemented in BOTH entry points: match when n_net == net AND (type == AF_UNSPEC ||
n_addrtype == type). Since fl stamps every /etc/networks entry AF_INET, that means AF_INET and
AF_UNSPEC match and nothing else does.

THE PART WORTH KEEPING: I got it wrong on the first attempt by trusting a COMMENT over a
MEASUREMENT. The gate's header asserted that a query with type 0 finds nothing; I wrote the guard
from that and it was wrong, because 0 is AF_UNSPEC and glibc treats it as a wildcard. The gate then
failed at type=0 on both arms and I corrected the rule against live glibc. The stale header is
corrected in the same commit, since a wrong comment that reads like a spec reproduces the bug in
whoever reads it next.

I also nearly shipped a wrong conclusion by grepping the failure output for the arm I had just
added, which hid an identical non-_r mismatch. Read the whole mismatch list.

COVERAGE GAP CLOSED. getnetbyaddr_r had NO live coverage at all -- every pre-existing test touching
it is #[ignore]d under bd-q3snos:
  cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test unistd_abi_test -- getnetby getnetent
  -> test result: ok. 0 passed; 0 failed; 6 IGNORED; 0 measured; 625 filtered out
That is a zero-passed run, which is not evidence of anything, so the identical bug in the reentrant
path could have sat there indefinitely. The gate now drives getnetbyaddr_r over the same (net, type)
matrix, so both fixes are proven rather than one inferred from the other.

NO REGRESSION: conformance_diff_getnetent 1 passed; conformance_diff_network_number 1 passed;
conformance_diff_netdb_iter_aliases 1 passed. fmt clean on both files.

title: Refine workload corpus with user-risk and proof-consumer coverage matrix
description:
Supplemental refinement for bd-rchk0.5.7.1. The workload corpus needs to be more than a bag of scenarios: each entry should explain what user risk it represents, which proof systems consume it, and what evidence a future closeout must produce. This prevents realistic workloads from becoming disconnected fixtures that do not support release claims.

Scope: define a coverage matrix for corpus entries that maps scenario id to README/runtime claim, filesystem flavor, operation class, user-risk category, required host capability, proof consumers, unit-test obligations, E2E/fuzz/soak obligations, expected logs, expected artifacts, and explicit non-applicability rationale.

Required proof before close:
1. Unit/schema tests reject corpus rows missing stable id, user-risk category, filesystem scope, capability tag, proof-consumer list, required log fields, required artifact fields, and explicit unsupported/non-goal rationale where applicable.
2. Unit tests cover duplicate scenario ids, stale proof-consumer names, orphaned high-risk categories, invalid capability tags, and rows that claim user-visible coverage without an E2E or long-campaign proof lane.
3. E2E/script smoke consumes representative rows across at least core parser, mounted-path, repair, and long-campaign consumers or emits structured host skips for unavailable lanes.
4. Logs include matrix version, row ids, selected scenarios, consumer names, capability decisions, generated artifact paths, pass/fail/skip/error state, and reproduction command.
5. Release gates and proof bundles can summarize corpus coverage by user risk and fail closed when a P1/P2 risk row has no active proof consumer.
close_reason: Completed: added workload corpus coverage matrix and validation gates

Implemented additional closure work for bd-w2c3.5.3 (admission/retirement/value-proof gate):

1) Retirement lockout hardening
- `scripts/runtime_math_admission_gate.py`
  - Added explicit error on RETIRE modules present in `production_modules` (`retired_module_not_in_production_manifest`).
  - Added gate-invariant checks for feature sets:
    - `production_feature_must_be_default`
    - `research_feature_must_be_optional`

2) Manifest integrity checks
- `scripts/runtime_math_admission_gate.py`
  - Added deterministic SHA-256 + size fingerprinting for consumed artifacts:
    - governance, manifest, ablation report, linkage, value proof, harness Cargo manifest.
  - Added `artifact_integrity` section to report and structured log details.

3) Tooling contract enforcement (`/dp/asupersync` + `/dp/frankentui` requirement)
- `scripts/runtime_math_admission_gate.py`
  - Added `tooling_contract` analysis of `crates/frankenlibc-harness/Cargo.toml`.
  - New hard-fail policies:
    - asupersync dependency + feature + default-enable
    - frankentui feature + dependency set completeness

4) Report/log/checker/test extensions
- `scripts/check_runtime_math_admission.sh`
  - Now requires/validates `artifact_integrity` and `tooling_contract` fields.
  - Structured log check now requires decision path to include integrity/tooling stages.
- `crates/frankenlibc-harness/tests/runtime_math_admission_gate_test.rs`
  - Added assertions for tooling contract and integrity hashes.
  - Added structured-log decision-path assertion for integrity/tooling stages.

Validation evidence:
- `bash scripts/check_runtime_math_admission.sh` => PASS
  - policies_enforced: 19
  - status: pass
  - blocked: 0
- Attempted `cargo test -p frankenlibc-harness --test runtime_math_admission_gate_test -- --nocapture`
  - blocked by unrelated pre-existing compile error in another file:
    - `crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/inet_abi.rs:576`
    - `error[E0425]: cannot find function libc_gethostbyaddr_r in this scope`

Agent coordination note:
- MCP Agent Mail transport is currently unavailable (`http://127.0.0.1:8765/api` connection failure), so coordination update is logged here in bead comments as fallback.
