title: ffs-ondisk: DX_HASH_LEGACY through SIPHASH constants + EXT4_HTREE_EOF_32BIT lack kernel-conformance pin
description:
Finding (via /testing-conformance-harnesses skill, NEW target): crates/ffs-ondisk/src/ext4.rs:4838-4845 declares 7 DX hash version constants and EXT4_HTREE_EOF_32BIT used by every htree directory lookup. These are file-private (no pub), not exposed for downstream consumers, and have NO conformance pin to canonical kernel values from fs/ext4/ext4.h:

  DX_HASH_LEGACY               = 0     (#define DX_HASH_LEGACY 0)
  DX_HASH_HALF_MD4             = 1     (#define DX_HASH_HALF_MD4 1)
  DX_HASH_TEA                  = 2     (#define DX_HASH_TEA 2)
  DX_HASH_LEGACY_UNSIGNED      = 3     (DX_HASH_LEGACY | DX_HASH_UNSIGNED_BIT)
  DX_HASH_HALF_MD4_UNSIGNED    = 4
  DX_HASH_TEA_UNSIGNED         = 5
  DX_HASH_SIPHASH              = 6     (kernel SipHash-2-4 variant)
  EXT4_HTREE_EOF_32BIT         = 0x7FFFFFFF  (= (1<<31) - 1, htree EOF sentinel)

A regression that swapped DX_HASH_TEA (2) and DX_HASH_HALF_MD4 (1) would silently mis-classify every htree directory and route lookups through the wrong hash function — invisible until end users notice broken lookups.

Critical: the unsigned variants are derived by OR'ing the signed variant with bit 2 (DX_HASH_UNSIGNED_BIT in some kernel headers). The structural invariant (unsigned == signed | 2) prevents drift between the two variants.

Acceptance: ext4_dx_hash_version_constants_match_kernel_header conformance test in crates/ffs-ondisk/src/ext4.rs that pins all 7 hash version values + EXT4_HTREE_EOF_32BIT, plus the structural invariant that unsigned variants are signed OR'd with 2. Pairs with bd-bevt2 (40 feature flags), bd-jbilz (magic + state flags), bd-glkri (BG flags), bd-tyeic (27 inode flags).

title: Investigate and fix ext4 bitmap CRC32C mismatch against real mkfs.ext4 images
description:
PROBLEM: The kernel_reference integration test ext4_bitmap_free_space_matches_kernel fails because our computed block bitmap checksum (via verify_block_bitmap_checksum -> block_bitmap_checksum_value -> ext4_bitmap_checksum) does not match the checksum stored by mkfs.ext4 1.47.2 on real images.

EVIDENCE: On a fresh 8MB ext4 image (mkfs.ext4 -L test -b 4096 -q -O ^has_journal), seed=0xba6605a8, our code computes 0xcd45611c but the stored checksum is 0xb8339b40. The ext4_chksum bridge function (!crc32c_append(!raw, data)) is verified correct for known test vectors (b'hello' produces the expected result). The GDT field offsets (bg_block_bitmap_csum_lo at 0x18, bg_block_bitmap_csum_hi at 0x38) match the kernel struct. The csum_seed derivation (from s_checksum_seed when CSUM_SEED is set) is verified correct.

POSSIBLE ROOT CAUSES:
(a) The crc32c crate 0.6.8 may have a hardware-acceleration edge case on this CPU (the test passes for small inputs but may diverge on 4096-byte inputs).
(b) There may be a subtle difference in how the kernel chains CRC32C for bitmap checksums vs how we do it (e.g., the kernel might zero some bits in the bitmap before checksumming, or exclude the last N bytes).
(c) The group descriptor checksum field offset may differ between mkfs.ext4 versions.
(d) There's a SECOND bitmap checksum function (compute_bitmap_checksum at line 1743) that uses csum_seed^group (XOR) instead of chaining — this function is wrong but verify_block_bitmap_checksum doesn't use it. However, it may have been copy-pasted from or to somewhere unexpected.

INVESTIGATION PLAN:
1. Add a test that creates a fresh ext4 image with mkfs.ext4, reads the raw bitmap bytes, and computes our CRC step-by-step, printing intermediate values.
2. Cross-validate by computing the same CRC using a second Rust CRC32C implementation (e.g., crc32c-hw or manual software CRC).
3. If the crate is correct, hexdump the raw GDT bytes and verify our parser reads the stored checksum from the right offset.
4. Check if mkfs.ext4 zeroes any bitmap bits before checksumming (e.g., unused tail bits beyond blocks_per_group).
5. Check the kernel source for ext4_block_bitmap_csum_set() to see if it modifies the bitmap before checksumming.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- ext4_bitmap_free_space_matches_kernel test passes on a fresh mkfs.ext4 image.
- The root cause is documented in a code comment.
- If the crc32c crate has a bug, switch to an alternative or add a workaround.
- The wrong compute_bitmap_checksum function (XOR-based) is either removed or clearly marked as deprecated.
close_reason: Root cause: (1) group_number was chained into bitmap CRC but kernel doesn't do this, (2) checksum length was full block instead of clusters/inodes_per_group/8. Fixed in commits 20d65f4 and 7f4d6eb. Kernel reference test now passes.

title: PORT: expand_number (FreeBSD libutil decimal-fraction size parser)
description: FreeBSD expand_number(buf, *num_out) parses a C string of optional whitespace + non-negative decimal (with optional fractional part) + optional one-character size suffix into a uint64_t. Companion to NetBSD dehumanize_number (just shipped) but: (1) writes uint64_t not int64_t — no negative numbers; (2) supports decimal fractions via integer scaling (2.5K = 2560 bytes). Suffix multipliers: same k/K=1024 m/M=1024^2 g/G=1024^3 t/T=1024^4 p/P=1024^5 e/E=1024^6 (no b/B in FreeBSD spec). Returns 0 on success, -1 with errno=EINVAL on malformed input, errno=ERANGE on overflow. Used by FreeBSD dd-conv, mkfile, ifconfig, ftpd. Currently missing from frankenlibc-abi. Ship: pure-safe core::stdlib::expand_number::parse returning Result<u64, ExpandError> with Invalid/Overflow variants, integer-arithmetic decimal handling (so 1.5K = 1024 + (5*1024/10) = 1536) + thin abi shim that maps the error categories to errno + writes the value through the caller pointer.

title: Investigate Python startup perf regression in LD_PRELOAD smoke suite (51/7/6)
description:
## Problem
LD_PRELOAD smoke suite regressed from 58/0/6 to 51/7/6. All 7 failures are Python-related with failure_signature=startup_perf_regression. Correctness is fine (parity_pass=true) — only startup latency exceeds the perf gate threshold.

## Failing Cases
- strict: python3_print, stress_python_{1..5}
- hardened: stress_python_5

## Probable Cause
Recent changes to signal handling and malloc that added overhead:
1. signal_abi.rs: Signal trampoline installation, SA_RESTORER marshalling, deferred delivery critical sections
2. malloc_abi.rs: Signal critical section entry/exit around every malloc/calloc/free/realloc call
3. host_resolve.rs: Streaming /proc/self/maps parser changes

Python startup is particularly sensitive because it calls sigaction dozens of times during interpreter init, and does heavy allocation.

## Investigation Steps
1. Profile Python startup under LD_PRELOAD to identify the hotspot
2. Check if the malloc signal critical section is the bottleneck (atomic ops on every alloc)
3. Check if sigaction trampoline installation overhead is significant
4. Consider: make signal critical sections opt-in (only when FRANKENLIBC_MODE=hardened)

## Acceptance Criteria
Smoke suite returns to 58/0/6 (or 57/0/7 with the new skipped binary). Python startup perf within threshold.
close_reason: Smoke gate back to 58/0/6; strict+hardened Python cases green

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Investigation finding: strace -c output is garbled under LD_PRELOAD because our printf engine does NOT support POSIX positional format specifiers (%n$s, %n$d). strace uses these extensively for column-aligned output. This is a separate correctness bug from the perf regression. The perf regression itself appears to be from the 275ms Python startup (vs 15ms native) — likely caused by signal trampoline overhead per sigaction call (67 calls) and /proc/self/maps reads (6 reads). The positional printf bug should be a separate bead.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Root cause analysis: The 275ms Python startup (vs 15ms native) is primarily from host symbol resolution overhead during early bootstrap, not from the signal trampoline per se. Each of the 67 sigaction calls triggers runtime_policy::decide() + kernel struct marshalling + trampoline installation, but the main cost is likely the resolve_host_symbol_raw calls reading /proc/self/maps (6 reads confirmed via strace). The signal trampoline itself is cheap after first install. Possible fixes: (1) cache /proc/self/maps content, (2) lazy-resolve symbols on first actual use not on every sigaction, (3) batch symbol resolution at startup. This is an optimization task, not a correctness bug.

Baseline avg ~16.99 ms, strict avg ~61.11 ms, down from the previous ~290.72 ms on the pre-patch release artifact. title: [bug][wordexp] two RED differential gates at HEAD: conformance_diff_wordexp_operators (${FOO:?} drops the value) and conformance_diff_wordexp_tilde (5 cases)
description:
Two RED gates in the wordexp family, found while closing bd-yb9f9r (arithmetic expansion) and
deliberately NOT folded into it. Both reproduce byte-identically at CLEAN HEAD with my tree
excluded, so neither is caused by that change:
  rch exec --base HEAD --clean-overlay --no-overlay -- \
    cargo test -j 2 -p frankenlibc-abi --test <target>

1. conformance_diff_wordexp_operators — FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed
     wordexp("${FOO:?}") diverged: fl=(0, []) glibc=(0, ["bar"])
   With FOO set to "bar", glibc's `${FOO:?}` expands to the VALUE; fl returns success with ZERO
   words. `:?` means "use the value, but error if unset/null" — fl appears to treat it as
   produce-nothing-on-success. Note fl returns rc=0, so it is not the error path being taken; the
   value is simply being dropped. Check the `:?` arm in the braced-parameter expander
   (crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs expand_braced_param / the core
   frankenlibc_core::stdlib::wordexp::expand_braced_param) against the `:-` and `:=` arms, which
   pass. The unset/null half of the contract (WRDE_BADVAL, and the message after `?`) should be
   measured too, not just the set case the gate happens to exercise.

2. conformance_diff_wordexp_tilde — FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed
     "wordexp tilde diverged from glibc (5 cases)"
   The assertion aggregates, so the five cases are in the panic body; run it with --nocapture to
   list them before touching anything. Likely `~user` forms resolving against the passwd backend
   (compare with bd-79p18u's hosts-backend work: fl honours override env vars that glibc does not).

WHY THESE ARE WORTH A BEAD RATHER THAN A NOTE: both are differential gates against live glibc that
are currently RED, which means the wordexp family's failure set has a floor above zero. Every
"compare the failure SET against clean HEAD" check in this repo — the method used to separate my
breakage from pre-existing breakage all session — gets noisier while they sit there, and a sixth
tilde case appearing would be invisible against a message that only says "5 cases".

DONE = each target green with a quoted non-zero passed count, each fix stating which field diverged
and against which measured glibc values, and each shown RED at clean HEAD beforehand (already
recorded above) so the change is demonstrably load-bearing. Do NOT narrow either gate's case list to
make it pass.
close_reason:
FIXED — both gates green, plus a third defect the work uncovered. Source commit 3b5f5b1ee.
The whole wordexp family now has a ZERO failure floor for the first time.

DEFECT 1 — `~user` was never implemented. crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs expand_tilde
handled `~` (HOME) and then fell out with the comment "~user → lookup (simplified: just return
as-is if we can't resolve)", so `~root` stayed literal. All five reported tilde cases were the same
missing lookup:
    "~root"     glibc ["/root"]     fl ["~root"]
    "~root/sub" glibc ["/root/sub"] fl ["~root/sub"]
    "~root/a/b" glibc ["/root/a/b"] fl ["~root/a/b"]
    "~daemon"   glibc ["/usr/sbin"] fl ["~daemon"]
    "~bin"      glibc ["/bin"]      fl ["~bin"]
Now resolved through frankenlibc_core::pwd::lookup_by_name over /etc/passwd. Measured contract,
including the cases that must NOT expand:
    ~nosuchuser -> ~nosuchuser (literal, rc=0)   ~nosuchuser/sub -> literal
    a~root -> a~root  (tilde only at word start)  "~root" and '~root' -> literal
The unknown-user fallback was already correct; only the lookup was missing, so the fix is additive.

DEFECT 2 — `${VAR:?}` DROPPED THE VALUE ON THE SUCCESS PATH, which is what made this worth fixing
rather than a corner case. The `?` arm was never implemented and fell through to
`plain(lookup_env(content), content)`, where `content` is the WHOLE braced text including the
operator. So `${FOO:?}` looked up an environment variable literally named "FOO:?", found nothing,
and expanded to zero words — with FOO=bar set, glibc gives ["bar"] and fl gave []. A caller using
`${VAR:?}` as "use the value, and complain if it is missing" got NOTHING even when the value was
present.
Measured contract, now implemented (FOO=bar, EMPTY="", UNSET unset):
    ${FOO:?}  ${FOO?}  ${FOO:?msg}   -> ["bar"]
    ${EMPTY:?}                       -> [] + stderr "EMPTY: parameter null or not set"
    ${EMPTY?}                        -> []    (set-but-null is NOT an error without `:`)
    ${UNSET:?}  ${UNSET?}            -> [] + stderr "UNSET: parameter null or not set"
    ${UNSET:?custom message}         -> [] + stderr "UNSET: custom message"
Note rc=0 in every one of those: wordexp reports this condition by DIAGNOSTIC plus an empty
expansion, not by an error code — so it is carried as a typed ExpandError::NullOrUnset that the abi
renders to stderr and turns into an empty expansion, rather than as a failure.

DEFECT 3 — FOUND WHILE FIXING 2, not in the bead. The same literal-lookup fallthrough silently
ACCEPTED bash-only forms: `${FOO:1}` (substring) returned rc=0 with zero words where glibc returns
WRDE_SYNTAX(5). Only `-`, `=`, `+`, `?` (each optionally preceded by `:`) are POSIX operators — `#`
and `%` are handled earlier in the function — so everything else is now
ExpandError::BadSubstitution -> WRDE_SYNTAX. This surfaced only because fixing `?` moved the gate
past its first failure, which is the argument for fixing the earliest failure and re-running rather
than reading the whole list up front.

GATES — the two named by this bead, and every neighbour, all run and all green:
  conformance_diff_wordexp_operators  ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out   (was RED)
  conformance_diff_wordexp_tilde      ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out   (was RED)
  conformance_diff_wordexp            ok. 2 passed; 0 failed
  conformance_diff_wordexp_arith      ok. 2 passed; 0 failed
  wordexp_differential_fuzz           ok. 1 passed; 0 failed
  wordexp_differential_probe          ok. 1 passed; 0 failed
  frankenlibc-core --lib wordexp      ok. 20 passed; 0 failed
Both target REDs were confirmed at clean HEAD when this bead was filed
(rch exec --base HEAD --clean-overlay --no-overlay), so the change is demonstrably load-bearing.

REGRESSION CHECK: unistd_abi_test 535 passed; 5 failed; 91 ignored — failure SET byte-identical to
the clean-HEAD baseline (abi_argp_parse_version x2, cuserid, kexec_load, mount_setattr), none
wordexp-related. Notably `cuserid_resolves_current_uid_from_passwd_backend` is in that pre-existing
set and stayed exactly as it was, so the new passwd read in expand_tilde did not disturb it.
fmt clean.

KNOWN GAP, STATED: glibc also writes the `?` diagnostic to stderr and fl now does too, but I did not
verify the two byte streams match beyond the message text measured above — the gates compare
(rc, words) only. If exact stderr parity matters, that needs its own probe.

title: Succinct structures for free-space bitmaps (Graveyard Entry 7.1)
description:
# Succinct structures for free-space bitmaps (Graveyard Entry 7.1)

## GOAL
Replace traditional free-space bitmaps with succinct data structures (rank/select bitmaps) that support O(1) rank and select queries while using near-optimal space.

## BACKGROUND
From Alien CS Graveyard 7.1: Succinct bitmaps (Jacobson 1989, Clark 1996) store bitmaps in n + o(n) bits while supporting:
- rank(i): count set bits in positions [0, i) — O(1)
- select(k): find position of k-th set bit — O(1)

For free-space bitmaps, this enables:
- O(1) "how many free blocks in range?" (rank)
- O(1) "find k-th free block" (select) — replaces linear scan for allocation

## DESIGN
- Two-level rank structure: superblocks (every 2^16 bits) + blocks (every 2^9 bits)
- Select via rank binary search or Vigna's select structure
- Space overhead: ~6.25% over raw bitmap (vs 0% for plain bitmap, but queries are O(n))
- Integration: replace ffs-ext4 block bitmap and inode bitmap

## APPLICABILITY
- Optimization for large filesystems where bitmap scans are expensive
- Most impactful when block groups are large or filesystem is >90% full
- Could also accelerate mballoc buddy allocator queries

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] Succinct bitmap with O(1) rank and select
- [ ] Space overhead < 10% over raw bitmap
- [ ] Benchmark: allocation scan time vs plain bitmap
- [ ] Drop-in replacement for block/inode bitmaps
acceptance_criteria: Succinct bitmap with O(1) rank and select operations. Space overhead below 10% over raw bitmap. Two-level rank structure: superblocks (every 2^16 bits) plus blocks (every 2^9 bits). Drop-in replacement for block and inode bitmaps via BlockBitmap trait. Benchmark: allocation scan time vs plain bitmap at 50%, 80%, 95% fullness. Benchmark: rank/select latency vs linear scan. Unit tests: rank correctness for all-zeros, all-ones, random patterns. Unit tests: select correctness for sparse and dense bitmaps. Unit tests: round-trip serialization/deserialization. Property test: rank(select(k)) == k for all valid k.

title: [MEDIUM] fuzz: sched-family differential harness
description:
[MEDIUM] fuzz: add sched-family differential harness

Add a differential fuzz target for the scheduler-related wrappers that have accumulated many hand-written errno-precedence tests but still expose a wide combinatorial input surface.

Recommended syscall set:
- `sched_getaffinity` (`crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs:3598`)
- `sched_setaffinity` (`crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs:3614`)
- `sched_setscheduler` (`crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs:4430`)
- `sched_getparam` (`crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs:4445`)
- `sched_setparam` (`crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs:4456`)

Fuzz shape:
- mutate pid classes (self, -1, huge nonexistent, recycled child)
- mutate cpusetsize, scheduler policy, param pointers, and priority contents
- compare exact errno/return-value parity against host libc
- keep a small process sandbox so invalid pid and privilege-dependent paths stay reproducible

Why now:
- the recent backlog burn-down added many one-off parity tests here, which is a strong corpus seed for a structure-aware differential fuzzer.
notes:
Closed by cc-libc (JSONL edit — br CLI lookup bug continues).

Delivered crates/frankenlibc-fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_sched.rs with 11 op variants across the sched-family surface: sched_getscheduler, sched_setscheduler (SCHED_OTHER and fuzz-policy variants), sched_getparam, sched_setparam, sched_getaffinity, sched_setaffinity, sched_get_priority_min, sched_get_priority_max, sched_rr_get_interval, sched_yield.

Two oracles:
1. Return-code contract: every call must return its documented success value or -1.
2. Direct-syscall differential for the read-only getters: raw libc::syscall(SYS_*) is ground truth (it bypasses both our ABI and libc's wrapper). Priorities, scheduler policy, affinity mask, and timespec fields are compared byte-for-byte after both succeed. Used instead of extern "C" differential because both our ABI and libc export the same `sched_*` symbol names — naive extern binds to only one impl.

Safety: all pids come from a bounded set {0 (self), huge-nonexistent, -1, own pid}. The only set_scheduler call that can succeed without CAP_SYS_NICE is SCHED_OTHER with priority 0; every other policy/priority is expected to fail EPERM — the invariant is 'no crash, rc in contract'. A process-wide SCHED_LOCK serializes iterations.

Wired as `fuzz_sched` bin in crates/frankenlibc-fuzz/Cargo.toml.

Validation: `cargo build --bin fuzz_sched` clean (0.40s incremental); `cargo clippy --bin fuzz_sched --no-deps -- -D warnings` clean.
close_reason: done

title: wordexp: no arithmetic expansion $((...)) + WRDE_NOCMD misclassifies $(( as command substitution (over-rejects)
design: Root cause: scan_command_substitution (unistd_abi.rs ~6980/7016) treats $( as command sub in BOTH unquoted and double-quote branches without checking for a second '(', so $((1+2)) sets has_command_substitution=true. Divergences from glibc: (1) fl has NO arithmetic-expansion support (grep arithmetic/$(( = empty in unistd_abi + core/stdlib/wordexp.rs); (2) under WRDE_NOCMD glibc ALLOWS arithmetic (rejects only command sub $(...) + backticks) but fl returns WRDE_CMDSUB for $((...)). Fix: implement $((expr)) integer arithmetic per POSIX AND make the WRDE_NOCMD scan distinguish $(( (arithmetic, allowed) from $( (command sub, rejected). A classification-only partial fix is unsafe — without arithmetic expansion fl would leave $((...)) unexpanded, a different divergence. Found via WRDE_NOCMD security-control audit.
close_reason:
FIXED, both halves. Source commit 8140fc7a9.

THE BEAD UNDERSTATED THE DEFECT. It says fl returns WRDE_CMDSUB for arithmetic "under WRDE_NOCMD".
Measured at clean HEAD with the new gate, fl returns rc=4 (WRDE_CMDSUB) with NO FLAGS AT ALL:
  wordexp("$((1+2))", 0): fl=(rc=4, []) glibc=(rc=0, ["3"])
because fl rejects every `$(` unconditionally (it has no command substitution, so both branches of
the has_command_substitution check return WRDE_CMDSUB regardless of the flag). Arithmetic was
therefore refused outright in the DEFAULT configuration, not only in the hardened one.

The bead's warning was also correct and worth restating: a classification-only fix would have been
worse than the bug, because accepting `$((...))` without an evaluator leaves it unexpanded — a
silent wrong answer instead of a loud error.

ORACLE MEASURED FIRST, and it is NOT POSIX shell arithmetic. glibc's wordexp implements only:
  + - * /, parentheses, unary sign, decimal / hex (0x) / octal (0) literals.
Everything else is absent in a very specific way — it does NOT error, it silently STOPS at the
first unimplemented operator and returns the value parsed so far:
  $((10%3)) -> 10    $((5%2+1)) -> 5     $((1<<4)) -> 1     $((256>>2)) -> 256
  $((1<2)) -> 1      $((2<=2)) -> 2      $((3>4)) -> 3      $((3==3)) -> 3
  $((6&3)) -> 6      $((6|3)) -> 6       $((6^3)) -> 6      $((1&&0)) -> 1
  $((1?42:7)) -> 1
  $((1+2*3<4)) -> 7   <- the case that PINS the rule: 1+2*3 is evaluated, "<4" is dropped
And these are WRDE_SYNTAX: $((~5)) $((!0)) $((1/0)) $((1+)) $(( )) $((abc)) and, notably,
$((FLVAR+1)) with FLVAR set and exported — glibc's wordexp has no variables in arithmetic at all.
Under WRDE_NOCMD every arithmetic result above is unchanged, and only $(cmd) and backticks are
refused with WRDE_CMDSUB.
The early-stop behaviour is reproduced DELIBERATELY. Implementing full shell arithmetic would have
been a fresh divergence from the oracle dressed up as a fix.

Method note: my first probe mislabelled the return codes (I assumed BADCHAR=1) and made
$(echo hi)/WRDE_NOCMD look like WRDE_NOSPACE. glibc's wordexp.h is NOSPACE=1, BADCHAR=2, BADVAL=3,
CMDSUB=4, SYNTAX=5; corrected before any code was written, and the gate uses the real values.

IMPLEMENTATION — three sites, because a word passes through three stages and every one of them had
to learn about `$((`. Finding that took two failing gate runs, each of which named the next stage:
  1. crates/frankenlibc-core/src/stdlib/wordexp.rs — eval_arith(), a recursive-descent evaluator for
     exactly the grammar above, i64 and wrapping so no input can panic; scan_arith_end() finds the
     matching `))` with parenthesis depth starting at 2, so $(((2+3)*4)) closes correctly. New
     ExpandError::ArithSyntax, mapped to WRDE_SYNTAX at the abi boundary.
  2. crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/unistd_abi.rs, the WRDE_NOCMD scanner — `$((` is arithmetic and is
     skipped; `$(` remains command substitution. BOTH the double-quoted and unquoted branches had
     the bug, and both are fixed.
  3. the same file's tokenizer and split-mask expander:
     - the tokenizer splits on whitespace BEFORE expansion, so `$(( 1 + 2 ))` was torn into five
       words and the evaluator never saw an expression. It now tracks parenthesis depth and copies
       arithmetic verbatim, and an unterminated `$((` is WRDE_SYNTAX like an unclosed quote.
     - has_unquoted_parameter_expansion routes any word containing an unquoted `$` to
       expand_vars_with_split_mask_dyn, which is a SECOND expander; the core expander's copy of the
       rule was necessary but never reached for these words.

GATE: new crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/conformance_diff_wordexp_arith.rs — 38 words x 2 flag modes
against the live host wordexp, deliberately mixing all three classes (evaluated, silently
truncated, rejected) so a reimplementation that "corrected" the early-stop behaviour fails. It also
asserts both directions of the security property: WRDE_NOCMD must never reject arithmetic, and must
always reject $(cmd) and backticks (with the oracle's refusal asserted first, so neither

title: [parity][bug] wcsxfrm truncation: writes n-1 chars + always-NUL instead of glibc fill-n
description: Found by NEW wcsxfrm_wcscoll_differential_fuzz (400k vs live glibc, exact dest-buffer comparison). On truncation (n <= src_len) glibc wcsxfrm fills min(n, src_len+1) wide chars of the transform and writes a terminating NUL ONLY when it fits, so for n <= src_len the written prefix is left UNTERMINATED (e.g. wcsxfrm('abc', n=2) yields dest=['a','b'], no NUL). fl's wcsxfrm (own inline impl in wchar_abi.rs, NOT shared with the correct narrow strxfrm core) reserved n-1 and ALWAYS wrote a NUL, so it produced ['a',0] — fewer transform chars + a spurious terminator. The narrow strxfrm core already matched glibc (copy_len<limit conditional NUL); only the wide reimpl was wrong (same 'ABI reimplements inline' pattern as wcscasecmp). Return value (src_len) was always correct; only the truncation buffer diverged. Fixed: copy_len=min(src_len,n), NUL only if copy_len<n. 400k 0-div; updated wchar_abi_test contract that pinned the old behavior.

description:

Fallback trigger: revert if string-test golden sha256 changes, if first-difference/NUL ordering changes, or if RCH post p50 does not improve at 256 equal.

title: [CRITICAL] bd-g2bd5 regression: glibc_internal_abi_test still SIGABRTs on free(): invalid size under parallel test execution
description:
## Regression against bd-g2bd5

bd-g2bd5 was closed at 2026-04-22T14:01:10Z with close_reason 'Scoped __cxa_thread_atexit_impl capture to local TLS dtor tests and revalidated glibc/startup ABI suites' (commit a581f0ac 'br-bd-g2bd5: isolate tls dtor test registrations'). That fix is partial — the heap corruption still reproduces.

## Fresh repro at current HEAD (901b7bcc / 693bb766)

```
$ rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/rch_target_frankenlibc_cc cargo test --workspace --all-targets
...
test e2e_string_pipeline_strlen_malloc_memcpy_strcmp ... ok
free(): invalid size
error: test failed, to rerun pass `-p frankenlibc-abi --test glibc_internal_abi_test`
  process didn't exit successfully: `.../glibc_internal_abi_test-bcae966c1a14117c` (signal: 6, SIGABRT: process abort signal)
```

Same binary re-run in isolation (`cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test glibc_internal_abi_test`) now appears to pass — so the race has moved from 'reliably reproducing on isolated run' (pre-fix) to 'only reproducing when other workspace tests run concurrently in the same process pool' (post-fix). That's measurable progress, but the heap write onto a freed-or-wrong-size chunk is still live.

## Diagnosis

The a581f0ac fix scoped  capture to its test-local TLS dtor registrations. That closed **one** source of cross-test thread-local leakage. The SIGABRT still firing near  (in a different test binary) suggests either:

1. another set of test TLS/thread-local state is leaking through the same path (e.g. resolv-context override, IDNA allocation pool, wcstof128 static, obstack globals), OR
2. the fix captured TLS dtor registrations correctly but freed its scratch buffer via a path that is inconsistent with the allocation size metadata (e.g. Box::from_raw on a pointer allocated by a different allocator, or layout mismatch on dealloc).

## Fix direction

1. Rerun with MALLOC_CHECK_=2 to get a glibc backtrace from the first write past chunk-size metadata.
2. Rerun under ASan (RUSTFLAGS='-Zsanitizer=address' cargo +nightly test --workspace) — ASan will point at the exact offending free/realloc.
3. Audit remaining thread-local state init/teardown in crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/glibc_internal_abi.rs plus any Box::from_raw / custom Drop impl that crosses allocators.

## Provenance / cross-reference

- Previous bead: bd-g2bd5 (closed 2026-04-22T14:01:10Z).
- Previous fix commit: a581f0ac br-bd-g2bd5: isolate tls dtor test registrations.
- Also closed this session: bd-i3om4 (70d3f3ea br-bd-i3om4: serialize runtime policy test state) and bd-nnjiz (901b7bcc br-bd-nnjiz: normalize elimination flake threshold). Both appear to hold under parallel reruns.

## Blast radius

Still blocks cargo test --workspace --all-targets from completing cleanly. --test-threads=1 is a workaround, not a fix.

title: ABI .init_array deadlock: HOST_CXA_THREAD_ATEXIT_IMPL OnceLock self-recurse
description:
## Reproduction

```bash
LIB=target/release/libfrankenlibc_abi.so
cc -O2 tests/integration/fixture_setjmp_edges.c -o /tmp/fx
timeout 15 env LD_PRELOAD=$LIB /tmp/fx
# hangs forever; SIGTERM exits 124
```

`bash scripts/check_setjmp_native.sh` and `cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test setjmp_abi_test` both inherit the hang.

## Diagnosis

strace shows the process stuck at `futex(<addr>, FUTEX_WAIT_BITSET_PRIVATE, 5, NULL, ...)` in libfrankenlibc_abi data segment, before ever reaching `main`. wchan=`futex_do_wait`, syscall=202.

Address resolution against `nm --numeric-sort` localizes the futex word to offset 8 of `HOST_CXA_THREAD_ATEXIT_IMPL` (a `std::sync::OnceLock<usize>` declared at crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/startup_abi.rs:934). Futex value 5 = std `Once` RUNNING + has-waiter.

Cycle:
1. .init_array entry `frankenlibc_abi_stdio_init_entry` runs while ld.so still holds the loader lock.
2. Path eventually triggers `__cxa_thread_atexit_impl` (Rust TLS init for some thread_local with a non-trivial drop).
3. Our interposed `__cxa_thread_atexit_impl` calls `host_cxa_thread_atexit_impl()`.
4. That enters `OnceLock::get_or_init`, transitions state to RUNNING.
5. Closure invokes `dlfcn_abi::dlsym(RTLD_NEXT, "__cxa_thread_atexit_impl")`.
6. The dlsym path itself touches Rust TLS, triggering another `__cxa_thread_atexit_impl` registration.
7. Recursive call enters `OnceLock::get_or_init` again, sees RUNNING, futex-waits — on its own thread.

The existing `TLS_ATEXIT_REENTRY` guard only fires AFTER the host lookup, so it doesn't break this cycle.

## Fix (committed in same change as this bead)

Replace `OnceLock<usize>` with `AtomicUsize` (sentinel = `usize::MAX` for resolved-but-absent) plus a thread-local reentry guard that returns `None` if the resolver re-enters us mid-lookup. AtomicUsize never blocks, so recursive lookups simply re-resolve or fall through to the in-Rust fallback list. Mirrors the proven pattern already used by `host_resolve.rs`.

## Validation

- `LD_PRELOAD=…/libfrankenlibc_abi.so /tmp/fx` → "fixture_setjmp_edges: PASS" in <1s
- `bash scripts/check_setjmp_native.sh` → "check_setjmp_native: PASS"

## Severity

[CRITICAL] — every LD_PRELOAD-loaded binary hangs at process start under release profile. Affects all conformance scripts that go through .init_array bootstrap.
notes: Fixed in 16da65d8: AtomicUsize cache + per-thread reentry guard replace OnceLock for HOST_CXA_THREAD_ATEXIT_IMPL. Verified: LD_PRELOAD fixture binaries run in <1s (was: hung at futex_wait); check_setjmp_native.sh + setjmp_abi_test pass.

title: [perf] frankenlibc-core::stdio::parse_format_string (printf.rs:853) — per-call Vec<FormatSegment> heap alloc on whole printf family (26.8ns for %-free literal)
description:
PROFILING handoff from SnowyMill (run 20260601-perf-26a69011, git 26a69011). MEASUREMENT ONLY.

SCENARIO: format-string parse cost on the printf hot path. criterion stdio_bench, rch AMD EPYC, sample-size 50.

BASELINE p50: stdio_printf_parse/literal 26.8ns, positional 101.2ns, mixed 119.9ns. The 'literal' case has NO '%' (zero parse work) yet costs 26.8ns -> the cost is the per-call Vec<FormatSegment> heap allocation, not parsing. Render for contrast: bounded_string 12.5ns, signed_decimal 54.3ns.

HOT PATH CONFIRMED: parse_format_string returns an owned Vec and is called per-call by the ENTIRE printf family: crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/stdio_abi.rs snprintf:3389, sprintf:3462, vsnprintf:3532, dprintf:3689, and :3152/:3840/:3883; plus err/warn (err_abi.rs:159) and fortify fmtcheck (fmtcheck.rs:127). Every formatted-output call therefore pays one heap alloc + free for the segment vector.

ROOT CAUSE (source): printf.rs:853 parse_format_string -> let mut segments = Vec::new(); ... segments.push(...) -> Vec<FormatSegment>. 

FIX DIRECTIONS (optimizer, one lever; preserve exact semantics incl. positional %n$ args and width/precision '*'): (a) stream the existing parse_format_spec in a single parse+render pass so no segment Vec is materialized; or (b) use a SmallVec<[FormatSegment; N]> to avoid heap alloc for typical (<=N segment) formats; or (c) memoize parsed segments keyed by format-string content/hash. Re-run: rch exec -- cargo bench -p frankenlibc-bench --bench stdio_bench -- --sample-size 50. Validate against existing printf conformance/golden tests (positional, width.*, %%, %n).

EVIDENCE: tests/artifacts/perf/20260601-perf-26a69011/stdio_condvar_bench.summary.md + stdio_bench.raw.log.

Isomorphism proof: parser byte order, positional width/precision, argument counting, formatting math, and RNG/global state unchanged; printf golden fixture hashes unchanged. title: [perf] frankenlibc-core::string strcspn/strspn/strpbrk general arm (str.rs ~547) — O(n*m) set.contains per byte; add >=4-char-set bench
description:
PROFILING handoff from SnowyMill (run 20260601-perf-26a69011). CODE-CONFIRMED latent algorithmic issue + BENCH-COVERAGE GAP (not yet measured).

FINDING (source): for accept/reject sets of length >=4, the general arm of strcspn (str.rs ~547), strspn, and strpbrk does `set.contains(&byte)` — a LINEAR scan of the set — for every haystack byte => O(n*m). glibc builds a 256-entry bitset/bool table once (O(m)) then O(1) lookup per byte => O(n+m).

IMPORTANT HONESTY NOTE: the current string_bench does NOT exercise this path. bench_strcspn_absent uses reject=b"Z\0" (len 1), which hits the special-cased size-1 scalar arm. The measured 3938ns/4096B (string_bench.summary.md) is that scalar size-1 scan, NOT the O(n*m) general arm. So this hotspot is code-confirmed but UNMEASURED.

ASKS (for optimizer): (1) add a string_bench case with a >=4-char accept/reject set to actually measure the general arm; (2) replace the per-byte linear `set.contains` with a 256-entry [bool;256] / 32-byte bitset built once. Preserve semantics (NUL termination, empty-set behavior). Re-run string_bench to quantify.

EVIDENCE: tests/artifacts/perf/20260601-perf-26a69011/string_bench.summary.md (H-setmembership-Onm).
close_reason: Fixed in fa515194. General >=4-byte strspn/strcspn/strpbrk arms now use a local [bool;256] byte-membership table instead of O(n*m) slice.contains scans. rch ts2 p50 4096-byte before/after: strcspn 9238.067->2418.668 ns, strpbrk 9036.853->2386.458 ns, strspn 3159.075->2633.772 ns. title: [bug][RED][resolv] res_mkquery omits the AD bit glibc sets by default (RES_TRUSTAD): header byte 3 is 0x00 vs glibc 0x20
description:
SURFACED by bed1a9226, which linked conformance_diff_res_mkquery's res_init as __res_init. The target had NEVER linked, so this divergence was invisible.

MEASURED, worker hz2, harness 'rch exec -- cargo test -j 1 --no-fail-fast -p frankenlibc-abi --test conformance_diff_res_mkquery -- --test-threads=1'. Same query built by both libraries in the same process, packet compared from offset 2 (the 2-byte ID is randomized):
  fl    = [01, 00, 00, 01, 00, 00, 00, 00, 00, 00, 07, 'example', 03, 'com', 00, 00, 01, 00, 01]
  glibc = [01, 20, 00, 01, 00, 00, 00, 00, 00, 00, 07, 'example', 03, 'com', 00, 00, 01, 00, 01]
Everything matches except header byte 3: glibc 0x20, fl 0x00. Byte 3 is RA(7) Z(6) AD(5) CD(4) RCODE(3..0), so 0x20 is the AD (Authentic Data) bit. glibc has set AD on outgoing queries by default since RES_TRUSTAD entered RES_DEFAULT (glibc 2.31); the QNAME encoding, QTYPE/QCLASS, counts and RD bit all already agree.

WHERE IT COMES FROM: fl's res_mkquery -> __res_mkquery (crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/glibc_internal_abi.rs:1298) builds the header with frankenlibc_core::resolv::dns::DnsHeader::new_query(tx_id). The comment there says 'flags (RD=1)' and nothing sets AD.

DO NOT JUST OR IN 0x20. new_query is shared by fl's real query path, so this changes what fl puts on the wire, not just what a gate observes. The prior question is whether fl models resolver options at all: glibc sets AD because RES_TRUSTAD is in _res.options, and a caller that clears RES_TRUSTAD gets AD=0. Check whether fl has an options word, whether res_init/res_ninit populate it, and whether any other flag in that byte is also unconditional. If fl has no options model, say so and pin the default explicitly rather than pretending the bit is a constant.

Gate already exists and is RED at HEAD by design (conformance_diff_res_mkquery). Do not close by comparing only the length or by masking byte 3 out of the comparison.
close_reason: Fixed in 20369ef4f: DnsHeader::new_query now sets AD (0x0100 -> 0x0120), matching glibc's RES_TRUSTAD default. fl has no resolver options model (_res is an opaque blob; RES_TRUSTAD is undefined tree-wide), so the default is pinned as a literal with that limitation documented in the source, per this bead's instruction. conformance_diff_res_mkquery is 1 passed / 0 failed on hz2; core resolv 271 passed; the 7 resolv_abi_test failures are identical at clean HEAD and filed separately.

ANSWERING THIS BEAD'S PRIOR QUESTION FIRST, because it asked me not to just OR in 0x20: fl has NO resolver options model. _res is an opaque [u8; 600] in glibc_internal_abi.rs:5104, and RES_TRUSTAD, RES_DEFAULT and any options word appear NOWHERE in the tree (grepped across crates/). So there is nothing to make the bit conditional on. Per this bead's own instruction I pinned glibc's default explicitly and documented it: the comment states that glibc derives AD from _res.options, that a caller clearing RES_TRUSTAD gets AD=0, that fl cannot express that today, and that this literal must become conditional if fl ever grows an options word. No other flag in that byte is set unconditionally -- RD was already there and is correct.

CHANGE: DnsHeader::new_query flags 0x0100 -> 0x0120 in frankenlibc-core/src/resolv/dns.rs. This is fl's shared query builder, so it changes what fl puts ON THE WIRE, not just what the gate sees -- which is the point, since the wire format was what diverged.

GATE: conformance_diff_res_mkquery res_mkquery_matches_glibc, 1 passed / 0 failed on hz2. It builds the same query with both libraries in one process and compares the packet from offset 2, so it cannot pass by length alone and byte 3 is not masked out.

title: [HIGH] build_btrfs_readdir_image fixture leaves are missing tree_block_csum stamping
description:
# Review finding

`build_btrfs_readdir_image()` builds synthetic root-tree and fs-tree leaves for the readdir suite, but it never stamps `tree_block_csum` on either leaf.

## Evidence
- Builder: `crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:23165-23311`
- It writes the root-tree leaf at `root_tree_logical = 0x4000` and the fs-tree leaf at `fs_tree_logical = 0x20000`.
- Unlike the fsops fixtures, this builder never invokes the existing checksum helper (`stamp_btrfs_test_tree_block_crc32c`), and it switches to `nodesize = 16384`, so both synthetic tree blocks must be stamped consistently with the parser’s current checksum expectations.
- The workspace rerun still fails all readdir-specific consumers with `Format("invalid field: tree_block_csum (CRC32C checksum mismatch)")`:
  - `walk_btrfs_dir_entry_items_includes_dir_index_items`
  - `btrfs_readdir_mixed_types`
  - `btrfs_readdir_empty_directory_returns_dot_dotdot`
  - `btrfs_readdir_sorted_by_index`
  - `btrfs_readdir_offset_pagination`
  - `btrfs_readdir_special_characters_in_names`

## Why this is high severity
This is a second stale synthetic-fixture family independent of the minimal open/root-tree fixture. It blocks all of the new btrfs directory-iteration regression coverage.

## Repro
`rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/rch_target_frankenfs_cod cargo test --workspace --all-targets`

## Expected fix direction
Stamp checksums for both generated leaves after all items/payloads are finalized, with nodesize-aware coverage for the 16 KiB fs-tree case.
close_reason: Fixed: build_btrfs_readdir_image at crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:23274 now stamps CRC32C on both root-tree leaf and fs-tree leaf at lines 23421-23424 with nodesize-aware slicing. All cited readdir consumers (walk_btrfs_dir_entry_items_includes_dir_index_items, btrfs_readdir_* family) pass under rch workspace run (17 readdir tests green).

Both the ABI sgetspent_r (glibc_internal_abi.rs) and core parse_shadow_numeric mapped ANY unparseable numeric field to -1 and accepted the entry. glibc parses shadow fields with strtoul (whole-field consume): empty->-1 sentinel, present non-empty must be non-neg decimal (+/ws ok); garbage 'abc', literal '-1', trailing junk '5x' -> NULL entry. fl also failed to strip leading +/space (' 5'->-1 vs glibc 5). title: JBD2 descriptor/revoke block checksum omits 4-byte tail instead of zeroing it
description: In crates/ffs-journal/src/lib.rs, verify_jbd2_block_checksum handles JBD2_BLOCKTYPE_DESCRIPTOR and JBD2_BLOCKTYPE_REVOKE by computing crc32c over &block[..bs - 4]. However, Linux jbd2_descriptor_block_csum_verify temporarily zeroes the 4-byte tail checksum field and then computes the checksum over the *entire* block size (j->j_blocksize). By slicing off the last 4 bytes instead of hashing 4 zero bytes, the rust implementation produces a different CRC32C value and will incorrectly fail validation for valid JBD2 descriptor blocks.
close_reason: Descriptor/revoke checksum verification now hashes the full block with a zeroed 4-byte tail, matching Linux jbd2 semantics; added regression coverage and passed targeted rch fmt/test/check/clippy.

title: [PERF] btrfs_ino_lookup scans entire fs-tree on every call — O(N) per ioctl with no caching
description:
# Performance concern from modes-of-reasoning pass

## Finding

`OpenFs::btrfs_resolve_inode_path` at crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:14447+ (added in f70dcca for bd-caex2) calls `self.walk_btrfs_fs_tree(cx)?` unconditionally on every invocation, walking every leaf entry in the subvolume fs-tree to build the `parent_by_child: BTreeMap` index. That means each BTRFS_IOC_INO_LOOKUP ioctl costs O(N) where N = total fs-tree items (inodes + dir entries + refs + xattrs + extents).

For a typical ext4/btrfs image the cost is negligible. For a large image (millions of inodes / tens of millions of items), a single ioctl can scan multi-megabyte indexes and iterate hundreds of thousands of entries. A caller issuing K ioctls imposes O(K*N) work — a slow query amplifier if a tool (e.g., `btrfs subvolume list`) iterates many inodes.

## Evidence

- Entry point: crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:14439 `fn btrfs_resolve_inode_path`
- Full-tree scan: `let entries = self.walk_btrfs_fs_tree(cx)?`
- Index built per call: BTreeMap<u64, (u64, Vec<u8>)> with one entry per INODE_REF item
- No cache, no early-termination (we build the full index before walking the chain even though we only need back-refs along the path)

## Fix directions (choose at implementation time)

1. **Early-exit walk.** Replace `walk_btrfs_fs_tree → build full index → walk` with a demand-driven search: at each step, search the fs-tree for items with key (objectid, INODE_REF, *) and stop at the first match. Each hop is an O(log N) btree lookup; total cost O(depth * log N).
2. **Per-subvolume cache** on `OpenFs` keyed on the fs-tree root generation. Invalidated on subvolume changes. Sub-μs per lookup after warmup.
3. **Batched multi-inode resolution.** If the caller is resolving multiple inodes in one request (e.g., a future `list_paths`), build the index once and amortize.

For V1, (1) is the simplest and keeps the code path stateless. (2) is the right long-term answer once we know the access pattern.

## Acceptance

- A synthetic image with 10K inodes completes a sequence of 100 INO_LOOKUP ioctls in bounded time (wall-clock cap, e.g., < 1s).
- Microbenchmark in `benches/` documents the per-ioctl cost.
- Unit tests from bd-caex2 continue to pass without regression.
close_reason: writable demand-driven walk + read-only cached index

title: e2compr: implement single-indirect block pointer read-modify-write
description:
Implement write support for indirect block pointers (i_block[12] -> pointer block -> data). This is the first level of indirect addressing and covers logical blocks 12 through 12+ptrs_per_block-1 (for 4K blocks: 12 through 1035).

STEPS:
1. When logical_block >= 12 and < 12 + ptrs_per_block:
   a. Read i_block[12]. If 0, allocate a new block, zero-fill it, write i_block[12].
   b. Read the indirect block.
   c. Write the target pointer at the correct 4-byte offset within it.
   d. Write the indirect block back to disk.
2. For freeing: when all pointers in the indirect block become 0, free the indirect block itself and set i_block[12] = 0.
3. Update set_indirect_block_ptr to dispatch to this path when lb >= 12 && lb < 12 + ptrs_per_block.

ACCEPTANCE: Compressed write works for files up to 4MB (1024 clusters * 4 blocks * 4K = 16MB with shift=2).

title: sigblock/sigsetmask sign-extend the int mask (mask as u64); glibc zero-extends ((unsigned int)mask)
close_reason:
Fixed in 433182d45. sigblock and sigsetmask both widened the BSD int mask with 'mask as u64', which SIGN-extends: sigblock(-1) asked the kernel to block signals 1..64 instead of 1..32, reaching signals a BSD int mask cannot name at all, including glibc's reserved SIGCANCEL(32) and SIGSETXID(33) that drive thread cancellation and setxid broadcast.

GROUND TRUTH (measured, not recalled) on live glibc 2.42, reading SigBlk from /proc/self/status after the call, each case in its own subprocess:
  sigblock(-1)         -> SigBlk 0x000000007ffbfeff
  sigsetmask(-1)       -> SigBlk 0x000000007ffbfeff
  sigblock(0x40000000) -> SigBlk 0x0000000040000000
  sigblock(1<<9)       -> SigBlk 0x0000000000000200
Two facts fall out of the -1 row: the UPPER WORD IS CLEAR, so glibc widens through 'unsigned int' (the filed defect); and BIT 31 IS ALSO CLEAR, because glibc's sigprocmask deletes signals 32 and 33 from every set handed to it. The clear bits at 8 and 18 are the kernel's own refusal to block SIGKILL/SIGSTOP. Both behaviours are now reproduced by a shared bsd_mask_to_sigset helper: '(mask as u32 as u64) & !SIGCANCEL_BIT'.

SECOND DEFECT FOUND, NOT FILED IN THIS BEAD: fl's own signal_abi::sigprocmask does NOT do that reserved-signal deletion, so a direct sigprocmask/pthread_sigmask caller can still block 32/33. Fixing that is a different surface, so bsd_mask_to_sigset clears the bit locally and the sigprocmask gap is filed as bd-wh14ly (P2), which notes that the local clear should probably move into sigprocmask once that lands, so the rule lives in one place.

EVIDENCE (remote via RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2, -j2, CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/tmp/rch_target_frankenlibc_greenglen):
  cargo test -j2 -p frankenlibc-abi --test conformance_diff_sigblock -> 4 passed; 0 failed.

GATE (crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/conformance_diff_sigblock.rs, new): compares the mask the KERNEL ends up holding after fl and after live glibc across -1, INT_MIN, bit 30, a single low signal, and empty -- rather than asserting a constant, so it catches the widening and the SIGCANCEL filter together and would catch a further divergence without being told about it. Two design points that matter: the mask is read with a PURE sigprocmask query (set=NULL), never through the function under test, which would otherwise report its own mistaken view; and each arm forks, because it mutates the signal mask while the harness runs tests in parallel threads of one process. The child reports through a pipe using only sigprocmask and write -- both plain syscalls -- because allocating after fork in a multithreaded process can deadlock on a lock another thread held at fork time. An earlier draft that shipped the mask out nibble-by-nibble through exit codes was discarded: a legitimate nibble of 15 collided with its error code, and it forked 16 times per case.
Also covers bd-ltggi7's roundtrip half: siggetmask must report the kernel's mask and change nothing (before/reported/after all compared).

NEGATIVE CASE (proved, not asserted): restoring 'mask as u64' gives fl=0xfffffffffffbfeff vs glibc=0x000000007ffbfeff, failing both differential arms and the named all-ones arm with the explicit message that signals 33..64 were blocked; siggetmask stays GREEN because its mask (1<<9) is unaffected by sign, so the gate is specific rather than globally failing. Probe removed; grep over crates/ confirms none remain.

GATES: rustfmt --edition 2024 on both touched files: clean. clippy -p frankenlibc-abi --all-targets -D warnings: zero findings in either. NO REGRESSION: unistd_abi_test 535 passed / 5 failed, identical to the clean-HEAD baseline measured this session.

CARE TAKEN: the helper was initially inserted between sigblock's #[cfg_attr(no_mangle)] attribute and its signature, which would have applied the ABI export attribute to the private helper; caught by reading the result back and corrected before building. source_commit=f6a87baae -> 433182d45. Unrelated working-tree changes by other agents were not reverted or disturbed.

title: REVIEW: [HIGH] locale_abi.rs setlocale/newlocale/textdomain/bindtextdomain walk unbounded memory via CStr::from_ptr on user-controlled pointers
description:
Location: crates/frankenlibc-abi/src/locale_abi.rs

Four POSIX/GNU locale entrypoints read user-supplied string pointers through CStr::from_ptr with no length bound. A caller that passes a non-NUL-terminated pointer walks arbitrary process memory until an accidental zero byte — info-leak or segfault, reachable from the libc.so boundary.

Affected sites:
- setlocale line 125: `let name = unsafe { CStr::from_ptr(locale) }.to_bytes();`
- textdomain lines 351, 355: dereferences `*domainname` (line 351) then CStr::from_ptr (line 355) — both on user-supplied pointers.
- bindtextdomain lines 377, 391: CStr::from_ptr on both `domainname` and `dirname`.
- newlocale line 441: CStr::from_ptr on `locale`.

Other parts of this file (lines 662, 741, 750, 759) read known-terminated internal strings and are fine.

Reachability: setlocale is called by essentially every C/C++ program at startup; newlocale is used in POSIX.1-2008 thread-safe locale code; textdomain/bindtextdomain are used by every gettext-enabled program. An adversarial caller (or corrupted pointer) triggers an unbounded memory walk.

Severity: HIGH. The same pattern was just fixed in __assert_perror_fail (bd-9bijw); locale entry points are more commonly invoked, so this is at least as reachable.

Fix plan:
- Introduce a shared read_bounded_cstr helper that wraps scan_c_string + known_remaining and returns Option<Vec<u8>>.
- Replace each CStr::from_ptr in the four functions with read_bounded_cstr; on None, treat the locale/domain as invalid (null return / query-mode default) per each function's existing contract.
- Also null-check *domainname byte read in textdomain by reading through the helper instead of dereferencing directly.

Tests: setlocale/newlocale are not in the abort-barrier category — add a regression test that feeds a non-NUL-terminated buffer via a short page-aligned slice and asserts the return is null without walking past the allocation.
close_reason: All four named sites (setlocale L158, textdomain L392, bindtextdomain L419+L435, newlocale L491) now use read_bounded_cstr (locale_abi.rs:36) which delegates to scan_c_string + known_locale_string_remaining. catopen L715 also uses it. 50/50 locale_abi tests + 8/8 locale lib tests pass. Regression test deferred: known_locale_string_remaining returns None in cfg(test), so unit-test exercising the bound is impossible without production-mode harness.

title: Expand inode checksum metamorphic relations beyond field-content invariance
description:
The current inode-checksum metamorphic harness in crates/ffs-core/tests/metamorphic.rs (added in 785bb74) covers exactly one relation: the checksum is computed after zeroing the on-disk checksum bytes, so any prior garbage in those bytes does not affect the new checksum.

That is a useful but narrow property. The checksum function has several other behavioral contracts that protect against collision attacks and silent corruption, none of which are currently exercised:

- MR-INO: writing identical inode bytes to two different inode numbers must produce different on-disk checksums (so a per-inode forgery cannot be replayed at a different inode slot).
- MR-SEED: identical inode bytes + identical inode number with a different filesystem checksum seed must produce different checksums (so cross-filesystem tampering is detectable).
- MR-GEN: changing only the generation field flips the checksum (verifies generation participates in the digest, the standard kernel anti-replay mechanism for NFS handles).
- MR-DETECT: flipping any single bit outside the checksum field bytes must invalidate verify_inode_checksum (proves the digest covers the full inode body, not just a prefix).

Each of these maps directly onto a class of real-world ext4 vulnerabilities. Add them as proptest cases alongside the existing inode_checksum_field_content_invariance test.
close_reason: Added MR-INO, MR-SEED, MR-GEN, MR-DETECT proptests covering inode-number sensitivity, seed sensitivity, generation sensitivity, and single-bit-flip detection. All 5 metamorphic.rs cases pass (cargo test -p ffs-core --test metamorphic), clippy clean. sha=99e8455

title: [compat][iconv] add UCS-2 / UCS-4 / UTF-7 charset support (iconv_open fails; glibc supports)
description: Differential probe of iconv_open(charset, UTF-8) vs host glibc over 34 charset names found fl rejects UCS-2, UCS-4, and UTF-7 (iconv_open returns -1) where glibc opens them. These are real compatibility gaps — programs using these charset names by exact spelling break entirely on fl. NOT clean aliases: (1) UCS-4 = UTF-32BE-no-BOM for ENCODE (verified byte-exact vs fl's UTF-32BE across valid+astral inputs) but on DECODE glibc UCS-4 accepts the full ISO-10646 31-bit range and emits NON-STANDARD extended UTF-8 for code points > U+10FFFF (e.g. U+110000 -> f4 90 80 80), while fl's Unicode-strict UTF-32BE rejects them; a true UCS-4 codec needs the extended range + extended-UTF-8 emission (or a documented Unicode-strict divergence per the ecvt precedent). (2) UCS-2 = UTF-16LE-no-BOM but BMP-restricted (rejects astral with EILSEQ, vs UTF-16's surrogate pairs) — needs a range-restricted variant. (3) UTF-7 = stateful base64-modified encoding, a full new codec. Charset table is in frankenlibc-core/src/iconv/mod.rs (canonical/normalized/aliases entries). Implement each with a byte-exact differential vs glibc (both directions, valid + edge/invalid inputs) + golden sha256. Decide per-codepoint-range whether to match glibc's extended behavior or document a Unicode-strict divergence.
close_reason: COMPLETE. All three charsets shipped: UCS-2/UCS-2LE/UCS-2BE (10b77df65, BMP-only no-surrogate codec), UCS-4/BE/LE (d5f65a0e9, UTF-32BE/LE alias, Unicode-strict on >U+10FFFF), and UTF-7 (d93b5a3a4, full RFC 2152 stateful shift codec — dedicated whole-buffer branch in iconv(), byte-exact vs host glibc both directions incl. the omit-'-' optimization + end-of-input flush + astral surrogate pairs). Plus ~18 charset-name aliases (4250fc53a/482bde33a/cf54ad63d) and the dead-alias bug-class fix. Gates: conformance_diff_iconv_{ucs2,ucs4,utf7,aliases}. Known residual (documented in the UTF-7 commit): a shift sequence split across multiple iconv() calls is not yet supported — the single-call path is exact.

title: [HIGH] cross-allocator-free pattern: 30+ raw_alloc sites return buffers callers libc::free (bd-dqqh1 cluster)
description:
## Pattern audit (bd-dqqh1 generalization)

Following the bd-dqqh1 root cause (host2netname allocates via internal arena, caller frees via libc::free → free(): invalid size SIGABRT), grep for the pattern `crate::malloc_abi::raw_alloc` across crates/frankenlibc-abi/src returns 30+ call sites. Each one returns a heap buffer to its caller. If the caller is C user code under LD_PRELOAD, our interposed free() catches it correctly. If the caller is a Rust test binary (debug build, no preload), libc::free binds to glibc's free at link time and the cross-allocator free aborts with the same fingerprint.

## Confirmed sites (free-by-caller pattern, POSIX 'caller must free')

inet_abi.rs:382, 393   - getifaddrs / gethostbyname pattern
dirent_abi.rs:524, 556, 567 - scandir family
stdlib_abi.rs:4026     - realpath et al
rpc_abi.rs:666, 667, 1091, 1151, 1228, 1293 - XDR/RPC strdup-likes
rpc_abi.rs:2995        - host2netdomain (sibling of host2netname, same shape)
wchar_abi.rs:76, 1315, 4365 - wcsdup et al
unistd_abi.rs:3335, 3544, 4907, 4927, 6985, 7002, 7026, 7046,
              7218, 7224, 9868, 10097, 16246
                       - getcwd / wordexp / getifaddrs / strdup-likes
string_abi.rs:3484     - strdup probably

Each site allocates with raw_alloc (our internal arena) and the caller is expected to free via the standard free(). This works under LD_PRELOAD (our interposed free routes correctly) but fails on debug-test builds where libc::free binds to glibc's free.

## Bead bd-dqqh1 fix shape

`let buf = libc::malloc(name.len()) as *mut c_char;` instead of `raw_alloc(name.len())`. Under LD_PRELOAD libc::malloc IS our interposed malloc, so functionality is preserved. Under non-preload (test context) libc::malloc is glibc's, which pairs correctly with libc::free.

## Sweep recommendation

For each call site listed above:

1. Confirm the buffer is returned to a CALLER (vs freed in same module).
2. Confirm the contract is 'caller must free()' (POSIX docs / glibc man pages).
3. Replace raw_alloc with libc::malloc.
4. Add a regression test that calls the function under cargo test default parallelism, frees with libc::free.

Rough scope: ~30 mechanical edits + ~30 regression tests. Could be split per-module: rpc (5 callsites), unistd (13), wchar (3), inet (2), dirent (3), stdlib (1), string (1).

## Provenance

bd-dqqh1's host2netname fix at HEAD post-17431c7a fixed one site of the pattern. This umbrella bead tracks the remaining 30+. The bd-ye0f4 cluster (a581f0ac, e289f838, b04d7238 partial fixes) was likely chasing different facets of the SAME root cause.
notes: Closed via cumulative drain across the session. Caller-freeable sites converted to libc::malloc/free in: 322b1254 (scandirat + IDNA + argz family), 82d9bf1f (scandir/realpath/user2netname), 61d71aa3 (strdup/strndup/wcsdup), 25ccfd15 (get_current_dir_name/tempnam), eeb9d2a7 (host2netname/user2netname), d503e6ce (xdr_bytes/string/array/reference). Remaining raw_alloc sites are internal-paired (wordexp/wordfree, glob/globfree, ftw/nftw, getifaddrs/freeifaddrs, if_nameindex/if_freenameindex, xdrrec_create/destroy) — verified safe by audit. Underlying root cause (cross-thread reentry guard race) was fixed by bd-wbqeo (6c60fbf7) which converted NATIVE_*_REENTRY guards to thread_local Cell<bool>.

title: EPIC: Eliminate all remaining host delegations (resolve_host_symbol_raw to 0)
description:
## Goal
Eliminate every remaining resolve_host_symbol_raw call across the ABI crate (except host_resolve.rs which IS the resolver infrastructure), bringing FrankenLibC to zero host libc runtime dependencies for its classified symbol surface.

## Background
As of commit d974b43, 64 host delegations were eliminated (57 from unistd_abi.rs, 6 from rpc_abi.rs, 1 from glibc_internal_abi.rs). Code audit reveals 31 remaining calls across 7 files (excluding host_resolve.rs):

### Remaining by file (31 total, verified by code audit)
| File | Calls | Unique Symbols | Category |
|------|-------|---------------|----------|
| io_internal_abi.rs | 7 | 3 (_IO_list_all, _IO_file_jumps, _IO_wfile_jumps) | glibc stream internals |
| setjmp_abi.rs | 6 | 4 (setjmp, _setjmp, __sigsetjmp, longjmp/siglongjmp) | register save/restore |
| stdio_abi.rs | 5 | 5 (stdin/stdout/stderr, setvbuf, host fn cache) | host FILE* bootstrap |
| pthread_abi.rs | 5 | 5 (getattr_np, cond_clockwait, timedjoin, tryjoin, clockjoin) | pthread extensions |
| dlfcn_abi.rs | 4 | 3 (dlopen x2, dlsym, dlclose) | dynamic loader |
| stdlib_abi.rs | 3 | 3 (setenv, unsetenv, putenv) | environ array |
| resolv_abi.rs | 2 | 2 (getaddrinfo, freeaddrinfo) | DNS resolution |

Note: host_resolve.rs has 3 calls but is the resolver infrastructure itself — not a promotion target.

### Two categories of remaining delegations
**Category A — Intentional Interpose Delegations (18 calls):**
These delegate to host ONLY for objects the host created (non-managed). Native paths already work for FrankenLibC-managed objects. Correct for LD_PRELOAD mode; dead code in replace mode.
- pthread_abi.rs: 5 (all conditional on !is_managed_*)
- dlfcn_abi.rs: 3 (dlsym/dlclose for host-opened handles)
- stdio_abi.rs: 2 (setvbuf + host fn cache for non-registry FILE*)
- stdlib_abi.rs: 3 (prefer host to avoid environ ownership conflict)

**Category B — Genuinely Missing Native Implementations (13 calls):**
These need new code — the host delegation is the primary/only path.
- setjmp_abi.rs: 6 (UNCONDITIONAL — always delegates, needs assembly)
- io_internal_abi.rs: 7 (bootstrap host glibc _IO_* structures)
- stdio_abi.rs: 3 (stdin/stdout/stderr global resolution)
- resolv_abi.rs: 1 (getaddrinfo DNS fallback — /etc/hosts already native)
- dlfcn_abi.rs: 1 (dlopen bootstrap passthrough)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Zero resolve_host_symbol_raw calls in ABI crate except host_resolve.rs
- All existing tests pass (156 lib + 113 unistd + 88 stdio + 35 rpc + 21 dlfcn + 21 setjmp + 163 pthread + all others)
- Full workspace clippy clean
- Each sub-bead includes: unit tests, e2e script, structured logging, verification commands
- Category A beads may be deferred to replace-mode milestone if interpose behavior is correct

Host delegations reduced from ~102 to ~8 (5 intentional dlfcn interpose + 3 host_resolve infrastructure). LD_PRELOAD smoke: 58/0/6.

title: Promote pthread extension APIs to native futex/syscall (5 delegations)
description:
## Goal
Classify 5 pthread host delegations as intentional interpose behavior and ensure native paths are robust.

## Classification: INTENTIONAL INTERPOSE DELEGATIONS
All 5 delegations are CONDITIONAL — they only fire for non-managed (glibc-created) objects. For FrankenLibC-managed objects, native paths already exist and work via futex/syscall. This is correct LD_PRELOAD behavior.

### Current code structure (verified by audit)
1. pthread_getattr_np (line 3658): delegates for non-managed threads; native path reads /proc/self/task/[tid] for managed threads
2. pthread_cond_clockwait (line 5185): delegates for non-managed condvars; native path uses futex with clock conversion for managed condvars
3. pthread_timedjoin_np (line 5237): delegates for non-managed threads; native path uses futex-based timed wait for managed threads
4. pthread_tryjoin_np (line 5332): delegates for non-managed threads; native path checks managed thread state atomically
5. pthread_clockjoin_np (line 5401): delegates for non-managed threads; native path converts clock and delegates to timedjoin

### What needs to happen
Phase 1 (this bead): Verify native paths are complete and correct. Add comprehensive tests. Add FORCE_NATIVE_THREADING/FORCE_NATIVE_MUTEX e2e coverage. Document the intentional delegation pattern.
Phase 2 (replace-mode milestone): When FrankenLibC owns all thread creation, non-managed paths become dead code. Remove host delegation at that point.

## Implementation tasks
1. Add unit tests for each extension API on managed objects (native path exercised)
2. Add e2e test script that sets FORCE_NATIVE_THREADING=1 and exercises all 5 APIs without host delegation
3. Add a guard assertion: if FORCE_NATIVE_THREADING is set, resolve_host_symbol_raw must never be reached (add debug_assert or metric)
4. Update support_matrix classification for these 5 symbols to Implemented (native path) with interpose note

## Testing requirements
- Unit tests: nominal + edge cases for each API (timeout=0, timeout=past, invalid args, EINVAL paths)
- e2e script: scripts/check_pthread_extensions_native.sh exercising all 5 with FORCE_NATIVE_THREADING=1
- Structured log fields: trace_id, api_family=pthread, symbol, mode (native vs host), decision_path, errno, latency_ns
- Verify: cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test pthread_abi_test (all 163 tests pass)

title: Implement native setjmp/longjmp via x86_64 inline assembly (6 calls)
description:
## Goal
Eliminate 6 UNCONDITIONAL host delegations in setjmp_abi.rs by implementing setjmp/longjmp via x86_64 assembly.

## Classification: GENUINELY MISSING NATIVE IMPLEMENTATION
All 6 calls are UNCONDITIONAL — they always prefer host, falling back to a managed capture/restore_entrypoint that does NOT actually save/restore CPU registers. The native fallback uses a cooperative unwinding approach that works for simple cases but is NOT ABI-compatible with C programs that expect real register save/restore.

### Current code structure (verified by audit)
1. setjmp → resolve "setjmp" → fallback: capture_entrypoint()
2. _setjmp → resolve "_setjmp" → fallback: capture_entrypoint()
3. sigsetjmp → resolve "__sigsetjmp" → fallback: capture_entrypoint() with savemask
4. longjmp → resolve "longjmp" → fallback: restore_entrypoint()
5. _longjmp → resolve "longjmp" → fallback: restore_entrypoint()
6. siglongjmp → resolve "siglongjmp" → fallback: resolve "longjmp" → fallback: restore_entrypoint() with mask restore

### Why assembly is required
setjmp/longjmp save and restore CPU registers (callee-saved: rbx, rbp, r12-r15, rsp, rip on x86_64). The compiler cannot generate this code because it would clobber the registers it needs to save. This MUST be written in assembly.

### Implementation plan
1. Write x86_64 __sigsetjmp in global_asm! or naked fn with #[naked]:
   - Save rbx, rbp, r12-r15 to jmp_buf[0..6]
   - Save rsp to jmp_buf[7] (adjusted for return address)
   - Save return address (from stack) to jmp_buf[8]
   - If savemask != 0: call SYS_rt_sigprocmask(SIG_BLOCK, null, &jmp_buf[9], 8) to save signal mask
   - Return 0

2. Write x86_64 __longjmp in global_asm!:
   - Restore rbx, rbp, r12-r15 from jmp_buf[0..6]
   - Restore rsp from jmp_buf[7]
   - If signal mask was saved: call SYS_rt_sigprocmask(SIG_SETMASK, &jmp_buf[9], null, 8) to restore
   - Set return value to val (or 1 if val==0, per POSIX)
   - Jump to saved return address

3. Wire ABI entries:
   - setjmp(env) → __sigsetjmp(env, 1)
   - _setjmp(env) → __sigsetjmp(env, 0)
   - sigsetjmp(env, savemask) → __sigsetjmp(env, savemask)
   - longjmp(env, val) → __longjmp(env, val)
   - _longjmp(env, val) → __longjmp(env, val)
   - siglongjmp(env, val) → __longjmp(env, val)

### jmp_buf ABI compatibility under LD_PRELOAD
Under LD_PRELOAD, our setjmp/longjmp symbols shadow glibc's. A C program calls OUR setjmp and OUR longjmp, so our jmp_buf layout only needs to be self-consistent. We do NOT need to match glibc's PTR_MANGLE layout. However, the jmp_buf SIZE must be >= sizeof(jmp_buf) from glibc (200 bytes on x86_64) since programs allocate jmp_buf on stack using glibc's header definition.

### Risks
- Inline assembly correctness is critical — register save/restore bugs cause silent corruption or crashes
- Must handle setjmp called from signal handlers correctly
- Must not clobber the red zone (128 bytes below rsp on x86_64 SysV ABI)
- The rsp save must account for the call instruction's push of the return address

## Testing requirements
- Unit tests: setjmp returns 0, longjmp returns nonzero val, val=0 returns 1
- Unit tests: nested setjmp (two buffers, longjmp to each)
- Unit tests: signal mask save/restore (sigsetjmp with savemask=1, verify mask round-trips)
- Unit tests: _setjmp does NOT save signal mask, _longjmp does NOT restore it
- e2e script: scripts/check_setjmp_native.sh with multi-level longjmp + signal mask tests
- Structured log fields: trace_id, symbol, savemask, register_snapshot_hash
- Verify: cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test setjmp_abi_test (all 21 tests pass)
- Verify: LD_PRELOAD smoke with programs that use setjmp (error recovery paths)
close_reason: All 3 children closed by SunnyBear: bd-zh1y.2.1 (sigsetjmp asm), bd-zh1y.2.2 (longjmp asm), bd-zh1y.2.3 (host delegation removal). Native x86_64 setjmp/longjmp fully operational.

If savemask arg is nonzero, call SYS_rt_sigprocmask to save current signal mask. jmp_buf layout: 8 registers x 8 bytes = 64 bytes for regs, then 128 bytes for sigset_t. setjmp = __sigsetjmp(env,1), _setjmp = __sigsetjmp(env,0). Return 0 on direct call.

title: Build native FILE struct and stream vtable to replace _IO_* host interop (7 calls)
description:
## Goal
Eliminate 7 host delegations in io_internal_abi.rs by building a native FILE struct, stream vtable, and stream registry to replace glibc _IO_* interop.

## Classification: GENUINELY MISSING — requires architectural work
All 7 calls resolve glibc's internal _IO_list_all (stream linked list), _IO_file_jumps (file vtable), and _IO_wfile_jumps (wide-char vtable). These are used by two functions:
- bootstrap_host_libio_exports() — called once at init to copy host glibc _IO structures
- _IO_list_all_get/_IO_file_jumps_get/_IO_wfile_jumps_get — runtime accessors for cached host structures

### Current code structure (verified by audit)
| Line | Symbol | Function | Condition |
|------|--------|----------|-----------|
| 61 | dynamic (param) | copy_host_object() | conditional |
| 76 | _IO_list_all | bootstrap_host_libio_exports() | conditional |
| 84 | _IO_file_jumps | bootstrap_host_libio_exports() | conditional |
| 97 | _IO_wfile_jumps | bootstrap_host_libio_exports() | conditional |
| 129 | _IO_list_all | _IO_list_all_get() | conditional (cache) |
| 151 | _IO_file_jumps | _IO_file_jumps_get() | conditional (cache) |
| 175 | _IO_wfile_jumps | _IO_wfile_jumps_get() | conditional (cache) |

### Why this is the hardest elimination target
glibc's stdio implementation uses _IO_list_all as a linked list of all open FILE* streams. When a program calls fflush(NULL), glibc walks this list. When a program exits, glibc flushes/closes all streams via this list. FrankenLibC currently hooks into this list to make its streams visible to glibc's cleanup.

Eliminating this requires FrankenLibC to:
1. Own the entire FILE lifecycle (open → buffer → read/write → flush → close)
2. Own the stream registry (replacement for _IO_list_all)
3. Own the stream vtable (replacement for _IO_file_jumps)
4. Handle atexit/exit flushing without glibc's help

### Dependencies
- stdio_abi.rs delegations (stdin/stdout/stderr, setvbuf) depend on this work
- bd-3rnx (Complete stdio host FILE* delegation) is the broader epic

### Risks
- This is the single largest architectural change remaining
- Incorrect FILE buffering causes silent data loss (writes never flushed)
- Programs that mix FrankenLibC stdio with direct glibc calls need coherent state
- stdout line-buffering vs full-buffering must match expectations (affects every program that prints)
- Exit-time flushing (atexit handlers) must work before process teardown
- Thread safety of the stream registry (concurrent fopen/fclose from multiple threads)

## Testing requirements
- Unit tests: FILE lifecycle (fopen → fwrite → fflush → fclose), verify data written
- Unit tests: fflush(NULL) flushes all open streams
- Unit tests: setvbuf modes (_IONBF, _IOLBF, _IOFBF) affect buffering correctly
- Unit tests: concurrent fopen/fclose from multiple threads (no UB, no leaks)
- Unit tests: stdin/stdout/stderr are pre-registered and functional from process start
- Unit tests: line-buffered stdout flushes on newline
- Unit tests: exit-time flush (atexit handler registered, streams flushed before exit)
- e2e script: scripts/check_native_stdio_file.sh
  - Build libfrankenlibc_abi.so in release mode
  - Run echo/cat/ls/sort/git under LD_PRELOAD, capture stdout, verify output matches non-preload
  - Test with FRANKENLIBC_MODE=strict and FRANKENLIBC_MODE=hardened
- Structured log fields: trace_id, api_family=stdio, symbol, stream_id, buffer_state, bytes_written, flush_reason
- Verify: cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test stdio_abi_test (88+ tests pass)
- Verify: cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test io_abi_test (39 tests pass)
- Verify: zero resolve_host_symbol_raw in io_internal_abi.rs after promotion
close_reason: All 4 children closed: bd-zh1y.3.1 (NativeFile struct), bd-zh1y.3.2 (stream vtable), bd-zh1y.3.3 (stream registry), bd-zh1y.3.4 (host resolution removal). Native FILE struct, vtable, and stream registry replace _IO_* host interop. Zero resolve_host_symbol_raw in io_internal_abi.rs. LD_PRELOAD smoke passes.

title: Promote stdio stdin/stdout/stderr and setvbuf to native FILE (5 delegations)
description:
## Goal
Eliminate 5 host delegations in stdio_abi.rs by owning stdin/stdout/stderr globals and removing host function cache.

## Classification: MIXED
- 3 calls are GENUINELY MISSING (stdin/stdout/stderr global resolution — Category B)
- 2 calls are INTENTIONAL INTERPOSE (setvbuf + host fn cache for non-registry FILE* — Category A)

### Current code structure (verified by audit)
| Line | Symbol | Function | Category |
|------|--------|----------|----------|
| 328 | dynamic (param) | host_stdio_symbol() cache | A — interpose |
| 587 | _IO_2_1_stdin_ | init_host_stdio_streams() | B — missing |
| 588 | _IO_2_1_stdout_ | init_host_stdio_streams() | B — missing |
| 589 | _IO_2_1_stderr_ | init_host_stdio_streams() | B — missing |
| 2001 | setvbuf | setvbuf() | A — interpose |

### Why stdin/stdout/stderr resolve from host
Currently, FrankenLibC's exported stdin/stdout/stderr pointers are set to glibc's internal _IO_2_1_stdin_ etc. This makes them real FILE* that glibc functions can operate on. Without this, any glibc function that touches stdin/stdout/stderr would crash.

### Implementation plan
BLOCKED BY bd-zh1y.3 (native FILE struct). Once we have native FILE:
1. Create static FrankenLibC-owned FILE structs for fd 0/1/2
2. Initialize buffer state: stderr=unbuffered, stdout=line-buffered if isatty(1), stdin=full-buffered
3. Export these as stdin/stdout/stderr globals
4. Native setvbuf: set buffer mode/size on our FILE struct
5. Remove host_stdio_symbol cache (no longer needed)

### Coordination
JadeOtter is currently working on stdio_abi.rs (bd-2vv.3.2 printf family). Coordinate to avoid conflicts.

## Testing requirements
- Unit tests: stdin/stdout/stderr are non-null at program start
- Unit tests: fprintf(stdout, ...) produces output to fd 1
- Unit tests: setvbuf(stdout, NULL, _IONBF, 0) makes stdout unbuffered
- Unit tests: setvbuf(stdout, buf, _IOFBF, 4096) switches to full buffering
- Unit tests: line-buffered stdout flushes on \n
- e2e script: scripts/check_native_stdio_globals.sh
  - Verify echo/printf/puts produce correct output under LD_PRELOAD
  - Verify stderr output appears immediately (unbuffered)
  - Compare output of 10+ common programs with and without LD_PRELOAD
- Structured log fields: trace_id, api_family=stdio, symbol, stream (stdin/stdout/stderr/other), buffer_mode
- Verify: all stdio_abi_test tests pass
- Verify: zero resolve_host_symbol_raw in stdio_abi.rs

Exported stdin/stdout/stderr now publish FrankenLibC-owned NativeFile pointers; standard-stream FILE* values canonicalize back to stdio registry keys across stdio entrypoints; native setvbuf path synchronizes NativeFile buffering metadata; printf/vprintf raw-stdout leak removed; stdio_abi.rs now contains zero resolve_host_symbol_raw references.
