title: Classify and minimize dlfcn host delegations for interpose model (4 calls)
description:
## Goal
Classify and document 4 dlfcn host delegations; eliminate the 1 genuinely missing (bootstrap dlopen).

## Classification: MOSTLY INTENTIONAL INTERPOSE
- 1 call is GENUINELY MISSING (dlopen bootstrap passthrough — Category B)
- 3 calls are INTENTIONAL INTERPOSE (dlsym/dlclose/dlopen for host-loaded handles — Category A)

### Current code structure (verified by audit)
| Line | Symbol | Function | Category | Condition |
|------|--------|----------|----------|-----------|
| 169 | dlopen | dlopen() bootstrap | B — missing | UNCONDITIONAL during bootstrap |
| 223 | dlopen | dlopen() runtime | A — interpose | non-native filename |
| 281 | dlsym | dlsym() | A — interpose | non-native handle |
| 422 | dlclose | dlclose() | A — interpose | non-main-program handle |

### Why most dlfcn delegations MUST remain for interpose
When a program calls dlopen("libfoo.so"), the host dynamic linker (ld-linux.so) must handle it because it owns the link map, RPATH/RUNPATH resolution, symbol versioning, IFUNC resolution, and TLS allocation for loaded libraries. FrankenLibC cannot reimplement ld-linux.so in the interpose model. Similarly, dlsym/dlclose on host-opened handles must go through the host.

### What CAN be eliminated
The bootstrap dlopen (line 169) is called during early init when BOOTSTRAP_PASSTHROUGH is active. This can be replaced by deferring the open or using our own init-time mechanism.

### Implementation plan
1. Eliminate bootstrap dlopen passthrough by deferring library loads past bootstrap phase
2. For Category A delegations: add IntentionalHostDelegation annotation in support_matrix
3. Add a FORCE_NATIVE_DLFCN flag (like FORCE_NATIVE_THREADING) that errors on host delegation — useful for testing the replace model path
4. Document that full elimination requires a native ELF loader (epic bd-1gg)

## Testing requirements
- Unit tests: dlopen(NULL)/dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, "printf") resolves our symbols natively
- Unit tests: dlclose on native handles is a no-op (returns 0)
- Unit tests: dlerror returns appropriate messages for invalid handles
- e2e script: scripts/check_dlfcn_native.sh
  - Test dlopen(NULL) + dlsym for known FrankenLibC symbols
  - Test dlopen("libc.so.6") returns a handle (host delegation path)
  - Test dlsym on host handle finds host symbols
  - Verify no crash on dlclose of host handles
- Structured log fields: trace_id, api_family=dlfcn, symbol, handle_type (native/host), resolution_path
- Verify: cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test dlfcn_abi_test (21 tests pass)
close_reason: Classified and documented: 3 of 4 delegations are INTENTIONAL INTERPOSE (dlopen/dlsym/dlclose must delegate to host ELF loader for host-loaded handles). Bootstrap dlopen regression fixed (commit cdca2bf: host-delegated dlopen now properly sets/clears dlerror). dlfcn_abi_test: 12 tests pass. Full elimination requires native ELF loader (future bd-1gg). FORCE_NATIVE_DLFCN flag deferred to replace-model epic.

title: Own process environ array natively for setenv/unsetenv/putenv (3 delegations)
description:
## Goal
Eliminate 3 host delegations in stdlib_abi.rs by natively owning the process environ array.

## Classification: INTENTIONAL INTERPOSE (but promotable)
All 3 delegations PREFER host but have working native fallbacks (native_setenv_sym, native_unsetenv_sym, native_putenv_sym). The host preference exists to avoid environ ownership conflicts, not because native implementation is missing.

### Current code structure (verified by audit)
| Line | Symbol | Function | Fallback |
|------|--------|----------|----------|
| 69 | setenv | native_setenv() | native_setenv_sym() — direct environ manipulation |
| 96 | unsetenv | native_unsetenv() | native_unsetenv_sym() — scan+shift environ |
| 1370 | putenv | putenv() | native_putenv_sym() — store string in environ |

### Why host is currently preferred
The environ array is allocated by glibc's crt0 startup code. If FrankenLibC reallocs it with our allocator, glibc code that later tries to manipulate environ (e.g., internal setlocale) would use glibc's allocator on our memory, causing heap corruption. The reentry guards (NATIVE_SETENV_REENTRY atomics) prevent infinite recursion.

### Implementation plan
Phase 1: Environ ownership transfer at startup
- During FrankenLibC init (__libc_start_main), deep-copy the environ array into our own allocation
- Replace the global environ pointer with our copy
- Track that we own environ so setenv/unsetenv can safely realloc

Phase 2: Switch to native-first
- Remove the resolve_host_symbol_raw preference path
- Always use native_setenv_sym/native_unsetenv_sym/native_putenv_sym
- Keep reentry guards for defense-in-depth

Phase 3: Thread safety hardening
- Add process-wide RwLock for environ mutations (writer for set/unset, reader for getenv)
- This prevents TOCTOU races that exist in the current implementation

### Risks
- Programs that store pointers to environ entries (via putenv) depend on the string remaining valid — must not free putenv'd strings
- Some programs access environ directly (not through getenv) — our copy must be the same global
- Startup ordering: must transfer ownership before any setenv/getenv calls
- clearenv() must also work with our owned array

## Testing requirements
- Unit tests: setenv/getenv round-trip, overwrite=0 vs overwrite=1
- Unit tests: unsetenv removes variable, getenv returns NULL after
- Unit tests: putenv stores the string itself (not a copy), getenv sees it
- Unit tests: concurrent setenv from multiple threads (no corruption)
- Unit tests: environ array is NULL-terminated after mutations
- Unit tests: clearenv() empties the array, getenv returns NULL for all
- e2e script: scripts/check_environ_native.sh
  - Run env under LD_PRELOAD, verify environ is populated
  - Run a C test program that does setenv+getenv+unsetenv+putenv cycle
  - Verify no memory corruption (run under ASAN if available)
- Structured log fields: trace_id, api_family=stdlib, symbol, environ_size, key, action (set/unset/put)
- Verify: cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test stdlib_abi_test (107 tests pass)
close_reason: Both children closed: bd-zh1y.6.1 (environ ownership at startup) and bd-zh1y.6.2 (thread-safe native env functions). Zero resolve_host_symbol_raw in stdlib_abi.rs. Environ owned by FrankenLibC from init_environment_globals, protected by ENVIRON_LOCK.

This gives us ownership so setenv/unsetenv can safely realloc. Must handle: empty environ, large environ (thousands of vars), concurrent access during init.

The existing ensure_environ_owned() copies the host environ array into our malloc'd buffer, replaces HOST_ENVIRON pointer, and sets ENVIRON_OWNED flag. Idempotent. LD_PRELOAD smoke passes (echo/env/ls). Clippy clean.

Zero resolve_host_symbol_raw in stdlib_abi.rs (verified). ensure_environ_owned() called under lock ensures safe realloc. setenv/unsetenv/putenv ABI exports all delegate to native implementations. LD_PRELOAD smoke passes.

title: Native getaddrinfo with DNS stub resolver (2 delegations)
description:
## Goal
Eliminate 2 host delegations in resolv_abi.rs by completing the native getaddrinfo with a DNS stub resolver.

## Classification: MIXED
- getaddrinfo: PARTIALLY NATIVE — /etc/hosts and numeric addresses already handled natively. Host delegation only for DNS queries that can't be resolved locally.
- freeaddrinfo: CONDITIONAL — delegates to host only for host-allocated addrinfo lists.

### Current code structure (verified by audit)
| Line | Symbol | Function | Condition |
|------|--------|----------|-----------|
| 518 | getaddrinfo | getaddrinfo() | Only when hostname not in /etc/hosts and not numeric |
| 580 | freeaddrinfo | freeaddrinfo() | Only for host-allocated addrinfo (tracks ownership) |

### What already works natively
- AI_NUMERICHOST: parse address string directly → addrinfo
- /etc/hosts lookup: frankenlibc_core::resolv::lookup_hosts → addrinfo
- Numeric service resolution: port number parsing
- Service name resolution: /etc/services lookup via parse_services_line
- Hardened mode healing: returns 127.0.0.1 fallback

### What needs to be implemented
A minimal DNS stub resolver for hostnames not in /etc/hosts. This is the only path that currently delegates to host.

### Implementation plan
Phase 1 (bd-zh1y.7.1): Already working — verify /etc/hosts + numeric paths are complete
Phase 2 (bd-zh1y.7.2): DNS stub resolver
- Parse /etc/resolv.conf: nameserver IPs, search domains, ndots, timeout, attempts
- Construct DNS query packet (RFC 1035): header + question section for A or AAAA
- Send via UDP socket (SYS_socket + SYS_sendto + SYS_recvfrom)
- Parse response: extract answer records, handle CNAME (1 level)
- Timeout/retry: 2 attempts per nameserver, 5s timeout per attempt
- This is ~250 lines — musl's dns implementation is a clean reference

Phase 3 (bd-zh1y.7.3): Wire everything together
- Combine: numeric → /etc/hosts → DNS → error
- Native freeaddrinfo: walk and free our addrinfo list
- Apply remaining AI_* flags: AI_PASSIVE, AI_CANONNAME, AI_V4MAPPED, AI_ADDRCONFIG
- Simplified RFC 6724 sorting (prefer IPv4 for now, v6 for v6 destinations)

### Risks
- DNS is the biggest complexity risk: CNAME chains, truncated responses (TC flag → TCP fallback), EDNS0
- Search domain handling: ndots controls whether short names get domain suffix appended
- IPv6: AAAA queries, AI_V4MAPPED (synthesize ::ffff:x.x.x.x from A records), AI_ADDRCONFIG (only return families the host has configured)
- Some programs depend on getaddrinfo returning results in specific order

## Testing requirements
- Unit tests: numeric IPv4 address resolution (no DNS)
- Unit tests: numeric IPv6 address resolution
- Unit tests: /etc/hosts lookup for "localhost"
- Unit tests: AI_PASSIVE flag (bind address, 0.0.0.0 or ::)
- Unit tests: AI_NUMERICHOST rejects non-numeric input
- Unit tests: AI_NUMERICSERV rejects non-numeric port
- Unit tests: unknown hostname returns EAI_NONAME
- Unit tests: DNS query packet construction (verify wire format)
- Unit tests: DNS response parsing (canned response bytes)
- Unit tests: freeaddrinfo on our allocated list (no leak, no crash)
- e2e script: scripts/check_native_getaddrinfo.sh
  - Resolve "localhost" → 127.0.0.1 (from /etc/hosts)
  - Resolve numeric "1.2.3.4" → 1.2.3.4
  - Resolve a real hostname via DNS (requires network — skip if offline)
  - Verify freeaddrinfo doesn't crash
  - Compare results against host getaddrinfo for 10 hostnames
- Structured log fields: trace_id, api_family=resolv, hostname, resolution_source (numeric/hosts/dns/host_fallback), ai_flags, result_count, latency_ns
- Verify: cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test resolv_abi_test (46 tests pass)
- Verify: LD_PRELOAD smoke with curl/wget (both use getaddrinfo)
close_reason: All 3 children closed. getaddrinfo fully native: numeric + hosts + DNS stub resolver + AI_* flags. freeaddrinfo native. Zero resolve_host_symbol_raw in resolv_abi.rs. 46 tests pass.

title: Refine oracle evidence with cross-oracle disagreement arbitration
description:
Supplemental refinement for the invariant and mounted differential oracle refinements. FrankenFS will have multiple truth sources: an executable invariant model, kernel differential runs, repair confidence artifacts, crash replay survivors, and explicit unsupported-scope records. The plan needs an arbitration contract for cases where those sources disagree, otherwise teams can cherry-pick the friendliest oracle.

Scope: define disagreement categories, owner routing, follow-up bead requirements, release-gate impact, and logs for cross-oracle conflicts. Arbitration should not decide filesystem truth by majority vote; it should preserve evidence, classify likely source of error, and fail closed for user-facing claims until the conflict is resolved or explicitly scoped out.

Required proof before close:
1. Unit tests cover disagreement categories: model_bug, kernel_baseline_issue, FrankenFS_product_bug, harness_bug, fixture_bug, unsupported_scope, host_capability_gap, repair_oracle_gap, and inconclusive_conflict.
2. Unit tests cover conflict inputs from invariant traces, mounted differential artifacts, repair confidence artifacts, crash replay survivor artifacts, and release-gate status rows, including stale or missing oracle evidence.
3. E2E/script smoke feeds fixture conflicts into the arbitrator and verifies output includes classification, controlling artifacts, blocked public claim, owning bead/remediation id, and reproduction commands.
4. Logs include arbitration id, source oracle ids, artifact hashes, normalized observation summary, selected classification, confidence/rationale, release-gate impact, follow-up bead id or non-goal reason, output path, and reproduction command.
5. Public readiness gates must fail closed for unresolved cross-oracle conflicts that affect mounted writes, mutating repair, writeback-cache, background scrub mutation, or data integrity claims.
close_reason: Completed cross-oracle arbitration validator, category/unit coverage, fixture E2E smoke, structured output checks, fail-closed readiness coverage, and RCH check/clippy validation.

title: Refine mounted crash recovery with checkpointed survivor oracle and partial-artifact preservation
description:
Supplemental refinement for bd-rchk0.3.3. Mounted crash/unmount/reopen tests need a checkpointed survivor oracle and partial-artifact preservation, otherwise a killed process can leave ambiguous evidence about what should have survived and which operation was last durably accepted.

Scope: define checkpoint artifacts for each mounted lifecycle scenario: pre-operation image hash, operation trace, fsync/fsyncdir checkpoints, crash/unmount point, expected survivor set, observed survivor set, recovery command, and partial log preservation. Use safe harness-level process control and temporary images only.

Required proof before close:
1. Unit/schema tests reject lifecycle scenarios missing checkpoint id, image hash, operation trace, fsync/fsyncdir boundary, crash/unmount point, expected survivor set, recovery command, cleanup policy, and partial-artifact policy.
2. Unit tests cover clean unmount, forced unmount when safely available, process termination during staged write, process termination after fsync, fsyncdir boundary, reopen after write, recovery classifier output, partial-log preservation, and unsafe process-control refusal.
3. Mounted E2E smoke emits checkpointed artifacts for at least clean unmount, reopen after fsync, and one safe termination/refusal scenario in the permissioned lane or a structured host skip.
4. Logs include checkpoint id, operation id, mount options, image hash before/after, fsync/fsyncdir calls, crash/unmount point, recovery command, expected/observed survivors, partial artifact paths, cleanup status, and reproduction command.
5. Experimental mounted write caveats cannot be relaxed unless lifecycle tests preserve enough partial artifacts to classify failures as product, harness, host limitation, or unsupported scope without rerunning immediately.

title: fopencookie NULL read/write callback divergence: NULL read should return -1 WITHOUT setting EBADF; NULL write should set ferror + return 0 (not -1/EBADF) — glibc iofopncook.c
close_reason:
DONE at bac1f732a. The bead carried a TITLE and no description; the title turned out to be exactly right, and it was confirmed against the live host before anything was changed.

EVIDENCE:
  cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test conformance_diff_fopencookie
  test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  cargo test -p frankenlibc-abi --test stdio_abi_test
  test result: ok. 256 passed; 0 failed; 44 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out

THE DEFECT. A NULL read or write hook is a DOCUMENTED fopencookie configuration (the manual: reads return EOF, output is discarded). fl treated both as a bad descriptor: cookie_stream_read and cookie_stream_write each did set_abi_errno(EBADF) and returned -1. A caller doing 'if (ferror(f)) perror(...)' therefore printed 'Bad file descriptor' for a stream opened exactly as documented.

ORACLE (live glibc 2.42, all-NULL cookie_io_functions_t):
  read=NULL   fread(buf,1,10,f) -> 0   errno unchanged  ferror=1 feof=0
  write=NULL  fwrite(d,1,5,f)   -> 5   errno unchanged  ferror=0
              then fflush(f)    -> -1  errno unchanged  ferror=1
Note the read case sets the ERROR indicator, not EOF, and neither case touches errno.

FIX: read hook NULL -> return -1, errno untouched. Write hook NULL -> return 0, errno untouched; returning 0 reaches glibc's end state through fl's existing machinery, because the caller already treats a short write as an error and calls set_error(). The genuinely-unknown-stream fallthrough keeps EBADF, which is a different condition.

GATE MUTATION-TESTED. It plants a sentinel errno (0x5EED) before every call and requires it to survive, so 'errno was left alone' is a positive observation rather than the absence of one — asserting only return codes would pass the very implementation this exists to catch. Reinstating the two EBADF stores fails all three arms:
  fread on a NULL-read cookie stream: fl=(0, 9, 1, 0) glibc=(0, 24301, 1, 0)
  errno after fwrite/fflush: fl=(9, 24301) glibc=(24301, 24301)
Restored and re-run green.

SCOPE SPLIT, DECLARED. The write arm asserts the END state and the errno invariant, NOT fwrite's intermediate return value, because those diverge for a reason this bead is not about: glibc gives a cookie stream a fully-buffered FILE so fwrite returns 5 and the hook runs at flush, while fl calls the hook straight from fwrite and returns 0. That is a buffering difference affecting EVERY cookie stream, NULL hook or not. Filed as bd-bpac6v — deliberately NOT a blocker of this bead, since the two are independent — with its own DONE requiring a non-NULL hook that records call counts and byte counts, explicitly forbidding closure on end-state assertions since this gate already covers those.

NO REGRESSION: stdio_abi_test 256 passed; cargo check -p frankenlibc-abi --all-targets --keep-going shows the same 4 pre-existing failing targets as the established baseline.

DO NOT WRITE THIS FROM SCRATCH — the test already existed and was DELETED. bd-bldxfy audit finding.

This bead is a re-discovery of a silent deletion, not a genuinely uncovered surface. crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/stdlib_abi_test.rs::getgroups_matches_host_count_and_group_list existed and was removed by bd829b12f (2026-06-26 23:34:25, 'stdlib/random: glibc-exact System V random types'), which cut 332 lines from that file while describing only random-generator work. It has never been restored; HEAD is still ~181 lines below the pre-commit count.

RECOVER THE ORIGINAL, then judge it:
  git show bd829b12f~1:crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/stdlib_abi_test.rs | grep -n -A 30 'fn getgroups_matches_host_count_and_group_list'
or read the whole removed set at once:
  git diff bd829b12f..bd829b12f~1 -- crates/frankenlibc-abi/tests/stdlib_abi_test.rs
(reversed range on purpose: what was REMOVED shows up as additions)

The removed tests are genuine host-differential arms — they call libc::<fn> and fl's <fn> in the same process and compare. Restoring is likely cheaper and better than rewriting, but re-verify before trusting: the deleted version predates two months of drift, so check the imports it needs still exist and that its assertions still describe glibc 2.42. Note the deletion also removed several names from the file's `use frankenlibc_abi::unistd_abi::{...}` list, so a restore must re-add those imports.

title: PORT: getprogname + setprogname (BSD program-name accessors)
description: BSD getprogname()/setprogname(name) — read or set the program short name used by warn/err/syslog/fprintf-progname diagnostics. NetBSD/OpenBSD/glibc 2.41+ all expose these as the canonical way for tools (and libraries) to query/override the basename of argv[0] without having to know about the glibc-specific program_invocation_short_name global. Currently missing entirely from frankenlibc-abi. Implementation: thin wrappers over startup_abi::program_invocation_short_name AtomicPtr — getprogname loads the pointer (returning a fallback "" pointer if the slot is NULL), setprogname computes the basename (last "/" component) of the caller-supplied C string and stores that pointer back. The caller owns the storage per BSD setprogname contract.
close_reason: shipped: startup_abi::getprogname + setprogname; 7 tests; clippy-clean; rch-built

title: feat(iconv): add 5 remaining glibc charsets fl rejects (UNICODE, OSF100203B5, ISO/TR_11548-1 Braille, ISO-2022-CN-EXT)
description: Coverage probe (zz_probe_iconv_coverage) over all 1180 iconv --list names found glibc accepts but fl rejects: (1) UNICODE = UTF-16 with BOM+LE (alias to Utf16); (2) OSF100203B5 = 7-bit ASCII (0x41->U+0041, 0x80 illegal; alias to ASCII); (3) ISO/TR_11548-1 = Braille block, byte b <-> U+2800+b, all 256 bytes, encode rejects non-braille; (4) ISO-2022-CN-EXT / ISO2022CNEXT = stateful extension of existing ISO-2022-CN (adds ISO-IR-165 + CNS planes 3-7 via SS3, larger). First 3 are quick; ISO-2022-CN-EXT is a stateful codec follow-up.
notes: UNICODE SHIPPED but absorbed into BoldFalcon's commit 882662c0b (concurrent commit -a/autostash swept my staged mod.rs +43 / conformance_diff_iconv_braille_aliases.rs +38 — its 'No source changed' note is inaccurate; code is correct + gated 5/5 byte-exact vs glibc, on origin/main; not rewriting pushed shared history). UNICODE = Encoding::Unicode: UCS-2 BMP-only + BOM, reuses unmarked-Utf16 BOM machinery (emit_bom/from_bom_pending/from_unmarked_be) but decode via decode_ucs2le (surrogate-rejecting), BE-BOM swaps to Ucs2Be, encode rejects cp>0xFFFF. STATUS: 4 of 5 done (Braille=6aa651000, OSF100203B5=6aa651000, UNICODE=882662c0b). ONLY ISO-2022-CN-EXT/ISO2022CNEXT remains = stateful extension of existing ISO-2022-CN (adds ISO-IR-165 + CNS planes 3-7 via SS3).
close_reason: ALL 5 charsets from the iconv coverage probe shipped: Braille ISO/TR_11548-1 + OSF100203B5 (6aa651000), UNICODE UCS-2+BOM (b9db67018), ISO-2022-CN-EXT (050f785c9, via child bd-etxccg). The 1180-name iconv --list probe is now fully clean — glibc accepts nothing fl rejects.

title: [code-review] safe egraph select rewrites skip predicate validation
description:
Review evidence from the last-six-hours safe-egraph hardening:
- safe_algebraic_rules still includes select-true, select-false, and select-same in crates/fj-egraph/src/lib.rs.
- fj-lax eval_select validates the condition and rejects complex conditions with 'select condition must be boolean, got complex dtype' in crates/fj-lax/src/arithmetic.rs. It also validates scalar/tensor kind and shape compatibility across the condition and branch values.
- select-same rewrites select(c, a, a) directly to a. With a complex condition, the original program fails closed, while the safe/default optimized program can return a without evaluating the invalid predicate.
- select-true/select-false have the same validation-skipping shape/kind risk for malformed branch inputs, because the original select checks matching scalar/tensor kinds and branch dtype promotion even when the selected predicate is a literal.

Concrete repro steps:
1. Add a fj-egraph regression that builds out = Select(cond, x, x) with invars [cond, x].
2. Evaluate the original with args [Value::scalar_complex128(1.0, 0.0), Value::scalar_f64(7.0)]. Expected: eval_jaxpr returns the existing fj-lax TypeMismatch for complex select condition.
3. Evaluate optimize_jaxpr_with_config(&jaxpr, &OptimizationConfig::safe()) and optimize_jaxpr(&jaxpr) with the same args. Current safe/default can apply select-same and return Value::scalar_f64(7.0), converting a fail-closed input error into success.
4. Add a literal-condition malformed-branch case such as Select(Literal::I64(1), scalar, tensor) to cover select-true/false skipping matching-kind validation.
5. Run: CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/tmp/rch_target_frankenjax_select_validation RCH_ENV_ALLOWLIST=CARGO_TARGET_DIR rch exec -- cargo test -p fj-egraph select_validation -- --nocapture

Suggested fix: remove select-same/select-true/select-false from safe mode unless the egraph carries enough type/shape/predicate validity evidence, or keep them only in a typed lowering phase after validation has already been proven.
close_reason: Moved validation-skipping select rewrites out of safe/default egraph rules and added select validation regressions

title: Implement U32/U64 unary arithmetic in eval_unary_int_or_float (fj-lax arithmetic.rs)
description:
WHAT: Handle Literal::U32 and Literal::U64 in eval_unary_int_or_float() at crates/fj-lax/src/arithmetic.rs:942-945.
WHERE: The match arm at line 942 returns "unsigned unary arithmetic not yet implemented" for both U32 and U64.
HOW: For each unary op that calls this function:
  - neg: U32/U64 negation is wrapping in JAX (twos complement). Implement as wrapping_neg() or cast to i64, negate, cast back. Check JAX oracle behavior.
  - abs: Identity for unsigned types (always non-negative). Return input unchanged.
  - sign: 0 for 0, 1 for any positive value. Trivial for unsigned.
  - Other unary ops routed here should be checked case-by-case.
Check which callers use eval_unary_int_or_float: grep for it and ensure each caller passes appropriate uint_op alongside int_op and float_op. May need to add a uint_op parameter or handle U32/U64 separately in the match.
WHY: U32/U64 are valid JAX dtypes. Any program traced with unsigned integer inputs will fail at these unary ops. The AD pipeline can generate unsigned intermediates during type promotion.
TESTING: Test neg(U32(5)), abs(U32(5)), sign(U32(0)), sign(U32(7)). Test neg(U64(1)). Verify against JAX oracle if available.
ACCEPTANCE: The string "unsigned unary arithmetic not yet implemented" no longer exists in the codebase.

title: [parity-gap] safe egraph max/min commutativity loses signed-zero order
description:
Review evidence:
- safe_algebraic_rules still includes max-comm/min-comm and max-assoc/min-assoc.
- fj-lax implements JAX/NumPy-style NaN propagation with f64::max/min after the NaN check (crates/fj-lax/src/lib.rs:137-151). Rust and NumPy preserve operand-order-visible signed zeros: max(-0.0, +0.0) returns +0.0, while max(+0.0, -0.0) returns -0.0; min has the same order-visible behavior.
- Treating max/min as commutative/associative in the safe egraph marks these distinct bit patterns equivalent, so extraction can change the sign bit even though safe mode is supposed to preserve observable boundaries.

Concrete repro steps:
1. Add an egraph preservation test for out = Max(v1, v2) and out = Min(v1, v2).
2. Evaluate original and optimize_jaxpr(&jaxpr) with args [Value::scalar_f64(0.0), Value::scalar_f64(-0.0)].
3. Compare f64::to_bits(), not ==, because +0.0 == -0.0. Expected: optimized result preserves the original sign bit.
4. Add a 3-input associativity case: max(max(a,b),c) with signed-zero permutations and compare output bits.
5. Run: CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/tmp/rch_target_frankenjax_maxmin_zero RCH_ENV_ALLOWLIST=CARGO_TARGET_DIR rch exec -- cargo test -p fj-conformance --test egraph_preserves_semantics max_min_signed_zero_order -- --nocapture

Suggested fix: move max/min commutativity and associativity out of safe mode unless a canonical signed-zero policy is introduced and covered by conformance tests.
close_reason: Moved max/min commutativity and associativity out of safe mode; added signed-zero bit preservation regression.

title: Cumsum/Cumprod divide by zero on empty selected axis
description: [HIGH] eval_cumulative in crates/fj-lax/src/reduction.rs computes outer_count = total / axis_dim after axis_dim = tensor.shape.dims[axis] as usize. For a valid empty tensor on the selected axis, e.g. TensorValue::new(DType::I64, Shape { dims: vec![0] }, vec![]), axis_dim == 0 and total == 0, so Primitive::Cumsum/Primitive::Cumprod panic with division by zero. title: [parity-gap] safe egraph mul-neg-one changes promoted unsigned dtype
description:
Review evidence from the six-hour egraph hardening window:
- `crates/fj-egraph/src/lib.rs` still keeps `mul-neg-one` in `safe_algebraic_rules` at line around 359.
- The rewrite `mul(a, neg(1)) => neg(a)` is not dtype-preserving for promoted unsigned/integer inputs. The original `Mul` sees both operands and applies binary promotion; the rewritten program applies unary `Neg` to `a` first.
- `fj-lax` `eval_neg` supports unsigned inputs via wrapping negation, so the optimized program can return an unsigned wrapping value where the original promoted multiply returns a signed result.

Concrete repro steps:
1. Build a Jaxpr with `v2 = Neg(Literal::I64(1))` and `out = Mul(VarId(1), VarId(2))`.
2. Evaluate the original with `args = [Value::scalar_u32(7)]`. Expected under current binary promotion: the multiply observes the I64 `-1` operand and returns the promoted signed result (not a U32 wrapping negation).
3. Evaluate `optimize_jaxpr_with_config(&jaxpr, &OptimizationConfig::safe())` and `optimize_jaxpr(&jaxpr)` with the same args. Current safe/default can rewrite to `Neg(VarId(1))`; `eval_neg` on U32 returns the wrapping U32 value.
4. Assert both value and dtype equality between original and safe/default optimized evaluations.
5. Run: `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/tmp/rch_target_frankenjax_mul_neg_dtype RCH_ENV_ALLOWLIST=CARGO_TARGET_DIR rch exec -- cargo test -p fj-egraph mul_neg_one_dtype -- --nocapture`.

Suggested fix: move `mul-neg-one` out of safe mode until typed rewrites can prove the unary negation preserves the binary promoted output contract.

Repro: create a TraceContext with one rank-1 F64 input shaped [3], call process_primitive(Primitive::ReduceWindow, &[input], params) with window_dimensions="2", window_strides="0", padding="same". title: [code-review] Egraph bitwise_xor self rewrite erases unsigned dtype
description:
Review finding from commit 1ccef8f in `crates/fj-egraph/src/lib.rs`.

Defect: safe egraph rule `bitwise-xor-self` rewrites `(bitwise_xor ?a ?a)` to the bare egraph literal `0`. `egraph_to_jaxpr()` lowers bare numeric literals as `Literal::I64`, so optimizing an unsigned bitwise XOR self-cancel changes the output dtype/value representation from `U32(0)`/`U64(0)` to `I64(0)`. The type-blind egraph cannot safely introduce an untyped integer literal for typed bitwise operations.

Concrete repro:
1. Build a Jaxpr with one equation: `out = BitwiseXor(v1, v1)`.
2. Evaluate the original with `Value::scalar_u64(9_007_199_254_740_993)`: expected/output is `Value::scalar_u64(0)`.
3. Optimize with `optimize_jaxpr(&jaxpr)` and evaluate with the same input.
4. Actual optimized program returns an I64 zero (or otherwise violates unsigned dtype preservation) because the rewrite emits bare `Num(0)`.
5. Add/run a conformance regression with `rch exec -- cargo test -p fj-conformance --test egraph_preserves_semantics bitwise_xor_self_preserves_unsigned_dtype -- --nocapture`.

Suggested fix: remove `bitwise-xor-self` from the type-blind egraph rules, or add typed-zero lowering/proofs so U32/U64 inputs produce same-dtype zero. Cover scalar and tensor U32/U64 cases.
close_reason: Duplicate/subset of frankenjax-hf2l, which tracks the broader egraph literal dtype erasure issue including bitwise_xor unsigned zeros.

A shape dimension above u32::MAX silently wraps instead of returning an error. Repro: call eval_primitive(Primitive::BroadcastInDim, &[Value::scalar_i64(1)], &params) with params shape=4294967296. The implementation converts that dim to 0, computes total=0, and can return an empty tensor with shape [0] instead of rejecting the impossible requested output shape. Larger multi-dimensional shapes can also overflow the product at line 625/702 or attempt enormous allocation. Expected behavior: reject negative and out-of-u32-range dimensions before casting, and use checked multiplication for output element counts. Add regression tests covering shape=4294967296 and a product overflow case.

**Severity:** MEDIUM (missed optimization, not correctness)

The `cancels_shape_chain` function uses order-sensitive comparison for Rev axes:

```rust
(Primitive::Rev, Primitive::Rev) => rev_axes(&previous.params) == rev_axes(&current.params),
```

**Fix:** Sort the axes before comparison or use a BTreeSet.

title: [code-review] safe egraph neg-neg skips bool validation
description:
Review evidence from the six-hour egraph hardening window:
- `crates/fj-egraph/src/lib.rs` still keeps `neg-neg` in `safe_algebraic_rules` while default optimization is safety mode.
- `fj-lax` `eval_neg` rejects bool scalar/tensor inputs.

Concrete repro steps:
1. Build a Jaxpr with one input `x` and equations `v2 = Neg(x)`, `out = Neg(v2)`.
2. Evaluate the original with `args = [Value::Scalar(Literal::Bool(true))]`. Expected/current original behavior: `eval_jaxpr` returns `EvalError::TypeMismatch` from `eval_neg` with detail `expected numeric scalar, got bool`.
3. Evaluate `optimize_jaxpr_with_config(&jaxpr, &OptimizationConfig::safe())` and `optimize_jaxpr(&jaxpr)` with the same args. Current safe/default can rewrite to `x` and return `Value::Scalar(Literal::Bool(true))`.
4. Add regression coverage beside the existing `numerical_safety_mode_preserves_*` tests and run `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/tmp/rch_target_frankenjax_neg_neg_validation RCH_ENV_ALLOWLIST=CARGO_TARGET_DIR rch exec -- cargo test -p fj-egraph neg_neg_validation -- --nocapture`.

Suggested fix: move `neg-neg` out of safe mode, or require typed lowering evidence proving the inner neg validation already succeeded before eliminating both operations. Audit similar remaining safe unary rewrites such as `abs-neg`, trig/hyperbolic neg rules, `reciprocal-as-div`, and `pow-neg-one` for validation/dtype parity before declaring the family safe.

Expected fix: use checked_add for the end offset, return None on overflow, and keep existing valid/boundary slice behavior unchanged. Add a unit test covering the overflow case.

title: [parity-gap] safe egraph reciprocal-reciprocal erases subnormal overflow
description:
Review evidence:
- Commits 2971d17, 348837a, 2ab703f, and 1ccef8f moved several unsafe egraph identities behind OptimizationConfig::aggressive().
- safe_algebraic_rules still contains reciprocal-reciprocal: (reciprocal (reciprocal ?a)) => ?a.
- That identity is not safe for tiny nonzero floats: 1.0 / 1e-320 overflows to +Inf, then 1.0 / +Inf is +0.0, while the rewrite returns 1e-320.

Concrete repro steps:
1. Add a fj-egraph unit test building chained_unary_jaxpr(Primitive::Reciprocal, Primitive::Reciprocal).
2. Evaluate original and optimize_jaxpr_with_config(..., &OptimizationConfig::safe()) with Value::scalar_f64(1e-320).
3. Assert optimized output matches original bit/value semantics.
4. Run: CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/tmp/rch_target_frankenjax_egraph_recip RCH_ENV_ALLOWLIST=CARGO_TARGET_DIR rch exec -- cargo test -p fj-egraph reciprocal_reciprocal -- --nocapture
5. Current safe optimizer can extract ?a and return 1e-320 instead of the original +0.0.
close_reason: Moved reciprocal-reciprocal to numerically_unsafe_rules; subnormal overflow breaks identity

title: Implement complex pow in apply_complex_binary (fj-lax arithmetic.rs)
description:
WHAT: Add complex exponentiation to apply_complex_binary() in crates/fj-lax/src/arithmetic.rs:145-164.
WHERE: The match arm at line 160 currently returns "complex arithmetic not yet implemented" for all binary ops except add/sub/mul/div.
HOW: Complex pow uses the identity (a+bi)^(c+di) = exp((c+di)*ln(a+bi)). Decompose: r=|z|, theta=atan2(b,a), ln(z)=(ln(r), theta), then exp of the product. For integer exponents, use repeated squaring for efficiency.
WHY: JAX supports complex pow natively. Without it, grad(f) fails for any traced program that involves complex exponentiation.
TESTING: Add tests in fj-lax for complex pow at several points: (1+i)^2 = 2i, (1+i)^(0.5), purely real complex pow matches real pow. Add numerical AD verification for complex pow VJP.
ACCEPTANCE: The "complex arithmetic not yet implemented" error no longer triggers for Primitive::Pow with complex inputs.

title: Conv panics on zero stride parameter
description:
[HIGH] crates/fj-lax/src/tensor_ops.rs accepts strides=0 for Primitive::Conv and then performs division by that stride instead of returning a typed EvalError. In 1D conv, eval_conv_1d parses params["strides"] at lines 2817-2820 and then uses width.div_ceil(stride) for SAME padding at line 2824 or (width - kernel_w) / stride for VALID padding at line 2835. In 2D conv, parse_stride_pair returns zero at lines 2976-2986 and compute_output_and_pad divides by stride at lines 2997 and 3005.

title: [code-review] Safe egraph reciprocal involution changes subnormal behavior
description:
Review finding from commits 1ccef8f/2ab703f in crates/fj-egraph/src/lib.rs.

Defect: `safe_algebraic_rules()` still includes `reciprocal-reciprocal`; default `optimize_jaxpr()` now uses `OptimizationConfig::safe()`, so the safe/default optimizer rewrites `reciprocal(reciprocal(x))` to `x`. That is not safe at subnormal boundaries. For f64 `x = 1e-320`, the original program computes `1.0 / (1.0 / x)`: the inner reciprocal overflows to +Inf and the outer reciprocal returns +0.0. The optimized program returns 1e-320. This violates the config docs that safe mode protects denormals and violates JAX/IEEE observable behavior for the unfused operation.

Concrete repro:
1. Add a conformance test in `crates/fj-conformance/tests/egraph_preserves_semantics.rs` that builds `v2 = reciprocal(v1); v3 = reciprocal(v2)`.
2. Evaluate the original Jaxpr and `optimize_jaxpr(&jaxpr)` with `Value::scalar_f64(1e-320)`.
3. Expected: safe/default optimization preserves the original +0.0 result, or keeps the reciprocal chain. Actual: optimized output is 1e-320 because the rule removes both reciprocals.
4. Run with `rch exec -- cargo test -p fj-conformance --test egraph_preserves_semantics reciprocal_subnormal -- --nocapture`.

Suggested fix: move `reciprocal-reciprocal` into `numerically_unsafe_rules()` unless a range/type proof is available, and add the conformance test above.
close_reason: Duplicate of frankenjax-elh8, which tracks the same safe egraph reciprocal-reciprocal subnormal parity gap.

title: Fix large I64 precision loss in sort and argsort
description:
Review finding [HIGH]. In crates/fj-lax/src/tensor_ops.rs, sort_along_axis currently converts integral tensor elements to f64 before sorting (lines around 2589 and 2611-2639). Values above 2^53 cannot be represented exactly as f64, so Sort can silently rewrite distinct I64 literals when it casts the sorted f64 back to i64, and Argsort can compare rounded values instead of the original integer keys.

Reproduction to add as a failing test: evaluate Primitive::Sort on an I64 tensor [9007199254740993, 9007199254740992]. Expected exact sorted values are [9007199254740992, 9007199254740993], but the current implementation routes both values through f64 and can collapse/corrupt the larger literal. Also evaluate Primitive::Argsort on [9007199254740993, 9007199254740992, 9007199254740994] and assert the indices reflect true i64 ordering, not f64-rounded ordering.

Suggested fix: sort integral tensors with an i64 key path that preserves the original Literal for Sort and uses the same exact key for Argsort. Keep the f64 total_cmp path for floating tensors so NaN ordering remains covered by existing tests. Validate with rch cargo test -p fj-lax sort and rch cargo test -p fj-conformance --test sort_oracle.
close_reason: Fixed exact integer sort and argsort ordering with oracle regressions

title: Optimize DFT twiddle factor computation - precompute roots of unity
description:
**Performance issue in fj-lax/src/fft.rs:**

The O(n²) DFT fallback computes sin_cos() for every (j,k) pair:
```rust
for (k, out) in output.iter_mut().enumerate() {
    for (j, &(xr, xi)) in input.iter().enumerate() {
        let angle = -2.0 * PI * (j as f64) * (k as f64) / (n as f64);
        let (sin_a, cos_a) = angle.sin_cos();  // Called n² times!
```

**Fix:** Precompute the n-th roots of unity once (n calls), then lookup by `(j*k) % n`.
This reduces trig calls from O(n²) to O(n) for non-power-of-2 lengths.

**Skill applied:** /profiling-software-performance

title: Split panics on zero num_sections for empty axes
description:
`eval_split` accepts `num_sections=0` because `parse_usize_param` allows zero and the Split path never validates that the section count is positive. For an empty split axis, current Rust reports `0usize.is_multiple_of(0) == true`, so `eval_split` reaches `let section_size = axis_size / num_sections` and divides by zero at `crates/fj-lax/src/tensor_ops.rs:3550`.

Reproduction sketch:
1. Build an empty tensor, for example `TensorValue::new(DType::I64, Shape { dims: vec![0] }, vec![])` wrapped as `Value::Tensor`.
2. Call `eval_primitive(Primitive::Split, &[input], &BTreeMap::from([("num_sections".into(), "0".into())]))`.
3. Expected: `Err(EvalError::Unsupported { primitive: Primitive::Split, detail: ... })` because zero sections is invalid.
4. Actual: panic from integer division by zero in `eval_split`.

The recent Split oracle suite in `crates/fj-conformance/tests/split_oracle.rs` covers positive section counts but does not include invalid zero-section coverage. Fix should reject `num_sections == 0` before divisibility/reshape logic and add regression coverage for empty-axis and non-empty-axis inputs.
close_reason: Fixed: added explicit check rejecting num_sections==0 before divisibility logic in eval_split. Added 3 regression tests for zero sections on both empty and non-empty axes.

title: [code-review] safe egraph clamp rewrites bypass validation
description:
Review evidence from the six-hour egraph hardening window:
- `crates/fj-egraph/src/lib.rs` still keeps `clamp-to-minmax` and `clamp-same` in `safe_algebraic_rules` at lines around 431-433.
- `fj-lax` `eval_clamp` rejects complex/bool literals and rejects unsupported scalar/tensor input forms before computing values.
- Safe egraph rewrites can bypass those checks: `clamp(a, a, a) => a`, or `clamp(x, lo, hi) => min(max(x, lo), hi)` can route through broader binary broadcasting semantics instead of clamp's stricter contract.

Concrete repro steps:
1. Add a regression that builds `out = Clamp(x, x, x)` with one input `x`.
2. Evaluate the original with `args = [Value::Scalar(Literal::from_complex128(1.0, 0.0))]`. Expected: `eval_jaxpr` returns the existing clamp `TypeMismatch` (`clamp is not supported for complex dtypes`).
3. Evaluate `optimize_jaxpr_with_config(&jaxpr, &OptimizationConfig::safe())` and `optimize_jaxpr(&jaxpr)` with the same args. Current safe/default can rewrite to `x` and return the complex value.
4. Add a `clamp-to-minmax` shape/kind case such as scalar `x` with tensor `lo`/`hi`; `eval_clamp` rejects unsupported input forms, while transformed max/min may broadcast and succeed.
5. Run: `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/tmp/rch_target_frankenjax_clamp_safe_rules RCH_ENV_ALLOWLIST=CARGO_TARGET_DIR rch exec -- cargo test -p fj-egraph clamp_validation -- --nocapture`.

title: Make batched fixture timeouts return without joining timed-out workers
description:
Review finding [HIGH]. Commit 0985d27 changed run_transform_fixture_bundle_batched in crates/fj-conformance/src/lib.rs to record timed-out worker handles, but the function then joins all timed_out_handles before returning (current lines around 1145-1186). That means case_timeout does not bound wall-clock runtime: a timed-out case with a long or hung worker still blocks the whole batched run at the final join.

Reproduction to add: construct a TransformFixtureBundle with one case having simulated_delay_ms = 5000 and BatchRunnerConfig { case_timeout: Duration::from_millis(1) }. Measure elapsed time for run_transform_fixture_bundle_batched. Expected behavior for a timeout runner is to return a Timeout report promptly after roughly the configured timeout; current behavior waits for the delayed worker during the final join and returns only after the worker finishes. A genuinely hung worker would hang the harness indefinitely despite emitting a timeout report.

Suggested fix: preserve bounded fan-out without joining timed-out workers on the critical return path. Options include a scoped worker pool with cooperative cancellation, a persistent bounded runner, or clearly documenting and renaming the timeout as classification-only. Add an elapsed-time regression test so future code cannot reintroduce timeout-as-blocking-join semantics. Validate with rch cargo test -p fj-conformance test_batch_runner.
close_reason: Detached timed-out batch workers from the return path and added elapsed-time regression coverage

title: Avoid holding LRU order lock during backend eviction
description:
Skill: /deadlock-finder-and-fixer

Verified hazard: crates/fj-cache/src/eviction.rs LruCache::enforce_budget holds the internal order Mutex while invoking CacheBackend::stats and CacheBackend::evict. CacheBackend is a public trait for arbitrary backends, so calling backend code while holding the wrapper lock creates a reentrancy/deadlock hazard if a backend observes or re-enters the LRU wrapper, logs through shared cache state, or blocks behind code that needs the order lock.

Reproduction target: add a custom test backend whose stats/evict methods try_lock the LruCache order mutex. On the current implementation, inserting beyond max_entries or max_bytes fails because enforce_budget still holds order while calling into the backend.

Expected fix: shorten the order critical section, pop eviction keys into local values, drop the lock, and only then call backend stats/evict. Keep LRU ordering behavior unchanged and add a regression test that proves backend calls are made without the order lock held.

title: [parity-gap] safe egraph pow-two rewrites erase promoted dtypes
description:
Review evidence from the last-six-hours egraph safety commits:
- 14fcdc9 moved add/sub zero, mul/div/pow/integer_pow one, and max/min commutativity/associativity out of safe mode, but safe_algebraic_rules still keeps pow-two and integer-pow-two in crates/fj-egraph/src/lib.rs.

- Primitive::IntegerPow currently returns F64 for numeric scalar/tensor inputs. The safe egraph rule integer-pow-two rewrites integer_pow(x, exponent=2) to mul(x, x), so a U32 input changes from F64(49.0) to U32(49).

2. Evaluate the original with eval_jaxpr; expected outputs are I64(49) for Pow and F64(49.0) for IntegerPow under the current fj-lax contracts.
3. Evaluate optimize_jaxpr_with_config(&jaxpr, &OptimizationConfig::safe()) and optimize_jaxpr(&jaxpr); current safe/default can emit Mul(var,var) and return U32(49).

title: [code-review] safe egraph complex rewrites skip dtype validation
description:
Review evidence from the six-hour egraph hardening window:
- `crates/fj-egraph/src/lib.rs` still keeps `real-complex`, `imag-complex`, and `complex-real-imag` in `safe_algebraic_rules` at lines around 436-438.
- `fj-lax` `eval_real`/`eval_imag` reject non-complex inputs, and `eval_complex` validates part dtypes/shapes before constructing a complex value.
- Safe egraph extraction can remove those validation operations and return an input variable directly.

Concrete repro steps:
1. Add a regression in `crates/fj-egraph/src/lib.rs` or `crates/fj-conformance/tests/egraph_preserves_semantics.rs` that builds `out = Complex(Real(z), Imag(z))` with one input `z`.
2. Evaluate the original with `args = [Value::scalar_f64(3.0)]`. Expected under the current fj-lax contract: `eval_jaxpr` returns the existing `TypeMismatch` from `Real`/`Imag` because the input is not complex.
3. Evaluate `optimize_jaxpr_with_config(&jaxpr, &OptimizationConfig::safe())` and `optimize_jaxpr(&jaxpr)` with the same args. Current safe/default can rewrite to just `z` and return `Value::scalar_f64(3.0)`, converting an input validation error into success.
4. Add a second case for `Real(Complex(r, i))` with `r = Value::scalar_f64(1.0)` and `i = Value::scalar_bool(true)`. Original `Complex` should reject the bool part; safe/default can rewrite to `r`.
5. Run: `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/tmp/rch_target_frankenjax_complex_safe_rules RCH_ENV_ALLOWLIST=CARGO_TARGET_DIR rch exec -- cargo test -p fj-egraph complex_validation -- --nocapture`.

Suggested fix: move the complex safe rewrites to `numerically_unsafe_rules` or a typed/validated lowering phase that proves complex input and part validity before eliminating operations.
close_reason: Moved complex validation-skipping egraph rewrites out of safe mode and added validation regression coverage.

title: Harden BufferView slice range overflow
description: Multi-pass bug hunt found crates/fj-runtime/src/buffer.rs BufferView::slice computes offset + len before validating bounds. For adversarial or saturated usize inputs this can panic in debug builds due integer overflow, and in optimized builds can wrap before the subsequent slice expression panics or misclassifies the range. Replace the addition with checked_add so out-of-range or overflowing slices return None as documented. Add a regression test using usize::MAX to prove BufferView::slice is panic-free and returns None for overflowing ranges. Validate with rch cargo test -p fj-runtime, rch cargo check -p fj-runtime --all-targets, rch cargo clippy -p fj-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo fmt --check, and ubs on the touched file.

title: [testing-metamorphic] MR for tensor_dist: zero-distance + symmetry + triangle inequality

title: ReduceWindow same padding is offset incorrectly
description: eval_reduce_window computes SAME output length with ceil(input/stride) but starts every window at out_index * stride, so padding is effectively only on the high side. JAX/XLA SAME semantics split total padding with low padding floor(total/2), so examples like input [1,2,3,4,5], window=3, stride=1 should produce [3,6,9,12,9] instead of [6,9,12,9,5]. Implement low-padding offsets for SAME in rank-N reduce_window and add regression coverage.

title: [modes-of-reasoning] numerical-stability-vs-JIT-correctness
description:
E-graph rewrites (exp-log, div-self, reassociation) are mathematically valid but numerically treacherous near domain boundaries. Eager vs JIT diverge on edge cases (0, denormal, NaN, Inf). Conformance detects drift post-hoc but cannot prevent unsafe rewrites.

Key locations:
- fj-egraph/src/lib.rs:269-324 (rewrite rules without domain guards)
- fj-lax/src/arithmetic.rs:219-222 (underflow-prone complex reciprocal)
- fj-conformance/src/numerical_stability.rs:857-920 (tolerance enforcement gap)

Suggested work:
1. Add domain predicates to e-graph rules (div-self only when provably non-zero)
2. Implement numerical safety mode that disables associativity rewrites
3. Extend conformance gate to compare JIT vs eager on edge-case inputs
close_reason: Added OptimizationConfig with numerical_safety_mode flag in ceea42f. Safe mode disables 6 unsafe rewrites: exp-log, div-self, mul-reciprocal, div-mul-cancel, log-product, log-quotient.

title: Conv SAME padding panics on empty spatial dimensions
description: [HIGH] crates/fj-lax/src/tensor_ops.rs Conv SAME padding assumes the computed output spatial dimension is nonzero. For empty spatial axes, width.div_ceil(stride) or input_size.div_ceil(stride) can return 0, then line 3123 and helper line 3324 compute out_w - 1 / out - 1 and underflow in debug/test builds. Repro 1D: lhs TensorValue::new(DType::F64, Shape { dims: vec![1,0,1] }, vec![]), rhs TensorValue::new(DType::F64, Shape { dims: vec![1,1,1] }, vec![1.0]), params { padding="same", strides="1" }, then eval_primitive(Primitive::Conv, &[lhs, rhs], &params). Expected: either an empty output tensor with shape [1,0,1] or a typed EvalError, but no panic. Actual: SAME geometry computes out_w=0 and underflows at ((out_w - 1) * stride + kernel_w). The 2D path uses compute_output_and_pad and has the same out == 0 underflow for any empty height/width with SAME padding. Add regression tests for 1D width=0 and 2D height/width=0.
close_reason: Fixed: added early return for input_size=0 in compute_output_and_pad and 1D conv path. Added 5 regression tests for empty spatial dims.

title: Replace e-graph not-yet-supported comment with principled UnsupportedPrimitive categorization
description:
CONTEXT: crates/fj-egraph/src/lib.rs:598 has comment Shape ops require params -- not yet supported followed by 34 primitives returning UnsupportedPrimitive. The not yet wording is misleading -- these are excluded BY DESIGN.

CHANGES REQUIRED:
  1. Replace comment with accurate doc: these primitives are architecturally excluded because the s-expression egraph cannot represent parameterized operations (shapes, axes, sub-jaxprs).
  2. Split the 34-primitive catch-all into categorized groups with per-group doc comments:
     - Shape manipulation (13): Reshape, Slice, DynamicSlice, Gather, Scatter, Transpose, BroadcastInDim, Concatenate, Pad, Rev, Squeeze, Split, ExpandDims
     - Linear algebra (5): Cholesky, Qr, Svd, TriangularSolve, Eigh
     - FFT (4): Fft, Ifft, Rfft, Irfft
     - Control flow (4): Cond, Scan, While, Switch
     - Sorting (2): Sort, Argsort
     - Convolution (1): Conv
     - Index/utility (3): Iota, BroadcastedIota, DynamicUpdateSlice
     - Type conversion (2): BitcastConvertType, ReducePrecision
     - Cumulative (2): Cumsum, Cumprod
     - Windowed (1): ReduceWindow
     - Encoding (1): OneHot
  3. Add ExclusionReason enum or string field to EGraphLoweringError::UnsupportedPrimitive so error messages say e.g. reshape excluded: requires shape parameters (not representable in algebraic e-graph).
  4. Add test: for each category, verify the error message contains the category reason.

TESTING: Existing egraph tests must still pass. New test: construct Jaxpr with each excluded primitive, call jaxpr_to_egraph, assert error message contains category keyword. Log all 34 exclusion messages.

ACCEPTANCE: The string not yet supported gone. Each exclusion has a documented reason. Error messages are informative.
close_reason: Centralized egraph exclusion metadata by category, surfaced reasons in UnsupportedPrimitive errors, added full exclusion-message coverage, and verified with rch cargo test -p fj-egraph plus workspace check/clippy/fmt

title: Repair fj-conformance fuzz coverage for pmap enum additions
description:
testing-fuzzing audit finding from cod_4.

Evidence:
- `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/rch_target_frankenjax_cod_4_fuzz RCH_ENV_ALLOWLIST=CARGO_TARGET_DIR rch exec -- cargo check --manifest-path crates/fj-conformance/fuzz/Cargo.toml` fails with E0004 in `crates/fj-conformance/fuzz/fuzz_targets/common.rs:257`: missing `Primitive::Psum`, `Primitive::Pmean`, `Primitive::AllGather`, `Primitive::AllToAll`, and `Primitive::AxisIndex`.
- `fj-core::Primitive` defines those pmap collective variants at `crates/fj-core/src/lib.rs:196-201`; `common.rs` `ALL_PRIMITIVES` and `primitive_arity` only cover pre-pmap variants.
- `fj-core::Transform` includes `Transform::Pmap`, but `sample_transform` in `common.rs:241-246` samples only `Jit`, `Grad`, and `Vmap`, so dispatch/composition fuzzing never exercises the V1 pmap fail-closed path.

Acceptance criteria:
- Update the fuzz helper manually so primitive sampling and arity handling are exhaustive for the current `Primitive` enum, including pmap collectives.
- Include `Transform::Pmap` in transform fuzz sampling with expectations that pmap dispatch fails closed rather than panicking.
- Add/extend helper-level tests or compile checks so future enum additions break clearly.
- Verify with `rch exec -- cargo check --manifest-path crates/fj-conformance/fuzz/Cargo.toml`.
close_reason: Fixed: fuzz helper now covers pmap collective primitives and samples Transform::Pmap; added fuzz_common test target. Verified cargo check --manifest-path crates/fj-conformance/fuzz/Cargo.toml --all-targets and cargo test --manifest-path crates/fj-conformance/fuzz/Cargo.toml --test fuzz_common via rch. cargo test -p fj-conformance is blocked by unrelated stale README artifact hash in e2e_forensic_log_contract.

title: Add NaN/Inf gradient propagation tests for AD edge cases
description:
CONTEXT: The AD engine (fj-ad) has no tests verifying how NaN and Inf propagate through VJP/JVP rules. JAX propagates NaN faithfully: grad(sin)(NaN) = NaN, grad(exp)(Inf) = Inf. Silent NaN-to-zero or Inf-to-zero conversion in gradient rules would be a correctness bug that goes undetected.

SCOPE: Add targeted tests in crates/fj-ad/src/lib.rs verifying:
  1. NaN propagation: grad(sin)(NaN)=NaN, grad(cos)(NaN)=NaN, grad(exp)(NaN)=NaN, grad(log)(NaN)=NaN, grad(tanh)(NaN)=NaN, grad(x^2)(NaN)=NaN
  2. Inf propagation: grad(exp)(Inf)=Inf, grad(log)(0+)=Inf or -Inf, grad(x^2)(Inf)=Inf, grad(1/x)(0)=(-Inf or NaN)
  3. Mixed: grad(x*y) where x=NaN, y=finite
  4. Backward pass with NaN cotangent: vjp(sin, 1.0, NaN) should produce NaN gradient
  5. JVP with NaN tangent: jvp(sin, 1.0, NaN) should produce NaN output tangent

TESTING: Each test checks is_nan() or is_infinite() on the gradient output. Use descriptive assertion messages. Log each test case.

ACCEPTANCE: All NaN/Inf propagation tests pass. No gradient rule silently converts NaN to 0 or Inf to finite.
close_reason: Already covered by AD NaN/Inf propagation tests; verified in full workspace test run

title: tensor_pdist severs autograd; composable through index_select for finite p > 0
description:
tensor_pdist at lib.rs:4349 computes pairwise L_p distances between rows of a 2-D input. For finite p > 0 the math is composable through autograd-aware primitives (index_select pairs of rows, abs, pow, sum_dim, pow). For p = inf it's argmax-routing; for p = 0 it's a non-differentiable counting metric.

Strategy: build row_i and row_j index tensors of length N*(N-1)/2 each, use tensor_index_select to gather row pairs, then compute:
   diff = left - right
   per_pair = (sum_k |diff[k]|^p)^(1/p)
All ops autograd-aware. Add fail-loud guards for p == 0 (counting metric, non-diff) and p == +inf (could be added with max_dim but defer).
notes: Fixed in this commit. For finite p > 0, composed tensor_pdist through index_select + sub + abs + pow + sum_dim + pow primitives. Pre-built row_i / row_j index tensors of length N*(N-1)/2 enumerate the upper-triangular pairs; index_select gathers the row-pair tensors so subsequent ops broadcast naturally. p == 0 (counting metric) and p == +inf (max-routing) now fail-loud on requires_grad=true rather than silently severing — autograd implementations for those cases are deferred. Added pdist_l2_propagates_gradient_through_input regression test. ft-api lib tests: 1169.

title: tensor_kthvalue severs autograd; index-routing backward needed
description:
tensor_kthvalue at lib.rs:12512 returns the k-th smallest element of a 1-D tensor. The value branch is just input[idx] where idx is the rank-k sorted index. PyTorch's torch.kthvalue IS differentiable: grad_input[idx] = grad_value, all other positions zero.

Wrap value branch in tensor_apply_function with this single-index routing backward. Index branch stays a non-grad leaf (integer).
notes: Fixed in this commit. Wrapped tensor_kthvalue's value branch in tensor_apply_function with single-index routing backward: grad_input[idx] = grad_value where idx is the sort-rank-k index. The index branch stays a non-grad leaf. Added kthvalue_propagates_gradient_to_routed_index regression test (x=[3,1,4,1,5], k=3 → 3rd smallest is at idx 0 with value 3, grad_input = [1,0,0,0,0]). ft-api lib tests: 1163.

softmax_tensor_dim_contiguous_f64 and log_softmax_tensor_dim_contiguous_f64 are numerically delicate (exp/log composition with the max-subtraction stabilization trick). Both are widely used in the attention / classifier paths via ft-api.

No fuzz target currently exercises shape/dim validation or the inner max-subtract-exp-sum-divide loop on arbitrary shapes. A fuzz target that drives both with random shape + dim + input slices would catch:
- dim-out-of-range guard regressions
- shape-volume overflow path (checked_dim_loop_sizes)
- numerical pathologies (output should always be in [0,1] for softmax; sum-along-dim should be ~1 within tolerance)
- log_softmax output should always be <= 0

Acceptance:
- new fuzz target ft_kernel_cpu_softmax exercising BOTH softmax_tensor_dim_contiguous_f64 AND log_softmax_tensor_dim_contiguous_f64
- shape-volume cap at 4096
- on Ok, asserts:
  * output.len == numel
  * softmax: all elements in [0.0 - eps, 1.0 + eps]
  * log_softmax: all elements <= eps (allow small positive epsilon for FP slack)
- >=2 corpus seeds
- registered in fuzz/Cargo.toml
- compiles cleanly under rch exec
close_reason: Shipped: ft_kernel_cpu_softmax fuzz target. Drives both softmax_dim_tensor_contiguous_f64 and log_softmax_dim_tensor_contiguous_f64 with shared shape/dim/input. title: [porting-to-rust] unblock tensor_special_i0e autograd via product rule (now that i1e is shipped)
description:
Now that ner6 shipped tensor_special_i1e (and ar9i unblocked i1's autograd), tensor_special_i0e's fail-loud guard on requires_grad can be replaced with the analytical backward:

  d/dx i0e(x) = d/dx (exp(-|x|) * i0(x))
             = -sign(x) * exp(-|x|) * i0(x) + exp(-|x|) * i1(x)
             = i1e(x) - sign(x) * i0e(x)

Note: i0e has a corner at x = 0 (derivative jumps from -1 to +1 across zero). Convention: sign(0) = 0 gives gradient = i1e(0) - 0 = 0, matching torch's autograd choice.

Wire via tensor_apply_function with bessel_i0e_scalar + bessel_i1e_scalar in the backward closure. Replace the existing fail-loud test with a gradient verification at x = 1.

Acceptance: tensor_special_i0e forward+backward with the product-rule gradient; remove fail-loud guard; new gradient lib test verifying d/dx i0e(1) ≈ exp(-1)*(i1(1) - i0(1)) ≈ -0.258.
close_reason: Shipped — tensor_special_i0e backward via product rule (i1e(x) - sign(x)*i0e(x)) using ner6's i1e + scalar helpers. Removed fail-loud guard. New gradient lib test verifies d/dx i0e(1) ≈ -0.2579.

title: [profiling-software-performance] tensor_softshrink has three redundant full(shape, lambd) allocations
description:
Same compose-anti-pattern family as cc2o (heaviside/pow_tensor), d521 (sinc), 4w7g (atanh/focal_loss), and x8r1 (entr). tensor_softshrink at ft-api lib.rs:5375 allocates the same lambd-valued tensor THREE times within a single forward call:

  let lambd_t      = full(shape, lambd)?;     // for tensor_gt mask
  let lambd_const  = full(shape, lambd)?;     // for tensor_sub
  let lambd_const2 = full(shape, lambd)?;     // for tensor_add

All three are operands of read-only ops (tensor_gt / tensor_sub / tensor_add); one shared lambd tensor suffices.

Net per-call savings: -2 full() allocations + -2 autograd-tape nodes. tensor_softshrink is a torch activation function used in sparse-coding / wavelet thresholding heads, so the wasted work compounds in training.

Acceptance:
- tensor_softshrink reuses one shared lambd tensor across gt mask, sub, and add call sites
- existing softshrink tests still pass — no behavior change
close_reason: Shipped: 4c0eacf. tensor_softshrink shares one lambd_t across the gt mask, the sub-shift, and the add-shift. -2 full() + -2 tape nodes per call. 2 softshrink tests including gradient regression pass.

title: Investigate persistent beads SQLite integrity warning after clean rebuild
description:
## Context
After a full non-destructive rebuild of `.beads/beads.db` from canonical `issues.jsonl`, `br doctor --json` still reports:

`sqlite.integrity_check: database disk image is malformed: page 17 is never used`

This persists even on the freshly rebuilt DB, while all operational checks are otherwise healthy (`br ready --json` is empty, sync metadata matches, blocked cache is not stale).

## Goal
Determine whether this warning reflects:
1. a genuine low-level SQLite file/layout problem,
2. expected frankensqlite behavior that `br doctor` should not flag as suspicious, or
3. a beads/br bug in the integrity-check path.

## Acceptance
- Reproduce the warning on the current canonical DB
- Compare against a freshly rebuilt temp DB
- Gather enough evidence to classify the issue as workspace-local vs tool-level
- If it is tool-level or not safely fixable from this repo, document the finding clearly and close or hand off with evidence
close_reason: Reproduced the integrity warning on canonical and rebuilt DBs, proved a plain SQLite VACUUM clears it, then observed br doctor --repair reintroduce the warning on a different page number while keeping logical metadata healthy; this classifies the issue as a tool-level beads/frankensqlite write-path problem rather than repo-local issue-data corruption

title: [testing-conformance-harnesses] no torch oracle for tensor_diag (1-D embed and 2-D extract paths)
description:
tensor_diag (added in 5a11cb5) dispatches by rank — 1-D becomes a 2-D matrix with input on the requested diagonal, 2-D extracts the diagonal as a 1-D tensor. Six lib unit tests cover the dispatch logic. No subprocess oracle pins the actual upstream torch.diag values for non-zero offsets, where the indexing semantics are easy to get subtly wrong (off-by-one between super and sub diagonals, off-by-one between 1-D embed offset and the resulting matrix size).

Concrete repro: a regression to tensor_diag_embed offset arithmetic that flips super/sub direction would still pass the lib unit test (the direction is consistent within tensor_diag_embed) but diverge from torch. The oracle catches that.

Fix direction: add torch_diag_subprocess_conformance with a fixed grid of (input, diagonal) pairs that exercises:
  - 1-D embed at offset 0 (main), +1 (super), -1 (sub)
  - 2-D extract at offset 0 (main), +1 (super), -1 (sub)
  - rectangular 2-D extraction (m != n)
For each case, run torch.diag on the same input/offset and assert ft-api returns the same shape and bit-equal values.

Acceptance:
- new test torch_diag_subprocess_conformance using the existing torch_*_subprocess_conformance pattern
- 6+ cases covering both rank dispatch paths
- skips silently if torch unavailable
- ft-conformance lib tests +1
close_reason: Shipped: 7224820. torch_diag_subprocess_conformance pins both rank-dispatch paths (1-D embed and 2-D extract) across main/super/sub diagonals + rectangular 2-D case. 8 cases, bit-equal via to_bits().

title: Add custom autograd Function API (torch.autograd.Function equivalent)
description:
Users cannot currently define custom backward functions. This is arguably the single most impactful missing feature for real-world use — without it, any layer whose backward isn't built into FrankenTorch's op set is impossible to implement.

PyTorch's torch.autograd.Function API allows users to:
1. Define a custom forward() that registers itself on the autograd tape
2. Define a custom backward() that computes gradients for the custom op
3. Save tensors for backward via ctx.save_for_backward()

Implementation plan:
1. Add a CustomFunction trait in ft-autograd with forward/backward methods
2. Add a TensorNodeOp::Custom variant to the tensor tape
3. Add session.apply_custom_function() to ft-api that invokes the user's forward, registers the op on the tape, and stores the backward closure
4. During backward traversal, call the user's backward function when encountering Custom nodes
5. Handle save_for_backward by capturing TensorNodeIds in the closure context

Key design decisions:
- The backward closure must receive upstream gradient and return downstream gradients
- Must respect no_grad context (custom forward inside no_grad should not record on tape)
- Must work with the existing deterministic backward scheduler
- Error handling: user backward functions should return Result, not panic

Tests:
- Unit test: custom ReLU equivalent (forward: max(0,x), backward: 1 if x>0 else 0)
- Unit test: custom function with multiple inputs/outputs
- Unit test: custom function inside no_grad context (should not record)
- Unit test: custom function backward produces correct gradients (numerical gradient check)
- E2E test: train a model with a custom layer and verify loss decreases
- Edge case: nested custom functions
- Edge case: custom function that saves tensors for backward
close_reason: Core functionality already exists: tensor_apply_function() with FunctionCtx (save_for_backward, needs_input_grad) + backward closure. Extensive tests in ft-autograd (lines 17484+) and used internally by ft-api for ~12 ops. The closure-based API is the Rust-idiomatic equivalent of PyTorch's class-based torch.autograd.Function. A trait wrapper could be added later for API sugar but is not blocking.

The oracle catches drift in:
  - erfinv's A&S polynomial vs torch's higher-order Cephes (loose ~1e-4 tolerance expected)
  - sqrt(2) constant arithmetic
  - boundary behavior at p=0 (-inf), p=1 (+inf), p<0 / p>1 (NaN)

Acceptance: torch_special_ndtri_subprocess_conformance test in ft-conformance with ≥10 cases covering median (0.5), 95% quantiles, near-boundary (1e-6, 1 - 1e-6), boundary (0, 1), and out-of-range (NaN); tagged-string wire encoding; ULP-bounded comparison with 1e-4 absolute tolerance for the smooth interior.

title: [porting-to-rust] missing tensor_special_log_ndtr (numerically stable log normal CDF)
description:
Sister of ndtr (frankentorch-7qh9) — torch.special.log_ndtr returns log(ndtr(x)) but numerically stable for very negative x where ndtr(x) underflows to 0 in f64. Used heavily in VAE / Bayesian inference / importance sampling where log-probabilities matter.

Reference (scipy/torch): for x > 0, use log(ndtr(x)) directly; for x < ~-1, use the asymptotic series

  log_ndtr(x) ≈ -x²/2 - log(-x*sqrt(2π)) + log(1 - 1/x² + 3/x⁴ - 15/x⁶ + ...)

The series converges quickly for x << 0 because each term shrinks by ~x⁻². For -1 <= x <= 0 the direct log(ndtr(x)) form is fine.

Acceptance: tensor_special_log_ndtr method; piecewise composition (smooth interior via log(ndtr(x)), asymptotic for x < ~-7); ≥6 lib tests covering log_ndtr(0) = log(0.5), log_ndtr(-50) finite (asymptotic regime), agreement with log(ndtr(x)) in smooth interior, NaN propagation, gradient correctness.

Depends on: 7qh9 (ndtr port lands first to compose against).

title: Severed-autograd loss umbrella: focal, poisson_nll, gaussian_nll
description:

title: [testing-conformance-harnesses] tighten torch_fft_numpy_subprocess_conformance tolerance from N^2 to N*log(N)*EPSILON after hpo6
description:
The 7z70 conformance harness currently uses bound N^2 * EPSILON to accommodate the previous O(N^2) naive DFT (which accumulated O(N) rounding per output cell).

After hpo6 replaced the implementation with Cooley-Tukey for power-of-2 N, the actual error growth is O(log N) per output cell — much tighter. The tolerance can be tightened proportionally:
- Power-of-2 N: bound = N * log2(N) * 32 * EPSILON
- Non-power-of-2 N: keep N^2 * EPSILON (fallback path is still naive)

- ft-conformance/src/lib.rs torch_fft_numpy_subprocess_conformance updated with branched tolerance
- All 6 existing seed inputs (including 6-element non-power-of-2 case) still pass
- Commit message documents the math (Cooley-Tukey log2(N) butterfly error growth)

At N=8 modest tightening (5.7e-15 → 5.3e-15); at N=4096 this would be ~2000x tighter. All 6 corpus cases still pass.

title: Use norm_dim in functional_normalize for p=0 and infinity parity
description: Discovery pass with empty ready queue: ft-api::functional_normalize hand-rolls the denominator as (sum(abs(x)^p))^(1/p). title: porting: add tensor_asinh / tensor_acosh / tensor_atanh for torch parity
description:

  asinh(x) = log(x + sqrt(x^2 + 1))
  acosh(x) = log(x + sqrt(x^2 - 1))   (x >= 1)
  atanh(x) = 0.5 * log((1 + x) / (1 - x))   (|x| < 1)
Gradient-correct since all sub-ops are on the autograd tape. Useful for normalizing-flow models, conformal maps, and porting numpy code.

All autograd-aware via existing primitives. 5 unit tests cover known values (asinh(sinh(t)) = t round-trip etc.) and analytic gradient regression for asinh and atanh (d/dx asinh = 1/sqrt(1+x²), d/dx atanh = 1/(1-x²)). ft-api now at 1250 lib tests.

title: [porting-to-rust] missing tensor_special_i0 / i0e (modified Bessel of first kind, order 0)
description:
torch.special.i0(x) is the modified Bessel function of the first kind, order 0 — used in the von Mises distribution PDF and various scientific-computing pipelines. torch.special.i0e is the exponentially-scaled variant (i0(x) * exp(-|x|)) that avoids overflow at large |x|.

FEATURE_PARITY.md doesn't list either — they're a real torch.special parity gap. Implementation requires either:

  - power-series for |x| < ~3.75 (Abramowitz & Stegun 9.8.1)
  - asymptotic expansion for |x| >= 3.75 (A&S 9.8.2)

This is closer to a libm port than a compose; it would live in ft-kernel-cpu with a tensor_special_i0 wrapper in ft-api. Consider implementing via libm crate's i0 if available, otherwise hand-coding the standard Cephes-style approximation.

Acceptance: tensor_special_i0 + tensor_special_i0e on FrankenTorchSession; autograd-aware (d/dx i0(x) = i1(x) — would also need i1, or implement via finite-difference for now); ≥6 lib tests covering known values (i0(0) = 1, i0(1) ≈ 1.266065878), exponentially-scaled regime, NaN/inf propagation, sign symmetry (i0(-x) = i0(x)).
close_reason: Shipped in e398972 — tensor_special_i0 + tensor_special_i0e via A&S 9.8.1/9.8.2 piecewise polynomial. Forward-only with fail-loud on requires_grad (autograd needs tensor_special_i1 for d/dx i0 = i1 — file follow-up bead when needed). 7 lib tests cover known values, even symmetry, NaN, fail-loud, and i0e bounded at x=100. - tanh is the workhorse for RNN/LSTM
- silu/swish (= x*sigmoid(x)) is used in transformer FFN
- mish (= x*tanh(softplus(x))) is used in detection / vision

title: [testing-fuzzing] no fuzz target for isnan + isinf + isfinite (predicate trio)
description:
isnan_tensor_contiguous_f64 (1085), isinf_tensor_contiguous_f64 (1092), and isfinite_tensor_contiguous_f64 (1099) are the three IEEE-predicate kernels. Each maps an f64 to f64 (0.0 or 1.0) — mask outputs.

Despite the simplicity, regressions are possible:
- isnan masking the wrong bit pattern (catching subnormals as NaN)
- isinf catching NaN as inf
- isfinite returning true for inf

Mutual exclusion invariant: for any input x, exactly one of isnan(x), isinf(x), isfinite(x) is 1.0 (the other two are 0.0).

Acceptance:
- new fuzz target ft_kernel_cpu_predicates driving all 3 ops
- inputs include adversarial special values: NaN, -NaN, +inf, -inf, ±0, finite
- on Ok, asserts: output.len == numel; each cell is exactly 0.0 or 1.0; mutual exclusion (sum across the 3 ops == 1.0 per cell)
- >=2 corpus seeds
- registered in fuzz/Cargo.toml
- compiles cleanly under rch exec
close_reason: Shipped: ft_kernel_cpu_predicates fuzz target covering isnan/isinf/isfinite. Inputs inject adversarial special values every 12th byte (NaN, +inf, -inf, +0, -0) so all three predicates see positives + negatives every run. Two per-cell invariants: (1) output domain exactly {0.0, 1.0} catches any value-leak regression; (2) mutual exclusion (sum across 3 ops == 1.0) catches NaN-as-finite or inf-as-NaN regressions immediately and pinpoints the offending op. title: [deadlock-finder-and-fixer] legacy oracle stdin write happens BEFORE stdout/stderr reader threads spawn — classic pipe deadlock
description:
run_legacy_oracle_script (ft-conformance/src/lib.rs ~9095) does:

  spawn child(stdin=pipe, stdout=pipe, stderr=pipe)
  take child.stdin
  stdin.write_all(body)            // writes entire payload
  drop(stdin)                       // child sees EOF
  take child.stdout, child.stderr
  spawn stdout_reader thread
  spawn stderr_reader thread
  wait_for_legacy_oracle_exit(...)

The ordering allows a classic UNIX pipe deadlock when:

  1. body.len() > 64 KB (Linux default pipe buffer; payload
     limit is 1 MB so this is 16x the buffer). Parent's
     write_all blocks waiting for child to read.
  2. Child (python + torch import) writes anything to stdout
     or stderr during stdin read — torch imports commonly emit
     UserWarning, deprecation warnings, FutureWarning, or
     CUDA-init messages on stderr at import time, well before
     the script reads sys.stdin.
  3. Child stderr write blocks because the 64KB pipe buffer
     fills (no reader is draining yet — they don't spawn
     until AFTER write_all returns).
  4. Parent blocked on stdin.write_all, child blocked on
     stderr.write. No progress. Deadlock until timeout reaper.

Fix: spawn the stdout/stderr reader threads BEFORE writing to stdin so all three pipes drain concurrently. Take all three pipe handles up-front, spawn the two readers, THEN write to stdin and drop it. The post-write timeout reap path is unchanged.

Acceptance: stdin write_all moved to AFTER stdout/stderr reader threads are spawned; existing legacy-oracle conformance tests still pass; the 1 MB stdin payload + chatty stderr scenario no longer deadlocks.
close_reason: Shipped in 2421733 — stdout/stderr reader threads now spawn before the stdin write, eliminating the classic 64 KB-pipe-buffer deadlock when payloads exceed pipe capacity and the child writes to stderr (e.g. torch import warnings) during stdin drain. All 16 legacy_oracle lib tests pass.

title: Remaining ft-api ops with fail-loud autograd guards: stft, istft, affine_grid, grid_sample, complex/view_as_real/view_as_complex
description:
After closing frankentorch-1tax (statistical/special ops), 7 ops in ft-api still reject requires_grad=true inputs with hard errors instead of carrying gradients:

- stft (line 1248) — short-time Fourier transform; PyTorch's torch.stft supports backward via inverse FFT.
- istft (line 1411) — inverse short-time Fourier transform; symmetric to stft.
- stft window tensor (line 6733) — separate guard rejecting tracked window inputs.
- affine_grid (line 7774) — torch.nn.functional.affine_grid supports backward.
- grid_sample (line 7905) — torch.nn.functional.grid_sample supports backward.
- complex (line 994/1001) — torch.complex(re, im) supports backward through real and imaginary inputs (Wirtinger derivatives).
- view_as_real / view_as_complex (lines 1101, 1145) — complex view ops also support gradients in PyTorch.

These are not 'severed-autograd' — they're explicit guards that fail-loud, so users can't accidentally lose gradients silently. But they DO block training paths that would work in PyTorch (e.g., audio models using STFT, vision models using affine_grid + grid_sample for spatial transformer networks).

Each child needs its own fix bead. Children grouped by domain:
  Audio:   stft + istft + stft-window
  Vision:  affine_grid + grid_sample
  Complex: complex + view_as_real + view_as_complex (deferred — Wirtinger calculus is non-trivial; PyTorch's complex autograd took years to stabilize)

Priority for audio/vision (P2): real downstream training paths blocked. Priority for complex (P3): Wirtinger calculus is genuinely tricky and may need its own design doc first.
notes:
affine_grid slice closed in 669df96 (frankentorch-bfj5). Remaining children that still need work:
  - stft / istft / stft window — Audio. Backward via inverse FFT or windowed-overlap-add gradient. Non-trivial.
  - grid_sample (bilinear mode) — Vision. Backward via bilinear interpolation derivatives in both input and grid; nearest mode is non-differentiable in grid.
  - complex / view_as_real / view_as_complex — Wirtinger calculus. PyTorch's complex autograd took years to stabilize; needs a design doc first.
